meta.title: FACE data dictionary
meta.ids: A variable id is the name of the column in the tables that facedata.<cohort>.load() returns (data, patients, treatments, relatives). The raw column of the extraction is in cohorts.<cohort>.source.columns.
meta.how_to_load: from facedata import bp; result = bp.load('<extraction>', instruments=[...]); result.data[['usubjid', 'visit', '<id>']]

fields.meta: Where the file comes from and how to read it.
fields.cohorts.<cohort>: Title, extraction file, Excel dictionary, tabs in the order of the workbook, patients, visits (label, planned month, number), tables (rows, columns), about (population, design, traps and tutorial, written by hand in dictionary/cohorts.yaml).
fields.subjects.<key>: One subject (depression rated by the clinician, sleep, impulsivity...) and the instruments that measure it in each cohort (dictionary/same_subject.yaml): title, bp, sz, dr, asp (lists of instrument ids), note. Instruments of one subject are not on one scale and never share a column.
fields.constructs.<key>: area and label of each construct that a variable can measure (dictionary/constructs.yaml).
fields.flags.<code>: severity and meaning of each flag code of facedata (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, section 6).
fields.instruments.<name>: title, description, version, reference, reference_confidence, respondent, construct, period, sources, flags (caveats written by hand), common (stack verdict across cohorts, variables to use, note), cohorts.<cohort> (tab, tab_all, section, level, table, schema file, notes of the schema, edition, difference from the other cohort), variables (ids), incomplete.
fields.variables.<id>: One record per delivered column name. The id is the column name in the tables returned by facedata.<cohort>.load().
fields.variables.<id>.level: item (counted in a score), subscore, score, standalone (belongs to no score), companion (censoring or edition column), key.
fields.variables.<id>.kind: continuous, ordinal, binary, nominal, date, text or key: how to treat the values in an analysis. type is the type of the schema (number, item, band, category, date, time, text, score).
fields.variables.<id>.meaning: Plain sentence written by hand; absent when only the label is known.
fields.variables.<id>.construct: Key of constructs: of the variable when its annotation gives one, else of its instrument.
fields.variables.<id>.direction: higher_means, polarity (worse, better, neutral, not_applicable), basis (stated, anchors, literature: written by hand with a source; formula, coding, measurement: derived from the schema), source, in_score (the score an item counts in, keyed same, reversed or recoded). Empty when no source says it.
fields.variables.<id>.cutoffs: List of value, meaning, source, confidence. Only cut-offs that a project document gives.
fields.variables.<id>.parents / children / comp: The hierarchy: the scores that count this value, the values a score counts, the raw score a standard score is read from, the variable a companion column goes with.
fields.variables.<id>.harmonisation: stack (yes, with care, no: can the cohorts be put under one another), recommended (named among the variables to use across cohorts), note, exception and raw_column_note (facedata/shared_names.yaml), differences (fields that the schemas of two cohorts do not give alike).
fields.variables.<id>.incomplete: Names of the fields that no source gives: meaning, construct, direction, range, answer_labels.
fields.variables.<id>.cohorts.<cohort>: What one cohort says. label, level, kind, type, unit, instrument and tab are written here only when they differ from the record: an absent field has the value of the record. table (data, patients, treatments or relatives: where the value is delivered, under the column name <id>), source.columns (raw columns of the extraction file named in cohorts.<cohort>.extraction; source.stored_score: the raw column of the score as stored), range, categories (delivered labels), raw_codes (raw text to delivered value), answer_labels and excel (labels and codings of the Excel dictionary, not verified: only in a build with excel_labels: true, never in the committed files), missing_codes, edition (column and values: the visits on which it is read), derivation (method, formula in words, items, reverse, points, scale, min_items, norm_table, function, stored_in), reading (fields of the schema), rules (the same as sentences).
fields.variables.<id>.cohorts.<cohort>.n: rows (rows of the table), valid (rows with a value), patients (patients with a value), patients_2plus (patients with a value at two visits or more), baseline (patients with a value in the baseline row).
fields.variables.<id>.cohorts.<cohort>.missing: Percentages. all: rows of the table without a value. baseline: patients without a value in the baseline row (inclusion visit, completed by the screening visit, facedata.common.baseline). in_instrument: visits without a value among the visits that hold at least one value of the instrument.
fields.variables.<id>.cohorts.<cohort>.timepoin: Number of values at each visit label, in visit order.
fields.variables.<id>.cohorts.<cohort>.stats: all (every row) and baseline (one row per patient): n, mean, sd, min, max, p01, p05, p25, median, p75, p95, p99, n_distinct, at_minimum_pct and at_maximum_pct (share at each end of the range); for a date first_year and last_year; for a text n and n_distinct only. Values are not winsorised.
fields.variables.<id>.cohorts.<cohort>.dist: all and baseline. kind bins: x holds the edges (one more than n) between the 1st and 99th percentile, the end bins hold the tails. kind levels: one count per answer or label. kind years: one count per year.
fields.variables.<id>.cohorts.<cohort>.flags: Number of cells per flag code (see flags). censored: left and right. years: first and last year with a value. n_sites: number of centres with a value.
fields.counts: A count from 1 to 4 is never written: it is given as -1 and means 'fewer than 5', and a percentage that would give it away is left out. A variable with fewer than 5 values has no statistics, one with fewer than 20 no distribution.

about.population: Adults with a bipolar disorder (type 1, type 2 or not otherwise specified), assessed in the FondaMental network of expert centres for bipolar disorder.
about.design: A screening record, then an inclusion visit (V0) and follow-up visits every six months or every year. Few patients are followed beyond five years.
traps: `_v0` and `_fu` are two different questions: the inclusion visit asks about the whole life, the later visits about the time since the last visit or about an update of the inclusion form. Never put the two in one column.

Editions and forms have their own columns: WAIS-III and WAIS-IV, BIS-10 and BIS-12, the long and short ALS, WURS-25 and WURS-61, DSM-IV and DSM-5. A column such as `wais_version`, `bis_form` or `dsm_version` says which one a visit used.
Empty does not mean no: an empty cell is not asked, not answered or not usable. A no is written 0.
Sex, diagnosis and family history are in the table `patients`: join them to the visits on `usubjid`.
The screening visits hold only a few questionnaires (Altman, QIDS, MDQ). Start from V0.
Patients leave: a figure over time mixes change and departures.

Centres differ, and the forms changed over the years, most of all around 2022 (a "no for all" shortcut leaves the diseases of a section empty). Look at a variable per centre and per year before concluding.
The suicide answers of the follow-up visits of 2022 and 2023 are not delivered: the form of these two years asked about the whole life again.

about.population: Adults with schizophrenia, a schizoaffective or a schizophreniform disorder, assessed in the FondaMental network of expert centres for schizophrenia.
about.design: A screening record (an EQ-5D only), an inclusion visit (V0) and yearly follow-up visits. Fewer than half of the patients are seen at one year.
traps: `_v0` and `_fu` are two different questions (whole life, or since the last visit, or a yearly update of the inclusion form). Never put the two in one column.
WAIS-III and WAIS-IV have their own columns, for every subtest and every IQ; `wais_version` says which one a visit used.
Empty does not mean no: a no is written 0.

Some scores were wrong in the database and are delivered corrected (three PANSS factors, two WAIS-IV indices, the laterality quotient). Others are flagged: the CVLT z-scores of 2022 to mid-2025, and the Barona expected IQ, whose occupation is most often a copy of the diploma.

Some answers are lost by the export: no patient is married or living as a couple, no income is a salary, the date of death is not exported, and `substance_disorder_v0` is missing on most inclusion visits (use the column of each substance).
Patients leave, centres differ, and the tests changed around 2015 to 2018 and part of the medical history in 2022: look at a variable per centre and per year.

about.population: Adults with a treatment-resistant major depressive disorder (TRD), assessed in the FondaMental network of expert centres for resistant depression. The inclusion criteria ask for a MADRS above 20.
about.design: A screening visit, a row of its own, then an inclusion visit (V0) and follow-up visits at 6, 12, 18 and 24 months and later. Half of the patients are seen at six months, a quarter at two years. The visits at 6 and 18 months are short: depression scales, weight and laboratory tests only.
traps: The MINI, the Thase and Rush stage and the inclusion criteria are on the `screening` row of a patient, not on the V0 row. The MADRS is rated at both, on separate rows.
`_lifetime` and `_since_visit` are two different questions. Never put the two in one column.
Empty does not mean no, but a 0 in a box can mean not asked: in the MINI, the family form and the traumatic events, some boxes hold 0 wherever the form was opened. Look at the flag `derived_doubt`.

Since 2018 a simplified visit leaves out eleven self-questionnaires (STAI, Altman, MAThyS, Rosenberg, PSQI, Epworth, CSM, MARS, PRISE-M, BIS-10, BFI) and three clinician scales (YMRS, FAST, BAS). An empty scale is then not asked, and the extraction does not say which visits are simplified; some centres use it much more than others.
Some scores were wrong in the database and are delivered corrected: the CTQ, the BIS-10, the MARS, the SHAPS and the Fagerström total; the QIDS total is computed where the database stores none.
The medication lists are damaged: for a patient with several products there is no dose and no date, and the `on_...` columns are often empty.
Centres differ: look at a variable per centre and per year.

about.population: Children from 5 years and adults assessed for an autism spectrum disorder (Asperger syndrome and ASD) in the FondaMental network of expert centres. `diagnosis` says whether the centre confirmed the disorder (`asd_confirmed`) or not (`asd_not_confirmed`): both groups are delivered.
about.design: A screening record and an inclusion visit (V0). About one patient in ten has a follow-up visit. The dictionary of the cohort arrived after the module was written: every instrument was identified from the data, then checked against it.
traps: A child form and an adult form are two instruments with different columns and ranges: STAIC and STAI, CDI and BDI-II, BRIEF and BRIEF-A, the child and adult ADHD-RS. Never add them up or put them on one axis without saying so.

Two generations of forms: an old set of questionnaires until about 2017 (AQ, Empathy Quotient, RBS-R, Hamilton scales), a new set from 2019 to 2021 (RAADS-R, BDI-II, GSQ). An old scale is empty after the change because it was no longer asked.
The ADOS has four modules, each with its own columns and cut-offs; `ados_module` says which one was given.
The codes 7, 8 and 9 of the ADI-R and ADOS items are not levels. Never average the items: use the algorithm scores.
The centres do not give the same instruments: check that every centre fills a score before comparing them.
A treatment list belongs to a visit (in the other cohorts it is the history of the patient), and a missing list is not "no treatment".

depression_clinician.title: Depression, rated by the clinician
depression_clinician.note: The Calgary scale is built for schizophrenia (it avoids the negative symptoms); `calgary_total` is the sum of its nine items (0 to 27), not on the scale of the MADRS. The HAM-D is on the old forms of the autism cohort only.

depression_patient.title: Depression, rated by the patient
depression_patient.note: The BDI-II is for adults and the CDI for children.

anxiety.title: Anxiety
anxiety.note: In the autism cohort the STAI Y-A is for adults and the STAIC for children.

functioning.title: Functioning
functioning.note: The EPHP is filled by someone close to the patient.

sleep.title: Sleep
sleep.note: In the autism cohort the CSHQ is for children.

impulsivity.title: Impulsivity
impulsivity.note: BP used the BIS-10, then the BIS-12: two editions, two sets of columns. The autism cohort has the BIS-10 in a pilot of its old forms only, on too few visits to analyse.

adhd_adults.title: ADHD in adults
adhd_adults.note: The WURS-25 and the WURS-61 are two forms with their own columns.

suicide.title: Suicidal thoughts and acts
suicide.note: The inclusion visit asks about the whole life and the later visits about the time since the last visit: two questions, never one column.

comorbid_diagnoses.title: Comorbid psychiatric diagnoses
comorbid_diagnoses.note: BP and SZ use the forms of the expert centres; DR uses the MINI, at the screening visit; the autism cohort has forms of its own.

intellectual_ability.title: Intellectual ability
intellectual_ability.note: WAIS-III and WAIS-IV are two editions with their own columns; the WISC is the children's scale. BP has subtests only, no full-scale IQ.

thymic_activation.label: Thymic state from inhibition to activation

social_cognition.label: Social cognition and theory of mind

substance_use.label: Substance use and substance use disorders

missing_code.meaning: The cell held a missing code

date_partial.meaning: Day or month was unknown, or the day was replaced by the day that the export writes (`day`)

format_repaired.meaning: A number was written unusually but unambiguously

censored_left.meaning: The cell was `<limit`. For a band: this band or a lower one

censored_right.meaning: The cell was `>limit`. For a band: this band or a higher one

band_from_z.meaning: The band is the one a z-score has under the normal law: the z-score of the cell, or one computed with the regression of the norms

unit_inferred.meaning: Unit taken from the magnitude; the label was missing, unknown or impossible

sign_flipped.meaning: A value stored in the other direction was turned (around the middle of its range, or multiplied by −1)

version_inferred.meaning: No version was recorded for the patient; it was taken from the inclusion date

version_overridden.meaning: The form labels the visit with one edition, a column that only another edition has is filled: the visit has the other edition

visit_removed.meaning: The visit has several impossible values in the instrument (`implausible_visits`): its block is shifted, so its other values are not delivered

duplicate_row.meaning: A duplicated visit record was dropped

unit_doubt.meaning: The value was possible under its label but fits another unit better

sign_doubt.meaning: The value is dated within 90 days of the day the direction changed, or has no date; or the visits of its centre and year lean to the other direction, not clearly enough to decide

band_middle.meaning: The cell held a band of values (`60-51`); the value is the middle of the band

column_conflict.meaning: Two raw columns of one variable hold different values; the first one listed is kept

score_as_stored.meaning: None of the items of the score is recorded: the score typed in the extraction is delivered, unchecked. Also a total built on such a score

derived_doubt.meaning: The value was computed by the EMR from a stored score that differs from the recomputed one

patient_value_varies.meaning: A patient-level variable, or an answer about a relative, changes between visits

list_crossed.meaning: An item of a list that the export crossed: the patient has several products, and the file does not say which dose or date belongs to which (SCHEMA_SPEC, section 15)

visit_order.meaning: Visit dates are not in visit order

check_failed.meaning: A custom check named in the schema failed, or a value is above the value it may not exceed on the same row (`not_above`)

period_doubt.meaning: The visit is dated in a period in which the schema says the column is not reliable

period_removed.meaning: The visit is dated in a period in which the schema says the column is not reliable and asks for the value not to be delivered; `raw` holds what was written

unparsed.meaning: The cell could not be read as its type

unknown_code.meaning: A category value is not in the code list

out_of_range.meaning: The value is outside the hard range. Also a visit date before the cohort opened or after today, an impossible age, and a date that must come before its visit on the day of the visit or later (`before_visit`)

not_shown.meaning: The cell answers a question that the form did not show for the answer given (`shown_if`): a value the form wrote by itself; `raw` holds it

unit_unknown.meaning: No usable unit label and the magnitude fits several units; or a percentage of a value that is missing

version_unknown.meaning: Data present but version not recognisable

norm_missing.meaning: No standard score could be read: the norm table was not found, or it has nothing for this age, raw score and second variable. For a z-score computed with a regression: the table was not found, or a variable of the regression is missing

score_not_recomputed.meaning: The extraction stores the score but an item is missing: the score is not delivered; `detail` holds the stored value

allergic_history_fu.title: Medical history: allergic and inflammatory diseases (yearly follow-up visits)

bp.notes: One yes/no question (does the patient have an allergic or inflammatory disease), then a list of five boxes: asthma, allergy other than asthma, lupus, rheumatoid arthritis, another autoimmune disease. Yes/no answers are delivered as 1 and 0; "unknown" (U, "Ne sais pas") is a missing code. The list. The boxes ticked are written in one cell ("Asthme (allergique ou non),Lupus") and delivered as one yes/no variable each. They are 0 after a "no" to the first question (asked_if), and missing when it is "unknown" or when the list is empty after a "yes". The extraction also holds one 0/1 column per disease, written by the export on every row: where the list is filled they say the same as the list, elsewhere they are 0 whatever the first answer. They are not read. Two forms in the same columns (decision D59 in PROGRESS.md). The same questions are asked at the inclusion visit and at the yearly visits, never at the six-monthly ones: the 3,352 six-monthly visits of the follow-up version (11,686 visits, of which 8,334 are yearly) and the screening visits never hold a cell of this section. At inclusion they are about the whole life. At the yearly visits a disease answered "yes" at inclusion is often answered "no": 414 of the 717 "yes" of this section that are answered again (66 of 131 for asthma, 147 of 219 for an allergy). The yearly form is the inclusion form again: the same questions, with no period in their wording, after one more question, "is there a change since the last visit?", which the extraction does not hold (read in the application in November 2026, decision D84 in PROGRESS.md). A yearly answer is an update given at that visit: neither a history of the whole life nor strictly an answer about the time since the last visit. The two are delivered as separate columns, ending in _v0 (inclusion visit) and _fu (yearly visits); visit_form says which form a visit used and is read from the visit label. The question "is there a change since the last visit?" is shown at the yearly visit only and is not exported (rad_pas_dechangement, DM-10): an empty yearly section may mean "no change". This section is not emptied in 2022 like the others, because it has no "no for all" shortcut (decision D83 in PROGRESS.md): it is answered at 88% of the inclusion visits until 2021 and at 82% from 2022, with the same share of "yes" among the answers (8.8% and 8.0%). The yearly visits answer it at 31% of the visits until 2021 and at 20% from 2022. Details. The date of onset, "treated" and "controlled" (équilibrée) are asked only after a "yes" and are missing otherwise. 1000-01-01 is written in a date that was not typed, and in every empty date of a form saved from 2025 (in the nine sections together, 64% of the inclusion visits and 34% of the yearly visits dated 2025 or later hold one; at inclusion 0% to 3% of the visits up to 2024Q4, 28% in 2025Q1, 70% in 2025Q4, 94% in 2026Q3): date_placeholder. Hard limits of the dates: 1900 to 2026. "Another autoimmune disease" is named in a free text delivered as written. Details under the boxes. The form shows the date, "treated" and "controlled" of a disease under its box of the list. 46 of these cells are filled although the box is not ticked (34 at inclusion, 12 at the yearly visits), 45 of them under an empty list: they stay as recorded, with no shown_if (decision D145 in PROGRESS.md). Dates and the visit. Of the 1,181 delivered dates of the section (both forms), 6 are after the visit (6 later, by up to 3 months), 7 are on the day of the visit and 4 are before the year of birth. They stay as recorded: no before_visit (decision D145 in PROGRESS.md). Years and centres. The report panels show a shift for three items of the inclusion form: asthma_treated_v0 (449 answers, 62% yes: 48% to 74% by year, 46% to 82% in 8 centres), allergy_treated_v0 (862, 34%: 20% to 50% by year, 16% to 55% in 9 centres) and allergy_controlled_v0 (831, 69%: 49% to 86% by year, 54% to 83% in 8 centres). The shift is the distance between the median of a year or a centre and the overall median, and the median of a yes/no item is 0 or 1: it reads 1 as soon as a year or a centre lies on the other side of one half. The centres differ by 29 to 39 points, with no step by year and no mixture of units.

sz.notes: One question, "Pathologies allergiques", then two boxes written in one cell, as in BP (asked_if: no allergic disease means neither). BP and DR ask about "pathologies allergiques et inflammatoires": the SZ question is not the same one, so its gate is named allergic_disease_fu and not allergic_inflammatory_fu (decision D53); 29% of the inclusion answers are yes, against 8.8% in BP. The columns asthme_mhoccur and allergie_mhoccur repeat each box in a column of its own and are ignored. Lupus and rheumatoid arthritis, boxes of this list in BP, are with the auto-immune diseases here. Yes/no answers are delivered as 1 and 0; "U" is a missing code. "Treated" and the other details are asked after a yes and are missing otherwise. Two forms in the same columns, as in FACE BP (BP decisions D59 and D84; here decisions D20 and D56 in PROGRESS.md). The same questions are asked at the inclusion visit and at the yearly follow-up visits (every follow-up visit of the extraction is a yearly one; the 1,675 screening records hold no cell of the section). At inclusion they are about the whole life. At the yearly visits a disease answered yes at inclusion is most often answered no (39 of 47 follow-up answers for a head injury, 43 of 54 for acne). The yearly form is the inclusion form again, with no period in the wording of its questions, after one more question that the extraction does not hold: "Pas de changement de l'histoire somatique depuis la dernière visite?" (rad_pas_dechangement, shown at the yearly visit only; export request R78). An empty follow-up section may therefore mean "no change". A yearly answer is an update given at that visit: neither a history of the whole life nor strictly an answer about the time since the last visit. The two are delivered as separate columns ending in _v0 and _fu; visit_form says which form a visit used. The section is answered at 81% to 100% of the inclusion visits of every year (lowest in 2017), with no fall in 2022. Three other sections of the medical history do fall in 2022: the digestive diseases, the autoimmune diseases and the other diseases (decisions D23 and D51 in PROGRESS.md). At follow-up the section is held by 405 of the 2,588 yearly visits (4% to 44% of the yearly visits of a year from 2012); the other yearly visits leave it empty, which may mean "no change" (see the two forms above). The SZ form is shorter than the BP one: one question "treated" per disease, and no date of onset and no "controlled". The names are those of BP where the question is the same.
sz.difference: the shorter SZ history form; the first question is 'Pathologies allergiques' where BP and DR ask about the allergic and inflammatory diseases, so the gate is named allergic_disease_fu

dr.notes: The BP schema with the columns and the codes of this extraction, at the visits of 2 and 4 years: 131 visits. The questions and what is specific to this cohort are described in allergic_history_v0.yaml. Two forms in the same columns, as in BP: the inclusion visit (form 164 of the application) and the visits of 2 and 4 years (form 191), where the same questions are asked again. visit_form says which form a visit uses, and each form has its own schema and its own variables (_v0 and _fu). A follow-up answer is a yearly update (BP D84): an answer given at that visit on the inclusion form asked again, with no period in the wording of the questions. It is neither a history of the whole life nor strictly an answer about the time since the last visit, and it is never mixed with the inclusion answers. Form 191 has no question "is there a change since the last visit?" (BP and SZ have one, which the extraction does not hold): the whole block is asked again. The block is filled at 90 of 146 visits of 2 years, 36 of 69 visits of 4 years, 3 of 4 of 5 years, 1 of 3 of 3 years and 1 of 298 six-monthly visits, and at none of the 253 visits of 1 year and the 150 of 18 months. Form 191 is form 164 without the perinatal block and with no period wording. Answers are numbers here (1 yes, 0 no), where BP has words. The forms offer only Oui and Non: no cell holds "not known" and none is read. "Treated" and "controlled" are in columns named _tr_mhdecod and _eq_mhdecod. Dates are whole dates.
dr.difference: the answers are numbers; the five diseases are boxes in columns of their own

allergic_history_fu.description: Medical history at the yearly follow-up visits: allergic and inflammatory diseases (asthma, another allergy, lupus, rheumatoid arthritis, another autoimmune disease). The inclusion form asked again, as an update given at that visit.
allergic_history_fu.period: an update given at the yearly visit (neither the whole life nor strictly the time since the last visit)
flags: A follow-up answer is the inclusion form asked again, with no period in its wording: a disease answered yes at inclusion is often answered no. Do not stack the _fu answers with the _v0 answers.

BP and SZ: the yearly form starts with 'is there a change since the last visit?', which is not exported, so an empty yearly section may mean 'no change'. DR has no such question and asks the block at the visits of 2 and 4 years.

SZ asks about 'allergic diseases' only (asthma and allergy; the gate is named allergic_disease_*): it is not the BP and DR question, and 29% of its inclusion answers are yes against 8.8% in BP. In SZ lupus and rheumatoid arthritis are in the auto-immune section.
This section has no 'no for all' shortcut and is not emptied in 2022, unlike most sections of the BP medical history.
Yes is 1 and no is 0; 'unknown' is a missing code. The details (date of onset, treated, controlled) are asked only after a yes and are missing otherwise (SZ asks 'treated' only).

common.note: The follow-up form is the inclusion form asked again at the yearly visit: its questions carry no period, and an answer is a yearly update, neither the whole life nor strictly the time since the last visit (a yes of the inclusion is often a no a year later). It is delivered in columns of its own (_fu) and is not to be added to the inclusion answers. The six-monthly and the screening visits hold no cell of these sections, and an empty yearly section may mean "no change since the last visit" (the question is not exported). The same reserves as at inclusion apply.
