The date of onset, "treated" and "controlled" (équilibrée) are asked only after a "yes" and are missing otherwise, except 6 detail cells typed after a "no" (kept as recorded). 1000-01-01 is written in a date that was not typed, and in every empty date of a form saved from 2025 (in the nine sections together, 64% of the inclusion visits and 34% of the yearly visits dated 2025 or later hold one; at inclusion 0% to 3% of the visits up to 2024Q4, 28% in 2025Q1, 70% in 2025Q4, 94% in 2026Q3): date_placeholder. Hard limits of the dates: 1900 to 2026. Dates and the visit. Of the 1,598 delivered dates of the section (both forms), 19 are after the visit (10 in the month of the visit, 9 later, by up to 8 months) and 58 are on the day of the visit. They stay as recorded: no before_visit (decision D145 in PROGRESS.md). Years and centres. Three items show a shift. dyslipidaemia_controlled_v0 (0.5 by year): 36% yes, 21% to 50% by year (16 years) and 18% to 48% by centre (10 centres), no step. At the yearly visits dyslipidaemia_treated_fu (363 answers, 36% yes) and dyslipidaemia_controlled_fu (335, 34%) show a shift of 1 by year and by centre: the share of yes falls from 51% and 46% in 2015-2016 to 31% and 34% in 2017-2018 and 25% and 22% in 2019-2021, and the centres range from 14% to 57% and from 18% to 55%. It follows which centres answer: two centres at 18% and 8% yes (treated; 13% and 16% for controlled) hold 75 of the 137 answers of 2019-2021 (71 of 125 for controlled) and 3 of the 102 of 2015-2016. It is a spread between centres, not a change of the form.

sz.notes: The SZ form asks about type 2 diabetes here (type 1 is with the auto-immune diseases), where BP asks one question and then the type. Yes/no answers are delivered as 1 and 0; "U" is a missing code. "Treated" and the other details are asked after a yes and are missing otherwise. At inclusion one centre ticks "treated" on 21% of the yes answers of the whole medical history (54 of 262 answers), the other centres on 45% to 63% (53% pooled, 679 of 1,293): a habit of that centre, which makes the site shift of the "treated" columns of this section and, with the mix of centres in groups of 20 to 30 answers, their year shift. The follow-up answers are too few per centre to show it. Two forms in the same columns, as in FACE BP (BP decisions D59 and D84; here decisions D20 and D56 in PROGRESS.md). The same questions are asked at the inclusion visit and at the yearly follow-up visits (every follow-up visit of the extraction is a yearly one; the 1,675 screening records hold no cell of the section). At inclusion they are about the whole life. At the yearly visits a disease answered yes at inclusion is most often answered no (39 of 47 follow-up answers for a head injury, 43 of 54 for acne). The yearly form is the inclusion form again, with no period in the wording of its questions, after one more question that the extraction does not hold: "Pas de changement de l'histoire somatique depuis la dernière visite?" (rad_pas_dechangement, shown at the yearly visit only; export request R78). An empty follow-up section may therefore mean "no change". A yearly answer is an update given at that visit: neither a history of the whole life nor strictly an answer about the time since the last visit. The two are delivered as separate columns ending in _v0 and _fu; visit_form says which form a visit used. The section is answered at 81% to 100% of the inclusion visits of every year (lowest in 2017), with no fall in 2022. Three other sections of the medical history do fall in 2022: the digestive diseases, the autoimmune diseases and the other diseases (decisions D23 and D51 in PROGRESS.md). The shortcut "Non pour tous" of the form copies "no" to each disease of this section, as its script is meant to (decision D51). The SZ form is shorter than the BP one: one question "treated" per disease, and no date of onset and no "controlled". The names are those of BP where the question is the same.
sz.difference: the shorter SZ history form

dr.notes: The BP schema with the columns and the codes of this extraction, at the inclusion visit: 573 visits (86% to 93% of the inclusions in every period). Two forms in the same columns, as in BP: the inclusion visit (form 164 of the application) and the visits of 2 and 4 years (form 191), where the same questions are asked again. visit_form says which form a visit uses, and each form has its own schema and its own variables (_v0 and _fu). A follow-up answer is a yearly update (BP D84): an answer given at that visit on the inclusion form asked again, with no period in the wording of the questions. It is neither a history of the whole life nor strictly an answer about the time since the last visit, and it is never mixed with the inclusion answers. Form 191 has no question "is there a change since the last visit?" (BP and SZ have one, which the extraction does not hold): the whole block is asked again. The block is filled at 90 of 146 visits of 2 years, 36 of 69 visits of 4 years, 3 of 4 of 5 years, 1 of 3 of 3 years and 1 of 298 six-monthly visits, and at none of the 253 visits of 1 year and the 150 of 18 months. Form 191 is form 164 without the perinatal block and with no period wording. Answers are numbers here (1 yes, 0 no), where BP has words. The forms offer only Oui and Non: no cell holds "not known" and none is read. "Treated" and "controlled" are in columns named _tr_mhdecod and _eq_mhdecod. Dates are whole dates. The thyroid disorder has one date of onset (BP has one for hyperthyroidism and one for hypothyroidism). Its kind is stored 1 hypothyroidism, 2 hyperthyroidism, 0 "Ne sais pas" (forms 164 and 191, in the order of the BP list): 54 and 8 at inclusion; the 0 (7 inclusion visits and 1 follow-up visit) is a missing code. The type of diabetes is stored 1 type I, 2 type II, 0 "Ne sais pas": 4 and 29 at inclusion, and one 0, a missing code. "Induced by a treatment" is 1 lithium, 2 another treatment, as in BP. No question "induced by a treatment?" gates it: the form shows it under the disease. It is empty under a yes on 55 of 70 forms at inclusion (79%) and 19 of 25 at follow-up: an empty cell cannot be told from "not asked" and must not be read as "not induced". The kind of dyslipidaemia is two yes/no questions here (hypercholesterolaemia, hypertriglyceridaemia), shown after a dyslipidaemia yes: after a no they are empty, and asked_if reads them as 0 (902 cells at inclusion, 212 at follow-up). BP has one list of three answers, missing after a no. Among the 121 yes at inclusion both boxes are ticked on 34, cholesterol only on 57, triglycerides only on 10, neither on 6, and 14 are incomplete: the same split as the BP list. Of the 22 follow-up visits of patients with dyslipidaemia at inclusion, 13 answer no; thyroid disorder 6 of 20. The date of onset is empty under a yes on 53 of 121 dyslipidaemias. DR has no text for another endocrine disease (BP has one): the form asks only for a date.
dr.difference: the answers are numbers; one date for the thyroid disorder; the kind of dyslipidaemia is two yes/no questions (after a no they are 0 here, missing in BP); no text for another endocrine disease; the types are stored as numbers and read on the BP labels, with 0 for "not known"

endocrine_history_v0.description: Medical history at the inclusion visit, about the whole life: endocrine and metabolic diseases (diabetes and its type, thyroid disorder, dyslipidaemia and its type, another one).
endocrine_history_v0.period: whole life, asked at the inclusion visit
flags: BP from 2022: the section is mostly left empty (answered at 30% of the inclusion visits, against 88% until 2021), because the shortcut 'no for all' of the form is not exported. An empty section is missing, not 'no', and the share of yes among the answers from 2022 is not a prevalence.
SZ asks about type 2 diabetes here (type 1 is in its auto-immune section), where BP and DR ask one question and then the type.
'Induced by' (lithium or another treatment) is empty under most thyroid disorders: an empty cell must not be read as 'not induced'.
Yes is 1 and no is 0; 'unknown' is a missing code. The details (date of onset, treated, controlled) are asked only after a yes and are missing otherwise (SZ asks 'treated' only).
BP: 1000-01-01 is the placeholder of the application for a date that was not typed (most forms saved from 2025); it is delivered as missing (date_placeholder).

common.note: The same questions as the other history sections (treated, controlled, type, date of onset), with the reserves of their notes. Diabetes: BP and DR ask one question and its type (diabetes_v0, diabetes_type_v0); the SZ form asks type 2 here (diabetes_type2_v0) and type 1 in its auto-immune section (diabetes_type1_v0). DR also reads the two kinds of dyslipidaemia (cholesterol, triglycerides) as two yes/no boxes where BP has one list.

family_history.title: Family history, one row per relative

bp.section: Enfants, Fratrie, Parents, Grands-parents, Antécédents filles, Antécédents fils, Antécédents sœurs, Antécédents frères, Antécédents maternels, Antécédents paternels
bp.notes: One row per patient and relative: the mother, the father, up to five sisters, five brothers, five daughters and five sons, and the four grandparents. 29,849 relatives of 5,555 patients, delivered in the table relatives (decisions D58 and D70 in PROGRESS.md). The columns fdr_ and gp_ of the table patients sum them up (family_history_per_patient, below). Who has a row. The questions on a sister, a brother, a daughter or a son are asked for as many of them as the patient counted as affected in family_structure: "sister 1" is the first of the affected sisters, not the eldest sister, and at most five are described (read in the application in November 2026; decision D95 in PROGRESS.md). On the form of today the birth date, the death and its date of a sibling or a child are asked for the affected ones only; the older form asked them for every relative, which is why a birth date exists for unaffected ones: 850 birth dates of the extraction lie beyond a known number of affected relatives (357 visits of 352 patients, all up to February 2014). For these patients "sister k" is the k-th relative listed, not the k-th affected one. In this table 239 sister rows, 257 brother rows, 191 daughter rows and 205 son rows lie beyond the known number of affected ones. A parent or a grandparent is described after a "yes" in family_structure. So a row does not say that the relative has a disorder: half of the rows (15,040) hold only a birth date, a death or a date of death. A relative for whom nothing is known has no row. No row under a no. A parent or a grandparent answered "no" in family_structure has nothing to describe: 14,350 such answers, 10,210 with a row (a birth date or a death was typed) and 4,140 without. A missing block under a "no" means none, not an unknown disorder, and so does a missing block of a sibling or a child beyond the counted affected ones. To ask "does a relative have it", use the columns fdr_ and gp_ of the table patients, which apply this rule, and not the rows of this table. Read once. A family is described at the inclusion visit, and sometimes again later: 378 patients have the family questions answered at two or more visits. The yearly visit uses the same form again (D84), after the question "is there a change since the last visit?", which is not exported (R80 of EXPORT_REQUESTS.md): a later family form that is empty may mean "no change". A later answer is a yearly update (D84): neither the whole life nor strictly the time since the last visit. There is no yearly twin of this schema, as there is for the medical history, and a later answer is ignored. For each relative and question the first visit that holds an answer is read; where a later visit holds another one, the first is kept and the cell gets patient_value_varies (up to 257 relatives per variable). The later answers change in one direction mostly: 231 of the 378 patients differ at least once on the counts or the parents and grandparents; among the answers of the parents and the grandparents 190 "yes" become "no" and 55 "no" become "yes", and for 60 parents or grandparents (48 patients) the first answer says alive and a later one deceased. Disorder. One answer per relative: unipolar (a major depressive episode or unipolar disorder), bipolar, schizophrenia or none. "None" is the answer for 5,329 relatives who are described for something else: an anxiety disorder, a substance, a suicide attempt, a cardiovascular risk factor. "Unknown" (written U for the parents, "Ne sais pas" for the others) is a missing code: 2,473 relatives. Suicide. One answer too: none, attempt or completed. A relative who died by suicide is therefore not among the attempts. The answer of the second brother (frere2_suicide) is filled in 74 of the 178 visits that hold any answer for him (42%), against 90% to 100% for each of the 15 other blocks with at least 30 answers: a gap of the stored data, not an answer. Substances and cardiovascular risk factors. The form lets the rater tick several boxes, and the extraction writes them in one cell ("Alcool,Cannabis"). Each box is delivered as a yes/no variable, and relative_substance is 1 when at least one of the three substances is ticked. "None" ticked together with "do not know" is read as unknown. The type of diabetes is shown only after the box diabetes is ticked (shown_if): 3 of the 811 types are filled although another box is ticked; they are delivered as missing and flagged not_shown. A type is given for 808 of the 1,597 relatives with diabetes ticked. The extraction also holds three 0/1 columns per relative (alcool, cannabis, autre_substance), written by the export on every row from the list of the cell (R82 of EXPORT_REQUESTS.md): alcool and cannabis are 1 only when the list is exactly that word, and autre_substance is 1 for any list that is not empty, "Alcool" or "Cannabis". Over all the visits, autre_substance is 1 on 11,258 cells whose list does not hold "Autre substance" and alcool or cannabis is 0 on 742 cells whose list holds the word (454 and 288). For the mother, autre_substance is 1 on 2,820 visits, 2,721 of them with a list that does not hold it, and alcool misses 55 of the 396 visits whose list holds it. The three columns are not read; the list is. Dates. 1000-01-01 is written in a date that was not typed: the application puts it in every empty date of a form saved from 2025 (DEV-13 in QUESTIONS.md; R19 of EXPORT_REQUESTS.md). The 52 date columns hold 28,582 such cells, by year of the visit: 103 in 2021, 104 in 2022, 104 in 2023, 493 in 2024, 12,164 in 2025 and 15,614 in 2026. This table keeps the first answer of each relative: 11,781 birth dates and 11,984 dates of death are placeholders and are delivered as missing (date_placeholder), 42% of the birth dates and 68% of the dates of death that were given. Six real birth dates typed at a later visit are lost: the reader skips 0000-00-00 but not 1000-01-01, so a placeholder that comes first hides a later real date. From 2022 the dates are almost never typed: the birth date is filled for 70% of the relatives of the patients included until 2020 and for 8% of those of the patients included from 2022, the date of death for 52% and for 1% of the deceased relatives. The form explains it (D95): the birth dates and the dates of death of the parents and the grandparents are no longer shown (they are among its hidden fields), from May 2022 (the last real birth date of a parent or a grandparent comes from a visit of that month), and those of the siblings and the children are asked for the affected ones only. Hard limits: a birth from 1840, a death from 1900. 19 dates are outside (out_of_range): ten have a year below 100 and nine are deaths in the nineteenth century. Three birth dates have a month written 00 with a day (unparsed). Dates that are possible one by one but not together are kept and not flagged: 97 relatives (90 of them grandparents) died before they were born; 25 mothers, 23 fathers and 217 grandparents were born after the patient; 155 relatives of 43 patients were born on or after the first visit of the patient (58 parents or grandparents, 97 siblings or children). Death. Written Y or N for the parents and the grandparents, Oui or Non for the others. 4,303 mothers have an answer (727 have died) and 4,161 fathers (1,199). Until the first extraction of 13 November 2026 the column of the mother (mere_dthfl) held something else, for 165 patients: the export filled it from the anxiety question about the second brother (the two columns were equal on every filled row). The data managers corrected the mapping and ran the extraction again (decision D70 in PROGRESS.md). The mother now follows the father: "no" comes with the placeholder date, "yes" with a date or the placeholder, and the share of "yes" is the same every year (12% to 21% for the mothers, 23% to 37% for the fathers, by year of inclusion from 2011 to 2025). The question was not asked everywhere at the first inclusions: the death of the mother is filled at 1% of the inclusion visits of 2009, 5% of 2010, 12% of 2011, 44% of 2012, 57% of 2013 and 82% of 2014. So relative_deceased is empty for 938 relatives who have a date of death (935 of patients included from 2009 to 2013, 3 of 2014): an empty cell is not "alive". Not delivered: the cause of death, a free text (8,306 cells). It is empty for 19% to 23% of the dead parents and 41% to 47% of the dead grandparents. Years and centres. The report panels of the table relatives show a shift of 1 for degree and relative_deceased. They count rows, and the mix of the rows changes. The grandparents (degree 2) are 28% of the rows of 2009, 34% of 2010, 38% of 2011 and 47% to 54% from 2012: the rows of siblings and children per patient fall from 2.1 and 2.2 (2009, 2011) to 1.4 in 2012, 1.0 in 2013 and 0.5 to 0.7 from 2014 (the old form dated every relative, see Who has a row), and the rows of grandparents rise from 1.5 and 1.6 (2009, 2010) to 2.5 to 2.9 from 2011. relative_deceased is 50% yes over the rows because the grandparents, mostly dead, make half of them; by kinship it stays in the narrow bands given under Death, and the early years are those where the question was not asked. In the table patients, fdr_bipolar (34% yes), fdr_depression (61%), fdr_substance (44%) and gp_depression (38%) show a shift of 1 by centre (gp_depression 26% to 52%): a median near one half. The first three also show a higher share by year in 2009 and 2010 (225 patients of 9 centres, 96 to 115 of them with an answer): fdr_bipolar 53% and 52%, fdr_depression 83% and 71%, fdr_substance 65% and 59%, against 26% to 44%, 51% to 69% and 35% to 53% from 2011. It is the denominator, not a higher prevalence: as a share of all the patients of the year the yes is steady (fdr_bipolar 20% to 23% in each year from 2009 to 2016), while the 0, which needs every first-degree relative to be known, is 19% of the patients of 2009, 21% of 2010, 31% of 2011 and 42% to 44% from 2014 (the same drift for fdr_depression and fdr_substance): the first forms were less completely filled.

sz.section: Antécédents filles, Antécédents fils, Antécédents sœurs, Antécédents frères, Antécédents maternels, Antécédents paternels
sz.notes: One row per patient and relative: the mother, the father and up to five sisters and five brothers, in the table relatives. The columns fdr_ of the table patients sum them up (family_history_per_patient, below). The 22 relative keys are those of the BP schema (26) without the four grandparents: filter degree == 1 to compare with BP. Two questions per relative: the mood or psychotic disorder (none, depression or unipolar disorder, bipolar disorder, schizophrenia) and suicide (none, attempt, completed). "U" and "Ne sais pas" are missing codes. They are asked for the relatives who have something to describe: a parent answered "yes" in family_structure, and the sisters and brothers that the patient counted as affected there. 688 mothers, 659 fathers, 239 sisters and 294 brothers are described. The SZ form has no block for the daughters and the sons (their counts are in family_structure). The extraction has their columns, which hold 13 cells on 7 visits (6 daughters, 1 son): they are delivered as recorded, and the ten keys stay because the invariant reads every raw column. The dictionary gives "yes, no, unknown" as the coding of the sisters, brothers, daughters and sons; the data hold the same lists of disorders as for the parents. The rows of the parents follow the step of the yes in family_structure (open question O33): a mother is described for 41% of the patients included in 2010-2017 and for 29% of those included in 2018-2026, a father for 40% and 29%. The BP schema with the two questions that the SZ form has: no birth and death, no substance, anxiety, dementia or cardiovascular risk, no grandparents and no detail block for the children (decision D57).
sz.difference: two questions per relative (disorder, suicide), no grandparents, and no detail block for the daughters and sons

dr.notes: One row per patient and relative, in the table relatives: the mother, the father, the four grandparents, and one row for the children and one for the brothers and sisters. BP has a row per sister, brother, daughter and son (26 rows per patient at most); here a patient has 8 rows at most (6.5 on average): 3,748 rows of 577 patients. The form is on the inclusion visit only (one patient has it on the screening visit too, none at follow-up): it has no follow-up twin. The children and the siblings are ONE ARBITRARY RELATIVE per group. The row describes one of the affected children and one of the affected siblings: the export keeps one record per patient and visit of the tables of the children and of the siblings (select distinct on (usubjid, visitnum) without an ORDER BY), so which one is left to chance. The patients who counted two or more affected children or siblings (psychiatric or cardiovascular) in family_structure are 13 for the children and 54 for the siblings; a count above 0 with no row: 6 children and 25 siblings. Rows survive a "no" (one sibling row sits under counts of 0 and 0) and nothing checks the count. These rows do not join the rows of BP (sister, brother, daughter, son): compare the questions of the relatives of degree 1, or the columns fdr_ of the patients table. Who has a row. A parent or a grandparent of every patient who has the family form has a row (577 patients): the table of the application holds the boxes of the substances and of the cardiovascular risk factors of these six relatives as NOT NULL, so an unticked box is saved 0 on every saved form (not so for the children and the siblings, see below). So 1,245 of the 3,748 rows hold nothing but boxes at 0 (1,124 grandparents, 120 parents, 1 sibling; 1,252 now that the answers "not known" are missing): a row does not say that the relative has a disorder. A box is flagged derived_doubt where its question is empty (14,335 cells: 2,925 for each of the three substance boxes, 1,390 for each of the four risk boxes). What the form asks, and what is not implemented. The questions on the disorders (mood disorder and its kind, schizophrenic disorder, suicide, substance, anxiety disorder, dementia) are asked when the relative has a psychiatric history (family_structure). The block of the cardiovascular risk factors is in the same section of the form and is asked after a "no" too (293 of the 312 mothers without a psychiatric history answer it), so a gate of the relative on the psychiatric history cannot be written in the schema (it would blank the risk factors with the disorders): not implemented. 1,895 parents and grandparents answered "no psychiatric history": their questions on the disorders are missing, and that means "none", not "not asked". Read family_structure, or the columns fdr_ and gp_ of the patients table (below), which do it. A mood disorder is reported for 536 of the 737 relatives with an answer to that question (the relatives described for a psychiatric history), in the families of 343 patients. Boxes of the children and the siblings. The substances (alcohol, cannabis, another) and the cardiovascular risk factors (diabetes, obesity, hyperlipidaemia, hypertension) are lists of check boxes in the form (form 165). For a parent or a grandparent an unticked box is saved 0; the tables of the children and of the siblings hold them as nullable, and an unticked box is saved empty. The boxes of one list are read together (box_list: substance_kinds and cv_kinds): an empty box beside a ticked box of its list is 0. 241 cells become 0: 39 of the children, 202 of the siblings, none of the parents (their boxes are never empty). A row where every box of the list is empty stays missing. Codes. "Not known" is a missing code: 2 in the yes/no questions (1,621 cells), 0 for the type of diabetes (40), 0 for the kind of mood disorder (79) and 1 for the suicide (98): 1,838 cells, flagged missing_code. The dictionary does not give the two lists, but the form does, and they are the lists of BP. The kind of mood disorder (relative_mood_disorder_kind, asked after a mood disorder "yes") is unipolar (a major depressive episode or unipolar disorder, 416 relatives) or bipolar (41); it is not BP's relative_disorder, which is one list with schizophrenia and "none", but has its labels. The suicide (relative_suicide, the name and labels of BP) is none (557), attempt (85) or completed (55); a relative who died by suicide is not among the attempts. The type of diabetes is read 1 type 1, 2 type 2 and 0 "not known", as for the patient. In the form the type of diabetes of the siblings has the field name of the children (the table of the siblings holds it under ATCDFAMCV_ENFANT_TYPDIAB); the export maps it correctly (7 values for the 11 siblings with diabetes). Per patient: the columns fdr_ and gp_ of the patients table sum up these rows with the counts of family_structure (family_history_per_patient, below), under the names of BP. For a comparison with BP use them, not the rows. Year and centre (report). The anxiety disorder of the relative (asked for the relatives with a psychiatric history, so it carries the centre difference of family_structure) is 9% to 52% by centre (13 centres, chi-square p < 0.0001) and 20% to 60% by year in groups of 20 to 81 relatives, with no trend (p = 0.04). The cardiovascular risk is 10% to 41% by centre (p < 0.0001; the question is answered on 48% to 75% of the relatives of a centre) and moves by 10 points or less between three periods for each parent and grandparent: the yearly shares of the whole table (14% to 43%) come from the mix of relatives. These are differences of centres (rater habit or case mix, the data cannot tell), not steps in time. The second form of the one patient who has the family form twice holds another answer for one box of one relative (the hyperlipidaemia of the father): the first answer is kept, flag patient_value_varies, 1 cell.
dr.difference: the children and the siblings are each one arbitrary affected relative of the group (BP has a row per sister, brother, daughter and son); the disorders are separate yes/no questions, the kind of mood disorder and the suicide are read from the form with the labels of BP; the boxes of the parents and grandparents are 0 on every saved form; the per-patient columns fdr_ and gp_ are computed from the counts of the psychiatric history

family_history.description: Family history, one row per patient and relative in the table relatives: the mood or psychotic disorder of the relative and suicide, and in BP and DR also substances, anxiety, dementia and cardiovascular risk factors (BP: also the birth and the death of the relative). A family is described once, most often at the inclusion visit, and the first answer is kept.
flags: A row does not say that the relative has a disorder (half of the BP rows hold only a birth date or a death), and a relative answered 'no' in family_structure has nothing to describe. To ask 'does a relative have it', use the columns fdr_ and gp_ of the table patients (1, 0 or missing), not the rows.
BP: 'sister 1' is the first of the affected sisters, not the eldest; at most five relatives of a kind are described.
SZ: the parents, the sisters and the brothers only, with two questions (disorder, suicide); filter degree == 1 to compare with BP.

DR: the children and the siblings are one arbitrary relative per group (the export keeps one record), so these rows do not join the BP rows; DR asks the kind of mood disorder (relative_mood_disorder_kind), not the BP list relative_disorder.
relative_suicide is one answer (none, attempt, completed): a relative who died by suicide is not among the attempts.
BP: an empty relative_deceased is not 'alive' (the question was not asked everywhere before 2014), and from 2022 the dates of birth and of death are almost never typed.

common.note: In the table relatives. The relatives asked about are not the same: SZ has 22 of the 26 relatives of BP (no grandparents, no daughters and sons: filter degree == 1), and in DR the children and the siblings are one row for the group, which holds one arbitrary affected relative (request R110), so they do not join to the sisters, brothers, sons and daughters of BP and SZ. The psychiatric disorder of a relative is one list in BP and SZ (relative_disorder) and separate questions in DR (the suicide has the same labels in the three cohorts). BP and DR share the questions on substances, anxiety, dementia and cardiovascular risk. In DR many of these boxes are written 0 where the question was not asked (flag derived_doubt). A missing block under a parent answered no means none: use the per-patient summary.

family_history_per_patient.title: Family history, per patient

bp.section: Enfants, Fratrie, Parents, Grands-parents, Antécédents filles, Antécédents fils, Antécédents sœurs, Antécédents frères, Antécédents maternels, Antécédents paternels
bp.notes: One answer per patient: is there a relative with bipolar disorder, depression, schizophrenia, a completed suicide, a suicide attempt or a substance problem? The columns fdr_ look at the first-degree relatives (mother, father, sisters, brothers, daughters, sons), the columns gp_ at the four grandparents. Computed from the rows of the table relatives and from the counts of family_structure (decision D58 in PROGRESS.md). 1 when at least one relative of the group has it. 0 when every part of the group is answered and nobody has it: each parent is answered yes or no, the number of affected sisters, brothers, daughters and sons is known, and every relative counted there is described with a known answer. Missing otherwise: one "do not know" is enough, unless another relative says yes. Of the 5,733 patients with a family answer (a number, the yes or no of a parent, or a row that holds more than a birth date), fdr_bipolar is 1 for 1,213, 0 for 2,399 and missing for 2,121. For 1,238 of these a part of the family is not answered (a parent answered "unknown", or a count left empty); for 883 a relative counted as affected has no known disorder. The columns gp_ are missing more often: "unknown" is the answer for a fifth to a third of each grandparent. For "a relative is known to have it, or not", compare the column with 1. A parent or a grandparent answered "no" counts as no without any row. The twelve columns were recomputed outside the package from the rows of the table relatives and the counts of family_structure: they come out identical. Depression means the answer "major depressive episode or unipolar disorder", not bipolar disorder. A suicide attempt does not include a completed suicide: the form takes one answer per relative. The shares do not move with the year of inclusion (fdr_bipolar is 1 for 26% to 39% of the known answers every year from 2011 to 2025).

sz.section: Antécédents filles, Antécédents fils, Antécédents sœurs, Antécédents frères, Antécédents maternels, Antécédents paternels
sz.notes: One answer per patient: is there a parent, a sibling or a child with bipolar disorder, depression, schizophrenia, a completed suicide or a suicide attempt? Computed from the rows of the table relatives and from the counts of family_structure, as in FACE BP. 1 when at least one of these relatives has it. 0 when every part of the family is answered and nobody has it. Missing otherwise: one "do not know" is enough, unless another relative says yes. fdr_bipolar is 1 for 110 patients, 0 for 1,340 and missing for 903: no family form 179, a parent unknown or empty 258, a count left empty 144, a counted relative with no known disorder 322. The SZ form asks nothing about substances or about the grandparents, so the columns fdr_substance and gp_ of BP do not exist here.

dr.notes: One answer per patient: is there a relative with bipolar disorder, depression, schizophrenia, a completed suicide, a suicide attempt or a substance problem? Same names, labels and rule as BP. The columns fdr_ look at the first-degree relatives (mother, father, children, siblings), the columns gp_ at the four grandparents. Computed from the rows of the table relatives and from the counts of family_structure: the psychiatric history of each parent and grandparent (1 or 0), and the number of children and of siblings with a psychiatric history. BP counts the affected relatives of its own question, which joins psychiatric and cardiovascular histories: the counts are not the same notion. 1 when at least one relative of the group has it. 0 when every part of the group is answered and nobody has it: a parent or a grandparent with no psychiatric history is a no (the form asks the disorders only after a yes: 1,895 of them), one with a history needs a known answer to the question, and as many children and siblings are described as the patient counted with a psychiatric history. Missing otherwise: one "do not know" is enough, unless another relative says yes. Of the 634 patients, 1 / 0 / missing: fdr_bipolar 37 / 242 / 355, fdr_depression 259 / 137 / 238, fdr_schizophrenia 17 / 342 / 275, fdr_suicide 36 / 323 / 275, fdr_suicide_attempt 64 / 308 / 262, fdr_substance 118 / 286 / 230; gp_bipolar 3 / 212 / 419, gp_depression 74 / 168 / 392, gp_schizophrenia 3 / 253 / 378, gp_suicide 18 / 236 / 380, gp_suicide_attempt 11 / 246 / 377, gp_substance 41 / 238 / 355. Why fdr_bipolar is missing, in this order of precedence: no answer in the family form 76 (57 patients with no form, 19 with a form that holds nothing but boxes at 0); a parent "not known" or left empty 46; the number of children or siblings left empty 65; a counted relative with no known answer to the question 134; more children or siblings counted than described 34. The other five columns fdr_ lose 76 patients with no answer too, then 35 to 50 for a parent, 40 to 65 for a count left empty, 21 to 71 for a counted relative with no known answer (fdr_depression 71, the others 21 to 43) and 16 to 51 for children or siblings counted above the rows. The columns gp_ are missing mostly for a grandparent "not known" or empty (266 to 286): "not known" is the answer for 27% to 40% of the patients who answer about each grandparent. Two limits. (1) The children and the siblings are one arbitrary relative each (see family_history above): a patient who counted two or more of them (13 children, 42 siblings with a psychiatric history) is 1 if the described relative has it, and missing otherwise; a count above 0 with no row (3 children, 18 siblings) is missing. (2) The kind of mood disorder is asked only after a mood disorder "yes". A relative with a psychiatric history and no mood disorder has no kind, and the language cannot count it as a known "no" for bipolar or unipolar disorder (the variables of `where` must all have a value). So fdr_bipolar is missing for 60 patients whose answer is no, fdr_depression for 29, gp_bipolar for 27 and gp_depression for 19; every 1 and 0 delivered is the same under the other reading, which counts the "no mood disorder" of the relative. For "a relative is known to have it, or not", compare the column with 1. Depression means the answer "major depressive episode or unipolar disorder", not bipolar disorder. A suicide attempt does not include a completed suicide: the form takes one answer per relative. Year and centre (report). fdr_substance, fdr_depression and gp_depression have a shift in the report because a 0/1 item moves its median when the share of a group of 20 to 48 patients crosses one half. By centre fdr_substance is 8% to 55% (11 centres, chi-square p = 0.0006; the largest centre is the highest, as for the psychiatric history of the father in family_structure), fdr_depression 44% to 81% (10 centres, p = 0.05) and gp_depression 16% to 60% (6 centres, p = 0.02): differences of centres (rater habit or case mix, the data cannot tell), not steps in time. Compare a share of 1 between centres, or with BP, with care.

family_history_per_patient.description: Family history, one row per patient and relative in the table relatives: the mood or psychotic disorder of the relative and suicide, and in BP and DR also substances, anxiety, dementia and cardiovascular risk factors (BP: also the birth and the death of the relative). A family is described once, most often at the inclusion visit, and the first answer is kept.
flags: A row does not say that the relative has a disorder (half of the BP rows hold only a birth date or a death), and a relative answered 'no' in family_structure has nothing to describe. To ask 'does a relative have it', use the columns fdr_ and gp_ of the table patients (1, 0 or missing), not the rows.
BP: 'sister 1' is the first of the affected sisters, not the eldest; at most five relatives of a kind are described.
SZ: the parents, the sisters and the brothers only, with two questions (disorder, suicide); filter degree == 1 to compare with BP.

DR: the children and the siblings are one arbitrary relative per group (the export keeps one record), so these rows do not join the BP rows; DR asks the kind of mood disorder (relative_mood_disorder_kind), not the BP list relative_disorder.
relative_suicide is one answer (none, attempt, completed): a relative who died by suicide is not among the attempts.
BP: an empty relative_deceased is not 'alive' (the question was not asked everywhere before 2014), and from 2022 the dates of birth and of death are almost never typed.

common.note: In the table patients. A first-degree relative with each disorder, computed the same way in BP, SZ and DR. In DR fdr_bipolar and fdr_depression are missing more often (the kind of mood disorder is asked only after a mood disorder yes), and the children and siblings are one relative per group.

family_structure.title: Family: number of relatives, and how many have a disorder

bp.notes: How many daughters, sons, sisters and brothers the patient has, how many of them have something to describe, and whether each parent and grandparent has. One value per patient, delivered in the table patients (decision D58 in PROGRESS.md). The details of each relative are in family_history. The question. For the mother, the father and each grandparent the form asks whether the relative has "a psychiatric disorder, an abuse of or dependence on a substance, a history of suicide attempt or a cardiovascular risk factor": yes, no or unknown. For the daughters, the sons, the sisters and the brothers it asks how many of them have one of these. A yes is therefore not a psychiatric history: it can be hypertension alone. The names of the variables say "affected" for short. Counts. Numbers go from 0 to 5. The form offers "none", 1 to 5 and "more than 5" for each number of relatives, and "none" and 1 to 5 for the number of affected ones (read in the application in November 2026; decision D95 in PROGRESS.md). "More than 5" is lost by the export, not written 5: the cell is empty (R34 of EXPORT_REQUESTS.md; DM-14 in QUESTIONS.md). So a 5 is exactly five. The trace of the lost answers is a number of relatives that is empty next to a filled number of affected ones: on 55 visits of 49 patients (19 patients for the sisters, 31 for the brothers, 1 for the sons). One of the 19 gives the number of sisters at another visit, so the table patients holds 50 such cases (18 sisters, 31 brothers, 1 son). The number of relatives stays empty: it cannot be told from a count that nobody gave, and nothing is written in its place. The number of affected sisters is asked only when the patient has sisters: with no sister it is 0 (asked_if), and the same for the brothers, the daughters and the sons. It is left empty for 180 patients with daughters, 210 with sons, 252 with sisters and 268 with brothers: unknown. Four rows count more affected relatives than relatives; they are kept as recorded. Unknown. "Unknown" (U) is the answer for 199 mothers, 348 fathers and 1,158 to 1,684 of each grandparent: a missing code. One value per patient. The family is described at the inclusion visit and sometimes again later: 378 patients have these questions answered at two or more visits. The first answer is kept, as for family_history, which has no yearly twin of its own (D84: a later answer is a yearly update; family_history says what changes). 9 to 63 patients per variable give another answer later and get patient_value_varies. Years and centres. The report panels show a shift of 1 for the answers about the mother (60% yes), the father (57%), the maternal grandmother (40%) and the number of daughters (mean 0.49; 35% of the patients have at least one), and of 0.5 for the maternal grandfather (34%). The median of such an item is 0 or 1 and flips when a year or a centre lies on the other side of one half. By centre (14 or 15 centres with 20 answers or more) the mother is 47% to 68% yes, the father 44% to 68%, the maternal grandmother 28% to 51%, the maternal grandfather 24% to 50%, and the mean number of daughters 0.28 to 0.76; by year (18 years) 53% to 69%, 47% to 64%, 30% to 48%, 24% to 43% and 0.37 to 0.62. No step, no mixture of units.

sz.notes: How many daughters, sons, sisters and brothers the patient has, how many of them have something to describe, and whether each parent has. One value per patient, in the table patients. The details of each relative are in family_history. The question, as in FACE BP: a relative "with a psychiatric disorder, an abuse of or dependence on a substance, a history of suicide attempt or a cardiovascular risk factor". A yes is therefore not a psychiatric history. The names of the variables say "affected" for short. The number of affected sisters is asked only when the patient has sisters: with no sister it is 0 (asked_if), and the same for the brothers, the daughters and the sons. "U" is a missing code (133 mothers and 191 fathers of the delivered patients). The affected count is empty while the total is above 0 for 32 patients (sisters), 23 (brothers), 8 (sons) and 5 (daughters): it stays missing, an empty count is not answered. One patient counts more affected brothers than brothers. The export turns the answer ">5" of the form into an empty cell (the same CASE as in BP, R34): the string never appears in SZ and the largest count is 5 (8 patients with 5 sisters, 6 with 5 brothers), so a 5 is exactly five. The lost ">5" show as an empty count beside a filled affected count: 18 patients (11 for the sisters, 10 for the brothers, 3 for both; none for the daughters and the sons). Their count stays missing, it is not 5. The form is asked once: 65 follow-up rows, dated 2011 to 2015 (63 to 2014), hold family answers. The earliest answer of a patient is kept, and a later one that differs is ignored with patient_value_varies (35 flags in this schema, 1 in family_history). There is no shortcut on the family form. The share of parents with a disorder or a risk factor falls with the year of inclusion: mothers 43% of 896 patients included in 2010-2017 and 30% of 1,127 included in 2018-2026 (48% in 2017, 31% in 2018), fathers 43% of 860 and 32% of 1,096. The affected sisters and brothers do not move (12% and 14% of the patients in both periods), nor do the psychiatric columns of family_history_per_patient (fdr_depression 33% and 31%, fdr_bipolar 7% and 8%). The fall is uneven between centres: of the nine centres with 40 patients in each period, six fall by 4 to 41 points (one goes from 67% to 26%), one is flat and two rise; over the whole period the share of mothers goes from 29% to 52% by centre. BP shows no such step. The cause is not known (open question O33). The BP schema without the four grandparents, which the SZ form does not ask about. About 2,200 patients answer (decision D57).
sz.difference: no grandparents in the SZ form

dr.notes: One value per patient, in the table patients: for the mother, the father and each grandparent, whether the relative has a history of psychiatric illness (1 yes, 0 no, 2 "not known": 808 cells, missing_code); whether the patient has children and brothers or sisters, how many of them have such a history, and how many have cardiovascular risk factors. Asked once, at the inclusion visit, with no follow-up twin: the family form was saved for 577 patients (91% of 634; 88% to 96% per period of inclusion from 2013, 6 of 6 before), 553 of whom answered the question on the mother (532 yes or no, 21 not known), 558 at least one question of this schema. 19 forms hold only the boxes of family_history, set to 0. Not the BP question. BP asks one question per relative, "a psychiatric disorder, a substance, a suicide attempt or a cardiovascular risk factor". Here the psychiatric history and the cardiovascular risk factors are two questions, so the variables have other names (mother_psychiatric_history, where BP has mother_affected). The mother has a psychiatric history for 220 of 532 patients, the father for 153 of 523. The numbers about the children and the siblings are 0 when the patient has none (asked_if). The four dates of birth of the form are empty in the extraction (ignored.yaml). The counts. Of the 371 patients who have children, the number with a psychiatric history is left empty for 26 (82 have at least one), the number with cardiovascular risk factors for 36 (12 have at least one). Of the 480 who have brothers or sisters, the number of them is left empty for 57, the number with a psychiatric history for 44 (181 have at least one) and the number with cardiovascular risk factors for 64 (75 have at least one); 6 of them answer "yes" and count 0 brothers and sisters. Where both are given, no count of affected relatives is above the number of brothers and sisters. These counts are the ones of the per-patient columns fdr_ and gp_ of family_history: an empty count leaves them missing, and the row of the children or of the siblings in family_history is one arbitrary affected relative of the group. Year and centre (report). The psychiatric history of the mother and of the father, and the counts of the siblings, have a shift in the report because a yes/no item or a small count moves its median when the share of a group of 20 to 60 patients crosses one half. By year the share of mothers with a history is 25% to 62% with no trend (chi-square p = 0.03) and that of fathers 18% to 43% (p = 0.21); the number of brothers and sisters has a median of 1 to 2 and a mean of 1.5 to 3.1 by year, and the number with a psychiatric history a mean of 0.4 to 0.7. By centre the share of mothers is 23% to 61% (p = 0.19, chance); one centre, the largest, has a history for 54% of the fathers in each of three periods (50%, 50%, 57%) against 17% to 33% in the 13 others (p = 0.02, 14 centres): a difference of centres (rater habit or case mix, the data cannot tell), not a step in time. Use the centre when comparing the share of 1.
dr.difference: the psychiatric history and the cardiovascular risk factors are two questions (BP asks one question per relative); children and siblings are counted as groups, with the number affected by each of the two questions

family_structure.description: Family structure, one value per patient in the table patients: how many daughters, sons, sisters and brothers the patient has, how many of them are 'affected', and whether each parent (and each grandparent in BP and DR) is. Asked once, most often at inclusion; the first answer is kept.
flags: BP and SZ: 'affected' means a psychiatric disorder, an abuse of or dependence on a substance, a suicide attempt or a cardiovascular risk factor. A yes is therefore not a psychiatric history: it can be hypertension alone.
DR asks the psychiatric history and the cardiovascular risk factors as two questions, under other names (mother_psychiatric_history, n_siblings_cardiovascular_risk): not the BP and SZ variables.
BP and SZ: the answer 'more than 5' relatives is lost by the export (empty cell). A 5 is exactly five, and an empty number beside a filled number of affected relatives may be 'more than 5'.
SZ: the share of parents answered yes falls with the year of inclusion (mothers 43% in 2010-2017, 30% in 2018-2026); the cause is not known.

common.note: In the table patients. The numbers of brothers, sisters, sons and daughters and how many are affected are the same in BP and SZ. 'Affected' also covers a substance use disorder and a cardiovascular risk factor: a yes is not a psychiatric history. DR asks other questions (a psychiatric history of each parent, children and siblings counted as groups) under names of its own.

gynaecological_history_fu.title: Medical history: pregnancies, menopause and gynaecological diseases (yearly follow-up visits)

bp.notes: Numbers of pregnancies, children born alive, miscarriages, voluntary terminations and terminations for a medical reason; menopause, its date and its hormone therapy; a gynaecological disease other than a cancer, named in a free text delivered as written. Yes/no answers are delivered as 1 and 0; "unknown" (U, "Ne sais pas") is a missing code. Numbers. "Aucune" and "Aucun(e)" are an answer: 0. The four other numbers are 0 when the number of pregnancies is 0 (asked_if): the form has no gate on them, so this zero is by logic and a typed number stays (decision D122 in PROGRESS.md). One answer is ">15", which is not a number: unparsed. Of the women who answer, 1,349 of 3,450 have had no pregnancy at inclusion. The births, miscarriages and terminations add up to more than the pregnancies on 154 inclusion rows and 55 yearly rows where the five numbers are typed: they stay as recorded. Menopause. The hormone therapy and its start date hang on the menopause: they are typed after a "yes" only (never after a "no": 0 of 2,766 inclusion rows and 0 of 888 yearly rows), and the therapy is missing otherwise, not 0 (no asked_if: it is a detail of the menopause, not a count or a box). The therapy is answered for 570 of the 670 menopause "yes" at inclusion and 190 of 253 at the yearly visits. The start date hangs on the menopause, not on the hormone answer: it is empty under a menopause "yes" for 84% of the inclusion rows and 90% of the yearly rows, hormone therapy or not. Two forms in the same columns (decision D59 in PROGRESS.md). The section is filled at the inclusion visit and at the yearly visits, and delivered as separate columns ending in _v0 and _fu, like the other sections of the medical history; visit_form says which form a visit used. Here the two mostly agree: the number of pregnancies given at a yearly visit is the one of the inclusion visit for 582 of 708 women, higher for 70 and lower for 56, and a menopause is almost never taken back (6 of 134). Only the gynaecological disease behaves like the diseases of the other sections: 62 of the 105 "yes" answered again are then "no" (the yearly form is the inclusion form again, decision D84). The six-monthly visits (3,352 visits of the follow-up version, 8,334 of its 11,686 being yearly) and the screening visits never hold a cell of this section. The question "is there a change since the last visit?" is shown at the yearly visit only and is not exported (rad_pas_dechangement, DM-10): an empty yearly section may mean "no change". This section is not emptied in 2022 like the others, because it has no "no for all" shortcut (decision D83 in PROGRESS.md): it is answered at 87% of the inclusion visits of women until 2021 and at 80% from 2022, with the same share of "yes" among the answers (12.4% and 12.5%). The yearly visits answer it at 28% of the visits of women until 2021 and at 15% from 2022. Men. The form shows the section to everyone: 203 of the 2,389 inclusion rows of men and 60 of their 3,095 yearly rows hold a cell of it, almost always with "none" and "no"; 3 have a pregnancy and 5 a menopause at inclusion. These answers are kept as recorded: filter on the sex of the patient. Dates. 1000-01-01 is written in a date that was not typed, and in every empty date of a form saved from 2025 (in the nine sections together, 64% of the inclusion visits and 34% of the yearly visits dated 2025 or later hold one; at inclusion 0% to 3% of the visits up to 2024Q4, 28% in 2025Q1, 70% in 2025Q4, 94% in 2026Q3): date_placeholder. Hard limits: 1900 to 2026. Four dates are on the day of the visit and none is after it. Years and centres. The report panels show a shift of 0.5 for the numbers of pregnancies and of live births. The interquartile range is 2 and the median is 1 pregnancy and 0 live births at inclusion (1 and 1 at the yearly visits); the median of a year or of a centre is one more or one less: a difference of parity between the populations, no step.

sz.notes: Shown to everyone, answered mostly by the women: 668 visits of women (569 at inclusion, 99 at follow-up) and 141 of men (127 at inclusion, 14 at follow-up). The SZ form has three of the nine BP questions. Yes/no answers are delivered as 1 and 0; "U" is a missing code. "Treated" and the other details are asked after a yes and are missing otherwise. Two forms in the same columns, as in FACE BP (BP decisions D59 and D84; here decisions D20 and D56 in PROGRESS.md). The same questions are asked at the inclusion visit and at the yearly follow-up visits (every follow-up visit of the extraction is a yearly one; the 1,675 screening records hold no cell of the section). At inclusion they are about the whole life. At the yearly visits a disease answered yes at inclusion is most often answered no (39 of 47 follow-up answers for a head injury, 43 of 54 for acne). The yearly form is the inclusion form again, with no period in the wording of its questions, after one more question that the extraction does not hold: "Pas de changement de l'histoire somatique depuis la dernière visite?" (rad_pas_dechangement, shown at the yearly visit only; export request R78). An empty follow-up section may therefore mean "no change". A yearly answer is an update given at that visit: neither a history of the whole life nor strictly an answer about the time since the last visit. The two are delivered as separate columns ending in _v0 and _fu; visit_form says which form a visit used. 127 of the 1,706 inclusion visits of men hold answers (114 of the 141 visits of men say 0 pregnancies, 116 no menopause), against 569 of the 647 of women (88%): filter on the sex. The section is answered at 18% to 30% of the inclusion visits until 2020 and at 29% to 48% since 2021 (27% of the cohort are women): the rise comes from more men answering (47 of 1,176 inclusion visits of men until 2020, 80 of 530 since), the women stay at 88% and 87%. The hormonal treatment is asked of every woman, whether or not in menopause, as in BP and DR (no asked_if on it). It is "no" on all 39 answers (BP 98 yes of 783, DR 36 of 412), and empty on 13 of the 52 menopause "yes" (open question O32). At follow-up the section is held by 113 of the 2,588 yearly visits (2% to 10% of the yearly visits of a year from 2012); the other yearly visits leave it empty, which may mean "no change" (see the two forms above). The SZ form is shorter than the BP one: one question "treated" per disease, and no date of onset and no "controlled". The names are those of BP where the question is the same.
sz.difference: the shorter SZ history form

dr.notes: The BP schema with the columns and the codes of this extraction, at the visits of 2 and 4 years: 89 visits. The questions and what is specific to this cohort are described in gynaecological_history_v0.yaml. Two forms in the same columns, as in BP: the inclusion visit (form 164 of the application) and the visits of 2 and 4 years (form 191), where the same questions are asked again. visit_form says which form a visit uses, and each form has its own schema and its own variables (_v0 and _fu). A follow-up answer is a yearly update (BP D84): an answer given at that visit on the inclusion form asked again, with no period in the wording of the questions. It is neither a history of the whole life nor strictly an answer about the time since the last visit, and it is never mixed with the inclusion answers. Form 191 has no question "is there a change since the last visit?" (BP and SZ have one, which the extraction does not hold): the whole block is asked again. The block is filled at 90 of 146 visits of 2 years, 36 of 69 visits of 4 years, 3 of 4 of 5 years, 1 of 3 of 3 years and 1 of 298 six-monthly visits, and at none of the 253 visits of 1 year and the 150 of 18 months. Form 191 is form 164 without the perinatal block and with no period wording. Answers are numbers here (1 yes, 0 no), where BP has words. The forms offer only Oui and Non: no cell holds "not known" and none is read. "Treated" and "controlled" are in columns named _tr_mhdecod and _eq_mhdecod. Dates are whole dates. Year (report). Among the 89 answers a single year (2017) has 20 answers or more: the year shift of menopause_fu compares that one group with the whole and shows no step. The share of menopause follows the age of the women (see gynaecological_history_v0.yaml).
dr.difference: the answers are numbers; the section is hidden for men and holds no answer for them (BP holds a cell for 203 of its 2,389 men's inclusion rows); the counts are typed numbers; the hormonal treatment is asked whether or not in menopause (as in BP, no gate on the menopause)

gynaecological_history_fu.description: Medical history at the yearly follow-up visits: numbers of pregnancies, live births, miscarriages and terminations, menopause, its date and its hormone therapy, and a gynaecological disease other than a cancer (SZ: number of pregnancies, menopause and hormone therapy only). The inclusion form asked again, as an update given at that visit.
gynaecological_history_fu.period: an update given at the yearly visit (neither the whole life nor strictly the time since the last visit)
flags: A follow-up answer is the inclusion form asked again, with no period in its wording: a disease answered yes at inclusion is often answered no. Do not stack the _fu answers with the _v0 answers.

BP and SZ: the yearly form starts with 'is there a change since the last visit?', which is not exported, so an empty yearly section may mean 'no change'. DR has no such question and asks the block at the visits of 2 and 4 years.
BP and SZ show the section to everyone: some men have answers (almost always 'none' and 'no'). Filter on the sex of the patient. In DR the section is hidden for men.
The numbers of pregnancies and the menopause mostly agree between the inclusion and the yearly answers; only the gynaecological disease behaves like the diseases of the other sections.
This section has no 'no for all' shortcut and is not emptied in 2022.
Yes is 1 and no is 0; 'unknown' is a missing code. The details (date of onset, treated, controlled) are asked only after a yes and are missing otherwise (SZ asks 'treated' only).

common.note: The follow-up form is the inclusion form asked again at the yearly visit: its questions carry no period, and an answer is a yearly update, neither the whole life nor strictly the time since the last visit (a yes of the inclusion is often a no a year later). It is delivered in columns of its own (_fu) and is not to be added to the inclusion answers. The six-monthly and the screening visits hold no cell of these sections, and an empty yearly section may mean "no change since the last visit" (the question is not exported). The same reserves as at inclusion apply.

It is neither a history of the whole life nor strictly an answer about the time since the last visit, and it is never mixed with the inclusion answers. Form 191 has no question "is there a change since the last visit?" (BP and SZ have one, which the extraction does not hold): the whole block is asked again. The block is filled at 90 of 146 visits of 2 years, 36 of 69 visits of 4 years, 3 of 4 of 5 years, 1 of 3 of 3 years and 1 of 298 six-monthly visits, and at none of the 253 visits of 1 year and the 150 of 18 months. Form 191 is form 164 without the perinatal block and with no period wording. Answers are numbers here (1 yes, 0 no; 2 is "Ne sais pas" on the questions that offer it: the question on a nephropathy linked to lithium; no cell holds a 2), where BP has words. "Treated" and "controlled" are in columns named _tr_mhdecod and _eq_mhdecod. Dates are whole dates. The question on a nephropathy linked to a past or current treatment names lithium in the form: nephropathy_lithium (BP: the same name). The causes of a urinary retention are three boxes that the form sets to 0 on every saved form: flagged derived_doubt where the question on the retention is empty. In the form they hang on "started under a treatment", itself under the retention (a chain of two levels, see the one-level cascade in decision D36); the schema keeps the retention as the gate of the doubt.

aim20.title: Affect Intensity Measure, 20 items (AIM-20)

bp.notes: AIM-40 and AIM-20 are two instruments. The 20-item AIM-20 replaced the 40-item AIM between January 2021 and January 2023, depending on the centre (October 2021 to May 2022 in the large ones) (answer of the data managers in November 2026, decision D66 in PROGRESS.md). Its 20 questions are 20 of the 40, and the extraction stores both in the same columns. This schema reads those columns on the visits where the 20-item questionnaire was filled. Nothing in the AIM columns says which form a visit used; it is read from the ALS and the BIS of the same visit: "aim20" when the visit holds ALS or BIS answers and nothing that only the long questionnaires have. aim40.yaml reads the other visits and explains the rule and its limit. Both files carry the same version block. Filled at the inclusion visit (1,403 of 1,442 visits; 39 follow-up visits also hold one). Each item is 1 (never) to 6 (always). Item names. The EMR kept the numbers that the questions have in the 40-item questionnaire: aim20_02 is the question numbered 2 there. On the 20-item form the questions are numbered 1 to 20 in the rising order of these numbers (2, 7, 9 ... 40): the rank of an item is its number on the form (read in the application in November 2026; decision D97 in PROGRESS.md). Score. The mean of the 20 items (1 to 6), six of them reversed (7 - value): 12, 24, 29, 33, 37 and 40. The stored score (aim_) is exactly this mean in all 6,084 rows where both exist (the export's score step writes it, D120). Before 2021. The data managers found no visit with only the reduced questionnaires before 2021, and advise not to deliver the questionnaires of a visit that looks like one (decision D71 in PROGRESS.md). The version block says so (since): a visit dated before 2021 that would be read here has no form, gets version_unknown, and its answers are not delivered. 8 visits, dated 2017 to 2020, each with its 20 answers; als18.yaml says what they look like.

aim40.title: Affect Intensity Measure, 40 items (AIM-40)

bp.notes: AIM-40 and AIM-20 are two instruments. The 40-item AIM was filled until 2021 (2022 in two centres); the 20-item AIM-20 replaced it (answer of the data managers in November 2026, decision D66 in PROGRESS.md). The 20 questions of the AIM-20 are 20 of the 40, and the extraction stores both in the same columns. The columns are therefore split by form: this schema reads the visits where the 40-item questionnaire was filled, aim20.yaml reads the others. Both files carry the same version block. Which form a visit used. Nothing in the AIM columns says it, and no field of the source database records it. The form is read from the other self-questionnaires of the same visit, with the rule of the WURS (wurs61.yaml): "aim40" when the visit holds something that only the long questionnaires have, a score of the 54-item ALS (als58 or als60) or one of the 22 items that only the 34-item BIS-10 has; "aim20" when it holds ALS or BIS answers and none of those. This rests on the AIM having changed with the ALS and the BIS in each centre, which the AIM columns cannot confirm. A visit with an AIM and neither an ALS nor a BIS (4 visits) has no form: version_unknown, and its answers are not delivered. A visit dated before 2021 is never read as the 20-item form (since, in the version block): aim20.yaml says why. Filled once, at the inclusion visit. Each item is 1 (never) to 6 (always). Bridge to the AIM-20: aim40_score20 is the score of the AIM-20, computed from the 20 items both forms have: their mean (1 to 6), six of them reversed (7 - value): 12, 24, 29, 33, 37 and 40. als18.title: Affective Lability Scale, 18 items (ALS-18)

bp.notes: ALS-54 and ALS-18 are two instruments. The 18-item ALS-18 replaced the 54-item ALS (confirmed by the developers of the EMR, decision D47 in PROGRESS.md). Its 18 questions are 18 of the 54, and the extraction stores both in the same columns. This schema reads those columns on the visits where the 18-item questionnaire was filled: the visits that hold ALS answers and nothing that only the long questionnaires have (no score of the 54-item ALS, no item that only the BIS-10 has). als54.yaml reads the other visits and explains the rule. Both files carry the same version block. Filled once, at the inclusion visit, from September 2021 to May 2022 depending on the centre; 12 visits dated January to June 2021 also hold an ALS-18 (two centres opened with the reduced forms, one ran both). Each item is 0 (not at all like me) to 3 (very much like me). Item names. The EMR kept the numbers that the questions have in the 54-item questionnaire: als18_05 is the question numbered 5 there. On the 18-item form the questions are numbered 1 to 18 in the rising order of these numbers (5, 8, 12 ... 46): the rank of an item is its number on the form (read in the application in November 2026; decision D97 in PROGRESS.md). The form prints "19" for the last one. Scores (means, 0 to 3): anxiety-depression (items 5, 12, 16, 17, 20), depression-elation (8, 25, 34, 36, 42, 43, 45, 46), anger (14, 21, 23, 33, 41) and the total. The extraction stores them under the names of scales of the long form (als55 "Depression", als56 "Elation", als59 "Anger", als_ "Total"), but they are exactly the means of these items in every row. The data managers confirmed the three keys in November 2026 (decision D67 in PROGRESS.md): the eight items of als56 come from the depression, elation and bipolar scales of the long form, so it is a depression-elation score and the label "Elation" does not fit; "Anger" is right. als55 is written by the score step of their pipeline: the mean of items 5, 12, 16, 17 and 20 on every visit where the five are answered, in the long and in the reduced form alike (decision D72). It is the anxiety-depression score of the 18 items under the label "Depression". Not read. On these visits als57 holds the anxiety-depression score a second time (the same value as als55 on 94% of the visits, empty on 5%, different on 0.8%), as the data managers confirmed. On the visits of the 54-item form the column holds another score, read by als54.yaml. Before 2021. The data managers found no visit with only the 18 items before 2021, and advise not to deliver the questionnaires of a visit that looks like one (decision D71 in PROGRESS.md). The version block says so (since): a visit dated before 2021 that would be read here has no form, gets version_unknown, and its answers are not delivered. 8 visits, dated 2017 to 2020. They read them as long questionnaires with unanswered items. The extraction suggests something else: seven of the eight hold the 18 answers, and their BIS holds none of the 22 long items (five of the eight hold the twelve BIS-12 items); five of the eight are from one centre, in two quarters of 2019, which looks like reduced questionnaires typed under an early visit date. Either way the form or the date is wrong.

als54.title: Affective Lability Scale, 54 items (ALS-54)

bp.notes: ALS-54 and ALS-18 are two instruments. The 54-item ALS was filled until 2021; the 18-item ALS-18 replaced it (confirmed by the developers of the EMR, decision D47 in PROGRESS.md). The 18 questions of the ALS-18 are 18 of the 54, and the extraction stores both in the same columns. The columns are therefore split by form: this schema reads the visits where the 54-item questionnaire was filled, als18.yaml reads the others. Both files carry the same version block. Which form a visit used. No column says it. A visit is "als54" when it holds something that only the long questionnaires have: a score of the 54-item ALS (als58 or als60), or one of the 22 items that only the 34-item BIS-10 has. The BIS is used because the reduced questionnaires replaced the long ones together: of the 6,107 visits that have both an ALS and a BIS, 99.2% have the two in the same generation. The 45 others have ALS answers, a BIS-10 and no score of the 54-item ALS: questionnaires with unanswered items, for which the EMR computed no long score. Each centre changed at its own date, between September 2021 and May 2022. A visit dated before 2021 is never read as the 18-item form (since, in the version block): als18.yaml says why. Filled once, at the inclusion visit. Each item is 0 (not at all like me) to 3 (very much like me). What the extraction holds. Only the 18 items that the ALS-18 also has, out of 54; the 36 others were not exported. als54_05 is item 5 of the 54-item questionnaire. The data managers confirmed in November 2026 (decision D67 in PROGRESS.md) that the patients filled the 54 items until 2021 (2022 in two centres), that the 36 other items are still in the source database, and that no field records the form of a visit. Scores of the 54-item form: anxiety-depression (als57), anxiety (als58) and bipolar (als60). Their items are not in the extraction, so they cannot be checked and are delivered as stored. The data managers recomputed als57 from the source: on these visits it is the mean of eight items of the long form (3, 10, 16, 17, 22, 37, 38 and 49). Bridge to the ALS-18: the four scores of the ALS-18, computed from the 18 items both forms have (means, 0 to 3): anxiety-depression (items 5, 12, 16, 17, 20), depression-elation (8, 25, 34, 36, 42, 43, 45, 46), anger (14, 21, 23, 33, 41) and the total. The extraction stores them under the names of scales of the long form (als55 "Depression", als56 "Elation", als59 "Anger", als_ "Total"), but they are exactly the means of these items in every row: the score step of the data managers' pipeline writes them on every visit where the items are answered, whatever the form (decision D72). Whether an answer given inside a 54-item questionnaire can be compared with the same question asked in an 18-item one is a scientific choice; the two are delivered as separate columns (als54_total18 here, als18_total there) so that nobody mixes them by accident. From July 2021 to June 2022, when both forms were in use, the two totals have the same mean (1.44 and 1.39; different centres; inside a centre, 12 months either side of its switch, the difference is -0.01, SE 0.05).

aq12.title: Short aggression questionnaire (12 items, four sub-scores)

bp.notes: Named AQ12 by the EMR; titled here by its content, a short aggression questionnaire. Its four sub-scores are the four factors of the Buss-Perry Aggression Questionnaire (physical aggression, verbal aggression, anger, hostility). A published 12-item short form with these four factors of three items each exists (Bryant and Smith 2001; French version rated 1 to 6, Genoud and Zimmermann 2009, as cited by later papers); that these twelve items are that form, and the published item numbers of each sub-score, could not be confirmed (literature check 2026-11-21). It is not the Autism-Spectrum Quotient: in the ASP extraction the variable aq12 is item 12 of that scale, another instrument, and the two are not joined. In the extraction from 2021, filled at the inclusion visit; it took the place of the BDHI. The dictionary lists it among the questionnaires reduced in 2021, but the extraction holds no longer form. Twelve items, each 1 (not at all like me) to 6 (completely like me). Four sub-scores of three items each (3 to 18): physical aggression (items 1, 5, 9), verbal aggression (2, 6, 10), anger (3, 7, 11) and hostility (4, 8, 12). The stored sub-scores equal these sums on all but one visit of 1,336 (physical +2, verbal +1). The extraction stores no total; the sum of the twelve items is added here (12 to 72).

asrs.title: Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale (ASRS v1.1, 18 items), last 6 months

bp.notes: Two visits date from 2018 and 2020, 28 from 2021, the rest from 2022; filled at the inclusion visit (1,265 of 1,325 visits). Eighteen items, each 0 (never) to 4 (very often), about the last 6 months (the instruction of the form). The screening result is computed here from part A, the first six items: an item counts when it is 2 or more (items 1 to 3) or 3 or more (items 4 to 6), and the result is positive (1) from four items on, negative (0) below. It exists on every visit that has the six items (1,320). The stored result (asrs_) is the check and is not delivered, because the script of the application tests the wrong variable for an unanswered item (it tests the field and not the count, autoq_asrs.js, lines 20 to 60): an incomplete part A gives "negative", and the result stays empty when the score button is never clicked. Against the stored result, the rule gives 92 results where it was empty (the six items answered, the button not clicked), 2 positive results where it was negative (count of 4 or 5), and no result on 6 visits where it was negative with an incomplete part A (score_not_recomputed): 100 cells in all. Elsewhere the two agree on all of 1,226 visits. The name asrs_screen now holds 1 or 0, not a category. The same part A is in the ASP schema. The extraction stores no total. The sum of the eighteen items is added here (0 to 72).

asp.notes: Eighteen items from 0 to 4 about the past six months, at the inclusion visit: 586 visits, from 2019 to 2026, and 4 follow-up visits (590 in all). It belongs to the new set of forms. It is filled by adults only. The children have the ADHD rating scale. Same instrument as in FACE BP, in columns named asrs1 to asrs18. The column of the stored total (asrs_scoretot) is empty on every row (ignored.yaml), and the form (343) has no field for the screening result that FACE BP stores: nothing is stored to check here, so the total and the screen are computed. **The screen of part A is computed.** The part A of the published form is the items 1 to 6; the screen is positive when 4 or more of them are past their threshold (items 1 to 3 at "sometimes" or more, items 4 to 6 at "often" or more). `asrs_parta` counts the items past the threshold (0 to 6) and `asrs_screen` is 1 when the count is 4 or more, 0 otherwise, as in FACE BP, where the stored result is the check (the script of the BP application tests the wrong variable for a missing answer, so its stored result is empty or wrong on some visits). The screen is delivered on 579 visits. It is numeric (0 and 1) in both cohorts. **Year and centre.** 15 of the 21 variables reach 0.5 or more (10 by year, 13 by centre): the eighteen items are on a 0 to 4 scale (one level is 1.0 or more of the interquartile range). The total stands at 0.18 by year and 0.30 by centre, part A (a count of 0 to 6) at 0.00 and 0.50, and the screen (0 or 1) at 0.00 by year and 1.00 by centre, a median that flips between 0 and 1 (positive for 48% of the visits of centre D and 63% to 74% in B, C, E and H). Centre D reads lower on every score (median total 35 against 40 to 45): a difference of 0.30 of the interquartile range with no known cause (the case mix or the rater). The six years 2021 to 2026 differ by 0.18 or less (median 38 to 43).

bdhi.title: Buss-Durkee Hostility Inventory (BDHI, 75 items)

bp.notes: Filled once, at the inclusion visit, until 2022; the short aggression questionnaire (aq12.yaml) took its place. Seventy-five true/false statements. Coding. The extraction stores the items already keyed to hostility: 1 is the hostile answer, whether that answer is "true" or "false" (the dictionary lists the fifteen statements for which it is "false"; the script of the form keys them the same way). The items are delivered as asked, 1 true and 0 false: the fifteen statements for which false is the hostile answer (items 1, 10, 17, 21, 27, 34, 39, 50, 55, 63, 66, 67, 71, 72 and 74) are read back with a code table, and the sub-scores reverse them (1 minus the value). A sub-score is the same number as the stored one. Eight sub-scores: assault (10 items), indirect hostility (9), irritability (11), negativism (5), resentment (8), suspicion (10), verbal hostility (13) and guilt (9). Two components: attitudinal (resentment and suspicion) and motor (assault, indirect hostility, irritability and verbal hostility). The item lists were read from the data: each stored sub-score and the attitudinal component equal ours in every row where both exist (4,506 to 4,527 rows; 4,474 for the component); the motor component differs on 1 of 4,452 rows. The extraction stores no total. The usual one is added here: the seven hostility sub-scores, guilt left out (66 items).

bdhi.description: Buss-Durkee Hostility Inventory. Seventy-five true/false statements answered by the patient once, at the inclusion visit, until 2022. Eight sub-scores, two components and a total.
bdhi.reference: Buss AH, Durkee A. An inventory for assessing different kinds of hostility. J Consult Psychol 1957;21:343-349

The two components follow the literature notes (attitudinal = resentment + suspicion, motor = assault + indirect + verbal + irritability, Confirmed, direct: Etain 2025). Some papers also put guilt in the attitudinal score; here it is not.
