bis10.title: Barratt Impulsiveness Scale, BIS-10 (34 items)

bp.notes: BIS-10 and BIS-12 are two instruments. An error in the EMR stored the answers of the 12-item BIS-12 (used from 2021 on) in twelve of the columns of the 34-item BIS-10 (used from 2009 to 2022). The columns are therefore split by form: this schema reads the visits where the 34-item form was used, bis12.yaml reads the visits where the 12-item form was used. Both files carry the same version block. There is no column saying which form was used: a visit is "bis10" when at least one of the 22 items that only the 34-item form has is filled. A visit dated before 2021 is never read as the 12-item form (since, in the version block): bis12.yaml says why. The 34-item form fits the BIS-10 (34 items on a 4-point scale: Barratt 1985, read only as cited by others), whose French translation is Baylé et al. 2000 (Can J Psychiatry 45:156-165). That the form is this French version, and its published item keys, reversed items and coding, could not be confirmed: only the abstract of Baylé 2000 was read (literature check 2026-11-21). The column bis11 of the extraction is a third thing: the export's own set of 12 items, not the BIS-11 (bis10_score11). Items are coded 1 to 4. Reversed items, from the dictionary: 1, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12, 13, 15, 21, 33, 34. The stored scores were recovered exactly from the items on every complete row. Three things follow. 1. The extraction reverses an item as 6 - value. With a 1 to 4 scale the usual rule is 5 - value, which is what this schema does. Each stored score is therefore higher than ours by one point per reversed item; that is the compare_offset of each score. The rule kept is 5 - value (decision D92 in PROGRESS.md): it is the usual one, and the script of the application itself reverses 4, 3, 2, 1 (read in November 2026). The 6 - value is in the score step of the data managers, which writes these columns. 2. The dictionary formula for the planning subscale is incomplete. The stored score also includes items 14, 18 and 31 (not reversed). 3. The stored behavioural and general scores (bis1039, bis1040) are rounded to one decimal. Comparing them would flag most rows for a rounding difference: they are compared with a tolerance of 0.051 (the general score with an offset of 0.5). The export also writes a score when an item is missing, as the sum of the answers present (27 of 27 checked): 264 score_not_recomputed over the nine scores, on 63 visits, and 4 stored motor sums (7 to 10) fall under the declared range. The last four scores use only the 12 items that the BIS-12 also has. They are the only bridge between the two instruments. Whether an answer given inside a 34-item questionnaire can be compared with the same item asked in a 12-item one is a scientific choice; the two are delivered as separate columns (bis10_sum12 here, bis12_total there) so that nobody mixes them by accident.

dr.notes: The BP scale, with eleven items turned back to the answer as asked. Only the 34-item BIS-10 is in this extraction: no visit holds the twelve items of the BIS-12 alone, so there is no bis12.yaml here. The version block is the one BP uses, because the two cohorts share the column names; every BIS visit is read as "bis10" (549 visits). Filled at inclusion and at the visits of 2 and 4 years. Items are coded 1 to 4. Eleven items are stored reversed here. The key reverses items 1, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12, 13, 15, 21, 33 and 34 (see the notes of the BP schema; the planning sub-scale also holds items 14, 18 and 31). In BP these items are stored as asked: the seven that work best (1, 8, 9, 10, 12, 13, 21) fall when the 23 other items rise (r = -0.44 between the two sums). In this extraction they rise with them (r = +0.28; positive in each of the 11 centres that have twenty visits or more, 0.08 to 0.55, in every period and at every kind of visit). The 34 values as stored hold together better (Cronbach's alpha 0.76) than after the reversal of the key (0.65); BP shows the opposite (0.62 and 0.81). The mean of item 33 is 3.4 here against 1.9 in BP. So the form of this cohort stores the eleven items already reversed. They are read back to the answer as asked (5 - value, written as codes), so that bis1001 to bis1034 mean the same in the two cohorts and the BP key applies. After this the item means of the two cohorts agree (r = 0.84 over the 34 items, 0.51 before). Stored scores: wrong, not delivered. The form keys the eleven items 4, 3, 2, 1 (form 215; the form 138 before it keys items 33 and 34 as 4, 2, 3, 1: A82, M75), so the stored items are already reversed. The application adds the items as they are stored, which is right for items stored reversed (the sub-scores bis1035 to bis1037, below). The export then reverses the eleven items a second time (6 - value, as it does in BP: the score definition of the export names this cohort's table together with BP's) and writes its own scores, which put them back in the wrong direction. The form's own keys and script confirm that it stores the items already turned (question M20, answered). Each stored score (bis10_imp_mot, bis10_imp_att, bis10_imp_pla, bis10_score_total, bis11, bis10, bis1038) is reproduced exactly by adding the items with none reversed, plus the BP offset of one point per reversed item: these are the twin scores named _as_stored, read to check the stored values and not delivered (no mismatch on the 530 to 547 visits where a twin exists). The delivered scores use the key (open question O17, request R146). A stored score is also computed when an item is missing (5 to 19 visits); ours needs every item. The column bis11 is the export's sum of 12 items (1, 6, 8, 9, 12, 14, 17, 19, 20, 22, 24, 25), not the score of a BIS-11. Three more columns, bis1035 to bis1037, hold the motor, attention and planning sub-scores of the application: plain sums of the items as stored. They are read as hidden checks (bis10_motor_app, bis10_attention_app, bis10_planning_app) and each is compared with our sub-score of the same name: they are equal on 530 visits of 530 for each of the three (no mismatch). So the application's sub-scores agree with ours and the export's agree with neither. Two application sums (one motor and one planning, on two visits) are partial, with a value of 1, and out_of_range. The break of 2018 (open question O1, answered by the application). 93% and 89% of the inclusion visits of 2012 to 2014 and of 2015 to 2017 hold the scale, 43% to 49% in 2018 to 2020, 2021 to 2022 and 2023 to 2026. The BIS (form 215) is one of the forms that the simplified visit leaves out (visite.SVUPDES = 1, config/globale2.php, DESTVISIMP; PROGRESS.md D55): an empty scale after 2018 is "not asked" on a simplified visit, not "no". The extraction does not say which visits were simplified (request R127 and R155: the svupdes column; question M69).

bis12.title: Barratt Impulsiveness Scale, BIS-12 (12 items)

bp.notes: BIS-10 and BIS-12 are two instruments. An error in the EMR stored the answers of the 12-item BIS-12 (used from 2021 on) in twelve of the columns of the 34-item BIS-10. The BIS-12 has no column of its own in the extraction and no section in the dictionary; the dictionary's contents tab only lists "Bis10 (12 items)" among the questionnaires reduced since 2021. This schema reads those twelve columns on the visits where the 12-item form was used: the visits where none of the 22 other BIS-10 items is filled. bis10.yaml reads the other visits. Both files carry the same version block. The 34-item form fits the French BIS-10 (Baylé et al. 2000), which could not be confirmed beyond the abstract of that paper (bis10.yaml). The 12-item form is the one that the EMR prints from 2021. No published version called BIS-12 was found; a 12-item three-factor structure by Reid and colleagues, cited by Tsatali et al. 2021, was not read. Whether the twelve items are a published short form or a selection by the developers therefore stays open (literature check 2026-11-21). Before 2021. The 12-item form did not exist, and the data managers advise not to deliver the reduced questionnaires of a visit dated before 2021 (decision D71 in PROGRESS.md). The version block says so (since): such a visit has no form, gets version_unknown, and its answers are not delivered. 8 visits, dated 2018 to 2020; als18.yaml says what they look like. Item names. The twelve questions are BIS-10 items 1, 6, 8, 9, 12, 14, 17, 20, 21, 23, 25 and 28 (confirmed, decision D8 in PROGRESS.md). The form prints these BIS-10 numbers (the question stored in bis1006 is printed 6), not 1 to 12. The variables are numbered 1 to 12 in the order of the questions, bis12_01 to bis12_12, and the label of each says the number that the form prints. Items are coded 1 to 4. The reversed items are those stored in the columns of the reversed BIS-10 items 1, 8, 9, 12 and 21, that is bis12_01, 03, 04, 05 and 09. Stored scores. The extraction stores the 12-item total in the column bis10 and the cognitive mean in bis1038, both reversing items as 6 - value. This schema reverses as 5 - value, hence the compare_offset. The rule kept is 5 - value (decision D92 in PROGRESS.md): the script of the application reverses 4, 3, 2, 1, writes two decimals and exists on the 12-item form only, whereas bis1038 to bis1040 are filled with one decimal on every visit that has the twelve items, from 2009 on (all 4,581 complete BIS-10 visits). They are written by the score step of the data managers. The stored behavioural and general means are rounded to one decimal: they are compared with a tolerance of 0.051 (the general score with an offset of 0.5). The export also writes a score when an item is missing, as the sum of the answers present (22 stored scores on 7 visits; one stored total of 5 is below the declared range). Not read. On these visits the EMR also filled bis10_imp_mot, bis10_imp_att, bis10_imp_pla, bis10_score_total and bis11, using the 4, 4, 4, 12 and 9 items that happen to exist. They are not BIS-12 scores.

circadian.title: Circadian Type Inventory (CTI, French ITC, 11 items)

bp.notes: Habits around sleep. Filled at the inclusion visit and, for part of the patients, at the yearly visits. Eleven items, each 1 (almost never) to 5 (almost always). The instrument is the Circadian Type Inventory in its French version, the "Inventaire du type circadien" (ITC; the application's table is autoq_type_circadien). It has eleven items and two scales, flexibility or rigidity of the sleep habits (5 items) and languid or vigorous (6 items, the capacity to overcome drowsiness). The original authors are Folkard and colleagues (1979); the literature check of 2026-11-21 found no source on this instrument, so the exact citation and the French validation are still unknown. The form asks for what the patient prefers or is able to do, not what work obliges them to do, and to answer quickly; there is no time frame. The item labels below are short paraphrases of the French wording, with the scale of each item. Two scores: flexibility of the sleep habits (items 2, 4, 6, 8, 10; 5 to 25) and languidness, the difficulty to overcome drowsiness (items 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11; 6 to 30). The item lists were read from the data: the stored flexibility equals ours on all but 3 of 8,311 rows and the stored languidness on all but 3 of 8,308; a higher answer is more flexible (flexibility) or more languid (languidness) on every item, so nothing is reversed.

circadian.description: Circadian Type Inventory in its French version (Inventaire du type circadien). Eleven items on habits around sleep, each answered by the patient from 1 (almost never) to 5 (almost always), at the inclusion visit and, for part of the patients, at the yearly visits.
circadian.reference: Folkard and colleagues, 1979 (exact citation and French validation unknown)
circadian.reference_confidence: cited in schema notes; the literature check of 2026-11-21 found no source on this instrument
circadian.period: no time frame (what the patient prefers or is able to do)

csm.title: Composite Scale of Morningness (CSM, 13 items)

bp.notes: Filled at the inclusion visit (6,051 of the 6,113 visits that hold it); 62 visits at follow-up, from 60 patients (two of them twice). Thirteen questions on the preferred hours of the day, with no time frame. Items 1, 2 and 7 have five answers, the others four. Coding. The items are stored as points: a higher value is the more morning-type answer, for every item (each item rises with the sum of the others). The dictionary lists the answers in the order of the form, which for some items is the reverse; its numbers are not those of the data. The stored total (csm_) equals the sum of the thirteen items (13 to 55, higher is more of a morning type) in every row where both exist. Item 7 (the hour at which one needs to go to bed). Until the extraction of November 2026 its earliest answer (5, between 20:00 and 21:00) was lost in the export, whose spelling of that answer differed from the one of the form; the item was empty on 450 visits and the total was missing there (decision D33 in PROGRESS.md). The data managers corrected the export (D64): item 7 now holds a 5 on 451 visits, and the total exists on them.

dr.notes: The BP schema as it is: the Composite Scale of Morningness, thirteen items, total 13 to 55 (higher is more of a morning person). Filled at inclusion and at the visits of 1, 2 and 4 years: 727 visits. The stored total (csm_) equals ours on the 718 visits where the thirteen items are filled. The break of 2018 (open question O1, answered by the application). 94% and 89% of the inclusion visits of 2012 to 2014 and of 2015 to 2017 hold the scale, 44% to 47% in 2018 to 2020, 2021 to 2023 and 2024 to 2026. The CSM (form 143) is one of the forms that the simplified visit leaves out (visite.SVUPDES = 1, config/globale2.php, DESTVISIMP; PROGRESS.md D55): an empty scale after 2018 is "not asked" on a simplified visit, not "no". The extraction does not say which visits were simplified (request R127 and R155: the svupdes column; question M69). Bands. The script of the form holds the bands of the score (evening type up to 30, intermediate 31 to 45, morning type 46 or more); no band is stored or delivered. The published bands are 22 or less evening and above 44 morning in the original (Smith 1989, cited by Shahid 2012), and below 31 evening and above 44 morning in the French version (Caci 1999, abstract; Spano 2022 writes below 32). The script's evening bound is the French one; its morning bound (46) is one point above the published one (45). Which three items are scored 1 to 5 (here 1, 2 and 7) was not confirmed by the literature check of 2026-11-21.

Items 1, 2 and 7 have five answers, the others four. The items are stored as points; the numbers of the dictionary are not those of the data.

ctq.title: Childhood Trauma Questionnaire, short form (CTQ, 28 items)

bp.notes: Filled once, at the inclusion visit (93 patients have items on 2 or more visits (90 with a total)). Twenty-eight items, each 1 (never true) to 5 (very often true). Five sub-scores of five items each (5 to 25): emotional abuse (items 3, 8, 14, 18, 25), physical abuse (9, 11, 12, 15, 17), sexual abuse (20, 21, 23, 24, 27), emotional neglect (5, 7, 13, 19, 28) and physical neglect (1, 2, 4, 6, 26). Seven items describe a good childhood and are reversed (6 - value): 2, 5, 7, 13, 19, 26 and 28. The total is the sum of the five sub-scores (25 to 125). The stored sub-scores and the stored total equal these sums in every row where both exist (6,190 for the total, 6,219 to 6,227 for the sub-scores). Severity classes. The EMR cuts each stored sub-score in four classes (1 none, 2 low, 3 moderate, 4 severe). The limits found in the data are those of the manual: 8, 10 and 13 for physical abuse and physical neglect; 9, 13 and 16 for emotional abuse; 6, 8 and 13 for sexual abuse; 10, 15 and 18 for emotional neglect. The classes are delivered as stored: the table of the manual is not kept in the package, so they are not computed again. They follow these limits on the delivered sub-score in every row but four (one in each sub-score but sexual abuse, from 2010 to 2021), where the class was not updated with its sub-score; those four keep the stored class. The class is the application's own, written with the sub-score when the score button is clicked, whereas the stored sub-scores and the total are written again from the items by the export (D120); it is empty on 67 to 71 visits per sub-score where the sub-score exists (67 emotional abuse, 71 physical abuse, 68 sexual abuse, 71 emotional neglect and 71 physical neglect), and filled on 0 to 4 where the sub-score is empty. Denial. Items 10, 16 and 22 do not enter the sub-scores. The denial score is the number of them answered 5, exactly (0 to 3), and is computed here from the three items when all three are answered. The stored score (ctq40) is the check and is not delivered, because the script of the application counts an unanswered item as 0 (only an answer 5 counts 1) and writes the score on an incomplete form. The stored score is empty on 66 visits whose three items are answered (64 of them hold the stored total) and is filled on 42 visits where one or more of the three items is empty (36 of them stored 0, 6 stored 1 or more): the score is delivered on the first 66 and left missing on the 42 (flag score_not_recomputed). Where both exist they are equal on every visit. ctq41 only says whether the stored score is 1 or more and is not read (ignored.yaml). Time frame and direction. The form asks about the patient's childhood and adolescence ("during my childhood and/or adolescence"), and every item label says so, with the sub-scale of the item. The items are delivered as the form stores them, 1 (never true) to 5 (very often true); the seven positive items (2, 5, 7, 13, 19, 26 and 28) are reversed in the scores, not recoded.

sz.notes: Childhood Trauma Questionnaire, short form: 28 items from 1 (never true) to 5 (very often true), about childhood and adolescence. Filled mostly once, at inclusion: 2,216 visits have items (1,965 at inclusion) and 2,166 have a stored total. Same instrument and same variables as in FACE BP, where the notes give the scoring keys: five sub-scores of five items, seven items worded as a good childhood that the score reverses, a total of 25 items and a denial score of three. The labels give the sub-scale and the direction of each item, not its text (the questionnaire is copyrighted). Every stored sub-score and the stored total equal ours on the visits that have both: no score_mismatch on the 2,166 totals. The answers 1 to 5 all occur on every item; the scan's lead (items that never hold an answer the others have) came from the class columns, which go from 1 to 4. The item answers have the BP profile and every item rises with its scale (checked 2026-11-18). Denial. Items 10, 16 and 22 do not enter the sub-scores or the total. The denial score is the number of them answered 5, exactly (0 to 3). The script of the form counts a blank item as 0 (A73 of docs/EXPORT_REQUESTS.md), so the stored score (ctq40) exists on 20 visits where one of the three items is blank and is missing on 43 visits that have the three. The package delivers the strict score: the three answers are needed. Against the stored one that is 43 more values and 20 fewer (the 20 are score_not_recomputed), and on the 2,148 visits that have both the stored score is lower than the three items give on 2 visits (2013: score_mismatch). 65 cells change. The stored score is kept as the hidden check ctq_denial_stored. ctq41 only says whether the stored score is above 0 and is not read (ignored.yaml). Severity classes. The EMR cuts each stored sub-score in four classes (1 none to 4 severe) with the limits of the manual, which are not in the package; the classes are delivered as stored and no class is computed here. A class is empty on 45 (emotional abuse), 49 (physical abuse), 46 (sexual abuse), 48 (emotional neglect) and 46 (physical neglect) visits that have the sub-score, both stored and recomputed: the EMR stored the sub-score and no class (61 to 70 visits per sub-score have items and no class). The class is not the class of its sub-score on 6 visits (one or two per sub-score), where it was not updated with its sub-score; they keep the stored class. They are doubtful wherever the sub-score is (derived_from). The form has a box "done / not done" (rad_ctq_nf) that the export does not select, as for the PSQI, MARS, Fagerström and the other questionnaires of the tab (the extraction has no rad_*_nf column): a blank questionnaire cannot be told from one that was not done (export request R152).

dr.notes: The BP scale, with seven items turned back to the answer as asked, and without the five severity classes. Childhood Trauma Questionnaire, 28 items about childhood and adolescence, coded 1 (never true) to 5 (very often true), filled once, at inclusion: 528 patients (95% of the inclusions of 2012 to 2014, 69% of those of 2021 to 2023, 79% since). The form (167) is on the list of the simplified visit of the inclusion, so the break of 2018 does not touch it. Seven items are stored reversed here. Items 2, 5, 7, 13, 19, 26 and 28 describe a good childhood, and the key reverses them (6 - value). The form of this cohort keys the answers of these seven items 5 (never true) to 1 (very often true) and the 21 others 1 to 5, so its own script (167_score.js) adds the 28 values as they are and gets the right sub-scores. In BP the seven items are stored as asked: each falls when the fifteen abuse items rise (r = -0.30 to -0.57). In this extraction each rises with them (+0.17 to +0.56), and their means are far from BP (item 2: 2.1 against 4.0; between 1.8 and 2.3 in every period and between 1.6 and 2.5 in every centre). Items 16 and 22 of the denial scale, which nobody reverses, fall with abuse in both cohorts (r = -0.5 to -0.6). So the form of this cohort stores the seven items already reversed. They are read back to the answer as asked (6 - value, written as codes), so that ctq01 to ctq28 mean the same in the two cohorts and the BP key applies. After this the item means of the two cohorts agree (r = 0.99 over the 28 items, 0.76 before). Each item label gives its sub-score, its direction and the time frame; the wording of the items is not copied. Scores. Five sub-scores of five items (5 to 25): emotional abuse (items 3, 8, 14, 18, 25), physical abuse (9, 11, 12, 15, 17), sexual abuse (20, 21, 23, 24, 27), emotional neglect (5, 7, 13, 19, 28) and physical neglect (1, 2, 4, 6, 26); the total is their sum (25 to 125). Stored neglect scores and stored total: wrong, not delivered. The cause is the export, not the EMR: the score definition of the export (nucleus ctq.yaml, lines 71 to 126) names the table of this cohort with the BP list of reversed items, which is made for answers stored as asked, and reverses the seven items a second time. So the stored emotional neglect is in fact a score of good childhood: it falls when emotional abuse rises (r = -0.61; +0.67 in BP), and its mean is 16.7 where ours is 13.3 (12.4 in BP). The three stored values (ctq31, ctq33, ctq39) are reproduced exactly by adding the items with none reversed: the twin scores named _as_stored, read to check the stored values and not delivered (no mismatch on 521, 523 and 517 visits). The delivered emotional neglect rises with emotional abuse (+0.61); the delivered means are close to BP (physical neglect 7.5 against 7.3, total 44.1 against 43.8). The three stored abuse scores have no reversed item and equal ours (522 to 525 visits). Open question O17 (request R146). Denial. The number of items 10, 16 and 22 answered 5 (0 to 3), computed here from the three items, all three being needed (522 visits). The stored score (ctq40) is written by the script of the form, which counts an unanswered item as 0 (167_score.js, eval_deni): it exists on 430 visits, equals the count on the 429 where the three items are filled, exists on one visit with only two items answered (not delivered: the score cannot be recomputed there) and is empty on 93 visits that have the three items, most of them from 2020 (the script of the form: A73). The stored score is kept as the check (ctq_denial_stored). Not in this extraction: the five columns of BP that hold the severity class of each sub-score (ctq30 to ctq38, even numbers). They are not recomputed here: the classes need the limits of the manual, a copyrighted table that the package does not hold.
dr.difference: seven reverse-keyed items are stored already reversed (the form keys them 5 to 1) and are read back to the answer as asked; the export, not the EMR, reverses them a second time in the stored neglect scores and total, which are checked by twin scores that are not delivered; no severity classes in the extraction; the stored denial score is the form script's, which counts an unanswered item as 0

asp.notes: Twenty-eight items from 1 to 5, five stored sub-scores, a total and the denial score, at the inclusion visit: 395 visits, from 2020 to 2026, and 11 follow-up visits. It belongs to the new set of forms. It is filled by adults only. Same instrument as in FACE BP, SZ and DR, and the same key. **The answers were compared with BP before the schema was copied** (the lesson of FACE DR, where seven items are stored already reversed). Here the seven "good childhood" items fall when the abuse items rise, as in BP (correlations of -0.38 to -0.55): the coding is the BP one. The items are delivered as the form stores them, 1 (never true) to 5 (very often true); the seven positive items (2, 5, 7, 13, 19, 26 and 28) are reversed in the scores only (`reverse`). The form asks about childhood and adolescence (growing up), and every item label says so, with the sub-scale of the item. **Two stored sub-scores leave out an item, and the stored total with them.** The stored physical abuse is the sum of the items 9, 11, 15 and 17 (400 of 404 visits): the item 12 is missing. The stored emotional abuse is the sum of the items 3, 8, 18 and 25 (400 of 401): the item 14 is missing. The cause is in the script of the form (`334_score.js`, lines 45 and 72), which reads two radios named CTQ012 and CTQ014 that do not exist in the form, so that the items 12 and 14 count 0. The stored sexual abuse is right (405 of 405). The stored total is the sum of the five stored sub-scores (400 of 400), so it misses two items. **The stored neglect scores follow the script, not the key.** The stored physical neglect follows the key on 377 of 403 visits and the stored emotional neglect on 321 of 404. The script maps the answer 1 of a reversed item to 1 (`334_score.js`, line 15), where the key gives 5, and counts every other answer as the key does: the 83 visits of the emotional neglect and the 26 of the physical neglect that differ are exactly the visits where a reversed item is answered 1 (no rule was found before the review, O12 (7)). The EMR rule is written as formulas "as stored" (`ctq_emotional_neglect_as_stored`, `ctq_physical_neglect_as_stored`, with `points`) that reproduce the stored scores on every visit: no score_mismatch is left on the two neglect scores, and the delivered neglect scores are not compared with the stored ones. The five sub-scores and the total are therefore computed with the BP key and delivered. The stored values are read to be checked and are not delivered: formulas "as stored" reproduce the two abuse scores and the total (5 visits keep a stale stored value: 4 physical abuse and 1 emotional abuse), and the stored neglect scores are reproduced by the formulas of the previous paragraph. The columns are not those of BP: the even numbers from ctq30 to ctq38 hold the sub-scores here, and there is no severity class. The stored sub-scores come from the script of the EMR here; in FACE DR the cause is the export (DR O17). **Denial.** Items 10, 16 and 22 do not enter the sub-scores. The denial score is the number of them answered 5, exactly (0 to 3), and is computed here from the three items, with the same rule in the four cohorts; the stored score (ctq40) is the check and is not delivered. They agree on every visit (401 of 401): the script of this cohort needs the three answers, where the scripts of BP, SZ and DR count an unanswered item as 0. **Year and centre.** 7 of the 24 variables reach 0.5 or more (6 by year, 7 by centre): the 28 items are on a 1 to 5 scale (one level is 1.0 or more of the interquartile range). The scores stand at 0.00 to 0.25 by year and 0.00 to 0.19 by centre, the total at 0.17 and 0.19 (median 40 to 43 by year, 38 to 43.5 by centre). Adults only, 2021 to 2026 (2020 has fewer than 20 totals). No step.

epworth.title: Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS, 8 items)

bp.notes: Eight situations of daily life; for each, the chance of dozing off, from 0 (would never doze) to 3 (high chance). Filled at every visit. The total is the sum of the eight items (0 to 24, higher is sleepier). History. Until the extraction of November 2026 only the answers equal to 0 reached the extraction: the text of the three other answers holds an apostrophe, which the export step lost, so the scale was not loaded (decision D33 in PROGRESS.md). The data managers corrected the export (D64). Items. The dictionary gives the same label to the eight items ("Items EPWORTH") and not the situations. The labels below are those of the published scale in its usual order. The answers support that order: item 5 (lying down in the afternoon) is the most endorsed (mean 2.2), items 6 (talking to someone) and 8 (in a car stopped in traffic) the least (0.2 and 0.4). The wording of the eight situations on the application form is that of these labels, in this order (checked in November 2026). Total. The stored total (ess0109) exists where the eight items are filled and equals their sum in every row. Its mean is the same in every year (8.3 to 9.3) and close at inclusion and at follow-up (9.3 and 8.4): the same question at every visit, one schema. Time frame. The form asks about "the recent months" and, for a situation that the patient has not met lately, to imagine how it would have affected them (the instruction of the application's form, read in November 2026). The same question is asked at every visit, so the total says the sleepiness of the months before each visit. A last question (essdorm) asks when the sleepiness comes. It is a category and is not part of the score: it is an addition of the French form, which the published scale (the eight situations) does not have. Its fourth answer ("at any time of the day") was lost for the same reason and is back.

Filled at inclusion and at the visits of 1, 2 and 4 years: 723 visits. The stored total equals ours on the 719 visits where the eight items are filled; it is the export's (nucleus epworth.yaml). The ninth question, "when do these urges to sleep come" (epworth_when), is a French addition to the published eight-item scale: it does not enter the total. The break of 2018 (open question O1, answered by D55). 94% and 89% of the inclusion visits of 2012 to 2014 and of 2015 to 2017 hold the scale, 43% to 48% in the three periods since 2018. The form (144) is in none of the lists of the simplified visit: an empty scale since 2018 is "not asked" on a simplified visit, not "no", and it is missing data here, never 0. The extraction has no flag that tells a simplified visit from a full one with an empty scale (R127, R139, R155).

eq5d.title: EQ-5D-5L, health-related quality of life

bp.notes: Five dimensions, each rated 1 (no problem) to 5 (extreme problem), and a visual scale of the health of the patient today, from 0 to 100. In the extraction from 2012 (6 visits in 2012, 193 in 2013, 12,469 from 2014 to 2026; 12,668 visits with the five answers in all). The index (eq5d_) is the value of the "France" column of the EuroQol crosswalk (van Hout and colleagues, 2012) from the five-level profile to the three-level value set: a table of the 3,125 profiles, in the application's script (hetero_eq5d.js) and in the export, which names the crosswalk and the country (nucleus eq5d5l.yaml). It is a crosswalk value, not a value set built on five-level preferences. A French EQ-5D-5L value set exists (Andrade et al., PharmacoEconomics 2020;38:413-425); it is not in the sources, and whether to use it is for the project lead to decide. The lowest value in the data is -0.53 (153 negative indices, which the clean model of the export strips of their minus sign and the score step then writes again, R50). The stored index equals the table on all 12,668 visits with the five answers, and one index goes with one profile in BP, SZ and ASP, the same in the three. Since decision D133 the index delivered is the table's value, read from the five answers (the table is norms/eq5d_index.csv, outside the repository), and the stored one is a check (score_mismatch: none in BP). The same score is computed in SZ, DR and ASP, so the index is the same variable in the four cohorts. The visual scale is not part of the index. The script of the ASP application asks for it before it gives an index; the BP script has a test that should do the same and never fires (A18: it compares a list of elements with an empty text), so the index exists on the 1,305 visits that have the five answers and no scale, and is delivered there.

sz.notes: EQ-5D-5L, filled at every visit from 2011 (3,927 visits, 57 of them screening rows): five dimensions of 1 to 5, the visual scale and the index. Same instrument as in FACE BP. Index. The extraction holds a stored index; the package reads the index from the five answers in a table with one value per profile, as in BP (BP D133). The table is the crosswalk of the 5L profile to the French 3L value set (the EuroQol crosswalk of van Hout et al., Value Health 2012;15:708-715, which maps a 5L profile to the 3L value set of any country; country France): 3,125 profiles, identical in the scripts of the BP, SZ and ASP applications; the score step of the export names the same country. It is not a French value set for the 5L itself; one exists (Andrade et al., PharmacoEconomics 2020;38:413-425) but its table is not in the sources, so it is not used. The stored index equals it on all 3,909 visits with the five answers: nothing is flagged. The visual scale (0 to 100) is not needed: the script of the application tests a missing scale on a node list that is never empty, so its test never fires (defect A18) and the index exists on 3,909 visits against 3,169 scales. The index goes from -0.53 to 1.

dr.notes: The BP schema without the stored utility index. EQ-5D-5L: five questions with five levels (1 no problem to 5 extreme) and a visual scale of the health of the day (0 to 100). Filled at inclusion and at every follow-up visit: 1,436 visits, 90% or more of the inclusions until 2023 and 82% since. It is one of the scales that the break of 2018 does not touch. One visual scale is above 100: out_of_range. Index. The extraction has no index column; the index is read in a table from the five answers, as in BP (BP D133), so that it is the same variable in the four cohorts: 1,434 visits. The table is the crosswalk of the 5L profile to the French 3L value set (the EuroQol interim crosswalk of van Hout and colleagues, Value Health 2012, which maps the 5L answers onto any country's 3L value set, here France's; the values of the scripts were not compared with the published French column): one value for each of the 3,125 profiles, the same in the scripts of the BP, SZ and ASP applications and in the score step of the export for BP and SZ (the DR application and the DR export compute no index). It is not a French value set for the 5L itself; one exists (Andrade and colleagues, PharmacoEconomics 2020, values -0.525 to 1) but its table is not in the sources, so it is not used.
dr.difference: the extraction has no stored utility index (the index is computed from the answers, as in BP)

asp.notes: Five dimensions answered from 1 to 5, the visual scale of health and a stored index, about the state of health today: 1,021 visits hold an answer (913 at inclusion, from 2009 to 2026, and 108 follow-up visits). Children and adults: 344 of the 1,020 visits with the five answers are visits of patients under 18, who fill the same adult form. Same instrument as in FACE BP, SZ and DR (five levels), in other columns (mobility, selfcare, activity, pain, anxiety, eq_vas). **The index is the crosswalk of the 5L profile to the French 3L value set.** The table of the application's script (`250_score.js` here, `hetero_eq5d.js` in BP and SZ) gives one index per profile of the five answers, and the three tables are identical on the 3,125 profiles: it is the France column of the EuroQol crosswalk from the 5L profile to the 3L value sets (van Hout and others, 2012), not a value set of the 5L form. A value set made for the 5L form exists for France (Andrade and others, 2020); its table is not in the sources, and which set to use is a choice for the analyst. For a patient under 18 the adult form and the adult value set are used (344 visits). The index is read from the five answers (the stored index is a check: score_mismatch) on 1,020 visits, 45 more than the stored index covers. The stored index equals the table on 974 of 974 visits where the five answers and a possible stored index exist. Four things differ. **28 stored indices are above 1**: whole numbers typed without the decimal separator (26 with three digits, 2 with two: 1000 times a value of the table), 27 of them on visits with none of the five answers, in 2020 to 2022 in two centres; where the five answers exist (1 visit) the table value is delivered. **6 stored indices sit on visits with fewer than five answers**: they cannot be recomputed (score_not_recomputed). **11 negative indices are dropped by the export** (`easperger_aut_eq5d.sql`, line 43: R51): the stored index is empty on 11 visits whose profile has a negative value, which the table gives. **34 visits with the five answers have no visual scale and no stored index**: the script requires the scale before it writes the index (`250_score.js`, lines 15-19); the index is delivered there all the same, since it does not depend on the scale. (In BP and SZ the same test on the scale never fires, because the script reads a NodeList instead of a value: A18.) **Year and centre.** 5 of the 5 variables reach 0.5 or more (5 by year, 3 by centre): the five answers are levels of a whole-number scale, and the index (the value of the table for the five answers) stands at 0.55 by year and 0.50 by centre. The age mix: children are 34% of the visits, 100% of centre A, 53% of B, 45% of C, 3% of D and none of E (median index 0.86 in A, 0.77 in D, 0.64 to 0.67 in B and C, 0.54 in E). Among adults the median index is 0.80 to 0.91 in 2014 and 2015, 0.71 to 0.88 in 2016 to 2018 and 0.62 to 0.70 from 2019 (year shift 0.72 within adults, 0.36 within children); centre D, 97% adults, reads 0.77 against 0.65 to 0.66 in B and C and 0.54 in E, which takes part of it. A step with no known cause (the case mix; the table of the index does not change).

fagerstrom.title: Fagerström Test for Nicotine Dependence (6 items)

bp.notes: Six questions for smokers. Filled at every visit by the patients who smoke. Items 1 and 4 are 0 to 3, the others 0 or 1; the total is their sum (0 to 10). Item 3 ("which cigarette would you hate most to give up?") has two answers: the first of the day (1 point) or any other (0). History. Until the extraction of November 2026 the answer "any other" was lost in the export (its text holds an apostrophe): item 3 was 1 or empty, and the stored total was missing for every patient who had given that answer. An empty item 3 was then read here as "any other" (decision D33 in PROGRESS.md). The data managers corrected the export (D64): item 3 is now 0 on 2,119 visits, and nothing is assumed any more. Total. The stored total (fagers) exists where the six items are filled and equals their sum in every row. It is recomputed here with the same rule: the six items are needed.

sz.notes: Fagerström test for nicotine dependence, 6 items, filled on 2,044 visits (1,042 at inclusion). Same instrument and same schema as in FACE BP. Item 3 lost its answer "any other cigarette" until the extraction of 13 November 2026 (decision D1 in PROGRESS.md); it is back, and the stored total equals the sum of the six items on the 1,981 visits that have it. Who is asked. The test is for smokers. The form hides it by a smoking-status question named rad_tabac that no table of the SZ extraction holds, so the gate cannot be read from the extraction; against the tobacco status of the same visit (tobacco.yaml) the items are filled on 1,833 of the 2,087 current smokers, 44 of the 614 ex-smokers, 35 of the 1,728 non-smokers and 132 of the 2,177 visits with no status. These 79 cells of non-smokers and ex-smokers and the 132 with no status are kept as recorded (no shown_if: the status is of the day of the visit and "Non fumeur" is not "never smoked"). A visit with no item is missing, never 0. The form's box "done / not done" (rad_fagerstrom_nf) is not in the extraction (export request R152).

This extraction stores the code of the answer, 1 for the first and 2 for any other, and the stored total (fagers) adds the code as if it were the points: it is 2 points too high on each of the 129 visits where the answer is "any other" (77 patients, 13 centres, 2013 to 2026), and equal to ours on the 263 others. Two steps add the code: the script of the form (112, line 49: the sum of the six values as keyed) and the score step of the export (fagers.yaml, a plain sum of the six columns, which names this cohort's table). Here the code 2 is read as 0 points, as in BP, and the total is recomputed: the 129 visits carry score_mismatch, which marks the stored value as the wrong one (open question O15).

mars.title: Medication Adherence Rating Scale (MARS, 10 items, past week)

bp.notes: Ten yes/no questions on taking the treatment, about the week that has just passed (the instructions of the form). Filled at every visit. Coding. The dictionary says 1 = yes and 0 = no. The data say the opposite for the ten items: 96% of the answers to item 5 ("I take my medication only when I am sick") are 1, and 91% of the answers to item 8 ("By staying on medication I can prevent getting sick") are 0. The items are therefore read as 1 = no and 0 = yes, which the project lead confirmed (decision D37 in PROGRESS.md). They are delivered as the numbers stored. Total. One point for "no" to items 1 to 6, 9 and 10, and one point for "yes" to items 7 and 8: with the coding above, the sum of the ten items with items 7 and 8 reversed. A higher total is a better adherence (0 to 10). The stored total (mars_) is exactly this in every row where both exist (16,071). mars11 is "do you take a medication at present?" (1 yes, 0 no; 95% of the 4,433 answers are yes): 1 to 14 answers a year from 2017 to 2020, 108 in 2021, 957 in 2022 and about 1,000 a year in 2023 and 2024. The form shows the ten items only after a yes to it: of its 231 visits with a no, none holds an item, so the MARS is missing (not zero) for a patient who takes no medication.

sz.notes: Medication Adherence Rating Scale, 10 items, filled at every visit (4,316 visits, 2,078 at inclusion). The BP schema: ten items coded 1 = no and 0 = yes, and a total that counts items 7 and 8 the other way (decision D37 of the BP file). The stored total was fitted on the items here too and follows the same formula: 2 score_mismatch on the 4,204 visits that have both a stored and a recomputed total; 62 more visits have a recomputed total and no stored one. Item 10 is in the column mars010 (mars10 in BP), which the dictionary does not list. The BP question "takes a medication at present" (mars11) is not in the SZ extraction and the SZ form has no such question: there is no gate (in BP the form hides the MARS after a no to that question). An empty MARS in SZ is a questionnaire not filled, never a no: it is missing, not 0. The form's box "done / not done" (rad_mars_nf) is not in the extraction (export request R152).
sz.difference: item 10 is in the column mars010, and the question "takes a medication at present" (mars11) is not extracted

dr.notes: The BP scale, with the answers turned to the BP coding, and without the question added in 2021 (mars11). Ten yes/no questions on taking the treatment. Filled at inclusion and at every follow-up visit: 1,036 visits. Coding: the opposite of BP. BP stores 1 = no and 0 = yes (decision D37 of the BP progress file). This extraction stores 1 = yes, as the dictionary says: on the items that tell, the share of answers 1 is the mirror of BP (item 3: 9% against 91%; item 4: 16% against 86%; item 5, "I take my medication only when I am sick": 14% against 96%; item 8, "by staying on medication I can prevent getting sick": 76% against 9%; item 9: 27% against 83%), in every period (item 5: 9% to 15%) and in every centre (6% to 31%). The ten items are delivered on the BP coding, 1 = no and 0 = yes (written as codes), so that they mean the same in the two cohorts. Total: the stored one is wrong, not delivered, and the error is the export's, not the EMR's. The total gives one point for "no" to items 1 to 6, 9 and 10 and one point for "yes" to items 7 and 8: 0 to 10, higher is a better adherence. The form's own script (form 220) turns items 1 to 6, 9 and 10 for the 1 = yes coding and is right. The score step of the export (the definition mars.yaml) applies the BP formula, which turns items 7 and 8 only, to the columns of this cohort, whose coding is the opposite of BP's, and writes the result in mars_: the stored total counts the answers that show poor adherence, and its median is 3, against 8 in BP. It is reproduced exactly by the twin score mars_total_as_stored (10 minus the total; no mismatch on 1,026 visits), which is not delivered. The delivered total has a median of 7 (quartiles 6 and 8; BP 8, 6 and 9) and falls when depression rises (r = -0.38 with the QIDS). Open question O17. The export needs a separate entry for this cohort, with items 1 to 6, 9 and 10 turned (request R146). mathys.title: Multidimensional Assessment of Thymic States (MAThyS, 20 items)

bp.notes: Twenty visual scales from 0 to 10, on the last week. Filled at every visit except the screening visit. The seven questions on emotions that follow them in the form are in mathys_emotions.yaml. Items. A third of the visits (36%) hold at least one value with a decimal (5.5); 10% of the values. In 52 cells the decimal point is lost: 55 for 5.5, and once 510 for 5.10. A value above 10 is divided by 10 or by 100 (unit_inferred). Key. Eight items are reversed (10 - value): 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 17 and 18. The total is the sum of the twenty items, from 0 (inhibition) to 200 (activation). Sub-scores: emotional reactivity (items 3, 7, 10, 18), motivation (2, 11, 12, 15, 16, 17, 19), sensory perception (1, 6, 8, 13, 20), interpersonal communication (4, 14) and cognition (5, 9). It is the key of the application, read in its code in November 2026, and the wording of the twenty scales on its form is that of the published scale. Two forms, two directions (decision D91 in PROGRESS.md). The old form stored the eight reversed scales already turned towards the score; the form that replaced it, centre by centre between September 2021 and May 2022, stores them as written. Evidence. Against the mania and depression scales of the same visit (Altman and YMRS, QIDS and MADRS), item 17 as stored goes with activation until 2021 (rank correlation +0.39 to +0.41 against the twelve other items) and against it from 2023 (-0.39); about 0 in 2022, when the forms are mixed; items 8, 9, 10 and 18 turn the same way. The internal consistency of the twenty items until 2021 is 0.85 to 0.87 with no item reversed and 0.64 to 0.67 with the key; from 2023 it is 0.66 and 0.85. The sub-scores that the application itself stored were plain sums on the old form (10,043 visits) and reversed the eight items on the new one (3,422 visits; extraction of October 2026). In FACE DR, another application, the key holds in every year. What is delivered. Every item is delivered as written on the form of today. (1) A visit dated before 2021-09-01 is expected to use the old form: its eight items are turned (10 - value, flag sign_flipped) and the key then gives the right scores. (2) From 2021-09-01 to 2022-12-31 the centres changed one after the other and the two directions are mixed, also among the visits of the new form: the eight items of these visits are not delivered (period_removed), nor the total and the four sub-scores that use them. Their twelve other items and the interpersonal sub-score are delivered. (3) From 2023 the items are expected as stored. (4) In each centre and year the data decide where they are clear (the sign block, SCHEMA_SPEC section 9; decision of 2026-11-21 in PROGRESS.md): on the form of today the sum of the eight scales goes against the sum of the twelve others, on the old form with it. A centre-year with 10 visits or more that hold the twenty scales, whose rank correlation is two standard errors or more away from 0, is turned or left as the correlation says, whatever the date. The 84 visits of one centre in 2024 and 2025 (r = +0.43 and +0.44 as stored) are turned this way. No centre-year before September 2021 clearly follows the form of today. Elsewhere the date decides, and a centre-year whose data lean the other way gets sign_doubt on its eight items: 1,134 visits of 17 centre-years. Limits. Most centre-years are too small, or their correlation too weak, for the data to decide: before September 2021, 2,278 visits follow the date for that reason. The visits with sign_doubt are the ones to watch: 1,010 before September 2021 (12 centre-years, 699 of them in one centre in 2013 and 2016 to 2019, where the correlation as stored is -0.15 to 0.00), which are turned and may have been typed or saved again with the new form; and 124 from 2023 (the same centre as above in 2023 and 2026, r = +0.28 and +0.34, and a second centre in 2023 to 2025, 51 visits), which are delivered as stored and may be in the old direction. A third centre (64 visits from 2023) is mixed and has no flag. After the rule, no centre-year of 10 complete visits or more goes the wrong way by two standard errors (2 did before: the 84 visits above); 17 of 167 have a correlation above 0, of at most +0.43. The questions stay in QUESTIONS.md (DM-12): which visits were typed on which form. Status. Reviewed on 2026-11-20 with these limits stated (decision D190 in PROGRESS.md); the data-driven rule of (4) was added on 2026-11-21. An analysis of the MAThyS scores from 2023 should allow for the centre. Stored scores. The total (mathys_) and the five sub-scores (mathys29 to mathys33) of the extraction are not read. Until October 2026 the sub-scores were those of the application, right for each form. Since 10 November 2026 the data managers recalculate them with the key applied to the values as stored, in every year, which is wrong for the old form (decisions D34, D65 and D75, replaced by D91). They are in ignored.yaml.

dr.notes: The BP schema as it is. Twenty visual scales from 0 to 10, on the last week. Filled at inclusion and at every follow-up visit: 1,043 visits. The seven questions on emotions that follow them in the form are in mathys_emotions.yaml. No value has lost its decimal point here (none is above 10). Total. Eight items are reversed (10 - value): 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 17 and 18. The total is the sum of the twenty items, from 0 (inhibition) to 200 (activation). The stored total (mathys_) equals ours on the 937 visits where the twenty items are filled, except the 21 visits turned as below. Sub-scores: the stored ones are wrong on 68 visits and ours are delivered. Emotional reactivity (items 3, 7, 10, 18), motivation (2, 11, 12, 15, 16, 17, 19), sensory perception (1, 6, 8, 13, 20), interpersonal communication (4, 14) and cognition (5, 9), with the same reversed items. The stored sub-scores (mathys29 to mathys33) are read to check ours and are not delivered. They differ on 68 visits of 34 patients, from 2013 to 2018, in two centres (49 of the 50 MAThyS visits of one centre in these years, 19 of 36 in the other): 244 score_mismatch flags on four sub-scores (62 more come from the visits turned as below). On every one of these 244 the stored value is the plain sum of the items with none reversed. The fifth sub-score, interpersonal communication, has no reversed item and never differs, and the stored total of the same visits is right. So the reversal was left out of the sub-scores there, and the error is in the stored value, not in ours. Cause. The script of the form (141) carries a comment dated 10/12/2018 (10 December 2018) saying that it was changed that day "to take the reversed values into account": before it, the sub-scores were summed with none reversed. The 68 visits run from 2013-11-06 to 2018-12-18 and none is later, so they are the visits saved by the old script (open question O14). In BP the same error covered every visit until 2021, and since 10 November 2026 the data managers recalculate the sub-scores; this extraction is of 30 October 2026. Limit: the direction of the form by centre. The key supposes that every centre enters the eight reversed items as the form does. In three centres, in some periods, the eight items go with the twelve others instead of against them: 70 visits of one centre in 2013 to 2015 (the sum of the eight items against the sum of the other twelve: r = +0.29; alpha with the key 0.59), 30 visits of another from 2019 (r = +0.10 to +0.84 by period; alpha 0.50 on the 13 visits of 2019 to 2021) and 15 of a third in 2022 to 2023 (r = +0.31; alpha 0.71), about 115 of the 937 visits with the twenty items (12%). What is done (decision of 2026-11-21 in PROGRESS.md; the sign block, SCHEMA_SPEC section 9). In each centre and year the data decide where they are clear, as in BP but with no date: a centre-year with 10 visits or more that hold the twenty scales, whose rank correlation between the sum of the eight and the sum of the twelve is two standard errors or more above 0, is in the old direction and its eight items are turned (10 - value, sign_flipped). One centre-year is: the 25 visits of the first centre in 2014 (r = +0.61). Its other years (8 visits in 2013, r = -0.02 in 2015) and the other two centre-periods hold too few visits a year to decide, and stay as stored. Five centre-years lean to the old direction without being clear and get sign_doubt on their eight items (77 visits). After the rule no centre-year goes the wrong way by two standard errors (1 did before). The stored total and sub-scores of the 25 turned visits are now wrong against ours (score_mismatch: 21 totals, and 20, 16, 11 and 15 more on the four sub-scores with reversed items). About 90 visits of the limit above stay as stored, and the question is in QUESTIONS.md. The break of 2018 (open question O1, answered by the application). 92% and 87% of the inclusion visits of 2012 to 2014 and of 2015 to 2017 hold the scale, 44% to 48% in 2018 to 2020, 2021 to 2023 and 2024 to 2026. The MAThyS (form 141, with the seven emotions of mathys_emotions.yaml) is one of the forms that the simplified visit leaves out (visite.SVUPDES = 1, config/globale2.php, DESTVISIMP; PROGRESS.md D55): an empty scale after 2018 is "not asked" on a simplified visit, not "no" and not 0. The extraction does not say which visits were simplified (request R127 and R155: the svupdes column; question M69).

mdq.title: Mood Disorder Questionnaire (MDQ), lifetime

bp.notes: Filled once per patient, at the screening visit (2,553 patients, all at the screening visit). Thirteen yes/no questions on past periods of elation (1 = yes), then two questions: did several of these happen during the same period (mdq14), and how much of a problem they were (mdq15, 0 none to 3 serious). The form asks whether there "ever" was such a period, so the answers are lifetime ones and have no time frame (after Hirschfeld and colleagues, 2000, as the form says). The stored total (mdqtot) equals the number of "yes" among the thirteen questions in all but 3 of 2,482 rows. The screening result (mdq_) is delivered as stored. It is positive when the total is 7 or more, mdq14 is yes and mdq15 is 2 or more: this rule gives the stored result on the 2,485 visits with all 15 answers. On 28 visits mdq14 or mdq15 is empty and the stored result is negative, although 19 have 7 yes or more (export request R88). A check score (mdq_screen_check, hidden) applies the three criteria to the answers that exist: a known failure gives 0, and where nothing known fails it gives 1. It is compared with the stored result: it differs on 17 visits (score_mismatch), the 17 of the 19 where the missing answer is the only thing that could have made the result negative (the 2 others fail a criterion that is known). The stored result is not changed, as the answer that is missing could be a no.
