In DR the simplified visit of 2018 onward does not offer it: it is on nine inclusions in ten to 2017 and about one in two since 2018. BP hides the items after a no to the medication question of the MARS form (since 2022).

psqi.title: Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI)

bp.notes: Sleep over the last 30 days. Filled at 89% to 95% of the visits other than the screening visit (none of the 3,987 screening visits holds it). Four questions ask for a time or a duration, the others are rated 0 to 3 (the dictionary says 1 to 4; no cell holds a 4). Seven component scores of 0 to 3 add up to the total (0 to 21, higher is worse). Times. Bedtime, rising time and hours of sleep are written HH:MM and delivered in hours (23:30 is 23.5). 635 bedtimes are typed between 6:00 and 17:00. On 554 of them the night would last more than 16 hours: the bedtime was typed on a 12-hour clock (11:00 for 23:00), and the delivered bedtime (psqi_bedtime, a score of custom.py) gets 12 hours; the 81 others (shorter nights: patients who sleep by day) stay as typed. The bedtime as typed is read as psqi_bedtime_typed and not delivered; the efficiency applies the same test to it (psqi_clock_of_12) and does not change (decision of the user, 2026-11-21, which reverses the "as typed" part of D132). No bedtime of this export is 24:xx (it writes 0:xx). 13 visits give more than 16 hours of sleep. Three nights of more than 24 hours are out_of_range, and one visit holds a time written with one digit of minutes in two fields (the rising time and the hours of sleep: 2 cells, unparsed): it is not guessed. Minutes to fall asleep (psqi02). 312 values are above 5 hours. Most are the minutes multiplied by 60: 300, 600, 900, 1800 and 3600 are frequent, and the patients who wrote them answer item 5a ("cannot fall asleep within 30 minutes") like those who wrote 5, 10, 15, 30 and 60 minutes, not like those who need hours. A value above 240 is therefore divided by 60 (unit_inferred). The exception is 1260 to 1439: these are bedtimes typed in the wrong field (22:30 is 1350 minutes after midnight). They fit no unit and end out_of_range. The minutes are not winsorised: the default limits of a number (the 1st and 99th percentiles) brought 148 values above 150 minutes down to 150 and 146 values of 0 up to 1, and these are real answers (winsor: false). Components. Checked against the items on all rows: the EMR computes each of them as the PSQI manual says. Quality is item 6 and medication is item 7, so their copies (psqi15, psqi16) are not read (ignored.yaml). Duration is delivered as stored. Latency, efficiency, disturbances and daytime dysfunction are computed here from the items by functions of custom.py (psqi_latency, psqi_efficiency, psqi_disturbances, psqi_dysfunction), and the stored component is the check (score_mismatch). The latency component uses the corrected minutes and item 5a, because the stored one (psqi14) used the minutes as written: it differs on the visits above, and so does the stored total. Measured (score_mismatch): 234 stored latency components, 521 stored efficiencies (the application takes the bedtime as typed, wrong on a 12-hour clock, D132) and 725 stored totals differ from ours; 83, 24 and 106 cannot be recomputed (minutes or times out_of_range: score_not_recomputed, neither value is delivered). The stored disturbances and daytime dysfunction never differ. Disturbances and a blank 5j. The component adds the items 5b to 5j: 0 counts 0, 1 to 9 count 1, 10 to 18 count 2, more count 3. Item 5j asks how often another reason disturbed the sleep, and a patient with no other reason often leaves it blank: 137 visits have no 5j, against 12 to 35 for each of the items 5a to 5i. The script of the application asks for it ("Questionnaire incomplet" and no component otherwise) and so does the score step of the export (D120, strict sum of 5b to 5j), so the stored component and the stored total are empty on the 108 visits whose items 5b to 5i are all answered and whose 5j is blank. The package reads a blank 5j as 0 and computes the component there (108 more components and 87 more totals; the 21 others lack another component). On the visits where the stored component exists, ours is equal to it. The published scoring sheet (University of Pittsburgh, after Buysse et al. 1989) counts 5j as 0 when its answer or its comment is missing, by an instruction of Buysse dated 20 May 2005: the package does the same. The daytime dysfunction component (items 8 and 9) is the same as the stored one on every visit. The text of the other reason (psqi05k) is shown by the form only after a 5j of 1, 2 or 3: 3,655 of the 3,657 texts follow one of these answers, and the 2 others (one under a 5j of 0, one under a blank 5j) are not_shown. Sleep of 7 hours exactly counts as 0 in the duration component, as in the application, whose script tests "7 hours or more" on the hours typed and leaves the minutes out (read in November 2026). The published sheet says "more than 7 hours: 0, 6 to 7 hours: 1" and does not settle exactly 7 hours; scoring programs in use read it as the application does. Kept as stored, in the four cohorts (decision D93 in PROGRESS.md; 2,780 visits answer 7 hours). The dictionary marks the PSQI as reduced in 2021. Questions 1 to 9 are filled alike in every year, so what was removed is not among the columns of the extraction.

sz.notes: Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, about the past month (30 days), filled from 2012 on 3,234 visits. The BP schema, where the notes give the rules, with the steps below. The minutes to fall asleep multiplied by 60 are divided (15 unit_inferred), a bedtime typed in that field is out of range (1), and 26 durations written like a time ("0:30") end unparsed. The minutes are not winsorised (winsor: false): the default limits brought 15 values above 180 minutes down to 180, and they are real answers. Components. The duration (component 3) is delivered as stored. The latency (2), the efficiency (4), the disturbances (5) and the daytime dysfunction (7) are computed here by functions of custom.py from the items, and the stored component is the check. The stored latency and efficiency use the minutes and the bedtime as typed: the latency differs on 15 visits and the efficiency on 104 (the 109 visits with a bedtime written on a 12-hour clock are corrected here; D43, BP D132), and the stored total is higher than ours on 106. 35 stored totals have no recomputed total (an item is missing), 26 stored latency components none (the 26 durations written like a time are unparsed) and 13 stored efficiencies none (11 visits with the same bedtime and rising time, so no hours in bed, and 2 with the hours of sleep out of range): score_not_recomputed. The delivered bedtime (psqi_bedtime, a score of custom.py) is corrected as in BP: the 109 bedtimes typed on a 12-hour clock get 12 hours, and the 20 bedtimes typed 24:00 become 0, as the BP export writes them (the SZ form has no 24-hour warning: A75 of docs/EXPORT_REQUESTS.md). The bedtime as typed is read as psqi_bedtime_typed and not delivered; the efficiency reads it, with the same 12-hour test, and does not change. Two bedtimes stay out_of_range, as every time above 24 hours: one of 24:30 and one of 30:xx (decision of the user, 2026-11-21, which reverses the "as typed" part of D43). Disturbances and a blank 5j. The component adds the items 5b to 5j. Item 5j (another reason, how often) is blank on 70 visits, against 12 to 39 for each of the other items of question 5. The score step of the export is a strict sum of 5b to 5j and its definition lists the SZ table, so the stored component is empty on the 45 visits whose items 5b to 5i are answered and 5j is blank. The package reads a blank 5j as 0 and computes the component there: 45 more components and 35 more totals. Where the stored component exists, ours equals it (no score_mismatch). The published scoring sheet counts a missing 5j as 0 (instruction of Buysse dated 20 May 2005; BP schema), as the package does. The text of the other reason (psqi05k) is shown only after a 5j of 1, 2 or 3 (shown_if): none of its 608 texts is hidden. The SZ extraction also holds the questions about the bed partner, which BP does not have: psqi10 (none, or a partner in the same room or bed, 0 to 3) and psqi10a to psqi10d (the dictionary does not list them), shown by the form only when psqi10 is 1, 2 or 3 (shown_if; no cell is hidden in SZ). They are delivered and are not part of the score. The column psqi10e of SZ holds the free text of "other restlessness" only: it is called psqi10f here, as the text of the same question is in the DR and ASP schemas, where psqi10e is the 0 to 3 answer of that question. Not loaded: psqi15 and psqi16, copies of items 6 and 7 on every row (ignored.yaml), as in BP. The form's box "done / not done" (rad_psqi_nf) is not in the extraction (export request R152).
sz.difference: the SZ extraction also holds the questions about the bed partner (psqi10 and psqi10a to psqi10d, and the free text of the other restlessness in the column psqi10e, named psqi10f as in DR and ASP), each shown only when psqi10 is 1 to 3

dr.notes: The BP schema, plus the questions on the bed partner. Sleep over the last 30 days. Four questions ask for a time or a duration, the others are rated 0 to 3. Seven component scores of 0 to 3 add up to the total (0 to 21, higher is worse). Filled at inclusion and at every follow-up visit: 1,084 visits. Times. Bedtime, rising time and hours of sleep are written HH:MM:SS here (HH:MM in BP) and delivered in hours (23:30:00 is 23.5). One bedtime cannot be read (unparsed). A rising time of 00:00:00 is the default of the time widget saved untouched, not an answer: it is a missing code (not_recorded; A75) on 39 visits, and the efficiency and the total are then missing on 3 visits. A bedtime of 00:00:00 is a real answer. A bedtime after midnight is a small number (00:30 is 0.5). The delivered bedtime (psqi_bedtime, a score of custom.py) is corrected as in BP: the 19 bedtimes typed on a 12-hour clock get 12 hours (see the efficiency below), and the 7 typed 24:00:00 become 0, as the BP export writes them (decision of the user, 2026-11-21). The bedtime as typed is read as psqi_bedtime_typed and not delivered (its one unparsed cell is flagged there). The median and the year and centre panels of the bedtime still mix bedtimes before and after midnight: read the efficiency and the hours of sleep. Minutes to fall asleep (psqi02): the BP rule. A value above 240 is the minutes multiplied by 60 and is divided by 60 (unit_inferred, 1 visit). Not winsorised (the 99th percentile would bring 7 real answers down). Components. As in BP: quality is item 6 and medication is item 7, so their copies (psqi15, psqi16) are not read (ignored.yaml); the duration is delivered as stored; latency, efficiency, disturbances and daytime dysfunction are recomputed by the functions of custom.py and compared with the stored values. The stored components and the stored total are the export's (nucleus psqi.yaml, strict sums). Latency (psqi_latency): from the corrected minutes and item 5a; the stored component differs on the one visit with the corrected minutes. Efficiency (psqi_efficiency): hours of sleep over the hours in bed, counted across midnight. A bedtime from 6:00 to 17:00 with more than 16 hours in bed is a bedtime typed on a 12-hour clock, and 12 hours are added (19 visits). The stored efficiency takes the bedtime as typed: it differs from ours on 17 of these 19 visits, and the stored total on the same visits (the total differs on 17 visits: 16 of these and the visit of the latency). The script of the form (192_score.js, lines 165 to 196) takes the absolute difference between the two clock times, which is wrong across midnight (16 hours in bed from 23:00 to 07:00; A74); the stored values of this extraction are the export's, which counts across midnight, so they are not the script's. Disturbances (psqi_disturbances): the export needs item 5j ("another reason", with its free text 5k) and leaves the component empty when 5j is blank, on 19 visits that have 5b to 5i. A blank 5j is far commoner than any other blank item and reads as "no other reason": it counts 0 here and the component is delivered on those 19 visits (and the total on 18). This is the published rule: since 2005 the scoring instructions count 5j as 0 when its value or its comment is missing (PSQI scoring sheet, University of Pittsburgh). Daytime dysfunction (psqi_dysfunction): items 8 and 9, as stored. More than BP: question 10, on a bed partner or room mate (psqi10, 0 none to 3 in the same bed), and what this person noticed (psqi10a to psqi10e, each 0 to 3, psqi10f the free text of "other restlessness"). They do not enter the total. They are shown only after a bed partner is declared (1 to 3): the 171 cells of the five ratings filled on the 35 visits that answer "none" (34 or 35 per rating) and 3 cells of the text are not shown (not_shown); the text 5k is shown only after an answer 1 to 3 to item 5j (1 cell). In this extraction psqi10e is the rating of "other restlessness" and psqi10f its free text; in FACE SZ the column psqi10e holds the free text, delivered under the name psqi10f as here. The break of 2018 (open question O1, answered by D55). 96% and 93% of the inclusion visits of 2012 to 2014 and of 2015 to 2017 hold the scale, 40% to 52% in the three periods since 2018. The form (192) is in none of the lists of the simplified visit: an empty scale since 2018 is "not asked" on a simplified visit, not "no", and it is missing data here, never 0. The extraction has no flag that tells a simplified visit from a full one with an empty scale (R127, R139, R155).
dr.difference: the questions on the bed partner (psqi10, psqi10a to psqi10f) are in this extraction and not in BP, and are shown only after a bed partner (shown_if); a rising time of 00:00:00, the default of the time widget saved untouched, is a missing code; the times are written HH:MM:SS

asp.notes: Sleep over the last 30 days (the wording of items 1 to 9 and of the partner items on the form). Nineteen questions, five questions about the bed partner, seven component scores and a total, filled by adults: 162 inclusion visits (1 of children) and 44 follow-up visits, from 2009 to 2021 (202 of the 206 from 2013). It belongs to the old set of forms; the Epworth scale is the sleep questionnaire of the new set. Same instrument as in FACE BP, SZ and DR, in other columns, delivered under the same names. The hours of sleep (item 4) are a whole number here: the field of the form takes two digits, where BP, SZ and DR write hours and minutes, so the efficiency is coarser. On 8 visits the rising time is 00:00:00, the bedtime of the same visits is 00:00:00 too and no hours of sleep are typed: the rising time is the untouched default of the time field and is read as missing (not_recorded); the bedtime of these visits is delivered as written (midnight is a possible answer). The delivered bedtime (psqi_bedtime, a score of custom.py) is corrected as in BP: the 5 bedtimes typed on a 12-hour clock (a bedtime from 6:00 to 17:00 with more than 16 hours in bed, the test of the efficiency) get 12 hours and the 2 typed 24:00:00 become 0, as the BP export writes them (decision of the user, 2026-11-21). The bedtime as typed is read as psqi_bedtime_typed and not delivered; the efficiency reads it. Here the seven components are stored, and each was checked against the published rule: - component 1 (quality) and component 6 (medication) are the items 6 and 7: the two stored columns are copies (ignored.yaml); - component 2 (latency): right, 188 of 188 visits; - component 3 (duration): the stored score counts 0 from 7 hours, 1 at 6, 2 at 5 and 3 below (192 of 192 visits). The publication says 0 above 7 hours and does not settle exactly 7 hours. Delivered as stored, as in the other cohorts (BP decision D93); - **component 4 (efficiency) is wrong when the patient goes to bed before midnight.** The script of the form takes the hours in bed as the absolute difference of the two clock times, without crossing midnight (191 of 192 visits reproduced): a night from 23:00 to 07:00 counts sixteen hours in bed. The stored component is 3 on 90 of the 104 visits with a bedtime before midnight. It equals the published rule on 101 of 192 visits only; - **component 5 (disturbances) is 3 as soon as one disturbance is reported**: the script joins the answers 5b to 5j as text ("0" then "1" make "01", and the string is compared with 0, 9 and 18; 182 of 183 visits reproduced), so 95 visits whose sum of the items 5b to 5j is from 1 to 9, which counts 1, and 63 from 10 to 18, which counts 2, hold a 3. Published rule: 25 of 183 visits. The script leaves the component empty when 5j is blank (17 visits have 5b to 5i and no 5j); the function psqi_disturbances counts a blank 5j as 0, the published rule (since 2005 the PSQI scoring sheet of the University of Pittsburgh counts 5j as 0 when its value or its comment is missing); - **component 7 (daytime dysfunction) does not follow its two items** (published rule: 103 of 201 visits): the script joins the answers of the items 8 and 9 as text ("1" then "2" make "12"), so it is right only when the item 8 is 0 and it is 0 as soon as the item 8 is 1 or more (200 of 201 visits reproduced); it is 0 on 69 visits where the two items add up to 3 or more. The stored total is the sum of the seven stored components (172 of 172 visits) and carries the three errors. The components 4, 5 and 7 are therefore computed with the published rules (functions psqi_efficiency, psqi_disturbances and psqi_dysfunction) and delivered, and the total is their sum with the four others; the stored values are read to be compared (score_mismatch) and are not delivered. In FACE BP, SZ and DR the stored components 4, 5 and 7 follow the published rules where they are filled (decision D22 in PROGRESS.md): the errors of these three components are those of the ASP form only. On 1 visit (2018) an item is blank and the latency component and the total are stored: they cannot be recomputed and are not delivered (`score_not_recomputed`). **Year and centre.** 16 of the 32 variables reach 0.5 or more (14 by year, 9 by centre); the patients are adults, 176 of the 204 visits with an item are of centre D and 25 of E. Six are scores. The bedtime (median 20.8 hours in 2014, 22 in 2018, 2.75 in 2019, 3.5 in 2020) is a clock time that wraps at midnight: 25% to 57% of the bedtimes of a year (8 visits or more) are before 06:00 (41 of the 206 are exactly 00:00:00), and the median jumps between evening and night when that share crosses a half (52% in 2019, 54% in 2020); counted past 24 hours the median is 23 to 24 in every year with 8 visits or more (measured on the bedtimes as typed; A2-11, the 24:00:00 bedtimes, is decided: they become 0). The latency, efficiency, disturbances and dysfunction components are whole numbers from 0 to 3 whose median moves by one unit, and the hours of sleep move from 7 to 8 in 2019. The disturbances component is higher in 2020 (mean 1.74 against 1.12 to 1.44 in 2013 to 2019) and in centre E (1.80 against 1.29 in D), small groups (34 and 25 visits) that differ beyond chance (permutation test, p below 0.01); the total (median 8, 7, 6, 8 in 2014, 2018, 2019, 2020) is within chance. No step with a form cause.
asp.difference: other columns; the seven components are stored, and the components 4, 5 and 7 are wrong (the hours in bed do not cross midnight, a 3 as soon as one disturbance is reported), so they are recomputed with the published rules and the stored ones are only compared; the hours of sleep are a number, not a clock time

psqi.description: Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index. The patient describes the sleep of the last 30 days. Four questions ask for a time or a duration, the others are rated 0 to 3. Seven components of 0 to 3 add up to the total.
psqi.version: 19 questions and 7 components; the questions on the bed partner are asked in SZ, DR and ASP only
psqi.reference: Buysse DJ, Reynolds CF, Monk TH, Berman SR, Kupfer DJ. Psychiatry Res 1989;28:193-213 (PMID 2748771)
sources: schema notes (bp, sz, dr, asp psqi)
flags: Components 2, 4, 5 and 7 and the total are recomputed with the published rules in the four cohorts. The stored ones are checks and differ on some visits (725 stored BP totals).
A blank item 5j counts 0, as on the published scoring sheet since 2005.
Exactly 7 hours of sleep count 0 in the duration component, as in the application. The published sheet leaves 7 hours open.
psqi_bedtime is a clock time. A bedtime after midnight is a small number, so a higher value is not simply a later bedtime.
In DR an empty PSQI since 2018 can be 'not asked' (simplified visit). In ASP the form belongs to the old set (2009 to 2021, adults) and the hours of sleep are whole numbers.

common.note: Seven components of 0 to 3 and their sum, on the same rules in the four cohorts, over the last 30 days; components 1 and 6 are the answers to questions 6 and 7 (psqi06, psqi07). Components 2, 4, 5 and 7 are recomputed with the published rules in the four cohorts. A blank item 5j (other reason for waking) counts 0 in the four cohorts: it is a blank in the export's score (BP 108, SZ 45, DR 19 and ASP 17 visits); 0 is the published rule (since 2005 the PSQI scoring sheet of the University of Pittsburgh counts 5j as 0 when its value or its comment is missing). In ASP the EMR script is wrong for components 4, 5 and 7 (an absolute difference of the two times, and answers added as text). Exactly 7 hours of sleep count 0: the application tests "7 hours or more", where the published sheet says "more than 7 hours" and leaves 7 hours open; the four cohorts do the same. Bedtimes typed on a 12-hour clock are delivered as typed (BP 554 visits, SZ 109, DR 19, ASP 5). The partner questions are asked in SZ, DR and ASP only. In ASP the PSQI belongs to the old set of forms (2009 to 2021, adults). In DR the simplified visit of 2018 onward does not offer it: it is on nine inclusions in ten to 2017 and about one in two since 2018.

qids_sr16.title: Quick Inventory of Depressive Symptomatology, self-report (QIDS-SR16), last 7 days

bp.notes: Sixteen items, each 0 to 3, on the last seven days. Filled at 89% to 96% of the visits other than the screening visit, in every period (89% in 2022-23, 91% from 2024), and at 66% of the screening visits (2,622 of 3,987: the application gives the screening visit a QIDS of its own, D90). Total. The sixteen items cover nine symptoms, and the total adds one value per symptom (0 to 27): the highest of the four sleep items (1 to 4), item 5, the highest of the four appetite and weight items (6 to 9), items 10 to 14, and the highest of the two psychomotor items (15 and 16). This is not a sum: hidden scores take the highest of each group (qids_sleep, qids_appetite_weight, qids_psychomotor) and the total adds the nine values, all in the schema. The stored total (qidsr120) is written by the score step of the export (D120; a maximum that needs every item of its group), not by the application. It is exactly ours in every row where it exists (19,331), so stored and recomputed agree on the items and on the export's formula; it is stored only when the sixteen items are filled. One answer of each pair is enough. The form asks for item 6 or item 7 (appetite down or up) and for item 8 or item 9 (weight down or up), not for both. On 99 visits, spread over all the years, the patient did so, and the export stores no total. Ours is computed there (19,430 totals against 19,331): the highest of the appetite and weight items that are answered. The other twelve items must all be filled. The rule was found in FACE DR, where the form is filled this way on most visits from 2022.

dr.notes: The BP schema as it is. Sixteen items, each 0 to 3, on the last seven days (the two weight items on the last 15 days, as the form prints them). Filled at the screening visit (72% of them), at inclusion (91%) and at every follow-up visit (92% to 96%): 1,902 visits, and still 83% of the inclusions of 2024 to 2026. The form (126) is on the four lists of the simplified visit, so the break of 2018 does not touch it. Level: the DR totals are higher than in BP (mean 15.1 against 9.4), as expected in a cohort of treatment-resistant depression; the item profiles agree with BP, so it is not a difference of coding. Total. The sixteen items cover nine symptoms, and the total adds one value per symptom (0 to 27): the highest of the four sleep items (1 to 4), item 5, the highest of the four appetite and weight items (6 to 9), items 10 to 14, and the highest of the two psychomotor items (15 and 16). It is written in the schema with hidden maxima (qids_sleep, qids_appetite_pair, qids_weight_pair, qids_appetite_weight, qids_psychomotor), no function of custom.py. The stored total (qidsr120) is exactly this on the 1,643 visits where it exists: the visits with the sixteen items filled. One answer of each pair is enough. The form asks for item 6 or item 7 (appetite down or up) and for item 8 or item 9 (weight down or up), not for both. Until 2021 nearly every visit answers the four (1% to 3% of the visits answer one of each pair, 7% in 2017). From 2022 the patients do as the form asks: 26% of the QIDS visits of 2022, 47% in 2023, 64% in 2024, 58% in 2025 and 74% in 2026 (of the visits with the twelve other items filled), in 8 of the 10 centres that have ten QIDS visits or more since 2022. On these 227 visits the EMR stores no total, and the cause is the export: the score definition (nucleus qids.yaml, lines 19 to 30 and 46 to 60) takes the highest of each block in strict mode, so a blank answer of a pair blanks the total, whereas the script of the form (126_score.js, lines 35 to 45) sets the unanswered partner of an item to 0 and computes the total. Ours follows the script (the highest answered of each pair, at least one answer): 1,870 totals, the twelve other items being filled. Without this the total would be missing for most recent visits (open question O13; requests R147 and R155). The export takes no selector of the form (QIDS6A, QIDS8A), and the form's own rule that clears the weight details (formulaires.js, line 3965) names the wrong block when QIDS8A is 2 (2 visits show an answer that the form hides: A77).

qids_sr16.description: Quick Inventory of Depressive Symptomatology, self-report. Sixteen items, each rated by the patient from 0 to 3, on the last seven days. They cover nine symptoms of depression.
qids_sr16.reference: Rush AJ, Trivedi MH, Ibrahim HM, et al. Biol Psychiatry 2003;54:573-583 (PMID 12946886)
qids_sr16.period: last 7 days (the two weight items: last 15 days)
flags: One answer of each pair is enough: appetite down or up (items 6, 7) and weight down or up (items 8, 9). The package then computes a total that the export leaves empty (99 BP and 227 DR visits).
The total is not the sum of the sixteen items.
The DR totals are higher than in BP (mean 15.1 against 9.4), as expected in resistant depression; it is not a difference of coding.
No French validation paper was found ('To verify'). No cut-off is used in the code.

common.note: Sixteen items and a total of 0 to 27 over the last seven days, computed by the same YAML rule in both cohorts (the highest answer of each of the three multi-item symptoms; one answer of each appetite and weight pair is enough). The package delivers 99 BP and 227 DR totals that the export leaves empty (its strict maximum). Filled at the screening visit and at the inclusion visit in both. The DR level (QIDS about 6 points above BP) follows the clinical severity, not a different coding.

stai_ya.title: State-Trait Anxiety Inventory, form Y-A (state anxiety right now, 20 items)

bp.notes: Twenty items on how the patient feels right now (state anxiety, not the trait). Filled at 89% to 95% of the visits other than the screening visit, in every period (89% in 2019-21 and 2022-23, 91% from 2024); none of the 3,987 screening visits holds it. The items are stored 1 to 4 (1 = no, 4 = yes). The dictionary says 0 to 3; no cell holds a 0. Ten items describe calm (1, 2, 5, 8, 10, 11, 15, 16, 19 and 20) and are reversed in the total (5 - value), so that a higher total is more anxiety. The total goes from 20 to 80. The stored total (staya) is written by the score step of the export (D120), not by the application, and is exactly this sum in every row where both exist (16,678): it checks the items and the export's formula.

dr.notes: The BP scale, with the answers brought to one coding first. Twenty items on how the patient feels right now (state anxiety, form Y-A), four levels each. Filled at inclusion and at every follow-up visit: 1,076 visits. The form (133) has no display rule of its own: it is offered at every visit except on a simplified visit (below). Three codings in the same columns. BP stores the answers 1 to 4. This extraction stores them 0 to 3, 1 to 4 or 2 to 5, and no column says which. A visit tells its own coding when it holds a 0, a 5, or both a 1 and a 4: 655 visits are coded 0 to 3 (ten centres, 2012 to 2024), 184 are coded 1 to 4 (ten centres, 2012 to 2026) and 100 are coded 2 to 5 (one centre, 2013 to 2021). The 137 other visits could be read two ways (answers from 1 to 3, or from 2 to 4). The coding belongs to the centre and the year: of the 110 centre-years with a visit that tells its coding, 108 have one coding only. So a visit that cannot tell takes the coding of its centre in the same year, when there is only one and its answers fit: 133 visits. The function stai_shift of custom.py does this and gives the number to add (staya_shift: +1, 0 or -1), known on 1,072 visits; on the 4 others the items are not delivered. What is delivered. The stored answers (stayaNN_stored) are read and not delivered. staya01 to staya20 are the answers on the BP coding, 1 to 4 (1 = no, 4 = yes): the stored answer plus the shift. After the shift the mean of the items is the same in the three codings (2.23, 2.18 and 2.24), which supports the shift. The level of the DR totals (about 11 points above BP) is clinical, as for the QIDS, not a difference of coding. Total. Ten items describe calm (1, 2, 5, 8, 10, 11, 15, 16, 19 and 20) and are reversed, so that a higher total is more anxiety (20 to 80). With ten items counted as they are and ten reversed, the total does not depend on the coding: it is computed from the stored answers, also where the coding is not known. The stored total (staya) equals it on the 1,065 visits where the twenty items are filled, whatever the coding (open question O16). The break of 2018 (open question O1, answered by D55). 96% and 91% of the inclusion visits of 2012 to 2014 and of 2015 to 2017 hold the scale, 43% to 49% in the three periods since 2018. The form (133) is in none of the lists of the simplified visit: an empty scale since 2018 is "not asked" on a simplified visit, not "no", and it is missing data here, never 0. The extraction has no flag that tells a simplified visit from a full one with an empty scale (R127, R139, R155).
dr.difference: the answers are stored on three codings (0 to 3, 1 to 4, 2 to 5); they are read as stored, not delivered, and delivered on the BP coding once the coding of the visit is known

asp.notes: Twenty items and a total, about how the patient feels right now (state anxiety), at the inclusion visit: 579 visits, from 2018 to 2026, and 8 follow-up visits (587 in all). It belongs to the new set of forms. It is filled by adults only. The children fill the STAIC. Same instrument as in FACE BP and DR, in the same columns. The answers are stored from 0 to 3 on every visit of this cohort, where the published form counts from 1 to 4: the schema of FACE DR, which reads the coding from the answers of the visit and delivers the items from 1 to 4, is used as it is. The total does not depend on the coding. **Year and centre.** 14 of the 21 variables reach 0.5 or more (14 by year, 13 by centre): the 20 items are on a four-level scale (one level is 1.0 or more of the interquartile range). The total stands at 0.20 by year and 0.15 by centre (median 45 to 53 by year, 46 to 51 by centre). Adults only, 2021 to 2026. No step.

The item entries carry no single direction, because ten items describe calm and ten describe anxiety.
No universal cut-off. The bands of the French manual are 'To verify' in the literature notes.

stop_bang.title: STOP-BANG, risk of obstructive sleep apnoea

bp.notes: First filled in November 2020 (1 visit), then in 2021 (67 visits); regular from 2022 (719 to 962 visits a year to 2025). Seven yes/no questions (1 = yes): snoring, tiredness, observed apnoea, blood pressure, body mass index above 35, age above 50, neck size. The eighth criterion is male sex; its column (apnee08) is filled on two visits only and is not read (ignored.yaml). The risk class is delivered as the EMR wrote it. It is the rule of the application, not the published count: the seven questions are added without male sex; high from 5 of them, or from 2 of the first 4 with male sex, a body mass index above 35 or a large neck; intermediate from 3; low below. It differs from the published rule (male sex counted in the total) on 182 of the 3,939 visits that have a sex and a class (4.6%; 175 are men), mostly men with 2 criteria shown as low (159). On 26 visits the stored class does not follow the application's own rule (score computed on a click, D106), and it is empty on 89 of the 4,032 visits that answer the seven questions (51 other visits hold a class and miss a question). The class stays the application's, as the project lead decided (D134); the published rule is given here to be compared. stopbang_count7 is the number of the seven criteria met (add 1 for male sex for the published total of 0 to 8): it is computed from the answers and does not depend on the click. A few cells hold "d?AOS": the apostrophe was damaged by the export.

stop_bang.description: STOP-BANG questionnaire on the risk of obstructive sleep apnoea. Seven yes/no questions answered by the patient (snoring, tiredness, observed apnoea, blood pressure, body mass index above 35, age above 50, neck size), and a risk class written by the EMR.

wurs25.title: Wender Utah Rating Scale, 25 items (WURS-25), recall of childhood

bp.notes: WURS-61 and WURS-25 are two instruments. The 25-item WURS-25 replaced the 61-item WURS (confirmed by the developers of the EMR, decision D47 in PROGRESS.md). Its 25 questions are 25 of the 61, and the extraction stores both in the same columns. This schema reads those columns on the visits where the 25-item questionnaire was filled. Nothing in the WURS columns says which form a visit used; it is read from the ALS and the BIS of the same visit: "wurs25" when the visit holds ALS or BIS answers and nothing that only the long questionnaires have. wurs61.yaml reads the other visits and explains the rule and its limit. Both files carry the same version block. Filled once, at the inclusion visit: symptoms of attention deficit and hyperactivity in childhood. Each item is 0 (not at all) to 4 (very much). Item names. The EMR kept the numbers that the questions have in the 61-item questionnaire: wurs25_03 is the question numbered 3 there. The 25-item form shows the questions in the rising order of these numbers and prints the numbers themselves (3, 4, 5 ... 59) (read in the application in November 2026; decision D97 in PROGRESS.md). The stored total (wurs) equals the sum of the 25 items (0 to 100) in all 6,082 rows where both exist (the export's score step writes it, D120). Before 2021. The data managers found no visit with only the reduced questionnaires before 2021, and advise not to deliver the questionnaires of a visit that looks like one (decision D71 in PROGRESS.md). The version block says so (since): a visit dated before 2021 that would be read here has no form, gets version_unknown, and its answers are not delivered. 8 visits, dated 2018 to 2020, each with its 25 answers; als18.yaml says what they look like.

sz.notes: Wender Utah Rating Scale, the 25-item form, a recall of childhood: 305 visits from 2012 (285 at inclusion, 125 dated before 2021), 295 of them with the 25 items. The questions are numbered as in the 61-item questionnaire (wurs25_03 is the question numbered 3 there, as in BP). The stored sum (wurstot) equals the sum of the items on all 295. Which form? The SZ form is the 25-item form only: its group is named "Echelle WURS 25", its table holds exactly the 25 items numbered 3 to 59, the score step of the export has a WURS-25 entry for the SZ table, and the SZ application has no 61-item questionnaire (the open question O9 is answered). In FACE BP the 61-item form was used until 2021 and the two forms share columns, so BP has two schemas (wurs25 and wurs61) split by the ALS and BIS answers of the visit; SZ needs no split and no ALS or BIS to read it. Who is asked. The WURS is not a questionnaire of every patient: 285 of the 2,353 inclusion visits have it. It follows the screening question on attention deficit hyperactivity disorder asked at inclusion (adhd_symptoms_v0): 240 of the 285 inclusion visits with a WURS have a yes to it (84%), and 240 of the 309 yes have a WURS (78%). Its mean is that of a selected group, not of the cohort. The form's box "done / not done" (rad_wurs_nf) is not in the extraction (export request R152).
sz.difference: the SZ form is the 25-item form only, so there is no version block (BP splits wurs25 and wurs61 by the ALS and BIS answers of the visit), and the stored total is in the column wurstot

wurs25.description: Wender Utah Rating Scale, 25-item form. The adult patient recalls symptoms of attention deficit and hyperactivity in childhood. Each item is 0 (not at all) to 4 (very much).
wurs25.reference: Ward MF, Wender PH, Reimherr FW. Am J Psychiatry 1993;150:885-890 (PMID 8494063)
flags: In BP the form of a visit is not recorded: it is read from the ALS and the BIS of the same visit (an assumption). Not to be mixed with wurs61_sum25.
BP visits dated before 2021 that look like the 25-item form are not delivered (version_unknown).
In SZ the scale follows a screening question on ADHD, so its mean is that of a selected group, not of the cohort.
That the 25 items have no reversed item is 'To verify' in the literature notes. The application reverses none.

common.note: The 25 items of the ADHD subset, 0 to 4, total 0 to 100, in the same names in BP and SZ. BP also has the 61-item form (wurs61, until 2021; the 25 shared items are delivered as wurs61_NN and as the sum wurs61_sum25), which is another instrument. The SZ form is the 25-item form only (its table, its menu and its score definition say WURS 25). In SZ the questionnaire is asked of a selected group (the application reminds it only when the diagnosis form says ADHD): 12% of the inclusion visits, 78% of those with ADHD yes, against 93% of the BP inclusions.

wurs61.title: Wender Utah Rating Scale, 61 items (WURS-61), recall of childhood

bp.notes: WURS-61 and WURS-25 are two instruments. The 61-item WURS was filled until 2021; the 25-item WURS-25 replaced it (confirmed by the developers of the EMR, decision D47 in PROGRESS.md). The 25 questions of the WURS-25 are 25 of the 61, and the extraction stores both in the same columns. The columns are therefore split by form: this schema reads the visits where the 61-item questionnaire was filled, wurs25.yaml reads the others. Both files carry the same version block. Which form a visit used. Nothing in the WURS columns says it: the 25 items and their sum are stored alike in both forms. The form is read from the other self-questionnaires of the same visit, because the reduced questionnaires replaced the long ones together (99% of the visits that have an ALS and a BIS have the two in the same generation). A visit is "wurs61" when it holds something that only the long questionnaires have: a score of the 54-item ALS (als58 or als60) or one of the 22 items that only the 34-item BIS-10 has. It is "wurs25" when it holds ALS or BIS answers and none of those. This rests on the WURS having changed at the same moment as the ALS and the BIS in each centre, which the WURS columns cannot confirm. A visit with a WURS and neither an ALS nor a BIS (49 visits) has no form: version_unknown, and its answers are not delivered. A visit dated before 2021 is never read as the 25-item form (since, in the version block): wurs25.yaml says why. Filled once, at the inclusion visit: symptoms of attention deficit and hyperactivity in childhood. Each item is 0 (not at all) to 4 (very much). What the extraction holds. Only the 25 items that the WURS-25 also has, out of 61; the 36 others were not exported. wurs61_03 is item 3 of the 61-item questionnaire. The data managers confirmed in November 2026 (decision D67 in PROGRESS.md) that the patients filled the 61 items until 2021 (2022 in two centres), that the 36 other items are still in the source database, and that no field records the form of a visit: the rule above stays an assumption until the export names the form. Bridge to the WURS-25: wurs61_sum25 is the sum of these 25 items (0 to 100), the score that the WURS has always used. The stored total (wurs) equals it in every row where both exist. Whether an answer given inside a 61-item questionnaire can be compared with the same question asked in a 25-item one is a scientific choice; the two are delivered as separate columns (wurs61_sum25 here, wurs25_total there) so that nobody mixes them by accident. From July 2021 to June 2022, when both forms were in use, the two sums have the same mean (35.5 and 35.5).

wurs61.description: Wender Utah Rating Scale, 61-item form, filled by the patient once, at the inclusion visit, until 2021. A recall of symptoms of attention deficit and hyperactivity in childhood, each item 0 (not at all) to 4 (very much). Only the 25 items that the WURS-25 also has are in the extraction.
wurs61.reference: Ward MF, Wender PH, Reimherr FW. Am J Psychiatry 1993;150:885-890 (PMID 8494063)
flags: Only 25 of the 61 items are exported. A total of the 61 items is not in the extraction.
wurs61_sum25 and wurs25_total are separate columns: whether an answer given inside a 61-item questionnaire can be compared with the same question in a 25-item one is a scientific choice.
Which form a visit used is read from the ALS and the BIS of the same visit. This stays an assumption until the export names the form; a visit with neither is not delivered.

bhcg_prolactine.title: Beta-hCG and prolactin

bp.notes: How the units are read (the same in every schema of this tab). The unit column is filled by the form with a default label, also where there is no result, so it proves little. Each analyte lists the units that occur, with the values one expects on each scale. A value that fits its label keeps it. A value that cannot be on the labelled scale and fits exactly one other is converted and flagged (unit_inferred, or unit_doubt when it was possible but unlikely under its label). A value that fits no scale is left as it is and the hard range decides (out_of_range). Beta-hCG is a pregnancy test: of 3,768 results, 2,094 (56%) are a detection limit, 2,039 written "<" and 55 with the mark in the unit column ("inf") and the limit in the result column. The limits run from 0.1 to 12, the commonest being 2 (898 results), 5 (406) and 1 (377). 7 results are ">". 420 are 0 (419 typed 0 and one "<0") and are delivered as 0. 24 rows carry a word in the unit column ("negatif", "enceinte", "inferieur", "nf"...) and none of them holds a result: they are empty. Men give 86 results. A hCG above 25 (37 visits) goes with a high prolactin: 15 of these visits have a prolactin typed and 11 deliver one, with a median of 32 ng/mL against 11 for all results. Prolactin: a 0 is "nothing measured", not a result (19 cells, now a missing code instead of out_of_range; decision D130). Prolactin (decision D31 in PROGRESS.md). The results are on two scales, ng/mL (µg/L is the same number) and mUI/L (1 ng/mL = 21.2 mUI/L). They overlap between about 30 and 500: a value there can be a high prolactin in ng/mL (under antipsychotics) or an ordinary one in mUI/L. The extraction has the unit column of the form (prolctn_lborresu) and the unit choice itself (rad_prolactine, not read). They agree wherever a unit was chosen. On 4,682 of the 6,567 results the unit column holds the form's default label, "mg/L" (295 of them have it chosen, A23 in EXPORT_REQUESTS.md, with a median of 12.7: ng/mL values). The results under that label are on the ng/mL or the mUI/L scale, with one exception (below), so the label is ignored (ignore_units). A chosen unit is believed (1,885 results): ng/mL or µg/L up to 500, mUI/L from 30 on. The 34 results of 100 and more written in ng/mL or µg/L stay as they are; 31 of them are women's, as one expects of a truly high prolactin. Where no unit was chosen, the function prolactin_unit of custom.py decides: - under 0.2, the result is mg/L (44, see below); from 0.2 to 30, ng/mL (3,770, among them 3 under 0.5 that end out_of_range); from 500 on, mUI/L (73); - in between, the centre's other results within 180 days decide. In ng/mL 2 results in 100 reach 100. Where a quarter or more of them do, the centre was reporting in mUI/L: a result of 100 to 500 is mUI/L (250), and one of 30 to 100 cannot be told (35); - elsewhere a result of 30 to 100 is ng/mL (350), and one of 100 to 500 cannot be told (141). The 176 results that cannot be told are missing, with unit_unknown. Open question O20 in PROGRESS.md. Two checks of the rule. The centre with the most results reported in mUI/L during two periods, where its median as written is between 165 and 320; after the rule its median is between 9 and 15 in every half-year. And men are 38% of the 250 results read as mUI/L by the period, as among the 176 results labelled mUI/L (40%), against 9% of the 34 high results written in ng/mL and 17% of the 141 that cannot be told: those are a mixture. A result typed in mg/L (decision D144). 44 results under the label mg/L lie under 0.2: 43 from 0.0005 up, with three or four decimals for most of them, and one lower. They are ng/mL values written in the default unit (x1000: median 11 ng/mL; for the 22 whose patient has other results, 0.9 times the patient's median), and they were out_of_range as ng/mL. The function prolactin_unit answers mg/L for a result under 0.2, and the unit mg/L (factor 1000, expect 0.0005 to 0.2) reads it, with unit_inferred, since the label itself is ignored. 43 results are now delivered; the one under 0.0005 stays out_of_range (x1000 would be under 0.5). 3 results of 0.2 to 0.5 stay out_of_range as ng/mL: x1000 would be 200 to 500 ng/mL, above the 99th percentile of the cohort (88 ng/mL). They are left, not read as doubtful, since a result under an ignored label can only be unit_inferred. Shifted block and pool. This schema belongs to the pool biology (implausible_visits: 3, see biochimie): a visit with three or more impossible values over the seven laboratory schemas of BP loses all its values here too and gets visit_removed. The pool removes 29 visits in all (998 cells); this schema loses 14 cells on 12 visits (hCG 12, prolactin 2: 6 on the shifted block of one centre, 8 on other visits). None of the removed hCG is a 0, so the 420 zeros are still delivered, and none of the 4 block visits that escape the pool holds a result here. Winsorising (step 12) clips each number at its 1st and 99th percentile, so a clinical tail becomes the cut value (in BP an hCG above 22.2 UI/L, which is a pregnancy, is delivered as 22.2 and a prolactin above 88.5 ng/mL as 88.5: 38 and 126 values are clipped, so the delivered hCG tells positive or not, not the level), while the hard range ([0, 300000] for the hCG, [0.5, 500] for the prolactin) is what removes impossible values. Centre and year steps (qc site_shift and year_shift, read on 2026-11-19): the hCG median is 0 to 5 by centre and 0.1 to 2 by year (up to 3.0 and 1.9 IQR from the overall median of 2, IQR 1), with no unit involved, because each laboratory writes a negative result its own way: 56% of the results are detection limits ("<5" in the centre whose median is 5, "<2" in four others), 420 are typed 0 (37% of the results of one centre) and two centres type 0.1. A median or a mean of the hCG therefore measures a limit or a habit, not a level: it is read with hcg_cens and left as measured.

sz.notes: Prolactin, read like in FACE BP (the SZ extraction has no beta-hCG). The unit column holds mUI/L on 678 results (two of them misspelt) and ng/mL or µg/L on 718 (two misspelt). The form's default label mg/L, which nobody chose, is on the other 1,818 of the 3,214 results: that label is ignored, as in BP (decision D31 of the BP file), and a misspelt label counts as no label. 633 results are converted from mUI/L. Where no unit was chosen, the rule of BP (custom function prolactin_unit: the size of the value, then the other results of the centre at that time) reads 130 results as mUI/L and leaves 162 that fit both units (unit_unknown, missing). 36 results labelled mUI/L fit ng/mL better (unit_doubt). 15 are written with "<" (censored_left). Typed in mg/L: 56 results lie between 0.0007 and 0.19, all under the default label, 52 of them with three or four decimals (0.022 for 22 ng/mL). They are ng/mL written in mg/L: the unit mg/L (factor 1000, window 0.0005 to 0.2, as in BP) reads them, the rule prolactin_unit names it for a value under 0.2, and they get unit_inferred. Before, they were out of range. Their median is 13 ng/mL, against 15 for all results. Ten more lie between 0.2 and 0.5: 6 under the default label and 4 with a unit chosen on the form (3 ng/mL, 1 mUI/L). Read as mg/L they would be 235 to 490 ng/mL, where 6 of the 718 results labelled ng/mL are 200 or more: they are not converted and stay out of range. One more result is out of range (over 10,000, it fits no unit). The clip at the 1st and 99th percentile turns a clinical tail into the cut value (60 results here); the hard range, 0.5 to 500 ng/mL, is what removes impossible values. Same instrument as in FACE BP, with the SZ column of the result.
sz.difference: prolactin only, in the column prolctn; no beta-hCG

dr.notes: Beta-hCG and prolactin. Same instrument as in FACE BP, in the columns of the TRD extraction. Beta-hCG: 308 results, 276 delivered (one is above the hard range and 31 are on removed visits, see below), all of women: the 19 results of men were on those visits. 38 are written "<" a limit and keep their mark. 136 (49%) are 0, and 127 of the 136 come from three centres: a 0 is probably how these centres write a result below the detection limit, where BP writes "<" (56% of its 3,768 results are censored). The levels of the two cohorts are therefore not comparable at the low end. Prolactin: 683 results, 645 delivered. The form has a choice of unit, exported as a code: 1 is ng/mL (349 results), 2 µUI/mL (229), 3 µg/L (79), the same scale as ng/mL. Code 4, which the dictionary does not list, goes with a result of 0 on 7 visits, and 19 results have no code. A 0 is "nothing measured" (35 cells, a missing code since BP D130). 223 results are converted from mUI/L, 8 have a size that does not fit their label and are read in the other unit (unit_inferred), 1 is impossible (out_of_range). Two results below 0.2, typed in mg/L under the label µg/L, are read as mg/L and multiplied by 1,000, as in BP (no code of the form names mg/L: that unit is found by the size of the value). Open question for the centres. Under code 1, 66 of the 349 results are 100 or more (19%): 46 from one centre, 12 from another, 58 dated 2013 to 2015. The script of the application that fills the unit afterwards (script_unit.php) wrote code 1 on every result that had no unit chosen, so code 1 is not always a choice, and these results look like mUI/L typed under the first option. They are not converted, because nothing proves it. The delivered 95th percentile is 172 ng/mL against 43 in BP, and 8.0% of the men's results are 100 or more (BP 0%, SZ 0.8%): the upper tail of the prolactin of this cohort is not comparable with BP until the centres answer. Values are winsorised at the 1st and 99th percentiles (the hCG at the 99th only, its lower tail being censored): the tails become the cut values (5 IU/L for the 3 highest hCG, 1.9 and 363 ng/mL for 12 prolactin results), so a clinical tail turns into the cut value, and the hard ranges (0 to 300,000 IU/L and 0.5 to 500 ng/mL) remove the impossible values. A result above 5 IU/L is delivered as 5. Shifted block and pool. A block of results is shifted on the 30 visits of one centre, dated up to 2022 (see the blood-count schema): on the 23 of them whose unit field holds a number, the prolactin is 0 on 22 and the hCG is 0 on 21 (on the 30 visits, 29 and 28). This schema belongs to the pool biology (implausible_visits: 3, implausible_pool: biology; see the blood-count schema): a visit with three or more impossible values over the eleven laboratory schemas of DR loses all its values and gets visit_removed. The pool removes 35 visits in all (1,403 cells); this schema loses 33 cells on 32 visits: 30 hCG and 1 prolactin on the block visits (28 of the hCG are the 0 above, so a 0 typed in the shifted block is no longer delivered), and 1 hCG and 1 prolactin on other visits. The 0 of the prolactin is a missing code and was not delivered. Year step: the 26 results of 2013 have a median of 111 ng/mL against 12.1 for all (7.7 interquartile ranges, groups of 20 results or more); 14 of them are 100 or more (54%, against 33% of the 57 results of 2014, 24% of 83 in 2015 and 6% of 83 in 2016), which is the open question above, and without the results of 100 or more the yearly medians stay between 9.9 and 13.6 ng/mL from 2013 to 2026. The centre step (0.74) is the same results: 45 of the 124 results of that centre are 100 or more.
dr.difference: the results are in columns named for the analyte; the unit of prolactin is exported as a code (1 and 3 are ng/mL, 2 mUI/L, 4 is not in the dictionary), and a result typed in mg/L is found by its size

asp.notes: Prolactin, on 100 inclusion visits and 4 follow-up visits: the form asks for it only of the patients treated with antipsychotics. Same analyte, name and target unit (ng/mL) as in FACE SZ and DR; the beta-hCG is not in this extraction. Its unit column holds a catalogue number, which the list of the form names: 67306 (µg/L, ng/ml) on 86 results (median 12.55: ng/mL) and 67405 (µUI/ml, mUI/L) on 18 (median 164.45: mUI/L, the number that the TSH uses). The sizes agree with the form: 14 results are converted, and 4 are of the size of the other unit (unit_doubt on 3, unit_inferred on 1). No result is 0, the value that BP types where nothing was measured. The default clip at the 1% and 99% percentiles turns a clinical tail into the cut value (2 of the 104 values here); the hard range is what removes impossible values (none here).
asp.difference: prolactin only, with a unit column that holds catalogue numbers

bhcg_prolactine.description: Beta-hCG (a pregnancy test; BP and DR only) in UI/L and prolactin in ng/mL, from the blood sample of the visit.
sources: schema notes (bp, sz, dr, asp bhcg_prolactine)
flags: Beta-hCG: most results are a detection limit (56% in BP, marked in the censoring column hcg_cens) or a typed 0 (half of the DR results), written differently by each laboratory, and the upper tail is clipped. The delivered value tells positive or not, not the level.

Prolactin is typed in ng/mL or in mUI/L and the unit is often not chosen: the size of the value and the other results of the centre decide. 176 BP and 162 SZ results cannot be told and are missing (unit_unknown).
DR: results that look like mUI/L typed under the first unit option are not converted, so the upper tail of the DR prolactin is not comparable with BP.
ASP: prolactin is asked only of the patients treated with antipsychotics.

By default each number is clipped at its 1st and 99th percentiles (winsorising), so a clinical tail becomes the cut value; only the hard range removes impossible values. Load with winsorise=False to keep the tails.

common.note: Prolactin is in the four cohorts, in ng/mL (a value typed in mg/L in the default unit of the form is read x1000; the unit is unknown on about 3% of the BP and SZ results, which are not delivered). In DR the results labelled ng/mL reach 100 or more on 19% of the results of two centres in 2013-2015, probably mUI/L: open question. Beta-hCG is in BP and DR, mostly censored at the limit of the laboratory in BP: levels are not comparable, and a value in a man or in a pregnancy is not handled.

bilan_hepatique.title: Liver tests

bp.notes: How the units are read (the same in every schema of this tab). The unit column is filled by the form with a default label, also where there is no result, so it proves little. Each analyte lists the units that occur, with the values one expects on each scale. A value that fits its label keeps it. A value that cannot be on the labelled scale and fits exactly one other is converted and flagged (unit_inferred, or unit_doubt when it was possible but unlikely under its label). A value that fits no scale is left as it is and the hard range decides (out_of_range). Bilirubin in µmol/L and in mg/L are on almost the same scale (factor 1.71), so only the label can tell them apart: 184 results are labelled mg/L. The form also offers "mmol/L" (29 results, A24 in EXPORT_REQUESTS.md); a bilirubin of 7 mmol/L does not exist, so that label is read as µmol/L. 360 results are left-censored ("<8", "<3"). Alkaline phosphatase: 37 results between 0.2 and 5 are in µkat/L (1 µkat/L = 60 UI/L). A bilirubin of 0 is nothing measured, as for the prolactin (decision D130): 19 results, 18 of them in one centre in 2016 and 2017, are missing (missing code, not_recorded) in place of a delivered 0. A 0 of the ALT or the GGT (one each) was already out_of_range, because the hard range of the enzymes starts at 1: the delivered value is the same, missing. Shifted block and pool. This schema belongs to the pool biology (implausible_visits: 3, see biochimie): a visit with three or more impossible values over the seven laboratory schemas of BP loses all its values here too and gets visit_removed. The pool removes 29 visits in all (998 cells); this schema loses 123 cells on 27 visits (alkaline phosphatase 24, AST 25, ALT 25, bilirubin 23, GGT 26): 84 on 18 visits of the shifted block of one centre and 39 on 9 other visits. This schema alone would remove none: the 9 impossible values (including the 2 zeros above) are on 9 different visits. The 4 block visits that escape the pool (see biochimie) still deliver 19 values here. Winsorising (step 12) clips each number at its 1st and 99th percentile, so a clinical tail becomes the cut value (in BP an AST above 61 UI/L, an ALT above 99, a GGT above 176, an alkaline phosphatase above 135 and a bilirubin above 28 µmol/L are delivered as those values: 232 to 268 enzyme values and 125 bilirubin values are clipped), while the hard range ([1, 3000] for the transaminases and the GGT, [10, 1000] for the phosphatase, [0, 500] for the bilirubin) is what removes impossible values. Two bilirubin results carry a unit label that the schema does not know and a value that fits both µmol/L and mg/L: they are unit_unknown and delivered as missing.

dr.notes: Alkaline phosphatases, ASAT, ALAT, total bilirubin and gamma-GT, on about 1,170 visits. 7 alkaline phosphatases were typed on another scale (unit_inferred); 8 alkaline phosphatases and 1 ASAT are impossible; 6 results are given as "less than" a limit and keep their mark (3 ASAT, 2 ALAT, 1 bilirubin). The unit column of an analyte holds the default label of the form on every row that has any result of the tab (1,254 rows) and on no other, so it says nothing: the size of the value decides, as in BP and SZ. A 0 typed where nothing was measured is out of range. On the 30 visits of one centre whose block of results was typed in the wrong fields, shifted by seven fields of the eCEDR table (dated up to 2022, see the blood-count schema), the ASAT, ALAT, bilirubin and GGT have the size of a white-cell count, a red-cell count, a haemoglobin and a haematocrit. They fall inside their ranges (22, 22, 22 and 21 results, and 12 alkaline phosphatases) and would be delivered as results. This schema belongs to the pool biology (implausible_visits: 3, implausible_pool: biology; see the blood-count schema): a visit with three or more impossible values over the eleven laboratory schemas of DR loses all its values and gets visit_removed. The pool removes 35 visits in all (1,403 cells); this schema loses 124 cells on 27 visits: the 99 of the block, none of which is delivered any more, and 25 on 5 other visits. No visit holds more than one impossible value in this schema alone. The 1% and 99% winsorising turns a clinical tail into the cut value, and only the hard range removes impossible values. Centre step of the ASAT: one centre has a median of 28.5 UI/L against 21 for all (0.83 interquartile range, 90 results, groups of 20 results or more), and the ALAT (30.5 against 22) and the GGT (35 against 26) of the same centre are the highest of the centres too, so its patients or its method differ on the three enzymes; the cause is not known. Same instrument as in FACE BP.

asp.notes: Alkaline phosphatase, AST, ALT, bilirubin and GGT, on 485 inclusion visits and 49 follow-up visits. Same analytes, names, target units and ranges as in FACE DR. The cohort holds children: 37% of the 534 visits with a liver result are those of a patient under 18. Their alkaline phosphatase is that of growing bones, a median of 190 UI/L against 66 UI/L for the adults; their ALT and GGT are lower (medians 14 against 19 and 12 against 16 UI/L). The extraction has no unit column for these analytes (open question O6): the unit is read from the size of the value, and a result that only another unit explains is converted and flagged unit_inferred. What the values show: 4 alkaline phosphatase results are under 10, which no UI/L result can be: they are in µkat/L (1 µkat/L is 60 UI/L, as in BP and DR) and are converted. The window of the µkat/L runs to 10, where BP and DR stop at 5: one of the four sits at the top of their window, at a level (300 UI/L) that a child reaches. The default clip at the 1% and 99% percentiles turns a clinical tail into the cut value (40 of the 2,509 values here); the hard range is what removes impossible values (none here). Steps of the alkaline phosphatase that the age explains (0.75 interquartile range or more, groups of 20 results or more): the centre of the children (106 results, all of patients under 18, median age 11) has a median of 215 UI/L against 77.5 for all (1.61 interquartile ranges) and 65 to 82.5 at the three other centres, and the year 2023, with 73% of its 77 results from patients under 18, has 183 (1.24).

bilan_lipidique.title: Blood lipids

bp.notes: How the units are read (the same in every schema of this tab). The unit column is filled by the form with a default label, also where there is no result, so it proves little. Each analyte lists the units that occur, with the values one expects on each scale. A value that fits its label keeps it. A value that cannot be on the labelled scale and fits exactly one other is converted and flagged (unit_inferred, or unit_doubt when it was possible but unlikely under its label). A value that fits no scale is left as it is and the hard range decides (out_of_range). Cholesterol is reported in mmol/L or in g/L (1 g/L = 2.586 mmol/L). The two scales overlap, so the label matters here; where a value can only be on the other scale, it is converted. LDL. The form has a unit choice (rad_chol_hll) that the export copies into the unit column for every analyte except this one: 246 results chosen as g/L are labelled mmol/L in ldl_lborresu. The unit is therefore read from rad_chol_hll first, and from ldl_lborresu when the choice is empty. Total cholesterol. About 230 results labelled mmol/L lie between 1.5 and 2.6, with a mode under 2: these are g/L. They are converted (unit_inferred below 1.5 mmol/L, which is impossible; unit_doubt above). Triglycerides in g/L and in mmol/L are on almost the same scale (factor 1.129), so only the label can tell them apart. The ratio of total to HDL cholesterol is the only lipid value that the form computes (A8 in EXPORT_REQUESTS.md): total divided by HDL on each key-up in either field, with no unit, rounded to 2 decimals and with no else branch, so that the old ratio stays when a field is emptied. It is recomputed here from the harmonised values (custom function cholesterol_ratio) and compared with the stored one. The stored ratio equals the ratio of the numbers as typed on 12,629 of the 12,648 visits that have both. It differs from the recomputed ratio on 366 visits, 349 of them unit mixes (1 g/L = 2.586 mmol/L): the stored ratio is the recomputed one divided by 2.586 on 170 visits (a total in g/L over an HDL in mmol/L, 12 to 41 in each period) and multiplied by 2.586 on 179 (a total in mmol/L over an HDL in g/L: 78 in 2022-23, 81 from 2024 and 20 before 2022). The mismatches are 1.3% to 1.8% of the visits to 2021, then 7.1% in 2022-23 and 6.8% from 2024: the unit choice of the HDL and the LDL began to be filled in 2022 (1% to 2% of the HDL results to 2018, 7% in 2019-21, 88% in 2022-23, 97% from 2024) while the total cholesterol has no choice, so an HDL chosen in g/L is divided into a total in mmol/L. In 2022-23 one centre carries 45 of the 78 mismatches of the second kind. The recomputed ratio is the one delivered. The 50 visits where the ratio cannot be recomputed (score_not_recomputed): 28 have an HDL typed above 4, removed as impossible (not an HDL: no conversion saves it), 6 have a removed total cholesterol, and 16 have an empty typed field beside a stored ratio, the stale ratio that the form keeps when a field is emptied. LDL is a calculated value, not an independent measurement: it lies within 0.15 mmol/L of total minus HDL minus triglycerides divided by 2.2 on 90.2% of the 12,568 visits with triglycerides under 4.5 mmol/L. About 9 removed values of BP look like mg/dL (LDL of 100 to 200: 3, triglycerides of 60 to 200: 4, total cholesterol of 100 or more: 2). The form offers no mg/dL, so they are left removed. Shifted block and pool. This schema belongs to the pool biology (implausible_visits: 3, see biochimie): a visit with three or more impossible values over the seven laboratory schemas of BP loses all its values here too and gets visit_removed, so the ratio computed from them is empty as well. The pool removes 29 visits in all (998 cells); this schema loses 101 delivered cells on 27 visits (75 on 19 visits of the shifted block of one centre, 26 on 8 other visits) and 6 cells of the stored ratio, which is a check and not delivered; an impossible stored ratio counts in the pool like any other impossible value. The 4 block visits that escape the pool (see biochimie) still deliver 20 values here. Winsorising (step 12) clips each number at its 1st and 99th percentile, so a clinical tail becomes the cut value (in BP a total cholesterol above 7.94 mmol/L, an LDL above 5.62, triglycerides above 4.8 and a ratio above 8.35 are delivered as those values, and an HDL below 0.68 as 0.68: 235 to 263 values per variable are clipped), while the hard range (total cholesterol [1.5, 15], triglycerides [0.1, 40]) is what removes impossible values.

sz.notes: The four lipids of FACE BP with the same units and limits, and the ratio of total to HDL cholesterol, recomputed from the harmonised values and compared with the stored one. HDL: 27 results labelled g/L are converted, 6 fit g/L under the label mmol/L, 14 are out of range. Total cholesterol: 46 results fit g/L under the label mmol/L (11 unit_inferred, 35 unit_doubt). LDL: 17 unit_doubt. The stored ratio is the one the EMR computes from the two numbers as typed, on key-up, with no unit. It differs from the ratio of the two typed numbers on 120 of 3,172 visits (3.8%, against 19 of 12,648 in BP, 0.15%), 103 of them since 2022; two centres carry 48 and 29 of the 120. It differs from the ratio of the two harmonised values on 157 of 3,578 visits (4.4%, score_mismatch). 44 of these hold the ratio of numbers typed in two units (a value on another scale, the BP case: on 37 the stored value is the recomputed one times 2.59 or divided by it). 13 hold LDL over HDL and 9 total over LDL (16 and 13 before the 44 are taken out). 91 are not explained: 78 date from 2022 or later, 46 are in one centre, and the stored value is off by more than 1 on 32. The centres should be asked. That any of them was typed by hand is not proven. The recomputed ratio is delivered and the 157 get score_mismatch. LDL is not exported with its unit (export request R27; BP has the choice in rad_chol_hll). Typed LDL from 1.0 up to 1.8, where a result in g/L would fall, is 7.7% of the 3,530 SZ results, against 8.2% of the 9,575 BP results with no choice (6.3% where mmol/L was chosen, 55% where g/L was chosen): there is no sign of a large group in g/L, at most about 3% of the results (100). The 2 results labelled g/L are converted. LDL is a calculated value: it is within 0.15 mmol/L of total - HDL - triglycerides / 2.2 on 86.8% of the 3,424 visits with triglycerides under 4.5 mmol/L (unwinsorised values). The clip at the 1st and 99th percentile turns a clinical tail into the cut value, on 66 to 72 results per variable; the hard range is what removes impossible values. Same instrument as in FACE BP. The 14 visits where the ratio cannot be recomputed (score_not_recomputed; 50 in BP): on 10 both fields are typed but the HDL (8) or the total cholesterol (2) was removed as impossible, and 4 have an empty typed field beside a stored ratio, the stale ratio that the form keeps.
sz.difference: the results are in columns named for the analyte; the unit chosen on the form for LDL is not extracted

dr.notes: HDL, LDL, total cholesterol and triglycerides, and the ratio of total to HDL cholesterol computed from the harmonised values; the TRD extraction stores no ratio. For HDL and LDL the form has a choice of unit, exported as a code: 1 is g/L and 2 mmol/L (the median HDL is 0.54 with code 1 and 1.39 with code 2, the median LDL 1.25 and 3.49). 207 HDL and 270 LDL results are converted from g/L (unit_converted). Total cholesterol has the default label only: 29 results fit g/L better than mmol/L and are kept with a doubt (unit_doubt), 6 are converted. The LDL is not computed by the form, but it is a calculated value: it is within 0.15 mmol/L of total cholesterol - HDL - triglycerides / 2.2 on 94.5% of the 1,061 visits with triglycerides below 4.5 mmol/L (values before winsorising). 27 HDL and 24 LDL values are impossible, 23 and 22 of them on the visits of one centre whose block of results was typed in the wrong fields, shifted by seven fields of the eCEDR table (30 visits dated up to 2022, see the blood-count schema). On 21 of them the unit cell of the HDL holds a number other than the code 1 or 2. This schema belongs to the pool biology (implausible_visits: 3, implausible_pool: biology; see the blood-count schema): a visit with three or more impossible values over the eleven laboratory schemas of DR loses all its values and gets visit_removed. The pool removes 35 visits in all (1,403 cells); this schema loses 45 cells on 25 visits: 36 on 21 visits of the block, which leaves no lipid value on the 30 block visits, and 9 on 4 other visits (two of them hold 3 and 4 impossible values of the 4 lipids, with 5 and 3 in the biochemistry). The 1% and 99% winsorising turns a clinical tail into the cut value, and only the hard range removes impossible values. Same instrument as in FACE BP, without the stored ratio.
dr.difference: the results are in columns named for the analyte; the unit of HDL and LDL is exported as a code; no stored ratio

asp.notes: HDL, LDL and total cholesterol and triglycerides, on 329 inclusion visits and 25 follow-up visits. Same analytes, names and target unit (mmol/L) as in FACE SZ and DR. Cholesterol and triglycerides have a unit column that holds a catalogue number (the list of the form: 64387 is mmol/L, 42576 is g/L): 64387 on 281 cholesterol results (median 4.3: mmol/L) and 42576 on 71 (median 1.74: g/L). The triglycerides carry the same two numbers (288 and 64), and the two units are on the same scale (13% apart), so their number is believed. The two columns disagree on 26 of the 351 visits that have both results (10 with mmol/L on the cholesterol and g/L on the triglycerides, 16 the other way round). The data support the numbers: the cholesterol has the size of its own number on 23 of the 26 visits (the three others are read in mmol/L, unit_inferred), and the triglycerides, read in the unit of their number, are closer to 2.2 x (total - HDL - LDL) than in the other unit on 22 of the 26. HDL and LDL have no unit column, and their level does not move with the number of the cholesterol (HDL median 1.33 against 1.41): they are read as mmol/L. The LDL is not computed by the form, but it is a calculated value of the laboratories: it is within 0.15 mmol/L of total cholesterol - HDL - triglycerides / 2.2 on 91.0% of the 344 visits that have the four results (all with triglycerides under 4.5 mmol/L; measured on the values before the clip). The cohort holds children: 29% of the 354 visits with a lipid result are those of a patient under 18. Their total cholesterol, LDL and HDL are lower than the adults' (medians 3.95 against 4.54, 2.17 against 2.51 and 1.32 against 1.43 mmol/L). Four HDL results are above the hard range of 4 mmol/L, which is that of BP and DR: rare but not impossible values, removed. The ratio of total to HDL cholesterol is computed from the harmonised values, as in the other cohorts. The default clip at the 1% and 99% percentiles turns a clinical tail into the cut value (36 of the 1,751 values here); the hard range is what removes impossible values (5 results here, the four HDL and one triglyceride).
asp.difference: the unit column of cholesterol and triglycerides holds catalogue numbers; HDL and LDL have no unit column and are read as mmol/L; no stored ratio to compare

bilan_lipidique.description: Blood lipids from the blood sample of the visit: HDL, LDL and total cholesterol and triglycerides in mmol/L, and the ratio of total to HDL cholesterol.

flags: The ratio stored by the form (BP, SZ) divides the two numbers as typed, with no unit: it mixes g/L and mmol/L, mostly from 2022. The delivered ratio is the recomputed one; the visits that differ carry score_mismatch (in SZ 91 of 157 are not explained). The DR extraction stores no ratio.

Cholesterol in g/L and in mmol/L overlap, and triglycerides in the two units are on almost the same scale: the label decides where it exists. Units are harmonised. Where the unit label is absent or says nothing, the unit is read from the size of the value: a converted value carries unit_inferred or unit_doubt, and a value that fits two units is missing (unit_unknown).

By default each number is clipped at its 1st and 99th percentiles (winsorising), so a clinical tail becomes the cut value; only the hard range removes impossible values. Load with winsorise=False to keep the tails.
