bilan_thyroidien.title: Thyroid tests

bp.notes: How the units are read (the same in every schema of this tab). The unit column is filled by the form with a default label, also where there is no result, so it proves little. Each analyte lists the units that occur, with the values one expects on each scale. A value that fits its label keeps it. A value that cannot be on the labelled scale and fits exactly one other is converted and flagged (unit_inferred, or unit_doubt when it was possible but unlikely under its label). A value that fits no scale is left as it is and the hard range decides (out_of_range). TSH. The three labels of the form (µUI/L, mUI/L, microUI/ml) hold values on the same scale, with the same median: the default label "µUI/L" is a misprint for µUI/mL, which is the same as mUI/L. They are one unit here. Free T4: 107 results between 0.3 and 3 are in ng/dL (1 ng/dL = 12.87 pmol/L): 100 under the default pmol/L label and 7 labelled ng/dL. The 10 results between 3 and 4 fit ng/dL and pg/mL alike, so they keep their pmol/L label. Free T3 and free T4 in pg/mL overlap the pmol/L scale and are recognised by their label only. The TSH field of the form rejects a value above 10 (A27 in EXPORT_REQUESTS.md): BP has 44 TSH above 10 among 8,608 results before 2022 and none among 3,443 from 2022. The TSH tail from 2022 is capped by the form, so a mean, a share above a limit or a maximum is not comparable before and after 2022. A TSH of 0 is nothing measured (one result): missing code, not_recorded, in place of the delivered clip value. Shifted block and pool. This schema belongs to the pool biology (implausible_visits: 3, see biochimie). With three analytes it could not use the rule alone (a visit would need all three impossible), but the pool counts the impossible values of the seven laboratory schemas of BP: a visit with three or more loses its TSH, free T3 and free T4 and gets visit_removed. The pool removes 29 visits in all (998 cells); this schema loses 49 cells on 25 visits (TSH 23, free T3 7, free T4 19). In the shifted block of one centre the free T3 is impossible (a blood-count value above 30 pmol/L) on 19 of the 24 visits; the TSH and the free T4 of the 20 block visits that the pool removes go with them, and the 4 that escape hold none of the three. Winsorising (step 12) clips each number at its 1st and 99th percentile, so a clinical tail becomes the cut value (in BP a TSH above 7.9 mUI/L is delivered as 7.9, a free T3 above 7.2 pmol/L as 7.2 and a free T4 above 21.6 pmol/L as 21.6: 223 to 258 values per analyte are clipped, and from 2022 the form already caps the TSH at 10), while the hard range ([0, 150], [1.5, 30] and [3, 100]) is what removes impossible values.

dr.notes: TSH, free T3 and free T4, on about 1,160 visits. The eCEDR form offers a choice of unit for each of the three (TSH: microUI/mL, pmol/L or mUI/L; free T3: pmol/L or pg/mL; free T4: pmol/L or ng/dL), but the extraction does not carry it (request R31): the size of the value decides, as in BP and SZ. 36 free T4 are read as ng/dL by their size and brought back (unit_inferred), 6 of them on the shifted visits below. A 0 typed where nothing was measured is out of range. The unit column of an analyte holds the default label of the form on every row that has any result of the tab (1,254 rows) and on no other, so it says nothing. 21 free T3 and 15 free T4 are impossible, all on the visits of one centre whose block of results was typed in the wrong fields, shifted by seven fields of the eCEDR table (30 visits dated up to 2022, see the blood-count schema): the free T3 and the free T4 there have the size of a basophil and an eosinophil count, the TSH that of a neutrophil count, which is inside its range. At most two of the three numbers are impossible on a visit, so the schema alone could not tell a shifted visit. It belongs to the pool biology (implausible_visits: 3, implausible_pool: biology; see the blood-count schema): a visit with three or more impossible values over the eleven laboratory schemas of DR loses all its values and gets visit_removed. The pool removes 35 visits in all (1,403 cells); this schema loses 43 cells on 27 visits: 28 on 22 visits of the block (22 TSH and 6 free T4, the 6 read as ng/dL above) and 15 on 5 other visits. The 1% and 99% winsorising turns a clinical tail into the cut value, and only the hard range removes impossible values. Centre step of the free T3: one centre has a median of 3.25 pmol/L against 4.4 for all (-1.04 interquartile range, 44 results, groups of 20 results or more) and the oldest patients (median age 68 against 53 years); the pg/mL choice of the form is not exported (R31) and its window overlaps that of pmol/L, so the size of the values cannot tell whether results were typed in pg/mL, and the cause is not known. Of the 36 free T4 read as ng/dL, 27 are of one centre and 6 of the shifted centre, so the unit that the export does not carry follows the centre. Same instrument as in FACE BP.

asp.notes: TSH, on 469 inclusion visits and 49 follow-up visits. Same analyte, name and target unit as in FACE DR; the free T3 and T4 are not in this extraction. Its unit column holds a catalogue number: 67405 (mUI/L, µUI/ml on the form) on 512 results and 67434 on 6. The form prints pmol/L for 67434, but its 6 results have the size of the others (median 1.4 against 1.7), so both numbers are read as mUI/L (67434 is an alias). 515 rows carry the number 67405, 3 of them with no result. The default clip at the 1% and 99% percentiles turns a clinical tail into the cut value (10 of the 517 values here); the hard range is what removes impossible values (1 result here, above 150).

biochimie.title: Blood biochemistry

bp.notes: How the units are read (the same in every schema of this tab). The unit column is filled by the form with a default label, also where there is no result, so it proves little. Each analyte lists the units that occur, with the values one expects on each scale. A value that fits its label keeps it. A value that cannot be on the labelled scale and fits exactly one other is converted and flagged (unit_inferred, or unit_doubt when it was possible but unlikely under its label). A value that fits no scale is left as it is and the hard range decides (out_of_range). CRP. Of 13,095 results, 2,328 are written with "<" and 5 with ">", and in 31 more rows the mark sits in the unit column ("inf") and the result column holds the limit. There are 18 different detection limits from 0.1 to 60 mg/L depending on the laboratory. The limit is kept as the value and crp_cens marks it. 399 results are exactly 0: no assay measures a CRP of 0, so it is a result below a limit that was not written. They are delivered as missing (missing code; decision D101 in PROGRESS.md, of the project lead, was open question O3), in the four cohorts. Glucose. Of 12,993 results, 356 are labelled g/L and look like g/L (converted). 124 are labelled mmol/L but are too low to be mmol/L; these are g/L values with the wrong label (unit_inferred). 23 are possible under their label but fit the other unit better (unit_doubt). 7 fit neither (3 of them are 0). The unit mg/dL (60 to 400: no mmol/L result reaches it, the hard range stops at 40) is listed so that a result typed in mg/dL is read; none is in BP. The 4 results of 41 or more that stay out_of_range are 10 times (2 of them) or about 100 times (the 2 others) the usual glucose of the same patient, a misplaced decimal point, where a result in mg/dL would be 18 times. The window starts at 60 because a result of 41 to 60 is 10 times the usual value, not a low glucose in mg/dL. Hidden scales found in the other analytes, all under the default label: uric acid in mg/L (102 values, with a clear mode at 40 to 70), in mg/dL (31) and in mmol/L (22); creatinine in mg/L (76); urea in g/L (56); phosphate in mg/L (83) and in mg/dL (15); calcium in mg/L (51) and in mEq/L (17); iron in µg/dL (362), in µg/L (57) and in mg/L (24); albumin with a lost decimal point (11) or in g/dL (2). Iron cannot always be told apart: a low iron in µg/dL (20 to 45) looks like a normal iron in µmol/L and is kept as such. This happens in one centre that typed µg/dL from 2013 to 2018: 59% of its 485 results of those years are 50 or more (2.5% in its other years, 1.4% in the other centres) and are converted, while its 198 results below 50, which would be 9 µmol/L or less if they were in µg/dL, stay read as µmol/L. The delivered median of that centre in those years is 19.5 µmol/L, against 16.8 for all other results. Open point: ask the centre which unit it used and when. HbA1c: eight results labelled %, in five centres, are 20 to 53, impossible as a percentage: they are in mmol/mol (IFCC) and are converted with the IFCC-NGSP master equation, % = 0.09148 x mmol/mol + 2.152 (unit_inferred; 4.0% to 7.0%; decision D127, which recovered these mmol/mol results only). 32 results under 3 (a 0 and 31 of 0.2 to 3, in five centres) stay out_of_range: no fraction is recovered (a fraction would be under 0.2), and they are not the glucose of the visit in g/L (7% of them within 0.05 g/L of it), so their scale is unknown. 24 of the 31 belong to the shifted block described below. Creatinine clearance: 0 stands for "not computed" (246 cells, missing code). Results such as ">90" are right-censored at the laboratory's ceiling. The form computes the clearance itself on each key-up in the creatinine field (Cockcroft-Gault: 1.23 for a man or 1.04 for a woman, times the weight of the nursing record of the visit, times 140 minus the age on the day of typing, divided by the creatinine as typed) and writes 0 when the weight is not saved (A21 in EXPORT_REQUESTS.md). A recomputation with the age at the visit differs from the stored value by 10% or more on about 4,600 of 10,800 visits (43%): the stored clearance depends on the weight and the age that the form saw. It is delivered as stored. Centres (report page, read on 2026-11-18). No step between the years in any analyte. The centres differ by their laboratories, not by a unit: two centres have an albumin 3 to 4 g/L lower than the others (median 40 against 42 to 45), the size of the gap between the two usual methods of measure (bromocresol purple and green); one centre has a calcium 0.1 mmol/L lower (2.26 against 2.30 to 2.40). The CRP falls from a median of 4 mg/L in 2009 to 1 to 2 from 2019, while the share of results given as "less than" a limit goes from 6% to 35% by year (35% in 2009, 9% in 2013, about 30% in 2017, 6% in 2026): the assays and the mix of laboratories change, so the median is read with the censoring column. The centre medians go from 1.1 to 3.0 mg/L, except for one centre whose median is 5: it writes exactly 5 on 86% of its results and marks "<" on only 44%, so its 474 unmarked results of 5 are limits delivered as measured values. No rule can find them without naming the centre, so none is made: a pooled analysis should treat a CRP of exactly 5 as a limit. Shifted block and pool (implausible_visits: 3, implausible_pool: biology). This schema belongs to the pool of the seven laboratory schemas of BP. The impossible values (out_of_range) of the whole pool are counted on each visit, and a visit with three or more loses all its values in every schema of the pool and gets visit_removed, with the number of impossible values as detail (section 4 of SCHEMA_SPEC.md). The rule reads the content, not the centre. It removes 29 visits in all (998 cells: 992 delivered values and 6 of the stored cholesterol ratio, a check that is not delivered). This schema loses 361 cells on the 29 visits: 246 on 20 visits of the block below and 115 on 9 other visits. A result of 0 counts as impossible (not the CRP and the clearance, where 0 is a missing code). The block. In one centre, from 2019 to 2023, a block of results of the form was typed in the wrong fields on 24 visits: blood-count values stand as the iron, the HbA1c, the calcium, the phosphate, the uric acid and the clearance, and the differential count is empty on 19 of the 24 visits. The iron (23 values) and the HbA1c (24) fall outside their hard range, but 91 values of the block (calcium, phosphate, uric acid and clearance) fall inside it and would be delivered as results; the same block gives an impossible free T3 on 19 of the 24 visits (see bilan_thyroidien) and fills the drug levels (see dosage_psychotropes). The pool removes 20 of the 24 visits and 75 of those 91 values. 4 visits escape, because the iron and the HbA1c, their only impossible values, make 2 and not 3: they still deliver 48 values here (16 of the 91 among them), 19 in bilan_hepatique, 20 in bilan_lipidique, 25 in nfs and 11 in dosage_psychotropes, and none in the two other schemas. The 9 other visits removed, in three other centres from 2011 to 2018, are another pattern: 3 to 12 impossible values spread over two to four schemas (biochemistry and lipids mostly), with a blood count that is filled on 8 of the 9. Winsorising (step 12) clips each number at its 1st and 99th percentile, so a clinical tail becomes the cut value (in BP a CRP above 24.8 mg/L, a creatinine above 118 µmol/L, a fasting glucose above 8.4 mmol/L, an HbA1c above 8.0% and a sodium below 135 mmol/L are delivered as those values: 190 sodium and 276 creatinine values are clipped), while the hard range of each variable is what removes impossible values (out_of_range); the load with winsorise=False keeps the tails. The form also has the ferritin, the corrected calcium, the sampling date (date_prelevement, the only mandatory field) and the sampling place. None of them is in the extraction: to be requested. The visit date stands for the sampling date. Chloride (qc site_shift, read on 2026-11-19): three centres (140, 240 and 66 results) have a median of 108, 107 and 107 mmol/L against 104 for the others (1.0, 0.75 and 0.75 IQR, on an IQR of 4), their median and 5th percentile both 3 to 4 mmol/L higher, with no unit conversion for chloride in BP: a difference of laboratory of unknown cause, left as measured.

sz.notes: Four analytes of the BP biochemistry, with the same units and limits. The result is in the column named for the analyte (urate, crp, gluc, hba1c) and the unit label in <analyte>_lborresu. The unit column holds the form's default label on the 4,065 visits of the form, also on the visits that have no result (502 for CRP, 745 for uric acid, 926 for glucose and 2,211 for HbA1c; as in BP), so a label says little: the unit is checked against the size of the value. Uric acid: 22 results fit another unit than their label (mg/L, mg/dL or mmol/L): 10 unit_inferred, 12 unit_doubt. Glucose: 66 results labelled g/L are converted; 17 labelled mmol/L can only be g/L (unit_inferred) and 3 are doubtful. 3 more, labelled mmol/L, lie between 45 and 100: they are mg/dL (factor 0.05551, unit_inferred), where they were out of range (two are low and are delivered as the cut value of the 1% clip). The window of mg/dL, 45 to 720, lies above the end of the mmol/L scale (its hard range stops at 40) and no result lies between 25 and 45, so it takes no mmol/L value. HbA1c: five results labelled % are 33 to 44, which is mmol/mol (IFCC): they are converted with % = 0.09148 x mmol/mol + 2.152 (unit_inferred; 5.2% to 6.2%, within 0.3 point of the patient's other results in the median); one 0 stays out of range. CRP: 477 of the 3,563 results (13%) are exactly 0, written 0 or 00. No assay gives 0: it is a result below a limit that was not written, delivered as missing (missing code unknown, as in BP D101). One centre holds 290 of them (73% of its results) and 39 results of exactly 5 with no mark; apart from them it has a single result between 0 and 5 and none between 5 and 6, so its limit looks written as 0 or as an unmarked 5. An unmarked limit is delivered as a measured value: 94 results of exactly 5 carry no "<" in the whole cohort, 31 carry one. 334 results are written with "<" (censored_left) and one with ">". The clip at the 1st and 99th percentile (CRP: the 99th only) turns a clinical tail into the cut value, on 31 to 65 results per analyte; the hard range is what removes impossible values. Same instrument as in FACE BP, with four of its sixteen analytes.
sz.difference: four of the sixteen BP analytes, in columns named for the analyte (urate, crp, gluc, hba1c)

dr.notes: The sixteen analytes of the BP schema, with two more that the TRD form has: ferritin (from 2017) and the kind of CRP assay. Blood results exist at the inclusion and follow-up visits (about 1,200 visits). The unit column of an analyte holds the default label of the form on every row that has any result of the tab (1,254 rows) and on no other, so it says nothing: the size of the value decides, as in BP and SZ. A 0 typed where nothing was measured is out of range. 59 results were typed on another scale and are brought back (unit_inferred): 17 phosphates, 10 glucoses in g/L, 7 creatinines, 7 calciums and others; 10 are kept with a doubt. CRP: 80 results are given as "less than" a limit; they keep the limit and the mark (crp_cens). The kind of assay is a code, 1 on 740 results and 2 on 377; the dictionary names the two kinds (CRP, high-sensitivity CRP) without saying which code is which (open question O11 in PROGRESS.md). The creatinine clearance is typed, not computed: the form only shows the Cockcroft-Gault formula as a help text. The typed values agree within 10% with the formula (age, weight, sex and creatinine of the visit) on 44% of 917 visits. HbA1c: 22 values are out of range as percentages; 19 have the size of a result in mmol/mol (IFCC, 18 to 52) and are converted with the IFCC-NGSP master equation, % = 0.09148 x mmol/mol + 2.152 (unit_inferred; 3.8% to 6.9%), and a 20th, of 18, is kept as a percentage with a doubt (unit_doubt). The others (0 and a value of seven digits) stay out of range. 19 of these 20 values are on the shifted visits of one centre (see the blood-count schema), where the HbA1c is 24 at the median against 5.5 elsewhere: it is the block typed in the wrong field, not a result in mmol/mol (open question O11 in PROGRESS.md). The pool removes these visits and their 19 values: only 1 of the 20 is still delivered. On the 30 shifted visits the glucose is out of range 13 times (it has the size of a platelet count), and nothing else of this schema is impossible: no visit holds more than one impossible value here, so this schema alone would not remove them. This schema belongs to the pool biology (implausible_visits: 3, implausible_pool: biology; see the blood-count schema): a visit with three or more impossible values over the eleven laboratory schemas of DR loses all its values and gets visit_removed. The pool removes 35 visits in all (1,403 cells); this schema loses 407 cells on 29 visits: 341 on 24 visits of the block and 66 on 5 other visits. The 5 other visits are of 5 other centres: 4 hold 3 to 5 impossible values in this schema (two of them also in the lipid schema) and the fifth holds one in each of the biochemistry, the blood count and the vitamins. The 1% and 99% winsorising turns a clinical tail into the cut value, and only the hard range removes impossible values. Steps between centres or years of 0.75 interquartile range or more (groups of 20 results or more; the cause is not known, an assay or a population): chloride, one centre at 102 mmol/L against 105 for all (-1.0, that is 3 mmol/L, 72 results); calcium, the year 2013 at 2.235 mmol/L against 2.34 (-0.75, 44 results) and one centre at 2.44 (0.71, 75 results); albumin, two centres at 39 g/L against 43 (-1.0, 49 and 39 results) and the year 2024 at 40 (-0.75, 30 results), where 53% of the results are those of a centre that appears in 2023 and has a median of 39 against 43.5 for the others; ferritin, one centre at 105.5 µg/L against 47 (0.81, 38 results). CRP: 35 of the 1,140 results are exactly 0 and are delivered as missing (BP D101), 27 of them dated 2013 to 2015. Same instrument as in FACE BP, with ferritin and the kind of CRP.
dr.difference: the results are in columns named for the analyte; ferritin and the kind of CRP assay are added

asp.notes: Fifteen analytes of the blood chemistry. Same analytes, names, target units and ranges as in FACE DR (and SZ for the uric acid, the CRP, the glucose and the HbA1c). The factors and the windows are those of BP (D127), but for the creatinine, whose µmol/L window starts at 20 (BP: 25) for the children. The scales that BP also declares and that no ASP result needs are not listed: albumin in g/dL, uric acid in mmol/L, calcium and phosphate in mg/dL. Biology starts late in this cohort: no chemistry result before 2016 (the blood count has one in 2015). 39% of the inclusions of 2021 and 26% to 44% of those of 2022 to 2026 hold a chemistry result. Over all the visits of the extraction (the screening visits hold none), a laboratory value of any kind is on 0.3% of the visits of 2013-15, 6.9% of 2016-18 and 13.6% to 16.9% from 2019 on; why is an open question (O10, third part). 517 inclusion visits and 52 follow-up visits hold at least one chemistry result; a laboratory value of any kind is on 22% of the inclusion visits and 15% of the follow-up visits. The cohort holds children: 39% of the 569 visits with a chemistry result are those of a patient under 18. Their creatinine and phosphate are not the adults' (medians 52 against 70 µmol/L and 1.37 against 1.04 mmol/L): compare the cohorts with the age in view. The extraction has no unit column for these analytes (open question O6): the unit is read from the size of the value, and a result that only another unit explains is converted and flagged unit_inferred. What the values show: 8 glucose results in g/L, 12 phosphate results in mg/L, 5 creatinine results (4 in mg/L, 1 in mg/dL), 5 uric acid results in mg/L or mg/dL, 2 urea results in g/L and 1 calcium result in mg/L are converted. No glucose is in mg/dL (none is above 13). One phosphate result is too large for the mg/L window and stays out_of_range. HbA1c lists mmol/mol (IFCC) as in the other cohorts, where some centres type it; no ASP result has that size. CRP. The form prints mmol/L beside it (open question O16, point 6); the values are of the size of mg/L. 45 of the 357 results (12.6%) are exactly 0 and are delivered as missing (BP D101): no assay gives 0. One result is given as "less than" a limit and keeps its mark (crp_cens). The 312 results kept are small: a median of 0.6 mg/L and 59% under 1 mg/L, against a median of 2.0 to 2.3 and 20% to 29% under 1 mg/L in BP, SZ and DR. The assays are probably high-sensitivity ones. Do not pool the CRP of this cohort with the others without the censoring column. The default clip at the 1% and 99% percentiles turns a clinical tail into the cut value (101 of the 5,533 values here); the hard range is what removes impossible values (18 results). Steps of 0.75 interquartile range or more (groups of 20 results or more): the creatinine of the centre of the children is 45 µmol/L against 62.85 for all (-0.79, 123 results, all of patients under 18) and 62.8 to 72 at the three other centres, which is the age; the chloride of the centre that gives 186 of the 490 results is 102 mmol/L against 103.5 to 105 at the three others (-0.67 from the overall 104) and the years 2017 to 2019 are 101 (-1.0, 21 to 34 results, nearly all of that centre), a step of 3 mmol/L between laboratories; the CRP of 2023 is 2.35 mg/L against 0.6 for all (1.03, 26 results, 20 of them of one centre, 9 of 5 mg/L or more against 38 of 312 overall), and the cause is not known.
asp.difference: no unit column, so the unit is read from the size of the value and the ranges of two units do not overlap; fifteen of the analytes of the other cohorts

biochimie.description: Blood chemistry from the blood sample of the visit: electrolytes, proteins, urea, creatinine and its clearance, uric acid, phosphate, calcium, iron, C-reactive protein, fasting glucose and HbA1c (sixteen analytes in BP; SZ has uric acid, CRP, glucose and HbA1c; DR and ASP add ferritin).
sources: schema notes (bp, sz, dr, asp biochimie)
flags: CRP: a result under the detection limit of the laboratory keeps the limit as its value, marked in the censoring column crp_cens; the limits differ between laboratories and change over the years, so read a median with that column. A CRP of exactly 0 is delivered as missing. Some limits are typed with no mark: in a pooled analysis treat a CRP of exactly 5 as a limit.

ASP: the CRP is much lower than in the other cohorts (probably high-sensitivity assays): do not pool it without the censoring column. DR: the kind of CRP assay (crp_type) is a code whose meaning is not documented.

BP: the stored creatinine clearance differs by 10% or more from a recomputation with the age at the visit on 43% of the visits. DR: the typed clearance agrees with the formula within 10% on 44% of the visits.
HbA1c typed in mmol/mol is converted to % (IFCC-NGSP equation, unit_inferred). BP iron: one centre typed µg/dL for some years, and its low values cannot be told from µmol/L.

Units are harmonised. Where the unit label is absent or says nothing, the unit is read from the size of the value: a converted value carries unit_inferred or unit_doubt, and a value that fits two units is missing (unit_unknown).

By default each number is clipped at its 1st and 99th percentiles (winsorising), so a clinical tail becomes the cut value; only the hard range removes impossible values. Load with winsorise=False to keep the tails.
BP and DR: a visit with three or more impossible values over the laboratory schemas loses all its laboratory values (visit_removed).
ASP holds children, whose creatinine and phosphate are not the adults': compare the cohorts with the age in view.

common.note: Glucose, HbA1c, CRP and uric acid are in the four cohorts; the other analytes in BP, DR and ASP (bicarbonate and iron in BP and DR only, ferritin in DR and ASP only). Each analyte is delivered in one unit, with the same range in every cohort; the levels are compatible (no factor of 10 or of a molar mass between cohorts). ASP has no unit column: the unit is read from the size of the value, and about 40% of its laboratory visits are of children under 18 (ALP, creatinine and phosphate are higher). An HbA1c typed in mmol/mol (IFCC) is brought to % with the IFCC-NGSP master equation in every cohort (a fraction such as 0.055 is not recovered). A CRP below the detection limit of its laboratory keeps the limit as its value (flag censored_left), the limits differ between laboratories, and some centres write the limit without its sign: treat a CRP of exactly 5 as a limit. ASP's CRP is probably a high-sensitivity CRP (median three times lower, 12.6% of zeros removed): do not pool it without the censoring column. The 1% and 99% clipping turns clinical tails into the cut value in every cohort. A shifted block of results (blood-count values typed in the biochemistry fields) is removed in BP and DR (visit_removed).

dosage_psychotropes.title: Plasma levels of psychotropic drugs

bp.notes: These columns have no unit column. The dictionary gives one unit per drug; a few results are on the molar scale instead and are recognised by their size: valproate above 200 (µmol/L), carbamazepine above 16, lamotrigine above 20. They are converted and flagged unit_inferred (5 valproate, 12 carbamazepine and 39 lamotrigine results). Lamotrigine cannot always be told apart: its usual levels in µmol/L (12 to 55) overlap its high levels in mg/L. Only the values of 20 and more are converted. Clozapine (65 results, 3 of them 0) is on three scales at least: µg/L, mg/L (13 results, read as µg/L) and probably µmol/L. Only the first two are recognised; 28 results fit neither and end out_of_range, all of 1 to 20: 20 of them are whole numbers from 2 to 4 and come from the centre of the shifted block (below), the 8 others could be µmol/L (1 µmol/L = 326.8 µg/L, so 1 to 5 would be 330 to 1,630 µg/L, the usual levels). Open question for the laboratories. The form labels the field mmol/L, which is wrong; the lamotrigine field has no unit label on the form. A level below the laboratory's limit is left-censored ("<0.1"). The upper tail only is winsorised. Lithium above 3 mmol/L is impossible in an outpatient and ends out_of_range (10 results, some with a lost decimal point). A level of 0 is nothing measured: the laboratories write "<x" for a level they cannot detect (56 lamotrigine results are written so). 41 zero levels were in the extraction: 38 were delivered as 0 (lithium 7, red-cell lithium 8, valproate 8, carbamazepine 4, oxcarbazepine 1, lamotrigine 10) and the 3 of clozapine were out_of_range. All are now missing, with the missing code not_recorded. They do not come with an undetectable level of a patient on treatment: only 3 of the 7 lithium zeros, 1 of the 8 valproate zeros and 5 of the 10 lamotrigine zeros have a dated active treatment of that molecule at the visit. The delivered names are the molecule strings of the treatments table (lithium, valproate, carbamazepine, oxcarbazepine, lamotrigine, clozapine; lithium_erythrocyte is the lithium of the red cells). A level above 0 falls on a day with a dated active treatment of that molecule (a treatment that started on or before the visit and has no end date or an end on or after it) for 78% of the lithium levels, 68% of the valproate levels (80% with valpromide) and 81% of the lamotrigine levels: a level with no treatment on file is not an error, since the treatment lists are incomplete. Only the answer to "treatment taken on the morning of the sample" is recorded (405 yes among 10,608 answers): the form shows the level fields only after the answer no, and 8,633 of the 8,666 visits with a level have it (33 have no answer, 18 of them because the pool removed the visit, and none has yes). The extraction has no sampling time and no dose, so a level cannot be put against the time since the last dose. Shifted block and pool. This schema belongs to the pool biology (implausible_visits: 3, see biochimie): a visit with three or more impossible values over the seven laboratory schemas of BP loses all its values here too and gets visit_removed. The pool removes 29 visits in all (998 cells); this schema loses 105 cells on 27 visits (90 on 19 visits of the shifted block of one centre, 15 on 8 other visits), among them 21 answers to the question on the treatment taken. On the 24 visits of the block (see biochimie) the fields of the drug levels are filled as nowhere else: red-cell lithium on 13 of the 24 visits (11% of the visits of the other centres), valproate on 21 (10%), carbamazepine on 15 (1.5%), oxcarbazepine on 17 (0.1%) and clozapine on 17 (0.2%), with levels of another scale (the median valproate is 2.4 mg/L against 61 for the other centres, the red-cell lithium 1.1 mmol/L against 0.28). These 66 values (without the clozapine, which is out of range) are removed with their visits, except 8 (4 valproate and 4 oxcarbazepine) on the 4 block visits that escape the pool: they stay delivered as typed. Not repaired. Winsorising (step 12) clips the upper tail at the 99th percentile, so a clinical tail becomes the cut value (in BP a lithium above 1.31 mmol/L, a valproate above 124 mg/L and a lamotrigine above 15.6 mg/L are delivered as those values: 46 lithium values are clipped, so a toxic level cannot be told from the 99th percentile), while the hard range (lithium [0, 3], valproate [0, 250]) is what removes impossible values.

sz.notes: The plasma level of clozapine, read like in FACE BP, and the question that precedes it on the form, "is the patient treated with clozapine?". clozapine_treated has 1,600 answers, 569 of them "yes". A level is given on 524 of the "yes" visits and on 68 visits with no answer: 592 levels in all, with a median of 424 µg/L (5th to 95th percentile 110 to 1,010), a plausible size for clozapine levels in treated patients. 11 levels are in mg/L (0.4 for 400 µg/L), 9 are written with "<" (censored_left) and 10 are out of range: 3 zeros and 7 under 20 µg/L. Six of the 7 results under 20 are from 1 to 20 with no mark, all on "yes" visits. Four of them, multiplied by 326.8 (µmol/L to µg/L), give 490 to 750 µg/L, the size of the other levels; the two others give over 3,000. They may be µmol/L, but no unit is recorded and six values do not prove it: they are not converted and stay out of range (an open question for the centres). The clip at the 99th percentile turns a high level into the cut value (6 results); the hard range, 20 to 3,000 µg/L, is what removes impossible values. Same instrument as in FACE BP for the level; the BP extraction has other drugs and another first question (was the treatment taken before the sample).
sz.difference: the clozapine level only, with the question "treated with clozapine"; no other drug

dr.notes: Drug levels measured with the blood sample: whether the treatment was taken that morning (958 answers, 138 yes), the hours since the last intake (631 answers, 594 delivered, median 12), twelve boxes that say which level was asked for, and the levels. The boxes are filled on every row that has a blood result (1,254 rows). Nothing else is recorded: no dose, no time of the sample. Lithium (146 levels, median 0.73 mmol/L; mEq/L and mmol/L are the same scale), valproate (11) and carbamazepine (1) keep the BP names and units; none of the 13 oxcarbazepine levels is delivered (they are all on removed visits, below). Valproate: 7 levels are in mmol/L and are converted to mg/L (unit_inferred). The names of the boxes are those of the treatments table, except assay_divalproate (the table has valproate and valpromide, no divalproate); the form has one field of valproic acid behind the three boxes valproate, divalproate and valpromide, and all 11 valproate levels have one of them ticked. Five antidepressant levels are TRD only: amitriptyline, clomipramine, imipramine, fluoxetine and venlafaxine. The dictionary says mg/L; the form asks for a unit (mg/L or µg/L) for clomipramine, fluoxetine and venlafaxine, and the extraction does not carry it (amitriptyline and imipramine have mg/L fixed). Each drug holds two groups of values a thousand times apart: clomipramine has 89 levels of the size of mg/L and 46 of the size of µg/L. They are delivered in µg/L, and those typed in mg/L are converted (unit_inferred: 209 in all, 201 of them still delivered); the two scales are 1,000 apart, so the size decides without risk. A level of 0 means that nothing was measured and is a missing code (52 cells: 8 for lithium, 1 for oxcarbazepine, 43 for the other drugs; the box is at 0 on all but 2). The delay of 0 too (28 cells, 27 of them written 0000 in one centre); 5 delays above 72 hours are impossible, three of them years. The delays are heaped: 42% are 12 hours and 20% are 24 hours, all in whole hours. The form shows the level of a drug only after its box is ticked (its script hides the field), yet 11 levels have no box, all of them lithium. The 26 others (oxcarbazepine 12, valproate 6, venlafaxine 5, amitriptyline 3) were all on visits of the shifted centre (below) and the pool removes them. No box is ever ticked for oxcarbazepine, whose 12 levels were all in that centre and have a median of 12, the usual delay: they were probably not levels. A box is ticked without a level on 16, 15 and 25 visits for clomipramine, fluoxetine and venlafaxine, and on 0 to 3 for the other drugs. Open: shown_if on the levels (the display rule of the form is known, decision D125) would remove the 11 lithium levels that have no box. A level can be checked against the dated treatments of the cohort only for 3% (lithium, 5 of 146) to 27% (venlafaxine, 45 of 165) of them: the match is a treatment of the same molecule, started before the visit and not ended, which is found for 12 of 135 clomipramine levels, 6 of 66 fluoxetine, 2 of 11 valproate, 1 of 19 amitriptyline and none of the others, against 78% for lithium in BP (3,642 of 4,648). The treatments of this cohort are too sparse to check a level. Shifted visits: the 30 visits of one centre, up to 2022, whose block of results is shifted (see the blood-count schema; 23 of them have a number in place of a unit code in the vitamin results, see vitamines_cortisol). This schema belongs to the pool biology (implausible_visits: 3, implausible_pool: biology; see the blood-count schema): a visit with three or more impossible values over the eleven laboratory schemas of DR loses all its values and gets visit_removed. The pool removes 35 visits in all (1,403 cells); this schema loses 478 cells on 35 visits, boxes included: 407 on the 30 visits of the block and 71 on 5 other visits. The block held 27 levels (oxcarbazepine 12, valproate 6, venlafaxine 5, amitriptyline 3, lithium 1), none of them delivered any more; its impossible values here are numbers in a box (10), years in the delay (3) and lithium levels of 35 or more (3). Levels are winsorised at the 99th percentile only: the 5 results above it become the cut value (lithium 1.32 mmol/L, clomipramine 424 µg/L, fluoxetine 738 µg/L and venlafaxine 742 µg/L, 2 results), so a clinical tail turns into the cut value (a lithium above 1.32 is delivered as 1.32), and the hard ranges remove the impossible levels (4 lithium results above 3 mmol/L). Steps of the delay since the last intake (groups of 20 results or more; the cause is not known, a habit of the centre, since the answers are heaped on 12 and 24 hours): one centre has a median of 24 hours against 12 for all (1.12 interquartile ranges, 48 results; 56% of its answers are 24, against 20% overall), and the year 2025 has 23.5 (1.07, 20 results), 70% of them from a centre that appears in 2023 (median 18 hours over its 42 results). Two levels are unparsed (one fluoxetine and one venlafaxine): a number of three digits followed by its unit, written in the level field. Same instrument as in FACE BP for the levels that BP has; the columns, the boxes and the antidepressants are those of the TRD form.
dr.difference: the columns and the boxes of the TRD form; five antidepressant levels that BP does not have; no clozapine, lamotrigine or red-cell lithium

asp.notes: The section of the drug levels is almost empty in this cohort. Eight boxes (psychotrop_1 to psychotrop_8: which level was asked for) are filled on 546 inclusion visits and 59 follow-up visits and are 0 on all of them but two (the Lamictal box on two inclusion visits): 544 of the 546 inclusion visits carry no information. A box before them (cmyn, from 2020) is yes on 7 of 118 visits. Of the five levels, only the lamotrigine has a value, on those two visits, and one of the two is out of range; the lithium, the carbamazepine, the oxcarbazepine and the valproate columns are empty (ignored.yaml). The order of the boxes is that of the level columns (lithium after the box 2, carbamazepine after 3, oxcarbazepine after 4, valproate after 7, lamotrigine after 8); the thesaurus names the eight boxes, the drug whose level is measured: Téralithe 250, Téralithe LP 400, Tégrétol, Trileptal, Dépakine, Dépakote, Dépamide, Lamictal. The first box (cmyn) says whether the patient took the treatment on the morning of the sample. Same instrument name as in FACE BP and DR, with this cohort's columns. The clip at the 1% and 99% percentiles turns a clinical tail into the cut value and the hard range removes impossible values; here no value is clipped and one is out of range.
asp.difference: eight boxes that name the drug whose level is measured (thesaurus), a box that says whether the treatment was taken that morning, and the lamotrigine level; the other level columns are empty

dosage_psychotropes.description: Plasma levels of psychotropic drugs measured with the blood sample of the visit (lithium, lithium in the red cells, valproate, carbamazepine, oxcarbazepine, lamotrigine and clozapine in BP; clozapine only in SZ; DR adds five antidepressants), and whether the treatment was taken that morning.
sources: schema notes (bp, sz, dr, asp dosage_psychotropes)
flags: No sampling time and no dose are recorded, so a level cannot be put against the time since the last dose. DR has the hours since the last intake, heaped on 12 and 24 hours.
A level of 0 is 'nothing measured' and is a missing code; a level below the limit of the laboratory is left-censored.
Only the upper tail is winsorised, at the 99th percentile: a toxic level cannot be told from the cut value (in BP a lithium above 1.31 mmol/L is delivered as 1.31).

A few results are on a molar scale and are converted by their size (unit_inferred). Lamotrigine in µmol/L overlaps its high levels in mg/L, so only values of 20 and more are converted; clozapine results of 1 to 20 that may be µmol/L are out of range, not converted.
DR: the antidepressant levels are delivered in µg/L, and those typed in mg/L are converted by their size.
A level with no dated treatment on file is not an error: the treatment lists are incomplete.

ASP: the section is almost empty (one delivered lamotrigine level). BP and DR: a visit with three or more impossible values over the laboratory schemas loses all its laboratory values (visit_removed).

common.note: Each cohort measures the drugs of its own treatments: lithium, valproate and carbamazepine are in BP and DR (few values in DR), clozapine in BP and SZ, and ASP has almost no level. No drug level is in the four cohorts. A level of 0 is a missing code (the laboratory writes '<x'). Only 'treatment taken that morning' is recorded, no sampling time and no dose.

nfs.title: Full blood count (NFS)

bp.notes: How the units are read (the same in every schema of this tab). The unit column is filled by the form with a default label, also where there is no result, so it proves little. Each analyte lists the units that occur, with the values one expects on each scale. A value that fits its label keeps it. A value that cannot be on the labelled scale and fits exactly one other is converted and flagged (unit_inferred, or unit_doubt when it was possible but unlikely under its label). A value that fits no scale is left as it is and the hard range decides (out_of_range). Haemoglobin. Almost all of the 13,505 results are labelled g/dL, but 476 of them are 50 or more: they are g/L. They come mostly from two centres between 2010 and 2022, mixed cell by cell with correctly scaled values, so a rule by centre or period would not work. The magnitude decides. Twelve cells are labelled mmol/L but hold values from 12 to 96; that label is not listed, so it counts as unknown and the magnitude decides. Haematocrit: 480 results are fractions (0.41 for 41%), and 58 have lost their decimal point (411 for 41.1). MCHC: 554 results are in g/L. The default labels of MCH and MCHC say "%"; the values are pg and g/dL. Counts per mm3. Leukocytes, platelets and the five kinds of white cells are sometimes written per mm3 (5300 for 5.3 G/L): 38 leukocyte results, 20 platelet results and 40 to 51 results of each kind of white cell. White cells in percent (decision D30 in PROGRESS.md). Some results are percentages of the leukocytes instead of counts: about 40 visits have the five kinds in percent, and several hundred single cells do, mostly basophils. Almost none is labelled "%". A percentage is recognised by its label or by its size: a value too large to be a count (25 G/L of neutrophils, 12 of lymphocytes, 2.5 of monocytes, 1.5 of eosinophils, 0.3 of basophils) is one. It is converted with the leukocytes of the same visit, value x leukocytes / 100: 845 results (462 basophils, 128 monocytes, 108 eosinophils, 84 lymphocytes, 63 neutrophils). Thirteen more cannot be converted, because the visit has no valid leukocyte count (unit_unknown). The limits were checked against the visit totals: with the other four kinds as read, does the visit add up when this value is a count, or when it is a percentage? For eosinophils the two scales overlap. From 1.5 on, the visit adds up as a percentage far more often than as a count (75 visits against 9), so the value is read as one, with unit_doubt up to 5. Under 1.5 it stays a count, although on 65 of the 376 visits with an eosinophil result of 0.6 to 1.5 the five kinds add up to the leukocytes only if that result is a percentage: those visits fail the check below and the value is left as it is (an eosinophil count of 0.6 to 1.5 G/L is possible, so the size alone does not decide). The custom check differential_differs flags the visits where the five kinds do not add up to the leukocytes within 10% (check_failed, on leukocytes): 221 of the 13,223 complete visits, 152 of them with the kinds adding up to more than the leukocytes and 69 to less. The kinds add up on 98% of the complete visits (96% before the percentages were converted). The failures show no step between the periods (1.3% to 2.2% in each) and are 9.6% in one centre against 0% to 4.3% in the other centres of 100 visits or more. The tolerance of 10% is sound: at 5% 359 visits would fail, at 15% 149. MCV: 31 results between 5 and 13 have a misplaced decimal point (9.07 for 90.7). MCH: 10 results are in fmol. Platelets: 58 results of 0.98 to 9.8 (52 of them in one centre; 47 of the 58 from 2011 to 2013, 28 in 2012) are counts typed in hundreds of G/L, as in 2.47 x 10^5 per mm3: the unit "x100 G/L" reads them (unit_inferred; median 252 G/L after the conversion, as for the whole cohort; decision D130). Four results stay out_of_range: 0.24, 0.39 and 0.43 (below 0.5, which would be 24 to 43 G/L) and a count of 2,950,000 per mm3. Shifted block and pool. This schema belongs to the pool biology (implausible_visits: 3, see biochimie): a visit with three or more impossible values over the seven laboratory schemas of BP loses all its values here too and gets visit_removed. The pool removes 29 visits in all (998 cells); this schema loses 239 cells on 29 visits (143 on 20 visits of the shifted block of one centre, 96 on 9 other visits). The 4 block visits that escape the pool (see biochimie) still deliver 25 values here. Winsorising (step 12) clips each number at its 1st and 99th percentile, so a clinical tail becomes the cut value (in BP a haemoglobin below 11.0 g/dL is delivered as 11.0, a neutrophil count below 1.48 G/L as 1.48, a platelet count above 445 G/L as 445 and a leukocyte count above 13.5 G/L as 13.5: 246 to 266 values per variable are clipped), while the hard range ([5, 25] for the haemoglobin, [0, 25] for the neutrophils, [10, 1500] for the platelets) is what removes impossible values. Centre and year steps (qc site_shift and year_shift, read on 2026-11-19), with no unit involved and no known cause: 2,068 basophil results (15%) are exactly 0, 53% of the results of one centre and 32% of another against 0% to 6% in 11 of the other 12 centres, and 55% of the results of 2010 against 2% of 2025, so the basophil median is 0 in the first centre and in 2010 (1.0 IQR below the overall 0.04 G/L, IQR 0.04) and 0.03 in the second (0.25 IQR); the MCHC of one centre of 2024 to 2026 (43 results) has a median of 32.3 g/dL against 33.6 (1.1 IQR below, IQR 1.2), with 15 of its values at the lower clip and an ordinary haemoglobin and haematocrit. Both are left as measured.

sz.notes: Seven of the thirteen values of the BP blood count, with the same units and limits: leukocytes, erythrocytes, haemoglobin, neutrophils, eosinophils, mean cell volume and platelets. Haemoglobin: 32 results are in g/L under the label g/dL (148 for 14.8), 2 labelled g/L are converted and 2 labelled mmol/L are read in g/dL by their size. Leukocytes (5) and platelets (3) per mm3; 2 platelet counts are written in hundreds of G/L (2.5 for 250, as in 2.5 x 10^5 per mm3, BP D130) and read with the unit x100 G/L (unit_inferred). Neutrophils: 20 results typed as a percentage of the leukocytes and 3 per mm3. Eosinophils: 37 results could be a percentage (unit_doubt), 2 are read as a percentage and 2 per mm3 (unit_inferred). Mean cell volume: 16 results ten times too small. 15 results are out of range: 1 leukocytes, 1 erythrocytes, 4 haemoglobin and 9 mean cell volume. The clip at the 1st and 99th percentile turns a clinical tail into the cut value, on 36 to 74 results per variable; the hard range is what removes impossible values. Same instrument as in FACE BP, without the six values that the SZ extraction does not hold (haematocrit, basophils, lymphocytes, monocytes, MCH, MCHC). The BP check that the five kinds of white cells add up to the leukocytes cannot be made with two kinds. The weaker test that neutrophils plus eosinophils do not exceed 1.1 times the leukocytes fails on 8 of 3,630 visits (unwinsorised values).
sz.difference: seven of the thirteen BP values, in columns named for the analyte; no check of the white-cell differential

dr.notes: The blood count: thirteen values on about 1,140 visits. For the haematocrit and the MCHC the form has a choice of unit, exported as a code: 1 is % and 2 L/L for the haematocrit (205 results converted), 1 is g/dL and 2 g/L for the MCHC (287 converted). The other values have the default label only: 26 haemoglobins are read as g/L (22 of them on the shifted visits below, 4 in one other centre), and 28 neutrophils and 26 basophils are written as a percentage or per mm3 (unit_inferred). In one centre the results of one laboratory block were typed in the wrong fields, shifted by seven fields of the eCEDR table, on 30 visits dated up to 2022 (the unit field of the vitamin results holds a number on 23 of them, see vitamines_cortisol). Here they show as a 0 for the MCV, the MCH, the MCHC and the platelets (115 cells: 29, 30, 26 and 30), a number other than the code 1 or 2 in the unit cell of the MCHC (19 visits), and red cells or basophils out of range. Every laboratory schema of DR carries `implausible_visits: 3` and `implausible_pool: biology`: the impossible values (out_of_range) of the eleven schemas are counted on each visit, and a visit with three or more loses all its values in every schema of the pool and gets visit_removed, with the number of impossible values as detail (section 4 of SCHEMA_SPEC.md). The pool removes 35 visits in all (1,403 cells): the 30 visits of the block (4 to 18 impossible values each; none escapes, and no other visit of that centre holds more than one impossible value) and 5 visits of 5 other centres (3 to 10 impossible values, 3 of them spread over several schemas and 2 with 3 in the biochemistry alone). This schema loses 180 cells on 29 visits: 124 on 24 visits of the block (among them 22 of the 26 haemoglobins read as g/L) and 56 on 5 other visits. The results of the block that fall inside their range are as wrong as those that do not. A 0 is not "nothing measured" here, as it is for the prolactin: all 115 are on these 30 visits and none is left once they are removed. They stay out_of_range because they count towards the rule: read as a missing code they would not, and the pool would catch only 23 of the 30 block visits. The white-cell differential does not add up to the leukocytes on 22 of 1,113 visits (2.0%, check_failed); the check is right. The 1% and 99% winsorising turns a clinical tail into the cut value, and only the hard range removes impossible values. Centre step of the basophils: one centre has a median of 0.00 G/L against 0.04 for all (-1.0 interquartile range, 147 results, groups of 20 results or more), which fits a laboratory that writes them with one decimal (13 distinct values, 92% on a grid of 0.1, 108 results exactly 0); two other centres have 26 of 65 and 13 of 55 results exactly 0, and the others 0% to 3%. Same instrument as in FACE BP.
dr.difference: the results are in columns named for the analyte; the unit of the haematocrit and of the MCHC is exported as a code

asp.notes: Ten values of the blood count, on 499 inclusion visits and 50 follow-up visits. Same analytes, names, target units and ranges as in FACE SZ and DR. The extraction has no unit column for these analytes (open question O6): the unit is read from the size of the value, and a result that only another unit explains is converted and flagged unit_inferred. What the values show: the form prints g/100ml beside the haemoglobin, but 113 of the 547 results (20.7%) are in g/L and are converted to g/dL: one haemoglobin in five has an inferred unit. A few differential counts are percentages of the leukocytes (4 neutrophil, 6 basophil, 6 eosinophil, 6 lymphocyte and 10 monocyte results) and are converted with the leukocytes of the visit. 13 mean corpuscular volumes are under 50 fL and one is above 130: no unit of this schema explains them (out_of_range). 12 of the 13 lie between 5 and 13, the pattern that BP reads with a "10 fL" unit (a misplaced decimal point); ASP does not declare that unit. The custom check differential_differs flags the visits where the five kinds of white cells do not add up to the leukocytes within 10% (check_failed, on leukocytes), as in BP and DR: 6 of the 503 visits that have the five kinds and the leukocytes. It only flags; no value changes. The default clip at the 1% and 99% percentiles turns a clinical tail into the cut value (83 of the 5,215 values here); the hard range is what removes impossible values (24 results here). Centre step of the basophils: one centre has a median of 0.00 G/L against 0.04 for all (-1.0 interquartile range, 182 results, groups of 20 results or more; 99 exactly 0, 11 distinct values, 70% on a grid of 0.1), which fits a laboratory that writes them with one decimal, as in DR; the years 2017 to 2019 (median 0, 71% to 75% of zeros) are the years of that centre, which gives 89% to 100% of their results.
asp.difference: no unit column, so a differential count is read as a percentage of the leukocytes from the size of its value; ten values

nfs.description: Full blood count from the blood sample of the visit: leukocytes and their five kinds, erythrocytes, haemoglobin, haematocrit, red-cell indices and platelets (thirteen values in BP and DR, seven in SZ, ten in ASP).
sources: schema notes (bp, sz, dr, asp nfs)
flags: Haemoglobin typed in g/L and white cells typed as a percentage of the leukocytes or per mm3 are converted by their size (unit_inferred or unit_doubt); in ASP one haemoglobin in five has an inferred unit. Units are harmonised. Where the unit label is absent or says nothing, the unit is read from the size of the value: a converted value carries unit_inferred or unit_doubt, and a value that fits two units is missing (unit_unknown).
A visit whose five kinds of white cells do not add up to the leukocytes within 10% carries check_failed on leukocytes (BP, DR, ASP); no value changes.
Basophils are exactly 0 for a large share of the results of a few centres (a laboratory that writes one decimal).

By default each number is clipped at its 1st and 99th percentiles (winsorising), so a clinical tail becomes the cut value; only the hard range removes impossible values. Load with winsorise=False to keep the tails.
BP and DR: a visit with three or more impossible values over the laboratory schemas loses all its laboratory values (visit_removed).

common.note: Seven values are in the four cohorts, in the same units; lymphocytes, monocytes and basophils in BP, DR and ASP; haematocrit, MCH and MCHC in BP and DR. The differential counts are checked against the leukocytes in BP, DR and ASP (SZ has two kinds only). The 1% and 99% clipping turns clinical tails (neutropenia, thrombopenia, anaemia) into the cut value.

ecg.title: Electrocardiogram

bp.notes: The intervals are in seconds in the dictionary. Part of them are written in milliseconds (413 for 0.413 s), more and more often since 2023, and a few in hundredths of a second (39 for 0.39 s). The unit is recognised from the size of the value and the cell is flagged unit_inferred. A value of 0 stands for "not measured" in the heart rate and the three intervals: missing code. The RR interval holds 76 values that fit no unit: 45 under 0.3, and 25 from 30 to 300, which look like heart rates typed in the wrong field. They are out_of_range. The RR against the heart rate of the same ECG (decision D114 in PROGRESS.md, by the project lead). The two say the same thing: RR is 60 divided by the heart rate. They agree within 10% on 81% of the 7,861 visits that have both, and differ by more than 30% on 739. Two centres hold most of these: their RR fits the heart rate on 23% of their visits (73% to 97% in the other centres with more than 100 visits), with a median RR of 1.1 s for a rate of 70, while their QT is the one of the other centres. There the typed RR equals the heart rate divided by 60 on 89% of the visits (58% in a third, small centre, 2% to 14% elsewhere): the help text of the field says to divide the heart rate by 60, the inverse of the right 60 / rate (defect A84 in docs/EXPORT_REQUESTS.md). The custom check rr_differs_from_rate flags these RR (check_failed); the value is kept. The question "ECG done" opens the four measures: none is filled after a no (2,538 visits). After a yes, 3,045 of 13,077 visits (23%) have no measure (26% to 31% in each period from 2019). 675 stored QTc have no RR (634 of them in 2013-2015, 659 in three centres); 611 of the 656 that have a QT and a heart rate are within 0.03 s of Bazett's formula on the heart rate, so these QTc were not computed by the form from a typed RR. The gate is delivered as it is: no change of encoding. QTc. The form computes it with Bazett's formula, QT divided by the square root of RR, on the numbers as typed. Two defects follow. When QT and RR are not on the same scale the stored QTc is absurd (0.013 or 13): 168 stored values are out_of_range. And where the typed RR does not fit the heart rate, the stored QTc is wrong: in the two centres above its median is 0.37, against 0.40 to 0.42 elsewhere, and a third are under 0.35. qtc_bazett is therefore computed from the harmonised QT and the heart rate of the ECG (RR = 60 / rate; custom function corrected_qt), and from the typed RR only where there is no heart rate (58 visits). It exists on 8,963 visits, against 8,470 valid stored values; in the two centres its median is 0.42 and under 1% are below 0.35, as elsewhere. It differs from the stored one by more than 0.03 s on 1,185 visits (score_mismatch), 737 of them in the two centres. qtc_stored is the stored value on the harmonised scale. The form also asks whether the ECG was sent to a cardiologist and whether an opinion was requested; the extraction does not hold these two answers. No value is winsorised (winsor: false on the heart rate, the QT, the RR and the stored QTc, and no winsor on the score qtc_bazett), the user's decision of 2026-11-21 for BP, SZ and DR: the hard ranges remove the impossible values, and the values beyond the 1st and 99th percentiles are real measures; a corrected QT above 0.5 s is the prolongation that a study of drug safety looks for, and the default limit (about 0.50 s) brought it back. Cells no longer clipped: heart rate 190, QT 141, RR 158, stored QTc 167, computed QTc 180 (winsorised 836 -> 0).

sz.notes: The SZ extraction holds one ECG column, the corrected QT interval that the EMR stores (2,855 visits). The form asks the QT and the RR intervals (mesqt and elec_rr in the field table of the application), but the export keeps the QTc only (eschizo_infirmier.sql, line 21; face_sz_7, line 21), so the QTc cannot be recomputed here and item 5 of the definition of done does not apply (request R159: export the QT and the RR). The form has no heart rate. The script of the clone of the application has its QTc and BMI handlers commented out (inf_dossier_infirmier.js, lines 39 to 43 and 93 to 95), yet a QTc is stored every year to 2026: which script computes it in the centres is question M80. It is in seconds in the dictionary. The unit is recognised from the size of the value and the cell is flagged unit_inferred: 1 value is in milliseconds and none in hundredths of a second. 27 values fit no unit and end out_of_range (12 under 0.05, 4 from 0.05 to 0.2, 11 from 0.7 to 2). A value of 0 would be "not measured" (missing code; none here). In BP the EMR computes this value from the QT and RR as typed, and it is absurd where the two are not on the same scale (0.013 or 13); in all four applications the help text of the RR field says to divide the heart rate by 60, the inverse of the right 60 / rate (A84). The out-of-range values here are of the same kind. Centre E stores almost no QTc: 5 of its 428 visits with a height have one (2014 to 2021), against 28% to 97% of these visits in the other centres. The values do not step by year or by centre (medians 0.39 to 0.42 s). Same instrument as in FACE BP, reduced to the stored value. No value is winsorised (winsor: false on the stored QTc), the user's decision of 2026-11-21 for BP, SZ and DR: the hard ranges remove the impossible values, and the values beyond the 1st and 99th percentiles are real measures; a corrected QT above 0.5 s is the prolongation that a study of drug safety looks for, and the default limit (about 0.50 s) brought it back. Cells no longer clipped: stored QTc 54 (winsorised 54 -> 0).
sz.difference: the SZ extraction holds the stored QTc only, so nothing is recomputed

dr.notes: Heart rate, QT and RR intervals and the corrected QT that the EMR stores, at the inclusion and follow-up visits (about 1,050 visits). The form asks whether an ECG was done (js/formulaires.js, lines 2833 to 2840) and the clean model of the export reads it, but the TRD extraction does not carry it, nor the boxes "sent to" and "read by the cardiologist" (request R158). The form asks for seconds. The QT was typed in milliseconds or centiseconds on 87 visits and the RR in milliseconds on 61, most of them from 2012 to 2016 and two thirds in one centre: they are converted (unit_inferred). Impossible values are removed (out_of_range): 24 heart rates, 12 QT, 38 RR and 15 stored QTc, among them heart rates of 1 and RR intervals of 0; one recomputed QTc is out of range too. The help text of the RR field says to divide the heart rate by 60, the inverse of the right 60 / rate (A84): the typed RR equals the heart rate divided by 60 on 51 of the 1,013 visits with both, 0% to 7% of the visits of each centre with 20 visits or more but 38% in one centre (10 of 26). The corrected QT is recomputed with Bazett's formula on the harmonised QT and the heart rate of the ECG (RR = 60 / rate), and on the typed RR only where there is no heart rate, as in BP (BP decision D114): in BP the RR typed in two centres does not fit the heart rate. Here the two agree within 10% on 90% of the visits and differ by more than 30% on 28, which get check_failed on the RR. The QTc is computed on 1,009 visits and differs from the stored one by more than 0.03 s on 70 (score_mismatch). The stored QTc is Bazett's formula on the typed QT and RR: on the numbers as typed it agrees within 1.5% on 520 of the 522 visits from 2017 (within 0.006 s on 502 once the units are harmonised), against 295 of the 435 visits until 2016 (329 within 0.006 s). The 106 visits of 2012 to 2016 that do not fit are a median 3% below Bazett; no formula fits them (Fridericia and Framingham fit worse in both periods; question M82). Centres (2026-11-20). One centre has a faster heart rate on 89 ECGs (median 82 against 72 in the cohort) and a shorter RR (0.73 s against 0.84), and also lying and standing (pression_arterielle: 84 and 95 against 75 and 82): the three measures agree with each other, so this is not a unit or a typing step; its cause (patients, treatments, the time of the recording) is not known. The centre medians of the heart rate go from 64 to 82, of the QT from 0.36 to 0.41 s and of the stored QTc from 0.40 to 0.44 s (at most 0.6 of an interquartile range); the years show no step above 0.3 of an interquartile range. Same instrument as in FACE BP, without the question "ECG done". No value is winsorised (winsor: false on the heart rate, the QT, the RR and the stored QTc, and no winsor on the score qtc_bazett), the user's decision of 2026-11-21 for BP, SZ and DR: the hard ranges remove the impossible values, and the values beyond the 1st and 99th percentiles are real measures; a corrected QT above 0.5 s is the prolongation that a study of drug safety looks for, and the default limit (about 0.50 s) brought it back. Cells no longer clipped: heart rate 14, QT 17, RR 18, stored QTc 20, computed QTc 20 (winsorised 89 -> 0).
dr.difference: the TRD extraction has no "ECG done" question

asp.notes: QT, RR and corrected QT intervals, recorded from 2024 only: 48 inclusion visits. Same instrument as in FACE BP and DR, without the heart rate of the ECG and with one more box (ecgcard, yes on 16 of 40 visits: the ECG was sent to a cardiologist). The intervals are typed in seconds or in milliseconds: the size of the value tells which, and a value in milliseconds is converted (unit_inferred). A 0 would be read as not recorded, as in BP and DR (none is in this extraction); the box ecgcard keeps its 0 (no). The corrected QT is typed by hand: form 194 (lines 30-34) prints the formula QTc = QT / square root of RR, with QT and RR in seconds, and computes nothing. It is recomputed here with Bazett's formula on the typed QT and RR, since this extraction has no heart rate of the ECG (BP and DR use the heart rate, BP decision D114), and the stored value is the check (and stays delivered as qtc_stored, the name SZ shares): it is within 0.005 s of the formula on 33 of the 36 visits that have both and within the tolerance of 0.03 s on 36; 8 visits have QT and RR and no stored QTc. The help text of the form says that RR may be computed by dividing the heart rate by 60, the inverse of the right 60 / rate (A84); here the typed RR is close to 60 / pulse on 17 of the 41 visits with a pulse and close to pulse / 60 on 1, so the error of the BP centres is not seen. The box 'ECG done' (egyn), which gates QT, RR, QTc and the cardiologist boxes in the form (eASPERGER.js lines 9600-9615), and the second cardiologist box (cardyn) are in the clean model of the export and not in the extraction (request R158). Years and centres (definition of done, D88; centres lettered as in D77, A the children's centre): 48 visits from 2024, no group of 20 by year with a shift; no step.
asp.difference: no heart rate of the ECG and no box 'ECG done' in this extraction (R158), so the corrected QT is computed from the typed RR; one more box (ecgcard), whose 0 is a no; no check of the RR against the rate

ecg.description: Electrocardiogram of the visit: whether it was done (BP), the heart rate, the QT and RR intervals in seconds, the corrected QT that the EMR stores, and the corrected QT recomputed with Bazett's formula. SZ holds the stored corrected QT only.
sources: schema notes (bp, sz, dr, asp ecg)
flags: Use qtc_bazett where it exists (BP, DR, ASP). The stored value is absurd where QT and RR were not typed on the same scale, and too short in two BP centres whose typed RR is the heart rate divided by 60 (the help text of the field says so, the inverse of the right 60 / rate); those RR carry check_failed.
SZ exports the stored corrected QT only: it cannot be recomputed there.
Intervals typed in milliseconds or hundredths of a second are converted to seconds (unit_inferred).
Bazett's formula over-corrects at high heart rates (Vandenberk et al. 2016, confirmed in scale_reference_rest.md section 3).
BP, SZ and DR: no value of the ECG is winsorised; the hard ranges remove the impossible values, and a corrected QT above 0.5 s stays as measured.
ASP: recorded from 2024 only (48 inclusion visits).

common.note: The stored corrected QT is in the four cohorts. The intervals, and the QTc recomputed with the Bazett formula, are in BP, DR and ASP; SZ holds the stored QTc only, with no way to check its formula. ASP has few ECGs. Prefer qtc_bazett: in BP and DR it is computed from the heart rate of the ECG, because the RR typed in the form does not always fit that heart rate, and the stored QTc follows the typed RR. The help text of the RR field in the four applications says to divide the heart rate by 60, the inverse of 60 / rate, and in some centres the typed RR is that (A84). qtc_stored stays delivered in the four cohorts so that SZ can be joined.

parametres_physiques.title: Height, weight, body mass index and waist

bp.notes: These columns have no unit column, and a few values are written on another scale: a height whose decimal point the export removed (1725 for 172.5 cm), a weight with a lost decimal point (8602 for 86.02 kg). The unit is recognised from the size of the value and the cell is flagged unit_inferred. The stored body mass index confirms these readings: on the visits where a height or a weight is rescaled and a body mass index is stored, the stored index equals the one computed from the rescaled values. Height. The form accepts a decimal (its help text gives 170.5), and the export removes the point (request R23 of docs/EXPORT_REQUESTS.md): 180 four-digit values (178 of them end in 5) and 2 five-digit values, half of them from one centre. The stored body mass index equals the weight divided by the square of value/10 on all 178 four-digit values that have one, and of value/100 on the two others: the centres typed the decimal. A height in metres (1.72) is read too, for the extractions made after the export is corrected; none holds one today. The body mass index is recomputed from the harmonised weight and height (custom function body_mass_index: weight divided by the square of the height, the formula of the form) and compared with the stored one, which is rounded to one decimal: 34 visits differ by more than the rounding (score_mismatch). It is also computed on the 246 visits where the EMR stored none. Seven stored values have no height or weight beside them and are not delivered. A waist under 40 cm is impossible for an adult: out_of_range (17 values). Pregnancy. The form has a box "pregnant woman" next to these measures; the extraction does not hold it, so the weight, the body mass index and the waist of a pregnant woman cannot be told apart. It is asked for in QUESTIONS.md (DM-10). One centre records these measures on 38% of its visits; the others on 59% to 86%. The medians do not move between the periods. No value is winsorised (winsor: false on the height, the weight and the waist, and no winsor on the score bmi), the user's decision of 2026-11-21 for BP, SZ and DR, as in ASP (D80, rule R34): the hard ranges remove the impossible values, and the values beyond the 1st and 99th percentiles are real measures (obesity, hypertension, a slow or fast pulse) that the default would bring back to the percentile. Cells no longer clipped: height 236 cells, weight 308, waist 309, body mass index 327 (winsorised 1,180 -> 0).

Of the 578 visits that hold the three raw numbers, 5 stored values differ from the formula, 3 of them next to a height that is not possible; 6 stored values are out of range and are not compared (out_of_range of the hidden bmi_stored). No value is winsorised (winsor: false on the four measures and on bmi, rule R34 of this review): the cohort pools children and adults (956 of the 2,318 patients are under 18; 561 of the 1,100 delivered heights are of children), so the 1st and 99th percentiles of the pooled values cut the smallest children and the tallest or heaviest adults, not errors. The change box eclichang is yes on 98% of the follow-up visits of centre C (2014 to 2020) and on 45% of A and 13% of D (2016 to 2020): the box is read differently by the centres, no known cause, documented here.

diva.title: DIVA, diagnostic interview for ADHD in adults (DSM-IV-TR criteria)

bp.notes: DIVA, the diagnostic interview for attention deficit and hyperactivity in adults, with the criteria of DSM-IV-TR: nine criteria of attention deficit and nine of hyperactivity-impulsivity, each answered for adult life and for childhood (1 = present, 0 = absent). It is on the DSM-5 inclusion form only. Filled at the inclusion visit of 50 patients, from 2019 to 2026, in eight centres; never at follow-up. Who was evaluated. The block is shown only after a yes to "has the patient been evaluated with the DIVA for ADHD?", a question that the extraction does not hold. The patients are a selection made by the clinician, not a screening of the inclusions, so the DIVA gives no prevalence of ADHD: 24 of the 48 patients with a childhood count reach 6 of 9 criteria in attention or in hyperactivity-impulsivity. The levels rise after 2021 (adult attention: mean 3.1 of 9 in 2019-2021, 6.1 from 2022), partly because the centre with the lowest levels (E) filled 13 of the 22 early ones. Centre C has no DIVA because its DSM-5 form is missing from the export (R20). Scores. The number of criteria present, for each of the four blocks (0 to 9). It is computed where the nine criteria are answered and compared with the stored number. The stored number is typed by the clinician: the application's script that adds up the DIVA answers is loaded for the DSM-IV table only (formspecial_bipolaire.php, line 87), and the DIVA is on the DSM-5 form, so nothing adds the criteria up and the field can be edited. 71 of the 169 complete blocks have no stored number (8 in 2019-2021, 16 in 2022-2023, 47 from 2024). Where it is stored, it agrees on 91 of 98 complete blocks; the 7 others differ by one (score_mismatch: 4 above, 3 below), and for 3 of those 7 the stored number is the right total of another block of the same inclusion, typed in the wrong block. 17 blocks have a stored number although some criteria were not answered (score_not_recomputed): in 13 it is the sum of those that were answered, in 3 no criterion is answered, in 1 it is another number; ours is missing in those 17. Two of the 3 blocks with no criterion answered are on an inclusion that holds no criterion at all, so 51 inclusions hold a DIVA cell and 50 are delivered (all at the inclusion visit, in eight centres, from 2019 to 2026). What the counts mean. The published threshold of the DSM-IV-TR criteria is 6 of 9 in attention or in hyperactivity-impulsivity, for adults and for childhood alike (Kooij and others 2010); the DSM-5 and DIVA-5 threshold for adults is 5 of 9 (Hong and others 2020; scale_reference.md, section 23). The form holds the counts only: the other questions of the interview (the symptoms present more than in other people, the onset before age 7, the impairment in two or more areas) are not in the form, so a diagnosis of ADHD cannot be rebuilt from this schema (request A68). The interview is DSM-IV-TR for every patient, so it is not split by DSM version. It is read whatever the edition of the mood sections of the same visit: 16 of the 50 inclusions are labelled DSM-IV (centres A and E, 2019 to 2022) because their mood answers are on the DSM-IV form, and their DIVA still comes from the DSM-5 form (R70 keeps it so).

dsm4_annee_ecoulee.title: Mood episodes of the year before inclusion, DSM-IV criteria

bp.section: Caractéristique du trouble au cours de l'année ecoulée
bp.notes: The mood episodes of the year before the inclusion visit: one yes/no question (at least one episode), then the number of each kind of episode (depressive, hypomanic, manic, mixed), and for depressive, manic and mixed episodes a yes/no and a number for those with psychotic features. Asked at the inclusion visit only. Yes/no answers are delivered as 1 and 0; "Ne sais pas" is a missing code. DSM-IV and DSM-5 are two editions (decision D9 in PROGRESS.md), asked on two inclusion forms and exported in the same columns. The application stores no edition: the export writes dsm_criteria on the inclusion row, DSM5 where the DSM-5 form holds one of five answers on the mood history, else DSM4 where the DSM-IV form does (DEV-11). The label is DSM-IV until 2019 (7 DSM-5 exceptions), DSM-5 on 24 of 380 labelled inclusions in 2020, 44 of 425 in 2021 and 203 of 238 in 2022 (the 35 DSM-IV ones of 2022 are dated January to May), and DSM-5 on all from 2023. This schema reads the DSM-IV visits; dsm5_annee_ecoulee.yaml reads the others. Both carry the version block of the follow-up schemas (D12, D14, D15): an inclusion with no label is read by the date of the patient's first visit (the screening, where there is one), DSM-IV before 2020 and DSM-5 from 2023 (version_inferred), and has no version from 2020 to 2022 (version_unknown, not delivered). Why labels are missing: see dsm4_depuis_derniere_visite.yaml. In this section 12 unlabelled inclusions are read by date (9 DSM-IV, 3 DSM-5) and 4 of 2020 and 2021 are not delivered (R69 would label them). The DSM-IV form counts mixed episodes; the DSM-5 form has none. The numbers. The form asks a number for each kind of episode, 0 to 20 or ">20" (read as 20 and censored_right: 4 depressive, 5 hypomanic and 1 mixed), only after a yes to the first question (asked_if). Where the first answer is no they are empty in the extraction and are read as 0: with no mood episode in the year, there was no depressive episode. Where the first answer is unknown or empty they stay missing. The boxes. The form has no box per kind of episode: the export writes the four boxes (mhoccur_edm_ly, mhoccur_ehman_ly, mhoccur_epman_ly, mhoccur_epmixt_ly) from the number, 1 where it is 1 or more (">20" included), 0 where it is 0, empty where it is "Ne sais pas" or empty (3,193, 3,039, 3,185 and 3,006 boxes). After a no they are read as 0 like the numbers (843 to 855 visits). They add nothing to the numbers and are delivered so that this section and the follow-up one have the same pair (D53); the export writes the three follow-up boxes the same way, with no mixed one. On 2 visits the first answer is no and the hypomanic number is "Ne sais pas": the box is 0 and the number is missing. Psychotic features. The form shows the three yes/no questions after a yes to the first question, whatever the number of that kind of episode. Where that number is 0 and the rater left the question empty, the answer is 0 too: with no manic episode, no manic episode had psychotic features (asked_if on the box, D122). This gives 90 depressive, 369 manic and 518 mixed zeros. The number with psychotic features is 0 where the yes/no is 0. Answers that contradict each other are delivered as typed: 15 inclusions say yes and then give 0 for every kind of episode; 2 give a number above 0 after a no and 4 give numbers with no first answer or "Ne sais pas"; 23 say yes to psychotic features with no episode of that kind; 9 give more episodes with psychotic features than episodes of that kind (3 depressive, 4 manic, 2 mixed; flagged check_failed, not_above); the number of episodes in the year is above the lifetime number for 88 inclusions (14 depressive, 29 hypomanic, 23 manic and 25 mixed numbers); 80 of the 1,386 inclusions in a current episode that answer here say no mood episode in the year, and so do 154 of the 2,871 with a most recent episode that started or ended within the year before the visit (dsm4_episode_recent.yaml).
