dsm4_depuis_derniere_visite.title: Mood episodes since the last visit, DSM-IV criteria

bp.section: Caractéristique du trouble depuis la dernière visite à la visite de suivi
bp.notes: The mood episodes since the last visit, asked at the follow-up visits only: one yes/no question (at least one episode), then the number of each kind of episode (depressive, hypomanic, manic, mixed) and their total, the numbers with psychotic features, and the type of the most recent episode. Yes/no answers are delivered as 1 and 0; "Ne sais pas" is a missing code. Editions. DSM-IV and DSM-5 are two editions, in the same columns (decision D9 in PROGRESS.md). The follow-up form is one form for every patient, changed in place from the DSM-IV to the DSM-5 version centre by centre between October 2021 and May 2022. The application stores no edition: the export writes dsm_criteria on the inclusion row only, DSM5 where the DSM-5 inclusion form holds one of five answers on the mood history (type and age of the first episode, numbers of depressive, hypomanic and manic episodes), else DSM4 where the DSM-IV form does (DEV-11). It is empty at 849 of 6,498 inclusions: 206 hold no answer of either form (202 at centre C, whose DSM-5 form the export leaves out, R20), 552 hold only default dates and 91 hold other answers (R69 would label 85 of them). The version of a follow-up visit comes from three decisions. D12. Before 2022 a follow-up visit takes the label of the patient's inclusion. D14. From 1 January 2022 a follow-up visit is DSM-5, whatever the inclusion, in every centre, unless it holds a column that only the old form has (the override, below). So a few visits are read in the other edition. 25 visits answering yes in October to December 2021 (six centres) hold neither the mixed nor the total number, the pattern of the new form, and are read as DSM-IV here, because nothing in the extraction marks them; from 2019 to September 2021 only 32 of the 959 DSM-IV visits answering yes hold neither. The date on which the form was filled ("Date de recueil des informations"), which would date the change of form, is not in the extraction. Override. The follow-up mixed numbers (evnum_epmixt_spv, evnum_epmixt_psy_spv) and the typed total of episodes (evnum_epthym_spv) exist only on the old form: the form of today has no mixed episode and never saves its total. A visit that holds one of these three columns is read as DSM-IV, whatever its label or its date (override in the version block, the same in the twelve schemas of the section). 49 follow-up visits, all answering yes, change edition: 35 that were read as DSM-5 (33 of January to May 2022, 25 and 8 visits in two centres, and 2 of 2021 of patients included with DSM-5; flag version_overridden) and 14 of 2020 and 2021 of patients with no label, which had no version (version_unknown falls from 32 to 18 in the tab). Their 44 mixed numbers and 22 mixed numbers with psychotic features, which were not read, are delivered here. The rule picks only visits that answered yes (the columns exist only after a yes), so the 33 DSM-IV visits of January to May 2022 are 33 yes visits of 33: the year 2022 of this section is not a profile of the year (a yes on 100% of them against 39% to 51% in 2010 to 2021, a depressive episode since the last visit on 94% against 36% to 38% in 2019 to 2021, a median total of 2 against 0). The year shift of the total, of the depressive number and of the current-episode box reads this selection, not a change of habit; leave 2022 out of a trend. D15. A patient with no label is read by the date of the first visit (the screening, where there is one): DSM-IV before 2020 (317 follow-up visits of this section, version_inferred) and DSM-5 from 2023. Patients first seen from 2020 to 2022 have no version before 2022, unless the visit holds a column of the old form (the override): 8 follow-up visits of 2021 (7 answer no, 1 does not know) are not delivered (version_unknown); the 14 that answered yes all hold such a column and are read as DSM-IV. R69 could label some of the patients of the 8 (not counted again). This schema reads the DSM-IV visits: 7,165 visits from 2009 to 2022 (33 of them of January to May 2022). dsm5_depuis_derniere_visite.yaml reads the others. Mixed episodes exist in DSM-IV only. The numbers. 0 to 20 or ">20" (read as 20 and censored_right: 6 depressive, 5 hypomanic and 2 mixed numbers; the typed total has 10, see the total). They are shown only after a yes to the first question; where it is no (3,978 visits) they are empty in the extraction and are read as 0 (asked_if, decision D53): with no mood episode since the last visit, there was no depressive episode. The boxes. The form has no box per kind of episode: the export writes the three boxes (mhoccur_edm_spv, mhoccur_ehman_spv, mhoccur_epman_spv) from the numbers, 1 where the number is 1 or more, 0 where it is 0, empty where it is "Ne sais pas" or empty. There is no mixed box. After a no they are read as 0 like the numbers. Psychotic features. A number with psychotic features is 0 where the number of that kind of episode is 0 and the cell is empty: with no manic episode, none had psychotic features (asked_if on the box, or on the mixed number, D122). This gives 235 depressive, 862 manic and 959 mixed zeros after a yes. The total. dsm4_fu_n_episodes is a score: the sum of the four numbers, depressive, hypomanic, manic and mixed. The form's field "Nombre d'épisodes total" (typed; read as dsm4_fu_n_episodes_stored and not delivered) carries the hint that it must equal the sum of all the episodes since the last visit. The application's script that would compute it (psy_diag_psychiatrique_semestriel.js) adds the depressive, manic and hypomanic numbers only, counts an empty number as 0 and writes into a disabled field, so it is never saved: the typed total is the rater's own. On the 2,533 visits answering yes where every number is known and the typed total is a number, it is the sum of the four numbers on 2,336 (92.2%), below it on 140 and above it on 57. It includes the mixed episodes on 156 of the 207 visits that have a mixed number (the sum without them on 41), and it is below the sum of the depressive, hypomanic and manic numbers on 98. One centre disagrees with the sum on 27% of its 59 visits, the others on 12% or less. Where the two differ, the sum is delivered and the row gets score_mismatch (204 visits, 3 of them typed after a no). Where a number is "Ne sais pas" or empty the sum cannot be made: a typed total is then delivered as typed and gets score_as_stored (349 visits: a number "Ne sais pas" on 89, empty on 257, both on 3; the typed total equals the sum of the known numbers on 303 of the 342 that have one, and 7 have none known). The rule is written with a hidden score (dsm4_fu_n_episodes_sum: the four numbers added where all four are known), because otherwise acts on a score only where none of its items is recorded. Answers that contradict each other are delivered as typed: 3 totals and 1 number with psychotic features above 0 are typed after a no, and a number with psychotic features is above the number of that kind of episode on 13 visits (4 depressive, 2 manic, 7 mixed; flagged check_failed, not_above). 32 visits answer yes and give 0 for every number. Of the 1,616 follow-up visits in a current episode (dsm4_episode_actuel.yaml) that answer this question, 377 say that no episode occurred since the last visit (the DSM-5 twin: 153 of 596): the episodes since the last visit are probably undercounted, or an episode that began earlier is not counted. Window. The question covers the time since the previous visit, which is not one window: the median gap is 195 days at the six-monthly visits and 357 at the yearly ones, and the share of yes answers rises from 40% when the gap is under 150 days (188 visits) to 54% when it is over 600 days (461). Do not compare counts of episodes across visits without the gap (the DSM-5 twin: 31% of 29 visits to 61% of 210). The type of the most recent episode is filled on 2,561 of the 3,185 visits answering yes. The list of today has no mixed type. It most likely had one, whose answers were emptied when the form changed (see dsm4_episode_actuel.yaml): where the only episodes since the last visit were mixed, the type is empty on 79 of 85 visits, against 109 of 1,304 where they were all depressive. A missing type after a yes often means a mixed episode. Not read (ignored.yaml): three columns named like this section (mhoccur_edm_psy_spv, mhoccur_epman_psy_spv, mhoccur_epmixt_psy_spv) are filled at inclusion only (5,056, 4,425 and 4,022 cells) and copy lifetime answers. R72 asks the export to compute them from the follow-up numbers.

A visit that holds a column of the old form (mixed numbers, typed total) is read as DSM-IV whatever its date (flag version_overridden).

common.note: DR's section is headed 'since the last visit', with a window of about six months at most visits (median gap 190 days); the BP window is six months or a year, and the BP DSM-5 edition of 2022 is another schema. Do not compare counts across windows.

dsm4_episode_actuel.title: Current mood episode, DSM-IV criteria

bp.section: Caractéristique du trouble de l'HUMEUR ACTUEL
bp.notes: The mood episode the patient is in on the day of the visit, if any: its type, specifier, severity, chronicity and whether it followed a birth. Filled at the inclusion visit and at every follow-up visit (six-monthly and yearly). It describes the day of the visit at every visit, so the inclusion and the follow-up answers are in the same columns. A third of the inclusions read here are in an episode (1,445 of 4,415) and a quarter of the follow-up visits (1,700 of 7,343). Yes/no answers are delivered as 1 and 0; "Ne sais pas" is a missing code. DSM-IV and DSM-5 are two editions (decision D9 in PROGRESS.md), asked on two inclusion forms and exported in the same columns. The application stores no edition: the export writes dsm_criteria on the inclusion row, DSM5 where the DSM-5 form holds one of five answers on the mood history, else DSM4 where the DSM-IV form does (DEV-11). The label is DSM-IV until 2019 (7 DSM-5 exceptions), DSM-5 on 24 of 380 labelled inclusions in 2020, 44 of 425 in 2021 and 203 of 238 in 2022 (the 35 DSM-IV ones of 2022 are dated January to May), and DSM-5 on all from 2023. This schema reads the DSM-IV visits; dsm5_episode_actuel.yaml reads the others. Both carry the version block of the follow-up schemas: a follow-up visit takes the label of the inclusion before 2022 (D12) and is DSM-5 from 1 January 2022 (D14); a patient with no label is read by the date of the first visit, DSM-IV before 2020 and DSM-5 from 2023 (D15, version_inferred), and has no version from 2020 to 2022 (version_unknown, not delivered). Why labels are missing and which visits D14 reads in the other edition: see dsm4_depuis_derniere_visite.yaml. Here 20 inclusions and 327 follow-up visits are read as DSM-IV by date; the 49 follow-up visits that hold a column of the old form are read as DSM-IV whatever their label (the override of the version block). 15 visits with an answer (5 inclusions of 2020 and 2021 and 10 follow-ups of 2021, 14 patients) have no version and are delivered in neither schema. The inclusion form of DSM-IV has a mixed type of episode (91 visits) and a yes/no "catatonic" asked for a manic or mixed episode (100 visits, 1 of them "Ne sais pas"). Each detail is asked for some types only: the specifier and the chronicity for a depressive episode, the severity for a depressive, manic or mixed one, the postpartum onset for every type but the unspecified one (the form's rule, on the positions of the type list: specifier and chronicity on the depressive type, severity on the depressive, manic and mixed ones, the yes/no "catatonic" on the manic and mixed ones, postpartum on the first four). No shown_if here, unlike dsm4_episode_recent.yaml: it would blank 341 cells (337 before the override), 319 of them at follow-up visits where the type is empty, the residue of the removed mixed type (see below), so that the type is the missing value and the details are real answers; 22 elsewhere. The details are asked only after a yes. After a no the form empties the type of episode, and the start date at follow-up, but not the details asked after the type. 33 visits answered no still hold details (10 inclusions and 23 follow-ups, 2011 to 2021): postpartum 27 (all no), severity 17, chronicity 15 (14 no), type 6, specifier 5. 2 follow-up visits with no answer to the first question hold a type and a start date. All are delivered as written, as in D50. "Chronic" is a judgement of the rater: of the follow-up episodes ticked chronic that have a start date, 45 of 307 began two years or more before the visit, and the share of chronic depressive episodes at inclusion goes from 18% to 74% between centres. The share of inclusions in an episode rises from 27% until 2012 to 37% in 2019-2021, and goes from 15% to 51% between centres; the mixed type is under 1% to 18% of the episodes by centre. One centre (K) gives a melancholic or atypical specifier to 55% of the depressive episodes, the others to 12% or less. At the follow-up visits. The follow-up form, one form for every patient, has no mixed type of episode today. It most likely had one until it changed (October 2021 to May 2022, D14), like the DSM-IV inclusion form whose answer rules it keeps, and those answers were emptied when the type left the list: 164 follow-up visits in an episode have no type (2010 to 2022), 141 of them with a severity and none with a chronicity, as a mixed episode would; 81 count a mixed episode since the last visit. "Episode non spécifié" has a severity on 0 of 44 DSM-IV follow-ups and on 18 of 18 DSM-5 ones. These visits are delivered with no type. The 33 follow-up visits of January to May 2022 that the override reads as DSM-IV (D180) all answered yes to an episode since the last visit, so 64% of them are in an episode today against 24% to 25% of the follow-ups of 2019 to 2021: this is the year shift of the box, a selection and not a change of habit (leave 2022 out of a trend). The follow-up specifier. Until September 2021 it holds almost only the answers that the DSM-5 list kept: 94 of its 99 values (93 of the 98 on a depressive episode) are melancholic, atypical or catatonic, and the DSM-IV answer "none" never appears, so an empty cell means "none" or not answered (87 of the 1,089 follow-up depressive episodes of 2011 to 2020 have a specifier). Its share cannot be compared with the inclusion one. From October 2021 the new list is used: 17 of the 19 values are "none". So 22 follow-up visits carry the DSM-5 wording of "none" (read as none; 17 of October to December 2021, 5 of 2014 to 2019), and 2 carry the DSM-5 specifier "mixed" (2019, 2021), which this form does not have: unknown_code. The start date of the episode exists at the follow-up visits only (1,559 dates). 54 are after the visit (1 to 640 days), delivered as written. 2 have no day or no month and are read as the middle of the period (date_partial). The placeholder 1000-01-01, which the application writes into empty dates since its version of 2024-07-25 (D98), never occurs here. Not in the extraction: the follow-up form asks whether a manic or unspecified episode is catatonic or has mixed features (R68).

dsm4_episode_recent.title: Most recent mood episode at inclusion, DSM-IV criteria

bp.section: Caractéristique  de l'EPISODE LE PLUS RECENT
bp.notes: The most recent mood episode before the inclusion visit: its dates, type, specifier, chronicity, severity and whether it followed a birth. Filled once, at the inclusion visit. Yes/no answers are delivered as 1 and 0; "Ne sais pas" is a missing code. DSM-IV and DSM-5 are two editions (decision D9 in PROGRESS.md), asked on two inclusion forms and exported in the same columns. The application stores no edition: the export writes dsm_criteria on the inclusion row, DSM5 where the DSM-5 form holds one of five answers on the mood history, else DSM4 where the DSM-IV form does (DEV-11). The label is DSM-IV until 2019 (7 DSM-5 exceptions), DSM-5 on 24 of 380 labelled inclusions in 2020, 44 of 425 in 2021 and 203 of 238 in 2022 (the 35 DSM-IV ones of 2022 are dated January to May), and DSM-5 on all from 2023. This schema reads the DSM-IV visits; dsm5_episode_recent.yaml reads the others. Both carry the version block of the follow-up schemas (D12, D14, D15): an inclusion with no label is read by the date of the patient's first visit (the screening, where there is one), DSM-IV before 2020 and DSM-5 from 2023 (version_inferred), and has no version from 2020 to 2022 (version_unknown, not delivered). Why labels are missing: see dsm4_depuis_derniere_visite.yaml. In this section 6 unlabelled inclusions are read by date (5 DSM-IV, 1 DSM-5) and 3 of 2020 and 2021 are not delivered (R69 would label them). The DSM-IV form has a mixed type of episode (245 visits). The specifier of a depressive episode is melancholic, atypical, catatonic or none of the three. Each detail is asked for some types only: the specifier and the chronicity for a depressive episode, the severity for a depressive, manic or mixed one, the postpartum onset for every type but the unspecified one. The form's rule is on the positions of the type list (1 depressive, 2 hypomanic, 3 manic, 4 mixed, 5 unspecified): specifier and chronicity on 1, severity on 1, 3 and 4, the yes/no "catatonic" on 3 and 4, postpartum on 1 to 4, and shown_if applies it. 28 answers of 2009 to 2015 filled where the form hides the question are missing and get not_shown: 24 under a type that hides the question (7 specifiers, 11 chronicities, 6 severities) and 4 under an empty type (2 chronicities, 2 postpartum), the few cells under an empty parent that the rule also blanks (an exception to the rule that a value under an empty parent stays as recorded). The most recent episode or the current one. Where the patient is in an episode at inclusion, the clinicians often described that episode here: of the 1,224 such visits with a type, 902 give the type of the current episode and 619 have no end date (with no current episode, 225 of 2,734 have none). The share with an end date goes from 35% to 69% between centres. Use dsm4_current_* for the episode of the day. Levels. The share of severe episodes without psychotic features falls from 45% of the severities until 2015 to 36% from 2016, within most centres; the DSM-5 form gives 38%. One centre (K) gives a melancholic or atypical specifier to 54% of the depressive episodes, the others to 18% or less. Dates. The start date is the date of an event before the visit (before_visit): 100 of the 3,823 start dates are on or after the visit (95 after it, 67 of them by more than a month, and 5 on the visit day), out_of_range and not delivered (3,723 delivered). The end date is not checked in this way, because the episode may be going on: 289 of the 3,176 end dates are on or after the visit (110 on the visit day, 87 more than a month after) and are delivered as written. 70 end dates are before the start (60 in the same year; swapping the day and the month of one of the two dates repairs 24); 21 of the 70 have a start after the visit, now removed, so 49 pairs remain. 1000-01-01 is the application's placeholder (2 start and 2 end dates, date_placeholder). 19 dates have no day or no month and are read as the middle of the period (date_partial). 1 start date has the year and the month 0000: unparsed, not delivered. The type of the most recent episode recorded at the follow-up visits is another column, read by the schemas of the follow-up form. Not in the extraction: the DSM-IV form asks whether a manic or mixed episode is catatonic (a field labelled "Type d'épisode Catatonique"; R140).

dsm4_premier_episode.title: First mood episode, DSM-IV criteria

bp.notes: The first mood episode of the patient: its type, the age at which it began, whether it came within six months of a birth and whether a cyclothymic period came before. Filled once, at the inclusion visit. Yes/no answers are delivered as 1 and 0; "Ne sais pas" is a missing code. DSM-IV and DSM-5 are two editions (decision D9 in PROGRESS.md), asked on two inclusion forms and exported in the same columns. The application stores no edition: the export writes dsm_criteria on the inclusion row, DSM5 where the DSM-5 form holds one of five answers on the mood history, else DSM4 where the DSM-IV form does (DEV-11). The label is DSM-IV until 2019 (7 DSM-5 exceptions), DSM-5 on 24 of 380 labelled inclusions in 2020, 44 of 425 in 2021 and 203 of 238 in 2022 (the 35 DSM-IV ones of 2022 are dated January to May), and DSM-5 on all from 2023. This schema reads the DSM-IV visits; dsm5_premier_episode.yaml reads the others. Both carry the version block of the follow-up schemas (D12, D14, D15): an inclusion with no label is read by the date of the patient's first visit (the screening, where there is one), DSM-IV before 2020 and DSM-5 from 2023 (version_inferred), and has no version from 2020 to 2022 (version_unknown, not delivered). Why labels are missing: see dsm4_depuis_derniere_visite.yaml. In this section 6 unlabelled inclusions, which hold only a postpartum or a cyclothymic answer, are read as DSM-IV by date, and 3 of 2020 and 2021 are not delivered (R69 would label them). No inclusion labelled DSM-IV holds a first-episode answer that only the DSM-5 form has; 9 inclusions labelled DSM-5 hold the DSM-IV form (see dsm5_premier_episode.yaml, R70). The DSM-IV form has two more types of first episode, mixed with and without psychotic features (91 patients). The age is the age at the first episode, whatever its type (D89). The form offers "<5", 5 to 89 and ">89": "<5" is read as 5 and censored_left (2 patients), ">89" as 89 and censored_right (none), as for the age at the first hospitalisation (D54, D122). 4 ages are above the age at the inclusion visit (by 0.1, 0.4, 2.3 and 4.2 years: only the two above one year are errors); they are delivered as written and flagged check_failed (not_above the age at the visit). The postpartum question is asked of every patient: the 1,628 men who answer give 0, and 169 of the 2,712 women (6.2%) give 1, so a rate is computed among women. The initial cyclothymic period is yes for 13% of the patients (496 of 3,887): 31% in centres G and H, 5% to 6% in L and I, steady over the years; "Ne sais pas" goes from 5% to 21% by centre. Answers that contradict others are delivered as written: 28 first episodes are of a kind whose lifetime number is 0; 46 with psychotic features go with a lifetime no to psychotic features of that kind (26 depressive, 13 manic, 7 mixed); 15 patients with a bipolar II diagnosis have a manic or mixed first episode.

dsm4_vie_entiere.title: Mood disorder over the whole life, DSM-IV criteria

bp.notes: The mood disorder over the whole life, as recorded at the inclusion visit: the number of episodes of each kind, those with psychotic features, induced episodes, rapid cycling, remission between episodes, seasonal pattern and the age at the first psychotropic treatment. Yes/no answers are delivered as 1 and 0; "Ne sais pas" is a missing code. DSM-IV and DSM-5 are two editions (decision D9 in PROGRESS.md), asked on two inclusion forms and exported in the same columns. The application stores no edition: the export writes dsm_criteria on the inclusion row, DSM5 where the DSM-5 form holds one of five answers on the mood history, else DSM4 where the DSM-IV form does (DEV-11). The label is DSM-IV until 2019 (7 DSM-5 exceptions), DSM-5 on 24 of 380 labelled inclusions in 2020, 44 of 425 in 2021 and 203 of 238 in 2022 (the 35 DSM-IV ones of 2022 are dated January to May), and DSM-5 on all from 2023. This schema reads the DSM-IV visits; dsm5_vie_entiere.yaml reads the others. Both carry the version block of the follow-up schemas (D12, D14, D15): an inclusion with no label is read by the date of the patient's first visit (the screening, where there is one), DSM-IV before 2020 and DSM-5 from 2023 (version_inferred), and has no version from 2020 to 2022 (version_unknown, not delivered). Why labels are missing: see dsm4_depuis_derniere_visite.yaml. In this section 6 unlabelled inclusions are read by date (4 DSM-IV, 2 DSM-5) and none is left without a version. The DSM-IV form counts mixed episodes; the DSM-5 form has none. Counts. The form stops at 20: ">20" is read as 20 with a mark in the censoring column (this value or more; 236 depressive, 190 hypomanic, 12 manic, 12 mixed, 4 induced and 3 with psychotic features). The range of every lifetime count is 0 to 20, as the form's: no number is out of range. "Ne sais pas" is 15% of the numbers of depressive episodes (5% to 33% by centre), 24% of the hypomanic (9% to 40%), 13% of the mixed and 5% of the manic ones. Psychotic features and induced episodes. The form asks the yes/no about psychotic features of every patient, with or without an episode of that kind. The number of episodes with psychotic features, and of induced episodes, is asked only after a yes (asked_if): it is 0 where the answer to "at least one" is no. The yes/no itself is 0 where the number of that kind of episode is 0 and the rater left it empty (asked_if on the number, D122, as in the DSM-5 lifetime schema and in the year and follow-up sections): 19 depressive, 256 manic and 293 mixed zeros, and the three numbers with psychotic features follow with 0 (1,136 cells in all). Where the number of that kind is "Ne sais pas" or empty the answer stays missing. Answers that contradict each other are delivered as written: 7 numbers above 0 are typed after a no (2 depressive and 3 manic with psychotic features, 2 induced), and 17 induced numbers "Ne sais pas" after a no stay missing; the number with psychotic features is above the number of that kind of episode for 15 manic and 8 mixed (flagged check_failed, not_above); a yes to psychotic features goes with no episode of that kind for 10 manic and 12 mixed. The age at the first psychotropic treatment is a list from "<5" to ">89" on the form: "<5" is read as 5 and censored_left (6 patients), ">89" as 89 and censored_right (none; D122). Delivered as written: 173 of the 4,053 patients with both ages have a first treatment more than two years before their first episode (dsm4_first_episode_age; 4.3%: a psychotropic treatment can come before the first mood episode, so this is not an error); 21 give an age at the first treatment above their age at inclusion (by up to 18.9 years; 8 by more than a year and 7 by two years or more, and only a difference above one year is an error); the 21 are flagged check_failed (not_above the age at the visit). In one centre (J, 74 inclusions of 2015 to 2022) the first treatment comes a median 6 years after the first episode, against 0 to 1 year in the other large centres. Not loaded (ignored.yaml). mhoccur_edm_lt, mhoccur_ehman_lt, mhoccur_epman_lt and mhoccur_epmixt_lt say "Y" where the count of the row is 1 or more and "N" everywhere else, also where the count is unknown or empty and on every row of the other visits: the export writes them, and their "N" does not mean "none" (R71). The three columns mhoccur_edm_psy_spv, mhoccur_epman_psy_spv and mhoccur_epmixt_psy_spv are copies of the lifetime columns read here, filled at inclusion only (R72).

flags: DSM-IV and DSM-5 are two editions, asked on two forms and exported in the same raw columns. Each has its own schema and its own columns (dsm4_ and dsm5_); the two are never delivered in one column (BP decision D9).

The application stores no edition: it is read from the label that the export writes on the inclusion row. The labelled inclusions are DSM-IV until 2019 (7 exceptions), DSM-5 on 24 of 380 in 2020, 44 of 425 in 2021 and 203 of 238 in 2022, and all DSM-5 from 2023. An inclusion with no label is read by the date of the patient's first visit (DSM-IV before 2020, DSM-5 from 2023; flag version_inferred) and is not delivered when that date is in 2020 to 2022 (version_unknown).
A count of 20 is a lower bound (236 depressive, 190 hypomanic, 12 manic, 12 mixed): use the censoring column.
'Ne sais pas' is 15% of the numbers of depressive episodes (5% to 33% by centre), 24% of the hypomanic ones (9% to 40%), 13% of the mixed and 5% of the manic ones.

The number of episodes with psychotic features, and of induced episodes, is asked only after a yes and is read as 0 after a no; the yes/no on psychotic features is read as 0 where the number of episodes of that kind is 0 (D122).

Mixed episodes exist on the DSM-IV form only. A DSM-IV mixed episode is not the DSM-5 specifier 'with mixed features' (scale_reference.md section 25: confirmed in source (Hergueta 2013; Tandon 2015; Cafaro 2023)).

The criteria of a manic episode differ between the editions (scale_reference.md section 25): DSM-5 asks for increased energy or activity besides the mood, DSM-IV for the mood only (confirmed in source (Grunze 2021)). DSM-IV excluded treatment-induced episodes; DSM-5 counts a full syndrome that persists beyond the effect of the treatment (confirmed in source (Tandon 2015; Grunze 2021); DSM-5 text to verify).

Rapid cycling is the rater's yes/no ('now or in the past'), not derived from the counts. Published definition: at least four episodes in 12 months (scale_reference.md section 25: confirmed in source (Miola 2023, DSM-5-TR wording); 'unchanged from DSM-IV' to verify).

The age at the first psychotropic treatment is not the first antipsychotic of FACE SZ (first_antipsychotic_age), although both are read from the same raw column (shared_names.yaml). A first treatment more than two years before the first episode (173 of 4,053 patients) is not an error.

dsm5_annee_ecoulee.title: Mood episodes of the year before inclusion, DSM-5 criteria

bp.section: Caractéristique du trouble au cours de l'année ecoulée
bp.notes: The mood episodes of the year before the inclusion visit: one yes/no question (at least one episode), then the number of depressive, hypomanic and manic episodes, and for depressive and manic episodes a yes/no and a number for those with psychotic features. Asked at the inclusion visit only. Yes/no answers are delivered as 1 and 0; "Ne sais pas" is a missing code. DSM-IV and DSM-5 are two editions (decision D9 in PROGRESS.md), asked on two inclusion forms and exported in the same columns. The application stores no edition: the export writes dsm_criteria on the inclusion row, DSM5 where the DSM-5 form holds one of five answers on the mood history, else DSM4 where the DSM-IV form does (DEV-11). The label is DSM-IV until 2019 (7 DSM-5 exceptions), DSM-5 on 24 of 380 labelled inclusions in 2020, 44 of 425 in 2021 and 203 of 238 in 2022 (the 35 DSM-IV ones of 2022 are dated January to May), and DSM-5 on all from 2023. This schema reads the DSM-5 visits; dsm4_annee_ecoulee.yaml reads the others. Both carry the version block of the follow-up schemas (D12, D14, D15): an inclusion with no label is read by the date of the patient's first visit (the screening, where there is one), DSM-IV before 2020 and DSM-5 from 2023 (version_inferred), and has no version from 2020 to 2022 (version_unknown, not delivered). Why labels are missing: see dsm5_depuis_derniere_visite.yaml. In this section 12 unlabelled inclusions are read by date (9 DSM-IV, 3 DSM-5) and 4 of 2020 and 2021 are not delivered (R69 would label them). The DSM-5 form has no mixed episode: the four mixed-episode columns are not read here. It asks instead about depressive and manic episodes with mixed features in the year (two yes/no and two numbers), which the extraction does not hold (R140). 9 inclusions labelled DSM-5 (2018 to 2022) also hold a DSM-IV record (a lifetime number of mixed episodes). The export takes each cell of this section from the DSM-IV record first, so their answers here may be those of the DSM-IV form; 5 of them hold mixed-episode cells, which are not read. They are delivered (R70). The numbers. The form asks a number for each kind of episode, 0 to 20 or ">20" (read as 20 and censored_right: 2 hypomanic), only after a yes to the first question (asked_if). Where the first answer is no they are empty in the extraction and are read as 0: with no mood episode in the year, there was no depressive episode. Where the first answer is unknown or empty they stay missing. The boxes. The form has no box per kind of episode: the export writes the three boxes (mhoccur_edm_ly, mhoccur_ehman_ly, mhoccur_epman_ly) from the number, 1 where it is 1 or more (">20" included), 0 where it is 0, empty where it is "Ne sais pas" or empty (803, 780 and 824 boxes). After a no they are read as 0 like the numbers (186 visits). They add nothing to the numbers and are delivered so that this section and the follow-up one have the same pair (D53); the export writes the follow-up boxes the same way. Psychotic features. The form asks about depressive episodes with psychotic features after a yes to the first question, and about manic ones only after 1 to 15 manic episodes in the year (no inclusion has more). Each answer is 0 where the number of that kind of episode is 0 (asked_if on the box, D122): for manic episodes because the form did not ask (718 zeros), for depressive ones because there was none to have psychotic features (10 zeros). So 68 of the 1,007 answers on manic episodes are yes, a share comparable with the DSM-IV form. The number with psychotic features is 0 where the yes/no is 0. Answers that contradict each other are delivered as typed: 6 inclusions say yes and then give 0 for every kind of episode; 1 gives a number after a no and 1 gives numbers with no first answer; 1 says yes to a depressive episode with psychotic features after 0 depressive episodes; 4 give more depressive episodes with psychotic features than depressive episodes, and 1 more manic ones than manic episodes; the number of episodes in the year is above the lifetime number for 10 inclusions (3 depressive, 5 hypomanic and 3 manic numbers); 6 of the 380 inclusions in a current episode that answer here say no mood episode in the year, and so do 25 of the 694 with a most recent episode that started or ended within the year before the visit (dsm5_episode_recent.yaml). Centres. Centre A fills this section for 4 of its 145 DSM-5 inclusions (O40) and centre C for none of its 119 (R20); in the other centres the first answer is filled for 88% of the DSM-5 inclusions, as with the DSM-IV form. Centre B leaves it empty for 65 of its 164 inclusions of 2022 to 2024. Centres B and E report a manic episode in the year more often (24% and 19%, against 6% in the other centres), as they did with the DSM-IV form (23% each in 2016-2021, against 12%). 22 of the 59 unknown numbers of hypomanic episodes come from centre F.

dsm5_depuis_derniere_visite.title: Mood episodes since the last visit, DSM-5 criteria

bp.section: Caractéristique du trouble depuis la dernière visite à la visite de suivi
bp.notes: The mood episodes since the last visit, asked at the follow-up visits only: one yes/no question (at least one episode), then the number of depressive, hypomanic and manic episodes, the numbers with psychotic features, and the type of the most recent episode. Yes/no answers are delivered as 1 and 0; "Ne sais pas" is a missing code (20 first answers, 35 depressive, 32 hypomanic and 7 manic numbers). Editions. DSM-IV and DSM-5 are two editions, in the same columns (decision D9 in PROGRESS.md). The follow-up form is one form for every patient, changed in place from the DSM-IV to the DSM-5 version centre by centre between October 2021 and May 2022. The application stores no edition: the export writes dsm_criteria on the inclusion row only, DSM5 where the DSM-5 inclusion form holds one of five answers on the mood history (type and age of the first episode, numbers of depressive, hypomanic and manic episodes), else DSM4 where the DSM-IV form does (DEV-11). It is empty at 849 of 6,498 inclusions: 206 hold no answer of either form (202 at centre C, whose DSM-5 form the export leaves out, R20), 552 hold only default dates and 91 hold other answers (R69 would label 85 of them). The version of a follow-up visit comes from three decisions. D12. Before 2022 a follow-up visit takes the label of the patient's inclusion. D14. From 1 January 2022 a follow-up visit is DSM-5, whatever the inclusion, in every centre, unless it holds a column that only the old form has (the override, see dsm4_depuis_derniere_visite.yaml): the 35 visits answering yes that hold the mixed numbers or the typed total and that were read as DSM-5 (33 of January to May 2022 in two centres, 2 of 2021 of patients included with DSM-5) are read as DSM-IV there, with 14 visits of 2020 and 2021 that had no version. Their mixed numbers are read there, so coverage() no longer counts them. 25 visits answering yes in October to December 2021 (six centres) hold neither number, the pattern of the new form, and are read as DSM-IV. The date on which the form was filled ("Date de recueil des informations"), which would date the change of form, is not in the extraction. D15. A patient with no label is read by the date of the first visit (the screening, where there is one): DSM-IV before 2020 and DSM-5 from 2023 (version_inferred). Patients first seen from 2020 to 2022 have no version before 2022, unless the visit holds a column of the old form (the override): 8 follow-up visits of 2021, none answering yes, are not delivered (version_unknown); the 14 that answered yes hold such a column and are read as DSM-IV. This schema reads the DSM-5 visits: 2,328 visits, all but 1 from 2022. 907 are of patients labelled DSM-5, 1,029 of patients labelled DSM-IV (D14) and 392 of patients with no label (D14, no flag). dsm4_depuis_derniere_visite.yaml reads the others. DSM-5 has no mixed episode, so the mixed numbers are not in this schema. The numbers. 0 to 20 or ">20" (">20" would be read as 20 and censored_right; none today). They are shown only after a yes to the first question; where it is no (1,219 visits) they are empty in the extraction and are read as 0 (asked_if, decision D53): with no mood episode since the last visit, there was no depressive episode. The boxes. The form has no box per kind of episode: the export writes the three boxes (mhoccur_edm_spv, mhoccur_ehman_spv, mhoccur_epman_spv) from the numbers, 1 where the number is 1 or more, 0 where it is 0, empty where it is "Ne sais pas" or empty. After a no they are read as 0 like the numbers. Psychotic features. The form shows each number with psychotic features only after 1 to 20 episodes of that kind; it is therefore 0 where the number of that kind is 0 (asked_if on the box, D122): 181 depressive and 886 manic zeros after a yes. The form also hides it after ">20", an application defect that touches no visit today. The total (dsm5_fu_n_episodes) is the sum of the depressive, hypomanic and manic numbers (D122): 922 of the 1,107 visits answering yes, and 0 after a no. The sum is strict: a visit where a number is empty (134 visits) or "Ne sais pas" (48; both on 3) gets no total (185 in all). The application's script ("Nombre d'épisodes total", psy_diag_psychiatrique_semestriel.js) counts an empty number as 0 and gives no number for "Ne sais pas", and it writes into a disabled field, so the form of today never saves its total (an application defect). The stored total therefore exists only on the old form, which is read as DSM-IV (the override): no DSM-5 visit holds one any more, and the check against it (dsm5_fu_n_episodes_stored) cannot fire: 0 score_mismatch and 0 score_not_recomputed. Before the override there were 6 and 4: the 35 stored totals sat on visits that hold an old-form cell (the last of May 2022), and 3 of the 6 mismatches were the old form's total, which includes the mixed episodes. The check stays for a later extraction. The type of the most recent episode is filled on 910 of the 1,107 visits answering yes. The list has no mixed type (see dsm4_depuis_derniere_visite.yaml). Answers that contradict each other: 6 visits answer yes and give 0 for every number. Of the 596 follow-up visits in a current episode (dsm5_episode_actuel.yaml) that answer this question, 153 say that no episode occurred since the last visit (the DSM-IV twin: 377 of 1,616): the episodes since the last visit are probably undercounted, or an episode that began earlier is not counted. The window is the time since the previous visit (median gap 186 days at the six-monthly visits, 367 at the yearly ones): the share answering yes rises from 31% of the 29 visits with a gap under 150 days to 61% of the 210 with a gap over 600 days. Do not compare counts of episodes across visits without the gap. Not in the extraction: the form also asks the numbers of depressive and manic episodes with mixed features since the last visit, and the dates of the first depressive, manic and hypomanic episode since the last visit (R140). Centres. Centre A holds an answer of the follow-up mood form (this section or the current episode) on 27 of its 287 follow-up visits from October 2022 to March 2024 and on 4 of its 129 from July 2025 (O40), against 85% of the follow-up visits of the other centres from 2022. In centre F the share of visits answering yes rises from 46% before 2022 to 73% from 2022, while it stays at 44% and 47% elsewhere; this is not explained.

bp.section: Caractéristique du trouble de l'HUMEUR ACTUEL
bp.notes: The mood episode the patient is in on the day of the visit, if any: its type, specifier, severity, chronicity and whether it followed a birth. Filled at the inclusion visit and at every follow-up visit (six-monthly and yearly). It describes the day of the visit at every visit, so the inclusion and the follow-up answers are in the same columns. A third of the inclusions read here are in an episode (396 of 1,066) and a quarter of the follow-up visits (631 of 2,390). Yes/no answers are delivered as 1 and 0; "Ne sais pas" is a missing code. DSM-IV and DSM-5 are two editions (decision D9 in PROGRESS.md), asked on two inclusion forms and exported in the same columns. The application stores no edition: the export writes dsm_criteria on the inclusion row, DSM5 where the DSM-5 form holds one of five answers on the mood history, else DSM4 where the DSM-IV form does (DEV-11). The label is DSM-IV until 2019 (7 DSM-5 exceptions), DSM-5 on 24 of 380 labelled inclusions in 2020, 44 of 425 in 2021 and 203 of 238 in 2022 (the 35 DSM-IV ones of 2022 are dated January to May), and DSM-5 on all from 2023. This schema reads the DSM-5 visits; dsm4_episode_actuel.yaml reads the others. Both carry the version block of the follow-up schemas: a follow-up visit takes the label of the inclusion before 2022 (D12) and is DSM-5 from 1 January 2022 (D14); a patient with no label is read by the date of the first visit, DSM-IV before 2020 and DSM-5 from 2023 (D15, version_inferred), and has no version from 2020 to 2022 (version_unknown, not delivered). Why labels are missing and which visits D14 reads in the other edition: see dsm5_depuis_derniere_visite.yaml. Here 7 inclusions are read as DSM-5 by date; the 2,391 follow-up visits with a value are of patients labelled DSM-5 (921), labelled DSM-IV (1,045) or with no label (425). The 49 follow-up visits that hold a column of the old form are read as DSM-IV (the override of the version block), 35 of them taken from this schema. 15 visits with an answer (5 inclusions and 10 follow-ups of 2020 and 2021) have no version and are delivered in neither schema. 9 inclusions labelled DSM-5 (2018 to 2022) also hold a DSM-IV record (a lifetime number of mixed episodes). bp.notes: The most recent mood episode before the inclusion visit: its dates, type, specifier, chronicity, severity and whether it followed a birth. Filled once, at the inclusion visit. Each detail is asked for some types only: the specifier and the chronicity for a depressive episode, the severity for a depressive, manic or unspecified one, the postpartum onset for every type. The form's rule is on the positions of the type list, as in dsm4_episode_recent.yaml (specifier and chronicity on 1, severity on 1, 3 and 4, postpartum on 1 to 4): position 4 is the unspecified type here, where it is the mixed one in the DSM-IV form. Where the patient is in an episode at inclusion, the clinicians often described that episode here: of the 374 such visits with a type, 272 give the type of the current episode and 187 have no end date (with no current episode, 79 of 622 have none). Centre B leaves this section empty for 66 of its 164 inclusions of 2022 to 2024, against 32 of 382 in 2016 to 2021. The type of the most recent episode recorded at the follow-up visits is another column, read by the schemas of the follow-up form. dsm5_premier_episode.title: First mood episode, DSM-5 criteria

bp.notes: The first mood episode of the patient: its type, the age at which it began, whether it came within six months of a birth and whether a cyclothymic period came before. Filled once, at the inclusion visit. Yes/no answers are delivered as 1 and 0; "Ne sais pas" is a missing code. DSM-IV and DSM-5 are two editions (decision D9 in PROGRESS.md), asked on two inclusion forms and exported in the same columns. The application stores no edition: the export writes dsm_criteria on the inclusion row, DSM5 where the DSM-5 form holds one of five answers on the mood history, else DSM4 where the DSM-IV form does (DEV-11). The label is DSM-IV until 2019 (7 DSM-5 exceptions), DSM-5 on 24 of 380 labelled inclusions in 2020, 44 of 425 in 2021 and 203 of 238 in 2022 (the 35 DSM-IV ones of 2022 are dated January to May), and DSM-5 on all from 2023. This schema reads the DSM-5 visits; dsm4_premier_episode.yaml reads the others. Both carry the version block of the follow-up schemas (D12, D14, D15): an inclusion with no label is read by the date of the patient's first visit (the screening, where there is one), DSM-IV before 2020 and DSM-5 from 2023 (version_inferred), and has no version from 2020 to 2022 (version_unknown, not delivered). Why labels are missing: see dsm5_depuis_derniere_visite.yaml. In this section 11 unlabelled inclusions hold only a postpartum or a cyclothymic answer: 2 of 2023 and 2024 are read here, 6 as DSM-IV, and 3 of 2020 and 2021 are not delivered (R69 would label them). The DSM-5 form has no mixed episode. 9 inclusions labelled DSM-5 (2018 to 2022) also hold a DSM-IV record (a lifetime number of mixed episodes), and the export takes their answers here from the DSM-IV record first: their age may then be the DSM-IV age at the first episode of any type. They are delivered (R70). The age at the first episode (decision D89 in PROGRESS.md). On the DSM-IV form the column agedebutpremier_episode is the age at the first episode, whatever its type. On the DSM-5 form the same column is labelled "Age du premier EDM" and is shown only after 1 to 15 depressive episodes (positions 3 to 17 of the form's list of numbers, which starts with "Ne sais pas" and 0): it is the age at the first major depressive episode, delivered as dsm5_first_mde_age. It is filled for 714 of the 906 patients with at least one depressive episode and for none of the 17 with none. Of the 192 others, 75 have 16 or more depressive episodes, for which the form does not ask the age (an application defect), and 117 left it empty or "Ne sais pas". Where the first episode was hypomanic it is later than the age at the first hypomanic episode (29 of 49) or equal to it (20), never earlier. This age and the age at the first mood stabiliser are lists from "<5" to ">89": "<5" is read as 5 and censored_left (1 patient), ">89" as 89 and censored_right (none; D122). Three columns exist in the DSM-5 form only; the dictionary gives them no label (section "New Columns"). age_ehman and age_epman, labelled on the form "Age au premier épisode hypomaniaque" and "Age au premier épisode maniaque", are typed as one or two digits. They are asked only after 1 to 15 hypomanic, or manic, episodes: they are filled for 530 of the 728 patients with a hypomanic episode and 283 of the 353 with a manic one, never where there was none and never for 16 or more episodes (56 and 7 patients). dsm5_first_episode_age is the earliest of the three ages that are known (D89). For 143 patients the kind of episode named as the first has no age (107 name a depressive episode, 23 a hypomanic one and 13 a manic one; for 72 of them the form did not ask it: 16 or more episodes of that kind, or a number unknown or empty). Their value is then the age at a later episode, an upper bound of the age at the first episode: its median is 25, against 20 for the others. rad_agethym is the age at the first mood stabiliser: its label on the form is "Age du premier traitement thymorégulateur" (decision D87 in PROGRESS.md, was open question O34). It is filled for 995 of the 1,121 inclusions labelled DSM-5 (60 "Ne sais pas", 34 of them in centre F). It is later than the age at the first mood episode (dsm5_first_episode_age) for 603 of the 779 patients with both (median difference 5 years), the same for 157 and earlier for 19. It is before the age at the first psychotropic treatment for 3 of 914 patients, which cannot be, since a mood stabiliser is a psychotropic, and the same for 316. Delivered as written: 13 ages are above the age at the inclusion visit, by up to 1.3 years (11 at the first mood stabiliser, 1 at the first depressive and 1 at the first hypomanic episode), flagged check_failed (not_above the age at the visit, D199); one man answers yes to the postpartum question; 7 of the 29 first episodes that are depressive with psychotic features go with a lifetime "no" to psychotic features of depressive episodes (22 yes, 11 with no answer); 4 first episodes are of a kind whose lifetime number is 0 (2 depressive, 1 depressive with psychotic features and 1 manic). Centres. There is no answer from centre C (R20) and almost none from centre A from 2023 (3 of 141 inclusions, against 842 of 911 in the other centres; O40). One centre (N) records a cyclothymic period before the first episode for 45% of its patients, against 16% overall.

dsm5_vie_entiere.title: Mood disorder over the whole life, DSM-5 criteria

bp.notes: The mood disorder over the whole life, as recorded at the inclusion visit: the number of episodes of each kind, those with psychotic features, induced episodes, rapid cycling, remission between episodes, seasonal pattern and the age at the first psychotropic treatment. Yes/no answers are delivered as 1 and 0; "Ne sais pas" is a missing code. DSM-IV and DSM-5 are two editions (decision D9 in PROGRESS.md), asked on two inclusion forms and exported in the same columns. The application stores no edition: the export writes dsm_criteria on the inclusion row, DSM5 where the DSM-5 form holds one of five answers on the mood history, else DSM4 where the DSM-IV form does (DEV-11). The label is DSM-IV until 2019 (7 DSM-5 exceptions), DSM-5 on 24 of 380 labelled inclusions in 2020, 44 of 425 in 2021 and 203 of 238 in 2022 (the 35 DSM-IV ones of 2022 are dated January to May), and DSM-5 on all from 2023. This schema reads the DSM-5 visits; dsm4_vie_entiere.yaml reads the others. Both carry the version block of the follow-up schemas (D12, D14, D15): an inclusion with no label is read by the date of the patient's first visit (the screening, where there is one), DSM-IV before 2020 and DSM-5 from 2023 (version_inferred), and has no version from 2020 to 2022 (version_unknown, not delivered). Why labels are missing: see dsm5_depuis_derniere_visite.yaml. In this section 6 unlabelled inclusions are read by date (4 DSM-IV, 2 DSM-5) and none is left without a version. The DSM-5 form has no mixed episode: the three mixed-episode columns are not read here. They hold 19 cells on 10 DSM-5 inclusions, 9 of which also hold a DSM-IV record (a lifetime number of mixed episodes); the export takes their answers here from the DSM-IV record first, so they may be those of the DSM-IV form. They are delivered (R70). The DSM-5 form asks instead about depressive and manic episodes with mixed features (yes/no and number) and about a seasonal pattern of depression and of (hypo)mania with its season; the extraction holds none of these 8 questions (R140). Counts. The form stops at 20: ">20" is read as 20 with a mark in the censoring column (this value or more; 58 depressive, 45 hypomanic, 4 manic). "Ne sais pas" is 14% of the numbers of depressive episodes, 31% and 38% in centres E and F. The range of every lifetime count is 0 to 20, as the form's: no number is out of range. Psychotic features. The form asks whether there was at least one depressive, or manic, episode with psychotic features only after 1 to 15 episodes of that kind, positions 3 to 17 of the form's list of numbers (the DSM-IV form asks every patient). The answer is 0 where the number of that kind is 0 (asked_if on the number, D122): 17 depressive and 639 manic zeros. So 252 of the 971 answers on manic episodes are yes (26%; 30% with the DSM-IV form). After 16 or more episodes the form does not ask (an application defect): the 75 patients with 16 or more depressive episodes and the 7 with 16 or more manic ones have no answer. The 9 answers given where the form does not ask (2 depressive, 7 manic) are all on the inclusions that hold a DSM-IV record. The number of depressive episodes with psychotic features, and of induced episodes, is asked only after a yes (asked_if): it is 0 where the answer to "at least one" is no. The number of manic episodes with psychotic features is not delivered: the export loses it for the DSM-5 form (R68), although 252 patients answer yes. The age at the first psychotropic treatment is a list from "<5" to ">89" on the form: "<5" is read as 5 and censored_left (1 patient), ">89" as 89 and censored_right (none; D122). Against the age at the first episode (dsm5_first_episode_age, D89), 72 of the 832 patients with both ages have a first treatment more than two years earlier. 50 of them have no age for the kind of episode named as the first (48, 41 of them a depressive one, and 2 with no named type), so the age compared is that of a later episode; where that age is known the count is 22 of 686 (22 and 50 make the 72). Against the first depressive episode (dsm5_first_mde_age) it is 42 of 691. 1 of the 1,003 ages is above the age at inclusion, by less than a year. Delivered as written and flagged check_failed (not_above the age at the visit, D199). Centres. There is no value from centre C (R20), and centre A has values for only 6 of its 145 DSM-5 inclusions (O40). Centre H reports a seasonal pattern for 8% and rapid cycling for 11% of its DSM-5 patients (23% to 51% and 20% to 42% in the other centres); delivered as written. Not loaded (ignored.yaml). mhoccur_edm_lt, mhoccur_ehman_lt, mhoccur_epman_lt and mhoccur_epmixt_lt say "Y" where the count of the row is 1 or more and "N" everywhere else, also where the count is unknown or empty and on every row of the other visits: the export writes them, and their "N" does not mean "none" (R71). The three columns mhoccur_edm_psy_spv, mhoccur_epman_psy_spv and mhoccur_epmixt_psy_spv are copies of the lifetime columns read here, filled at inclusion only (R72).

The criteria of a manic episode differ between the editions (scale_reference.md section 25): DSM-5 asks for increased energy or activity besides the mood, DSM-IV for the mood only (confirmed in source (Grunze 2021)). trouble_psychotique_fu.title: Psychotic disorder (follow-up visits)

bp.notes: Whether the patient has a psychotic disorder, which one, since when and whether symptoms were present in the past month. The form asks "Le patient a-t-il un trouble psychotique": it does not say "other than the mood disorder". At follow-up the four questions are on the follow-up diagnostic form ("Diagnostic psychiatrique de suivi"), one form for every patient whatever the DSM edition, filled at the six-monthly and the yearly visits (2,875 of the 9,463 answers are at a visit labelled in months) and never at screening. It asks the questions and offers the nine disorders of the inclusion forms, with no "change since the last visit" question. Two of the nine (shared psychotic disorder, and one due to a general medical condition) hold no answer today. Rare: 34 yes in 9,389 answers (0.36%), from 30 patients, 18 of whom answered no at inclusion; of the 12 yes followed by another answer, 8 are followed by a no. Yes/no answers are delivered as 1 and 0; "Ne sais pas" is a missing code (74). Two periods in the same columns (decision D53 in PROGRESS.md), as for the comorbidities (D49, D50): the question is asked at the inclusion visit and at every follow-up visit, with the same wording ("does the patient have a psychotic disorder"). The follow-up answer is an update given at that visit (decision D84 in PROGRESS.md). Of the 73 follow-up answers of patients who had a psychotic disorder at inclusion, 70 are "no" and 3 are "yes". The two are delivered as separate columns, ending in _v0 and _fu; visit_form says which form a visit used and is read from the visit label. Completeness. The question is answered on 9,463 of the 11,686 follow-up visits (81%): 87% to 92% by period until 2018, 81% in 2019-2021 and 66% to 68% from 2022, 24% in one large centre (A) from 2022. Where the follow-up diagnostic form holds any answer, this question is answered on 92% to 99% of the visits in every period: the missing answers are missing forms. The details are shown only after a yes. 1 answer about the past month is filled after a no; it is delivered as written, as in D50. Date of onset. 1000-01-01 is the placeholder that the application writes into empty dates since its version of 2024-07-25 (D98): 422 cells at follow-up, 396 of them on visits of 2025 and 2026, 405 next to a "no" and 15 next to an empty answer: date_placeholder. 22 real dates, 9 of them before the inclusion; 1 is 225 days after the visit and is delivered as written.

alda.title: Alda scale of the response to lithium

bp.notes: In use mostly from 2022: the first question is "is the patient treated with lithium at present?", answered on 3,892 visits (yes on 1,790), 53 of them before 2021 and 120 in 2021; the criteria are shown after a yes only: criterion A is rated on 1,720 visits of 999 patients, 26 of them before 2022. So a patient who has stopped lithium has no rating, and those who stopped because it did not work are among them: the scores describe the patients still treated, not everyone who ever took lithium. The ratings change from one visit to the next, so this is a visit-level instrument. Criterion A rates the response from 0 to 10. Criteria B1 to B5 (0 to 2 each) rate how sure it is that the response is due to lithium. The total is A minus the sum of B, and never below 0, as in the scoring script of the application (Grof and others 2002; Manchia and others 2013 for the total; the floor at 0 is described in later uses, not in the ConLiGen report: scale_reference.md, section 6). The floor acts on 245 of the 1,669 visits that have the six items, and the total is 0 on 346 of them (20.7%); B is above 4 on 216 of the 1,674 visits that have the five B items (ConLiGen analyses criterion A only where B is 4 or less: not applied here). The stored total is the application's (no definition in the score step of the export): it equals max(stored A - stored B, 0) on all 1,613 visits that hold the three stored values, so the script is the rule, but its inputs can be stale: the application computes the scores when a button is clicked and nothing recomputes them after an edit of an item. The stored criterion A differs from the item alda_a1 on 9 rows and the stored B score from the sum of its items on 11 rows. The total recomputed from the items then differs from the stored one on 14 rows. All get score_mismatch, and the values recomputed from the items are kept. The 9, 11 and 14 mismatches are all of 2022 to 2026. 56 recomputed totals have no stored total.

alda.description: Rating of the response to lithium, for the patients treated with lithium at the visit. Criterion A rates the response from 0 to 10; five B criteria (0 to 2 each) rate how sure it is that the response is due to lithium.
alda.reference: Grof P, Duffy A, Cavazzoni P, et al. Is response to prophylactic lithium a familial trait? J Clin Psychiatry 2002;63:942-947; Manchia M, et al. PLoS One 2013;8:e65636 (ConLiGen)
alda.reference_confidence: confirmed in source (bibliographic records; ConLiGen full text read)

cgi_egf.title: Clinical Global Impression (CGI) and Global Assessment of Functioning (EGF)

bp.notes: The code 0 means "not assessed" for the severity, the improvement, the therapeutic effect and the efficacy index. It is read as a missing code. Three items at the follow-up visits only (decision D113 in PROGRESS.md, by the project lead). The form asks the improvement, the therapeutic effect with its side effects, and the efficacy index at the follow-up visits, and says to tick "not assessed" at the initial evaluation: there is no earlier state to compare with. They are nevertheless filled at 1,068 inclusion visits (19%), 1% to 3% in four centres and 37% to 60% in three. These variables are read at the follow-up visits only (visit_form, from the visit label); the inclusion values are not delivered. The severity and the EGF are delivered at every visit. The efficacy index is a score: 4 x (therapeutic effect - 1) + side effects, the formula of the scoring script of the application, so it goes from 1 to 16 (cgi_te_steps is the first term, not delivered). The stored index (cgi_efficacy_index_stored, not delivered) is the check. The application computes the index only when a side-effect option is clicked (the tooltip of the field says to tick the side effects again after changing the effect), so the stored index is stale after an edit of the therapeutic effect. On the 7,985 follow-up visits that have the effect, the side effects and the stored index, the stored index differs from the formula on 74 (score_mismatch): always by a multiple of 4 (the stored one is 4 higher on 41, 4 lower on 20, and 8 or 12 away on 13), as if the effect had been changed after the index was computed. The recomputed value is delivered: 74 values recomputed, 6 visits with an effect and side effects and no stored index get the index, and 6 visits hold a stored index with the effect or the side effects missing: the index is missing there (score_not_recomputed). Before this review the stored index was delivered and checked by a custom function (check_failed on the same 74 visits). The numbers 1 to 16 are the cell labels of the grid of Guy's ECDEU Assessment Manual (1976): rows are the therapeutic effect (marked, moderate, minimal, unchanged or worse), columns the side effects, numbered row by row (6 = moderate effect, side effects that do not interfere significantly, the example printed on the form). They are position labels, not an ordered score: Guy gives a table from the cell to a ratio of effect to side effects (0.25 to 4.00), and the cell number does not rise with that ratio (scale_reference.md, section 3: Guy p. 221, read in the OCR text of the manual in two agreeing extractions; the page scan itself was not checked, literature check 2026-11-21). The side-effect question is shown only after a therapeutic effect from 1 to 4 (the form hides it after "not assessed"): 1 side-effect value sits under "not assessed" and 2 under an empty effect, kept as recorded (a rule would mostly blank values under an empty parent), and 107 of the 9,174 effects from 1 to 4 have no side-effect answer. The EGF is a number from 1 to 100, typed in a free text field (no limit in the form) under the ten bands of the scale. The form prints the bands from 100-91 down to 1-10; the five lowest are written from the low number up (41-50, 31-40, 21-30, 11-21, 1-10) and "11-21" is a misprint for 11-20, the published band. 149 cells hold a band of ten points instead of a number ("60-51", "90-81"), 87 of them in one centre: 140 in the wording printed on the form (8 of them 100-91), 6 written in rising order (71-80, 51-60, 61-70, 81-90, 91-100: not the printed wording), 3 with another separator or a typing slip. They are read as the middle of the band (55.5) and flagged band_middle (decision D24 in PROGRESS.md). One band is impossible and ends out_of_range. Two cells hold 0 (missing code: in the published scale 0 means inadequate information). 81% of the numbers typed are multiples of 5 (47% of 10). The CGI-I at inclusion is not delivered (D113): its 1,068 values at inclusion correlate with the severity as strongly as the follow-up ones do, so they do not look like a blank form (open question, no change).

sz.notes: The code 0 means "not assessed" for the severity, the improvement, the therapeutic effect and the efficacy index. It is read as a missing code. Three items at the follow-up visits only, as in BP (BP decision D113, SZ D36). The form asks the improvement, the therapeutic effect with its side effects, and the efficacy index at the follow-up visits, and says to tick "not assessed" at the initial evaluation. They are nevertheless filled at 353 to 650 of the 2,231 inclusion visits with a CGI. These variables are read at the follow-up visits only (visit_form, from the visit label). The efficacy index is a score: 4 x (therapeutic effect - 1) + side effects, the formula of the script of the form (hetero_cgi_egf.js, line 23), so it goes from 1 to 16 (cgi_te_steps is the first term, not delivered). The stored index (cgi_efficacy_index_stored, not delivered) is the check. The application computes the index only when a side-effects option is clicked (the tooltip of the field says to tick the side effects again after changing the effect), so the stored index is stale after an edit of the therapeutic effect. On the 2,036 follow-up visits that have the effect, the side effects and the stored index, the stored index differs from the formula on 23 (score_mismatch): always by a multiple of 4 (4 higher on 9, 4 lower on 10, 8 or 12 away on 4), as if the effect had been changed after the index was computed. The recomputed value is delivered: 23 values recomputed, no visit with an effect and side effects and no stored index, and 3 visits hold a stored index with the effect or the side effects missing: the index is missing there (score_not_recomputed). Before this review the stored index was delivered and checked by a custom function (check_failed on the same 23 visits). The numbers 1 to 16 are the cell labels of the grid of Guy's ECDEU Assessment Manual (1976): rows are the therapeutic effect (marked, moderate, minimal, unchanged or worse), columns the side effects, numbered row by row (6 = moderate effect, side effects that do not interfere significantly, the example printed on the form). They are position labels, not an ordered score: Guy gives a table from the cell to a ratio of effect to side effects (0.25 to 4.00), and the cell number does not rise with that ratio (scale_reference.md, section 3: Guy p. 221, read in the OCR text of the manual in two agreeing extractions; the page scan itself was not checked, literature check 2026-11-21). The EGF is a free text field in the form (varchar(25), NOT NULL, no pattern) under the ten bands of the scale, so a band such as "60-51" can be typed, as in BP. It is a whole number in every cell of this extraction (2 to 100 observed): the earlier note that SZ holds no band is an artefact of the export, which casts the field to a whole number and drops every other text (eschizo_hetero_cgi_egf.sql, lines 21 and 22; request R138: keep the raw text). The variable keeps bands: middle for the day the text arrives. The form prints '41-50' and '11-21' (the published band is 11-20) and has no 100-91 band, which the BP form has. 123 of the 4,647 visits with a CGI severity have no EGF (2.6%). The export drops the Fait / Non fait flags of the CGI-EGF form and of the PSP form (rad_cgi_egf_nf and rad_psp_nf): a visit with an empty form cannot be told from a visit where it was not done (request R141). The severity is rated at every visit. Same instrument as in FACE BP; the SZ columns are named cgi0101 to cgi0103 where BP has cgi01 to cgi03.
sz.difference: the SZ columns are named cgi0101 to cgi0103 where BP has cgi01 to cgi03

dr.notes: Two ratings by the clinician, at the inclusion and follow-up visits: the CGI severity (1,434 visits, form 127) and the GAF, called EGF in French (1,351 visits, form 140). The two are two forms of the application and two tables (hetero_cgi_egf holds CGI1 only; hetero_egf holds the EGF), both on the simplified visit. The TRD extraction has no CGI improvement and no efficacy index, which BP and SZ have: the application does have a CGI-I (form 184, table autoq_cgi_i, CGII1, offered at the follow-up visits) and the clean model of the export reads it, but the hub table of this tab does not select it (request to the data managers; PROGRESS.md D61). CGI severity: 0 means "not assessed" and is a missing code (2 visits). The GAF is the column egf_ (EGF_SCORE; the dictionary maps it to EGD_SCORE, a second column of the table that the export does not read: request R144). The form box is a digit-filtered text field of three characters (a char(3) column), so a band cannot be typed: BP's form lets the rater type a band ("60-51") that is read as the middle of the band, and its schema carries bands: middle; here the option is not set (it never had an effect: 0 cells, every one of the 1,351 cells is a whole number from 1 to 100). The export keeps digits only (request R138, which changes nothing for DR). The GAF is typed in round numbers: 40% of the values are multiples of 10 and 77% of 5. Same instrument as in FACE BP and FACE SZ, with the two columns that the TRD extraction holds.
dr.difference: the TRD extraction has the CGI severity and the GAF only (no improvement, no side effects, no efficacy index; the CGI-I of form 184 is not exported), the GAF is in the column egf_ and its box takes digits only, so no band is typed and the option bands is not set

asp.notes: The severity item of the Clinical Global Impression (1 to 7) and the Global Assessment of Functioning (EGF, 1 to 100): 1,249 and 1,226 inclusion visits, 119 and 125 follow-up visits, from 2011 to 2026. Children and adults. Same two ratings as in FACE BP, SZ and DR, in other columns (gravmdi, egfval), delivered under the same names. The improvement and the efficacy index of the CGI are not in this extraction. The EGF is typed in a box that takes digits only, so no band ("51-60") arrives and none is read as a middle value; a 0 is read as not recorded (none in this extraction), as the 0 of the CGI is "not assessed" in the thesaurus. cgi_changed and gaf_changed are the boxes "changed since the last visit" of the follow-up form. At follow-up the severity is filled on 71 of the 73 visits where the box is "yes" and on 48 of the 138 where it is "no". The boxes are also filled at the inclusion visit until 2021 (385 visits), as the other boxes of this kind in the old forms (D5); they say nothing there. **Year and centre.** 1 of the 2 variables with a shift value reach 0.5 or more (1 by year, 1 by centre): the severity of the CGI (1 to 7, median 4 in every year but 2016, which is 5, and in every centre but D, 4.5, and F, 5), a median that moves by one level of a seven-level scale. The GAF stands at 0.38 by year and by centre (median 54.5 to 60). Both follow the age mix: children are 100% of the visits of centre A, 42% to 57% of B and C, 2% of D and none of E; the GAF median is 59 among the children and 55 among the adults, and it moves inside each group: among adults 52 to 52.5 in 2020 to 2022 against 57 to 63 in 2014 to 2018 and 60 from 2024 (year shift 0.67), among children 50 in 2013 and 2016 against 55 to 60 from 2018 (0.64). Steps with no known cause (the case mix or the rater; the GAF is typed in a box that takes digits only).
asp.difference: the severity of the CGI and the GAF only, in other columns (gravmdi, egfval); two boxes of the follow-up form (changed since the last visit)

The CGI improvement, therapeutic effect, side effects and efficacy index are in BP and SZ, at the follow-up visits only.

sources: schema notes and labels (bp, sz, dr, asp cgi_egf)
flags: The code 0 means 'not assessed' and is read as missing.
The efficacy index is a cell label of a grid, not an ordered score: the cell number does not rise with the ratio of effect to side effects (0.25 to 4.00) that Guy's manual gives.

The CGI improvement, therapeutic effect, side effects and efficacy index are delivered at the follow-up visits only; the values typed at inclusion are not delivered. DR and ASP have the severity and the GAF only.

The published GAF records the worse of the symptom level and the functioning level (Aas 2010, confirmed in source), so it is not a pure measure of functioning. No standard threshold: the bands are the interpretation.

common.note: The CGI severity (1 to 7) and the GAF (1 to 100) are in the four cohorts. The CGI improvement, therapeutic effect, side effects and efficacy index are in BP and SZ only: the index is recomputed as 4 x (therapeutic effect - 1) + side effects, with the stored value as a check (the application computes it only when the side-effects label is clicked, so the stored index goes stale).
