etat_depressif.title: Depressive symptoms present at the visit (DSM-IV criterion A checklist)

bp.notes: Part of the "État du patient" form (the section is called "Episode dépressif majeur actuel"): a checklist of the nine symptoms of criterion A of a DSM-IV major depressive episode, filled at the inclusion visit and at the follow-up visits. The instruction of the form is to fill it whatever the mood state of the patient (euthymic, depressed, manic, hypomanic or mixed) and to tick the symptoms present: it lists the symptoms present at the visit, it is not an episode and not a diagnosis. It is the same form for every patient, so it does not depend on dsm_version. The answers are Y, N and U in the extraction. Y and N are delivered as 1 and 0, so that the symptoms can be counted. U ("does not know") is a missing code. The stored count (etatd) is the application's own: the score step of the export has no definition for it. The application computes it when the button "Calculer le score" is clicked (hetero_etat_patient.js): Oui is 1, Non is 0, any other answer ("Ne sais pas") is -999 and gives "Score non calculable", and a blank item makes the script stop with an error (line 82, the variable champ does not exist there), so the field keeps its old value (request A64). The package counts the symptoms from the answers, and needs all nine to be yes or no, like the stored count. It is delivered on 15,414 visits and the stored count is absent on 1,952 of them. It differs from the stored one on 61 visits (stored higher on 17, lower on 44): they get score_mismatch and the recomputed count is kept; one stored count sits on a visit where an item is missing (score_not_recomputed). 268 visits (1.7% of the 15,682 where the nine are answered) get no count because one answer is "Ne sais pas", and 141 more have an item left blank. The form does not store the published rule of criterion A (five or more of the nine symptoms in the same two weeks, one of them depressed mood or loss of interest: the DSM-5 criterion as reproduced by Osipov 2016; reviews report it unchanged from DSM-IV-TR (Tandon 2015, Grunze et al. 2021), whose own text could not be read, literature check 2026-11-21; scale_reference.md section 25), and does not ask the duration: a count of 5 or more is met on 3,146 of the 15,414 counts (20%), and with depressed mood or loss of interest on 2,979 (19%). Five symptoms have a detail that says which way the change goes (reactivity, loss or gain, insomnia or hypersomnia, agitation or retardation, racing or slowed thoughts). The form shows it only after a yes (position 0 of the parent, "Oui"), so each detail has shown_if on its symptom: 11 filled cells of the 18,170 are delivered as missing (not_shown): 9 under a no, 1 under "Ne sais pas" and 1 under an empty symptom (that last one is an exception to the rule that a value recorded under an empty parent stays, accepted because the other ten are explicit contradictions). The detail is filled for 79% to 94% of the symptoms present. The form is filled less and less: of the visits that hold a MADRS, YMRS, FAST or CGI rating, 95% have it up to 2017, 88% in 2018-2022 and 86% from 2023; one centre goes from 98% to 44% and 10%. DR asks the ninth symptom with an addition (or a precise plan to commit suicide) that BP does not have, so its yes rates are not comparable (at a MADRS suicide item of 2, 38% in BP and 64% in DR).

dr.notes: A checklist of the nine DSM-IV criterion A symptoms of a major depressive episode, filled at the inclusion visit (605 visits) and at the follow-up visits (874). The form says to fill it whatever the mood state: it lists the symptoms present at the visit and is not an episode (the dictionary calls it one: request R144). Nine symptoms, answered 1 (yes), 0 (no) or 2 ("does not know", a missing code); the extraction of BP writes Y, N and U for the same form. No count of symptoms is stored here (the BP count is the application's own, computed on a button): etatd_total is the number of symptoms present, when the nine are answered yes or no (1,403 visits; 75 visits have a "does not know" and get no count). Five symptoms have a detail that says which way the change goes. The form shows it only after a yes to the symptom (js/formulaires.js, lines 4607-4616). In TRD the details of mood reactivity, psychomotor change and thinking speed are each two yes/no boxes (hyper- and hypo-reactivity, agitation and retardation, racing and slowed thoughts), where BP has one answer. After a no they are empty and are 0 (asked_if: 3,001 cells, 487 and 488, 598 and 598, 415 and 415); after a "does not know" they stay missing. Under a yes both boxes are answered on 972 of 980, 858 of 863 and 1,051 of 1,058 visits, neither on 3, 1 and 2: the boxes are radios, so there is no box_list. Two forms in the same columns, for the details of weight and of sleep (decision D6 in PROGRESS.md). Form 182 has two boxes for each: etatd03b "loss" and etatd03c "gain", etatd04b "insomnia" and etatd04c "hypersomnia" (348 visits). Forms 128 (inclusion) and 183 (follow-up) have one list for each, in etatd03b and etatd04b, with the options 1 (loss, insomnia), 2 (gain, hypersomnia) and 3 ("ne sais pas"); etatd03c and etatd04c are then empty. Form 182 is in no menu and in no list of simplified visits now (request A70; its "Score total" ETAT_SCORE is never filled); the boxes last appear between 2016-02 and 2016-12, in 10 centres, and no visit from 2017 holds them. No column names the form: a visit that holds etatd03c or etatd04c has the boxes (etatd_detail_form), the others the list, which includes 429 visits with no detail at all (weight and sleep both "no", or the detail left empty): 148 of them are dated to 2016 and 144 of these have weight and sleep both "no", so their form is unknown; they are delivered as list. By the detail columns alone the two forms meet in 9 of the 146 centre-years; counting the visits with no detail as list, in 28 (and the list is in 6 centres in 2012-13 and 12 of 14 by 2016-09, against 3 and 6 by the detail columns alone). A comparison of the yes rates by form is therefore biased. The option 3 of the list is "ne sais pas", not "both". An earlier reading of the other scales of the same visits (the MADRS "reduced appetite" and the QIDS "weight loss" are high with code 1 and low with code 2, which stands: 1 is a loss or an insomnia, 2 a gain or a hypersomnia) had called 3 "both". The options of ETAT6 and ETAT9 in forms 128 and 183 settle it, so 3 is a missing code: 44 cells (29 weight, 15 sleep) go from a category to missing. The wording of etatd09 adds "or a specific plan" to the BP wording ("ou plan precis pour se suicider"): the yes rates are not comparable. At a MADRS suicide item of 2, 64% of the DR visits answer yes against 38% in BP; at 3, 87% against 73%; at 4, 96% against 86%. Same instrument as in FACE BP, with the codings and the details of the TRD form.

etat_maniaque.title: Manic symptoms present at the visit (DSM-IV checklist)

bp.notes: Part of the "État du patient" form (the section is called "Episode maniaque actuel"): a checklist of the nine symptoms of a DSM-IV manic episode (two mood items and seven symptoms), filled at the inclusion visit and at the follow-up visits. The instruction of the form is to fill it whatever the mood state of the patient (euthymic, depressed, manic, hypomanic or mixed) and to tick the symptoms present: it lists the symptoms present at the visit, it is not an episode and not a diagnosis. It is the same form for every patient, so it does not depend on dsm_version. The answers are Y, N and U in the extraction. Y and N are delivered as 1 and 0, so that the symptoms can be counted. U ("does not know") is a missing code. The stored count (etatm) is the application's own: the score step of the export has no definition for it. The application computes it when the button "Calculer le score" is clicked (hetero_etat_patient.js): Oui is 1, Non is 0, any other answer ("Ne sais pas") is -999 and gives "Score non calculable", and a blank item makes the script stop with an error (line 82, the variable champ does not exist there), so the field keeps its old value (request A64). The package counts the symptoms from the answers, and needs all nine to be yes or no, like the stored count. It is delivered on 15,283 visits and the stored count is absent on 677 of them. It differs from the stored one on 22 visits (stored lower on 19, higher on 3): they get score_mismatch and the recomputed count is kept; two stored counts sit on visits where an item is missing (score_not_recomputed). 106 visits (0.7% of the 15,389 where the nine are answered) get no count because one answer is "Ne sais pas", and 40 more have an item left blank. The count is the number of symptoms ticked, not a measure of mania: a count of 3 or more is met on 1,419 of the 15,283 counts (9.3%); the rule of criterion B (a mood item and 3 of the 7 other symptoms, 4 if the mood is only irritable: the DSM-5 counts as reproduced by Osipov 2016, scale_reference.md section 25; the list of the seven symptoms and the DSM-IV-TR counts could not be read in the manuals, literature check 2026-11-21) is met on 676 (4.4%); a YMRS of 12 or more on 519 of the 15,197 of those visits that have one. The duration is not asked. The form is filled less and less: of the visits that hold a MADRS, YMRS, FAST or CGI rating, 95% have it up to 2017, 88% in 2018-2022 and 86% from 2023; one centre goes from 98% to 44% and 10%.

No count of symptoms is stored here (the BP count is the application's own, computed on a button): etatm_total is the number of symptoms present, when the nine are answered yes or no (1,432 visits; 19 visits have a "does not know" and get no count). fast.title: Functioning Assessment Short Test (FAST)

bp.notes: 24 items scored from 0 (no difficulty) to 3 (severe difficulty), six domain scores and a total (Rosa and others 2007; the domains and the item numbers are those of the published form: scale_reference.md, section 5). The domains hold 4, 5, 5, 2, 6 and 2 items, so they run from 0 to 12, 15, 15, 6, 18 and 6; the total runs from 0 to 72 (observed 0 to 72, two visits at the maximum). The stored total equals the sum of the 24 items on all 16,604 visits that have one, because the score step of the export (nucleus, fast.yaml: a strict sum of the 24 items, the total only) writes it again from the items (D120; 1,151 rows of the BP table changed by the step in the run of 2026-11-13): it is a check of the package against the export, not against the application. The six stored domain scores (fast25 to fast30) are the application's, and the score step does not touch them. The application computes them when the button "Calculer le score" is clicked and not on saving (D106): each differs from the sum of its items on 0.2% to 0.8% of the visits that have both (446 cells in all: 50, 122, 69, 25, 91 and 89), in every period, and 3,240 recomputed domain scores have no stored one (549, 582, 554, 522, 527, 506). The domain scores are therefore recomputed here and compared with the stored ones (score_mismatch). The sums and the domains are those of the scoring script of the application. That script sums each domain alone, so a domain with every item answered has its score even when another domain is incomplete: 335 visits hold some but not all of the 24 items, 333 of them get a domain score and none a total. 48 stored domain values sit on visits where one of their items is missing (score_not_recomputed). The script of the DR application (form 130) differs: it stops at the first incomplete domain and empties every domain and the total. A score needs all its items, as in the EMR, which stores no score when an item is missing. No pro-rating (the original publication has none either).

dr.notes: 24 items rated 0 (no difficulty) to 3 (severe difficulty); six domain scores and a total (0 to 72, higher is worse; Rosa and others 2007; scale_reference.md, section 5). The 24 items are the same, in the same order, as in FACE BP (form 130 of the DR application checked against the BP form). The stored total is the export's: the data flow (nucleus definition fast.yaml, which names the DR table too) writes the strict sum of the 24 items. It equals the sum of the items on all 513 visits that have the 24 items, by construction, and is empty on the others. The six domain scores (fast25 to fast30) are the application's own and the export does not touch them: each equals the sum of its items wherever both exist (0 difference), and a domain score is stored less often than its items are complete (the recomputed one fills 61, 21, 60, 115, 45 and 66 visits). The script of the DR application differs from the BP one (form 130, js_scores/130_score.js; request A66): it stops at the first incomplete domain and empties all six domain scores and the total when one item is blank, where the BP domain scripts sum each domain alone. The package follows the BP rule (a domain with all its items has its score), so on the 59 visits that hold some but not all of the 24 items it delivers 273 domain scores that the DR script would have left empty (54, 11, 57, 56, 40 and 55 per domain) and no total. The DR script also leaves a domain empty on 95 complete visits where every item of the domain is 0 (7, 10, 3, 59, 5 and 11 per domain, of 527 zero-sum domains: the 432 others hold 0): the cause is not known (question to the data managers, PROGRESS.md D61). The schema is the BP one (no difference to list in differences.yaml: the difference is in the script). Rated at the inclusion visit and at two and four years. Filled at about 90% of the V0 visits until 2017 and at about half of them since 2018 (open question O1): FAST is one of the forms that the simplified visit omits (PROGRESS.md D55, request R139). Same instrument as in FACE BP.

fast.reference: Rosa AR, Sanchez-Moreno J, Martinez-Aran A, et al. Validity and reliability of the Functioning Assessment Short Test (FAST) in bipolar disorder. Clin Pract Epidemiol Ment Health 2007;3:5
fast.reference_confidence: confirmed in source (abstract + extracted full text)
fast.period: previous 15 days (published scale, Rosa 2007; the form of the paper gives no time frame)

The thresholds are published for the total only. Which of 12, 20 and 40 is the remission line and which the recovery line in Bonnin 2018 is 'to verify'.
In DR the scale is not asked on the simplified visits of 2018 onward: an empty FAST there is 'not asked'.
The original paper gives no rule for items that do not apply (work items of a retired patient).

madrs.title: Montgomery-Asberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS)

bp.notes: Ten clinician-rated items, each 0 to 6. The dictionary labels only the even anchors (0, 2, 4, 6); odd values are valid intermediate ratings and are present in the data. The stored total (madrs_) equals the sum of the ten items on every visit where both exist (17,334): no score_mismatch. That is true by construction and checks the items and the formula of the export, not the application. The score step of the export (nucleus, madrs.yaml: a strict sum of the ten items) writes madrs_ again after its models (D120); its changelog lists 206 rows of the BP table changed by the step in the run of 2026-11-13. The application computes the total only when the button "Calculer le score" is clicked (hetero_madrs.js, lines 20 to 24), so the value that it stores is stale after an edit of an item, and it writes "Questionnaire incomplet" when an item is missing, as the strict sum does. The rule is the plain sum of the ten items, 0 to 60 (Montgomery and Asberg, 1979; the range 0 to 60 is read in published analysis plans; the 1979 full text, which would state it, could not be read: literature check 2026-11-21, scale_reference.md, section 1). The observed maximum is 51. The export's madrs.yaml gives scale_max 50: it is used only to reverse items (none here), so it changes nothing, but the published maximum is 60 (request R137). 13% of the ratings are odd values (the dictionary labels only the even anchors 0, 2, 4, 6). The columns ending in _n1 (a separate dictionary section) are the mood at the neuropsychological assessment, which the forms of that tab open when the last MADRS is more than a week old (D119), not residuals; they are not loaded (decision D27 in PROGRESS.md; whether to deliver them is decided with the NEUROPSYCHOLOGIE tab, M37).

dr.notes: Ten items rated 0 to 6 by the clinician; the total is their sum (0 to 60, Montgomery and Asberg 1979; scale_reference.md, section 1). The stored total is the export's: the data flow (the nucleus definition madrs.yaml, which names the DR table too) writes the strict sum of the ten items over the total of the form, which is the same plain sum (the script js_scores/100_score.js empties the field when an item is empty). The stored total equals the sum on all 2,065 visits that have the ten items and is empty on the others, by construction: the comparison validates the items and the export formula, not the application. The observed maximum is 60. Two administrations in the same columns. The scale is rated at the screening visit (form 100: 561 ratings, median 30) and again at the inclusion visit (form 123: 605 ratings, median 28), then at every follow-up visit. 538 patients have both: the inclusion total is 1.8 points lower on average (SD 6.0, correlation 0.63) after a median gap of 14 days. The two are separate rows (screening and V0), so no split of the schema is needed; analyses that want one baseline must choose. Form 174 is a third copy of the form that no menu offers. The inclusion criterion "MADRS above 20" (inclusion_criteria) is ticked for 631 patients. 558 of them have a screening total, 10 of these are 20 or less, and 73 have no screening total (the box was ticked without the scale at screening). The MADRS is on the simplified visit (visite.SVUPDES = 1): it is kept there, with the QIDS, the CGI, the EQ-5D and the MDQ (open question O1, answered in PROGRESS.md D55). It is filled at 91% to 100% of the V0 visits in every period. Same instrument as in FACE BP.

Remission cut-offs differ between publications (4 to 10).

ymrs.title: Young Mania Rating Scale (YMRS)

bp.notes: Eleven items. Items 5, 6, 8 and 9 count double and are scored 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8 (the form offers the letters a to e, and the script of the application and the export both turn them into 0, 2, 4, 6, 8: hetero_ymrs.js, ebipolar_hetero_ymrs.sql); the others are scored 0 to 4. The total goes up to 60 (7 items of 0 to 4 and 4 of 0 to 8, the item ranges of the published scale, Young and others 1978, scale_reference.md section 2; the total is their sum). The observed maximum is 36. The stored total equals the sum of the 11 items on all 17,246 visits that have one: no score_mismatch. That is true by construction and checks the items and the formula of the export, not the application. The score step of the export (nucleus, ymrs.yaml: a strict sum of the 11 items) writes ymrs_ again after its models (D120; its changelog lists 215 rows of the BP table changed in the run of 2026-11-13). The application computes the total only when the button "Calculer le score" is clicked (hetero_ymrs.js, lines 21 to 32), so its stored value is stale after an edit and says "Questionnaire incomplet" when an item is missing: a total needs all its items. No doubled item holds an odd value. The dictionary gives no label for the items; the labels here are those of the published scale. The columns ending in _n1 are the mood at the neuropsychological assessment (see madrs): not loaded (D27).

sz.notes: Eleven items. Items 5, 6, 8 and 9 count double and are scored 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8; the others are scored 0 to 4. The total goes up to 60 (Young et al. 1978; scale_reference.md, section 2). The form is the one of FACE BP. Each item is a row of five options (a to e); the script of the form (hetero_ymrs.js) gives the position of the option for items 1 to 4, 7, 10 and 11 and twice the position for items 5, 6, 8 and 9, and the total adds the eleven. The cell of the extraction is the option turned into a number by the export, and the export does it in two ways (eschizo_hetero_ymrs.sql, lines 47 to 86): items 5, 8 and 9 give a to e as 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, the levels, where the form, FACE BP and FACE DR give points (0, 2, 4, 6, 8); only item 6 gives points. This is a slip of the export (request R135), not another form: the earlier reading that "the SZ form stores levels" (decision D26, open question O31) is wrong. The extraction therefore holds 0, 1, 2, 3 or 4 for items 5, 8 and 9: never a value above 4, and an odd value on 80%, 56% and 96% of the visits where the item is not 0, in every one of the 17 years from 2010 to 2026 and in 11 of the 12 centres (the twelfth holds one rating). Item 6 holds 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8 as published. In FACE BP and FACE DR the four items hold 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8 (no odd value on 17,246 and 1,033 visits). Items 5, 8 and 9 are read through the codes 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 to 0, 2, 4, 6, 8: they are real items of 0 to 8 and mean the same as in the other cohorts, and the total is the published one. WARNING. These codes are right for this extraction only. When the export is corrected (R135) the cells will hold the points, and the codes must then be taken out (or read as points, 0 to 0, 2 to 2, 4 to 4, 6 to 6, 8 to 8), or every value would be doubled without any flag. Stored total: not delivered. The nucleus score step of the export adds the eleven columns as they are (nucleus definition ymrs.yaml, strict sum; it overwrites the column of the application), so with the levels of items 5, 8 and 9 the stored total counts them once. It is reproduced exactly by the twin score ymrs_total_as_stored, which reads the levels (the hidden variables ymrs05_level, ymrs08_level and ymrs09_level), checks the stored value and is not delivered (no mismatch on the 4,538 visits that have one). The delivered total is higher than the stored one on the 776 visits (17%) where one of the three items is not 0, by 2.1 points on average and by 9 at most; at inclusion its mean is 2.25 where the stored one gives 1.86. The gap moves the totals across the usual lines: 57 visits reach 12 with the delivered total and not with the stored one, and 18 reach 21; 129 patients reach 12 or more at some visit (78 with the stored total) and 25 reach 21 or more (8). The dictionary calls a total of 12 or more a current manic episode (conventions for 12, 7 and 25 are in scale_reference.md, section 2). A total needs all its items. The dictionary gives no label for the items and says "0 normal to 4 severe anomaly" for all of them, which hides the items of 0 to 8; the labels here are those of the published scale (item names confirmed in scale_reference.md).
sz.difference: the export maps items 5, 8 and 9 to the levels 0 to 4 where BP, DR and the form give points (a slip of the export, request R135), so these three items are read through codes as points (0, 2, 4, 6, 8, as published and as in BP); the stored total counts the levels once and is checked by a twin score that reads the levels in hidden variables

dr.section: YMRS (Young Mania Rating Scale, Young et al. 1978)
dr.notes: Eleven items; items 5, 6, 8 and 9 are rated 0 to 8 and the others 0 to 4 (Young et al. 1978; scale_reference.md, section 2), so the total runs from 0 to 60. The form keys the four double-weight items 0, 2, 4, 6, 8 and the script (js_scores/125_score.js) adds the keys as they are: nothing is doubled in the package, as in FACE BP (where the script doubles the letters a to e). Mania is rare in this cohort: the median total is 0. The stored total is the export's: the data flow (nucleus definition ymrs.yaml, which names the DR table too) writes the strict sum of the eleven items. It equals the sum of the items on all 1,033 visits that have them (observed maximum 44), by construction, so the comparison validates the items and the export formula, not the application. Rated at the inclusion and follow-up visits. Filled at 90% of the V0 visits until 2017 (245 of 271) and at 50% since 2018 (183 of 363), like thirteen other scales (open question O1): a visit with the BAS holds the YMRS on 97% (the reverse, 98%). Answered by the application (PROGRESS.md D55): the simplified visit (visite.SVUPDES = 1, config/globale2.php, DESTVISIMP) keeps the MADRS, the QIDS, the CGI, the EQ-5D, the MDQ, the EGF, the ATHF and the etat du patient forms and omits the YMRS (form 125), the BAS (124), the FAST (130), the SACHS (225) and the ERD (228). An empty YMRS since 2018 is "not asked" on a simplified visit, not "no mania"; the extraction does not say which visits were simplified (request R127: the svupdes column). Since 2018, of the 12 centres with 10 V0 visits or more, three fill the YMRS on 89% to 97% of their V0 visits and five on 4% to 17%. Same instrument as in FACE BP and FACE SZ.

cpt2.title: Conners' Continuous Performance Test II (CPT-II)

bp.notes: A sustained-attention test on a computer; the psychologist copies the results of the report into the form. 3,154 visits hold any cell (3,152 a value or a T-score), 2,374 to 2017 and 777 in 2018 to 2021, 3 later. The CPT-3 took its place in 2022 (516 visits from 2022, 9 in 2018 to 2021) and has its own columns and its own schema (cpt3.yaml); the edition is whichever block is filled, and 2 visits (centre D, 2020 and 2021) have both. The column cpt_version follows the edition of the WAIS and is ignored, and so is visit_neuropsychologie, which equals visit. Twelve measures. Each has a value, a T-score, a percentile and the guideline printed by the report; omissions, commissions and perseverations also have a percentage. The T-scores, the percentiles and the guidelines come from the software and are delivered as stored: nothing can be recomputed (the eBipolar form has no script for them). A higher T-score or percentile is a more atypical performance (the T-score falls where the detectability rises), while the d-prime of the CPT-IP of SZ is better when higher. The names hit_rt and hit_rt_se are not those of the CPT-3 (hrt, hrt_sd): they are other statistics (a standard error against a standard deviation), and no CPT name is shared across cohorts. Winsorising. The values (counts, times, d-prime) are winsorised at the 1st and 99th percentiles of the cohort (585 cells flagged winsorised). The T-scores (12) and the percentages (3) are not: a T-score is a standard scale, and clipping it at cohort percentiles would make its tails depend on the cohort. The percentiles are not winsorised either. Without the clipping 805 cells (689 T-scores, 116 percentages) keep their stored number. Typing errors. 57 cells of 44 visits end out_of_range: a T-score 18 (16 above 1,000, 2 negative), a percentile 14 (8 above 1,000, 6 from 258 to 990), a percentage 4 and a value 21; centres B 11, C 9, D 24, E 1, F 3, I 8, L 1. They look like lost or misplaced decimal points (5045 for 50.45, but the number of decimals is not known), not like raw scores typed in the T columns: on the 15 T-scores out of range whose raw column is not zero, the T-score equals the raw column on none. One visit of centre B, in 2023, holds CPT-3 style T-scores (20 to 90) in 10 of its 12 value columns and nothing in its T columns. The limits are wide on purpose: an omission T-score above 100 is common (418 visits), because few healthy people miss a target. The guidelines are spelled as in the extraction (Midly atypical, Very good perfomance). Unparsed cells. The 23 cells that stay unparsed (18 variables) are typing errors that no rule can read: 8 hold a word, or a letter with a digit, and 15 a malformed number (two decimal points, a slash, a double minus or a superscript); none is repaired.

cpt2.description: A sustained-attention test on a computer. The psychologist copies the results of the software report into the form: twelve measures, each with a value, a T-score, a percentile and the guideline printed by the report.
flags: T-scores, percentiles and guidelines come from the test software and are delivered as stored: nothing can be recomputed.
For the detectability the value and its T-score go in opposite directions (the T-score falls where the detectability rises).

The notes do not say what a higher value means for the commissions, the perseverations, the variability, the response style and the change measures; only their T-scores and percentiles have a stated direction.
The values (counts, times, d-prime) are winsorised at the 1st and 99th percentiles of the cohort; the T-scores, the percentages and the percentiles are not.
An omission T-score above 100 is common and the limits are wide on purpose; cells with a lost decimal point end out_of_range.
The CPT-3 replaced this test in 2022 and is another instrument (cpt3): no variable name is shared, and hit_rt_se (a standard error) is not hrt_sd (a standard deviation).

cpt3.title: Conners' Continuous Performance Test 3 (CPT-3)

bp.notes: The third edition of the test, in the extraction from 2018: 526 visits hold any cell (525 a T-score), 516 of them from 2022 and only 9 in 2018 to 2021, when the CPT-II still ran (777 visits in 2018-21, cpt2.yaml). It is another instrument than the CPT-II, with its own columns: nothing has to be split, and the edition is whichever block is filled. Two visits of centre D (2020 and 2021) have both. The column cpt_version follows the edition of the WAIS (wais3, wais4) and visit_neuropsychologie equals visit: both are rightly ignored. The dictionary names these columns with a final underscore (cpt306a_) that the extraction does not have. Nine measures, each with a T-score and the level printed by the report. The level is filled on 17% (perseverations) to 67% (hit reaction time) of the visits that have the T-score, and it is a function of the T-score: on 1,822 of 1,843 cells it is the level that the same T-score has for the same measure. The T-score, the percentile and the level come from the Conners software, and the eBipolar form has no script for them (its only CPT script is the mean d-prime of the CPT-IP): nothing can be recomputed. The T-score is capped at 90 by the software (35 cells, in 6 of the nine measures): 90 means at least 90. A higher T-score is a more atypical performance, as in the CPT-II (the T-score falls where the detectability rises); in the CPT-IP of SZ a higher d-prime is a better performance. The names hrt and hrt_sd are not those of the CPT-II (hit_rt, hit_rt_se): a standard deviation of the reaction times is not a standard error of the hits, so they are other statistics, and no CPT name is shared across cohorts. Raw values typed in the T columns. On 36 visits, all of centre D (35 from January to September 2022 and one in 2020), the nine T columns hold the raw value of the report: a d-prime from -0.01 to 2.2, 0 to 18 omissions, 0 to 36 commissions, a hit reaction time of 296 to 619 ms, a hit reaction time SD of 3 to 13, and so on. A valid T-score of the hit reaction time never exceeds 90, so a value above 100 in cpt303a selects exactly these visits (cpt3_hrt_t_typed, read a second time and not delivered). Their raw values that fall outside 20 to 90 end out_of_range (312 of the 321 out_of_range cells). 12 raw values fall inside 20 to 90 (9 commissions, 1 variability, 1 block change, 1 ISI change) and would pass for T-scores: they keep their value and get check_failed (cpt3_typed_raw). There is no raw column to receive the raw values, so they are not delivered as such. 44 visits hold a value outside 20 to 90 (27 to 38 out_of_range cells per column): 36 carry raw values and 8 hold 9 cells from 4 to 19, below the 20 of the scale.

cpt3.description: The third edition of the Conners continuous performance test, a sustained-attention test on a computer. Nine measures, each with a T-score and the level printed by the report. In the BP extraction, mostly from 2022.
flags: The T-score is capped at 90 by the software: 90 means at least 90.
The T-scores and levels come from the test software: nothing can be recomputed.
On 36 visits the raw values of the report were typed in the T columns: those outside 20 to 90 end out_of_range, and the 12 that fall inside 20 to 90 keep their value with check_failed.
Another instrument than the CPT-II (cpt2), with its own columns: no variable name is shared between the two, nor with the CPT-IP of SZ, where a higher d-prime is a better performance.

cvlt.title: California Verbal Learning Test (CVLT)

bp.section: Troubles des acquisitions et des apprentissages
bp.notes: A list of 16 words ("Monday list") learned over five trials, a second list ("Tuesday list", list B), then recalls of the first list after a short and a long delay, free and cued, and a recognition task. 5,849 visits have a trial 1. In the dictionary the CVLT has no header: it follows the learning disorders. Raw scores. Recalls are numbers of words, 0 to 16. The total of trials 1 to 5 is recomputed and compared with the stored one (cvlt06_). Discriminability. It is recomputed, as the project lead asked: 100 x (hits + 28 - false alarms) / 44, from the correct and false recognitions (16 targets, 28 distractors). The clinician types the stored value (cvlt18_); it is only a check now, with a tolerance of 0.5, and it equals the formula within 0.5 on 4,819 of 5,153 visits (93.5%). Of the 334 others, 31 are on a scale of 0 to 1 (the formula divided by 100, within 0.01: one centre, 27 of them from 2024), 27 are 0 where the formula gives 50 or more, 20 equal 100 minus the formula (14 of them are among those zeros) and 270 differ by 2.3 points (median). The recomputed score is delivered on 5,754 visits (the stored one was on 5,182): 601 more, where the recognitions are filled and the discriminability is not, and 29 fewer, where a discriminability was stored without recognitions (score_not_recomputed). Its percentile band is read in the table from the recomputed value (cvlt_discriminability_band is a score now, not a band variable): it equals the percentile that the EMR wrote on 93.4% of the 5,162 visits that have both; 234 of the 340 differences are on visits whose stored value differs from the formula. The semantic and serial clustering indices, the perseverations, the intrusions, primacy and recency (percent) are delivered as stored, within wide limits. They cannot be rebuilt: they need the words that the patient said, in the order of the trials, which the extraction does not hold (the clinician types the indices, and the form only reads their percentile as they are typed). The response bias is delivered as stored too. It follows (false alarms minus the missed targets) / (false alarms plus the missed targets) only approximately (the missed targets being 16 - hits): within 0.01 on 87.6% of 5,080 visits, a perfect recognition giving 0 (stored on 2,561 of 2,577 of them). The formula of the software is to be asked of the data managers. Standardised scores (decisions D38, D39 and D108 in PROGRESS.md). The norms give a z-score (a regression on the age, the years of education and the sex) or a percentile (a table), depending on the measure and on the age group: - a z-score at every age: trial 1, trials 1 to 5, list B, primacy, recency, bias; - a percentile at every age: serial clustering, perseverations, intrusions, correct and false recognitions, discriminability; - trial 5: a percentile up to 69 years, a z-score from 70; - the four delayed recalls: a percentile up to 39 years, a z-score from 40; - semantic clustering: a percentile from 40 to 69, a z-score otherwise. The EMR writes both in the same column: a z-score with two decimals, a percentile as a band ("25 - 50", "<1") or as a whole number (1, 5, 25, 50, 75, 95 or 99). Z-scores computed again (decision D108, asked by the project lead). The twelve z-scores are not read from the extraction. They are computed with the regressions of the scoring script of the application, from the raw score, the age at the visit in completed years, the years of education (cclin08_, read here a second time) and the sex. The regressions are files of the norms folder (norms/cvlt_*_z.csv), which is not in the repository; without them the z-scores are missing with norm_missing. The stored z-scores are only compared with the computed ones. Why. With the age typed in the form, the script of today gives back the stored z-score to the hundredth on 95% to 99% of the visits for eleven measures. For trials 1 to 5 it is 91.5%: - 232 stored z-scores were computed with the coefficients of the age and of the sex exchanged: 160 of them in 2013 and 2014, and 60 for the patients of 70 and over, whom the script scored that way until a correction dated 2024-08-02. 216 of the 241 stored values above 5 are these; - 105, most of 2012 and 2015, were computed with no sex (the sex term counted 0), as were about 50 z-scores each of the delayed free recalls, of the primacy and of the recency; - on 43 visits the recency z-score was computed from an empty recency, as if it were 0; - the recency z-score of the patients of 40 to 69 holds "Non applicable" on 975 visits (982 in all): the older form wrote that, the form of today computes a z-score for them. Computed again, the z-score of trials 1 to 5 has the same mean in 2013 and 2014 as in the other years (-0.20 and -0.24), and no value above 5 where the stored column has 241. The age. The EMR used the age typed in the neuropsychology form; the package uses the age at the visit, as for every other norm. The two are the same number of years on 87% to 91% of the visits until 2023 and on 67% from 2024, when the application began to fill the field itself, with the age rounded to the nearest year. One year of age moves a z-score by a few hundredths, and by more on the 34 visits where it changes the age group. The stored z-score is therefore compared with a tolerance of 0.25. score_mismatch says that the stored one was further away: 380 visits for trials 1 to 5 (6.5% of 5,819; 16.3% in 2013-15, 7.6% to 2012, 1.7% to 4.2% in the later periods; for 254 of them the stored z-score is 3.5 or more above the computed one, for 166 in 2013 and 2014 and for 61 patients of 70 and over), about 100 for the primacy, 5 to 50 for the other measures, and 1,697 for the recency, whose norm is corrected (see below). The computed z-score is the one delivered. Where a z-score was stored and none can be computed, the cell gets score_not_recomputed (303 cells on the twelve z-scores, 305 with the total of trials 1 to 5): no raw score, no years of education, a computed z-score outside its limits, or an age for which the norms give a percentile. Recency: two lines of the norm are not those of the BP script (decision D109, by the project lead; to confirm with the manual, open question O50). The raw recency is the same at every age (25% on average), and the patients under 40 have a mean z-score of 0.05. As the BP script computes it, the patients of 40 to 69 are at -0.82 and those of 70 and over at -3.71. - From 40 to 69 the z-score is (recency - mean) / sd. The scripts of the application are not alike (open question O50; DM-16 for the data managers): the BP script has a mean of its own, the SZ script writes "Non applicable" at these ages, and a test script has a third mean that is within 0.01 of the intercept of the line of the patients under 40 (a copy of it?). The SZ z-scores that hold a number follow the third (2 mismatches at these ages). The BP mean is 0.78 standard deviation from the third, which is used here, for both cohorts: the mean z-score of the patients of 40 to 69 is then -0.04. - From 70 the sign of the age term is turned: the script adds a term that the other lines of the norm subtract. The line for 70 and over is the same in the three scripts. The mean z-score of the 62 visits that have one (63 have a recency) is then -0.27. The stored recency z-scores of these ages therefore all get score_mismatch (1,560 visits from 40 to 69, 61 from 70). One band for every age (decisions D44 and D45, asked by the project lead). Each measure has a band variable that is filled for all patients. Where the norms have a percentile table for the age of the patient, the band is read in it, from the raw score and the age at the visit (norms/cvlt_*.csv, not in the repository; without them these bands are missing with norm_missing). Elsewhere the band is the one the computed z-score has under the normal law, as the EMR note proposes: the cell gets band_from_z. So the bands of trial 1, trials 1 to 5, list B, primacy, recency and bias all come from z-scores, and those of the six mixed measures come from a table for one age group and from a z-score for the other. The conversion assumes a normal law in the norm group, which the note says is not validated clinically. For the recalls a higher band is a better performance. For primacy, recency and bias a higher band only means a higher value. The measures that have a table at every age keep their band variable (perseverations, intrusions, correct and false recognitions): where the cell holds a percentile, the band is read again in the table. The discriminability has a band score instead, read in the table from the recomputed discriminability on every visit that has one. The reason for reading the tables again is one rule for every test. When several limits of the norms fall on the same raw score, the EMR wrote the highest percentile for the CVLT: every cell written 99 for trial 5 and the delayed recalls is a perfect recall of 16 words. The table gives the lowest band such a score can be, with <variable>_cens = +1 (this band or a higher one), as for the TMT errors. Where no limits coincide the band of the table is the one the EMR wrote on 96% to 100% of the visits (serial clustering 96.4%, semantic clustering 97.8%, trial 5 98.0%, the other measures 99.4% to 99.9%). The exception is the discriminability, whose band reads the recomputed value (93.4%, see the raw scores). The stored percentile cells are compared with the recomputed bands only by hand, not in the load. Serial clustering is read in its table too (decision D129). The EMR note gave it in whole numbers although the index has decimals; the script of the application holds the exact limits, with decimals from 40 to 69 years, and the same table in the BP and in the SZ form. Of the 4,970 BP visits with an index, an age and a band, the script's rule gives the stored band on 96.5%; the others are bands computed before the index was changed. The table gives one rule for every year and both cohorts, with the same tie rule as the eleven others. What remains between the two sources of a mixed band. For the four delayed recalls, 18% to 27% of the bands read in the table are open bands at the top of the scale (the perfect recalls, "95 or higher"), against 2% to 4% of the bands computed from a z-score that reach 95; there a perfect recall is most often one band lower. This is not a difference of rule: the norm table and the regression do not place a perfect recall at the same level. Under band 25 the shares are 20% to 25% against 31% to 36%. Bands. The value is the lower limit of the band: 0 (under the 1st percentile), 1, 5, 25, 50, 75, 95 or 99. Limits. The z-score of a recall is kept from -8 to 5: a patient who recalls very few words is far below the norm group, and FACE SZ has 72 z-scores of trials 1 to 5 under -5 for raw totals of 28 words or fewer (BP has 4). No computed z-score of a recall is outside these limits. Primacy, recency and bias have long tails and keep wider limits (10). Semantic clustering: 13 z-scores are beyond 5 (out_of_range; 104 before the hard range of the index was cut), and here the raw index is the cause, not the formula. In 2012 and 2013, 23% of the indices are above 4 and 24% are whole numbers, against 2% to 7% and 2% to 6% in the other periods: another quantity was typed in that field, probably a number of clusters (open question O49 in PROGRESS.md). Checked on 2026-11-18 (decision D130): 96% of the 2012-2013 visits of one centre hold such a value (median 12 against 2.3, a correlation of 0.36 with the total recall), and the habit goes on at a lower rate in other years and in SZ. By band of the index the share of whole numbers is 2% to 3% up to 4, 17% to 37% from 4 to 6 and above 50% from 6 on. An index of 8 or more is far beyond the 99th percentile of the norm and is mostly a count: the hard range stops at 8 (it was 50), the same in SZ, so 216 BP and 17 SZ values are out_of_range (the typed text stays in the flag log) and so are their z-scores and bands. Between 4 and 8 a few counts remain: of the 200 BP values of 4 or more, 81 are whole numbers, and from 6 to 8, 26 of 43 (60%, against 3.7% of all the values); there are 73 whole numbers between 4 and 8 in BP and 7 in SZ (14 values of 4 or more, 8 whole). Whole numbers cannot be told from an index there, and the index cannot be rebuilt from the counts, which is asked of the data managers (DM-15). The BP thesaurus lists CVLT18Z_ to CVLT22_ twice, also to ask the data managers. Unparsed cells. The 11 cells that stay unparsed are typing errors: 7 decimals typed in whole-number counts, 2 durations typed as text in the delay, an index with two decimal points and a dash. Centre steps, unexplained and left as measured (use a centre term in a pooled analysis): centre H recalls fewer words at every trial and delayed recall (median total of trials 1 to 5 of 48 against 59, 170 visits), centre D has a median delay of 15 minutes against 20, and centre I a median serial clustering index of 0.33 against 1.28.

sz.section: Troubles des acquisitions et des apprentissages
sz.notes: A list of 16 words ("Monday list") learned over five trials, a second list ("Tuesday list", list B), then recalls of the first list after a short and a long delay, free and cued, and a recognition task. 2,298 visits from 2010 to 2026. The BP schema, where the notes give the rules and their evidence (decisions D38, D39, D44, D45, D108 and D109 of the BP file): the z-scores are computed again with the regressions of the norms, from the raw score, the age at the visit, the years of education and the sex; one band per measure for every age, read in the percentile table where the norms have one and the band of the z-score elsewhere. BP and SZ deliver the same 52 variables, with the same units, ranges and direction. What follows is what differs in the SZ extraction. Raw scores. Ten of them are in columns named avl01... (the five trials, list B, the two free recalls, the correct and false recognitions); the others have the BP names. The total of trials 1 to 5 equals the stored one but for 24 visits (score_mismatch). Discriminability. It is recomputed from the correct and false recognitions as in BP, 100 x (hits + 28 - false alarms) / 44, and the stored value (cvlt18_) is a check with a tolerance of 0.5: it equals the formula within 0.5 on 2,038 of 2,197 visits (92.8%). Of the 159 others, 84 are on a scale of 0 to 1 (the formula divided by 100, within 0.01: 5 centres, 81 of them from 2019), 1 equals 100 minus the formula and 74 differ by 2.7 points (median). The recomputed score is delivered on 2,277 visits (the stored one was on 2,202): 80 more, where the recognitions are filled and the discriminability is not, and 5 fewer, where a discriminability was stored without recognitions (score_not_recomputed). Its percentile band is read in the table from the recomputed value (a score, not a band variable): it equals the stored percentile on 93.7% of the 1,816 visits that have both; 86 of the 114 differences are on visits whose stored value differs from the formula. The semantic and serial clustering indices, the perseverations, the intrusions, primacy and recency cannot be rebuilt, as in BP: they need the words that the patient said, which the extraction does not hold; they are delivered as stored. So is the response bias, which follows (false alarms minus the missed targets) / (false alarms plus the missed targets) only approximately (the missed targets being 16 - hits): within 0.01 on 77.1% of 2,067 visits (87.6% in BP). The formula of the software is to be asked of the data managers. Years of education. They come from the first part of the assessment (cclin08_). Until the extraction of 17 November 2026 the export read them in the older form only and they stopped in 2016; they are now on every visit that has a CVLT (decision D35 in PROGRESS.md). The stored z-scores are only compared with the computed ones. For the six measures that give a percentile to one age group and a z-score to the other (trial 5, the four delayed recalls, semantic clustering), SZ has two columns, cvltNNz_ and cvltNNp_, where BP has one, and neither holds one kind of value: the check variable reads the two and keeps the cells written with decimals. The percentile cells are not delivered and are not compared with the recomputed bands in the load: in older rows the percentiles sit in the z column, and the p column holds those of the patients under 40. The SZ thesaurus names cvlt13p_ to cvlt18p_ where the extraction has cvlt13z_ to cvlt18z_ (six names), to ask the data managers. What the comparison shows (decision D35). The stored z-score of trials 1 to 5 was computed with the coefficients of the age and of the sex exchanged on 303 visits (the stored value is 3.5 or more above the computed one, by 3.8 to 12.5 points, 282 of them by 4 to 9.5), from January 2021 to June 2026, in eleven centres: until a correction dated 2024-08-02 the script of the SZ form did so for the patients under 70, and each centre runs its own copy of the application. After that date 83 of the 237 visits that have both z-scores still carry the exchanged coefficients, in 8 centres (the last on 2026-06-09; two centres have 58 of them, one with 39 of its 44 visits and the other with all 19 of its visits). These values were too high by 4 to 9.5 points on most visits. They are computed again like the others, and the doubt period that covered them is no longer needed. The stored z-score of trials 1 to 5 is a score_mismatch on 333 visits, 14.8% of the 2,243 that have both (60.6% in 2022-23, 46.9% from 2024, 0.8% to 3.9% in the other periods). Bands. Where no limits are tied, the bands read in the percentile tables equal the stored percentiles on 95.9% of the visits for serial clustering, 96.7% for semantic clustering, 97.8% for the correct recognitions and 98.6% to 99.1% for the other measures (BP: 96.4% to 99.9%). On the 608 SZ cells of the correct recognitions where several limits are tied, the stored percentile is the lowest band that the raw score can have on 68%, against 13% in BP and none for the other measures, where the EMR wrote the highest percentile. Limits. The patients of this cohort recall fewer words than the norm group, so a z-score of a recall may be far below 0: the limits of the recalls go from -8 to 5 here and in BP. Missing codes of this cohort: "xxx", "DCM" and "NF" (about 130 cells). The 48 unparsed cells (26 variables) are typing and export artefacts of raw counts and stored values: 14 band labels written with an HTML entity code (&#88...) in place of a sign, 8 words (six of two letters), 6 ranges typed in a count or a z-score, 6 counts written with a decimal point, 6 band labels with a letter or a plus sign, 4 delays written with their unit, 2 counts with a '>' sign and 2 negative decimals written with a comma. Unexplained and left as measured (use a centre term in a pooled analysis), the centre steps of list B and of the total of trials 1 to 5 (centre J, +0.5 to +0.6 SD) and of serial clustering (centre G, +0.7 SD) and the 5 to 27 mismatches of each z-score other than trials 1 to 5.
sz.difference: ten raw scores are in columns named avl01..., the stored z-scores of six measures are read in two columns, and three more missing codes

cvlt.description: A list of 16 words learned over five trials, a second list (list B), then recalls of the first list after a short and a long delay, free and cued, and a recognition task. Raw scores, z-scores and percentile bands.
cvlt.version: 16-word list ('Monday list') and list B ('Tuesday list')
sources: docs/bp/PROGRESS.md D38, D44, D45, D108, D109
flags: The z-scores are computed again with the regressions of the norms (raw score, age at the visit, years of education, sex). The z-scores that the application stored followed several rules over the years and are only checks.

The notes give a direction for the recalls only. For primacy, recency and bias a higher band only means a higher value. For the semantic and serial clustering, the perseverations, the intrusions, the recognitions and the discriminability, no document says whether a higher band is better.
A band taken from a z-score (flag band_from_z) assumes a normal law in the norm group, which the note of the application says is not validated clinically.
A band with <variable>_cens = +1 means this band or a higher one (several limits of the norms fall on the raw score, as for a perfect recall of 16 words).
Recency z-score: two lines of the norm are corrected by a decision of the project lead (D109), to confirm with the manual (open question O50).

Semantic clustering index: in some periods another quantity, probably a number of clusters, was typed in the field. Values of 8 or more are out_of_range; a few counts remain between 4 and 8 (open question O49).
A z-score needs the years of education; without the norm files the z-scores and bands are missing (norm_missing).
Centre steps are left as measured: use a centre term in a pooled analysis.
The edition of the test and its reference are not named in the project documents.

common.note: The raw scores stack, and so do the z-scores and the bands: in both cohorts they are computed again with the regressions of the norms, from the raw score, the age, the years of education and the sex. The percentile bands of the twelve measures that have a table (serial clustering too, since BP D129) are read in the same tables from the raw score and the age, with one rule for ties (the lowest band it can be, `_cens` = 1), so a band of BP and a band of SZ are on one scale. The semantic clustering index is out of range from 8 on in both (a typed count, BP D130); a few counts between 4 and 8 cannot be told from an index.

errands_test.title: Errands test (Test des commissions)

bp.notes: A planning test: the patient orders a list of errands under constraints of time and place. In the extraction from 2018 (813 visits with a count of detours, 781 of them from 2022). Raw scores: the time taken in minutes, the useless detours, the trips that miss an opening hour, the logical errors, and the total of the three kinds of errors. The stored total equals their sum on 98.9% of the visits (799 of 808); it is recomputed and compared. 37 times of 819 are written as a duration (5'30, N min N sec, N:N) and stay unparsed: the time, and what is computed from it, is missing there (a reading rule m + s/60 is left for later). Percentiles. They are typed by hand from the norms, with limits that differ from one measure to the next ("20-50", "75-80", ">75"). They are read as bands on one list of limits; the value is the lower limit of the band, and a band wider than one step has <variable>_cens = +1. 19 to 29 cells per measure are a number that is no limit and stay unparsed. z-scores are typed on 24 to 30 visits per measure (34 visits in all, 40 counting "."), from 2022 only; "." is a missing code. They are typed by hand, and they mix two sign conventions (decision D126: a third follow one straight line of the raw score per level of education, a third follow it with the opposite sign, a third follow neither, by centre and in every year). They were withdrawn; they are now replaced by the recomputed values below, and the typed ones are only a check. Recomputed. The percentile bands and the z-scores of the five measures (time, detours, late trips, logical errors, total of the three kinds of errors) are computed again from the raw counts, as the script of the application computes them, with the tables that FACE SZ uses (norms/errands_*_band.csv and errands_*_z.csv). The typed bands and z-scores are kept only as checks (errands_*_band_stored, errands_*_z_stored, not delivered). The band is the lower limit of the band the count falls in, in the table of the education of the patient: under 12 years, or 12 years and more (the baccalauréat is 12 years); a band wider than one step has <variable>_cens = +1. The z-score is (mean - count) / SD in the cell of the education and of the age (20 to 40 years, 41 to 60), so that a higher z-score is a better performance; the time is cut to whole minutes first, as the application does. The age is the one typed in the form (cclin01_) where it is within one year of the age at the visit, and the age at the visit elsewhere. The application computes nothing under 20 or over 60 years: no z-score is delivered there (86 visits with a count of detours, 59 with the ticked class; the bands do not depend on the age and are delivered). Education. The application's tables are two, below the baccalauréat and from it, chosen by the class that the rater ticks (comnsc_, kept as errands_education, no longer used). The package reads the years of education typed in the form (cclin08_) for every visit, as the other tests do, and the tables of norms/ are keyed by years (0 to 11 and 12 and over). Decision of the project lead. The ticked class is filled on 592 of the 813 visits with a count of detours; the years are filled on every one. Years of 12 or more equal the ticked class on 587 of the 596 visits where both exist (the 9 others: 5 at 12 years ticked as below, 1 at 10 years ticked as from, 3 at 14 to 17 years ticked as below); on these 9 visits 25 bands and 34 z-scores differ from the ones the class gave (4 more z-scores, at the clipped edge of the range, move with the winsorising limits). The 221 visits with no ticked class, mostly from 2022, now have their bands (1,091 cells) and z-scores (958 cells), where they had norm_missing. The application does not take the lowest class when none is ticked: the BP form has no script, its values are typed. A stored band on a visit with no ticked class equals the recomputed one in 337 of 374 pairs (90%), a typed z-score in 0 of 16 (7 with the opposite sign). Checks. A band that differs from the typed one is flagged score_mismatch: on 66 of 484 visits for the time (13.6%), 43 of 510 for the detours, 40 of 505 for the late trips, 83 of 500 for the logical errors (16.6%) and 39 of 504 for the total (7.7%): the bands are typed by hand, all the differences are from 2019 on, nearly all from 2022 (268 of 271). A typed value with no count to compute from is flagged score_not_recomputed (33 bands for the time, 0 to 3 for the other measures). The z-scores are delivered on 695 to 728 visits per measure (734 visits in all, from 2018), against 24 to 30 with a typed one. Of the 24 to 28 typed ones that can be compared, 4 to 12 are the recomputed value with the opposite sign (sign_flipped, compare_turned), 8 to 17 follow neither (score_mismatch), and the 3 to 11 others agree. errands_order is the order in which the patient ran the errands, as typed.

sz.notes: A planning test: the patient orders a list of errands under constraints of time and place. In the extraction from 2017 (1,034 visits, 1,025 with a count of detours). Raw scores: the time taken in minutes, the useless detours, the trips that miss an opening hour, the logical errors, and the total of the three kinds of errors. The stored total equals their sum on every visit; it is recomputed and compared. 3 times of 1,034 are written as a duration (5:30) and stay unparsed (a reading rule m + s/60 is left for later). Percentiles. They are typed by hand from the norms, with limits that differ from one measure to the next. They are read as bands on one list of limits; the value is the lower limit of the band, and a band wider than one step has <variable>_cens = +1 (672, 762 and 782 cells for the detours, the late trips and the logical errors, where most patients sit in the widest band; 106 for the total). Ten cells are a number that is no limit and stay unparsed. z-scores are typed on 517 to 520 visits per measure (521 in all); "." is a missing code. Recomputed. The percentile bands and the z-scores of the five measures (time, detours, late trips, logical errors, total of the three kinds of errors) are computed again from the raw counts, as the script of the application computes them (norms/errands_*_band.csv and errands_*_z.csv), and the stored ones are kept only as checks (errands_*_band_stored, errands_*_z_stored, not delivered). The band is the lower limit of the band the count falls in, in the table of the education of the patient: under 12 years, or 12 years and more (the baccalauréat is 12 years); a band wider than one step has <variable>_cens = +1. The z-score is (mean - count) / SD in the cell of the education and of the age (20 to 40 years, 41 to 60), so that a higher z-score is a better performance; the time is cut to whole minutes first, as the application does. The age is the one typed in the form (cclin01_) where it is within one year of the age at the visit, and the age at the visit elsewhere. The application computes nothing under 20 or over 60 years: no z-score is delivered there (36 visits with a count of detours, 30 with the ticked class; the bands do not depend on the age and are delivered). Education. The application's tables are two, below the baccalauréat and from it, chosen by the class that the rater ticks (rad_nsc_, kept as errands_education, no longer used). The package reads the years of education typed in the form (cclin08_) for every visit, as the other tests do, and the tables of norms/ are keyed by years (0 to 11 and 12 and over). Decision of the project lead. The ticked class is filled on 791 of the 1,025 visits with a count of detours; 22.8% (234) have none, from 2017 on in every year, and the years are filled on every visit. Years of 12 or more equal the ticked class on 778 of the 798 visits where both exist (16 of the 21 others, counting all visits, are at 11 or 12 years); on these visits 67 bands and 84 z-scores differ from the ones the class gave. The 234 visits with no ticked class now have their bands (1,170 cells) and z-scores (1,140 cells), where they had norm_missing. The application does not take the lowest class when none is ticked: the script (psy_neuropsychologie_comm.js) fails and writes nothing. A stored band on a visit with no ticked class equals the recomputed one in 193 of 235 pairs (82%), a stored z-score in 10 of 99. Checks. A recomputed value that differs from the stored one is flagged score_mismatch. The band differs on 51 of 744 visits for the time (6.9%), 34 of 743 for the detours, 24 of 742 for the late trips, 39 of 744 for the logical errors and 25 of 637 for the total (3.2 to 5.2%), nearly all from 2019 on (166 of 173), 102 of them in 2022-23. The z-score is delivered on 987 to 992 visits per measure (997 in all, from 2017), against 517 to 520 with a stored one; it differs on 34 to 40 of the 515 to 518 that can be compared (6.6 to 7.7%; 0 to 3 more with the opposite sign, sign_flipped), and 28 to 33 of these differences are from one centre in 2022-23 (16 to 19 are on visits with no ticked class). A typed value with no count to compute from is flagged score_not_recomputed (3 to 6 bands, 1 to 2 z-scores per measure). errands_order is the order in which the patient ran the errands, as typed. Same instrument as in FACE BP, with the ticked class in the SZ column rad_nsc_. The box "test not done" of the SZ form (chk_com_) is not extracted: ask the data managers. Besides the 3 durations and the 10 stored band cells with no limit (numbers, '<2', '>74', a text with a comment, an HTML entity code), 2 typed ages written 'NN ans' (the age at the visit is used), 2 education cells that hold a word (on visits with no test value) and 1 stored z-score and 1 count of late trips typed as ranges ('NN-NN') stay unparsed.

The age and the years of education are those the psychologist entered; the norms of the tests were read with them. The norms are read with the typed age where it is within 1 year of the age at the visit (computed from the dates), else with the age at the visit; neuropsy_age_used delivers the age that was used (missing on a visit with no form), so that a user sees which one it was. It carries no flag. The typed age differs from the age at the visit by more than 1 year on 221 of 6,302 visits (typed lower on 173; 1 to 2 years on 140, more than 2 years on 81). By period: until 2012 55, 2013-15 50, 2016-18 47, 2019-21 40, 2022-23 21, 2024 on 8; by centre D 56, C 42, B 29, A 23. The entry date of the form explains 15 of them (the typed age is within a year of the age on that day). 9 typed ages are written with their unit ("NN ans") and are not read (unparsed, not repaired). scip.title: Screen for Cognitive Impairment in Psychiatry (SCIP)

bp.notes: A short battery of five subtests, in the extraction from 2018 (234 visits hold any cell, 230 a raw score). The SCIP has three parallel forms; scip_form says which one was given (222 visits). Each subtest has a raw score and a z-score. The z-score is computed again as the application computes it: z = (raw score - mean) / SD with one mean and one SD per subtest, constants written on one line of the script of the form, with no age or education term and the same for the three forms (norms/scip_*_z.csv). It is delivered as recomputed and is not winsorised: a z-score of fixed constants is already on its scale, and the clipping at the 1st and 99th percentiles changed 10 cells (3, 2, 3, 0 and 2 for verbal learning, working memory, verbal fluency, delayed recall and visuomotor). Where these constants come from is not checked against the manual (open question DM-4). The stored z-score is kept only as a check (scip_*_z_stored, not delivered). A recomputed z-score that differs from it by more than 0.0101 is flagged score_mismatch: 0, 1, 1, 0 and 0 visits per subtest (the same visit, from 2024, for the working memory and the verbal fluency), against 230, 228, 228, 227 and 227 visits where they agree. A stored z-score with no usable raw score is flagged score_not_recomputed (3 in all). One is a verbal learning whose raw score is empty: the stored z-score is the formula applied to a raw score of 0. The two others are delayed recalls whose raw score is above the limit of 10: the stored z-score is the formula applied to that impossible raw score, and the raw score ends out_of_range. The limits of the test are 30 for verbal learning, 24 for working memory, 10 for the delayed recall and 30 for the visuomotor task. The dictionary writes "/24" for three subtests that have another maximum. The hour of the testing (rad_heure_passation_), listed in this section of the dictionary, is in neuropsy_conditions.yaml.

spatial_span.title: Spatial span (Wechsler Memory Scale III)

bp.notes: The psychologist taps blocks in a sequence that the patient repeats, in the same order (forward) and then in reverse (backward). Eight items of two trials for each order; the test stops after two failures on an item, so the last items are often empty. About 5,235 visits. An item score is the number of its trials passed (0 to 2): 4 of the 82,473 items that have a score and both trials differ. The raw score of an order is the sum of its item scores up to the first item scored 0 (stop_at_zero: the application does not count what is typed after the first failed item), an empty item before it counting 0 (0 to 16). It equals the stored one on every visit that has both (5,222 forward, 5,216 backward, 5,200 for the total of the two orders, 0 to 32); the plain sum of all the items differed on 0.5% of the visits. Recomputed. The scaled scores (1 to 19) and their z-scores are computed again as the application computes them, and the stored values are kept only as checks (*_stored, not delivered). The scaled score is read in the table of the manual (norms/spatial_*_scaled.csv, twelve age groups) from the raw score and the age typed in the form (cclin01_) where it is within one year of the age at the visit, and the age at the visit elsewhere. The z-score is the scaled score brought to mean 0 and SD 1, (scaled - 10) / 3. A scaled score that differs from the stored one is flagged score_mismatch (the z-score within 0.0101), and so is its z-score. Checks. The scaled score equals the stored one on 99.16% of the visits for the forward order (5,193 of 5,237) and for the backward order (5,189 of 5,233), and on 98.81% for the total (5,170 of 5,232): 44, 44 and 62 visits differ (0.8%, 0.8% and 1.2%), and so does the z-score of the same visits. Read with the typed age alone, as the application does, the table gives the stored value on 99.56%, 99.54% and 99.27% of the visits that have a typed age (5,228, 5,224 and 5,223). Of the differences, 24, 23 and 27 are visits whose typed age is more than a year from the age at the visit, mostly by one scaled point: the application read the table with the typed age and the package with the age at the visit. The others have ages that agree. 15, 17 and 32 of them have a stored scaled score 2 or more points from the table's value for the stored raw score: a stored 1 on 14, 17 and 32, for raw scores of 7 to 12 forward, 3 to 12 backward and 11 to 23 for the total, where the table gives more. 5, 4 and 3 differ by one point. One centre accounts for 30 of these 64 differences, and visits with the same raw scores outside them equal the table on 99.4% to 99.5% (99.9% where the ages agree). A possible cause is a scaled score that was computed while the raw score was still 0 and never refreshed: a hypothesis, to ask the data managers. By period, 0.45% to 1.43% of the visits differ (for each of the three scaled scores), and the differences are spread over the centres. One visit has a stored scaled score where no raw score can be computed (score_not_recomputed).
