stroop.title: Stroop Colour and Word Test (Golden)

bp.section: Planche A : Nombre total de mots lus en 45 secondes
bp.notes: Three plates of 45 seconds each: reading colour words (plate A), naming colours (plate B), naming the ink of colour words (plate C), then the interference score. About 5,800 visits. The dictionary gives one section per plate; they are one instrument here. Recomputed. For each plate the extraction holds the number of items, the same number corrected for age, two error counts, a T-score and a z-score. The score corrected for age, the T-score and the z-score are computed again as the application computes them, and the stored values are kept only as checks (stroop_*_stored, not delivered). The corrected score is the number of items plus a fixed number of items for each of three age classes (norms/stroop_age_correction_*.csv), read with the age typed in the form (cclin01_) where it is within one year of the age at the visit, and with the age at the visit elsewhere (200 of the 5,804 visits have a typed age further than a year away, 160 of them typed lower and 150 of them at V0, and the age class of the correction differs on 20 of them; 11 have none, 9 of them text, a number followed by a word). The T-score is read in the table of the manual from the corrected score (steps of two points, from 20 to 80; norms/stroop_*_t.csv, the same at every age). The z-score is the T-score brought to mean 0 and SD 1, (T - 50) / 10. Interference. The colour-word score minus the score predicted from the two other plates, A x B / (A + B), all three corrected for age (function stroop_interference of custom.py). The application rounds it to two decimals before it reads its T-score; the table of the interference has its limits moved down by half a hundredth, so that it gives the same T-score from the value with all its decimals. The T-score and the z-score of the interference are read from the recomputed value. Checks. A recomputed value that differs from the stored one is flagged score_mismatch (the T-score within 0.5, the z-score within 0.0101, the items exactly). Of the visits where both exist: the corrected score differs on 0.6% (34 to 37 visits for each plate), the T-score on 1.0 to 1.2% (56 to 68), the z-score on the same visits plus a few (58 to 68), the interference on 0.9% (54), its T-score and its z-score on 1.1% (64 and 65). About two thirds of the corrected-score differences (22 to 23 of 34 to 37) are visits whose typed age is more than a year from the age at the visit, where the application used the typed age and the package the age at the visit; on 20 of them the typed age and the age at the visit are in two age classes, and the corrected scores then differ by 4 to 33 items. The corrected score differs on 1.2% of the visits until 2012, 0.8% in 2013-15 and 0.4% or less after. The T-score differs more in 2009 and 2010: on 25 to 37 of its differences per plate the corrected score is the same, all of them in those two years and in five centres. The stored T-score is an odd number, which the table never gives, on 22 visits for the word plate, 27 for the colour plate, 23 for the colour-word plate and 26 for the interference (47 visits in all, 24 in 2009 and 23 in 2010, in centres B, E, C and I, and one in L; none after 2010). On 84 of these 98 odd values the stored T-score is the T-score of the table plus 1, and the corrected score is in the upper half of its row of the table on 59 of the 84: the early script read the T-score on a scale of one point, as it seems. The recomputed value is delivered. The stored z-score is (T - 50) / 10 of the stored T-score in all but 2 or 3 rows per plate. One visit has a T-score of 0 on the three plates; the stored values end out_of_range. Only BP has the Stroop; it has no entry in the catalogue of common instruments. Unparsed cell. The one unparsed count (uncorrected errors of the colour plate) is a number typed with a superscript. Unexplained and left as measured: a year step in 2010 (110 visits, 8 centres) on the corrected errors of the three plates, one or more on 36%, 61% and 55% of the visits against 7% to 19%, 21% to 50% and 31% to 53% in the other years, with no known cause (the uncorrected errors and every score stay in their usual range).

stroop.description: Three plates of 45 seconds each: reading colour words, naming colours, and naming the ink of colour words, then an interference score. For each plate the number of items, the score corrected for age, two counts of errors, a T-score and a z-score.
stroop.version: Stroop Colour and Word Test (Golden), three plates of 45 seconds
flags: No document says in words whether a higher T-score is a better performance: the direction of the T-scores is left out, and the z-scores are only said to rise with the T-score.
Corrected scores, T-scores and z-scores are computed again as the application computes them; the stored ones are only checks (about 1% of the visits differ).
The age correction is read with the typed age where it is within one year of the age at the visit, else with the age at the visit.
Only BP has the Stroop.
A year step in 2010 on the corrected errors of the three plates is unexplained and left as measured.

tmt.title: Trail Making Test, parts A and B

bp.notes: Times and errors, their z-scores and their percentile bands, for part A, part B and the difference B minus A. Z-scores and time bands: recomputed (decision PI-10). The EMR computes each z-score as z = (mean - raw) / SD, rounded to two decimals, with the mean and the SD of one cell of a table of its script (psy_neuropsychologie_tmt.js: three age groups by three levels of education), and reads the percentile band of a time in the same cell. The package computes the six z-scores and the three time bands again with the same tables (norms/tmt_*_z.csv and norms/tmt_*_time.csv, made from the script by norms/make_tmt_time_tables.py; the folder is not in the repository) and delivers them. A higher z-score is a better performance, in every cohort. The stored z-scores and bands are kept as checks (tmt_*_z_stored, tmt_*_time_band_stored, not delivered). The tables are read with the age typed in the form (cclin01_, tmt_age) where it is within one year of the age at the visit, and with the age at the visit elsewhere, which is the reconciled age, and with the years of education typed in the form (cclin08_). A visit without years of education has no z-score and no band (8 visits; the bands get norm_missing): the script then falls on its lowest class, and the package does not. Of these 8 visits, 2 have an empty field, 5 have text in it and 1 has a number above 30; none is repaired. The typed age has 9 cells of text (a number followed by a word): they stay unparsed and the age at the visit is used. The z-scores and bands of B minus A are read from part B minus part A as recomputed (the two check scores below), not from the stored difference; the agreement with the stored z-score is the same either way, to 0.1 point. The band of the B minus A errors reads the checked difference too: the stored difference exists from 2016 on only, so 800 more visits have that band (796 of them until 2015), and no other band changes, the stored and the checked differences being equal on every visit where both exist. Each delivered score is compared with the stored one. A stored z-score that is the delivered one with the opposite sign gets sign_flipped, any other difference above 0.011 (two decimals) gets score_mismatch, a stored value with no delivered one gets score_not_recomputed. The EMR wrote the five z-scores of times and of errors of parts A, B and B minus A (time) with the opposite sign in the early years: a slow time gave a positive z-score. Of the 5,772 to 5,877 visits where a stored z-score and the recomputed one both exist, the stored one equals the recomputed one on 86%, has the opposite sign on 12.6 to 13.0% (739 to 756 visits) and differs otherwise on 1.0 to 1.2% (56 to 68 visits). All the opposite signs but one are in the visits of 2015 or before, in many centres: from 2016 the two agree on 99.0 to 99.3% of the visits. The z-score of the B-A errors never had the opposite sign (99.0% the same). Of the visits that differ otherwise, about half have a typed age more than one year from the age at the visit (the EMR used the typed age, the package falls back on the age at the visit), and on nine in ten the stored value is that of another cell of the table (another age group or level of education: the form was changed after the score was computed). The EMR stored the z-score of the B-A errors from 2016 on only (the form had no such field before): it is now delivered on 808 more visits, 804 of them until 2015. The six z-scores are not winsorised: a winsorised tail depends on the cohort (the lowest part A time z-score was -3.00 in BP, -5.36 in SZ and -5.00 in DR, and is -10.3, -18.4 and -13.5 with the raw tails), and their range already bounds them. The range of the z-scores of errors is wide enough for the high counts of errors of the DR cohort. Percentile bands of the times (decision D38 in PROGRESS.md). The three time percentile columns mix plain numbers (50), bands ("25 - 50", also written "50 - 25" or "[25-50]") and a few one-sided classes (">95", "<5"). They are read as bands (the stored columns): the value is the lower limit of the band, 0 (under the 5th percentile), 5, 10, 25, 50, 75, 90 or 95. A higher band is a better performance. The recomputed band equals the stored one on 99.0% of the visits for A and for B (99.3% from 2016) and on 95.1% for B minus A (99.4% from 2016). Until 2015 the B-A band was written with another rule at its two ends: "10 - 5" for a time worse than the 5th percentile (203 visits, read as 5, recomputed as 0) and "<95" for a time better than the 95th (49 visits, read as 90, recomputed as 95); these are score_mismatch. The script of the application writes ">95" as the band of an empty time, "NaN" as the stored z-score of an empty count and scores an empty count as 0: this is most of the score_not_recomputed flags of the bands. On part B, 59 of the 69 flagged bands are a stored ">95" on an empty time; on B minus A, 39 of the 72 are ">95" and 21 are "<95" on an empty difference. Percentile bands of the errors: recomputed (decisions D42 and D43). The four error percentile columns of the extraction are not read (ignored.yaml): the EMR wrote them with three different rules over the years. A patient with no error in part A has ">95" until 2015 (1,662 of the 1,966 visits with no error), ">5", ">10" or ">25" from 2016 to 2021, and "<5" (435 of the 776 such visits) or another ">" class from 2022. These cells are free text of three eras, and the DR script writes "95" for no error: they are not read, the bands are computed again in the tables. The "<5" is a defect of the script of the application as it is today (read in November 2026; decision D98 in PROGRESS.md): where every limit of the norm is the number of errors of the patient, which is the case of a test with no error, the script falls in the branch that writes "below the lowest percentile". The four bands are read again in the norm tables of the EMR, from the number of errors (corrected plus uncorrected), the reconciled age and the years of education (cclin08_, read here a second time and not delivered). The tables are files of the norms folder (norms/tmt_*.csv); without them the four bands are missing with norm_missing. Most people make no error, so several limits of the norms fall on the same number of errors. The band of such a number is the lowest one it can be, with <variable>_cens = +1: this band or a higher one. With no error a patient gets a low band with that mark, as in the cells the EMR wrote from 2016 on (">5", ">10", ">25"). The lowest band, a number of errors above every limit, is exact and never marked open: "or a higher one" would say nothing there. The tables are made from the scripts of the application by norms/make_tmt_error_tables.py, as the time tables are. The bands say little, but they say the same thing in every year: between the six periods (to 2012, 2013-15, 2016-18, 2019-21, 2022-23, 2024 on) the share of a band differs by 7.4 points at most for part A, 7.9 for part B, 8.9 for B minus A (whose band now exists before 2016) and 5.0 for the perseverative errors (highest minus lowest share of a band). Check against the cells the EMR wrote from 2016 to 2021, the period whose rule is the one of the tables: the same band on 93% of the visits for the errors of part B, 98% for the perseverative errors, 95% for B minus A and 87% for part A. Reading the tables with the reconciled age instead of the age at the visit changes the band of 2 to 5 of the 2,490 to 2,644 visits compared (visits of 2016 to 2021 with a stored cell and a band under either age). Errors. The error z-scores and the stored B-A error difference were computed from corrected plus uncorrected errors, so the two are added up in tmt_a_errors and tmt_b_errors. Most patients make no error. The norms then have a very small standard deviation and a single error gives a z-score of -2 to -8: the error z-scores are extreme by construction. Perseverative errors are part of the errors of part B, so a check score (the errors of part B minus the perseverative errors, in 0 to 50) gets out_of_range where it is negative: 41 of the 4,625 visits that have both. It changes no value. Times are in seconds. In part B, "impossible" and "arrêt" (12 visits) mean that the patient could not finish; they are treated as missing codes. A few cells hold text such as "26s" and stay unparsed. The stored B-A time and B-A error difference are delivered as stored. Two check scores recompute them as part B minus part A: the time differs on 6 visits (score_mismatch), the error difference on none (SZ: 8 and 5, DR: none and 22). The TMT stacks across BP, SZ and DR for the times, the z-scores and the time bands: the names, the unit (seconds) and the direction (a higher z-score is a better performance) are the same. Unparsed cells. The 17 cells that stay unparsed are typed text: 5 times with a unit or in minutes and seconds (4 in part A, 1 in part B), and 12 cells of part B (3 times and 9 error counts) that hold a slash or a word. Unexplained and left as measured (use a centre term in a pooled analysis): a centre step on the perseverative errors of part B (tmt_b_errors_perseverative and its band): centre K (186 visits) has one or more on 27% of its visits against 2% to 12% in each of the other centres, with no known cause.

sz.notes: Times and errors, their z-scores and their percentile bands, for part A, part B and the difference B minus A. The BP schema, where the notes give the rules and their evidence (decisions D13, D38, D42 and D43 of the BP file, and PI-10); what follows is what the SZ data show. Columns. The two times are in tmt0101_ and tmt0102_ (tmta01_ and tmtb01_ in BP); the other columns have the BP names. Z-scores and time bands: recomputed as in BP (decision PI-10), with the tables of the script of the application, the reconciled age (the age typed in cclin01_ where it is within one year of the age at the visit) and the years of education (cclin08_). The stored z-scores and bands are kept as checks and compared; sign_flipped marks a stored z-score that is the recomputed one with the opposite sign. Of the 2,996 to 3,210 visits where a stored z-score and the recomputed one both exist, the stored one is the recomputed one on 97.3 to 98.8%, has the opposite sign on 0.9 to 1.0% of the visits of the three z-scores that rest on part B (29 to 31 visits) and never for the others, and differs otherwise on 1.2 to 1.7% (35 to 52 visits); from 2016 the two agree on 98.3 to 98.7%. Of the opposite signs, 27 or 28 per score are in 2012 or before, and 26 or 27 are in one centre. Every visit has its years of education since the extraction of 17 November 2026, so no z-score or band is missing for want of them. The z-scores of B minus A are read from part B minus part A as recomputed, and so is the band of the B minus A errors: 43 more visits have it and 5 change, the stored difference differing from the checked one on 5 visits. The z-scores are not winsorised (see BP). Percentile bands of the times. As in BP the three columns mix plain numbers, bands and one-sided classes; they are read as bands (the stored columns). The recomputed band equals the stored one on 99.4% (A), 98.9% (B) and 97.8% (B minus A) of the visits, and on 98.8 to 99.4% from 2016. Of the 68 B-A bands that differ, 46 are a stored ">95" on a time that is not above the 95th percentile, 44 of them in 2010 to 2013 and 38 in one centre. Percentile bands of the errors. The four error percentile columns are not read (ignored.yaml): they were written with other rules over the years than in BP: none of the 751 part A visits with no error until 2015 has ">95" (they have ">5", ">10" or ">25"), and from 2022 "<5" is on 332 of the 577 such visits, the defect of the script as in BP. The bands are read again in the norm tables, from the number of errors, the reconciled age and the years of education. Until the extraction of 17 November 2026 the export read the years of education in the older form only, so the bands stopped in 2016; they now exist on about 3,100 visits and none is missing for want of the education (decision D35 in PROGRESS.md). The tables are files of the norms folder, which is not in the repository. Missing codes. "DCM" is written in 25 cells of part B (on 8 visits; a missing-data code of this cohort), and "NaN" in 3, 100, 93, 176, 95 and 167 cells of the stored z-scores of the part A time, the part A errors, the part B time, the part B errors, the B minus A time and the B minus A errors: missing codes. A few cells hold text ("5'30", "x") and stay unparsed. The script of the application writes ">95" as the band of an empty time and scores an empty count as 0, as in BP: 110 of the 115 flagged part B bands and 111 of the 117 flagged B minus A bands are a stored ">95" on an empty time or difference, and the stored z-score of an empty count of errors gives 27 score_not_recomputed flags on part A and 50 on B minus A. Perseverative errors are part of the errors of part B: the check score of the errors that are not perseverative gets out_of_range where it is negative, on 9 of the 2,865 visits that have both. The stored B-A time and B-A error difference are delivered as stored. The two check scores differ on 8 and 5 visits (score_mismatch). 2 typed ages written 'NN ans' and 2 education cells that hold a word stay unparsed (the age at the visit is used; the education visits hold no test value). The 59 visits where at least one of the six z-scores differs from the stored one are spread over 17 years and 11 centres, 29 of them differ on all six, and the typed age explains little (it is more than 1 year from the age at the visit on 2 to 4 of the 35 to 52 visits of each score, against 3.7% of all visits). The stored z-scores differ from the recomputed ones on 35 to 52 visits per score (1.2% to 1.7%): most follow another typed age or education class, the rest has no known cause and is left as measured.
sz.difference: the two times are in tmt0101_ and tmt0102_, and "DCM" is a missing code of part B

dr.notes: The BP scale in the columns of this extraction, which keeps the kinds of errors apart. Times and errors, their z-scores and their percentile bands, for part A, part B and the difference B minus A. 718 visits. Errors. The form counts, for part A, errors of inattention and of impulsivity, and for part B, errors of inattention and perseverative errors, each corrected or not: eight columns, delivered under their own names. The BP columns are their sums (corrected, uncorrected, perseverative). The total of each part (tmta02, tmtb02) is delivered as stored, as tmt_a_errors and tmt_b_errors: it is the sum of the four kinds on all but 9 visits for part A and 31 for part B (score_mismatch on the check scores). The stored B minus A difference of errors is not part B minus part A on 22 visits, the stored time difference on none; both are delivered as stored. Z-scores and time bands: recomputed as in BP (decision PI-10), with the BP and SZ tables, the reconciled age (the age typed in cclin01 where it is within one year of the age at the visit) and the years of education (cclin08): one rule for every cohort. The stored z-scores and bands are kept as checks and compared (tolerance 0.011); sign_flipped marks a stored z-score that is the recomputed one with the opposite sign. The z-scores of the errors are computed from the stored totals (tmt_a_errors, tmt_b_errors), which the application used: they agree with the stored z-score on 1 to 4 points more visits than the sum of the four kinds. The z-score and the band of the B minus A time, and the band of the B minus A errors, are read from part B minus part A as recomputed. Three z-scores are stored with the other sign. In BP a higher z-score is a better performance. In DR that holds for the times of parts A and B. The z-scores of the errors of part A, of the errors of part B and of the B minus A time are stored as (raw - mean) / SD, as the script of the DR application writes them, where the times of A and B are (mean - raw) / SD: the stored value is the recomputed one with the opposite sign on 95 to 97% of the visits (94.8 to 97.0%, 662 to 668 visits), in every period and centre but for a few visits of 2014 and 2015. The package does not turn the stored z-score: the delivered z-score is the recomputed one, in the direction of the project (higher is better), and sign_flipped records every stored one that has the opposite sign. The medians of the delivered z-scores are those of BP (0.14 and 0.30 for the errors in both cohorts). The z-scores of the times of A and of B also have the opposite sign on 12 and 14 visits of 2013 to 2015, in two or three centres. The script of the application scores an empty count of errors as 0, so the stored z-score of an empty count is a number (BP and SZ write "NaN"): 22 stored z-scores of the part A errors and 15 of the part B errors have no recomputed one (score_not_recomputed). Otherwise the stored z-score is the recomputed one on 95% of the visits for the times of A and B, and differs otherwise on 2.2 to 3.2% (15 to 23 visits) of each z-score; from 2016 on 1.6 to 2.1%. The classes of education of the DR script are 0, 2 to 11 and 12 and over (one year gives no score), where the ones of BP and SZ are under 6, 6 to 11 and 12 and over. The recomputation uses the BP edges (one rule for the cohorts): 16 visits (education 2 to 5; 14 of them have a TMT) fall in another class than the DR script puts them in, and 10 to 14 of the visits that differ, for each z-score, are among them. The ten tables norms/tmt_*_dr.csv, made from the DR script, equal the BP tables in every cell of the same class and no schema reads them. The z-score of the B minus A errors, which DR never stored, is delivered on 684 visits that have both totals, with the BP and SZ table, and has no check. The z-scores are not winsorised, as in BP; the range of the z-scores of errors is wide enough for the high counts of errors of DR. Percentile bands of the times: labels cut by the export. The export loses the last character of the label of the B minus A time band, in 13 centres of 14 and mostly until 2021: "25-5" for "25-50", "10-2", "50-7", "75-9" and "90-9" (394 cells, 370 of them until 2021), "5-1" for "5-10" (5 cells), "<" for "<5" (12) and ">9" for ">95" (2). One "10-25" lost its dash ("1025") and one "25-" stays unparsed. The error percentile of part B (tmtb02a, not read) is cut the same way. Read as they stand, "25-5" would be another band. The z-score of the same measure has the same level under a cut label and under its full label (median 0.05 under "25-5" and 0.03 under "25-50"; 0.81 and 0.71 for "10-2" and "10-25"; these are in the sign of the stored z-score, the delivered ones are -0.05, -0.03, -0.81 and -0.71), so each cut label is read as its band (codes). The stored bands are the checks: the recomputed band equals the stored one on 97.3 to 97.9% of the visits (98.6 to 99.0% from 2016). Percentile bands of the errors: read again in the norm tables, as in BP. The two error percentile columns of the extraction (tmta02a, tmtb02a) are not read (ignored.yaml). The four bands come from the number of errors, the reconciled age and the years of education (cclin08, read here a second time and not delivered), in the tables of the norms folder; without them the bands are missing with norm_missing. Most people make no error, so most bands carry <variable>_cens = +1: this band or a higher one; the lowest band is never marked open. The DR script writes "95" as the stored percentile of no error (591 of the 594 visits with no error and a stored cell in part A), which is not the cell of BP. The band of the B minus A errors reads the checked difference, which differs from the stored one on 22 visits: 68 visits gain a band, 8 lose it (a stored difference with one total missing) and 20 change, and 684 visits have it. Times are in seconds; 2 times of part A and 3 of part B are out of range. The neuropsychological assessment is given at inclusion and at the visits of 1, 2 and 4 years: 741 visits of 433 patients have a typed age and 718 visits of 423 patients have a TMT. About three inclusions in four hold it until 2020 and about one in two since 2021 (open question O22). A lone dash is typed in the stored B minus A time of 2 visits and in the stored B minus A errors of 3 (unparsed, missing; the two parts are present on 4 of these 5 visits, and the delivered B minus A z-scores and bands are read from the parts). Left as measured: the stored part B total of errors differs from the sum of its four kinds on 31 visits with no known cause (25 above the sum; 11 at centre L in 2024-2025, which is 11 of its 28 visits of those years, and 7 at centre D), and the 2025 median of the delivered part B errors and of their z-score steps with them.
dr.difference: the kinds of errors are in eight columns and the totals are stored (the error z-scores are computed from them); three stored z-scores have the other sign and are only flagged sign_flipped; band labels cut by the export are written out; the B minus A z-score of the errors is computed (nothing is stored)

tmt.description: Trail Making Test: the time and the errors of part A and of part B, and the difference B minus A, each with a z-score and a percentile band.
sources: schema notes (bp tmt, sz tmt, dr tmt)
docs/bp/PROGRESS.md D13, D23, D42, D43, D135
flags: The delivered z-scores are computed again from the raw scores and have one sign in BP, SZ and DR: higher is better. The z-scores that the application stored had the opposite sign on about 13% of the BP visits (nearly all in 2015 or before), in one SZ centre in 2011-2012 and, in DR, for the errors of parts A and B and the B minus A time on 95% to 97% of the visits. The stored values are not delivered; the flag sign_flipped marks them.
The error z-scores are extreme by construction: most patients make no error, the SD of the norms is very small and a single error gives a z-score of -2 to -8. They are not winsorised.
Most error bands carry <variable>_cens = +1 (this band or a higher one): a patient with no error gets a low band with that mark. The bands say little.
A visit without years of education has no z-score and no band (norm_missing).
The tables are read with the typed age where it is within one year of the age at the visit, else with the age at the visit.

DR keeps the kinds of errors apart (inattention, impulsivity, perseverative; corrected or not) and its totals of errors are delivered as stored. One rule of education classes is used for the three cohorts (the BP and SZ one).
In part B, 'impossible' and 'arrêt' mean that the patient could not finish: they are missing codes.
Unexplained centre steps on the perseverative errors of part B are left as measured: use a centre term in a pooled analysis.

common.note: The times stack as they are. The z-scores and the time bands are computed again from the raw scores in the three cohorts with the table of the application's script (BP D135): z = (mean - raw) / SD for the age and the years of education, so a higher z is a better performance and the sign is the same everywhere; the age is the one typed in the form where it is within a year of the age at the visit. The stored z-scores are checks: where a centre wrote the opposite sign (13% of the BP visits, mostly before 2013, one SZ centre in 2011-2012, three z-scores of DR in every year) the cell gets sign_flipped, elsewhere a difference is a score_mismatch. A visit with no education has no z-score. The z-scores are not clipped (no winsorising). The error bands read the checked difference of B and A; the lowest band is never open (BP D138-D143). The raw error counts differ: BP and SZ store the corrected and the uncorrected, DR a typed total and four kinds.

verbal_fluency.title: Verbal fluency, letter P and animals

bp.notes: Two tasks of two minutes: words that begin with P, and names of animals. 5,865 visits. For each task: the number of correct words, its z-score and percentile band, the errors, and the clusters and switches (4,166 visits, from 2009: 46 visits in 2009-10, then 198 in 2011). Percentile bands. The column holds plain numbers, bands ("25 - 50") and the two end classes (">95", "<5"); every cell is one full band. The value is the lower limit of the band: 0, 5, 10, 25, 50, 75, 90 or 95. Rule breaks. The stored number is the sum of the derived words, the intrusions and the proper names in all but 0.5% of the rows (24 of 5,689 for the letter P, 25 of 5,586 for the animals); it is recomputed and compared. Counts of the rater. The perseverations, the intrusions, the derived words, the proper names, the clusters, the mean size of a cluster and the switches are counts that the rater makes on the transcript of the words: they cannot be recomputed (no word sequence is stored) and are delivered as stored. No identity holds among them: the switches equal the clusters minus one on 196 of 3,906 visits with clusters for the letter P and 149 of 3,981 for the animals, and the mean size times the number of clusters exceeds the number of words by more than half a word on 14 visits for the letter P and 64 for the animals. Recomputed. The z-score and the percentile band of each task are computed again as the application computes them (one script for the BP and the SZ forms), and the stored ones are kept only as checks (fluency_*_stored, not delivered). The norm has one cell for each of three age classes (under 40, 40 to 59, 60 and over) and three levels of education (under 6 years, 6 to 11, 12 and over): the z-score is (words - mean) / SD of the cell to two decimals (norms/fluency_*_z.csv), the band is the lower limit of the band the words fall in (norms/fluency_*_band.csv; 0 for "<5", then 5, 10, 25, 50, 75, 90, 95). The tables are read with the age typed in the form (cclin01_) where it is within one year of the age at the visit, and with the age at the visit elsewhere, and with the years of education typed in the form (cclin08_). The education edges are those of the BP and SZ script; the DR script has other ones (see the DR schema). Under 6 years (29 visits with a count for the letter, 27 for the animals) the script takes the lowest class, and the stored values follow it (the z-score on 25 of 29 and 25 of 27 visits, the band on all of them). Years of education. They are not empty on the 6 visits with a count where nothing is computed: 5 cells are text (a diploma written "BAC+n", years with a word) and one is out of range. They are not repaired (reading "BAC+n" as years is a guess): the band gets norm_missing and the z-score is missing there, where the script reads an empty education as the lowest class. Checks. A recomputed value that differs from the stored one is flagged score_mismatch (the z-score by more than 0.0101). Of the visits where both exist, the z-score differs on 59 of 5,856 for the letter P (1.0%) and 65 of 5,840 for the animals (1.1%), the band on 41 (0.7%) and 50 (0.9%). The share of visits that differ falls with the years, by period (to 2012, 2013-15, 2016-18, 2019-21, 2022-23, 2024 on): 1.6%, 1.3%, 1.2%, 0.9%, 0.6% and 0.4% (2 of 487 from 2024). The 124 (visit, task) pairs with a z-score that differs (65 visits; every band difference is one of them) are read in another cell of the table: 71 in another age class (59 of them with a typed age more than one year from the age at the visit), 41 in another class of education (23 at 11 or 12 years), 9 in no cell, 3 in a cell that differs both ways. The typed age is more than one year from the age at the visit on 3.5% of the visits that have one (221 of 6,302), and the script recomputes only when the words are typed, not when the age or the education is edited afterwards. One centre has 47 pairs of 2,037 (2.3%) with a difference, against 1.5% or less in each of the others. A stored band that is "<5" on an empty count of words (18 visits for the animals) is the percentile of an empty cell, which the EMR computes as if the count were 0: nothing is delivered and the row gets score_not_recomputed, as it does for the few stored z-scores and bands with no count or no education. Unparsed cells. The 27 cells that stay unparsed are counts typed with a decimal (26, a count of words cannot have one; on 4 of them the number equals the mean cluster size of the same task) and one fraction (words of the letter P). Unexplained and left as measured (use a centre term in a pooled analysis): centre steps on counts made by the rater, with no known cause: the animal clusters and their mean size in centre K (228 visits, median 2 clusters of size 1.0 against 7 and 2.1), the switches in centres C and I (median 4 and 7 for the letter P against 15 to 18 elsewhere), the clusters of the letter P in centre F (26 visits, median 10.5 against 4), and the derived words (one or more on 2% of the visits of centre K, 63% and 70% in centres I and J, 22% overall).

dr.notes: The BP scale for the visits that use form 1 (letter P and animals): the number of words, the z-score and the percentile band of each task. The 16 visits with a count and under 6 years of education (15 at 5 years, 1 at 2 years) follow the middle class in the DR application: every one of them differs and stays flagged score_mismatch (32 z-scores and 13 bands). wais3_code_symboles_ivt.title: WAIS-III coding, symbol search and processing speed index

bp.notes: WAIS-III and WAIS-IV are two instruments stored in the same columns (decision D10 in PROGRESS.md). This schema reads the WAIS-III visits (1,302 visits are labelled WAIS-III, 2009 to 2025: 1,254 have a coding score, 1,246 a symbol search score and 1,245 the index; 25 of them are dated 2016 or later and none holds a column that only the WAIS-IV has, so they stay as labelled); wais4_code_symboles_ivt.yaml reads the others. The two editions have the same subtests and the same columns, but different sheets and norms: the coding sheet has 133 boxes in WAIS-III and 135 in WAIS-IV. The confidence interval of the index (ivt03_w) is text such as "90-105" and is delivered as stored text. It comes with the stored sum and cannot be recomputed as text here: the tables norms/wais4_ivt_low.csv and wais4_ivt_high.csv reproduce the WAIS-IV one on 4,662 of 4,666 visits, but there is no such table for the WAIS-III, and delivering the interval as two numbers is left for later. Where the stored index differs from the recomputed one (30 visits) it gets derived_doubt. Raw scores. The stored raw score is delivered as it is, and checked: it is the boxes filled minus the boxes filled incorrectly (coding) or the correct answers minus the incorrect ones (symbol search) on 1,251 of the 1,252 coding visits that have the three values and on 1,245 of 1,245 symbol search visits; two coding visits and one symbol search visit have a raw score typed without one of the two values. Scaled scores, z-scores and index (decision of 18 November 2026). They are recomputed from the raw scores in the application's own norm tables (norms/wais3_code.csv, wais3_symbol.csv, wais3_ivt_index.csv, read from the scripts of the EMR; not part of the repository) and delivered; the stored ones are read as checks (keep: false) and a difference is score_mismatch on the delivered score. The EMR read the age tables with the age typed in the form (cclin01_); the package uses that age where it is within one year of the age at the visit, else the age at the visit (age: wais3_code_age). The z-score is (scaled score - 10) / 3 (tolerance 0.006). The processing speed index is read in an age-free table from the sum of the two recomputed scaled scores, which is delivered too. The percentile rank of the index is read in the application's table (norms/wais3_ivt_percentile.csv) from the same sum and delivered (wais3_ivt_percentile, 1,245 visits; a percentile of 0.1 is a censored value, wais3_ivt_percentile_cens, 1 visit). The stored percentile is a check (wais3_ivt_percentile_stored, tolerance 0.051 because it has one decimal): the table, read from the stored sum, gives it on 1,244 of 1,244 visits that have both. On 1,254 coding visits the scaled score differs from the stored one on 26 (16 to 2012, 10 in 2013-2015), on 1,246 symbol search visits on 25 (15, 9 and 1 in 2016-2018), and the sum of the two and the index on 30 of 1,245; on 23 of these 30 the typed age is more than a year from the age at the visit and on 1 there is none, and read with the typed age as it stands (the age at the visit where none was typed) the index differs on 9 visits. The z-scores differ on 38 (coding) and 43 (symbol search) visits: the stored z-score is not (stored scaled score - 10) / 3 on 14 coding and 19 symbol search visits (by 0.33 or more), in addition to the scaled scores that differ. The percentile rank differs from the stored one on the same 30 visits (score_mismatch on the delivered percentile); the interval, delivered as stored, keeps its derived_doubt on these 30 visits. The delivered scaled scores equal the stored ones on 97.9% of the coding visits and 98.0% of the symbol search visits, and the sum and the index on 97.6%; once the visits whose typed age is missing or more than 1 year from the age at the visit are set aside (73 coding, 72 symbol search and 72 sum visits), on 99.5%, 99.7% and 99.5% (the set-aside visits hold 20 of the 26 coding mismatches, 21 of the 25 symbol search ones and 24 of the 30 of the sum). 18 of the 25 visits labelled WAIS-III and dated 2016 or later hold coding and 17 hold symbol search. Other indexes. The BP form has no information, arithmetic, picture completion, block design or letter-number sequencing subtest (the extraction has no column for them), so no verbal comprehension, perceptual reasoning, working memory or full-scale index can be built: the processing speed index is the only index of BP. Unparsed cells. The 2 cells that stay unparsed (boxes filled of the coding, correct answers of the symbol search) are numbers typed with a superscript. Unexplained and left as measured (use a centre term in a pooled analysis): a centre step on wais3_symbol_errors: centre K (83 visits) has no error on 90% of its visits against 34% to 46% in the other centres, with no known cause (no score of the schema shows it).

wais3_memoire_chiffres.title: WAIS-III digit span

bp.notes: WAIS-III and WAIS-IV are two instruments stored in the same columns (decision D10 in PROGRESS.md). Each has its own schema and reads only its own visits, recognised by wais_version: 1,302 WAIS-III visits, mostly 2009 to 2015, and 5,011 WAIS-IV visits from 2011 on (4,695 with a digit span value). Every visit with WAIS data has a version. On WAIS-III visits the columns hold what the dictionary says, and the raw total equals forward + backward on all 1,249 rows where both exist. Trials. Each item has two trials (1 = correct) and an item score, the number of trials passed (0 to 2): this holds in all but one or two rows. The test stops after two failures on an item, so the last items are often empty; "Na" in an item score is a missing code. The stored raw score of each order is compared with the sum of its item scores, the items after the first one scored 0 not counted (stop_at_zero: the test stops there): they agree on 1,249 of 1,249 forward and 1,250 of 1,250 backward visits (without the stop rule 3 visits of each order differ). Scaled score, z-scores and spans (decision of 18 November 2026). The scaled score is recomputed from the stored raw total in the application's own norm table (norms/wais3_digit_span.csv, 12 age groups read from the scripts of the EMR; not part of the repository) and delivered; the stored scaled score and z-score are checks (keep: false) and a difference is score_mismatch on the delivered score. The EMR read its tables with the age typed in the form (cclin01_); the package uses that age where it is within one year of the age at the visit, else the age at the visit (age: wais3_ds_age). The z-score is (scaled score - 10) / 3 (tolerance 0.006). The z-scores of the longest spans are computed with a mean and a standard deviation per age group and per class of years of education typed in the form (norms/wais3_span_forward_z.csv and wais3_span_backward_z.csv, by: wais3_ds_education), as the scripts of the EMR do; where the years of education are missing there is no z-score (4 visits, norm_missing, and score_not_recomputed on the 2 of them that have a stored z-score) and where the norm has no cell the EMR wrote "Infinity" (1 visit), a missing code of the stored value. On the 1,249 visits with a stored and a recomputed scaled score, 13 differ (9 to 2012, 4 in 2013-2015); on 11 the typed age is more than a year from the age at the visit, and read with the typed age as it stands the table gives the stored score on all but 3 visits. The z-score differs on 24 of 1,248 visits: the stored z-score is not (stored scaled score - 10) / 3 on 13 of them. The z-score of the forward span differs from the stored one on 32 of 1,228 visits (20 to 2012, 11 in 2013-2015, 1 in 2016-2018) and that of the backward span on 32 of 1,228; the typed age is more than a year from the age at the visit on 25 of each, and read with the typed age as it stands the differences are 10 and 10. The EMR computes these z-scores when the button is clicked and does not recompute them after an edit. Of the 32 forward differences, 23 used the typed age, 3 the lowest education class (education empty at the click), 3 a neighbouring education class or the bound read lower, and 3 are not explained (2010 and 2011). Backward: 23, 3, 4 and 2. 17 visits have a recomputed span z-score and no stored one. The delivered scaled score equals the stored one on 1,236 of 1,249 visits (99.0%), and on 1,172 of 1,174 (99.8%) once the 75 visits whose typed age is missing or more than 1 year from the age at the visit are set aside; those visits hold 11 of the 13 mismatches (85%). 17 of the 25 visits labelled WAIS-III and dated 2016 or later hold a digit span; none holds a column that only the WAIS-IV has, so they stay as labelled.

The SZ extraction holds the summary scores only: the items of the two tasks, which BP has, are not extracted. So the two raw scores cannot be recomputed; the raw total is checked against their sum. The z-score is (scaled score - 10) / 3 (tolerance 0.006). The z-scores of the longest spans are computed with a mean and a standard deviation per age group and per class of years of education typed in the form (norms/wais3_span_forward_z.csv and wais3_span_backward_z.csv, by: wais3_ds_education), as the scripts of the EMR do. On the 706 visits with a stored and a recomputed scaled score, 7 differ (6 before 2013, 1 in 2013 to 2015), 4 of them with a typed age more than a year from the age at the visit (read with the typed age as it stands the table gives the stored score on all but 3 of the 704 visits that have a typed age). The tables and the bounds of the classes are those of the script (psy_neuropsychologie_memchiffre_sz.js: 43 of 43 cells for each span). 1 visit (2013, centre D) is not explained. The export gives one age and one number of years of education for the three neuropsychology forms (face_sz_4_neuropsychologie.sql, lines 15 and 17; request R168). Same instrument as in FACE BP, reduced to the summary scores; the z-scores of the spans are in the columns mcodempz_w and mcoiempz_w here. Two typed ages written 'NN ans' are unparsed; the age at the visit is used where the typed one is not read (both visits have this subtest), and 2 education cells hold a word and stay unparsed (visits with no test value). wais3_vocabulaire.title: WAIS-III vocabulary (33 items)

bp.notes: WAIS-III and WAIS-IV are two instruments stored in the same columns (decision D10 in PROGRESS.md). The columns vocab01_wais3 to vocab33_wais3 hold the 33-item WAIS-III vocabulary test on WAIS-III visits (1,219 visits, 2009 to 2016) and the 30-item WAIS-IV vocabulary test on WAIS-IV visits (2,109 visits, 2011 to 2021), in spite of their name. This schema reads the WAIS-III visits; wais4_vocabulaire.yaml reads the others. Every WAIS-III item is scored 0 to 2, so the raw total goes up to 66. The stored raw total is wrong on WAIS-III visits. It is the sum of the 33 items minus 3 on 1,207 of the 1,210 rows that have one, and it is never the sum itself. The total is therefore recomputed here from the items. The stored one is still compared with it, with that offset of -3, so that only the 3 rows that differ for another reason get score_mismatch. The scaled score is read in the application's own norm table (decision D19 in PROGRESS.md, which replaces D11). In the EMR the psychologist enters the items, and the application reads the scaled score in the table from the raw total and the age typed in the form (cclin01_); the field cannot be typed in. The table (norms/wais3_vocabulary.csv, not part of the repository) applied to the sum of the 33 items gives the stored scaled score, so the EMR used the true total and only the total column of the extraction is 3 points too low. Since the decision of 18 November 2026 the scaled score is recomputed from the sum of the 33 items and delivered; the stored scaled score and z-score are read as checks (keep: false), and a difference is score_mismatch on the delivered score. The table is read with the typed age where it is within one year of the age at the visit, else with the age at the visit (age: wais3_vocab_age). The z-score is (scaled score - 10) / 3, the stored one is rounded to two decimals (tolerance 0.006). The earlier design delivered the stored scores, checked them with the table read with the age at the visit, and gave derived_doubt to both on the 20 rows where the check differed; derived_from is gone. On the 1,210 visits that have a stored and a recomputed scaled score, 11 differ (8 to 2012, 3 in 2013-2015); on 8 of them the typed age is more than a year from the age at the visit, and read with the typed age as it stands the table gives the stored score on all but 4 visits. The z-score differs on 11 visits. The delivered scaled score equals the stored one on 1,199 of 1,210 visits (99.1%), and on 1,139 of 1,142 (99.7%) once the 68 visits whose typed age is missing or more than 1 year from the age at the visit are set aside; those visits hold 8 of the 11 mismatches (73%). 4 of the 25 visits labelled WAIS-III and dated 2016 or later hold a vocabulary; none holds a column that only the WAIS-IV has, so they stay as labelled. The table is the one cited as "Wechsler, 1997"; the spreadsheet of that name has the same cells as the scripts of the EMR.

wais4_code_symboles_ivt.title: WAIS-IV coding, symbol search and processing speed index

bp.notes: WAIS-III and WAIS-IV are two instruments stored in the same columns (decision D10 in PROGRESS.md). This schema reads the WAIS-IV visits (5,011 visits are labelled WAIS-IV; 4,685 of them hold a value of this tab: 4,670 coding scores, 4,670 symbol search scores and 4,658 indices); wais3_code_symboles_ivt.yaml reads the others. The two editions have the same subtests and the same columns, but different sheets and norms: the coding sheet has 135 boxes in WAIS-IV and 133 in WAIS-III. Symbol search has 60 items. 6 visits hold impossible values (a negative raw score, or more than 60 correct answers); they are flagged out_of_range (5 raw scores and 5 counts of correct answers). The confidence interval of the index (ivt03_w) is text such as "90-105" and is delivered as text. Scaled scores, z-scores and index. They are recomputed and delivered (decision of the project lead for the standard scores of the neuropsychological tests). The raw scores stay as delivered, except the coding raw score (below). The scaled scores are read in the WAIS-IV tables of the application (norms/wais4_code.csv and wais4_symbol.csv) from the raw scores, and the z-scores are (scaled score - 10) / 3. The table is read with the age typed in the form (cclin01_, delivered as neuropsy_age by neuropsy_conditions) where it is within 1 year of the age at the visit, and with the age at the visit elsewhere. The sum of the two recomputed scaled scores is delivered as wais4_ivt_sum_scaled, and the index and its percentile rank are read from it in the index tables (norms/wais4_ivt.csv and wais4_ivt_percentile.csv, the same in the four applications). A percentile of 0.1 or 99.9 is a censored value (wais4_ivt_percentile_cens). The stored values are wais4_*_stored, not delivered. The confidence interval is delivered as stored: it comes with the stored index and cannot be recomputed here (it is a text). The tables norms/wais4_ivt_low.csv and wais4_ivt_high.csv reproduce it from the stored sum on 4,662 of 4,666 visits; delivering it as two numbers is left for later, and the 124 visits where the stored sum is not the recomputed one carry the interval of the stored sum (no derived_doubt here, unlike the WAIS-III schema). Verified on the visits that have both. Coding scaled score: 119 of 4,669 differ (2.5%; 42 of 4,674 before the coding raw score was computed again), and its z-score too. Symbol search scaled score: 33 of 4,670, and 7 more are not recomputed (5 because the raw score is out of range, 2 because none is typed: score_not_recomputed). Sum of scaled scores: 124 of 4,657 differ and 9 are not recomputed; the index differs on the same 124, the percentile rank on 120 (of 4,653). The mismatches are spread over 2013 to 2026 (44 of the 124 sums to 2021, 80 from 2022) and over 12 centres (13 for the coding); on 80 of the 124 the coding raw score differs from the stored one (the errors were not taken off); no raw score gives norm_missing. Other indexes. The BP form has no information, arithmetic, picture completion, block design or letter-number sequencing subtest (the extraction has no column for them), so no verbal comprehension, perceptual reasoning, working memory or full-scale index can be built: the processing speed index is the only index of BP. A two-subtest IQ from similarities and matrices would be possible on 791 visits, but no formula is known here and none is invented. Coding raw score. It is computed: the boxes filled minus the boxes filled incorrectly, as the application did until 2021 (302 of the 481 visits with errors); since then it stores the boxes filled alone (178 visits from 2021, and 1 visit in 2015). The application stored the boxes filled alone from 2021 (its WAIS-IV form calls that field the boxes filled correctly and the raw score equal to it), but the data say that the clinicians go on typing all the boxes, errors included: at the same age and the same symbol search score, one more error goes with 0.85 fewer boxes in the typed total up to 2021, when it is all the boxes, with 0.21 fewer from 2021 (BP), against 1.85 fewer for a count of correct boxes; DR and ASP, whose forms always had the new wording, give 0.12 and 0.09 fewer. The stored raw score therefore gives credit for the errors; the stored value is wais4_code_raw_stored, not delivered (decision D136). 184 raw scores change, 85 scaled scores and z-scores, 84 sums and indices; 5 visits have a stored raw score but no usable errors or boxes (4 with no errors typed, 1 with a cell that cannot be read) and get no raw score (score_not_recomputed). The stored scaled score follows the stored raw score, so it now differs from the delivered one on the visits whose errors were not taken off. Unparsed cell. The one unparsed cell (coding errors) is a decimal typed in a count. Unexplained and left as measured (use a centre term in a pooled analysis): centre steps on the counts of errors, with no known cause: centre K has no symbol search error on 92% of its 177 visits against 34% to 59% elsewhere, and centre G has one or more coding errors on 35% of its 352 visits against 6% to 16% in the other centres but K (1%).

sz.notes: WAIS-III and WAIS-IV are two instruments stored in the same columns (decision D10 of the BP file). This schema reads the coding columns on the WAIS-IV visits (531 visits, from 2013 to 2025, 529 of them with a raw score); wais3_code_symboles_ivt.yaml reads the WAIS-III visits. The dictionary files the coding columns under the WAIS-III; the section of this schema repeats that label, '(WAIS-3) ancienne version', and the WAIS-IV visits are recognised by the version rule, not by the label. Edition rule (decision D138, question O16): the 33 visits that the form labels WAIS-III and that hold the WAIS-IV digit-span sequencing task (columns mcoc_w and mcocemp_w) are read as WAIS-IV (override in the version block, flag version_overridden). 25 of them hold coding values and are read here, not in wais3_code_symboles_ivt.yaml. The raw score is the boxes filled minus the boxes filled incorrectly, and the z-score is (scaled score - 10) / 3, on every visit. The processing speed index, its percentile rank and the sum of scaled scores it comes from are in the WAIS-IV index columns (ivt04_wais4, ivt01_wais4, ivt02_wais4). "NaN" in the sum is a missing code: the index could not be computed. The index of this schema is a coding-only estimate: the sum of the scaled scores is twice the coding scaled score (the stored sum is twice the stored coding scaled score on 527 of 528 visits). It carries the name wais4_ivt_index of the processing speed index that BP and DR read from the coding and the symbol search, and the two are not the same measure. Same instrument as in FACE BP, without the symbol search, which the SZ extraction does not hold, and without the confidence interval. Scaled score, z-score and index. They are recomputed and delivered (decision of the project lead for the standard scores of the neuropsychological tests). The coding raw score is computed as the boxes filled minus the errors (decision D136, as in BP, DR and ASP); it equals the stored one on all 529 visits that have both. The scaled score is read in the WAIS-IV coding table of the application (norms/wais4_code.csv) from the raw score, and the z-score is (scaled score - 10) / 3. The table is read with the age typed in the form (cclin01_) where it is within 1 year of the age at the visit, and with the age at the visit elsewhere. This extraction has no symbol search: the sum of scaled scores of the index is twice the coding scaled score, delivered as wais4_ivt_sum_scaled, and the index and its percentile rank are read from it in the index tables (norms/wais4_ivt.csv and wais4_ivt_percentile.csv). A percentile of 0.1 or 99.9 is a censored value (wais4_ivt_percentile_cens). The stored values are wais4_*_stored, not delivered. Verified on the 529 visits that have both: the coding scaled score differs on 3 (0.6%; 1 in 2013 to 2015, 1 in 2016 to 2018 and 1 from 2024), and so does its z-score; the sum, the index and the percentile rank differ on 2. No raw score gives norm_missing. The processing-speed sum and percentile columns are filled on 2 visits labelled WAIS-III that hold no sequencing task: they are read as WAIS-III and the 4 cells are not delivered. Centre C (25 visits) counts more coding errors (mean 1.9 against 0.2; 36% of its visits have one against 11%) with little effect on the raw score (53.2 against 54.9): a small-centre habit in counting the errors.
sz.difference: coding in columns named sdmt01..., the index in ivt01_wais4...; no symbol search and no confidence interval, so wais4_ivt_index is an estimate from the coding alone (the sum is twice the coding scaled score), not the two-subtest index of BP; the version block also names the WAIS-IV sequencing columns under override (O16, D138)

dr.notes: The BP schema in the columns of this extraction: WAIS-IV Coding, Symbol Search and the processing speed index. 726 visits. One edition. No column names the edition of the WAIS in this cohort. The data show the WAIS-IV in every year. Within a band of the typed age a raw score has one stored scaled score for digit span and similarities, and for arithmetic, coding and symbol search on every cell but one (2, 3 and 4 visits). The stored score is the same before and after 2018 on every cell seen in both periods but one (symbol search). 95 digit span totals are above 30, the maximum of the WAIS-III. The processing speed index stored by DR follows the WAIS-IV table of BP (norms/wais4_ivt.csv) on each of its 35 distinct sums, all seen in BP (the WAIS-III table on 21 of 35). The version block gives wais_version = wais4 on the 731 visits that hold a subtest, so that the column exists as in BP and SZ. Coding, raw score. Where a box is filled incorrectly (76 visits), the stored raw score is the boxes filled minus the errors on 58 visits and the boxes filled alone on 17 (1 has no stored raw score): the centres do not all count the same way. Centre N counts the boxes alone: 8 of its 9 visits with errors hold the boxes filled alone, which are 8 of the 17 raw scores that lose the errors. The DR application script has set the raw score to the boxes filled alone only since 2019-08-06, but each centre runs its own copy: before that date 47 of the 50 visits with errors follow the boxes minus the errors and 2 the boxes alone, from that date 11 of the 26 follow the boxes minus the errors and 15 the boxes alone. The clinicians go on typing all the boxes, errors included: at the same age and the same symbol search raw score, one more error goes with 0.14 fewer boxes in the typed total in DR (linear regression, 692 visits). In BP, where the application stored the boxes filled alone from 2021, it goes with 0.85 fewer boxes up to 2021 and 0.21 fewer from 2021, against 1.85 fewer for a count of correct boxes; ASP, whose form always had the new wording, gives 0.09 fewer. The stored raw score therefore gives credit for the errors where it is the boxes alone; the stored value is wais4_code_raw_stored, not delivered (decision D136). The coding raw score is computed as the boxes filled minus the errors, with the two counts next to it. 40 raw scores change: 17 lose the errors, 21 have boxes typed and the errors blank, and 2 have more errors than boxes (out of range). The last 23 get no raw score (score_not_recomputed on the 21, out_of_range on the 2), so no scaled score and no z-score. The 21 visits with the errors blank (2018 to 2026, 8 of them at centre K) have a stored raw score and a stored scaled score. Open question: does a blank mean 0 errors? If it does, their stored raw score is the right one. Symbol search, raw score. The stored raw score is the correct answers minus the incorrect ones on every visit that has the three values (704 of 704). The DR script does not stop it at 0 (the ASP one does): 5 raw scores are negative and 1 is above the maximum of 60, so 6 are out of range; they get no scaled score (score_not_recomputed) and stay flagged. Scaled scores, z-scores and index. They are recomputed and delivered (decision of the project lead for the standard scores of the neuropsychological tests). The raw scores stay as delivered, except the coding raw score (above). The scaled scores are read in the WAIS-IV tables of the application (norms/wais4_code.csv and wais4_symbol.csv) from the raw scores, and the z-scores are (scaled score - 10) / 3. The plain table that the other cohorts use is used here too, not the table of the DR script (norms/wais4_code_dr.csv for coding): where the script has another value (a typo), the stored score is flagged. The DR coding script puts the ages 18 and 19 in the band of 16 and 17 (its condition is age>17 && age>=20; 102 age-by-raw cells differ from the table): 1 of the 701 visits with a coding raw score has a coding score that this changes (the stored one is the script's, 1 point above the table's). Age. The tables are read with the age typed in the form (cclin01, delivered as neuropsy_age by neuropsy_conditions) where it is within 1 year of the age at the visit, and with the age at the visit elsewhere: 672 of the 724 visits with the coding boxes use the typed age and 52 have a typed age more than 1 year away (42 typed younger); symbol search 660 of 708 and 48 (40 typed younger). The 9 coding and the 9 symbol search mismatches among them equal the table at the typed age (see wais4_memoire_chiffres.yaml for the four schemas together). The sum of the two recomputed scaled scores is delivered as wais4_ivt_sum_scaled, and the index and its percentile rank are read from it in the index tables (norms/wais4_ivt.csv and wais4_ivt_percentile.csv). A percentile of 0.1 or 99.9 is a censored value (wais4_ivt_percentile_cens). The stored values are wais4_*_stored, not delivered. The confidence interval of the index is a text ("86-104") delivered as stored. Verified on the visits that have both. Coding scaled score: 17 of 699 differ (9 typed age, 5 change of the raw score, 1 table typo, 2 unexplained) and 23 are not recomputed (score_not_recomputed, the 23 above); its z-score 17 of 696. Symbol search scaled score: 10 of 708 differ (9 typed age, 1 unexplained) and 6 more are not recomputed because the raw score is out of range; its z-score 9 of 697. Sum of scaled scores: 20 of 685 differ and 27 are not recomputed (22 without a coding score, 6 without a symbol search score, 1 without either); the index and the percentile rank differ on the same 20. The mismatches are spread over 2013 to 2026 (11 before 2019); no raw score gives norm_missing.
dr.difference: the columns are named code01 to ivt04; no column names the edition, which is read from the columns that are filled

asp.notes: Coding and symbol search: boxes filled, errors, raw score, scaled score and z-score, on about 278 inclusion visits; then the processing speed index with its sum of scaled scores and its percentile rank (267 visits), and a second set of the same three numbers whose names end in _a (276 visits); the first set is recomputed on 262 visits and the second on 271. The WAIS-IV of this cohort is recorded item by item, on about 210 to 295 inclusion visits depending on the subtest (302 visits in all, 12 of patients under 18), from 2013 to 2026. It is on 14% of the inclusion visits of 2013, 42% of 2014, 36% of 2015, 18% to 19% of 2016 and 2017, 3% to 11% of 2018 to 2023, 21% to 22% of 2024 and 2025 and 7% of 2026 so far. It is the fourth edition: the visual puzzles and the sequencing part of the digit span exist only in it. No other edition of the scale is recorded in this table. The extraction has no column for the edition: wais_version (wais4) is read from the first item of each subtest, with the same block in the eleven schemas of the WAIS-IV, and is filled on the 302 visits that hold one of them. Coding: the stored raw score is the number of boxes filled, errors not taken off, on 276 of the 277 visits that have it (the script has the subtraction of the errors commented out); it is computed again as the boxes filled minus the errors. The application stored the boxes filled alone from 2021 (its WAIS-IV form calls that field the boxes filled correctly and the raw score equal to it), but the data say that the clinicians go on typing all the boxes, errors included: at the same age and the same symbol search score, one more error goes with 0.85 fewer boxes in the typed total up to 2021, when it is all the boxes, with 0.21 fewer from 2021 (BP), against 1.85 fewer for a count of correct boxes; DR and ASP, whose forms always had the new wording, give 0.12 and 0.09 fewer. The stored raw score therefore gives credit for the errors; the stored value is wais4_code_raw_stored, not delivered (decision D136). 25 raw scores change (20 differ, 5 are missing) and 13 scaled scores (8 differ, 5 are missing); the 5 visits (2024 to 2026) have more errors than boxes (out of range, probably two swapped fields) and get no raw score. Symbol search: the raw score is the correct answers minus the errors on 273 of 274 (the check wais4_symbol_raw_check, filed under wais4_symbol_raw; the script clamps a negative raw score at 0, which explains the other visit). The z-scores are the scaled score minus 10, over 3, on every visit. The index is one function of the sum of the two scaled scores on every visit (the stored index is the table value of the stored sum on 267 of 267 visits, the second set on 276 of 276, and the percentile ranks to 0.051 on 265 and 262). The clinician copies it into the medical evaluation (wais4_ivt_index_clinician, schema wais4_indices): the delivered index of this form and the clinician's copy agree on 185 of the 206 visits that hold both (89.8%; the stored index of the form and the clinician's copy on 185 of 207). The index of this form has the name that BP, SZ and DR give it, wais4_ivt_index, and the clinician's copy the ending _clinician. The second set (_a) is the index of the abbreviated form (thesaurus): its sum of scaled scores is twice the coding scaled score, and the index is read from it in the same table. Same instrument and index names as in FACE SZ and DR, in other columns; the second set is specific to ASP. Scaled scores, z-scores and indices. They are recomputed and delivered (decision of the project lead for the standard scores of the neuropsychological tests). The raw scores stay as delivered, except the coding raw score (above). The scaled scores are read in the WAIS-IV tables of the application (norms/wais4_code.csv and wais4_symbol.csv) from the raw scores, and the z-scores are (scaled score - 10) / 3. The form has no typed age in this cohort: the tables are read with the age at the date of the assessment form (age basis, below; 15.9 to 65 years; the visit of 15.9 years gets norm_missing). bp.notes: WAIS-III and WAIS-IV are two instruments stored in the same columns (decision D10 in PROGRESS.md). The table is read with the age typed in the form (cclin01_, delivered as neuropsy_age by neuropsy_conditions) where it is within 1 year of the age at the visit, and with the age at the visit elsewhere. Of the 4,298 visits with a total, 4,175 use the typed age, 116 have a typed age more than 1 year away and 7 have none usable. The stored scores are read as wais4_mat_scaled_stored and wais4_mat_z_stored, which are not delivered, and compared: of the 4,293 visits that have both, 37 differ (score_mismatch, 0.9%, in every period from 2013 and in 10 of the 16 centres), on the scaled score and on its z-score; on 22 of the 37 the typed age is more than 1 year from the age at the visit, and read with the typed age as it stands the table gives the stored score on those 22. wais4_memoire_chiffres.title: WAIS-IV digit span

bp.notes: WAIS-III and WAIS-IV are two instruments stored in the same columns (decision D10 in PROGRESS.md). This schema reads the WAIS-IV visits, recognised by wais_version (5,011 visits are labelled WAIS-IV, 2011 on; 4,695 of them hold a digit span value). The summary scores, the trial of each item, the item scores and the z-scores of the three longest spans are all read (below). On WAIS-IV visits four summary columns are shifted by one against their dictionary labels. mcodemp_w holds the raw total (forward + backward + sequencing: it equals the sum of the three raw scores on 4,654 of the 4,667 visits that have the four values, 99.7%; the 13 others are in the 21 visits described below), mcoiemp_w the forward span, empdid_w the backward span, and nbrut_w the forward span minus the backward span (4,661 of 4,682 rows, 99.5%; the 21 others are the same 21 visits). This was checked against the span z-score columns (rank correlations of 0.955 to 0.969 with the matching span). The variables below read the columns for what they really hold. Trials. Each item has two trials (1 = correct) and an item score, the number of trials passed (0 to 2): this holds in all but 2 forward, 4 backward and 2 sequencing visits. The test stops after two failures on an item, so the last items are often empty; "Na" in an item score is a missing code. The stored raw score of each order is compared with the sum of its item scores, the items after the first one scored 0 not counted (stop_at_zero: the test stops there, as in the WAIS-III schema): they agree on 4,687 of 4,687 forward, 4,684 of 4,684 backward and 4,673 of 4,673 sequencing visits (without the stop rule 15, 18 and 13 visits differ, the 46 false score_mismatch of the earlier check). The z-scores of the three longest spans are computed with the mean and the standard deviation of the age group (norms/wais4_ds_forward_span_z.csv and the two others, a regression with the age coefficient 0), compared with the stored z-scores to 0.011 because they have two decimals. Scaled score and z-score. They are recomputed and delivered (decision of the project lead for the standard scores of the neuropsychological tests): the scaled score is read in the WAIS-IV table of the application (norms/wais4_digit_span.csv) from the raw total wais4_ds_total (the sum of the three raw scores, see below), and the z-score is (scaled score - 10) / 3. The table is read with the age typed in the form (cclin01_, delivered as neuropsy_age by neuropsy_conditions) where it is within 1 year of the age at the visit, and with the age at the visit elsewhere. Of the 4,667 visits with a total, 4,525 use the typed age, 135 have a typed age more than 1 year away and 7 have none usable (a text such as '38 ans'). The stored scores are wais4_ds_scaled_stored, wais4_ds_z_stored and the three wais4_ds_*_span_z_stored, not delivered. Verified on the visits that have both: the scaled score differs on 37 of 4,667 (0.8%), its z-score on 36, the forward span z-score on 47 of 4,675, the backward on 57 of 4,675 and the sequencing on 47 of 4,665 (score_mismatch, 2011 to 2025). The z-scores of the spans are delivered on a few more visits (4,687, 4,684 and 4,673) than the stored ones. No raw total gives norm_missing. Twenty-one visits (21 patients, 2011 to 2023, in 8 centres) hold a digit span form of both editions (M38 in docs/EXPORT_REQUESTS.md). The export takes mcodemp_w, nbrut_w, nstand_w and vstand_w from the WAIS-III form first and the other columns from the WAIS-IV form first (R59 in the same file), so on these visits those four columns hold the WAIS-III form's values. nbrut_w, the difference of the spans on every other row (4,661 of 4,661), holds a number of 12 to 24 (out_of_range on wais4_ds_span_difference, 21 flags); mcodemp_w, the raw total on every other row, holds a number of 9 or less; the stored scaled score is the value of the WAIS-III table read with nbrut_w on 21 of 21, and the value of the WAIS-IV table read with nbrut_w, with the sum of forward and backward or with the sum of the three raw scores on none. 13 of the 21 have the sequencing task, which only the WAIS-IV has: each of their three raw scores is the sum of its item scores (13 of 13) and the stored total is not their sum (13 score_mismatch). The 8 others have no sequencing score, so no WAIS-IV total exists for them. The raw total is therefore computed as the sum of the three raw scores (wais4_ds_total) and the stored mcodemp_w is a check (wais4_ds_total_stored): the two agree on 4,654 of the 4,667 visits that have the three raw scores and the stored one, the 13 others being the 13 visits above, so no other cell changes. The 13 visits get the sum, the scaled score read in the WAIS-IV table and its z-score (13 cells each; the span was read as a total before) and stay flagged score_mismatch against the stored WAIS-III scores (13 of 13 for the scaled score, 12 for the z-score); the 8 without sequencing have no total, scaled score or z-score (8 cells each, score_not_recomputed). The columns taken from the WAIS-IV form first are left as delivered. Read in the trials (the rank of the last item with a trial passed, plus one for the forward and sequencing spans), the forward span (mcoiemp_w) is right on 16 of the 21 visits (4,648 of 4,666 on the others), the backward span (empdid_w) on 15 of 21 (4,571 of 4,663) and the sequencing span on 13 of 13 (4,645 of 4,660); the z-score of the span differs from the stored one on 9 of the 21 visits for the forward span, 9 for the backward span and 1 for the sequencing span.

wais4_similitudes.title: WAIS-IV similarities (18 items)

bp.notes: Similitudes exists only in WAIS-IV, in its own columns (823 visits with a total, 2018 to 2026; 15 more visits are ticked test not done and hold no item). It replaced the vocabulary test in the WAIS-IV battery. No WAIS-III visit has any value here; the version block is kept so that this stays true: a value on a WAIS-III visit would be reported as unread. Every item is scored 0 to 2, so the raw total goes up to 36. The stored raw total equals the sum of the items on every row (822 visits have a stored total, 823 a recomputed one; the one visit without a stored total has all its items). Scaled score and z-score. They are recomputed and delivered (decision of the project lead for the standard scores of the neuropsychological tests): the scaled score is read in the WAIS-IV table of the application (norms/wais4_similarities.csv) from the raw total, and the z-score is (scaled score - 10) / 3. The table is read with the age typed in the form (cclin01_, delivered as neuropsy_age by neuropsy_conditions) where it is within 1 year of the age at the visit, and with the age at the visit elsewhere. The stored scores are wais4_simil_scaled_stored and wais4_simil_z_stored, not delivered. The stored scaled score is wrong on a good part of the visits: of the 822 visits that have both, 284 differ (34.5%, score_mismatch, on the scaled score and on its z-score): 16 in 2019 to 2021, 142 in 2022-2023 and 126 from 2024, in 14 centres. Of the 284, 226 are the value of the youngest age group of the table (16 to 19 years; the script of the application reads an empty age as 16, and the table has one row for 16 to 19 because the script's rows for 16-17 and 18-19 are equal), 2 more are explained by an age one year off, and 56 are not explained by any age (all dated 2020 to 2023, probably an older version of the script). The application was fixed on 2026-07-31 (BP): of the 32 visits dated after it, 10 still differ (centres G, H and M, all with the value of the youngest group). The recomputed score is the delivered one, the stored one is the check. The table has no row below 16 years or from 80 years: such a visit would get norm_missing. No BP visit is concerned (ages at the visit from 18 to 77.6), so there is none. The Test non fait box is delivered as not_done, the code of the errands schema (15 visits, none with an item).

sz.notes: WAIS-III and WAIS-IV are two instruments stored in the same columns (decision D10 of the BP file). This schema reads the similarities columns on the WAIS-IV visits (1,899 visits, from 2013; 1,890 have a stored total): 18 items scored 0 to 2. wais3_similitudes.yaml reads the WAIS-III visits. The dictionary files the columns under the WAIS-III, and does not list the items; the section of this schema repeats that label, '(WAIS-3) ancienne version', and the WAIS-IV visits are recognised by the version rule, not by the label. Edition rule (decision D138, question O16). The form labels 33 visits WAIS-III although they hold the WAIS-IV digit-span sequencing task (the columns mcoc_w and mcocemp_w, which only the WAIS-IV has). They are read as WAIS-IV: the version block lists the two columns under override, and the visits get the flag version_overridden. 25 of them hold similarities items and are read here (they were in wais3_similitudes.yaml before the rule); 2 of them have a stored scaled score that differs from the recomputed one. One of the 25 (2013) looks like a WAIS-III test given with the sequencing task: its items 10 and 11 differ, it holds WAIS-III-only columns (similarities item 19, the WAIS-III efficiency columns) and its digit-span total is forward + backward only; the marker reads it as WAIS-IV. One of items 10 and 11 is lost on the WAIS-IV visits. The columns simil10_w and simil11_w are the same cell on 1,894 of the 1,895 visits that have both (the exception is the visit of 2013 above), while they differ on the WAIS-III visits as two items do. The form of the application has 18 distinct items (rad_wais_simi1 to rad_wais_simi18) and its script adds the 18; the export fills one of the two columns from the field of the other, the error found for the matrices (decision D14 and open question O12 in PROGRESS.md). Which of the two is the copy cannot be told, so neither is delivered: the schema gives items 1 to 9 and 12 to 18, and the total as stored. The stored total is the sum of 18 real items, and it is the total delivered. It is not the sum of the 18 columns (the two are equal on only 1,061 of the 1,890 visits that have a total, since one real item is lost), and it exceeds the sum of the 16 distinct items plus the shared cell by 0 to 2 on 1,885 of the 1,890 visits. 9 visits have items but no stored total, and get none. The scaled score and the z-score are recomputed from the stored total and delivered; the stored ones are checks (see below). Same instrument as in FACE BP, where the items have their own columns (simil01_wais4...) and the total is recomputed from the 18 items. Scaled score and z-score. They are recomputed and delivered (decision of the project lead for the standard scores of the neuropsychological tests): the scaled score is read in the WAIS-IV table of the application (norms/wais4_similarities.csv) from the stored raw total, and the z-score is (scaled score - 10) / 3. The table is read with the age typed in the form (cclin01_, delivered as neuropsy_age by neuropsy_conditions) where it is within 1 year of the age at the visit, and with the age at the visit elsewhere (1,815 of the 1,890 visits that have a total use the typed age, 75 have a typed age more than 1 year away). The table has no row below 16 years or from 80 years (norm_missing); no SZ WAIS-IV visit is outside it. The stored scores are wais4_simil_scaled_stored and wais4_simil_z_stored, not delivered. The stored scaled score is wrong on many visits: it differs from the recomputed one on 133 of the 1,890 visits that have both (7.0%; 1 in 2013 to 2015, 2 in 2016 to 2018, 11 in 2019 to 2021, 68 in 2022-2023, 51 from 2024), and the z-score on 82 (score_mismatch). Of the 133, 83 are the value of the 16-17 year olds' table (the script reads an empty age as 16, as in BP); of the 50 others, 48 carry a stored scaled score 2 above the one implied by the stored z-score, so the stored scaled score is the wrong one (the stored z-score follows the stored scaled score on 1,837 of 1,891 visits, and is the one of the recomputed scaled score on 52 of the 54 others). The fix of the application is dated 2026-03-12; 7 of the 66 visits after it still mismatch (centres H, B and E, all with the 16-17 value; each centre runs its own copy). One stored scaled score is not recomputed (score_not_recomputed).
