wais4_vocabulaire.title: WAIS-IV vocabulary (30 items)

bp.notes: WAIS-III and WAIS-IV are two instruments stored in the same columns (decision D10 in PROGRESS.md). The columns vocab01_wais3 to vocab30_wais3 hold the 30-item WAIS-IV vocabulary test on WAIS-IV visits (2,109 visits with at least one item, 2011 to 2021), in spite of their name. This schema reads those visits; wais3_vocabulaire.yaml reads the WAIS-III visits. From 2018 on the WAIS-IV battery uses Similitudes instead (wais4_similitudes.yaml). Items 1 to 3 are picture items scored 0 or 1; items 4 to 30 are scored 0 to 2, so the raw total goes up to 57. 27 cells of items 1 to 3 hold a 2, on 9 visits. They stay out_of_range (the range of these items is not widened), so that those 9 visits have no recomputed total, scaled score or z-score (score_not_recomputed on the stored ones). No rule explains the stored total of these 9 visits: it is the sum of the items with the 2 counted as typed on 1 of them, and with the 2 counted as 1 on 3. The stored raw total equals the sum of the 30 items on 2,082 of the 2,085 visits that have both (99.9%; 3 score_mismatch). Not read. Items 31 to 33 do not exist in WAIS-IV. They are filled on 11 WAIS-IV visits; coverage() reports those cells as unread. Scaled score and z-score. They are recomputed and delivered (decision of the project lead for the standard scores of the neuropsychological tests): the scaled score is read in the WAIS-IV vocabulary table of the application (norms/wais4_vocabulary.csv, the table of the BP application with the row for 25 to 29 years of the ASP application, see below; ASP has its own table) from the raw total, and the z-score is (scaled score - 10) / 3. The table is read with the age typed in the form (cclin01_, delivered as neuropsy_age by neuropsy_conditions) where it is within 1 year of the age at the visit, and with the age at the visit elsewhere. The stored scores are wais4_vocab_scaled_stored and wais4_vocab_z_stored, not delivered. Verified on the 2,085 visits that have both a stored and a recomputed scaled score: it differs on 146 (7.0%), and the z-score on the same 146 (score_mismatch, 143 on the scaled score; the stored scaled score of 3 visits is 20, out of its range 1 to 19, so it is not compared and those 3 are flagged on the z-score only). 136 of the 146 are at 25 to 29 years (255 visits are read in that row); the 10 others are dated 2012 to 2017 (2 under 25 years, 8 from 30 years). No total gives norm_missing. Ages 25 to 29. The row of the application's own script for these ages is not monotone, and the project lead decided (19 November 2026) to read the table with the row of the ASP application instead. The stored score of the BP application follows its own row, so it differs from the delivered one on 136 of the 255 visits of that age group; it stays as the flagged check (wais4_vocab_scaled_stored). The script's row gives 20 to the highest raw scores, one more than the scale has: 3 visits have a stored scaled score of 20 (out_of_range on the stored value); their delivered scaled score is 19, and no delivered scaled score is out of range any more. Total typed alone. 6 visits (2013 to 2020, in 4 centres) have a stored total, scaled score and z-score and no item at all. The total was typed alone: it is delivered as stored (otherwise: wais4_vocab_total_stored, score_as_stored on the total) and the scaled score and the z-score are read from it; the table gives the stored scaled score on all 6. Only the total carries score_as_stored: the flag passes to a score that adds up a score delivered as stored, not to one read in a table. The 9 other visits with a stored total and no recomputed one are those with an item of 1 to 3 typed 2 (7 of them in 2013 to 2015), see above. Unexplained and left as measured (use a centre term in a pooled analysis): a centre step: centre K (81 visits, 2014 to 2018) has a median scaled score of 16 and a median total of 45 against 11 to 13 and 36 to 40 in the other centres, 3.4 scaled points above what a straight line on the years of education gives, with ten of the items 15 to 28 scored higher, and no known cause.

fin_de_suivi.title: End of follow-up

bp.notes: One value per patient. An empty reason does not mean that the patient is still followed. A reason is recorded for 848 patients; 59 of them are "Ne sais pas" (does not know), a missing code, so 789 are delivered. Of the 4,972 patients whose last visit is more than three years old, 743 (15%) have a delivered reason. Four centres hold 81% of the reasons. To know who has left the cohort, use the date of the last visit. The extraction holds two generations of the same form. The columns ending in _patient (dictionary section "patient", a section of the patient form) hold a reason for 783 patients, mostly older ones: 51 of them have their last visit from 2022 and 13 from 2024. The columns ending in _stopsuivi (section "Fin de suivi", the form of its own) are used from 2018 on. The questions and the answers are the same, so each variable reads the new column first and the old one when the new one is empty (decision D17 in PROGRESS.md). The newer form wins because the application's button "Fin de suivi" opens it and its reminder lists read only it; it also always holds the detail its reason asks for (the date of death 3 of 3, the date and the new diagnosis of a change 9 of 9, the text of another reason 39 of 39), the older one less often. Five patients have a reason in both; for two of them the two reasons differ (column_conflict, the new one is kept). No patient mixes the two sets. The EMR writes the placeholder 1000-01-01 in the two date columns when there is nothing to record: 165 patients have it as their date of death and 303 as the date of a change of diagnosis. It becomes missing (date_placeholder). 22 patients are recorded as deceased and 17 have a date of death (one of them a year only); one of these dates belongs to a patient without that reason. No visit is dated after a death. 68 patients have a change of diagnosis as their reason, 55 of them with a date; 8 have a visit more than a month after that date. The free-text columns (other reason, new centre, new diagnosis, other cause of death) are delivered as text and never appear in the report. The new diagnosis of the newer form is in the extraction under the name lost_to_follow_up_chgdiag_stopsuivi; the dictionary spells it lost_to_follow_up_chdiag_stopsuivi. nom_centre_expert, which the dictionary also lists, is not in the extraction.

sz.notes: One value per patient. The three columns are not in the dictionary, which lists three other names (lost_to_follow_up, lost_to_follow_up_dcd, lost_to_follow_up_demenage) that the extraction does not hold. Same instrument as in FACE BP, with what the SZ extraction holds of it: the reason, the new centre after a move, and the cause of death. The export leaves out the columns filled for fewer than 25 patients, and the SZ extraction has only the newer generation of columns (_stopsuivi). Reason. 581 patients are no longer followed: the patient refused (238), another reason (195), "Ne sais pas" (91, a missing code), a move (23), a change of diagnosis (19), a death (12), the doctor refused (fewer than five). Cause of death. Since SZALL_20261123 the column causedec_stopsuivi holds what its name says, the main cause of death (rad_fin_suivi_arret_decede, "Spécifier la cause principale du décès"), with the three answers of BP: filled for the 12 patients recorded as deceased and for no one else, the same answer on every visit of a patient; suicide for 5, a somatic cause, another cause and "Ne sais pas" (a missing code) for fewer than five each. The answer "Somatique" is written with a space before it, which the reader removes. It is delivered as death_cause, as in BP. Date of death: no longer in the extraction. Up to SZALL_20261121 the same column held the date of death (date_fin_suivi_arret_decede: a real date for 8 of the 12 patients, the empty date 0000-00-00 for about a thousand others), because the clean model wrote the date into LOST_TO_FOLLOW_UP_DCD and the SZ export writes that column as CAUSEDEC_STOPSUIVI (face_sz_1_patients.sql, line 36; decision D4 in PROGRESS.md); it was delivered as death_date. The export now puts the cause there (eschizo_stop_suivi.sql, export commit a800f12c, eSchizo v4.45) and the date in no column, so death_date is not delivered any more (decision D105; request R163 asks for the date as dthdtc_stopsuivi, as in BP). The other fields of the form (the other reason, the other cause, the change of diagnosis and its date, the date of the consultation) are not exported either (R163). The new centre is a free text, delivered as text; it never appears in the report.
sz.difference: only three columns of the form are extracted, in one generation (the reason, the new centre and the cause of death); the date of death is not extracted (R163)

fin_de_suivi.description: End of follow-up, one value per patient in the table patients: the reason why the patient is no longer followed, a change of diagnosis and its date, and the date and cause of death (SZ: the reason, the new centre and the cause of death only; the SZ export does not hold the date of death).
flags: An empty reason does not mean that the patient is still followed: in BP 15% of the patients whose last visit is more than three years old have a reason. To know who has left the cohort, use the date of the last visit.
'Does not know' is a missing code, and the placeholder dates of the application are delivered as missing.

common.note: In the table patients. Filled for the few patients whose follow-up was closed; an empty cell does not mean that the patient is still followed. The date of death is in BP only: the SZ export does not hold it (R163). DR has a form but its exported columns are empty; ASP's are not exported (R164).

identite.title: Patient identity

bp.notes: One value per patient. The extraction repeats these columns on every visit row, and they never change between the visits of a patient. The date of birth is exported with the day set to the 15th for every patient. The stored age is the age at the inclusion visit (V0) in completed calendar years, from the date of birth and the V0 date: it is so for all 6,498 patients. The package's own rule (custom.age_at_inclusion, used where the stored age is not the age at inclusion, as in FACE DR) counts completed calendar years in the same way (DR decision D82); whole years of 365.25 days, its rule before, gave one year less for 8 of them. The type of disorder holds three values, plus the abbreviations BPNOS and TBNOS (one patient each), read as "not otherwise specified". The export takes it from the type of mood disorder of the DSM-5 diagnosis form, or of the DSM-IV form when the DSM-5 one is empty; both forms belong to the inclusion visit only (the export's edition column is filled on 5,649 rows, all at V0). For 509 patients the export replaces it by a value from a list of its own (298 type 2, 165 type 1, 46 not otherwise specified), 496 of them in centres A, C and B and most with no DSM edition at V0 (requests R6 and R20 of docs/EXPORT_REQUESTS.md). The cohort is made of the patients whose type is one of the five labels the extraction keeps. Type 2 rises from 40% of the patients included until 2012 to about 60% of those included from 2022, in most centres, and type 1 falls from 46% to 34%: no step at one date in one centre. fondacode (the column subjid) is the patient code of the foundation. Its first two digits are the centre that registered the patient (the same as siteid for the 17 centres), and a transfer between centres copies it unchanged. A usubjid is the id of the delivered record and encodes its centre (usubjid // 10000 is siteid for every patient). A patient transferred between centres has two records, and the export keeps one at random (FU-9; request R1): the usubjid and the centre of such a patient can change from one extraction to the next. 50 patients are delivered under a centre other than the one of their code. 824 usubjid numbers are also used in FACE SZ for other patients. The fondacode changes neither way: it is the key to join two extractions or two cohorts (decision D76 in PROGRESS.md). It is a text and never appears in the report. Not loaded: nom_centre, empty on every row (the application's export to the central database removes it and the export writes it empty; the centre is siteid; in ignored.yaml). usubjid and siteid are key columns. The dictionary also lists armcd and ageu, which are not in the extraction.

sz.notes: One value per patient. The extraction repeats these columns on every visit row, and they never change between the visits of a patient. The date of birth is exported with the day set to the 15th for every patient. The stored age is the age at the inclusion visit (V0) in completed years, computed by the export from the date of birth and the date of the V0 visit (face_sz_1_patients.sql, lines 20 to 24): it equals the calendar age from the exported date of birth and the V0 date for all 2,353 patients. The age at the visit that the package computes (days divided by 365.25, used for the norms) is one year less at V0 for 3 of them, whose V0 falls on the day of their exported birthday; the delivered age is the stored one. The type of disorder holds three values: schizophrenia (1,797 patients), schizoaffective disorder (513) and schizophreniform disorder (43). The dictionary lists other diagnoses (schizoid and schizotypal personality, brief psychotic disorder and others) that the extraction does not hold. The share of women is 26% of the patients included up to 2021 and 33% of those included from 2022. Centre D has 42% schizoaffective disorders (44% of its inclusions before 2016, 41% from 2016), against 14% to 25% in the other large centres. No cause of these steps is known; they are documented here. Same instrument as in FACE BP, with the diagnoses of this cohort. fondacode (the column subjid) is the patient code of the foundation. A usubjid is a number given inside the cohort: it can change from one extraction to the next for a patient registered in two centres, and 824 numbers are also used in FACE BP for other patients. The fondacode does neither: it is the key to join two extractions or two cohorts (decision D9 in PROGRESS.md). It is a text and never appears in the report. usubjid and siteid are key columns. The dictionary also lists nom_centre, which is not in the extraction.
sz.difference: the diagnoses are those of the SZ cohort (schizophrenia, schizoaffective, schizophreniform)

dr.notes: One value per patient. The extraction repeats these columns on every visit row, and they never change between the visits of a patient. Same instrument as in FACE BP and FACE SZ, with the diagnosis of this cohort: "Trouble dépressif majeur" on every row. The date of birth is exported with the day set to the 15th, as in the other cohorts, except for 88 patients of two centres, included from 2014 on, who keep another day. Their day is set to the 15th here (day: 15) and the cell is flagged date_partial, so that the three cohorts hold the same thing (open question O3 in PROGRESS.md). The column age, which the dictionary calls "age at inclusion", is not the age at inclusion: the export computes the calendar age at the date of one visit of the patient, taken in no order (face_dr_1_patients.sql, line 32, on a join with every visit of the patient, line 47; request R10). It equals the age at one of the visits of the patient for all 634 patients, and the age at the inclusion visit for 450: for 271 of the 284 patients who never came back (one year less for the 13 others, the age at the screening visit) and for 179 of the 350 who came back (one to five years more for 163, one year less for 8). age_at_inclusion is therefore computed from the date of birth and the date of the inclusion visit (decision D4); the stored age is read to be compared with it and is not delivered. With a tolerance of one year it differs for 70 patients (score_mismatch; 71 before D82). The function counts completed calendar years, as the BP, SZ and ASP exports store the age: the year of the visit minus the year of birth, one less when the birthday has not come yet that year (decision of the user, 2026-11-21; it counted days / 365.25 before, one year less for 2 patients). It reads the date of birth as exported (birth_date_stored, hidden), with the real day of the 88 patients who keep one. fondacode (the column subjid) is the patient code of the foundation, the same in every extraction and unique across the cohorts: no fondacode of FACE DR is in FACE BP or FACE SZ, while 199 usubjid are also BP numbers and 209 SZ numbers, for other patients. It is a text and never appears in the report. usubjid and siteid are key columns. Not loaded: armcd, the code 7 on every row (ignored.yaml).
dr.difference: the diagnosis is that of the DR cohort; the day of birth is set to the 15th for the patients who keep another one; the stored age is not the age at inclusion, which is computed

asp.notes: One value per patient. The extraction repeats these columns on every visit row, and they never change between the visits of a patient. Same instrument as in FACE BP, SZ and DR, with the diagnosis of this cohort. The column arm is 1 for 2,008 patients and 0 for 310: the export writes into it the conclusion of the DSM-5 criteria of autism of the inclusion visit (cridsm26 of form 198, face_asp_1_patients.sql lines 25 and 122; equal on 2,318 of 2,318 patients, dsm_criteria), so 1 is a patient whose autism spectrum diagnosis was confirmed at the expert centre and 0 a patient who was assessed and not diagnosed (decision D3, open question O3 closed). The conclusion is typed by the clinician, not computed from the criteria (O27). Both groups are delivered. 169 of the patients not diagnosed are children and 141 are adults. The cohort holds children and adults: 956 patients are 5 to 17 years old at inclusion and 1,362 are 18 to 65, so the range of the age starts at 3. The export keeps only the patients aged 3 to 89 at the inclusion visit (face_asp_1_patients.sql line 126). The date of birth is exported with the day set to the 15th for every patient, as in the other cohorts. age_at_inclusion is the stored age, as in FACE BP and SZ: the export computes it as the completed years of the calendar between the date of birth and the date of the inclusion visit (face_asp_1_patients.sql lines 26-30), and it is that age for 2,318 of the 2,318 patients. The package's own computation (custom.age_at_inclusion, which FACE DR uses) counted the days divided by 365.25 and was one year short for 4 patients; these 4 values are now the stored ones (decision D78). It now counts completed calendar years too (DR decision D82). fondacode (the column subjid) is the patient code of the foundation, the same in every extraction and unique across the cohorts: no fondacode of FACE ASP is in FACE BP, SZ or DR, while 378 usubjid are also BP numbers, 538 SZ numbers and 83 DR numbers, for other patients. It is a text and never appears in the report. usubjid and siteid are key columns. Years and centres (definition of done, D88; centres lettered as in D77, A the children's centre): the age at inclusion has a median of 11 in centre A and 17 to 30 elsewhere, and 17 to 27 by year: the age mix of the centres (children are 100% of A, 62% of B, 13% or fewer elsewhere apart from G). No other step.
asp.difference: the diagnosis is that of the ASP cohort (confirmed or not confirmed, from the codes 1 and 0, the DSM-5 conclusion of the inclusion visit); the cohort holds children, so the ranges of the age and of the date of birth are wider; the age at inclusion is the stored age, as in BP

identite.description: Patient identity, one value per patient in the table patients: the patient code of the foundation (fondacode), sex, the diagnosis of the cohort, the date of birth and the age at the inclusion visit.
sources: schema notes (bp, sz, dr, asp identite)
flags: fondacode is the key to join two extractions or two cohorts. A usubjid can change from one extraction to the next for a patient registered in two centres, and the same numbers are used in the other cohorts for other patients.
The date of birth is exported with the day set to the 15th.

diagnosis is the type of bipolar disorder in BP (for 509 patients the export fills it from a list of its own), the type of psychotic disorder in SZ and major depressive disorder for every DR patient. In ASP it says whether the autism spectrum diagnosis was confirmed at the expert centre: the patients assessed and not diagnosed are delivered too.

common.note: In the table patients. diagnosis holds the diagnosis of each cohort, so its labels are not the same from one cohort to the next (bipolar type; kind of schizophrenia; major depressive disorder; autism confirmed or not confirmed). The autism cohort has children and a group that was assessed and not diagnosed. fondacode is the patient code across the cohorts. age_at_inclusion is the age that the export stores, in completed years at the inclusion visit, in BP, SZ and ASP; the DR export takes it at another visit (R10), so DR recomputes it from the birth date and the date of V0.

provenance.title: How the patient came to the expert centre

bp.notes: One value per patient. The dictionary lists adresseur_date, connaissance_centre_expert and its free-text detail under "Fin de suivi". They describe the referral, so they are read here. The free-text detail is named connaissance_centre_expert_preci in the extraction (the name is cut). The purpose of the visit is a multiple choice, exported as a list in one cell; only three combinations occur. information_date is the date at which this information was collected. It is the screening date for about half of the patients and is before the inclusion visit for most. 24 dates before 2008, when the cohort did not exist yet, are flagged out_of_range, and 2 cannot be read as dates (unparsed). The date of the referral letter holds the placeholder 1000-01-01 for 54 patients (date_placeholder). The referral is recorded less and less: for 91% of the patients included until 2012 and 40% of those included from 2024, and for 3% to 15% in three centres (QUESTIONS.md, DM-6). Whether the patient lives inside the catchment area depends on the centre: in one, the share goes from 16% to 91% between the patients included until 2018 and from 2022; in another it is 1%. 81 referral letters are dated after the first visit (52 of them after the inclusion visit) and 24 more than three years before it; they are delivered as written. The answers are those of the form (read in the application in November 2026). Its list of associations also has "Unafam", which no patient of this extraction has: 14 patients were referred by an association, and 11 have its name. The two free-text details may hold names of people; they are delivered as text and never appear in the report.

sz.notes: One value per patient; no value changes between the visits of a patient. Filled for about two patients in three (1,591 have a referrer). Same instrument as in FACE BP, read in the columns of the SZ extraction: the free text of the referrer is adresseur_autres, the date of the referral letter is dsstdtc, the free text of "how did you hear of the centre" is connaissance_autre. The date at which the information was collected (dmdtc in BP) is not in the SZ extraction. The purpose of the visit is a multiple choice, exported as a list in one cell; only three combinations occur. The date of the referral letter holds the placeholder 1000-01-01 for 10 patients (date_placeholder). Four letters are dated before 2005 and 14 a year or more after the visit of the row; they are inside the hard range and are delivered as written. The referring association is known for 4 patients. The form is filled for 75% to 99% of the patients included up to 2018, 68% in 2019 and 42% to 58% from 2020: centres A and F nearly stopped filling it (85% and 78% of their patients included in 2016 to 2018, 11% and 10% from 2019), centre I in part (77%, then 35%). The share of patients from inside the catchment area rises with it (10% to 23% in 2014 to 2018, 39% to 53% from 2021), as centre A (81% from outside) left. The purpose of the visit differs between centres (treatment 71% of the answers at centre C, diagnosis 56% at centre H, both 76% at centres A and I). No cause of these steps is known; they are documented here. The two free-text details may hold names of people or places; they are delivered as text and never appear in the report.
sz.difference: the same questions under other column names (adresseur_autres, dsstdtc, connaissance_autre), a third association, and no information date

dr.notes: One value per patient; no value changes between the visits of a patient. The TRD extraction holds two of the questions of the BP form. The referrer is known for 111 of the 634 patients, 63 of them included in 2025 and 2026: the field came into use late, or the export loses it for the earlier years (open question O4 in PROGRESS.md). Its texts are not those of BP and two of them end with a stray quotation mark; they are read as the same answers. The export writes the texts of the two hospital psychiatrists swapped: the form (form/1.php) stores 2 for the psychiatrist of the centre's catchment area and 3 for one outside it, and the clean model of the export writes "hors secteur" for 2 and "du secteur centre" for 3 (edepression_patient.sql, lines 22 and 23; request R161). They are read as the form says (38 patients: 21 inside, 17 outside); this rests on the current form, which may have had another order in the early years. The purpose of the visit is exported as a code, 1, 2 or 3; the form (form/1.php, OBJET_VISITE) asks the BP and SZ question with 1 diagnostic advice, 2 therapeutic advice, 3 both, delivered with the BP words: 36, 250 and 307 patients. Filled for 593 patients, at 84% to 100% of the inclusions of every year. By centre (2026-11-20): empty for 24 of the 52 patients of one centre (0% to 10% elsewhere), and "diagnostic advice" for 33% of the patients of another (0% to 13% elsewhere): habits of the centres, no known cause. The referrer is filled mostly from 2024, in three centres (open question O4). Not loaded: adresseur_precis, the free text of the referrer, which is empty in the extraction (ignored.yaml).
dr.difference: two of the BP questions only; the referrer has other texts; the purpose of the visit is stored as the numbers 1 to 3 of the form where BP holds the words

provenance.description: How the patient came to the expert centre, one value per patient in the table patients: inside the catchment area or not, who referred the patient, the date of the referral letter, the purpose of the visit and how the patient heard of the centre (DR: the referrer and the purpose only).
flags: The form is filled less and less: in BP for 91% of the patients included until 2012 and 40% of those included from 2024; in DR the referrer is known for 111 of the 634 patients, most of them included in 2025 and 2026.
The catchment area and the purpose of the visit depend strongly on the centre.

common.note: In the table patients. referred_by is in the three cohorts. The catchment area and how the patient heard of the centre are in BP and SZ; the purpose of the visit is in BP, SZ and DR with the same three answers (DR codes read from its form). In DR the export swaps the referrers inside and outside the catchment area; the package reads them back as the form has them (R161).

visit_record.title: Visit record

bp.notes: One value per visit. The visit label, its date and the identifiers of this dictionary section are key columns, built by the pipeline for every instrument. What is left is the date at which the visit record was created: in the application it is a time stamp written when the record is opened for the first time. It is the visit date itself for 63% of the visits and within a month after it for 17%. It is before the visit date for 2,661 visits (2% of the visits until 2015, 23% from 2022: the records are more and more opened ahead of the visit) and more than a year after it for 451. It says when the form was created, not when the patient came. Not loaded: id_fiche_clinique, the identifier of the record (in ignored.yaml).

sz.notes: One value per visit. The visit label, its date and the identifiers of this dictionary section are key columns, built by the pipeline for every instrument. What is left is the date at which the visit record was typed. It is the visit date itself for 4,177 of the 6,616 visits. It is before the visit date for 881 visits and a year or more after it for 311: it says when the form was created, not when the patient came. Same instrument as in FACE BP.

dr.notes: One value per visit. The visit label, its date and the identifiers of this dictionary section are key columns, built by the pipeline for every instrument. What is left is the date at which the visit record was typed. It is the visit date itself for 1,183 of the 2,193 visits. It is before the visit date for 263 visits and a year or more after it for 302: it says when the form was created, not when the patient came. Same instrument as in FACE BP and FACE SZ.

asp.notes: One value per visit. The visit label, its date and the identifiers are key columns, built by the pipeline for every instrument. What is left is the date at which the visit record was typed. It is the visit date itself for 1,135 of the 4,500 rows. It is before the delivered visit date for 632 rows and a year or more after it for 549 (5 visit dates are out of range and not delivered): it says when the form was created, not when the patient came. The visits: 2,318 inclusions, 1,809 screening visits, then one year (177), two years (112), three (41), four (29) and five (8); three more labels (six, seven and nine years) are on fewer than five rows each. 41 visits are dated before the visit that precedes them (visit_order). Same instrument as in FACE BP, SZ and DR. Years and centres (definition of done, D88; centres lettered as in D77, A the children's centre): one delivered variable (the date of the record); no step.

visit_record.description: The date at which the visit record was created in the application, one value per visit.
sources: schema notes (bp, sz, dr, asp visit_record)
flags: It says when the form was created, not when the patient came: it is before the visit date for part of the visits (records opened ahead) and more than a year after it for others. Use the visit date for the timing of a visit.

common.note: The date the visit record was created. The date of the visit itself is the column visit_date of every row.

perinatal.title: The patient's own birth

bp.notes: How the patient was born: the age of each parent at the birth, term, gestational age, type of birth, stay in a neonatal unit, weight, length, head circumference and Apgar scores. Asked of an adult patient, so most answers are memories or come from a health booklet: the type of birth is known for 4,500 patients, the Apgar scores for 900. The section is held by 85% to 88% of the inclusions until 2015 and 67% to 70% from 2019. Centre I left it empty from 2019 (1 of its 74 inclusions of 2019-21) while filling the rest of the medical-history form; centres A and H from 2022 with the whole form (DM-6). The gestational age is given at 10% to 16% of the inclusions until 2016 and 21% to 28% from 2019. One value per patient (decision D51 in PROGRESS.md). A birth does not change, so the value is the one of the patient's earliest visit that has it (the inclusion visit for 99% of them). The heading of the section says that it is filled at the initial evaluation only, yet it is filled again at 421 yearly visits (never at screening or at 6 months). The ages and the weight then differ from the first answer for one patient in five (56 of 284 for the mother's age, 29 of 130 for the weight; most ages by 1 or 2 years), the classes for fewer than one in twenty (14 of 312 for the term). The first is kept and the patient gets patient_value_varies, on the visit of the answer that differs. Zeros. In 2009 and 2010 the form of the application saved a 0 in the measures that were not known (the export passes them on): 67 visits hold a 0 in the weight, the length, the head circumference or an Apgar score, 57 of them in these two years, and an Apgar score of 0 at one minute always comes with a 0 at five minutes. A 0 is therefore a missing code in these five measures, in the gestational age and in the two ages. An age of 99 is a missing code too (3 patients each). Gestational age, in weeks of amenorrhoea. 14 cells hold 6 to 9: months, counted from conception. They are converted to weeks with a factor of 4.345 (unit_inferred), which gives the middle of the month named, in weeks of amenorrhoea, within 0.2 week; 8 of these patients are recorded as premature. 12 cells hold a birth weight of 3,000 to 4,500 g typed in this field (10 of these patients have no birth weight delivered) and 11 hold other impossible values (2 to 4, 15, 47 and 48, 291, 361): out_of_range. The term (born at term, premature, post-term) and the gestational age are two answers of the patient and often disagree: of the patients recorded as premature who give a gestational age, a third give 37 weeks or more; of those recorded as born at term, 30 of 911 give less than 37 weeks and 94 give 42 or more. The gestational age is typed as text and the export keeps its first whole number (ebipolar_mh.sql lines 15 to 20): a half, or the days after the weeks, are lost (request R33). Hard limits. Weight 400 to 6,500 g (17 values outside: 12 below 100, of which 10 are 47 to 57, a birth length typed in the weight field, and 2 are 35; 2 of 300; 3 of 31,000 to 45,000, all multiples of 1,000); length 25 to 60 cm (5 outside); head circumference 20 to 42 cm (6 outside: 4 of 46 to 58.5 cm on visits whose length field holds another value, 47 to 52, and 2 of 10 on rows whose fields are shifted); Apgar 1 to 10 (3 above); mother's age 12 to 60, father's age 12 to 90 (1 below). On 3 visits the birth fields are shifted one place (a length in the weight field, a head circumference in the length field): 2 patients keep a birth length of 35 or 37 cm from them, delivered as written. No winsorising (decision D52 in PROGRESS.md). The weight, the length, the head circumference and the gestational age are delivered as they are inside their hard limits: a very low birth weight or an extreme prematurity is the information, and the limits already remove the impossible values. Apgar score at one minute. 10 for three quarters of the patients, far more than at a birth clinic, where 10 at one minute is unusual; the share goes from 45% to 95% between centres. Delivered as written. For 3 of the 837 patients with both scores, the score at five minutes is lower than at one minute. The export reads a score typed as two numbers "a/b" as their mean ("8/10" gives 9; ebipolar_mh.sql lines 107 to 110 and 124 to 127), so such a score cannot be told from a typed one; no delivered score holds a half (request R33). The dictionary sheet of this tab has one more column than the others (a list of CDISC codes before the names); the names used here are those of the column "NOM VARIABLE EXTRACTION". Not exported: the question "no change since the last visit" that opens the section at a yearly visit (DM-10).

sz.notes: Ages of the parents at the birth of the patient, term, gestational age, type of birth, neonatal admission and birth weight (the BP questions), and four questions that the SZ form adds: born in a town or in the country, obstetric complications, a viral infection of the mother during the pregnancy, and the events of the pregnancy. These four are filled from 2019 (1 or 2 visits of 2017 and of 2018 hold them). Filled at inclusion (about 1,800 visits for the term, 1,048 for the weight, 427 to 624 for the four questions). Same instrument as in FACE BP, without the birth length, the head circumference and the Apgar scores, which SZ does not have. The birth weight is in the column poidsna, which the dictionary files under the tab SOCIAL - PERINATALITE. Missing codes: 999 and 9999 ("does not know") in the ages of the parents, the gestational age and the weight, 0 as in BP, "Ne sais pas", "NC", "NSP" and "DCM". 7 weights under 400 g are out of range (typed in kg or cut). 17 gestational ages are typed as text and stay unparsed: weeks with a word or a number of days (6), months (3), two numbers or a range (4) and words without a number (4). 5 gestational ages outside 20 to 45 weeks (1 under, 4 over) and 1 age of the mother over 60 are out_of_range. The events of the pregnancy are a list of nine boxes and "none", several of which can be ticked: one yes/no per event. 348 of 469 answers are "none".
sz.difference: no birth length, head circumference or Apgar score; the weight is in the column poidsna; four questions of 2017 and the events of the pregnancy are added; 999 is a missing code

dr.notes: The BP schema with the codes of this extraction. Asked once, at inclusion: the form of the history (164) is shown at the inclusion visit only (visit type 2, config/global.php): 532 patients. Codes, from the form (164.php): the term is 1 preterm, 2 at term, 3 post-term, 0 "Ne sais pas"; the type of birth is 1 vaginal, 2 caesarean, 0 "ne sais pas"; the neonatal hospitalisation is 1 yes, 0 no, 2 "Ne sais pas" (84%, 4% and 12% of the answers for no, yes and "not known"; 87%, 8% and 6% in BP). "Not known" is a missing code (45, 51 and 63 cells). A 0 in a measure (ages of the parents, weight, length, head circumference, gestational age, Apgar scores) is "not recorded", as in BP (8 gestational ages). The weight is typed in grams (four digits) and the gestational age in weeks (two digits). Out of range: one age of the mother of 86, one gestational age of 19 weeks and two birth weights. Centres and years (2026-11-20). The term of birth is answered for 58% to 97% of the patients of each centre but for 8 of the 44 of one centre, and for 65% to 86% of the patients of each period from 2013: a fill rate, with no known cause.
dr.difference: the answers are stored as numbers, with 0 or 2 for "not known"

asp.notes: The term, the age of the parents, the delivery, the newborn's first days and the measures at birth: 2071 inclusion visits (878 of children) and 0 follow-up visits, from 2009 to 2026; asked once, at the inclusion visit. Same questions as the instrument perinatal of FACE BP, SZ and DR where they exist there: the term, the age of the parents, the weight, the length and the head circumference at birth, the two Apgar scores and the stay in a neonatal unit are delivered under the same names. None of these columns holds a 0 or a 99 that stands for "not known" (the Apgar scores hold three real 0), so they stack with the other cohorts by name. The delivery is described here by yes/no questions (natural, induced, caesarean, forceps, vacuum) where the other cohorts have one list. The term is known for 1709 patients: under 37 weeks for 163 of them. The birth weight is written in grams (1256 values) or in kilograms (fewer than five values under 10, converted); fewer than five values between 10 and 400 fit neither and are not delivered. **The delivery.** The form asks "natural delivery" first and shows the questions on the delivery (induced, caesarean, forceps, vacuum, the free text of another delivery) only when the answer is no: the gate is shown the other way round. The answer is yes for 1366 patients, no for 511, not known for 135 and empty for 306. not_natural_delivery (not delivered) is that question read the other way round, 1 for a delivery that is not natural. After a natural delivery induced_delivery, caesarean, forceps and vacuum_extraction are 0 (`asked_if`: 1366 patients each, 5464 cells); after a delivery that is not natural they are read as written (caesarean 326 yes, 149 no, 36 empty; induced 165 yes; forceps 65; vacuum 24); where the delivery is not known or empty they stay missing. Nothing is filled under a natural delivery (0 of the 475 caesarean answers, 0 of the 416 induced). With the natural births counted, caesarean is 326 yes among 1841 patients (the 1366 natural births and the 475 answers), where it was 326 of 475: it is now BP's birth_type equal to caesarean. The planned or urgent kind of an induction or of a caesarean and the free texts (another delivery, the kind of foetal distress) are details and stay missing after a no. **The first days.** The days in a neonatal unit (neonatal_hospitalisation_days) are shown after a yes to the stay: they are 0 after a no (1675 patients) and filled for 113 of the 168 patients with a stay. **Year and centre.** The medians of the term (39 or 40 weeks) and of the head circumference (34 or 35 cm) by year and by centre (years and centres with 20 values or more) differ by one unit of a whole number scale: no step. The planned or emergency kind of an induction or of a caesarean (126 to 256 answers) does not differ by year or by centre beyond chance. A section of the ASP cohort only.
asp.difference: other columns; the delivery is described by yes/no questions (natural, induced, caesarean, forceps, vacuum) and not by one list, and the four questions after the natural delivery are shown only when it is not natural (0 after a natural one, by `asked_if` on the answer read the other way round); the days in a neonatal unit are 0 after a no; the term is not asked as a class; the birth weight is typed in grams or in kilograms; more questions on the newborn

perinatal.description: The patient's own birth, one value per patient in the table patients: the age of each parent, the term, the gestational age, the type of birth, a stay in a neonatal unit, the weight, the length, the head circumference and the Apgar scores (SZ has no length, head circumference or Apgar score; ASP describes the delivery by yes/no questions).
perinatal.period: the birth of the patient, asked at the inclusion visit
sources: schema notes (bp, sz, dr, asp perinatal)
flags: BP, SZ and DR ask an adult patient: most answers are memories or come from a health booklet (in BP the type of birth is known for 4,500 patients, the Apgar scores for 900).

The Apgar score at one minute is 10 for three quarters of the BP patients, far more than at a birth clinic: delivered as written. In BP and DR a 0 in a measure is 'not recorded' (a missing code), so no Apgar score of 0 is delivered there; ASP holds real 0.

The term (preterm, at term, post-term) and the gestational age are two answers and often disagree: in BP a third of the patients recorded as premature who give a gestational age give 37 weeks or more.
A birth does not change: the first answer of the patient is kept. The measures are not winsorised.

common.note: In the table patients. The ages of the parents, the weeks of pregnancy, the birth weight (grams) and the stay in a neonatal unit are in the four cohorts. The term as a class and the kind of delivery as one list are in BP, SZ and DR; ASP describes the delivery with yes/no questions of its own (induced, caesarean, forceps, vacuum), asked only after a delivery that is not natural and 0 after a natural one: its caesarean yes is BP's birth_type equal to caesarean. The ASP columns of the parents' ages, the term, the weight, the length, the head circumference and the stay in a neonatal unit hold no 0 or 99 used as not known, so stack "yes" holds.

social.title: Social situation at inclusion

bp.notes: The social situation of the patient on the day of the inclusion visit: marital status, education, work, housing, household, income and debts. Filled once, at the inclusion visit (5,045 patients; no follow-up or screening visit holds any of these questions). One column, the class of the job, is filled at the follow-up visits instead. The way of living, the housing, the income and the debts are asked from 2010-2011. The tab is held by 29% and 39% of the inclusions of centre C in 2016-18 and 2019-21 (71% to 89% before and after), by 23% of those of centre F in 2019-21, and hardly by centres A and H from 2022 (O40, DM-6). Education. The level reached, as a list from the first year of primary school to the doctorate. The export writes most levels as a number (CP to CM2 = 1 to 5, collège = 6 to 9, lycée = 10 and 11, CAP = 13, BEP = 14, BAC+1 to BAC+5 = 15 to 19, doctorate = 20) and two as words, "BAC" and "Certificat d'études". The form has no Terminale, so code 12 never occurs. The numbers are codes of a list, not years of schooling (a CAP is 13, the 1ère 11), so the level is delivered as a category. The years of education asked on the neuropsychology form agree with it (a median of 12 years for "BAC", 17 for BAC+5). Work status. The form offers seven answers: without a job, in work, at home, retired, student, pension, other (decision D94 in PROGRESS.md). Code 3 (student) never appears in the extraction: the export tests "Étudiant" with an accent while the form stores "Etudiant", and writes 6 for every other answer, an empty one included (DM-13). Code 6 is given to 1,150 patients, 23%, with a median age of 30 and 39% under 25; 7 of them answered no other social question. Its share rises from 20%-23% of the inclusions until 2021 to 34% in 2022-23 and 27% from 2024. Code 6 is delivered as student_or_other until the export is corrected. The other codes behave as the dictionary says: the questions on the current job are filled for code 1 only (94%), the retired (code 2) have a median age of 65, and 143 of the 188 patients with code 4 live on a disability pension. The longest period of work is asked only when the current period of work is not the longest: for the employed an empty cell may mean that the current period (job_duration) is the longest. Main source of income. The form offers seven answers: salary, RMI or RSA, AAH, disability pension, unemployment benefit, APL, other. It has no "no income" and no eighth answer, so the dictionary's "7 = no income, 8 = other" is not the form: code 7 is "other" (decision D94). It is given to 1,071 patients, among them 187 of the 288 retired, who have a pension. The SZ form does have "no income" as its seventh answer: do not compare code 7 between the cohorts. Household. The number of persons under the same roof is 1 for most of the patients who live alone and 0 for 134 of them: some count themselves and some do not. Centre C writes 0 for 42 of its 99 patients who live alone, the other centres for 3% to 12%. The number is typed as text and the export keeps only its digits (ebipolar_social.sql line 108), so "2 ou 3" becomes 23: the five values above 20 (out of range) are most likely two numbers run together (request R42). Age at the first job. The form offers "<15", 15 to 60 and ">60"; the export keeps only the digits (ebipolar_social.sql line 74), so 15 holds "<15" and 15 together (182 patients, against 434 at 16) and 60 holds ">60" and 60 (3 patients). Delivered as exported (request R41). Durations of work, in years. Not winsorised: the long careers of the older patients are real (as in DR). A longest period or a total above 60 years is out of range (5 cells, up to 2,223). 42 totals are longer than the age at inclusion minus 14 years (11 longer than the age itself), and 51 longest periods are longer than the total (39 by more than a year); delivered as written. End of the last job. 1000-01-01 is the date the application writes in an empty date since July 2024 (D98): 176 cells, 171 of them from 2024, 168 on patients with another work status, who are not asked the question. The question asks about a job that has ended, so a date on the day of the visit or later is impossible (before_visit): 16 dates, 15 after the visit and 1 on its day, are delivered as missing with out_of_range. Debt. The answer "Non renseigné" of the form is delivered as missing (not recorded): 153 inclusions, 85 of them until 2012. Not loaded (ignored.yaml). empjob, the class of the current job, holds two of its nine codes only (5 for 110 patients, 1 for 12, of 2,308 employed): the export looks the 18 classes of the form (the second level of the INSEE nomenclature) up in the nine classes of the dictionary, whose labels are other ones, and keeps two (D74, D99). The mapping to the nine classes is in QUESTIONS.md (FU-8). protec, the legal protection measure, is not delivered (decision D111 in PROGRESS.md). Not in the extraction: the date of the social assessment, the class of the last job of a patient without one (asked for in FU-8) and, at follow-up, whether the work status changed and the new status. The sick leave questions of the form are read in the tab SOIN SUIVI HOSP ARRET TRAVAIL. Three cells of the other way of living hold only an escaped line break and are read as empty. The class of the job at follow-up (empjob_psytaitement) uses the 18 classes of the inclusion form (no patient has "Chef d'entreprise de 10 salariés ou plus"). It is filled on 219 follow-up visits of 200 patients from 2021, and asked only when the work status changed since the last visit and the new status is "in work". The change and the new status are not exported, so an empty cell does not say that the patient does not work.

sz.notes: Marital status, children, education, work, housing and income, at the inclusion visit (1,983 visits, all at V0). Same instrument as in FACE BP with the columns that SZ holds. Three BP names are read otherwise here: the way of living is in the column vie (BP: lvsbjind), with the same list written in words; the age at the first job holds "Jamais travaillé" (149, a missing code: not applicable) and values under a limit (11, censored_left); "-1 an" is "less than a year" in the time in work. The number of children, the months in the present job and the income level are SZ questions. The number of children equals the daughters plus the sons of the family structure (tab ANTECEDENTS) on 1,806 of the 1,819 visits that have both. Marital status: an answer lost by the export (open question O22, request R47). The form stores code 2 under the label "Marié (ou situation marital depuis au moins 6 mois)/ Concubin / Pacsé" (eschizo.sql, line 7724) and the export looks for "Marié / Concubin / Pacsé" (eschizo_social.sql, line 15), which it never finds, so the cell is left empty. The marital status never holds code 2: it is 1 on 1,652 visits, 3 or 4 on 72, 5 on 4, and empty on 8% to 19% of the inclusions of every year (253 of the 1,981 inclusions with a social form, 167 of them patients who live in their own family home). An empty cell is often a married patient or one living as a couple, and the shares computed from this variable are wrong. Delivered as extracted until the export is corrected. The source of income (saltyp) is not delivered (ignored.yaml, decision D94, request R46). The form asks the types of income as eight boxes, several of which can be ticked (salary, minimum income, disability allowance, disability pension, unemployment benefit, housing benefit, no income, other). The export keeps one code, the first that its own list of labels finds (eschizo_social.sql, lines 85 to 95); it looks for "Salarié" where the form writes "Salaire" (line 87) and never finds "Pension d'invalidité" (line 90), so codes 1 and 4 are on none of the 1,100 filled cells and 162 of the 236 employed patients have no source. The column is neither the main source nor the list. A period without work status (open question O23, request R48). The work status is empty on most inclusions from the spring of 2015 to mid-2019 (17 of 44 visits in the second quarter of 2015, 140 of 151 in 2016, 149 of 153 in 2017, 159 of 204 in 2018, 62 of 149 in 2019, 2 of 25 in the last quarter of 2019), and filled before and after, while the housing and the income level are filled all along. In that period the question was asked in the socio-demographic form (table socio_demog, with seven answers, the types of income and other social questions), which the export does not read: a comment of 27 May 2016 in the application (visite.php, lines 542 to 545) says that the variable was removed from the social form and is to be read in socio_demog. The current social form asks it again. The answers of the period are in socio_demog in the source database. The age at the first job left the form in 2019: it is filled on 67% to 92% of the inclusions of 2010 to 2018, on 48 of 149 in 2019 and on 1 of the 697 after; the current form has no such question. The income bands are in euros of the day. The share of 1,000 to 1,500 euros is 11% to 13% of the inclusions of 2018 to 2021, 21% in 2022 and 2023, 24% in 2024 and 41% to 43% in 2025 and 2026, and that of 500 to 1,000 euros falls from 52% to 60% (2018 to 2021) to 28% and 18% (2025, 2026). Most of the move is among the unemployed patients (54 of the 137 included from 2024 are in 1,000 to 1,500 euros). A likely cause is the disability allowance (AAH), which passed 1,000 euros a month in 2024; the step is documented here. The work status holds codes 0 to 6: the export writes "Au foyer" as 5. One number of months in the present job is over 600 (out_of_range). empjob, the class of the job, holds one code on 41 rows and is ignored (O2). The education level mixes years and words, as in BP.
sz.difference: the columns that SZ holds; the way of living is in the column vie; children, months in the job and income level are added; the source of income is not delivered (saltyp ignored, because the export keeps one of eight boxes and loses two of them, D94); maristat loses code 2 in the export (O22)

dr.notes: The BP schema with the questions of this extraction: marital status, education, work and the way of living. One form (168), shown at the inclusion and at the visits of 2 and 4 years (visit types 2, 6 and 8, config/global.php): the same questions at every visit, so no _v0 and _fu schemas. 681 visits; the form is filled at 95% of the inclusions until 2014, 88% in 2015-17, 84% in 2018-20, 62% in 2021-23 and 74% since. The education level is lower at the later visit on 12 of the 156 pairs of an inclusion and a follow-up answer (different on 34). Codes are those of BP and of the form. The education level code 12 is "BAC" on the form (168.php), not a third year of upper secondary school (87 visits; their median years of education on the neuropsychology form is 12, as BP's "BAC"). The person with whom the patient spends most time (lien) is read with the list of the form: 1 spouse, 2 mother, 3 father, 4 flatmate, 5 friend, 6 partner (concubin), 7 sibling, 8 grandparent, 9 other relative, 10 child, 11 other (672 visits). Work. The form (js/formulaires.js, lines 4933 to 4987) asks the months in the present job and whether it is full time of the employed only, the end of the last job of the unemployed only, and the occupational class of both: shown_if on the work status, 8 cells filled under another status are delivered as missing (not_shown: 1 month count, 2 full time, 3 classes, 2 end dates). The months in the present job are the SZ question and take the SZ name job_months (BP asks a class of duration); the export writes them as whole numbers (request R160). The occupational class (empjob) is the first level of the INSEE classes, read with the eight classes of the dictionary: of the current job for the employed (207 of 225 visits), of the last job for the unemployed (109 of 131). An end of the last job on or after the visit is impossible and is delivered as missing (before_visit, out_of_range: 3 cells). The age at the first job is defined in the form but never shown, and is not in the extraction. Household. The number of persons under the same roof is 0 for 29 of the 165 visits of patients who live alone with an answer (1 for 123): some count themselves and some do not, as in BP. Two values of two digits above 20 are impossible (out_of_range). Centres and years (2026-11-20). The shares differ between centres with 20 answers or more as the patients do: living in a couple 49% to 73%, employed 17% to 50%, the spouse as closest person 24% to 64%, clerical or service employees 24% to 70% of the occupational classes. By period they stay within 10 points of the cohort, except the clerical or service employees of 2022 and 2023 (5 of 23 classes, 22% against 43%): a small group, no known cause. The legal protection measure (protec) is not delivered, as in BP and SZ (BP D111): it is administrative (ignored.yaml).
dr.difference: the time in the job is a number of months (the SZ question, job_months); the occupational class is added; the person the patient spends most time with is added (the list of form 168); the code 12 of the education level is "BAC"; the questions of the job are gated on the work status; no questions on housing, income and debts

social.description: Social situation: marital status, education level, work status and history, housing, household, income and debts. Asked at the inclusion visit in BP and SZ; in DR the same form is filled at inclusion and at the visits of 2 and 4 years. SZ and DR hold part of the BP questions.
flags: BP work_status: the export loses the answer 'student' and writes the code of 'other' for every other answer, an empty one included. That code is delivered as student_or_other (23% of the patients).

SZ marital_status: the answer 'married or living as a couple' is lost by the export (empty cell), so shares computed from it are wrong. SZ work_status is empty on most inclusions from the spring of 2015 to mid-2019.
income_source (BP): the code 'other' also holds the pensions of the retired; the SZ form has other answers, and its source of income is not delivered.
household_size: of the patients who live alone, some count themselves (1) and some do not (0).
BP first_job_age: the export keeps only the digits, so 15 holds '<15' and 15, and 60 holds '>60' and 60.

No ISCED level is delivered; an approximate mapping of the French diplomas is in scale_reference_rest.md section 12 (to verify). The occupational class of DR (job_class) is the first level of the INSEE classes.

common.domain: Social situation and use of care
common.note: Education, work status and way of living are in BP, SZ and DR with the same labels; a full-time job is also in ASP. In SZ the export loses answers: no patient is recorded as married or living as a couple, and none with a salary or a disability pension (SZ O22; R46, R47): do not compare marital_status with SZ. SZ asks the sources of income as eight boxes and the export keeps one, so SZ delivers no income_source. The person the patient spends most time with is in BP and DR (closest_person), the months in the present job in SZ and DR (job_months), the INSEE class of the job in DR and ASP (job_class). In BP the export writes the students with 'other' (student_or_other). The other questions differ.

care_use.title: Use of care since the last visit (follow-up visits)

bp.notes: The care the patient used for the psychiatric disorder since the last visit, asked at every follow-up visit. Two parts: the usual follow-up (91% of the visits say yes) and unscheduled or emergency care (13%). In each, one yes/no per kind of professional and the number of consultations, and for the second part the visits to an emergency room without admission. Yes/no answers are delivered as 1 and 0. Asked only after a yes (asked_if). The boxes of a part are shown only after a yes to its first question, and a number only after a yes to its box; in the extraction they are almost always empty otherwise. They are read as 0 there: with no unscheduled care, there was no emergency consultation of a psychiatrist, and their number is 0. Empty boxes beside a ticked one (decision D131, was O51; kept by the project lead when the tab was reviewed again). The boxes are Oui/Non radio buttons, and on 824 visits of the usual part a rater ticked some and left others empty: 461 of them also hold an explicit "Non" and 363 hold none, so on those 363 an empty box may be unanswered rather than no. The empty ones are almost always the kinds of care that few patients receive (the psychiatrist box is empty on 3% of these visits, the others on 42% to 57%), so they are read as no, as for the non-drug treatments (D124): box_list, in the usual part (five boxes) and in the unscheduled part (six boxes, the emergency room included: 143 such visits, 71 with an explicit "Non", 72 without). 2,106 boxes (1,658 and 448) and 2,106 numbers of consultations become 0; no value written changes. A box whose number was typed is left as written (the number is shown only after a yes). A visit with every box empty keeps them missing. Where the first question of the usual part is not answered, 10 visits still hold boxes (42 answers, 17 of them yes), delivered as written; their numbers are read as usual (11 written after a yes, 25 read as 0 after a no to their box). The unscheduled part has no such visit. A few answers contradict the order of the form and are delivered as written, with no flag: 13 numbers are written although their box is empty after a yes to the part (12 visits); after a no to the unscheduled part, 4 visits hold boxes (23 answers, 3 yes); 8 numbers above 0 have a box at 0 (3 after a no to the box, 5 with the box empty after a no to the part); 39 numbers are 0 after a yes to their box; 21 visits say yes to the usual part and no to all five of its boxes. The unscheduled part also covers admissions, which have no box: on 141 of its 1,183 yes the six boxes are all no, and 104 of the 125 of these visits with a known number were hospitalised since the last visit (hospitalisations_fu). care_urgent is therefore not "any of the six boxes". Numbers. Typed freely. "NSP", "?" and "inconnu" are missing codes (19 cells). One ">10" is read as 10 with a mark in the censoring column. 100 cells on 79 visits hold words and end unparsed, all before 2022 and half of them in centre D: 53 hold a number with words ("1 fois par mois", a range), 47 words only. Since 2022 the form accepts only one or two digits for the numbers of consultations (the emergency-room count is the exception), so the words and the 13 numbers above 99 are all older. A number above 365 is out of range (none). 71 numbers are above 52, most of them for the psychiatrist (29) or the psychologist (32). After a yes to a box, the number is empty on 15% (psychiatrist) to 25% (general practitioner) of the visits in the usual follow-up, and on 9% (emergency room) to 32% (psychologist, 18 of 56) in the unscheduled part. It is more and more often empty: for the psychiatrist, 6% to 8% of the visits until 2018, 19% in 2019-2021 and 28% from 2022, and 54% to 66% from 2022 in centres A, C, F and I. A mean over the delivered numbers therefore leaves out more visits with care in recent years. The time covered. The form words both parts "depuis la dernière visite" and, unlike the history forms, has no question on a change (rad_pas_dechangement is not in the follow-up treatment form): the numbers cover the time since the previous visit, and that time is not one window. Over the 11,686 follow-up visits the median gap is 321 days (192 at the six-monthly visits, 363 at the yearly ones), longer when a visit was missed. After a yes, the median number of psychiatrist consultations is 6 after 4 to 8 months, 10 after 10 to 14 and 12 after 18 to 30. Divide by the time since the previous visit (from visit_date) before comparing visits. The form is filled on 82% to 91% of the follow-up visits until 2021 and on 70% to 72% from 2022 (centre A: 26% from 2022, DM-6). The share of visits with a psychologist rises from 27% to 30% until 2018 to 41% in 2022-2023 and 50% from 2024, in nearly every centre. The numbers are not winsorised (decision D54 in PROGRESS.md): they are counts of events, with a hard range of 0 to 365. Ten of the eleven are 0 on 70% to 99.8% of the visits, so their 99th percentile is low (0 to 2 for unscheduled care, 8 to 50 for the usual follow-up) and a cut there would bring the rare high counts down to it. The number of psychiatrist consultations is 0 on only 15% of the visits (median 6); it is left unwinsorised like the others, and its high values are left to the hard range.

care_use.description: Use of care for the psychiatric disorder since the last visit, asked at every follow-up visit (BP): the usual follow-up and unscheduled or emergency care, each with one yes/no per kind of professional and the number of consultations, and the visits to an emergency room without admission.
flags: The answers cover the time since the previous visit, which is not one window (in BP the median gap is 321 days: 192 at the six-monthly visits, 363 at the yearly ones). Divide by the time since the previous visit before comparing visits.

After a yes to a kind of professional the number of consultations is more and more often empty (psychiatrist: 6% to 8% of the visits until 2018, 28% from 2022): a mean over the delivered numbers leaves out more visits with care in recent years.
A box left empty beside a ticked box of the same part is read as no, and its number as 0.
care_urgent also covers admissions, which have no box: it is not 'any of the six boxes'.
The numbers are counts of events and are not winsorised (hard range 0 to 365).

hospitalisations_fu.title: Hospitalisations since the last visit (follow-up visits)

bp.section: VIE ENTIERE / DEPUIS LA DERNIERE VISITE
bp.notes: Hospitalisations since the last visit: their number and total duration. Asked at every follow-up visit, six-monthly and yearly, in the part of the follow-up diagnosis form on mood disorders since the last visit ("Troubles de l'humeur depuis la dernière visite"); the form does not say for what cause. 87% of the numbers are 0. Two periods in the same columns (decision D54 in PROGRESS.md). The number of hospitalisations and their total duration are asked at the inclusion visit, about the whole life, and at every follow-up visit, about the time since the last visit; the dictionary names the section "whole life / since the last visit". The patients have 2.5 hospitalisations on average at inclusion and 0.17 at a follow-up visit. The two are delivered as separate columns, ending in _v0 and _fu; visit_form says which form a visit used and is read from the visit label. Number. The form stops at 20: ">20" is read as 20 with a mark in the censoring column (this value or more; 1 visit). The range is 0 to 20, like the form (it was 0 to 50: the largest raw number is 13, so no cell changes). "Ne sais pas" is a missing code for the number (29 cells) and the duration (60, 29 of them after a number of 0). Duration, in months. A choice in a list: 0, a quarter, half or three quarters of a month, 1 to 20 months, more than 20 (censored at 20). A duration left empty where the number is 0 is 0 (asked_if on the number, D123): 978 visits. This happens more often in recent years (6% of the numbers of 0 until 2012, 18% from 2024) and in centres E and I (27% and 25%). The time covered. The form words the question "depuis la dernière visite" and, unlike the history forms, has no question on a change (rad_pas_dechangement is not in the follow-up diagnosis form): the answer is about the time since the previous visit, and that time is not one window. Over the 11,686 follow-up visits the median gap is 321 days (192 at the six-monthly visits, 363 at the yearly ones) and one visit in ten comes more than 16 months after the previous one. The numbers rise with it: 0.13 hospitalisations on average after 4 to 8 months, 0.44 after more than 30. Compare visits through the time since the previous visit (from visit_date). Filled at 72% of the follow-up visits: 84% until 2012 and 57% from 2024. The form is missing more often from 2022 (centre A, DM-6 in QUESTIONS.md), and where it is filled the number is skipped more often (filled on 94% of those visits until 2012, 81% from 2024). The share of visits with a hospitalisation stays between 11% and 14% in every period. Delivered as written: 20 visits give a number of 0 and a duration above 0, 36 give a number of 1 or more and a duration of 0 (a stay of less than a week fits 0 on this list), and 11 durations are longer than the time since the previous visit. No winsorising (decision D54 in PROGRESS.md): most answers are 0 (87% of the numbers, 88% of the durations), so the 99th percentile would bring the rare high values down to it. hospitalisations_v0.title: Hospitalisations before inclusion (inclusion visit)

bp.section: VIE ENTIERE / DEPUIS LA DERNIERE VISITE
bp.notes: Hospitalisations up to the inclusion visit: the age at the first one, their number and total duration over the whole life, and their number and duration in the 12 months before the visit. The two inclusion diagnosis forms (DSM-IV, then DSM-5) ask them in their part on mood disorders and do not say for what cause. Filled at the inclusion visit only. Two periods in the same columns (decision D54 in PROGRESS.md). The number of hospitalisations and their total duration are asked at the inclusion visit, about the whole life, and at every follow-up visit, about the time since the last visit; the dictionary names the section "whole life / since the last visit". The patients have 2.5 hospitalisations on average at inclusion and 0.17 at a follow-up visit. The two are delivered as separate columns, ending in _v0 and _fu; visit_form says which form a visit used and is read from the visit label. Number. The form stops at 20: ">20" is read as 20 with a mark in the censoring column (this value or more; 25 visits). The range is 0 to 20, like the form (it was 0 to 50: no raw number is above 20, so no cell changes). "Ne sais pas" is a missing code, here and in the age, the lifetime duration and the number for the year. Duration, in months. A choice in a list: 0, a quarter, half or three quarters of a month, 1 to 20 months, more than 20 (censored at 20; 32 visits). A duration left empty where the number is 0 is 0 (asked_if on the number, D123): 569 visits. Age at the first hospitalisation. The form asks it before the number, and its list starts with "<5" and has no answer for a patient never hospitalised. "<5" is therefore read as unknown, a missing code (D123): 16 of the 21 patients who chose it have a number of 0 and 3 have none. Of the 1,278 patients with a number of 0, the age is empty for 1,076, "Ne sais pas" for 176 and a number for 10. 30 patients with a number of 1 or more give no age, and 24 more answer "Ne sais pas". The 12 months before inclusion. The number and the total duration in weeks. The DSM-IV form (inclusions up to 2022) shows them only after a yes to "at least one mood episode in the past year"; the DSM-5 form (from 2020) asks every patient. After a "no" to that question both are 0 (asked_if, D123; the question is read from rad_tb_hum_epthyman and delivered in the DSM schemas): 850 numbers of DSM-IV inclusions (and 2 of inclusions with no DSM label) and 29 of DSM-5 inclusions were empty there. The DSM-5 form asks the number and the weeks of every patient, and the decision is kept (D123): of the 187 DSM-5 inclusions with no episode, 158 typed a number and 7 of them (4%) were hospitalised in the year, so one or two of the 29 zeros set here (29 numbers, 28 weeks) may be wrong. The weeks are 0 where the number for the year is 0 (1,989 visits: 1,119 after a typed 0, 870 after a 0 given by the mood question). 31% of the DSM-IV numbers and 28% of the DSM-5 numbers are above 0. A duration above 52 weeks is out of range (3 cells, all on the DSM-IV form; the DSM-5 form stops at 52). The dictionary also lists a yes/no question, hospitalised in the past 12 months (hooccur_hospitalisation_ly). No form has this field and no export model writes it; the dictionary row is to be deleted (R95). Centre C holds no answer from 2022: its DSM-5 table is missing from the export (R20). Centre A fills the number on 19% of its inclusions in 2022-23 and on none from 2024 (O40). Where a hospitalisation is counted, centre H leaves the lifetime duration empty on 33 of its 68 inclusions from 2022, and centre C on 102 of 449 up to 2021 (6% to 10% in the other centres). The lifetime number is answered on 86% of the inclusions dated up to 2018 and on 64% of those dated from 2022. The fall is in four centres, from 77% to 0%, 77% to 12%, 90% to 59% and 97% to 77% (the first two are the centres named above; O40). Delivered as written, with no flag: 5 ages at the first hospitalisation are 2 to 16 years above the age at inclusion (2015 to 2020), and 26 more are 1 year above, which fits an age counted by calendar year. 20 patients give more hospitalisations in the year than over their whole life (9 of them none over the life). 18 durations for the year exceed the lifetime duration by more than 2 weeks (5 of them with a lifetime duration of 0). 21 durations for the year are above 0 with a number for the year of 0, and 5 lifetime durations are above 0 with a lifetime number of 0. No winsorising (decision D54 in PROGRESS.md). The numbers and durations count events, and their rare high values are real. A quarter of the lifetime numbers are 0, and 70% of the numbers for the year. The default 99th percentile would bring 37 lifetime numbers of 16 to 20 down to 15, 34 numbers of 4 to 8 in the year down to 3, and 50 durations of 23 to 52 weeks in the year down to 22; for the lifetime duration it is 20, the top of the list, and would change nothing. The age at the first hospitalisation is not winsorised either, like the other ages at onset: the default would raise 17 ages of 9 to 12 to 13 and lower 37 ages of 61 to 77 to 60.

sz.notes: Asked at the inclusion visit: the age at the first hospitalisation for a psychotic disorder, its length and the length of the hospitalisations of the first psychotic episode (weeks), whether the patient was ever hospitalised in psychiatry, how many times and for how long in all (months). Not the BP columns: the SZ form asks about the first hospitalisation and the first episode, which BP does not, and names its columns otherwise. The BP names are kept where the question is the same. The age is the gate of the block (decision D70). Its list has 89 answers: "Pas d'hospitalisations" first, then 88 others (the ages 5 to 89, "<5", ">89" and "Ne sais pas"). The form shows the number of hospitalisations, their total length in months, the length of the first one and the weeks of the first episode only after one of the 88 others (field table of the diagnosis form, positions 1 to 88 of the age). The gate is asked the other way round, a question shown for any answer but one, so it is read once more as a hidden variable that lists the 88 answers (hospitalised_by_age, keep false; SCHEMA_SPEC section 4, R16), and the questions it hides get asked_if on it. An empty age stays missing. The age holds "Pas d'hospitalisations" on 397 inclusion visits (a missing code: not applicable), "Ne sais pas" on 37 and a value under a limit on 18 (censored_left); ">89" does not occur. On the 397 the export leaves the number empty on 384 visits and holds 0 on 13, the total length empty on 385, and the weeks of the first episode and the length of the first hospitalisation empty on all 397. The number, the total length and the weeks of the first episode are 0 there (asked_if, as decision D122): 384, 388 and 397 cells were missing. The length of the first hospitalisation is a detail of a stay that did not take place and stays missing (as every detail after a no). 28 of the 397 also say yes to the hospitalisations of the past year (hospitalisations_12m), delivered as written. 51 inclusion visits hold no age at all: 25 of them hold a number (2 above 0) and 21 a total length, kept as recorded (decision R2, no shown_if). The number and the total length hold "more than" on 20 and 105 visits (censored_right: the form stops at 20 times and 30 months) and "Ne sais pas" on 44 and 110. The two lengths in weeks stop at 50. The ranges are those of the form (months 0 to 30, weeks 0 to 50); no cell lay beyond. Ever hospitalised is not asked. The export derives it from the number (face_sz_10: empty if the number is empty, N if it is 0, else Y), so a "Ne sais pas" in the number becomes a yes (R73, R134). The variable is listed after the number, with derived_from: the 44 visits that hold Y with no number get derived_doubt, and no value changes (37 of the 44 give an age at the first hospitalisation). With the gate it is 0 after "Pas d'hospitalisations": 1,812 of 2,251 inclusion visits (80.5%) were hospitalised at least once, where only the visits with a number counted before (1,812 of 1,867, 97%). The hospitalisations of the past year, asked at every visit, are in hospitalisations_12m.yaml. There is no hospitalisations_fu in SZ.
sz.difference: other columns and questions (the first hospitalisation, the first episode, ever hospitalised); the block is hidden after the age answer "Pas d'hospitalisations" (a hidden gate lists the other 88 answers) and ever hospitalised is derived by the export from the number; the past year is in hospitalisations_12m, asked at every visit

dr.notes: Hospitalisations over the whole life, at the inclusion visit: 327 visits, about half of the inclusions (8% to 83% by centre). The SZ schema of this name, with the columns that this cohort has: ever hospitalised (written Y and N), the age at the first hospitalisation, their number and their total length in months. The questions are those of form 116, which sits inside the mood-history form and is shown only for the disorder types 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6 (TYPE_TROUBLE_SPE); it prints no period and is read as the whole life. When the block is absent the form is not shown, which is not a "no": the section is empty on 279 of the 281 inclusions where the ages of the first episode are empty too. The yes/no is computed by the export from the number (0 gives N, more than 0 gives Y, face_dr_11 lines 25-31). 6 ages are written "00": they are on 6 of the 19 inclusions (15 of them from 2024) whose number is "00" and whose yes/no is empty, because the export casts the number (R73). An age of 0 or 00 is "not applicable" (32 cells, missing_code): all the 26 zero ages have a number of 0 (the 6 "00" ages used to be out_of_range). The total length in months is asked after the number (asked_if: 0 after a count of 0, +14 cells). It is typed in a box that keeps digits only (StyleChiffre), so a decimal comma is lost: "0,35" is stored "035" and is read as 0.35 months (codes). The months are typed numbers, not capped (maximum 72, 17 values at 20 or above): no censoring.
