recommendations.title: Whether the recommendations of the first evaluation were followed (follow-up visits)

bp.notes: Whether the recommendations made at the first evaluation were followed, for the drug treatment and for the other treatments, and why not. A follow-up form, asked at every follow-up visit and never at inclusion or screening. The question names the first evaluation, not the time since the last visit. 9,499 of the 11,686 follow-up visits answer for the drug treatment (81%) and 9,322 for the other treatments (80%). Of these, the drug recommendations are fully followed on 62% and the others on 53% (SZ: 64% and 55%). The answer is a judgement made at each visit: 1,446 of the 2,608 patients who answer at two visits or more give different answers for the drug treatment. Centre A stops filling this form from 2019 (80% of its follow-up visits in 2016-18, 57% in 2019-21, 20% in 2022-23, 33% from 2024; O40); without centre A, 84% to 89% of the follow-up visits answer in every period. Centre G answers "partly" much more often than the others (59% for the drugs and 79% for the other treatments, against 25% and 27%). The reason is shown only after "partly" or "not followed" (the form makes the reason depend on those two answers of the list). It is empty on 4% to 5% of those visits (128 of 3,586 for the drugs, 211 of 4,348 for the others), more often in recent years. 11 reasons stand under another answer: 9 after "fully followed" (5 for the drugs, 4 for the other treatments, all before 2014) and 2 drug reasons with no answer to the first question. They are delivered as recorded, with no shown_if (R2). "Other" is the most frequent reason (32% and 38%), and the form has no field to say which. The date typed on the form (date_traitement_semestriel) is not exported; the answers carry the visit date.

sz.notes: At the follow-up visits (about 2,270): were the recommendations of the first evaluation followed (fully, partly, not), and if not fully, why. Four kinds of recommendation: the drug treatment and the other treatments, as in FACE BP, and two that the SZ form adds, the medico-social and the somatic recommendations. The reason is shown only after "partly" or "not followed" (positions 1 and 2 of the answer in the field table). It is filled after those answers on 797 of 818 visits for the drug treatment, 992 of 1,016 for the other treatments, 500 of 520 for the medico-social recommendations and 697 of 732 for the somatic ones. Three reasons of the other treatments stand under another answer (two after "fully", one with no first answer): they are kept as recorded (decision R2, no shown_if); the other three kinds have none.

sick_leave_fu.title: Sick leave for a psychiatric disorder since the last visit (follow-up visits)

bp.notes: Sick leave for a psychiatric disorder since the last visit (the form asks "en lien avec un trouble psychiatrique", D94 (6)): whether there was any, how many, and their total duration in weeks. Asked at every follow-up visit. Yes/no answers are delivered as 1 and 0; "Non applicable" (the patient has no job: a third of the answers) is a missing code. These three columns are filled at the follow-up visits only and have no label in the dictionary (DM-7); the inclusion visit has columns of its own, read by sick_leave_v0.yaml. The inclusion question covers the 12 months before inclusion and names no cause: do not stack the two as one question. "Non applicable" is mostly the answer of patients without a job (78% of the answers of the patients retired at inclusion, 11% of those of the employed). But "Non" is also given by patients without one: 797 of the 4,447 "Non" come from patients unemployed, retired, on a disability pension or at home at inclusion. To study sick leave among workers, select on the work status, not on this answer. Asked only after a yes (asked_if). The number and the duration are filled only after a yes; they are 0 where the patient had no sick leave. Where the first answer is "Non applicable" they stay missing; one visit with no first answer holds both and is delivered as written. After a yes, 152 numbers and 175 durations are empty (115 visits have neither); the duration is empty on 6% of the yes until 2012, 14% from 2024 and 22% in centre C. 7 numbers and 11 durations are 0 after a yes and are delivered as written. The export keeps only the digits of the number and the duration (since January 2026; ebipolar_trt_sem.sql lines 51-61): a text answer has its digits run together ("1,5" gives 15), and an answer with no digit becomes empty, so no cell is flagged unparsed. R128 asks the export to keep the text as typed: weeks above 99 are 29, above 260 are 2 (the largest is 880,410), and all 70 above 52 are dated 2021 or earlier. Hard limits. A number above 52 is out of range (1 cell). A duration above 104 weeks (two years) is out of range (22 cells, D123). The 20 of 120 to 250 weeks are all longer than the time since the previous visit (33 weeks at the median). The 2 above 260, one of them 880,410, are digits run together by the export, not values typed by a centre. Since late 2021 the form accepts at most 52 weeks: no duration is above 52 after July 2021, and from October 2021, 47 of the 426 durations after a yes are exactly 52 (30 of them more than 52 weeks after the previous visit), so a 52 may stand for a longer leave. Before, 70 durations were above 52 (48 of them up to 104, delivered). 152 durations are longer than the time since the previous visit (90 by more than four weeks); they are delivered as written. Centre K wrote 9 of its 52 durations more than four weeks longer than that time (all before 2022), more than any other centre. The question is answered on 97.5% of the follow-up visits where the follow-up form is filled. The empty visits are visits without the form: centre A from 2022 (DM-6), and centre B in 2025-2026 (perhaps not yet entered). The numbers and durations are not winsorised (decision D54 in PROGRESS.md): most answers are 0 (72% of the numbers, 73% of the durations), so the 99th percentile would bring the rare high values down to it.

The psychiatric question is "since the last visit" and is the one of FACE BP (the same field of the application, the same words), under the BP names (BP D123). The somatic one is "in the last 12 months" and is added by SZ under names of its own. After a "no", the number and the length are 0 (asked_if), as in BP. Weeks. sick_leave_v0.title: Sick leave before inclusion (inclusion visit)

bp.section: LES 12 DERNIERS MOIS / DEPUIS LA DERNIERE VISITE
bp.notes: Sick leave in the 12 months before the inclusion visit (whether there was any, how many, their total duration in weeks) and on the day of the visit (on sick leave, and whether it is a long-term one). Yes/no answers are delivered as 1 and 0. "Non applicable" (the patient has no job: 23% of the answers for the year, 28% for the day of the visit) and "Ne sais pas" are missing codes. Filled at the inclusion visit only; the follow-up visits have columns of their own, read by sick_leave_fu.yaml. These questions name no cause, while the follow-up question asks only about sick leave for a psychiatric disorder: they are not one question. Where the answers come from. The 12 months are read from the inclusion diagnosis form, the day of the visit from the social form. The DSM-5 form asks the yes/no in the words of the social form ("Arrêt de travail au cours de l'année passée"), then the number and the weeks, with no condition. The DSM-IV form has no yes/no, and it shows the number and the weeks only after a mood episode in the past year. Most answers (3,327 of the 4,057 yes/no) are from DSM-IV inclusions, where an application script, social_diag.php, wrote the yes/no. It first copied the social form's answer where the number or the weeks were empty or 0 (a yes as "Ne sais pas", a no as 0, "Non applicable" as "NA", and the social weeks as the weeks). Then it wrote the yes/no from the number: "NA" gives "Non applicable", "Ne sais pas" or 1 to 20 give yes, and 0 gives no (4,087 of the 4,094 DSM-IV answers follow this rule). So 872 of the 917 "Ne sais pas" numbers are a social yes with no number, and numbers also appear after a "no" to a mood episode (723 of the 879 DSM-IV inclusions with no episode). The script also created DSM-IV records that hold only these answers (A30 of EXPORT_REQUESTS.md): 178 inclusions with no DSM label hold exactly its pairs (R69), by year 1, 3, 6, 18, 21, 18, 17, 12, 10, 14, 8 and 19 from 2009 to 2020, then 29 in 2021 and 2 in 2022: the script last ran around the start of 2022 (M14). Its hazards: it tests empty("0"), which is true in PHP, so a typed 0 (the number or the weeks) is overwritten by the value of the social form; it joins the two forms by patient, not by visit; and its last loop compares the number with 0 loosely, so a text that is no number (">20") equals 0 and gives "Non". 147 inclusions labelled DSM-5 also hold the pairs of the script (89 "Non" with 0, 37 "Non applicable" with "NA", 21 "Oui" with "Ne sais pas"); 127 of them are from 2022, after the script stopped, so the raters typed them (the DSM-5 form asks the yes/no, then the number), 15 of the 21 "Oui" with "Ne sais pas" among them (R70). sick_leave_12m is a score (D123): the stored yes/no, except yes on the 8 DSM-IV inclusions with ">20" sick leaves, where the script wrote no (PHP 7 reads ">20" as 0). These 8 carry score_mismatch; the stored answer is the check (sick_leave_12m_stored, not delivered). The 2 DSM-5 inclusions with ">20" are stored yes: the score agrees. A "no" gives 0 to an empty number or duration (asked_if), because no sick leave in the year means 0 sick leaves: 168 numbers and 1,316 durations. The forms do not hide the number and the weeks after a "no", and a filled cell is read whatever the yes/no says. After "Non applicable" that is 20 numbers and 80 durations (72 of them 0); after an empty yes/no, 49 numbers and 23 durations (12 of them 0). Number. A count of sick leaves, in a list of both diagnosis forms (0 to 20, ">20", "NA", "Ne sais pas"): "NA" (963 cells) and "Ne sais pas" (917) are missing codes, and ">20" is censored at 20 (10 visits: 8 DSM-IV inclusions where the script stored "Non", and 2 DSM-5 inclusions that say "Oui"). Where the number is empty on both diagnosis forms, the export takes the social form's weeks instead (R74). These weeks show only where they leave the list: the 40 numbers above 20 are out of range (the range is [0, 20], D123), 2 decimals are delivered as numbers and 2 texts end unparsed. Smaller week values cannot be told from a number. Most of the 49 numbers delivered after an empty yes/no are probably such weeks (46 of them from 2022). The number has two parents, the 12-month block of the diagnosis forms and the social form: a check that follows one parent counts the cells of the other as filled under a no or an empty parent. 321 inclusions hold the current answer of the social form and no yes/no for the 12 months (208 with no DSM label, 75 DSM-5, 38 DSM-IV); R74, which adds the social yes/no to the export, would recover up to that many. Duration, in weeks. 52 (the whole year) is the most frequent answer after 0 (379 and 307 cells). After a yes the duration is empty on 353 of the 2,434 inclusions (15%; 80 of 394, 20%, from 2022) and the number on 43 (41 of them from 2022); in two centres the duration is empty after 14 of 33 and 16 of 32 yes from 2022. A duration above 53 weeks cannot be about 12 months and is out of range (43 cells, up to 208), like the one negative value; 32 of these 43 patients are on sick leave at the visit, so they may be the length of a sick leave still running, counted from its start. 91 cells hold words ("2 semaines", "3 mois") and end unparsed, and 19 hold a "not applicable" word and are a missing code. anxiety_fu.title: Anxiety disorders (yearly follow-up visits)

bp.notes: One yes/no question (does the patient have an anxiety disorder), then one box per disorder and, for each, the age at onset and whether symptoms were present in the past month. Yes/no answers are delivered as 1 and 0; "unknown" (U) is a missing code. Where the block comes from. It sits in three tables of the application: the DSM-IV diagnosis form (psy_diag_psychiatrique), the DSM-5 diagnosis form (psy_diag_psychiatriquedsm5) and the yearly comorbidity form (psy_troubles_comorbides, the only one with the question "no change since the last visit?", rad_pas_dechangement). The export takes each column from the first non-empty of the three. Apart from the age of the eating disorder (eating_disorder_v0) and the two panic type boxes (anxiety_v0) the three are identical, so there is no split by version (decision D153 in PROGRESS.md). Two forms in the same columns (decisions D49, D50 and D84 in PROGRESS.md). The same questions are asked at the inclusion visit and at the yearly visits, never at the six-monthly ones, with the same wording: the form asks "does the patient have an anxiety disorder", in the present tense. The yearly form is the inclusion form again, shown after one more question, "no change since the last visit?", which the extraction does not hold (read in the application in November 2026, decision D84 in PROGRESS.md). A yearly answer is an update given at that visit: neither a history of the whole life nor strictly an answer about the time since the last visit. The data show that the two differ: 48% of the patients have an anxiety disorder at inclusion, 35% at the yearly visits; of the patients answered "yes" at inclusion, the first answer given a year or more later is "no" for 40% (435 of 1,081), in every centre. The two are therefore delivered as separate columns, ending in _v0 (inclusion visit) and _fu (yearly visits); visit_form says which form a visit used and is read from the visit label. The follow-up version holds 11,686 visits, of which 3,352 are six-monthly visits: 1 of them holds the tab, and the screening visits never do. anxiety_disorder_fu is answered (yes, no or unknown) on 4,660 of the 11,686 visits (40%), which is 56% of the 8,334 yearly visits. The boxes are shown only after a yes to the first question: 0 means "not ticked". The extraction holds twelve boxes (ten are delivered, see the panic disorder below). Under a "yes" they are all filled (2,480 of the 2,508 inclusion visits, 1,579 of the 1,593 yearly visits) or none is (28 and 14 visits, which stay missing): there is no box_list. After a "no" they are empty in the extraction (2,660 of the 2,665 inclusion visits, 2,966 of the 2,967 yearly ones) and are read as 0 (asked_if, decision D50): a patient with no anxiety disorder has none of them. Five inclusion visits and one yearly visit have a box ticked after a "no": kept as written. Where the first answer is unknown or empty the boxes stay missing, and so do the ages at onset and the "symptoms in the past month" after a "no": they have no value. Panic disorder (decisions D150 and D151). The export's two panic type columns hold another answer. ceoccurtroubpanago ("with agoraphobia") is 1 where the choice list of the form holds "Trouble panique" and "Phobie sociale", and ceoccurtroubpansago ("without agoraphobia") where it holds panic and not social phobia (face_bp_6_substances_comorbidites.sql, lines 21-22): among the 1,193 visits with the panic box ticked (804 at inclusion, 389 at the yearly visits), "with agoraphobia" equals the social phobia box on all 1,193. The form's own type list (chk_anxieux_trouble_panique_type) is not exported. Neither column is delivered (ignored.yaml; request R113), and the type of the panic disorder is not known. The box panic_disorder is built with ILIKE '%Trouble panique%', which also matches the label "Agoraphobie sans trouble panique": wherever the agoraphobia box is ticked the panic box is ticked too (230 of 230 at inclusion, 165 of 165 at the yearly visits). A panic detail (age at onset or past month) is filled on 81% of the panic visits with no agoraphobia box (466 of 574 at inclusion, 78% or 175 of 224 at the yearly visits) and on 24 of the 230 (10 of the 165) with it. panic_disorder is therefore a score: the stored box (panic_disorder_stored, not delivered) but missing where the agoraphobia box is 1 and neither the age nor the past month of the panic disorder is filled. That is 206 inclusion visits and 156 yearly visits (155 with nothing filled, and one whose only detail is the answer "unknown", a missing code); they get score_not_recomputed, and the flag log holds the stored 1. The visits that have a detail keep their 1. Among the inclusion visits with an anxiety disorder the box is ticked on 39% of them up to 2017 and 14% in 2025-2026 as stored, and on 33% and 13% as delivered. One set of details for the panic disorder. The form has an age at onset and a "symptoms in the past month" for each of its two panic types, and the export keeps both columns. They follow the form's real type list, not the two boxes (which hold social phobia): the earlier claim that clinicians fill either column whatever the box (44%) was an artefact of reading them against those boxes. They are read as one detail of the panic disorder: the first that is filled, with column_conflict where both are and differ. Seven visits have both ages (6 at inclusion, 1 at the yearly visits) and 5 carry column_conflict. Four columns have a row of the dictionary with a name only (rows 25 to 28: no label, no code, no field and no visit): the box "panic disorder" and the boxes of the last three disorders (the dictionary lists one of them as a section title). They are read here. Details. A detail is sometimes filled although its box is not ticked, and often empty although it is. 144 cells are filled under a box that is not ticked (108 at inclusion, 36 at the yearly visits; 137 under a box that is 0 or a "no", 7 under an empty box): 2 to 15 visits per disorder at inclusion and 0 to 12 at the yearly visits. They are delivered as recorded, with no shown_if where the parent is empty (rule R2 of the review). The export casts the ages with ^[0-9]+$, so "Ne sais pas", "<5" and ">89" become empty: the empty age under a ticked box (26% to 50% of the boxes at inclusion, 46% to 63% at the yearly visits, for the disorders with 100 boxes or more) mixes unknown and not answered (request R117). The ages of the yearly visits equal the age given at inclusion in 33% to 82% of the pairs by disorder: they are lifetime ages, not ages "since the last visit". Years and centres (O40, R20). The whole tab is often left empty: the four gates (anxiety, substances, eating disorders, somatoform disorders) are all empty on 1,091 of the 6,498 inclusion visits (17%; 453 of the 1,127 inclusions of 2022 to 2024) and on 3,611 of the 8,334 yearly visits (43%: at a yearly visit an empty section may mean "no change"). Four centres stop holding the tab. Share of their inclusions with the four gates empty, up to 2018, 2019-2021 and 2022-2024: centre A 9%, 33% and 87%; centre C 17%, 27% and 100%; centre B 1%, 8% and 35%; centre I 2%, 20% and 58%. A gate that is empty while another is answered is rare (4.2% of the inclusion visits and 2.3% of the yearly ones) and flat by year: there is no shortcut pattern as in the history tab (D83). The values are delivered as recorded: an empty gate is missing, not "no". Spreads of the QC table (decision D157 in PROGRESS.md). The share of the yearly visits that hold something of the tab (one of the four gates) is 37% to 48% in 2010-2013, 55% in 2014, 67% to 73% in 2015-2019, 61% to 62% in 2020-2021 and 39% to 47% from 2022: until 2013 centre D held it on none of its 143 yearly visits and centres C, E and K on 15% to 19%, and these four hold it on 51% to 57% of their yearly visits in 2014-2018; the decline from 2022 is the one above. The yes/no variables whose median is 1 in some years or centres (shift of 1) are shares of "yes" around one half: the first question at inclusion is "yes" for 33% to 69% by centre and 38% to 57% by year (groups of 20 answers or more; 43% to 49% in 2010-2020, 52% to 57% in 2021-2024), and the rise of the last years goes with the DSM-5 form of the inclusion visit (47% "yes" on the visits with DSM- IV criteria, 54% with DSM-5 criteria; whether the cause is the wording of the form or the patients is not known). The "symptoms in the past month" of the panic disorder are "yes" for 27% to 73% by centre and 39% to 75% by year at inclusion, and 50% to 81% by centre at the yearly visits. The ages at onset have a median up to half an interquartile range away from the overall one in some centres or years (by centre 10 to 15 years for the social phobia at the yearly visits, 16 to 24 for the PTSD, 8 to 15 for the specific phobia and 10 to 18 for the unspecified anxiety at inclusion; 14 to 20 by year for the generalised anxiety at inclusion; groups of 20 to 71 answers): a spread with no step, unexplained.

sz.notes: The first question of anxiety_v0 (does the patient have an anxiety disorder), at the follow-up visits: 2,265 of the 2,588 yearly visits are answered, 716 yes, 1,510 no, "Ne sais pas" is a missing code (39). The yes share is 24% to 42% in every year of visit. It is the only anxiety answer of the extraction, and the yearly form asks more: it holds the list of the anxiety disorders ticked (ten boxes) with the past-month question of each and the type of the panic disorder, as the BP form does. The export reads only rad_tb_anx of that form (the model has the list and the panic type commented out), and no eating-disorder answer either: 2,588 yearly visits hold no cell of anxiety or eating detail, which is why there is no eating_disorder_fu (request R115, the yearly comorbidity form is not exported). Unlike BP, the SZ form has no "no change" gate. An answer at a yearly visit is an update (BP D84), not lifetime and not strictly the time since the last visit. Of the patients with a yes at inclusion, 397 of 837 later answers (47%) are a no. The yes share of the yearly visits differs by centre: one centre answers yes on 10% of its yearly visits where it did on 41% of its inclusions, the nine others on 19% to 54% (centres with 20 answers or more).

sz.notes: One yes/no question (does the patient have an anxiety disorder; 2,168 of the 2,353 inclusion visits are answered, 826 yes), then, for the patients answered yes, a tree of questions. Yes/no answers are delivered as 1 and 0; "U" is a missing code. Another form than in FACE BP (decision D17 in PROGRESS.md). BP ticks one box per disorder. Here each disorder comes after a screening question, in columns that the dictionary does not list (rad_attaq_paniq, rad_peur_*): panic attacks, then panic disorder; fear of agoraphobic situations, then agoraphobia; a social fear, then social phobia; a specific fear, then specific phobia; obsessions, then obsessional disorder; compulsions, then obsessive-compulsive disorder; feeling nervous or anxious, then generalised anxiety. The data show the tree: a disorder is filled only after a yes to its screening question (295 of 299 cells, 265 of 271, 228 of 231, 152 of 156, 166 of 173, 169 of 172 and 343 of 349 for the generalised anxiety). Post-traumatic stress and the unspecified disorder have no screening question. The exact French wording of every question is in the application's field table (psy_diag_psychiatrique_sz_nom_champ), which the labels follow. The form has no age at onset for the anxiety disorders (BP has): the table lists none. The tree was introduced centre by centre from 2012 to 2016. Of the yes visits, 4% hold a question of the tree in 2012, 23% in 2013, 32% in 2014, 66% in 2015 and 96% to 100% from 2016: 664 of the 826 yes visits have one, 162 have none (155 of them dated 2015 or before, among them all those of 2010 and 2011). 123 inclusion visits of 2010 to 2015 hold 195 past-month answers and no disorder answer: kept as written. The export writes other fields of the form in five columns, so each is named for what it holds, not for the dictionary (request R114; the names were checked against the export model eschizo_psy_diag.sql and the field table of the application). The column named for the panic disorder without agoraphobia (ceoccurtroubpansago, written from rad_trouble_panique) holds the panic disorder, with or without agoraphobia: the form's type list (with or without agoraphobia) is not exported, and the variable is panic_disorder_v0 (99 yes). The two past-month columns of the panic disorder, one per type, are read as one, as in BP: each is empty on 71% (without) and 45% (with) of the yes visits, the two together on 17 of 99, and one visit holds both. The column named for the panic disorder with agoraphobia (ceoccurtroubpanago) is written from the screening question on agoraphobic fear (rad_peur_agoraphobie, 274 yes of 634 answers), which is read as agoraphobic_fear_v0: nothing is lost (O19 is answered by the source; no question to send), and the column is ignored. The column named for the obsessive-compulsive disorder (ceoccurtoc, written from rad_trouble_obsessionnel) holds the obsessional disorder (96 yes), the variable obsessional_disorder_v0; the obsessive-compulsive disorder is the column rad_trouble_compulsif (116 yes), the variable ocd_v0, and its past-month question is filled under it on 105 of 116 yes and on 0 of 56 no (under the obsessional disorder: 63 of 96 yes and 7 of 77 no). Under a yes the past-month question is empty on 13% of the visits for agoraphobia, 6% for social phobia, 3% for specific phobia, 9% for obsessive-compulsive disorder, 0% for post-traumatic stress, 13% for generalised anxiety, 10% for the unspecified disorder, and the medical condition on 95% (text) and 50% (past month). eating_disorder_fu.title: Eating disorders (yearly follow-up visits)

bp.notes: Whether the patient has an eating disorder, which one, whether symptoms were present in the past month and the age at onset. Yes/no answers are delivered as 1 and 0; "unknown" (U) is a missing code. Where the block comes from. It sits in three tables of the application: the DSM-IV diagnosis form (psy_diag_psychiatrique), the DSM-5 diagnosis form (psy_diag_psychiatriquedsm5) and the yearly comorbidity form (psy_troubles_comorbides, the only one with the question "no change since the last visit?", rad_pas_dechangement). The export takes each column from the first non-empty of the three. Apart from the age of the eating disorder (eating_disorder_v0) and the two panic type boxes (anxiety_v0) the three are identical, so there is no split by version (decision D153 in PROGRESS.md). Two forms in the same columns (decisions D49, D50 and D84 in PROGRESS.md). The same questions are asked at the inclusion visit and at the yearly visits, never at the six-monthly ones, with the same wording: the form asks "does the patient have an eating disorder", in the present tense. The yearly form is the inclusion form again, shown after one more question, "no change since the last visit?", which the extraction does not hold (read in the application in November 2026, decision D84 in PROGRESS.md). A yearly answer is an update given at that visit: neither a history of the whole life nor strictly an answer about the time since the last visit. The data show that the two differ: 20% of the patients have an eating disorder at inclusion, 14% at the yearly visits; of the patients answered "yes" at inclusion, the first answer given a year or more later is "no" for 49% (232 of 469). The two are therefore delivered as separate columns, ending in _v0 (inclusion visit) and _fu (yearly visits); visit_form says which form a visit used and is read from the visit label. The follow-up version holds 11,686 visits, of which 3,352 are six-monthly visits: 1 of them holds the tab, and the screening visits never do. eating_disorder_fu is answered (yes, no or unknown) on 4,639 of the 11,686 visits (40%), which is 56% of the 8,334 yearly visits. Age at onset (decision D152, request A57). The age is absent from the DSM-5 inclusion form: the export reads occurtcaagedebuttca from psy_diag_psychiatrique and psy_troubles_comorbides only. Among the inclusion visits with an eating disorder it is filled on 84% of the 787 DSM-IV visits and on 2 of the 232 DSM-5 visits: by year 75% to 96% up to 2021, then 3 of 231 from 2022 (all in the first quarter of 2022) and none after. At the yearly visits, which the comorbidity form serves, it is filled on 57% to 83% of the "yes" visits from 2013 to 2021 and on 38% to 53% from 2022. An empty age is therefore "not asked" on a DSM-5 inclusion, not "unknown", and the inclusion ages are not comparable across the two forms. There is no split by version (the other columns are identical): the age is delivered as recorded. Which one. "Night eating syndrome" exists in the DSM-5 form only: 3 inclusion visits (1 in 2022, 2 in 2025). The ages at onset are cast with ^[0-9]+$ by the export, so "Ne sais pas", "<5" and ">89" become empty (request R117): an empty age under a "yes" mixes unknown and not answered. Years and centres (O40, R20). The whole tab is often left empty: the four gates (anxiety, substances, eating disorders, somatoform disorders) are all empty on 1,091 of the 6,498 inclusion visits (17%; 453 of the 1,127 inclusions of 2022 to 2024) and on 3,611 of the 8,334 yearly visits (43%: at a yearly visit an empty section may mean "no change"). Four centres stop holding the tab. Share of their inclusions with the four gates empty, up to 2018, 2019-2021 and 2022-2024: centre A 9%, 33% and 87%; centre C 17%, 27% and 100%; centre B 1%, 8% and 35%; centre I 2%, 20% and 58%. A gate that is empty while another is answered is rare (4.2% of the inclusion visits and 2.3% of the yearly ones) and flat by year: there is no shortcut pattern as in the history tab (D83). The values are delivered as recorded: an empty gate is missing, not "no". Spreads of the QC table (decision D157 in PROGRESS.md). The share of the yearly visits that hold something of the tab (one of the four gates) is 37% to 48% in 2010-2013, 55% in 2014, 67% to 73% in 2015-2019, 61% to 62% in 2020-2021 and 39% to 47% from 2022: until 2013 centre D held it on none of its 143 yearly visits and centres C, E and K on 15% to 19%, and these four hold it on 51% to 57% of their yearly visits in 2014-2018; the decline from 2022 is the one above. The "symptoms in the past month" have a median of 1 in some years and centres (shift of 1): the share of "yes" is 46% to 72% by year and 48% to 69% by centre at inclusion (groups of 20 answers or more), around one half, with no step. The step of the age at onset is the one of the DSM-5 inclusion form above.

substance_fu.title: Substance use disorders (yearly follow-up visits)

sz.section: Troubles lié à une SUBSTANCE AU COURS DE LA VIE / VISITE
sz.notes: The questions of substance_v0 at the yearly visits (see substance_v0.yaml, which holds the paragraphs that the two schemas share): for each of the substances a box (a symptom of a use disorder over the whole life), whether the disorder is present at the time of the visit, and the age at onset of the disorder. 2,311 visits answer the first question (744 yes, 55 "Ne sais pas", read as missing codes). Eight substances have a box here; the stimulants and the other substances exist at follow-up only. Where the questions come from. The first question is the clinician's answer of the comorbidity form (rad_tb_subst, attached to the yearly visit), which the export turns into "Oui" when any box is yes, even where the clinician said no or unknown (export request R116: the clinician's own answer, rad_tb_subst_raw, is dropped). The box has two sources: the list of substances ticked by the clinician in the comorbidity form (chk_substances_type) and, from 2015, a yes of the addiction form (addicto), which is added. The yes share of the cannabis box rises from 10% to 19% of the answers in 2012-14 to 22% to 29% from 2015; cocaine from 0% before 2015 to 1% to 7% after. The "present at the time of the visit" answers are written Y/N, Oui/Non or 0/1 depending on the substance; the schema reads the three. Hidden gate. After a "no" to the opening question of the drug section (rad_add_4, delivered as illicit_drugs_over_ten_times in drug_use.yaml) the export leaves the six boxes of the sedatives, opiates, cocaine, hallucinogens, stimulants and other substances blank on 72 of the 1,600 yearly visits that say no (on the other 1,528 they are filled). They are delivered as 0 (asked_if on drugs_over_ten_times_fu, a hidden variable that is not delivered): 432 cells missing become 0. The end of each section (disorder at the time of the visit, age at onset) is shown only with two or more DSM-5 criteria, a count that is in another tab: an empty cell means "not asked", not "no" (see substance_v0.yaml). The module is used from 2015, not from 2012: the opening question of the alcohol section is answered on 14% of the yearly visits of 2014, 55% of 2015 and 68% to 90% after. One centre answers it on 53% of its yearly visits in 2016-18, 23% in 2019-21 and 11% in 2022-26 (inclusion visits: 77%, 31% and 34%), and another on 79% in 2019-21 and 33% from 2022: centre practice, unexplained. A follow-up answer is a yearly update (BP decision D84): not the whole life, and not strictly the time since the last visit. Of the patients with an alcohol box at 1 at inclusion, 147 of the 319 later answers are no (175 of 487 for cannabis, 201 of 633 for the first question). The age at onset still describes the whole life, as in BP: at follow-up it equals the age given at inclusion in 65 of 97 pairs for alcohol and 119 of 169 for cannabis. Three columns are not loaded. chk_substances_type lists the substances in one cell on 540 visits: every one of them is also a yes in its box, and the boxes hold more. sutrt_autre, the name of the other substance, is a copy of sutrt_autre_produit (drug_use.yaml) on every row. By year, the yes share of the first question is 17% of the 95 yearly visits to 2013 (the roll-out above), 36% in 2014-16, 34% to 35% in 2017-22 and 30% from 2023; the cannabis box is 12%, 26%, 25% to 26% and 23%. Inside the centres these shares move in both directions, and the median age at onset of the alcohol disorder is 17 to 24 by centre (centres with 20 answers or more): no known cause.
sz.difference: the first question is the clinician's answer, Oui where any box is yes; the boxes (Y and N) come from the clinician's list and, from 2015, from the addiction form; the questions on six substances are hidden by the opening drug question and read as 0 after a no; no type of disorder and no duration

substance_fu.description: Substance use disorders at the yearly follow-up visits: the inclusion questions asked again. FACE BP: one question (does the patient have, or have they had, a substance use disorder), then for each of eight substances a box, the type (abuse or dependence), symptoms in the past month, the age at onset and the cumulated duration in months. FACE SZ: for each of eight substances a box (a symptom of a use disorder over the whole life), whether the disorder is present at the time of the visit and the age at onset.
substance_fu.version: FACE BP: the yearly comorbidity form, with the DSM-IV names abuse and dependence. FACE SZ: the clinician's list of the comorbidity form, to which a yes of the addiction form is added from 2015.
substance_fu.reference: Abuse and dependence are the DSM-IV names (FACE BP); the FACE SZ boxes rest on the DSM-5 criteria of a substance use disorder (Hasin DS, O'Brien CP, Auriacombe M, et al. Am J Psychiatry 2013;170:834-851). The forms are forms of the application, with no publication of their own.
substance_fu.period: at the yearly visit: an update given at that visit of a question worded over the whole life; symptoms: past month (BP), at the time of the visit (SZ)
sources: respondent: schema notes (sz substance_fu): 'the clinician's answer of the comorbidity form'; BP form 'does the patient have, or have they had, a substance use disorder'
flags: A yearly answer is an update given at that visit, on the inclusion form asked again: neither a history of the whole life nor strictly an answer about the time since the last visit (BP decision D84).

The question is about the whole life ('has or has had'), so a yes should not become a no; it does. FACE BP: the first question is yes for 37% of the answers at inclusion and 23% at the yearly visits, and 41% of the yearly answers given more than nine months after a yes at inclusion are 'no'. FACE SZ: of the patients with an alcohol box at 1 at inclusion, 147 of the 319 later answers are 'no'.

Same names, different content in the two cohorts. FACE BP: the box is the clinician's tick of abuse or dependence, and '_last_month' is 'symptoms in the past month'. FACE SZ: the box is 'a symptom of a use disorder over the whole life (at least one DSM-5 criterion)' and '_last_month' is 'use disorder present at the time of the visit'. Stack with care (common_instruments.yaml).

FACE SZ: the box has two sources, the clinician's list and, from 2015, a yes of the addiction form: the yes share of the cannabis box rises from 10% to 19% of the answers in 2012-14 to 22% to 29% from 2015. The stimulants and the other substances have a box at follow-up only.

FACE SZ: the end of each section (disorder present at the time of the visit, age at onset) is shown only with two or more DSM-5 criteria, a count that is in another tab: an empty cell means 'not asked', not 'no'. Two or more of 11 criteria within 12 months is the published DSM-5 threshold (scale_reference_aq_general.md section 3: Confirmed (direct: Miller 2023)).

FACE BP: the yearly form opens with the question 'no change since the last visit?', which the extraction does not hold: an empty yearly section may mean 'no change'. In FACE BP the first question is empty on 37% of the yearly visits up to 2021 and on 58% from 2022 (five centres make the step).
Asked at the yearly visits only, never at the six-monthly ones. In FACE BP the share of yearly visits that hold the tab is 37% to 48% in 2010-2013, 67% to 73% in 2015-2019 and 39% to 47% from 2022.

The ages at onset and the durations still describe the whole life at the yearly visits, but are retyped: in FACE BP the age equals the one of the inclusion visit in 66% of the pairs and the duration in 38%.

FACE BP uses abuse and dependence, the DSM-IV names, in every year, also for the patients evaluated with DSM-5 criteria. DSM-5 merges the two into one disorder (scale_reference_aq_general.md section 3: Confirmed (abstract: Hasin 2013)).

common.note: As at inclusion, asked again at the yearly visit: an answer is a yearly update (BP D84). The first question is the clinician's answer ('Oui' where any box is yes). SZ has no type of disorder and no duration.

The share of the yearly visits that answer the first question is 36% to 45% in 2010-2013, 55% in 2014, 66% to 71% in 2015-2019, 60% to 62% in 2020-2021 and 37% to 45% from 2022; until 2013 centre D held the tab (one of the four gates) on none of its 143 yearly visits and centres C, E and K on 15% to 19%, and these four hold it on 51% to 57% of their yearly visits in 2014-2018. The yes/no variables whose median is 1 in some years or centres (shift of 1) are shares of "yes" around one half: besides the first question and the alcohol "past month" by centre above, the alcohol "past month" at the yearly visits is "yes" for 26% to 55% by year and the cannabis one for 23% to 50% by year (groups of 20 answers or more). The duration of the alcohol disorder is a number typed freely (interquartile range of about 100 months) on small groups: at inclusion its median goes from 30 to 143 months between years (20 to 84 answers a year; 143 in 2026 on 20 answers, 82 in 2024, 66 in 2013) and at the yearly visits from 36 to 105 months between the 7 centres with 20 answers or more, one centre being at 105: a spread with no step, unexplained.

sz.section: Troubles lié à une SUBSTANCE AU COURS DE LA VIE / VISITE
sz.notes: For each of six substances (alcohol, sedatives, cannabis, opiates, cocaine, hallucinogens): a box (a symptom of a use disorder over the whole life), whether the disorder is present at the time of the visit, and the age at onset of the disorder. Yes/no answers are delivered as 1 and 0. A first question (substance_disorder_v0) sums the boxes up. SZ has no type of disorder (abuse or dependence) and no cumulated duration, which BP has; the stimulants and the other substances have no box at inclusion. Where the questions come from. The form is one block of the application, in three tables: the diagnostic form, the comorbidity form (attached to the yearly visit only, never to the inclusion visit) and the addiction form (addicto, at both). At inclusion the diagnostic form has no substance question, so everything here comes from the addiction form: the box is its question 7a or 8a, "a symptom of a use disorder over the whole life". It is yes on 293 of the 303 inclusion visits that tick at least one of the eleven DSM-5 criteria of alcohol and on 8 of the 697 that tick none (the criteria are in auto_questionnaire/dsm5_alcohol.yaml and the six other dsm5_ schemas). The hallucinogen box at inclusion is the question on other products (rad_add_autre7a). hallucinogen_onset_age_v0 has no cell; it is kept to match the follow-up. The "present at the time of the visit" answers are written Y/N, Oui/Non or 0/1 depending on the substance; the schema reads the three. The first question is derived by the export, not asked (open question O20, answered by the source: there is no question to send; export request R116, which also asks for the clinician's own answer, rad_tb_subst_raw, dropped by the export). At inclusion it is "Oui" when any box is yes (590 visits), "Non" when the six boxes are no (18) and "Ne sais pas" otherwise (975 of the 1,583 answered visits). Of these 975, 925 have a "no" to rad_add_4 (next paragraph): the export leaves the drug boxes blank after it, so "all six no" is never reached. "Ne sais pas" is a missing code, as everywhere, and nothing is guessed. The variable is 97% yes (590 of 608 valid answers): it does not measure the disorder. Hidden gate. The opening question of the drug section (rad_add_4, "more than ten times in your life: illicit drugs or medicines taken without a prescription", delivered as illicit_drugs_over_ten_times in drug_use.yaml) shows the questions on sedatives, heroin, cocaine, opiates and other products only after a yes. After a "no" the export leaves the boxes of the sedatives, opiates, cocaine and hallucinogens blank (1,354, 1,355, 1,354 and 1,355 of the 1,355 inclusion visits that say no). They are delivered as 0 (asked_if on drugs_over_ten_times_v0, a hidden variable that is not delivered): 5,418 cells missing become 0. The yes share of the four boxes falls from 14.9, 7.7, 26.3 and 15.7% to 2.2, 1.2, 3.7 and 2.0%, close to the follow-up shares (1.7, 1.6, 3.1 and 2.2%). The end of each section (disorder at the time of the visit, age at the first use, age at onset, longest abstinence, family history, craving) is shown only with two or more DSM-5 criteria, a count that is in another tab. Age at the first use, alcohol: filled on 0 of 1,500 visits with none or one criterion and on 85% of 546 with two or more; cannabis 1 of 433 and 83% of 835; cocaine 0 of 94 and 83% of 98; sedatives 0 of 41 and 82% of 60; opiates 0 of 18 and 91% of 34. An empty cell means "not asked", not "no"; it is not encoded. The module is used from 2015, not from 2012. The opening question of the alcohol section (the other sections are the same) is answered on 9% of the inclusion visits of 2012, 18% of those of 2014, 48% of 2015 and 83% to 93% from 2016 (6%, 17%, 52% and 84% of the inclusion and yearly visits together). The alcohol box is blank under a yes to that question on 5% to 8% of the inclusion visits of 2015 to 2017 and 14% to 23% from 2018. One centre answers the opening question on 77% of its inclusion visits in 2016-18, 31% in 2019-21 and 34% in 2022-26 (at follow-up 53%, 23% and 11%), and another on 79% of its follow-up visits in 2019-21 and 33% from 2022: centre practice, unexplained. Two periods in the same columns, as in FACE BP (BP decisions D49, D50 and D84; checked on the SZ data, decision D17 in PROGRESS.md). At inclusion the questions are about the whole life; a follow-up answer is a yearly update (D84): not the whole life, and not strictly the time since the last visit. Of the patients with an alcohol box at 1 at inclusion, 147 of the 319 later answers are no (175 of 487 for cannabis, 201 of 633 for the first question). The two are delivered as separate columns ending in _v0 and _fu; visit_form says which form a visit used. The export casts the ages with a pattern of digits: a typed "Ne sais pas" becomes an empty cell; 99 and 999 are read as missing codes (1 cell at inclusion). The ages run from 5 to 45 and none is above the patient's age. By year and centre. The sedatives box shows the step of drug_use.yaml: one centre ticks it on 18 of its 129 answers to 2016 (14%) and on 6 of 274 since (2%), the other centres on 3 of 163 (2%) and 8 of 1,023 (1%). The yes share of the cannabis box is 34% to 35% of the answers of 2014 to 2022 and 22% from 2023, and it falls in each of the four centres that have 20 answers in both 2020-22 and 2023-26: no known cause. The dictionary lists agedebut_autre (age at onset, other substances), which the extraction does not have.
sz.difference: the first question is derived by the export from the boxes, not asked; the boxes (Y and N) are the question of the addiction form on a symptom of a use disorder over the whole life; the questions on four substances are hidden by the opening drug question and read as 0 after a no; no type of disorder, no duration, six substances at inclusion

substance_v0.description: Substance use disorders at the inclusion visit. FACE BP: one question (does the patient have, or have they had, a substance use disorder), then for each of eight substances a box, the type (abuse or dependence), whether symptoms were present in the past month, the age at onset and the cumulated duration in months. FACE SZ: for each of six substances a box (a symptom of a use disorder over the whole life), whether the disorder is present at the time of the visit and the age at onset.
substance_v0.version: FACE BP: the block of the DSM-IV and DSM-5 diagnosis forms, with the DSM-IV names abuse and dependence. FACE SZ: built by the export from the addiction form (at least one DSM-5 criterion), used from 2015.
substance_v0.reference: Abuse and dependence are the DSM-IV names (FACE BP); the FACE SZ boxes rest on the DSM-5 criteria of a substance use disorder (Hasin DS, O'Brien CP, Auriacombe M, et al. Am J Psychiatry 2013;170:834-851). The forms are forms of the application, with no publication of their own.
substance_v0.period: lifetime ('has or has had', under the title 'over the whole life'); symptoms: past month (BP), at the time of the visit (SZ)
sources: respondent: BP form 'does the patient have, or have they had, a substance use disorder'; the SZ boxes come from the addiction form, whose respondent the notes do not state
flags: Same names, different content in the two cohorts. FACE BP: the box is the clinician's tick of abuse or dependence, and '_last_month' is 'symptoms in the past month'. FACE SZ: the box is 'a symptom of a use disorder over the whole life (at least one DSM-5 criterion)' and '_last_month' is 'use disorder present at the time of the visit'. Stack with care (common_instruments.yaml).
FACE SZ: substance_disorder_v0 cannot be used: the export derives it from the boxes and writes 'Ne sais pas' (read as missing) on 975 of the 1,583 answered inclusion visits (R116).

FACE SZ: the module is used from 2015, not from 2012 (its opening alcohol question is answered on 9% of the inclusion visits of 2012, 48% of 2015 and 83% to 93% from 2016). The sedative, opiate, cocaine and hallucinogen boxes are read as 0 after a no to the opening drug question (illicit_drugs_over_ten_times, instrument drug_use).

FACE SZ: the end of each section (disorder present at the time of the visit, age at onset) is shown only with two or more DSM-5 criteria, a count that is in another tab: an empty cell means 'not asked', not 'no'. Two or more of 11 criteria within 12 months is the published DSM-5 threshold (scale_reference_aq_general.md section 3: Confirmed (direct: Miller 2023)).
FACE SZ: six substances at inclusion (no stimulants, no other substances); the hallucinogen box at inclusion is the question on other products, and hallucinogen_onset_age_v0 has no cell.

Inclusion and yearly answers are delivered apart (_v0 and _fu): a later answer often says 'no' after a yes although the question is about the whole life (BP: 41% of the yearly answers given more than nine months after a yes at inclusion).

FACE BP uses abuse and dependence, the DSM-IV names, in every year, also for the patients evaluated with DSM-5 criteria. DSM-5 merges the two into one disorder (scale_reference_aq_general.md section 3: Confirmed (abstract: Hasin 2013)).

FACE BP: a ticked box often has empty details, and an empty detail is not 'not asked': at inclusion the type is empty for 22% of the ticked boxes and the duration for 42%; all four details are empty on 5% to 9% of the boxes of 2011 to 2016 and on 32% to 40% of those of 2018 to 2021.

FACE BP: the first question is empty on 14% of the inclusion visits up to 2021 and on 35% from 2022 (three centres make the step); an empty answer is missing, not 'no'. The boxes are 0 after a no and missing where the first answer is unknown or empty.
By year in FACE SZ: the cannabis box is yes on 34% to 35% of the answers of 2014 to 2022 and 22% from 2023; the sedative box falls after 2016 in one centre; no known cause.

common.note: The disorder, 'in the last month' and the age at onset of each substance are under the same names. In SZ the first question (any substance use disorder) is derived by the export, not asked: 'not known' on 975 of 1,583 inclusions, it cannot be used (R116); the boxes mean 'a symptom of a use disorder (at least one DSM-5 criterion)'; the sedative, opiate, cocaine and hallucinogen boxes are 0 after a 'no' to the opening drug question; the module is used from 2015. SZ has no type of disorder (abuse or dependence) and no duration, and six substances. DR uses the MINI. ASP's substance_use (clinician's list, inclusion only, form 202) carries the same names for alcohol, cannabis, cocaine, stimulants and hallucinogens: the 0/1 items are 0 after a no to the opening question as in BP, and the onset ages are the age at onset of the disorder; its benzodiazepines (narrower than the sedatives), solvents, tobacco and steroids have names of their own, it has no opiates, no 'last month' and no duration (its 'past or current' status is another question).

tobacco.title: Tobacco

bp.notes: The tobacco status at each visit, with the pack-years, the age when the patient started smoking and the age when they stopped. Filled at the inclusion visit and at every follow-up visit; the answer describes the day of the visit, so there is one form (decision D49 in PROGRESS.md). The shares of the status are close at inclusion and at follow-up (non-smokers 43.5% of 6,002 visits and 50.9% of 10,350) and the pack-years rise between the two (median +0.5 from the inclusion visit to the last later visit, 1,327 patients): the status is the one of the day and the details are cumulative over the life. "Statut inconnu" is a missing code (85 visits). The form leaves the details of a non-smoker blank (in the raw cell, never 0): under "Non fumeur" 3 of the 7,876 visits carry a detail, and one current smoker has a stop age. Two of the three belong to patients who are ex-smokers at another visit, so the status is the likelier error. They stay as recorded, no shown_if (decision D145 in PROGRESS.md). The details are filled for the smokers and the ex-smokers only: 75% and 84% of the raw cells, pack-years valid for 73% and 80% of them. "Non fumeur" is not "never smoked". Between consecutive visits of a patient, ex-smoker to non-smoker happens in 349 of 1,194 pairs (29%), current smoker to non-smoker in 248 of 4,034 (6%) and non-smoker to current or ex-smoker in 377 of 4,932. In 264 of the 284 pairs of the last kind that have a start age (253 at least a year before), the start age is at or before the age at the earlier visit: the earlier "non-smoker" was wrong. 957 of the 7,876 non-smoker visits (12%) are dated after the first visit at which the patient was a current or an ex-smoker, and 194 patients are ex-smokers at one visit and current smokers at a later one. Never derive 0 pack-years from "Non fumeur". Pack-years. Typed freely: the formula of the form (packs a day times years) is commented out of its script. 101 cells hold "NA" (a missing code) and 34 hold words or a fraction, which end unparsed. A value above 200 is out of range (29 cells, up to 51,050): 200 pack-years is four packs a day for fifty years. 83 typed values up to 200 are above three packs a day for the years the patient smoked (69 after the winsorisation), and 42 visits give less than 1 pack-year for a patient who smoked 10 years or more (they may be packs a day typed in the field). The values are winsorised at 1% and 99% like every number of the package: 116 cells change (61 values from 73 to 200 become 72; 55 values below 0.25, 7 of them zeros, become 0.25), so the delivered column is not the typed one. They also change between visits: the pack-years of a patient fall between two visits in 22% of 3,305 pairs (by more than 5 in 10%), and the start age takes more than one value for 44% of the 1,772 patients who give it twice or more. Ages. 4 visits (4 patients) give a start age more than a year after the age at the visit, 10 visits (6 patients) a stop age more than a year after it, and 4 visits (4 patients) a stop age before the start age; delivered as written. Fill by centre. From 2022 the pack-years of the smokers and ex-smokers are filled on 16% of the visits of one centre (73% before) and 45% of another (70% before), and the status is empty on 32% of the visits of the first one (13% before). A centre with 22 typed pack-year values has a median of 32.5 against 7.5 to 15.3 in the centres with 100 values or more (21 delivered values, median 30, against 7 to 15: the shift of the QC table). The status is filled on 67% to 84% of the follow-up visits of 2009-2013, 92% to 94% of those of 2014-2016, and 86% to 94% afterwards except in 2020 (76%: 63% in the second quarter and 71% in the fourth), at inclusion on 88% to 98% in every year; the screening visits never hold it. The cause of the dip of 2020 and of the first years is not known (D157). The form also asks whether a nicotine substitute is used, and which; the extraction does not hold it (R120 of EXPORT_REQUESTS.md).

sz.notes: Smoking status, pack-years and the ages at which the patient started and stopped smoking (the BP schema), and five questions that the SZ form adds: cigarettes per day in the last 12 months, age at the first cigarette, longest abstinence in months, a first-degree relative with a tobacco use disorder, and a craving score from 0 to 10 (the maximum in the last week). Asked at inclusion and at follow-up (4,439 visits with a status: 2,087 current smokers, 614 ex-smokers, 1,728 non-smokers, 10 unknown, a missing code). The status is the one of the day of the visit and the details are cumulative over the life, so there is one form, as in BP (decision D49). A non-smoker has no detail. The form hides the whole tobacco block for a non-smoker, the five questions of SZ included, and the export leaves the cells empty (never 0): under "Non fumeur" none of the three core details is filled, and 10 cells of the five questions are, on 5 of the 1,728 visits (2 of the 5 patients are smokers or ex-smokers at another visit). They are kept as recorded (no shown_if). The details are filled for the smokers and ex-smokers only: pack-years for 70% of the current smokers and 62% of the ex-smokers, the start age 82% and 77%, the stop age 77% of the ex-smokers. The five questions are asked only of current and ex-smokers and used from 2015, not from 2012: they are filled on 3% to 13% of the visits of the current and ex-smokers in 2012 to 2014, 46% to 48% in 2015 and 65% to 89% since. They come as a block: all five are filled on 1,499 of the 2,701 smoker visits. Among the ex-smokers the number of cigarettes per day in the last 12 months is 0 for 74% of the answers (314 of 422). "Non fumeur" is not "never smoked". Between two consecutive visits that have a status, an ex-smoker is a non-smoker on 65 of 310 pairs and a current smoker on 32 of 996; a non-smoker is a current or ex-smoker on 77 of 872. In 39 of the 41 such pairs that carry a start age the start age is at or before the age at the earlier visit, so the earlier "Non fumeur" was wrong. 52 patients start again after an ex-smoker visit. Never derive 0 pack-years from "Non fumeur". Pack-years fall between two consecutive values on 25% of 687 pairs (11% by more than 5), and the start age changes in 52% of the 510 patients with two or more values: the details are not kept from one visit to the next. 999 and 9999 mean "does not know" in the pack-years and in the abstinence (22 cells: 8 and 14), 99 in an age (2 cells, in the age at the first cigarette only). 14 pack-years above 200 are out of range (5 of them are 365), and 4 cigarettes a day above 100. The pack-years, the cigarettes per day and the abstinence are winsorised at the 1st and 99th percentiles, as everywhere (18, 16 and 15 cells change; the largest pack-year delivered is 86): they are not delivered as written. 2 start ages and 1 age at the first cigarette are above the patient's age. The questions of the form on the age of the strongest dependence and on a drug treatment of the tobacco use disorder are not in the extraction (export request R120). The Fagerström test is in auto_questionnaire/fagerstrom.yaml. By year the status drifts without a step: current smokers are 53% of the visits of 2014-16, 52% of 2017-19, 43% of 2020-22 and 36% from 2023, ex-smokers 9%, 13%, 18% and 20% (3% to 23% by centre). Among the smokers the median of cigarettes per day is 15 to 2019 and 10 since 2020, and the longest abstinence, a question over the whole life, has a median of 1 month to 2019, 2 in 2020-22 and 6 from 2023 (0 to 5 by centre); the family history is yes on 41% to 83% by centre: no known cause.
sz.difference: five more questions (cigarettes per day in the last 12 months, age at the first cigarette, abstinence, family history, craving), asked of the current and ex-smokers from 2015, and 999 as a missing code of the pack-years

dr.notes: The BP schema with the codes of this extraction (1 non-smoker, 2 ex-smoker, 3 current smoker). One schema: the status is that of the day of the visit and the details (pack-years, ages) are cumulative, so there is no `_v0` and `_fu`; the shares at inclusion and at follow-up are close (non-smokers 54% and 53%, current smokers 32% and 32%). It comes from the nurse's record (form 112), which holds these four questions and no other on tobacco. Filled at 1,310 visits (54% non-smokers, 32% smokers, 15% ex-smokers; BP 48%, 40% and 12%): 538 of 634 inclusions (85%; 70% to 100% by year, the lowest in 2025-26) and 771 of 925 follow-up visits (83%, at 6 months, 1, 1.5, 2 and 4 years). The dictionary lists v0, 6 months and 1 year only. The form hides and clears the details by status: a non-smoker has no pack-years, no start age and no stop age; a current smoker has no stop age; an ex-smoker has the three. A hidden box is saved empty, never 0: 0 of 701 non-smoker visits hold a detail and 0 of 417 current smokers a stop age. Nothing to encode (no `asked_if`, no `shown_if`). The details of a smoker are missing when the rater left them empty: pack-years are valid for 88% of the current smokers and 91% of the ex-smokers (BP 73% and 80%), the start age for 92% and 95%, the stop age for 94% of the ex-smokers. Pack-years. The form states the formula (cigarettes a day divided by 20, times the years of smoking) in a text and computes nothing; the box takes digits only, three characters, so the values are whole numbers (a half pack-year cannot be typed). One value, 225, is above 200 (out_of_range: 200 pack-years is four packs a day for fifty years) and one cell, "2,", is unparsed. The delivery winsorises the tails (limits 1 and 105), as in BP and SZ: 7 cells change, five values of 115 to 187 become 105 and two zeros become 1 (they are not "delivered as written"). "Non-smoker" is not "never smoked". Between two consecutive visits of a patient (760 pairs): ex-smoker then non-smoker 21 of 125, current smoker then non-smoker 8 of 249, non-smoker then current or ex-smoker 19 of 386. In 15 of the 15 last pairs that give a start age, the age is at or before the age at the earlier visit, so the earlier "non-smoker" was the likelier error; 36 of the 701 non-smoker visits (27 patients) are dated after the first visit of the patient as a current or ex-smoker (BP 12%). 12 patients restart (ex-smoker, then current smoker). Never derive 0 pack-years from "non-smoker". The details are retyped at each visit and are not constant: pack-years fall between two visits in 97 of 315 pairs (31%; by more than 5 in about 15%) and the start age takes more than one value for 63 of the 124 patients who have it twice or more (51%). Delivered as recorded. Years and centres (report panels). A step since 2021: the non-smokers are 50% of the visits until 2020 and 64% since (50% and 63% of the inclusions, 50% and 64% of the follow-up visits; 49% and 60% with the centres weighted as before 2021; 9 of 12 centres go up, one is level, two go down), while the details are given less often: pack-years are valid for 93% of the smokers until 2020 and 76% since, the start age for 96% and 82%, the stop age for 97% and 81%, and the status is filled on 90% and 76% of the inclusions. No cause is known (a real fall of smoking among the patients and a form filled with less care both fit: DM-8). The median pack-years of the smokers is 30 in 2013 (25 visits), 21 in 2014 and 14.5 to 19 a year after; the year shift of the QC table (0.6 interquartile range) is that first group, and the age of the smokers does not move (median 52 to 56 years in 2013 to 2019). The centres differ: non-smokers 37% to 71% of the visits, current smokers 15% to 48%, median pack-years 14 to 27 (nine centres with 20 values or more), the status filled on 36% to 100% of the inclusions; one centre holds no status at any of its 70 visits since 2017. The data cannot tell a rater habit from the case mix.
dr.difference: the status is stored 1, 2 and 3 and has no "unknown" answer; the form has these four questions only

asp.notes: Tobacco status, recorded from 2020: 563 inclusion visits (237 children). The codes are those of FACE DR: 1 for a non-smoker (492), 2 for an ex-smoker (22), 3 for a current smoker (49). The data agree: the age when the patient stopped is filled only with the code 2, and the dose and the starting age only with the codes 2 and 3. The dose (sudose_cig, 47 visits) is called pack-years in FACE DR. Here its median is 11 and 11 values are above 60, which is not possible for patients this young: the thesaurus says pack-years, so these values are entry errors or another unit (open question O10). All 11 values above 60 come from centre B. B's 20 values have a median of 73 (the other centres 3.8 to 10), and 13 of the 16 of them whose years of smoking are known mean more than a pack a day for every year smoked, against 3 of the 27 of the other centres. B's values are not the cigarettes a day of the Fagerström questionnaire (2 of 11 in its class). The unit is not known (O10; question M83). The three values above 200 are out of range; the others are delivered as typed. The clinician's list of comorbidities (evaluation_medicale, substance_use) asks the age at the start of smoking as well (utitabag, 68 inclusion visits) and delivers it as `smoking_start_age_clinician`: this examination keeps `smoking_start_age`, the name that BP, SZ and DR give to the same question. The two ages are equal on 12 of the 13 visits that have both. SZ's `tobacco_first_age` is the age at the first cigarette, another question: the three names stay apart. Same instrument as in FACE DR, in other columns. Years and centres (definition of done, D88; centres lettered as in D77, A the children's centre): the pack-years of centre B (above) are the only step; no other variable has a group of 20 values with a shift.
asp.difference: the status, the pack-years and the two ages, as in BP, in other columns and with the answers coded 1 to 3; the pack-years are doubtful (O10)

tobacco.description: The tobacco status at the visit (non-smoker, current smoker, ex-smoker), with the pack-years and the ages at which the patient started and stopped smoking. In the four cohorts. FACE SZ adds five questions: cigarettes per day in the last 12 months, age at the first cigarette, longest abstinence, a first-degree relative with a tobacco use disorder and a craving score from 0 to 10.
tobacco.period: status: the day of the visit; pack-years and ages: cumulative over the life; SZ: cigarettes per day in the last 12 months, craving in the last week
sources: schema notes (bp, sz, dr and asp tobacco)
flags: 'Non-smoker' is not 'never smoked': a patient is a non-smoker at one visit and a smoker or ex-smoker at another (12% of the non-smoker visits of FACE BP are dated after a visit as a smoker or ex-smoker). The details of a non-smoker are empty, never 0: never derive 0 pack-years from 'non-smoker'.

The pack-years and the ages are retyped at each visit and are not constant: in FACE BP the pack-years fall between two visits in 22% of the pairs and the start age takes more than one value for 44% of the patients who give it twice or more (SZ 25% and 52%, DR 31% and 51%).
The delivered pack-years are not the typed ones: they are winsorised at the 1st and 99th percentiles (FACE BP: 61 values from 73 to 200 become 72).

FACE ASP records tobacco from 2020 and its pack-years are doubtful (values that are not possible for patients this young, from one centre; the unit is not known, open question O10): compare the pack-years of BP, SZ and DR only (common_instruments.yaml).
FACE SZ: the five added questions are asked of current and ex-smokers only and are used from 2015 (filled on 3% to 13% of the smoker visits in 2012 to 2014, 65% to 89% since 2016).

Steps with no known cause. FACE DR: non-smokers are 50% of the visits until 2020 and 64% since, while the details are given less often. FACE SZ: current smokers go from 53% of the visits of 2014-16 to 36% from 2023. FACE BP: the status is filled on 67% to 84% of the follow-up visits of 2009-2013 and 76% in 2020, against 86% to 94% in the other years.

Who records the answers is stated for FACE DR only (the nurse's record, form 112). In FACE DR the form shows the pack-year formula and computes nothing; in FACE BP the formula is commented out of the script.

Not in the extraction: the nicotine substitute (BP, R120); the age of the strongest dependence and a drug treatment of the tobacco use disorder (SZ, R120). The Fagerström test is another instrument (fagerstrom).

common.note: The status (non-smoker, smoker, ex-smoker), the pack-years and the two ages are in the four cohorts, with the same three answers. ASP records tobacco from 2020, and its pack-years are doubtful (ASP O10): compare the pack-years of BP, SZ and DR only. ASP's clinician list also asks the age at the start of smoking (smoking_start_age_clinician, equal on 12 of 13 visits); SZ's tobacco_first_age is the first cigarette: the three names are not joined. 'Non fumeur' is not 'never smoked': a patient answers non-smoker at one visit and smoker or ex-smoker at another (about 12% of the non-smoker visits of BP follow a visit of a smoker), so no pack-year is 0 by derivation. SZ asks five more questions, from 2015.

cssrs_fu.title: Columbia Suicide Severity Rating Scale, suicidal ideation, since the last visit (follow-up visits)

bp.notes: The ideation part of the Columbia Suicide Severity Rating Scale (C-SSRS) at the follow-up visits, about the time since the last visit: five yes/no questions of rising severity, delivered as 1 (yes) and 0 (no), the most severe ideation as rated (1 to 5) and five ratings of its intensity, with their sum. The extraction holds no behaviour section and no stored total. One schema per form (decision D125 in PROGRESS.md). The application has one C-SSRS form for the inclusion and the follow-up visits; its instruction sets the period ("Depuis la semaine dernière pour une évaluation initiale ou depuis la dernière visite lors d'un suivi"): the past week at an initial evaluation, the time since the last visit at a follow-up. The inclusion answers are cssrs_v0 (variables in _past_week, decision D158). visit_form says which form a visit used; it is read from the visit label. The names are those of the DR follow-up schema, and the two are stacked with care (common_instruments.yaml); DR also has the behaviour section. Time frame (decision D159, rule R14a). The follow-up answers are about the time since the last visit, as the instruction says: they are not a yearly update (D84 does not apply to the suicide forms). The suicide forms have no question "is there a change since the last visit?" (rad_pas_dechangement is in other sections), so an empty follow-up form means that the form was not done, not "no change". 2,355 visits answer the first question (2,406 any question): 3 in 2019 and 2020, 37 in 2021, 471 to 564 a year in 2022 to 2025 and 285 in 2026 (to November). From 2022 the form is filled at 60% to 78% of the follow-up visits. The wish to be dead is answered yes on 680 visits (29%), active suicidal thoughts on 425 of 2,374 (18%). The answers are about the time since the last visit: from 2024 the wish to be dead agrees with isf02_since_visit of the same visit on 804 of 894 visits. The years 2022 and 2023 are delivered. Unlike the follow-up suicide questions (isf_since_visit, D88), the C-SSRS has no peak in these years: the wish to be dead is yes on 25% (2022) and 26% (2023) of the visits, against 30% to 35% from 2024. The C-SSRS takes the place of the five suicide questions at three centres from 2022 (one centre) or 2024 (two). At one more centre the whole tab is empty at most visits of 2023: 148 of its 191 follow-up visits hold neither the five questions nor the C-SSRS (77%, against 27% to 36% in each of 2019 to 2022 and 2024), and 137 of these 148 visits hold a MADRS (at the other centres, 35 of the 248 visits that hold neither do): the visit took place and the tab was left empty (O40, DM-6). Questions 3 to 5 (a method, an intent, a plan) are asked only after a yes to question 2. After a no they are 0 (asked_if): 1,949 visits. They were asked on 415 to 417 visits. The most severe ideation (428 visits; range 1 to 5) and the five intensity ratings (598 to 613) are to be rated after a yes to question 1 or 2 (718 visits). The application does not enforce it: 40 visits rate the most severe ideation or an intensity item although both questions are no (33 an intensity item), and 23 of them get an intensity sum; delivered as rated. After a yes, the most severe ideation is empty on 312 of the 718 visits and the five ratings on 141. The most severe ideation as rated differs from the highest question answered yes on 187 of the 428 visits that rate it: on 21 every question is no and on 1 none is answered, and of the 406 with a yes it is the highest on 241, higher on 106 and lower on 59; on 33 visits it names a level 3 to 5 although question 2 is no. It is delivered as rated. Intensity: code 0 of controllability ("does not try to control") and of deterrents and reasons ("does not apply") is not the mild end of the scale. The sum counts it as 0, the official rule (33, 72 and 84 cells; 127 of the 588 sums hold one). The sum is given where the five ratings are: 588 visits, 2 to 25, median 12. What the extraction does not hold (decision D159). After these questions the form has a behaviour section: non-suicidal self-injury, interrupted and aborted attempts with their counts, preparatory acts, and the observed and potential lethality of the most recent, the most lethal and the first attempt, with their dates. The application stores it in psy_suicide and psy_suicide_semestriel (rad_cssrs15, 16, 18 and 20, cssrs17 and 19, the lethality items 22c to 27c); the clean models of the export read it, face_bp_5_suicide.sql does not select it and the V4.34 dictionary does not list it (request R126). The seed of the form has no rows for rad_cssrs13 and 14, the parents of the dates: a dangling parent. The deterrents item (radhtml_cssrs11) carries the text of the controllability question above its options (application defect A59): the rating is delivered as rated.

dr.notes: The Columbia scale at the follow-up visits, asked again at each visit: 784 visits, 79% to 93% of the visits of each of the five main kinds (6 of the 8 visits of the three others). Columbia Suicide Severity Rating Scale: five levels of ideation (yes or no, each with a free description), the most severe level as rated, five ratings of its intensity, the suicidal behaviours (actual, interrupted and aborted attempts, preparatory acts, self-injury without intent) and the lethality of three attempts. BP has two forms too, cssrs_v0 and cssrs_fu (BP decision D125), read from other columns, with the ideation part only. BP's follow-up schema has the names of DR's cssrs_fu and stacks with it (common_instruments.yaml). BP's inclusion form asks about the past week, DR's about the whole life: the two inclusion schemas do not stack. Two forms in the same columns. The inclusion visit and the follow-up visits use the same columns. The two are never delivered in one column: visit_form says which form a visit uses (inclusion for the screening and inclusion visits, follow_up for the others), and each form has its own schema and its own variables. Period. Form 150 prints no period in its questions. At inclusion the dictionary reads it as the whole life; at follow-up the same form is asked again, a yearly update that the raters read both ways (R14c). The names since_visit of cssrs_fu are kept so that the schema stacks with BP's, whose form says "since the last visit". Two DR forms, one table. Form 150 is the full scale (39 yes/no questions); form 230 is the simplified one (10 yes/no questions), chosen by the visit (the column SVUPDES of the table visite), and both write the table cssrs. 346 of the 1,341 answered visits (26%) hold none of the 20 fields that only the full form has: 0% to 2% of the visits until 2017-Q3, 37% to 56% a year in 2018-2022 and 36% to 51% in 2023-2026; one centre fills the simplified form almost only (68 of its 78 visits), and 34 visits (13 at inclusion and 21 at follow-up) from 2024 hold only the ten answers. The extraction does not say which form a visit used (request R127: the svupdes column), so on a simplified visit an empty full-form field is "not asked", not "no". No earlier note of the package mentioned the simplified visits. The form follows its skips. Levels 3 to 5 are asked only after a yes to level 2, and after a no they are 0 (asked_if; DR decision D25): of the 533 visits that answer no to levels 1 and 2, 1 holds an answer to levels 3 to 5. The number of actual, of interrupted and of aborted attempts is asked only after a yes to its question (asked_if, review of the tab). After a no it is blank, except the number of actual attempts (cssrs14) up to 2017, when a stored 0 sits on 426 of 487 no-visits (4 of 572 since 2018): the three counts are now 0 after a no, as in BP (+2,497 cells; 9 counts above 0 under a no stay as written). The aborted-attempt question (cssrs18) and the counts of interrupted and aborted attempts exist from late 2017: 1.2% of the visits before 2017-10 hold the question, 94.6% from 2018-01 (an empty cell before that is "not asked"). The most severe ideation as rated (cssrs06) runs from 1 to 5. A 0 is out_of_range (8 cells at inclusion): the zeros sit next to a yes to the wish to be dead on 10 of 10 visits and to level 2 on 5 of 10, so they are not "no ideation". The dates of the three attempts are dates before the visit (before_visit): a date on the day of the visit or later is out_of_range. The lethality scales are 0 to 5 (actual) and 0 to 2 (potential). The potential lethality has no shown_if: the C-SSRS rates it for an attempt that caused no damage, but 233 of the 365 filled cells sit under a non-zero actual lethality. The summary question "suicidal behaviour observed during the evaluation" (cssrs21) is the rater's own summary: it is no on 183 of the 214 visits that answer it and say yes to an actual, interrupted, aborted or preparatory behaviour (31 yes); it is delivered as rated. The Columbia lists of DR are numeric form keys read as numbers, not code_N cells (0 code_N cells in the cssrs and sisv columns). The intensity score is the sum of the five ratings, as in BP. At follow-up the share of "yes" to the wish to be dead is 47% against 77% at inclusion, and 267 of the 577 follow-up visits of patients who said yes at inclusion answer no. cssrs03_since_visit is on 782 visits: asked on 219, 0 after a no on 563. The most severe ideation as rated (cssrs06) is the highest level answered yes on 198 of 244 follow-up visits, higher on 21 and lower on 25: it is delivered as rated. The dates of the attempts at follow-up do not hold "since the last visit": 37 of the 55 most-recent and 36 of the 44 first-attempt dates are older than the previous visit (no date is on the day of the visit or later).
dr.difference: the behaviour section, the lethality ratings, the dates and the descriptions are added; the columns are named cssrs; the screening visit is an inclusion visit

BP: the deterrents item shows the text of the controllability question above its options (application defect A59). The behaviour section of the form is not in the BP extraction (request R126).

DR: about a quarter of the visits (from 2018) are simplified visits with a form of ten questions; the extraction does not tell them apart (request R127), so an empty field of the full form can mean 'not asked', not 'no'.
DR: the aborted-attempt question and the counts of interrupted and aborted attempts exist from late 2017 only.
