isf_lifetime.title: Suicidal thoughts and acts over the whole life (inclusion visit)

bp.notes: Five yes/no questions of rising severity, each followed by "when did it last happen?". Delivered as 1 (yes) and 0 (no). 5,952 of the 6,498 inclusion visits hold at least one answer. Two forms in the same columns (decisions D46 and D85 in PROGRESS.md). The application has two suicide forms in two tables: the one of the initial evaluation asks "have you ever...", the one of the six-monthly and yearly visits asks the same questions "since the last visit". The export writes both into the same columns and picks the table by the visit label. At inclusion 83% answer yes to the first question and 38% say they have attempted suicide. At the follow-up visits the same columns read 38% and 3% (36% and 2.4% as delivered, without the period removed by D88 and D125). Of the 3,078 later answers delivered of the patients who said at inclusion that they had attempted suicide, 2,936 (95%) are no; 1,149 of these 1,274 patients (90%) say no at every later visit (before the removal of D88 and D125: 3,413 answers, 3,183 no (93%), 1,173 of 1,371 patients (86%)). The answers to "when did it last happen" differ too: last week, two weeks to a year ago or more than a year ago at inclusion; last week or since the last visit at follow-up. They never cross: no inclusion visit holds the follow-up answer, and no follow-up visit holds an inclusion one. The two forms are therefore two instruments, isf_lifetime and isf_since_visit, with their own output columns. visit_form says which form a visit used; it is read from the visit label. Time frame of the follow-up form (decision D159, rule R14a). The follow-up form asks "depuis la dernière visite" on the five questions and on the attempt counts: its answers are about the time since the last visit, not a yearly update (D84 does not apply to the suicide forms). The form has no question "is there a change since the last visit?" (rad_pas_dechangement is in other sections), so an empty follow-up form means that the form was not done. The inclusion form has no doubtful period (D88 and D125 are about the follow-up form). The share who have attempted suicide is 43% up to 2012, 36% to 43% a year from 2013 to 2021, 30% in 2022 and 2023, and 37% from 2024. The dip of 2022 and 2023 is seen alike in the centres with the follow-up rise of D88 (42% up to 2021, then 32% and 40%) and in the others (36%, then 29% and 34%); nothing explains it yet. The form asks "when" only after a yes. 56 to 83 yes answers per question have no "when"; 10 "when" answers follow a no and 8 an empty answer, and are delivered as written. The questions do not always nest: 626 of the 5,845 visits with five answers (11%) say yes to a question after a no to a milder one. From the end of 2021 the inclusion form also shows the history of attempts (suicide_attempts) after a no to "attempted" (D125, which said "from early 2022"; measured in D159, answers after a no become frequent at the end of 2021): 51 inclusions that say no here give a number of attempts above 0 there, 50 of them from 2022. Both answers are delivered as written. One centre left the form empty on most of its inclusions of 2023 (17 of 64 answered, against 85% of its inclusions from 2016 to 2021); the other centres answered 91% of theirs that year.

sz.section: Intentionnalité suicidaire (VIE ENTIERE ou depuis la DERNIERE VISITE)
sz.notes: Five yes/no questions of rising severity, each followed by "when did it last happen?". Delivered as 1 (yes) and 0 (no). 2,239 of the 2,353 inclusion visits hold at least one answer. Two forms in the same columns, as in FACE BP (BP decisions D46 and D85; checked on the SZ data, decision D16 in PROGRESS.md). At the inclusion visit the five questions are about the whole life: 64% answer yes to the first and 30% say they have attempted suicide. At the follow-up visits the same columns hold the answers for the time since the last visit: 31% and 2.4%. Of the 665 later answers of the patients who said at inclusion that they had attempted suicide, 631 (95%) are no; 300 of these 332 patients (90%) say no at every later visit. The answers to "when did it last happen" differ too: last week, two weeks to a year ago or more than a year ago at inclusion; last week or since the last visit at follow-up. The two forms are two instruments, isf_lifetime and isf_since_visit. Which form a visit used. visit_form says it and is read from the visit label. The SZ application has three visit types: screening (type 1), initial evaluation (type 2) and annual evaluation (type 4), and it shows the suicide form of the inclusion at the initial evaluation and the form of the follow-up at the annual evaluation only; FACE BP also has a six-monthly type and shows its follow-up form at types 3 and 4. The 1,675 screening rows hold none of these columns and their visit_form is empty. 21 to 38 "yes" answers per question have no "when" (inclusion visits).

isf_since_visit.title: Suicidal thoughts and acts since the last visit (follow-up visits)

bp.notes: The five yes/no questions of isf_lifetime, asked at the follow-up visits about the time since the last visit, each followed by "when did it last happen?". Delivered as 1 (yes) and 0 (no): the first question on 8,244 visits (36% yes), "attempted" on 8,221 (2.4% yes). Two forms in the same columns (decisions D46 and D85 in PROGRESS.md; see isf_lifetime.yaml). The inclusion form asks "have you ever...": 83% answer yes to the first question and 38% say they have attempted suicide. The follow-up form asks the same questions "since the last visit": 38% and 3% in the same columns, before the removal below. Of the 3,078 later answers delivered of the patients who said at inclusion that they had attempted suicide, 2,936 (95%) are no; 1,149 of these 1,274 patients (90%) say no at every later visit (before the removal below: 3,413 answers, 3,183 no (93%), 1,173 of 1,371 patients (86%)). The answers to "when did it last happen" differ too, and never cross: last week, two weeks to a year ago or more than a year ago at inclusion; last week or since the last visit at follow-up. The two forms are therefore two instruments, isf_lifetime and isf_since_visit, with their own output columns. visit_form says which form a visit used; it is read from the visit label. Time frame of the follow-up form (decision D159, rule R14a). The follow-up form asks "depuis la dernière visite" on the five questions and on the attempt counts: its answers are about the time since the last visit, not a yearly update (D84 does not apply to the suicide forms). The form has no question "is there a change since the last visit?" (rad_pas_dechangement is in other sections), so an empty follow-up form means that the form was not done. A doubtful period (decisions D48, D85, D88 and D125 in PROGRESS.md). From 2012 to 2021, 1.5% to 3.7% of the follow-up answers each year say that the patient attempted suicide since the last visit. In 2022 it is 16% and in 2023 9%, then 2.4% to 3.4% from 2024. The first question rises too, from 36% in 2021 to 54% in 2022. Of the eight centres with 30 answers or more in 2022 and 2023, five rise and three do not. By month the rise starts in December 2021 (8 yes of 64 answers, against 0% to 4% a month from July to November) and stops in the first quarter of 2024 (2 of 130). The years of the COVID epidemic, 2020 and 2021, are at 3% to 4%. The clinician's rating of suicidal thoughts at the same visits (MADRS item 10) has no peak in these years. On the "yes" visits of the period the number of attempts given at inclusion is often typed again (26 of the 58 numbers, against 23 of 145 from 2012 to October 2021). A date of the first attempt is typed on 55 visits of the period: 47 of the 51 readable ones are before the inclusion visit, yet only 2 of 33 equal the date given at inclusion. The question about the whole life was asked again. What the application shows (read in November 2026). The follow-up form of today asks every question "since the last visit" and has no date of the first attempt; it was already so in January 2024, the oldest version of the code that can be read. From November 2021 to 2023 the form was another one at some centres: a real date of the first attempt, a question about the whole life, is typed on 2 follow-up visits of November 2021, 5 of December 2021, 37 of 2022 and 11 of 2023, against 1 from 2012 to October 2021 and 4 from 2024. Each centre runs its own copy of the application, which is why only some centres are concerned. Eight centres typed such dates in the period, the three without a rise among them. The cell does not tell which answers are about the whole life: of the 124 "yes" to "attempted" in the period, about 24 are what the usual rate (2.4%) explains, so about four in five are more. The "when" answers of the period are those of the follow-up list (none says more than a year ago), but they were left empty after a yes more often: 77% of the yes to "attempted" have one, against 95% before and 93% after. Not delivered (decisions D88 and D125 in PROGRESS.md, of the project lead; D88 replaces the flag of D48). Every answer of a follow-up visit dated from 2021-11-01 to 2023-12-31 is delivered as missing and gets the flag period_removed, the "yes" and the "no" alike: with the "yes" alone removed, the period would read 0%. 6,360 cells of 1,002 visits (774 patients); the flag log keeps what was written. D125 moved the start from 2022-01-01 to 2021-11-01, the month of the first whole-life dates. The removal applies to every centre. In one centre the placeholder 2011-11-11 of the first-attempt date marks, visit by visit, its old follow-up form: it is on all but one of that centre's forms until May 2022, and on 86 visits of the period (3 "yes" to "attempted"). These visits are removed too, because the export will blank the placeholder (R22). What the form of the period asked cannot be read any more: the history of the code starts in January 2024. Some follow-up visits hold the C-SSRS (cssrs_fu) and none of these questions: 14 in 2021, then 118 to 199 a year from 2022. Three centres use it instead of these questions: none of their follow-up visits answers them from 2022 (one centre) or 2024 (two). The share of follow-up visits that answer these questions falls from 82% to 95% a year (2012 to 2021) to 45% to 63% (2022 to 2025); those visits hold the other form. At one more centre the whole tab is empty at most visits of 2023: 148 of its 191 follow-up visits hold neither these questions nor the C-SSRS (77%, against 27% to 36% in each of 2019 to 2022 and 2024), and 137 of these 148 visits hold a MADRS (at the other centres, 35 of the 248 visits that hold neither do): the visit took place and the tab was left empty (O40, DM-6). From 2024 the attempts are back to their usual rate, but the first three questions are not in four centres: the first question is at 47% from 2024 against 35% from 2019 to 2021, and 6 to 8 points higher at the same MADRS total. In the other centres it is steady (37% and 38%). Compare the thought questions across periods with care.

The five questions of the follow-up form end with "depuis la dernière visite", and the "when" has two options only: last week, or between a week ago and the last visit. most_serious_attempt.title: The most serious suicide attempt (method and lethality)

bp.notes: The most serious non-violent suicide attempt of the whole life, as asked at the inclusion visit after a yes to serious attempts: its method (drugs with or without a sedative effect, or cutting), the kind of drug, its medical consequences on a scale that has its own wording for each method, and whether an event triggered it, with which one. Delivered as categories; "triggered" as 1 (yes) and 0 (no). One schema per form (decision D125 in PROGRESS.md, as D86 did for the attempt counts). The follow-up form asks the same section about the most serious attempt since the last visit: those answers are most_serious_attempt_since_visit. visit_form says which form a visit used; it is read from the visit label. The follow-up form asks the section "depuis la dernière visite" (rule R14a, decision D159): since the last visit, not a yearly update. 432 methods on 448 inclusion visits, from 2009 to January 2022. The section left the forms during 2021, at one centre early in 2022: the last inclusion answer of each centre is between December 2020 and November 2021, except one in 2019 and one in January 2022. 116 of the 117 inclusions from 2022 that report a serious attempt (serious_attempts) have no detail. Until 2021 the method is given on 79% to 97% of the inclusions with a serious attempt in each period, less often in the later periods (97% to 2012, 79% in 2019-2021). Four centres never give it. Drugs with a sedative effect are 79% to 85% of the methods in each period. 16 inclusion visits of 2012 to 2021 with a serious attempt answer "triggered" with no method. Why the sections end in 2021 (decision D159, application defect A60). The application builds a form by listing the group table of its form, and the dumps of psy_suicide_groupe and psy_suicide_semestriel hold groups 1, 2, 3 and 5 only: the fields of group 4 (the most violent attempt) and of group 6 (the most serious attempt) have no group any more and are no longer displayed. Each centre runs its own copy of the application, which fits the dates: at inclusion the last answer of either section is dated between April 2021 and January 2022 by centre, the last serious method between January 2019 and January 2022 and the last violent method between October 2019 and November 2021 (the follow-up visits add the last violent method in December 2021 and the last serious one in February 2022). Over the two forms the method is given on 89% of the 512 visits with a serious attempt up to 2021 (454) and on 2 of the 136 from 2022, and on 94% of the 353 visits with a violent attempt up to 2021 (332) and on none of the 108 from 2022. Four centres never give a method although they report yes answers (14 visits with a violent attempt, 18 with a serious one). The codes are short names; the lethalities follow the order of the scale. Every list holds the whole list of the form, also answers that no visit holds (death after sedative drugs, the two most severe levels of cutting, recreational drugs, anticholinergics and appetite suppressants among the drugs without a sedative effect). A drug type "Inconnu" is a missing code (23 sedative, 5 non-sedative). Death is given after other drugs or substances on 2 visits (2013, 2018): the patient was seen at that inclusion visit, so it cannot describe the patient's own attempt. It is delivered as written. Lists that the form hid (decision D125, field shown_if). The form shows a drug type and a lethality only for their own method, and the trigger only after a yes to "triggered". The forms of 2009-2010 saved the first option of the lists that start with an empty choice, the hidden ones too (antipsychotic, other prescription, fully conscious, scratches, "Conjugal"). A filled cell that the form did not show is delivered as missing with the flag not_shown; the flag log keeps the text. 80 cells on 24 visits. 76 are on 20 visits of 2009 and 2010 at four centres, nearly all first options: 14 with no method, 6 with another method. The other 4 are on 4 visits of 2013 to 2020 and are not first options: a drug type or a lethality with no method (2), the drug type of another method (1), a trigger without a yes (1). This is an exception to the rule of D145 that a value recorded under an empty parent stays as recorded (decision D160, rule R15): 64 of the 80 cells sit under an empty parent (no method, or no answer to "triggered") and 16 under another answer, and 73 of the 80 are the first option of a hidden list, a form artefact of 2009-2010 and not an answer. The hiding is kept (decision of the project lead).

dr.notes: The most serious non-violent suicide attempt of the whole life (form 151, "section à coter uniquement pour la tentative de suicide la plus grave et non violente"): its method (drugs with or without a sedative effect, or cutting), the kind of drug, its medical consequences on a scale that has its own wording for each method, and whether an event triggered it, with which one. Delivered as categories on the names of the BP schema; "triggered" as 1 (yes) and 0 (no), 2 ("not known") a missing code. 70 visits: the method is sedative drugs on 61, other drugs or substances on 7 and cutting on 2. The form is shown after a yes to serious attempts (ISF9) at the inclusion visit and at 24 and 48 months (config/global.php, visit types 2, 6, 8) and is filled on 55 of the 66 visits with ISF9 yes and on 11 of the 102 with ISF9 no. One schema for all visits (58 inclusion and 12 follow-up visits hold it): the form is the same at follow-up. Decoded (review of the tab). The dictionary gives no list; the codes are the keys of the lists of form 151, read on the names of the BP schema. Cross-tabs agree with the form: every drug type, effect and trigger is filled under the method that shows it (0 cells under another method, 0 triggers after a "no") and the trigger is given on 31 of the 31 visits that say yes. The lethality scales are BP's in the same order, up to the last level that this form offers (8 levels for the sedative drugs, 4 for the other drugs, 5 for cutting): the BP level "death" is not in the DR form. A drug type "Inconnu" (code 9 for the sedative drugs, 8 for the others) is a missing code (3 and 1 cells). The trigger has one kind more than BP, "other, specify" (code 10, other_specified, 3 cells); "other interpersonal factor" (code 2) is 4 of the 31 triggers, so it is not rare here (BP 21% of its triggers). The earlier note that the lists could not be named is answered by the form (open question O25(3)). No shown_if: the forms of 2009-2010 that saved the first option of the hidden lists in BP do not exist in this cohort, and the DR data hold no cell under a method that does not show it (BP D125).

suicide_attempts.title: History of suicide attempts over the whole life (inclusion visit)

bp.notes: Date of the first attempt, number of attempts, and whether some were violent (firearm, hanging, jump...) or serious without being violent (intensive care after drugs or cutting), over the whole life, as asked at the inclusion visit. Violent and serious are two separate groups of the form. Yes/no answers are delivered as 1 and 0; "Ne sais pas" to the violent and serious questions is a missing code (7 and 21 answers). Two forms in the same columns (decision D86 in PROGRESS.md, was open question O47). The inclusion form asks "how many times have you attempted suicide" and the date of the first attempt. The follow-up form asks the same numbers "since the last visit" and has no date of the first attempt (read in the form definitions of the application in November 2026). The follow-up visits are therefore another instrument, suicide_attempts_since_visit, with its own output columns. visit_form says which form a visit used; it is read from the visit label. Time frame of the follow-up form (decision D159, rule R14a). The follow-up form asks "depuis la dernière visite" on the attempt question and on the three counts: its answers are about the time since the last visit, not a yearly update (D84 does not apply to the suicide forms). The form has no question "is there a change since the last visit?" (rad_pas_dechangement is in other sections), so an empty follow-up form means that the form was not done. Counts that are 0 by logic (decision D125, as D122). The number of attempts is 0 after a no to "have you ever attempted suicide" (isf05, read here and delivered as isf05_lifetime): 3,286 inclusions get their 0 this way. The violent and serious attempts are 0 after 0 attempts, and their numbers are 0 after a no. n_attempts is on 5,785 inclusions, 2,142 of them above 0. The history after a no to "attempted". The inclusion form of the application today shows the date, the count and the two yes/no questions to every patient (no condition on them; the follow-up form shows them only after a yes). The data say that a no left them empty until 2020: the inclusions that say no and hold a count or one of the two answers are 0% to 1% a year from 2011 to 2020 (4 of 2,385), 5% in 2021 (14 of 286: 5 in the first quarter and 9 in the last) and 37% to 48% a year from 2022 (382 of 900). D125 dated the change "from early 2022"; measured in D159, it starts at the end of 2021. From the end of 2021 a 0 is typed after a no (6 in the last quarter of 2021, 298 of the 900 no from 2022), and 51 inclusions that say no give a number above 0, 50 of them from 2022; 50 inclusions that say no carry a real date of the first attempt, 45 of them with a number above 0 (2022 to 2026). They are delivered as typed. The forms of 2009 and 2010 also typed 0 after a no (37 of the 114 inclusions that say no: 26 in 2009, 11 in 2010). 8 inclusions say yes with 0 attempts. Among the patients with at least one attempt the number is steady (mean 2.4 to 2.8 in every period): compare the counts there. Date of the first attempt, on 1,790 inclusions. A date on or after the inclusion visit is impossible and is delivered as missing (before_visit, D125): 306 cells are out_of_range, 229 on the day of the visit and 77 after it. 297 of them contradict the patient's own answer about when the last attempt was. The same-day dates stop in 2022 (4 that year, then 1 in 2025), as if an older form had filled the field with the day. One more date has the year 0000 (out_of_range). 162 cells hold the placeholder 1000-01-01 (the default of the column in the inclusion table). Dates are often rounded: 276 are a first of January and 629 of the 1,751 full dates a 15th, where only the year or the month was known. 28 dates typed without a month are delivered as 1 July and 11 without a day as the 15th (date_partial); 2 cannot be read (unparsed). The placeholder 2011-11-11 is written at the follow-up visits only and is read there: the date column of the follow-up table is NOT NULL with no default and the form does not show it, so the database stores 0000-00-00, or 2011-11-11 at one centre (8,073 and 1,142 follow-up visits, application defect A20). Number of attempts. At inclusion one cell holds 99 and ends out_of_range; at follow-up the largest number is 20. The form accepts one or two digits for the three counts (0 to 99); the ranges of this schema (0 to 50, 0 to 20) are plausible limits, not the form's. What follows the history in the form (decision D159). The sections of the most violent and of the most serious attempt are no longer displayed (see most_violent_attempt and most_serious_attempt, application defect A60), whereas this group is. Group 5 of the form, the Suicide Intent Scale of the most recent attempt (15 items, rad_SISR01 to 015, shown at follow-up after a yes to "attempted since the last visit"), is displayed but none of its answers is in the extraction: no export model selects it and the V4.34 dictionary does not list it (request R126). The behaviour section of the C-SSRS is in the same case (see cssrs_v0). The date of the most violent attempt (isf08_qsdtc) is in the dictionary but not in the extraction: the question was removed from the BP form, and the source database no longer holds it (answer of the data managers in November 2026, decision D69 in PROGRESS.md).

The form clears the whole history tab after a "no" or an empty answer to ISF5 (have you ever tried to kill yourself?): on the 292 inclusion visits that say no every field of the history is empty (the hidden dates are stored 0000-00-00 on 252 of them), and so it is on the 816 that leave ISF5 empty. Dates of events before the visit (before_visit, as BP D125): a date on the day of the visit or later is impossible and is delivered as missing with out_of_range: 2 first-attempt dates and 1 date of the most serious attempt. 0000-00-00, the content of a hidden or empty date field, is read as an empty date (388, 505 and 482 cells of the three date columns over all visits). The first-attempt date is delivered on 145 inclusion visits, the most violent on 29 and the most serious on 51. DR is not in this instrument: its lifetime form asked again is suicide_attempts_fu, and its number of attempts since the last visit comes from another question (n_suicide_attempts_since_visit of mood_course_fu).
The ranges of the schema (0 to 50, 0 to 20) are plausible limits, not the form's (0 to 99).

common.note: The follow-up form of eBipolar and eSchizo asks the same numbers since the last visit, after a "yes" to isf05_since_visit, and the numbers of violent and serious attempts after a yes to their own question: BP and SZ give 0 after a no (BP D125). BP does not deliver the visits of November 2021 to 2023 (period_removed): its follow-up form of that time also asked about the whole life. DR's number of attempts since the last visit, read from another question (the clinician's summary of the course, mood_course_fu), is n_suicide_attempts_since_visit (ASP's follow-up number is n_attempts_fu).

drug_classes_lifetime.title: Classes of medication taken over the life

bp.notes: For each of six classes of medication (antidepressants, first- and second-generation antipsychotics, benzodiazepines, hypnotics and anxiolytics, lithium, anticonvulsant mood stabilisers): whether the patient has taken one, the date of the first start and the cumulated months of exposure. Yes/no answers are delivered as 1 and 0; "Ne sais pas" is a missing code (9% of the answers for the first-generation antipsychotics, 10% for the anxiolytics and hypnotics). A form of the patient, not of a visit: it is opened from the medication menu, can be saved again later, and its date is not exported (asked of the export; D124). Its heading asks whether the patient has ever had each class, counting the treatments taken at the screening and inclusion visits: the answers cover the time up to the inclusion, not the whole life. 2,817 patients have a record of the form, and 2,641 of them answer at least one class yes or no. The six questions are Oui/Non/Ne sais pas radio buttons (rad_psylifetime_*), and the date and the cumulated months are shown after "Oui" only (position 0 of the radio). "Anticonvulsant mood stabilisers" is the application's own class ("Thymorégulateur AC"). One value per patient. The extraction repeats these columns on every row of the patient. Where a patient has two records of the form, the export keeps one of them with no rule (R18 asks for the lowest id, the record the application opens) and copies it onto every row: that is why the rows of a patient never differ. Months. A list of the form that stops at 240: ">240" is read as 240 with a mark in the censoring column (this value or more; 190 answers). The months are 0 where the patient has never taken the class (asked_if); the list has no answer 0. They are not winsorised. After a yes, neither the months nor a date is given for 245 patients (first-generation antipsychotics) to 797 (anxiolytics and hypnotics) per class. One patient has anticonvulsant months after the answer "no", and another has anticonvulsant months and a date with no answer: both are delivered as stored (R2); apart from them the months and the dates are empty under a "no" or an empty answer. Dates. 83% fall on the 1st or the 15th of a month: the day was seldom known. 38% are a 1 January (14%), a 1 July (14%) or a 15 June (11%), most of them standing for a year alone. Which day was typed depends on the centre and changed over time: for the patients included until 2015 and after, 1 July is 22% and 7% of the dates, 15 June 5% and 15%, 1 January 11% and 16%. A date with an unknown month or day becomes the middle of the period (date_partial, 7 cells; a year alone becomes 1 July). Two antidepressant dates are not delivered: one with a month 00 and a day (unparsed), one before 1950 (out_of_range). Placeholders. The application writes 0000-00-00 in a date that was not typed (read as empty, 9,927 cells) and, since its version of 2024-07-25, which each centre got at its own date, 1000-01-01 (date_placeholder, 332 cells of 111 patients). The hidden date after a "no" is 0000-00-00 in 4,926 of the 5,144 cells (96%) and 1000-01-01 in 218, and the months are blank. 272 of the 332 placeholders stand under a "no", a "Ne sais pas" or an empty answer, the default of the hidden date (the date columns of the table default to 1000-01-01). By the date of the inclusion visit, the 111 patients are 13 of 2019-2023, 9 of 2024, 36 of 2025 and 53 of 2026. Time elapsed. 162 of the 6,641 first starts (131 patients) are after the inclusion, 20 of them after the last visit. The months are longer than the time from the first start to the inclusion for 506 of the 5,902 classes that have both, to the last visit for 137 and to the extraction (13 November 2026) for 14, each time rounded up to the next answer of the list. This is noted, not flagged (D124): the dates are often approximate and the form can be saved again after the inclusion. Completeness. At least one class is answered yes or no for 57% of the patients included until 2012, 65% in 2013-2015, 39% in 2016-2018, 29% in 2019-2021, 24% in 2022-2023 and 22% from 2024. Three centres hardly fill it. Three fill it much less after 2015 and hardly at all from 2019, two others hardly from 2024, while two fill it for most of their patients included since 2019. After a yes, the date or the months are given for 72% of the answers: about half in three centres and 12% in one (among the centres with 100 answers or more). Another centre gives them for 28% of its anxiolytic and hypnotic answers, against 73% to 97% for the other classes. These answers are the clinician's summary. The table treatments (medications.yaml) lists the medications one by one with their dates; the two were typed separately and need not agree. Where the answer is "no", the table holds a medication of the class started on or before the inclusion for 7 (antidepressants) to 61 patients (first-generation antipsychotics, anticonvulsants). Where the answer is "yes" and the patient has a list, the list holds a medication of the class for 64% (antidepressants), 40% (first-generation antipsychotics), 74% (second-generation antipsychotics), 55% (anxiolytics and hypnotics), 79% (lithium) and 80% (anticonvulsants) of the patients: the list is not exhaustive.

drug_classes_lifetime.description: Classes of medication ever taken, one value per patient in the table patients (BP): for antidepressants, first- and second-generation antipsychotics, benzodiazepines, hypnotics and anxiolytics, lithium and anticonvulsant mood stabilisers, whether the patient has taken one, the date of the first start and the cumulated months of exposure.
drug_classes_lifetime.period: up to the inclusion (the form says 'ever', counting the treatments of the screening and inclusion visits)
flags: A form of the patient, not of a visit: it can be saved again later and its date is not exported.
The cumulated months stop at 240: '>240' is delivered as 240 with a mark in the censoring column. They are 0 where the class was never taken.
The dates are approximate: 83% fall on the 1st or the 15th of a month, and many stand for a year alone.
At least one class is answered for 57% of the patients included until 2012 and 22% of those included from 2024.
These answers are the clinician's summary. They were typed separately from the medication list (table treatments) and the two need not agree: neither source is complete.

medications.title: Psychotropic treatments, one row per treatment

bp.notes: The medications of each patient with their dates: 22,758 medications of 4,779 patients. The extraction writes them as lists in one cell (the name of each medication in one column, its start date in another, and so on), and every row of a patient holds the same lists: the patient's whole history, not the treatment of the visit. The lists are opened into one row per patient and medication, delivered in the table treatments (decision D56 in PROGRESS.md). Lists. 1,719 of the 6,498 patients have no list. The application has no answer for "no treatment": a patient without a list is unknown, not untreated. A list is held by 83% to 85% of the patients included until 2015 and by 60% to 63% of those included from 2022. The classes of the lifetime form (drug_classes_lifetime.yaml) were typed separately: of the patients who answer yes to a class there and have a list, the list holds a medication of the class for 40% (first-generation antipsychotics) to 80% (anticonvulsants), so neither source is complete. Item. The item number is the place of the medication in the exported list. Until the export orders the lists (R76 of EXPORT_REQUESTS.md), it changes between extractions: join the items of two extractions on their content (patient, name and dates), never on item. Name, molecule and group. The name is delivered as written: a brand, a brand with its dose and form, or a generic with the name of its maker. It is looked up in medications.csv, which gives the molecule (one word, with underscores for a combination), its ATC code and one of ten groups: lithium, anticonvulsant, antipsychotic_2g, antipsychotic_1g, antidepressant, benzodiazepine, other_anxiolytic_hypnotic, stimulant, other_nervous_system and non_psychotropic (292 names, 156 molecules; the ATC code of NOCTRAN has 5 characters, two rows, the homeopathic lithium and the trace-element lithium, have none, and the review found eight misspelled names: the table is shared by the cohorts, a correction goes through the lead). The table was checked against the application's own drug list and the ATC codes of the SZ extraction (D102); gabapentin and pregabalin are anticonvulsants, as in the application (117 medications). A name that is not in the table (173 medications, 0.8%) keeps what was written, has no molecule and no group, and gets unknown_code. Dates. The start date is filled for 22,608 medications, most often with the day set to 15 (the month is known, not the day). One centre wrote 1950-01-01 for an unknown start and 1950-01-02 for an unknown end: they are missing with the reason unknown (20 starts, 13 ends). The range of the start begins in 1951, so two more starts of 1950 are out_of_range; three other ends of 1950 are kept. 128 starts are 0000-00-00, the empty date of the form (127 of these treatments are running, one has an end date): they are missing with the reason not_recorded (they were empty with no flag), so the start has 148 missing codes with the 20 of 1950; the application shows "Aucune date indiquée" for the 127 and "Terminé le" with the end date for the one, and no value changes. The box "Traitement en cours" of the form hides the end date and writes it 0000-00-15 on today's add page and 0000-00-00 on the correction page; seven of the sixteen centres have 0000-00-15, mostly for treatments started from 2016, and the nine others only 0000-00-00. The application shows both as running "until today" (D96): both are missing with the reason running (11,855 medications: 8,738 and 3,117). The end date is filled for 10,890 medications. An end date before the start (148 medications, 147 of them with no date of 1950) is kept and gets check_failed (end_before_start). The add form alerts on an end before the start only if the end's year, month and day are each at or before the start's, so it catches 19 of the 147; the correction page has no check (A58). Dose. The form stores no strength since it took its names from the public drug list in 2015 (A38 of EXPORT_REQUESTS.md; of the two columns it writes empty, only the identifier of the strength, ID_medicament_posologie, is an integer and holds 0, while posologie is a varchar(255)): a strength is stored for 6,974 medications, 4 of the 11,593 started from 2016. The strength is in the name of the product, and the package reads it there with the rule of R54: exactly one amount of a mass, not per volume, not a percentage, not in units (UI); a number right after another number and a space is not read. Of the 15,784 medications with no stored strength, 14,355 get one from the name; 1,284 names hold no amount, 29 several, and 116 one per volume, in % or in UI. daily_dose is a score in mg (D124): the stored strength where one is stored (its leading number, unit MG; a strength in tablets, per volume or in % gives no dose), else the strength in the name, times units_per_day. strength_from_name says 1 (name) or 0 (stored). 19,349 medications have a daily dose, 12,948 of them from the name. By start date: 6,283 of the 7,900 started until 2013, 5,281 of the 6,054 started from 2014 to 2017 and 7,664 of the 8,654 started from 2018; 2,185 of the 2,225 patients with a medication started from 2018 have a dose. The review of the tab compared the doses with the usual maximum of each molecule: 46 of 15,562 doses of 24 molecules are above it, one by more than twice, so no systematic error shows (the usual maxima are not in the package). Stored dose. The extracted dose (the export's strength times units) is kept as daily_dose_stored, not delivered, and compared: 2 score_mismatch (the export reads the units "1/2" as 1 and doubles the dose, R75), 17 score_not_recomputed (8 whose units the package cannot read, 9 whose strength is in tablets; the stored value is in the flag). 3 doses read from the name are above 5,000 mg and out_of_range (300 to 500 mg at 50 to 100 units a day), and strength_from_name is missing there. Units a day. The add form offers 0.25 to 100, ">100" and "Si besoin" (as needed); the correction page takes free text. ">100" is read as 100 and censored (7); "Si besoin" and "sb" are a missing code (893); "1/2" is read as 0.5 (9); a decimal comma is repaired (22, format_repaired); 29 texts with words (ranges, counts with their form) are unparsed. A long-acting injection has no units a day: the form records ampoules every n weeks instead (nb_ampoule, nb_semaine), which the BP export computes in its model but does not select, with the date of entry (date_saisie): 109 medications of 90 patients have no dose (R123). date_saisie is to be exported only once A39 is fixed (a correction sets it to a fixed timestamp), which is why R76 orders the lists by start date and row identifier, never by date_saisie. At a visit. The columns of medications_at_visit say, for each visit, whether the patient was on a group or a molecule that day: a medication that started on or before the visit date and has no end date, or an end date on or after the visit (see their notes).

sz.section: Données détaillées des traitements psychotropes AU MOMENT DE LA VISITE
sz.notes: The medications of each patient with their dates: 11,038 medications of 1,975 patients. As in FACE BP, the extraction writes them as lists in one cell and every row of a patient holds the same lists, the patient's whole history, not the treatment of the visit (the 11 columns are identical on all the rows of every patient). The lists are opened into one row per patient and medication, in the table treatments. Lists. 378 of the 2,353 patients have no list. The application has no answer for "no treatment": a patient without a list is unknown, not untreated. A list is held by 88% of the patients included until 2015, 84% to 85% of those included from 2016 to 2023 and 73% of those included from 2024. Item. The SZ export orders each list by start date (the BP export does not yet, R76 of EXPORT_REQUESTS.md), but a medication added later with an earlier start moves the items after it: join the items of two extractions on their content (patient, name and dates), never on item. Name, molecule and group. The name is looked up in facedata/medications.csv, the table that the cohorts share: molecule (one word, with underscores for a combination), ATC code and one of ten groups. 27 names of this cohort were added to the table written for BP (BP D77). The table was checked against the application's own drug list and the ATC codes of this extraction (BP D102, D31 here); gabapentin and pregabalin are anticonvulsants, as in the application (18 medications). A name that is not in the table (149 medications, 1.3%) keeps what was written and gets unknown_code. The SZ extraction also gives the name, the ATC code and the active principle of the application's own list of medications, the list the form used until 2015: 3,331 of the 11,038 medications have them (3,324 of the 5,898 started before 2016, 7 of the 5,140 started from 2016). They are delivered next to those of the table, and they agree with it: the two ATC codes are the same on 3,314 of the 3,322 medications that have both. The 8 that differ: 7 are rows of Valdoxan (2011 to 2014) whose product in the list of the EMR is a nicotine patch (the id and the name typed disagree; the table, which follows the name, is right), and 1 is a gabapentin row that carries an old code of the EMR. Dates. Every medication has a start date, most often with the day set to 15 (8,785). The box "Traitement en cours" of the form hides the end date and writes it 0000-00-15 on today's add page and 0000-00-00 on the correction page; six of the twelve centres have 0000-00-15 and the six others only 0000-00-00. The application shows both as running "until today" (BP D96): both are missing with the reason running (5,246 medications: 4,182 and 1,064). The end date is filled for 5,792 medications. An end date before the start (41 medications) is kept and gets check_failed (end_before_start). The add form of the application alerts only if the end year, month and day are each at or before those of the start (A58 of EXPORT_REQUESTS.md); it catches 2 of these 41 rows, and the correction page has no check. No date of 1950 occurs here: the missing codes 1950-01-01 and 1950-01-02 are those of one BP centre. Dose. As in BP, the form stores no strength since it took its names from the public drug list in 2015 (A38 of EXPORT_REQUESTS.md): a strength is stored for 2,940 medications, 7 of the 5,140 started from 2016. The daily dose is computed with the BP rule (BP D124): the stored strength where one is stored (its leading number, unit MG; a strength in tablets, per volume or in % gives no dose), else the one amount of a mass in the name (the rule of R54), times units_per_day. strength_from_name says 1 (name) or 0 (stored). 9,014 medications have a daily dose, 6,504 of them from the name. By start date: 3,339 of the 4,356 started until 2013, 2,512 of the 2,997 started from 2014 to 2017 and 3,163 of the 3,685 started from 2018; 976 of the 1,067 patients with a medication started from 2018 have a dose. The SZ extraction has no dose of its own to compare with. 8 doses read from a name in grams (5.9 g to 40 g a day; 6 non-psychotropic, 2 not in the table) are above 5,000 mg and out_of_range, and strength_from_name is missing there. Units a day. Read for 9,409 medications. ">100" is read as 100 and censored (11); "Si besoin" (as needed) is a missing code (224); 3 values above 100 are out_of_range; 3 numbers written with a comma or a final point are repaired and 2 texts are unparsed. The number of weeks is the interval between two doses of a long-acting injection, for which the form hides the units a day (834 medications). At a visit. The columns of medications_at_visit say, for each visit, whether the patient was on a group or a molecule that day. The same columns as in BP, and four molecules more (clozapine, amisulpride, haloperidol, paliperidone). Year and centre. The interval between two injections (interval_weeks) goes from 2 to 4 weeks over the years because the products change, not the practice: long-acting risperidone (every 2 weeks) gives way to paliperidone and aripiprazole (every 4 weeks), and the median of each molecule is the same in both periods. The share of strengths read from the name (strength_from_name) is 8% to 59% by centre for medications started to 2014 and 98% to 100% from 2016: before 2015 the strength was typed in the name at some centres and stored at others.
sz.difference: no stored daily dose to compare with (the package computes it, as in BP); the interval in weeks and the name, ATC code and active principle of the drug list of the EMR are added

dr.notes: The psychotropic treatments recorded as current (PSYCHOTROPE ACTUEL), one row per treatment in the table treatments, where the column list says "medications". The variables keep the names of the BP and SZ lists with one exception: substance_name, not medication. BP and SZ deliver the product as it was typed (a trade name with its strength: a digit in 64% of the BP names); here the export writes the name of the substance of the drug catalogue (nomsubstance), with no digit on any of the 817 rows and a salt in brackets on 15% (123 rows). It is another notion than the typed product, so it has its own name. 480 patients have a list (85% of the patients included until 2017, 58% of those included since 2024; 46% to 97% by centre). The export crosses the lists (request R122). This is the answer to DEV-1: the export does it, not the form. Forms 157 (current) and 158 (somatic) are a table of rows that belong to the form of the visit (Tableau, multiple), form 156 (past) is a table shown by patient; each has an add button and no limit of rows. face_dr_12_traitements.sql keeps one arbitrary row of each list per visit (distinct on (usubjid, visitnum) with no order, lines 6-8), builds the classes from those rows (94-100) and joins the rows to the patient by the patient alone (161-162, 324-325, 482-483), with the arrays ordered by class (128-157, 290-319, 449-478): P products and L lines give P x L items, written on every visit of the patient (672-682). Nothing says which line belongs to which product. The number of units a day is the daily dose of one line over the strength of one product, computed for every pair: most of these numbers mean nothing. The raw table also holds three columns that look like the reasons for stopping (psy_arret_1 to 3; the form has a "Motif(s)" column) and that the export does not select. What is delivered (field crossed, SCHEMA_SPEC section 15). A patient with one product keeps every line. A patient with several products keeps one item per product, without form, dose or date (list_crossed on these variables): the molecules are known, their dates are not. In the file there are 1,852 items; the 286 patients with one product hold 332 of them, the 194 patients with several products 1,520, which become 485 items: 817 items delivered. Dates are tied to a product for the 286 one-product patients only; 20 of the 194 other patients have all their products in one group, and nothing safe can be added in the code. The class and catalogue-code columns (cmclas, cmclascd) are lists of another length, not in the order of the products, and are not read (ignored.yaml). Eight patients have catalogue (CIS) codes but no substance row (products with no ATC match), and 40 more have fewer substances than codes. When the export is corrected (one array item per row, as in ASP; a left join; order by visit and row; the visit of the row exported) the list becomes per_visit and the crossing note goes. The list of a patient is the same on every row of the patient, but it is not a history of the past: the rows are the current treatments of the visits, pooled by the export. Dates are written day/month/year. Molecule and group. The generic name of the catalogue (cmdecod) is looked up in the table medications.csv, shared by the cohorts; eleven generic names of this cohort were added to it. Every item finds its molecule. 293 patients have an antidepressant in their list, 125 a benzodiazepine, 75 a second-generation antipsychotic, 51 lithium; the most frequent molecules are venlafaxine, clomipramine, lithium and lamotrigine. Half of the patients have one molecule only, which is few for this cohort: the list may not hold every current treatment (the crossing loses the products with no ATC match). Doses. daily_dose is the daily dose in mg as typed: the forms title the field "posologie journalière en mg" (the column is headed "doses journalières cumulées"). The unit of the strength is mg on 780 of the 817 rows and g on 17. Median doses by molecule (7 to 12 doses each) are in the range of BP and SZ: lithium 900 (BP 1000), fluoxetine 40 (20), sertraline 100 (50), quetiapine 400 (300). units_per_day is derived by the export: the typed dose divided by the number of the strength (lines 134-150), which is wrong for strengths in g, in µg or in units, and meaningless for crossed pairs. No treatment ends before it starts (check end_date).
dr.difference: the lists of this extraction are crossed by the export (a product written next to every prescription line, request R122) and are put back with the field crossed; the name is the substance of the drug catalogue (substance_name), not the typed product; the daily dose is in mg as typed and the number of units a day is computed by the export; the generic name of the catalogue is looked up; no liquid strength; the form is added

asp.notes: The treatments recorded at a visit: the name, the generic name, the indication, the dose, the start and the end, and whether the treatment is still taken. 1,784 treatments for 966 visits of 896 patients (408 screening visits, 475 inclusion visits and 83 follow-up visits), from 2010 to 2026. One row per visit and treatment in the table treatments, where the column list says "medications". **The list is that of the visit, not the history of the patient.** In BP, SZ and DR every row of a patient holds the same list. Here 65 patients have a list on several visits, and they differ: the list of each visit is opened (field per_visit) and the table has the column visit. A current treatment is declared on 715 inclusion visits and a list is recorded on 456 of them: **a patient with no list is not a patient with no treatment**. Molecule and group. The name is looked up in the table medications.csv, shared by the cohorts, and the generic name where the name gives nothing (field otherwise): the name is written on 1,505 treatments and the generic name on 602. 1,523 of the 1,735 treatments that have a name find their molecule; thirty-one names of this cohort were added to the table, and the 212 others (most of them somatic drugs written once or twice) keep what was written. 203 of them get unknown_code (196 different names); the 9 that have only a generic name are not flagged. The accents of the names are written twice over in this export; the reader puts them back. The daily dose (daily_dose, the thesaurus says mg a day; the DR form is in mg too) is a number typed by the rater (1,143 treatments); the start is a full date on 622 treatments, a month or a year on 102, and empty on 1056. still_taken is 1 on 1,447 treatments and 0 on 184 (blank on 153). The end is typed only for a treatment that is no longer taken: 91 of the 184 have an end date, none of the 1,447 and none of the 153 blank. A missing end date under a treatment still taken is therefore not a gap (the audit line on end_date comes from reading the lists as single values). 24 cells are not read as a number or a date (unparsed, delivered missing, the text kept in the flag): 20 doses and 4 start dates. The doses are a range typed with a dash (5), a number followed by a unit or a word (9), a ratio or a number per word (2), a daily scheme of three numbers (1), a word followed by a number (1) and a word with no number (2). The start dates are a month and a year behind a leading slash (1), a day and a month with no year (1) and two with an extra or a too long group of digits (2). **Year and centre.** The median dose (no unit, doses of different molecules) is 15 to 36 by centre and 5 to 30 by year (years and centres with 20 doses or more); it follows the share of children, whose median by centre is 6 to 20 and the adults' 20 to 36.
asp.difference: the list is that of the visit, not the history of the patient (per_visit); other columns; the molecule is looked up from the name, then from the generic name; a dose with no unit, the indication and whether the treatment is still taken (the end date is typed only for a treatment that is no longer taken); no strength, unit or form

medications.description: Medications, one row per medication in the table treatments (list 'medications'): the name as written, the molecule, its ATC code and group, the start and end dates, the units a day and the daily dose.
medications.period: BP and SZ: the whole history of the patient (the same list on every visit); DR: the current treatments of the visits, pooled by the export; ASP: the treatments recorded at each visit
sources: schema notes (bp, sz, dr, asp medications)
flags: The application has no answer for 'no treatment': a patient without a list is unknown, not untreated. In BP a list is held by 83% to 85% of the patients included until 2015 and 60% to 63% of those included from 2022.
The item number is the place in the exported list and changes between extractions: join two extractions on the content (patient, name and dates), never on item.
Whether the patient was on a group or a molecule on the day of a visit is delivered in the visit table by the instrument medications_at_visit, from the dates of these rows.
An end date missing with the reason 'running' is a treatment still taken. 'As needed' in the units a day is a missing code, and a long-acting injection has no units a day (SZ: interval_weeks).
A name that is not in the table of molecules keeps what was written and has no molecule and no group (unknown_code).

DR: the lists are crossed by the export (every product of the patient next to every prescription line). A patient with one product keeps every line; a patient with several products keeps one item per product, without form, dose or date (flag list_crossed). DR delivers the name of the substance of the drug catalogue (substance_name), not the product as typed.
ASP: the list is that of the visit (the table has the column visit), and it holds somatic drugs too.

common.note: In the table treatments. The name, the molecule, the ATC code and the group come from one table of names shared by the cohorts. The lists are not the same thing: the treatments of the patient with their dates in BP and SZ; the treatments of each visit in ASP; in DR the current and somatic lists are per visit but the export crosses the products and the lines of a patient (R122), so no dose and no date can be tied to a product of a patient who has several (194 patients), and its product is a substance name (substance_name), not the typed product name of the other cohorts. The daily dose is in mg in the four cohorts: BP and SZ compute it with the same rule (the stored strength, else the one written in the name of the product: BP decision D124), DR and ASP hold it as typed in mg.

medications_at_visit.title: Psychotropic treatments on the day of the visit

bp.notes: For each visit, whether the patient was on a group of medications, or on one of seven molecules, that day: 1 or 0. Computed from the rows of the table treatments (medications.yaml), with the rule of the application's page "Psychotropes présents aux visites" (D124): 1 when a medication of the group started on or before the visit date and has no end date, or an end date on or after the visit. Missing for the patients who have no medication list at all (1,719 of 6,498 patients: unknown, not untreated), for a visit without a date (5 visits of patients with a list), and where a medication of the group has no start date (150 medications) and no end before the visit, unless another one gives 1. A medication without an end date is taken as still running: an end that was never typed keeps the patient "on" the medication at every later visit. At the follow-up visits the yes of on_antidepressant, on_lithium and on_antipsychotic_2g rests only on medications with no end date for 78%, 88% and 79% of the cells (2,305 of 2,954, 3,827 of 4,368 and 3,138 of 3,984 cells supported by a medication started on or before the visit). For a third of the patients with a list and a follow-up visit (1,180 of 3,543), no medication starts or ends more than 30 days after the inclusion: at their follow-up visits the columns mostly repeat the inclusion. A medication that ends before it starts (148) counts at no visit. The 13 ends written 1950-01-02 had ended (the box "Traitement en cours" was not ticked), but with no start either they give a missing value, not a 1. A name that is not in medications.csv belongs to no group. on_valproate counts valproate and valpromide (Dépamide, which the body turns into valproic acid; D124): 617 visit cells of 226 patients went from 0 to 1, and 9 from 0 to missing (a valpromide without a start date).

Computed from the rows of the list medications: 1 when a medication of the group started on or before the visit date and has no end date, or an end date on or after the visit. In this cohort the dates are known for the patients who have one product only (see medications.yaml): for a patient with several products the answer is 0 when no product of the list is in the group, and missing when one is, because its dates are lost. So "on an antidepressant" is known on 972 visits (yes on 286) of the 1,836 visits of the patients who have a list, and "on lithium" is 1 on 19 visits although 51 patients list it: a 0 means that no listed product is in the group, not that the patient took none. Use the table treatments to know which molecules a patient has; use these columns only where they are filled. on_valproate counts valproate and valpromide (Dépamide, which the body turns into valproic acid), as in BP and SZ. One valpromide in the list of a patient with several products has no dates, so the 6 visit cells of this patient went from 0 to missing (no cell went from 0 to 1). The list holds 5 valproate and 1 valpromide items, for 5 patients.

DR: the lists are crossed by the export (every product of the patient next to every prescription line). They are missing for the patients who have no list (about a quarter in BP, a sixth in SZ); a treatment with no end date counts at every later visit (78%, 88% and 79% of the antidepressant, lithium and 2nd-generation antipsychotic yes of the follow-up visits rest on treatments with no end date); in DR, whose lists the export crossed, they are known on about half of the visits and a 0 means 'no listed product', not 'no'. ASP has no such columns.

non_drug_fu.title: Non-drug treatments since the last visit (follow-up visits)

bp.notes: Non-drug treatments since the last visit, asked at the follow-up visits (six-monthly and yearly), never at the inclusion (0 answers at the inclusion and at the screening): one yes/no question, then for each of six kinds a box, the number of sessions and the dates. 9,358 of the 11,686 follow-up visits answer the first question, and a third of the answers are yes (3,148 of 9,304; 54 "Ne sais pas"). Yes/no answers are delivered as 1 and 0; "Ne sais pas" is a missing code. The form also asks the number of sessions of the cognitive behavioural therapy and the start date of the psychoeducation groups: the clean model ebipolar_trt_sem.sql reads both (lines 37 and 41) and face_bp_12 does not select them (R125, which also asks for the SZ columns). The lifetime form of the patient has columns of its own, read by non_drug_lifetime.yaml. Asked only after a yes (asked_if). The six boxes are shown only after a yes to the first question, and a number of sessions only after a yes to its box; they are empty otherwise in the extraction and are read as 0. The dates stay missing: they are details of a treatment that did not take place. Boxes of one list (box_list, D124; kept by the project lead when the tab was reviewed again, R13). After a yes, some raters tick only the kinds received and leave the other boxes empty, more and more often: among the yes visits where a box is ticked, one box or more is left empty on 11% in 2011-2012 and on 35% to 42% in 2022-2025. An empty box beside a ticked box of the six is read as no, and its number of sessions as 0: 3,508 boxes on 880 visits that said yes, and 7 boxes on two visits that tick a box after a "no" or no answer. The boxes are Oui/Non radio buttons, so an empty one is not certain to be a no: 245 of the 880 visits hold an explicit "Non" on another kind, and the 393 empty boxes of those visits (11% of the 3,508 zeros, 33 to 101 per kind) may be unanswered; on the 635 other visits the rater wrote only the "Oui" and the blanks fit a rater who ticked what applied. Under a yes the boxes are blank on 356 (another treatment) to 772 visits (TMS) of the 3,148. Where all six boxes are empty after a yes (34 visits), they stay missing. 68 visits say yes and then no to all six kinds; they are delivered as recorded. After a no. The six boxes are empty on all but one of the 6,156 visits that answer no, the numbers of sessions on all but 4 cells (1 psychoeducation, 3 other treatment), and the dates hold only the application's 0000-00-00 (read as empty) or 1000-01-01 (below), but for 13 dates on 8 visits (10 of them ECT dates of 2009-2010). The first question is empty on 2,328 visits, with every box empty on all but one of them. IPSRT format. A closed list of the form (En groupe, En individuel, several allowed), delivered as two yes/no boxes, ipsrt_group_fu and ipsrt_individual_fu, 0 after a no to IPSRT (D124). 7 visits give it, all in individual sessions. Numbers of sessions. They count the sessions since the previous visit, a median of 11 months before for the counts above 0: divide by that time before comparing visits. Range 0 to 365 (D124); no value is cut, the largest is 100. The form checks one or two digits in the browser. 66 cells hold words, a rate or other text and end unparsed (57 of them for another treatment); they are of visits from 2011 to October 2021, and none of the 397 numbers typed since 2022 fails the check. One count typed as a minimum is censored on the right. They are not winsorised. Dates. The application writes 0000-00-00 in a date that was not typed (read as empty, 98,722 cells on 9,268 visits) and, since its version of 2024-07-25, which each centre got at its own date, 1000-01-01 (date_placeholder, 4,386 cells on 411 visits, 387 of them in 2025-2026), also next to a no (80 to 153 placeholder start dates per kind stand next to a kind box that is no: CBT and other 80, psychoeducation 98 for the end date, TMS 149, ECT 151, IPSRT 153). A date typed with the year 0000 is out_of_range (1). After a yes, the end date is missing more often than the start date (CBT 853 against 473 of 1,130 visits, another treatment 1,087 against 571 of 1,457): the treatment may have been running. 13 visits have an end before the start. Delivered as recorded: 21 dates on 12 visits stand next to a box that is no (16 of them ECT dates on 8 visits of 2009-2010); 4 numbers of sessions stand next to a box that is no and 5 next to a missing box; one visit says no to the first question and ticks psychoeducation, and one leaves it empty and ticks another treatment. Completeness. The first question is answered on 88% to 90% of the follow-up visits until 2015, 80% to 83% in 2016-2021 and 69% to 70% from 2022. In one centre it falls to 17% in 2022-2023 and 32% from 2024, with the rest of the follow-up care form (O40). Among the answers, the share of yes is 36% until 2012 and 29% in 2013-2015, then rises to 41% from 2024; it goes from 20% to 49% between the centres with 100 visits or more. Kinds. CBT, psychoeducation groups and IPSRT are specific therapies, not aggregates of every psychotherapy: a patient in another therapy belongs to "another". The kind of "another treatment" is free text, delivered as written: the name of a method of therapy, most often. Of the 1,335 follow-up texts, key words find kinds that DR asks as boxes of its own: supportive or unspecified therapy about 28%, psychoanalytic or psychodynamic 7%, mindfulness 5% to 7%, family or couple therapy 2% (shares only; the texts are not printed).

sz.notes: At the follow-up visits, never at the inclusion: did the patient have a non-drug treatment since the last visit (R14a: the question says "depuis la dernière visite"; a follow-up answer here is about that period, as in BP), then one yes/no per treatment. 2,297 visits answer the first question (836 yes, 1,421 no, 40 "Ne sais pas"). 1 is yes, 0 is no; "Ne sais pas" is a missing code. The treatments are answered after a yes to the first question, and the five contents of the cognitive behavioural therapy after a yes to that therapy (last answered between March and July 2019). After a "no" they are delivered as 0 (asked_if). Under a "no" the treatments are empty on 1,419 of 1,421 visits (2 answers to "another treatment" stand there), and under an empty first question on 2,644 of 2,644; no content of the cognitive behavioural therapy stands under a "no" or an empty answer to it. Boxes of one list (box_list, D124 and D131, kept by decision of the project lead: R13). After a yes, some raters tick only the treatments received and leave the other boxes empty. An empty box beside a ticked box of the same list is read as no: 722 boxes on 163 visits among the seven treatments of the current form, and 138 boxes on 56 visits among the five contents of the cognitive behavioural therapy, a list of their own (the 67 visits where the therapy itself is read as no add 335 contents that are 0 by asked_if: 473 cells of the contents in all). The boxes are Oui/Non radios, which R3 would leave missing; the rule stays as decided. How safe it is: on 60 of the 163 visits the rater also answered an explicit "Non" to another treatment, and the zeros of those visits are 114 of the 722 (16%: electroconvulsive therapy 35 of 133, magnetic stimulation 31 of 133, cognitive behavioural therapy 15 of 67, cognitive remediation 5 of 77, psychodynamic approach 9 of 96, family therapy 11 of 114, family psychoeducation 8 of 102): there a blank may be an unanswered box. On the 103 other visits no explicit "Non" stands next to the ticks (for the contents of the therapy, 20 of the 56 visits hold one). Where all seven treatments are empty after a yes (50 visits), they stay missing. 79 visits say yes and then no to all seven; they are delivered as recorded. "Another treatment" is not in the list: the form dropped it in 2019. It was last answered in August 2019, and none of the 390 yes visits from 2020 answer it: since then it is 0 after a "no" to the first question and missing after a yes. Sessions, dates and groups are in the application and not in the extraction (decision D73, request R125). The table of the follow-up form (psy_traitement_semestriel_sz) holds the number of sessions for the electroconvulsive therapy, the magnetic stimulation, "other" and the cognitive remediation, a start and an end date for 12 kinds (the electroconvulsive therapy, the magnetic stimulation, "other", the five contents of the cognitive behavioural therapy, the cognitive remediation, the psychodynamic approach, the family therapy and the family psychoeducation), the sets "in group / individually" for the five contents and the remediation, and the text of the tool of the remediation. The clean model eschizo_trt_sem reads them (so do the production lists of columns in source/fond_yaml), but face_sz_11 selects only the PROCCUR_ answers. The field table of the dump lists 8 fields of the block only, and is older than the table. So "no sessions and no dates in the form", written here before, was wrong: the form can hold them. The same questions as in FACE BP for the first one, the electroconvulsive therapy, the magnetic stimulation, the cognitive behavioural therapy and "another treatment", under the same names, in columns without the suffix _sem. The SZ form asks about cognitive remediation, the psychodynamic approach, family therapy and family psychoeducation instead of the psychoeducation group and the IPSRT of BP.
sz.difference: the columns have no suffix _sem; the sessions, the dates and the group or individual sets that the SZ form holds are not in the extraction (R125); other treatments are asked (cognitive remediation, psychodynamic approach, family therapy and psychoeducation)

dr.notes: Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT), transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) and psychotherapy, asked again at the follow-up visits: 819 visits (84% to 91% of the visits of each kind). ECT on 134 of 810 visits, TMS on 64 of 804. The question has no period. Form 203 asks the same questions, with no time frame, at the inclusion visit and at every follow-up visit, and the raters read them both ways. The BP and SZ forms say "since the last visit"; here the answer is a yearly update (asked again at the follow-up visit), never "since the last visit". The names ect_fu and tms_fu are kept for the join with BP and SZ, whose question says "since the last visit" (the catalogue notes it). Neither reading holds alone. Not "ever": 101 of the 151 follow-up visits of patients who had had ECT at inclusion answer no. Not "since the last visit": of the 106 ECT start dates typed at follow-up, 42 are more than a year before the visit and 68 before the previous visit, and for the supportive therapy 92 of 141 are more than a year before. And 71 of the 579 follow-up visits of patients who said no to ECT at inclusion say yes: new treatments, which either reading allows. Two forms in the same columns: the whole life at the inclusion visit, the question asked again at follow-up. visit_form says which form a visit uses, and each form has its own schema, as in BP. Answers are 0, 1 and 2: 2 is "not known" (missing_code). The codes of the form (203) are decoded as in non_drug_lifetime.yaml: kind of ECT stimulation 1 unilateral right, 2 bilateral; mean seizure longer than 25 seconds an item (2 not known: 31 of the 123 answers); kind of TMS stimulation 1 high frequency, 2 low frequency, 0 not known (26 of 61 answers). The count "more than 30 sessions" of the high-frequency TMS is shown only after type 1, the low-frequency count and the 30,000 question only after type 2 (shown_if; no cell changes; the 30,000 question has 4 answers "not known", missing_code). The question on psychotherapy (TT_PSYCHO) is a question of its own: the fourteen kinds of psychotherapies_fu.yaml disagree with it (see there).

non_drug_lifetime.title: Non-drug treatments over the life

bp.notes: Non-drug treatments over the life, in the second part of the patient's lifetime treatment form (drug_classes_lifetime.yaml reads the first): one yes/no question, then for each of six kinds (electroconvulsive therapy, TMS, cognitive behavioural therapy, psychoeducation groups, IPSRT, other) a box, the number of sessions and the start and end dates. Yes/no answers are delivered as 1 and 0; "Ne sais pas" is a missing code. The application itself words the first question "depuis la dernière visite", as on the follow-up form, and the dictionary copies it (D124). The answers are about the life: 301 of the 438 patients with a start date have one more than a year before their inclusion. A form of the patient, not of a visit: it is opened from the medication menu, can be saved again later, and its date is not exported (asked of the export). 1,271 patients answer the first question (570 yes, 680 no, 21 "Ne sais pas"), a fifth of the cohort, and rarely those included before 2013 (58 of 1,016). One value per patient. The extraction repeats these columns on every row of the patient. Where a patient has two records of the form, the export keeps one of them with no rule (R18 asks for the lowest id) and copies it onto every row: that is why the rows never differ. Asked only after a yes (asked_if). The six boxes are shown only after a yes to the first question, and a number of sessions only after a yes to its box; they are empty otherwise in the extraction and are read as 0. The dates stay missing: they are details of a treatment that did not take place. Boxes of one list (box_list, D124; kept by the project lead when the tab was reviewed again, R13). After a yes, some raters tick only the kinds received and leave the other boxes empty. An empty box beside a ticked box of the six is read as no, and its number of sessions as 0: 308 boxes of 96 patients (95 answered yes to the first question, one left it empty). The boxes are Oui/Non radio buttons, so an empty one is not certain to be a no: 47 of the 95 patients who answered yes hold an explicit "Non" on another kind, and the 71 empty boxes of those patients (23% of the 303 zeros after a yes) may be unanswered. Where all six boxes are empty after a yes (4 patients), they stay missing. 12 patients answer yes and then no to all six kinds; they are delivered as recorded. IPSRT format. A closed list of the form (En groupe, En individuel, several allowed), delivered as two yes/no boxes, ipsrt_group and ipsrt_individual, 0 after a no to IPSRT (D124). 4 of the 7 patients treated with IPSRT give it: all 4 in individual sessions, one also in a group. Numbers of sessions are typed freely: the field has no check. 16 cells hold a number with words and end unparsed (CBT 2, another treatment 14). ">N" and "+ N" are read as N, censored on the right (3 cells). They are not winsorised. Dates. The application writes 0000-00-00 in a date that was not typed (read as empty, 26,754 cells of 2,295 patients) and, since its version of 2024-07-25, which each centre got at its own date, 1000-01-01 (date_placeholder, 1,327 cells of 122 patients, 99 of them included in 2025-2026), also next to a no or an empty box. After a yes, the end date is missing more often than the start date (another treatment 227 against 97 of 353, CBT 96 against 31 of 193): the treatment may have been running. 4 patients have an end before the start, and 46 have a date after their inclusion (69 dates); they are delivered as recorded. Completeness. The first question is answered for 6% of the patients included until 2012 and 18% to 26% after. Among the 13 centres with 50 patients or more, four answer it for 41% to 69% of their patients and six for fewer than 7%. The share of yes is 23% until 2012, 32% in 2013-2015, 45% to 52% in 2016-2023 and 59% from 2024; it goes from 23% to 79% between the centres with 50 answers or more. Kinds. CBT, psychoeducation groups and IPSRT are specific therapies, not aggregates of every psychotherapy: a patient in another therapy belongs to "another". The kind of "another treatment" is free text, delivered as written: the name of a method of therapy, most often (see non_drug_fu.yaml for the kinds the follow-up texts name).

dr.notes: Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT), transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) and psychotherapy over the whole life, at the inclusion visit (form 203, which prints no period; read as the whole life at inclusion): 517 visits (72% to 89% of the inclusions in every period). ECT for 87 of 504 patients, TMS for 48 of 498, a psychotherapy for 248 of 502. The form is a patient form (level patient): the answers are in the table patients. Two forms in the same columns: the whole life at the inclusion visit, and at follow-up the same questions asked again with no period (see non_drug_fu.yaml; of the 151 follow-up visits of patients who had had electroconvulsive therapy at inclusion, 101 answer no). visit_form says which form a visit uses, and each form has its own schema, as in BP. Answers are 0, 1 and 2: 2 is "not known" (missing_code). The number of sessions is 0 after a no (asked_if); the other details stay missing after a no. The codes of the form (203) are decoded. Kind of ECT stimulation: 1 unilateral right, 2 bilateral. Mean seizure on the EEG longer than 25 seconds: an item (1 yes, 0 no, 2 not known: 49 of the 81 answers at inclusion, missing_code). Kind of TMS stimulation: 1 high frequency (100% of the motor threshold), 2 low frequency (120%), 0 not known (21 of 46 answers, missing_code). The form shows the count "more than 30 sessions" of the high-frequency TMS only after type 1 and the count of the low-frequency TMS and "30,000 stimulations or more" only after type 2 (f_traitement in formulaires.js): the three variables carry shown_if on the kind of stimulation. The data agree on all visits: 48 of 48 high-frequency counts follow type 1, 12 of 12 low-frequency counts follow type 2, none follows type 0 or an empty type, so no cell changes. The 30,000 question has 2 answers "not known" (2, missing_code) at inclusion and 4 at follow-up. The psychotherapies are detailed in psychotherapies_v0.yaml; ever_psychotherapy (TT_PSYCHO) is a question of its own and disagrees with the fourteen kinds there (see that schema): it is delivered as stored, with no derived "any psychotherapy".
