autoimmune_history_fu.title: Auto-immune diseases, at follow-up

sz.notes: A section that BP does not have, asked from 2015-02 (1,426 visits hold an answer, 1,402 of them a valid one; 8 are dated earlier; the section reached 56% of the inclusions of 2015 and 90% of those of 2016, centre by centre between 2015-02 and 2015-10): thirteen diseases, each with "treated at present". Nearly every answer is no; "Nc" is read as unknown (about 28 answers per disease, 364 cells; 23 visits answer "Nc" to all thirteen diseases and 5 more to twelve, dated 2015-05 to 2022-06: not known, not no). Five of the "treated" columns (rheumatoid arthritis, Sjögren, giant cell arteritis, scleroderma, sarcoidosis) are empty in the extraction. Psoriasis is in this section, not in the skin one. Yes/no answers are delivered as 1 and 0; "U" ("Ne sais pas") and "Nc" ("Non connu") are missing codes, both read as unknown (decision D52). "Treated" is asked after a yes and is missing otherwise. Two forms in the same columns, as in FACE BP (BP decisions D59 and D84; here decisions D20 and D56 in PROGRESS.md). The same questions are asked at the inclusion visit and at the yearly follow-up visits (every follow-up visit of the extraction is a yearly one; the 1,675 screening records hold no cell of the section). At inclusion they are about the whole life. At the yearly visits a disease answered yes at inclusion is most often answered no (39 of 47 follow-up answers for a head injury, 43 of 54 for acne). The yearly form is the inclusion form again, with no period in the wording of its questions, after one more question that the extraction does not hold: "Pas de changement de l'histoire somatique depuis la dernière visite?" (rad_pas_dechangement, shown at the yearly visit only; export request R78). An empty follow-up section may therefore mean "no change". A yearly answer is an update given at that visit: neither a history of the whole life nor strictly an answer about the time since the last visit. The two are delivered as separate columns ending in _v0 and _fu; visit_form says which form a visit used. From 2022 the section is answered at 32% of the inclusion visits, against 81% from 2016 to 2021 (and 3% to 83% by centre since 2022), while the share of all included patients with a disease of the section does not change: the shortcut "Non pour tous" of the section stopped copying "no" to each disease (script defect, A31 of EXPORT_REQUESTS.md); the extraction does not hold the shortcut (R78); an empty section is missing, not no; values as recorded (decision D51, open question O26). Do not compute a prevalence on the inclusions from 2022: among the answered visits the share with a disease goes from 3.1% to 7.2%, while it is 2.5% and 2.3% of all inclusion visits. At follow-up the section is held by 256 of the 2,588 yearly visits (1% to 36% of the yearly visits of a year from 2015); the other yearly visits leave it empty, which may mean "no change" (see the two forms above). The SZ form is shorter than the BP one: one question "treated" per disease, and no date of onset and no "controlled". The names are those of BP where the question is the same.

birchwood.title: Birchwood Insight Scale

sz.notes: Birchwood Insight Scale, filled at every visit (4,327 visits): eight statements, each 0 (disagree), 1 (unsure) or 2 (agree). The dictionary does not give the statements. Until the extraction of 13 November 2026 the eight items were empty: the export lost them (decision D1 in PROGRESS.md). Scores. Each stored score was fitted on the items. Awareness of symptoms is item 1 + item 8. Awareness of illness is item 7 + item 2 reversed. Need for treatment is items 4 and 5 plus items 3 and 6 reversed, halved. Each goes from 0 to 4 and the total from 0 to 12. They equal the stored ones but for 2 to 5 visits (score_mismatch); ours needs all its items. Scores typed with no item. 57 visits of 2011 to 2016 have a stored total and every answer present is "unsure" (86 cells, all 1), so the answers "agree" and "disagree", which the export probably loses (the apostrophe of D'accord and Pas d'accord, the loss of D1), are what is missing; 19 of them have no item at all. Where none of the items of a score is recorded and the stored score is, the stored score is delivered and flagged score_as_stored (otherwise, R18): symptoms 36 visits, illness 32, treatment 39 and total 24 (19 typed totals, and 5 totals added up from sub-scores of which some are delivered as stored). Where only some items are missing the score stays missing, because the stored one may be a partial sum (score_not_recomputed on 14, 21, 17 and 33 visits). The raw answers of these 57 visits are asked of the export (request R151 of docs/EXPORT_REQUESTS.md).

dsm5_alcohol.title: DSM-5 criteria of a use disorder: alcohol

sz.section: Critères DSM5 de troubles lié à l'usage de: ALCOOL
sz.notes: Twelve criteria of a use disorder for alcohol, answered from 2012 on 2,042 visits (589 with one criterion or more). Each criterion is asked twice: ever, and in the last 12 months. 1 is yes, 0 is no, and 2 is "do not know", read as a missing code. The second question is asked after a yes to the first (asked_if). The extraction never fills it after a no (0 of 20,731 such cells), so every 0 of the 12-month criteria comes from asked_if. Under a yes, 8 are empty and 22 are "do not know". The block is shown after a yes to the question "more than ten times in your life" of the SUBSTANCES tab (alcohol_over_ten_times; addict.js, lines 50 to 56). It is not written as a shown_if: the form hides the block but keeps what was typed, and 72 delivered cells on 3 visits sit under a no, none under an empty answer. A block empty on a visit with a yes to the use question was not answered: it stays missing, as it does where the use question is empty. After a no (ten times or fewer in the life) the block is never asked, and its criteria are 0: asked_if on alcohol_over_ten_times_gate, a hidden reader of the SUBSTANCES column suoccur_alcoollt (the user's decision of 2026-11-21). 10,752 cells of the criteria ever and as many of the 12-month criteria (asked after a yes to ever, so 0 too) become 0, on 896 visits; the two counts are 0 there (the count ever is filled on 1,960 visits before, 2,856 after). A criterion typed under a no is read as typed. The same twelve questions are asked for seven substances, in seven schemas with the same variables (dsm5_alcohol.yaml and the others; the stems are alcohol_, cannabis_, cocaine_, heroin_, opiate_, sedative_ and other_substance_). The first eleven are the DSM-5 criteria; the twelfth, legal problems, is a DSM-IV criterion. No count of criteria is stored. Two are computed here: the number of yes among the criteria a to k, ever and in the last 12 months (0 to 11). A "do not know" leaves the count missing, and the legal problems are not counted. No severity band is delivered: DSM-5 reads 2 or 3 criteria as mild, 4 or 5 as moderate, 6 or more as severe (APA 2013, as stated by Miller et al. 2023 and Choi et al. 2025). The application counts the criteria a to k for its own message (calcul_sympt, addict.js, lines 448 to 490) and does not store the count. The same form is used at inclusion and at the yearly visits (the yearly update, no split). The count "ever" is not always kept from one year to the next: 62 of the 158 yearly answers of the patients with one criterion or more at inclusion give a count of 0. With the gate on the use question, 86 of 182: at 24 yearly visits these patients answer no to "more than ten times in your life", although they met a criterion at inclusion: these zeros come from the use question, not from the criteria.

The extraction never fills it after a no (0 of 711 such cells), so every 0 of the 12-month criteria comes from asked_if. Under a yes, none is empty and none is "do not know". The block is shown after a yes to the question "more than ten times in your life" of the SUBSTANCES tab (other_product_over_ten_times; addict.js, lines 50 to 56). It is not written as a shown_if: the form hides the block but keeps what was typed, and 24 delivered cells on 1 visit sit under a no, none under an empty answer. A block empty on a visit with a yes to the use question was not answered: it stays missing, as it does where the use question is empty. After a no (ten times or fewer in the life) the block is never asked, and its criteria are 0 (the user's decisions of 2026-11-21). The use question of this substance (other_product_over_ten_times) is itself asked only after a yes to illicit drugs more than ten times (rad_add_4, illicit_drugs_over_ten_times of drug_use.yaml), and drug_use.yaml delivers it as 0 after a no there. The gate reproduces that chain with two hidden readers: other_substance_illicit_drugs_gate reads rad_add_4, and other_substance_over_ten_times_gate reads the SUBSTANCES column suoccur_autre_produitlt with asked_if on it, so the criteria are 0 wherever the delivered other_product_over_ten_times is 0. 38,688 cells of the criteria ever and as many of the 12-month criteria (asked after a yes to ever, so 0 too) become 0, on 3,224 visits; the two counts are 0 there (the count ever is filled on 78 visits before, 3,302 after). A criterion typed under a no is read as typed. The same twelve questions are asked for seven substances, in seven schemas with the same variables (dsm5_alcohol.yaml and the others; the stems are alcohol_, cannabis_, cocaine_, heroin_, opiate_, sedative_ and other_substance_). The first eleven are the DSM-5 criteria; the twelfth, legal problems, is a DSM-IV criterion. No count of criteria is stored. Two are computed here: the number of yes among the criteria a to k, ever and in the last 12 months (0 to 11). A "do not know" leaves the count missing, and the legal problems are not counted. No severity band is delivered: DSM-5 reads 2 or 3 criteria as mild, 4 or 5 as moderate, 6 or more as severe (APA 2013, as stated by Miller et al. 2023 and Choi et al. 2025). The application counts the criteria a to k for its own message (calcul_sympt, addict.js, lines 448 to 490) and does not store the count. The same form is used at inclusion and at the yearly visits (the yearly update, no split). The count "ever" is not always kept from one year to the next: 2 of the 5 yearly answers of the patients with one criterion or more at inclusion give a count of 0. With the gate on the use question, 14 of 17: at 12 yearly visits these patients answer no to "more than ten times in your life" (or to the illicit-drugs question), although they met a criterion at inclusion: these zeros come from the use question, not from the criteria.

ephp.title: EPHP, assessment of the processes of psychic handicap, filled by someone close to the patient

sz.notes: EPHP, filled from 2013 (1,802 visits): 13 items from 0 (great difficulty) to 6 (no difficulty), in four domains. The dictionary says that someone close to the patient fills it, at V0, V1, V3 and V5; the extraction holds it at every yearly visit (V0 953, V1 363, V2 180, V3 173, V4 73, V5 48, later visits 12). The code 7 is "cannot be assessed": 377 cells on 231 visits, read as a missing code in the items (ephp01 to ephp13), and as 0 in the scores. Scores. The four stored sub-scores are the sums of their items (1 to 4, 5 to 8, 9 to 11, 12 and 13), and the total is their sum. The scores count the code 7 as 0 points, as the application does since 2026-10-28 (the commit "score non-evaluable answers as zero"; A80 of docs/EXPORT_REQUESTS.md): the user's decision of 2026-11-21. They add up hidden copies of the items (ephp01_scored to ephp13_scored, keep: false) that keep the 7 (missing: {}) and count it 0 (points); the items themselves are delivered with the 7 as missing. A sum needs all its items, so the 17 visits with an item empty for another reason have no score (and no stored score). Since 0 means great difficulty, a score leans toward the worst rating where an item could not be assessed. No published rule for a non-evaluable item was found: the article (Passerieux, Bulot and Hardy-Baylé, Alter 2012) could not be read and no other source gives the scoring (literature check 2026-11-21). The scores gain a value on the visits with a 7: cognition 66 (1,727 to 1,793 visits), motivation 118 (1,673 to 1,791), communication 87 (1,704 to 1,791), self-assessment 46 (1,748 to 1,794), total 228 (1,557 to 1,785). The stored scores stay the check. Until 2026-10-28 the EMR script counted the 7 as 7 points, and every stored score of the extraction was computed so: the total is the sum with the 7 on 224 of the 225 visits with a 7 and a stored total, and 16 stored totals are above the maximum of 78 (up to 82). These visits get score_mismatch (total 4 to 229, cognition 2 to 67, motivation 2 to 120, communication 1 to 87, self-assessment 1 to 45); the score_not_recomputed of the stored scores (225 on the total) are gone. Outside the 7 the scores match the stored ones but for 1 to 4 visits each.

physical_activity.title: Physical activity over the last seven days

sz.notes: Physical activity over the last seven days, filled from 2012 (3,266 visits): days of vigorous activity, of moderate activity and of walking, the time per day, the walking pace and the time spent sitting. Each duration has two fields, hours and minutes, and patients use them in three ways: both (1,575 visits for walking), hours only (615) or minutes only (662), and 25 to 42 cells per field hold 60 minutes or more, a whole duration typed in the minutes. The two fields are delivered as typed; a duration is hours + minutes / 60 where both are read as parts, which the analyst decides. Four values are out of range (minutes outside 0 to 1,440: vigorous 1, moderate 1, sitting on a weekday 2). No sitting time in hours is above 24, where the DR form holds 75 such weekday answers (M79 of docs/EXPORT_REQUESTS.md). The time per day is asked for "such a day", so the two fields and the walking pace are shown_if the number of days is 1 to 7 (the field table of the application lists no dependence for them: the rule is the structure of the question). 7 cells are not_shown: 4 typed under 0 days (vigorous hours 1, moderate hours 2, moderate minutes 1) and 3 under an empty number of days. The dictionary gives the labels of the moderate activity to the two walking durations (ipa0106a, ipa0106b); their fields are those of the walking question. The walking pace (ipa0106c; here 1 slow, 2 moderate, 3 brisk, as the form prints it) was empty until the extraction of 13 November 2026 (decision D1 in PROGRESS.md); the DR form stores the pace the other way round (1 brisk) and the DR schema reads it back to this direction. The form's box "done / not done" (rad_actphys_nf) is not in the extraction (export request R152).

dr.notes: The SZ schema in the columns of this extraction (qiap01a to qiap04bm). Physical activity over the last seven days: days of vigorous activity, of moderate activity and of walking, the time per day, the walking pace and the time spent sitting. Filled at inclusion and at the visits of 1, 2 and 4 years: 940 visits, 80% or more of the inclusions in every period. The break of 2018 does not touch it. Each duration has two fields, hours and minutes; both are delivered as typed, as in SZ. No total is computed. The form asks for the hours and minutes of an activity only when its number of days is 1 or more, and for the walking pace after a number of walking days (script of the form, the function f_autoq_qiap): the durations and the pace are delivered only then (shown_if). 42 typed cells are not delivered (not_shown): 34 under 0 days, the clear case, and 8 under an empty number of days (the same rule; the form hides them too). Walking pace. This form stores 1 brisk, 2 moderate and 3 slow (form 217); SZ stores 1 slow, 2 moderate and 3 brisk. The pace is turned to the SZ order (written as codes), so that the same number means the same pace in the two cohorts. As stored it went the wrong way: its rank correlation with age was +0.13 and with the days of vigorous activity -0.18, and it is -0.13 and +0.18 once turned (older patients walk more slowly, active ones more briskly). 347 cells change: every 1 and every 3. Hours above 24. The time spent sitting on a weekday is above 24 hours on 75 visits and on a weekend day on 28 (25 to 99: probably the hours of the whole week; 60 of the 75 are multiples of 5), the walking time on 4 and the moderate activity on 1: out_of_range, not delivered. The question to the centres is O21 (M79).

sogs.title: South Oaks Gambling Screen (SOGS)

sz.notes: South Oaks Gambling Screen, filled from 2014 by few patients (146 visits; the questions on borrowed money, 16a to 16k, on 13). Until the extraction of 13 November 2026 nine items were empty (decision D1 in PROGRESS.md). The dictionary gives the wording of questions 2, 4, 5 and 6 only (for 4, 5 and 6, the last 12 months); the yes/no items keep their number. 22 of the columns are not in its list. Coding, as the export writes it. Item 4 is not in order of frequency: 1 most of the times I lose, 2 sometimes (less than half of the times), 3 every time. Items 1a to 1g: 1 at least once a week, 2 less than once a week. The export reads the answers of item 6 as "no" and "yes, some months ago but not now" only: the answer "yes" is lost (0 on 90 visits, 1 on 28, empty on 28, never 2); export request R151 of docs/EXPORT_REQUESTS.md. Gate. Item 16 (borrowed money) opens 16a to 16k (asked_if): after a no they are 0 (130 of the 132 visits with a no had them empty; the other 2 hold an answer and keep it). Item 3a (the relatives, a text) is empty on the 118 visits with a no to item 3 and filled on 23 of the 24 with a yes: asked_if does not apply to a text, so no gate is written. Total. It is delivered as stored. Its key is in the application script (sogs.js, calcul, lines 118 to 139, the item 4 rule in valeur_champ, lines 49 to 58; A80 of docs/EXPORT_REQUESTS.md): item 4 counts 1 for any answer, "never" included, so that every stored total is 1 or more (58 of 122 equal 1; the published form scores item 4 only for "most of the time" and "every time" (Lesieur and Blume 1987; English form and score sheet revised 2003). The score-sheet line of item 4 is garbled, so this rule rests on the form, and the appendix of the 1987 paper is still to be read (literature check 2026-11-21); items 5 and 6 count 1 for any answer but the first; items 7 to 11, 13 to 15 and 16a to 16i count 1 for a yes; item 12 and 16j and 16k are not counted; the maximum is 20. On the 94 totals that the delivered items allow to recompute, the key gives the stored one on 90. The total is not recomputed here while the export loses the answer "yes" of item 6 and some answers written with an apostrophe (8 stored totals have no item 5); to be seen again once the export is put right, with the choice of the item 4 rule.

sqol.title: Schizophrenia Quality of Life questionnaire (S-QoL 18)

sz.notes: S-QoL 18, filled at every visit (4,330 visits): 18 items of 1 to 5, eight dimensions and an index, each from 0 to 100. Scoring, fitted on the items: a dimension is the mean of its items brought to 0 to 100, (mean - 1) x 25, and the index is the mean of the eight dimensions. The dictionary gives the items of each dimension, and the data agree: no score_mismatch on the eight dimensions recomputed here. The EMR export stores a dimension when at most one of its items is missing (the mean of the others, as the nucleus rule says), so the dimensions are computed with min_items 1 (two items) or 2 (three items: resilience and psychological well-being), all equal to the stored ones (D87). The stored index is the mean of seven or eight dimensions rounded to one decimal, hence the tolerance: the index recomputed with min_items 7 equals the stored one on its 4,256 visits (211 rest on seven dimensions). Items 17 and 18 were mis-coded by the export up to SZALL_20261117: it read them with the labels "much less than expected" to "more than expected", where the form gives them the answers of item 16 (from "much more than expected", 1, to "less than expected", 5, the best), so the answer 5 was delivered as 2, the answer 2 as 5, and the answers 1 and 3 were lost (D87, O8). The export reads them with the labels of item 16 since SZALL_20261121 (request R150, export commit fcbdfb31): the two items hold 1 to 5 and correlate +0.39 and +0.44 with item 16 (rank correlation), and the stored psychological dimension and index are computed again from them. Items 17 and 18, the psychological dimension and the index are delivered again (D104). The psychological dimension is recomputed like the others (min_items 2, three items) and the index is the mean of at least seven of the eight dimensions, the rule of the nucleus. The 18 boxes "does not concern me" of the form (chk_sqol_N_pc, exported as sqolNN_pc since SZALL_20261121) are delivered as 1 (ticked) and 0. The raw cell holds OUI, NON or def, and is empty on the visits without the questionnaire. def is read as a box not ticked: on 574 visits some boxes are OUI and all the others def, as on the visits of NON (the meaning of def is asked of the data managers, O47). The application leaves a ticked item out of its dimension and a dimension whose items are all ticked out of the index (autoq_qualite_vie.js); the export, and this schema, average the answers present, which gives the same value except where an answer sits beside a ticked box (124 cells): the answer is delivered as recorded and the dimension keeps it (O47).

sqol.description: Schizophrenia Quality of Life questionnaire, 18-item form, filled by the patient at every visit. Items of 1 to 5, a box 'does not concern me' beside each item, eight dimensions and an index from 0 to 100.
sqol.reference: Boyer L, Simeoni MC, Loundou A, et al. The development of the S-QoL 18. Schizophr Res 2010;121:241-250

The five stored totals are the sums of their ten items but for 1 to 4 visits each (score_mismatch: 2, 2, 1, 1 and 4). 62 to 66 visits per stage have the items and no stored total (the totals are computed on a button): the recomputed stage is delivered there. yale_brown.title: Yale-Brown Obsessive Compulsive Scale (Y-BOCS), past week

sz.notes: Y-BOCS, about the past week, filled from 2015 by the patients with obsessions or compulsions (291 visits): five items for the obsessions and five for the compulsions, each 0 to 4. The dictionary does not name the items; the labels are those of the published scale in its order. The sub-totals go from 0 to 20 and the total from 0 to 40 (range on the scores). The stored sub-totals are the sums of the five items on nine visits in ten: 25 and 26 score_mismatch, and 28 on the total. All of them are on visits of 2015 and 2016 (decision D23 in PROGRESS.md). Four stored scores (one sub-total of each kind and two totals) have an item missing and no recomputed score (score_not_recomputed). Not loaded: ybobse1 to ybobse5 and ybcomp1 to ybcomp5, which the dictionary calls "scores, level" of the same ten items (ignored.yaml; the open question O10 is answered, decision D84). They are the summary block of the form (the radio fields radhtml_syb1 to radhtml_syb10): a copy of the ten answers that the patient or the rater could edit by hand until the commit of 2026-10-26 of the application, which made it read-only and filled it from the ten items. The stored sub-totals that differ from the sum of the items (25 and 26 visits, all in 2015 and 2016) equal the sum of the summary block on every one of them, so the old script added the block, not the items. The block equals the item on 55% of the cells only, because it was typed apart. The delivered sums are the current rule (the items), the stored ones are the check, and the block has no twin score.

toxoplasmose.title: Toxoplasmosis serology

sz.notes: Asked from 2012. Was a toxoplasmosis serology done (2,159 "yes" of 2,828 answers), and if so: are the IgM positive (91 of 2,123), are the IgG positive (704 of 2,122), and the IgG titre of the positive patients (632 results). Where no serology was done the two results are empty, not "no". The titre depends on the centre: its median goes from 14 to 137 UI/mL between the six centres that have 30 results or more, ten times more in one than in another. The laboratories do not use the same assay, so the titres of two centres should not be compared. The titre is delivered as typed, to be read within one centre. Every titre belongs to an IgG-positive patient. 27 titres are under 5 UI/mL (3 written with "<") and 4 under 1 (one written with "<"): another assay or scale, or a status and a titre that disagree; the centres should be asked. 16 results are written with ">" (censored_right) and 5 with "<"; one is out of range. The clip at the 99th percentile turns a high titre into the cut value (6 results); the hard range, 0 to 10,000, is what removes impossible values. The unit column of the titre (tgnigmab_lborresu) is empty. A seventh centre, with 26 results, has a median of 240 UI/mL (1.9 IQR above the cohort median of 41, IQR 103), so the centre medians go from 14 to 240 UI/mL; it is read like the others, within one centre.

toxoplasmose.description: Toxoplasmosis serology (SZ, from 2012): whether it was done, IgM positive (recent infection), IgG positive (past infection), and the IgG titre of the positive patients in UI/mL.
flags: The titre depends on the assay of each centre (centre medians from 14 to 240 UI/mL): do not compare titres between centres; read it within one centre.
Where no serology was done the two results are empty, not 'no'.
The upper tail of the titre is clipped at the 99th percentile; results written with '<' or '>' are censored.

vitamine_d.title: Vitamin D

sz.notes: 25-hydroxyvitamin D, measured from 2013, and three questions that go with it: the time spent outdoors, the skin phototype and a supplement in the last twelve months. The three answers change between the visits of many patients, so they are kept per visit. The unit is not recorded: the dictionary gives none, and the unit column (vitd_lborresu) holds one cell. Among the nine centres with 30 results or more, eight have a median of 37 to 65, the size of results in nmol/L, with 8% to 38% of their results under 30. One centre (311 results) has a median of 24 and 66% of its results under 30, the size of results in ng/mL. That holds in 2015 to 2021 (258 results, median 22, 72% under 30) and from 2024 (29 results, median 28, 59% under 30), but not in 2022 (24 results, median 64, 12% under 30). The factor 2.496 (1 ng/mL in nmol/L) brings its median of 2015 to 2021 to 55, against 52 in the other centres in the same years (53 over all years): the two readings agree. A second centre has medians of 31 and 29 in 2016 and 2017 (108 results, about half under 30) and 36 to 56 in its other years with 9 results or more: a spell in ng/mL is possible there too. The value is delivered as written, with no unit, and no variable in nmol/L is delivered: the centres must say in which unit and in which period each of them reported (open question O7 in PROGRESS.md). 11 results are written with "<" (censored_left). Two results of 0 are out of range. The clip at the 99th percentile turns a high clinical value into the cut value (27 results); the hard range, 1 to 400, is what removes impossible values.

dr.notes: 25-hydroxy vitamin D, on 1,025 visits, delivered in nmol/L. The form has a choice of five units, exported as a code: 1 nmol/L, 2 ng/L, 3 µg/L, 4 mmol/L, 5 ng/mL. Codes 3 and 5 are the same scale (quartiles 15, 22 and 31): 198 results are converted to nmol/L. Code 4 is read as nmol/L: no vitamin D is counted in mmol/L, and its median (62) is that of code 1 (64). Code 2, "ng/L", holds 109 values of two kinds. 41 are 3,000 or more: true ng/L, read by their size and converted (unit_inferred). 68 are below 1,000 and have the quartiles of ng/mL (16, 23.5 and 31, against 15, 22 and 31 for codes 3 and 5) and not those of nmol/L (43, 64 and 84, code 1): the label names the wrong unit. The alias "2" of the ng/mL unit reads them as ng/mL: 60 are converted (unit_converted: a label that fits is believed), 2 of 160 or more fit only nmol/L and are read as such (unit_inferred), and 6 below 0.2 stay out_of_range. The 59 results that were removed before and are delivered now have a median of 60 nmol/L (quartiles 49 and 79), against 64 for code 1. Open question O10 in PROGRESS.md: did the centres mean ng/mL? Once harmonised, the yearly median stays between 47 and 67 nmol/L from 2013 to 2026 (years with 10 results or more). Values are winsorised at the 1st and 99th percentiles: the 20 cells in the tails become the cut values (11.7 and 168 nmol/L), so a clinical tail turns into the cut value, and the hard range of 8 to 400 removes the impossible values. A number typed in the unit field marks 23 of the 30 visits of one centre whose block of results is shifted (see the blood-count schema): 14 hold an impossible vitamin D, removed by the range, and none holds a vitamin D that would be delivered. This schema belongs to the pool biology (implausible_visits: 3, implausible_pool: biology; see the blood-count schema): a visit with three or more impossible values over the eleven laboratory schemas of DR loses all its values and gets visit_removed. The pool removes 35 visits in all (1,403 cells); this schema loses 4 cells on 4 of the 5 other visits and none on the block. The 41 results read as ng/L by their size are all of one centre, dated 2014 to 2016 (26 in 2015). FACE SZ has the same instrument without a unit: its values are delivered as written and must not be compared with these.
dr.difference: the unit is recorded and the result is delivered in nmol/L, where SZ has no unit; the form's "ng/L" holds values of the size of ng/mL and is read as ng/mL where the value fits that scale; the questions on sun exposure and supplements are not in the TRD extraction

asp.notes: 25-hydroxy vitamin D, on 255 inclusion visits and 46 follow-up visits. Same analyte, name and target unit (nmol/L) as in FACE DR. Vitamin D is one of the five analytes that have a unit column. It holds a catalogue number, not a label (the list of the form: 67432 nmol/L, 67306 µg/L, 64387 mmol/L, 67327 ng/L): 67432 on 251 results (read as nmol/L), 67306 on 19 (ng/mL: their median is 17.1), 64387 on 26 and 67327 on 5. 64387 is the number that the cholesterol column uses for mmol/L, a unit that no vitamin D result can be in. Its 26 results are read as nmol/L, as FACE DR reads its code 4: their median (39.5, 23% under 30) is that of the nmol/L results (median 48.0, 21% under 30) and not that of the ng/mL ones (89% under 30), and they come from the same four centres as the 67432 results. The confidence is medium: the size of the values decides, not the label. Before this reading they were delivered as missing. 67327 (ng/L on the form) holds 5 results of the size of ng/mL or nmol/L, not of thousands of ng/L: they are not read as ng/L, and 3 of them fit both units and stay unit_unknown. 7 results under 1 fit no unit (out_of_range). Delivered: 291 of the 301 results. The readings of the numbers stay open question O6. The default clip at the 1% and 99% percentiles turns a clinical tail into the cut value (5 of the 291 values here); the hard range is what removes impossible values (7 results here).
asp.difference: the unit column holds catalogue numbers, read as nmol/L and ng/mL; the number of mmol/L (64387) is read as nmol/L, as DR reads its code 4, because the values have that size

vitamine_d.description: 25-hydroxyvitamin D from the blood sample of the visit (SZ from 2013, DR, ASP); SZ adds the time spent outdoors, the skin phototype and a vitamin D supplement in the last twelve months.
flags: SZ: the unit is not recorded. vitamin_d_as_written must not be pooled across centres as one scale, nor compared with the vitamin_d of DR and ASP, until the centres say in which unit they reported.

DR and ASP: some unit codes name a unit that the values do not fit, and are read by the size of the value (medium confidence in ASP). By default each number is clipped at its 1st and 99th percentiles (winsorising), so a clinical tail becomes the cut value; only the hard range removes impossible values. Load with winsorise=False to keep the tails.

common.note: vitamin_d is in nmol/L in DR and ASP (DR code 2 read as ng/mL by size, ASP code 64387 read as nmol/L). SZ records no unit and one centre writes ng/mL, so its value is delivered under another name (vitamin_d_as_written) and must not be stacked.

lifetime_symptoms.title: Psychotic symptoms over the whole life and in the last month

sz.notes: Twenty-two symptoms (ten delusions, ideas of reference, four kinds of hallucination, catatonia, three signs of disorganisation and three negative symptoms), each answered twice at the inclusion visit: ever, and present in the last month. 2,185 visits answer at least one symptom, all of them inclusion visits, and 1,148 answer the 22. 1 is yes, 0 is no; "Ne sais pas" is a missing code (66 to 224 answers per symptom for the first question, 6 to 61 for the second). The second question is shown after a yes to the first and only then: the field of the form depends on the first one, at its first option, for each of the 22 pairs (the table of the form, psy_diag_psychiatrique_sz). The cell is filled after a yes (15,896 of the 15,911 cells of the second question, 1,649 of 1,650 for the delusion of persecution) and empty after a no. It is 0 here after a no (asked_if on the first question): 27,142 cells at inclusion, the 22 variables together. After "Ne sais pas" to the first question it stays missing. 8 answers "yes in the last month" sit under a "no" to the first question and stay as typed. After a yes, the second answer is blank on 1,560 of 17,456 cells, and on 87 of the 2,170 visits with a yes every second answer is blank (4%).

lifetime_symptoms.description: Twenty-two psychotic symptoms (ten delusions, ideas of reference, four kinds of hallucination, catatonia, three signs of disorganisation and three negative symptoms), each answered twice at the inclusion visit of FACE SZ: ever, and present in the last month.
lifetime_symptoms.period: lifetime (ever) and the last month, as recorded at the inclusion visit
sources: respondent: the questions are on the diagnostic form (table psy_diag_psychiatrique_sz), the form that asks 'does the patient have an anxiety disorder' (schema notes, sz anxiety_v0)
flags: Inclusion visits only: 2,185 visits answer at least one symptom and 1,148 answer the 22.
After a yes to 'ever' the last-month answer is blank on 1,560 of 17,456 cells, and on 87 of the 2,170 visits with a yes every last-month answer is blank: a blank there is missing, not 'no'.
'Ne sais pas' is a missing code: 66 to 224 answers per symptom for 'ever', 6 to 61 for the last month.

psychosis_course.title: Course of the psychotic disorder

sz.notes: At the inclusion visit: the age at the first psychotic episode and at the first antipsychotic treatment, the duration of untreated psychosis in months, the number of psychotic episodes and the course of the symptoms (2,244 visits answer at least one of these). At every visit: a psychotic episode in the past year, a suicide attempt in the past year and their number (4,549 visits answer at least one of the three). The follow-up form of the application has its own course question and its 12-month questions on violence and substances; the export does not read them (request R141, face_sz_9_evaluation_medicale.sql lines 20 to 34 and 81). The export keeps one row per visit, the most complete, and breaks ties arbitrarily (lines 118 to 133); no visit of the extraction has a duplicate (question to the data managers). "Ne sais pas" is a missing code (41 and 44 ages, 163 answers on the episode of the past year); so is 999 in the duration (14). The number of episodes holds "Aucun" on 37 visits, read as 0, and "more than 20" on 21 (censored_right). "<5" is read as 5 (censored_left) on 4 cells: one age at the first episode, two ages at the first treatment, one duration. Two more answers of the duration are words typed in the box of months (one word and one of three words): they are unparsed and stay missing. The name. first_psychotic_episode_age is the age at the first psychotic episode (it was first_episode_age; R12). DR delivered its age at the first depressive episode under the same name, which is another question; the hub of the export maps this column to AGEDEBUTPremier_episode (face_sz_all.sql, line 283), the name of the first mood episode in BP. The duration of untreated psychosis is a number of months, typed in a numeric field. It is not the difference between the two ages, which are in whole years, and it is not delivered as typed: 15 cells (192 to 360 months) are winsorised to 184, and the one cell of 680 is out of range (the maximum is 600). 14 durations are longer than the time since the first episode (the difference of the age at the visit and the age at the first episode, in whole years) plus 12 months. The number of attempts in the past year is shown after a yes to the attempt question and is 0 here after a no (asked_if): 4,319 cells, 2,041 at inclusion and 2,278 at follow-up. It is a number that is not winsorised (a count of events that is 0 for most visits), from 0 to 20: the list of the form is 0 to 20 and ">20", which would be read as censored at 20 (no cell holds it; 17 is the largest value). After a yes it is filled on 116 of the 126 inclusion visits and on 51 of the 53 follow-up visits; it is 0 after a yes on 3 inclusion visits and 1 follow-up visit. Consistency. The age at the first episode is above the age at the visit on 8 visits (2 by more than a year), and the age at the first antipsychotic treatment on 17 (2 by more than a year): they are delivered as written and flagged check_failed (not_above the age at the visit). The first treatment is before the first episode on 65 of 2,093 visits that have both (50 by 2 years or more). The course says a single episode and the number of episodes is 2 or more on 33 of 168 visits (165 have a number); it says episodic and the number is 1 on 172 of 1,183 (1,060 have a number). A psychotic episode in the past year (yes at inclusion) has a number of episodes of 0 on 7 inclusion visits and no number on 135.

psychosis_course.description: The course of the psychotic disorder in FACE SZ. At the inclusion visit: the age at the first psychotic episode and at the first antipsychotic treatment, the duration of untreated psychosis in months, the number of psychotic episodes and the course of the symptoms. At every visit: a psychotic episode in the past year, a suicide attempt in the past year and the number of attempts.
psychosis_course.period: lifetime (inclusion visit); the past year (every visit)
flags: Two periods in one instrument: the ages, the duration, the number of episodes and the course are asked at the inclusion visit (2,244 visits); the three past-year questions at every visit (4,549 visits).
The follow-up form has its own course question and 12-month questions on violence and substances; the export does not read them (R141).

Delivered as written: the first treatment is before the first episode on 65 of 2,093 visits (50 by 2 years or more); the course says a single episode with 2 or more episodes on 33 of 168 visits, and episodic with 1 episode on 172 of 1,183.

An age above the age at the visit is flagged check_failed (8 first-episode ages, 17 first-treatment ages). 14 durations of untreated psychosis are longer than the time since the first episode plus 12 months.
'Ne sais pas' is a missing code, and so is 999 in the duration. '<5' is read as 5 (censored_left) on 4 cells.
Who fills the form is not stated in the notes.

violent_behaviours.title: Violent behaviours

sz.notes: At the inclusion visit (1,816 visits; no other visit holds an answer): four kinds of violent behaviour of the patient over the whole life (verbal, physical, sexual, breaking of objects). For each: inside or outside the family, an intervention of the police, a conviction and its sentence; for the physical violence also blows and wounds, with or without a weapon, whether the other person needed care, and homicide; for the sexual violence its kind. 1 is yes, 0 is no. The form puts the question as "has the subject presented, over the whole life". The details hang on a gate in the form (the table psy_ecv_nom_champ): the type, the police and the conviction on the question of the kind of violence, the sentence on the conviction; for the physical violence the blows and homicide on the physical violence, and the weapon and the care needed on the blows, not on the physical violence. A detail is filled after a yes and empty otherwise. The ten yes/no questions that hang on a gate (the police and the conviction of the four kinds, the blows, the care needed) are 0 after a no on their gate (asked_if): 12,613 cells, the cascade included (the care needed hangs on the blows: 1,195 cells after a no to the physical violence, 211 after blows and wounds "no"). The sets (type, weapon, sentence) are left as they are: an empty cell of a set is not a no. Cells that list several boxes ("Intrafamiliale,Extrafamiliale", the weapons, the sentences) are read as one yes/no per box. The firearm is written "Arme ? feu" in the extraction: the accented letter was lost by the export. Homicide (decision D80; closes open question O21). rad_ecv_vp5 is the question "Homicide" of the physical violence (field 136 of the form), committed by the patient over the whole life, and is delivered as violence_physical_homicide: 603 answers (8 yes) after a yes to the physical violence and 0 after a no (1,195), 1,798 valid cells in all. 12 of the 615 visits with a physical violence have the answer blank. Of the 8 yes, 6 also hold blows and wounds, 6 an intervention of the police and 5 a conviction. Roll-out. The block is answered on 6%, 10% and 15% of the inclusion visits of 2010, 2011 and 2012, 33% in 2013, 50% in 2014 and 81% to 99% from 2015.

violent_behaviours.description: Violent behaviours of the patient over the whole life, at the inclusion visit of FACE SZ: four kinds (verbal, physical, sexual, breaking of objects) and, for each, inside or outside the family, an intervention of the police, a conviction and its sentence; for the physical violence also blows and wounds, with or without a weapon, whether the other person needed care, and homicide; for the sexual violence its kind.
sources: respondent: the form puts the question in the third person ('has the subject presented, over the whole life')
flags: Roll-out: the block is answered on 6%, 10% and 15% of the inclusion visits of 2010, 2011 and 2012, 33% in 2013, 50% in 2014 and 81% to 99% from 2015. Inclusion visits only (1,816 visits).
The ten yes/no questions that hang on a gate (police and conviction of the four kinds, blows and wounds, care needed) are read as 0 after a no on their gate.
The sets (inside or outside the family, weapon, sentence) are one yes/no per box and are left as they are: an empty cell of a set is not a 'no'.

aims.title: Abnormal Involuntary Movement Scale (AIMS)

sz.notes: Rated by the clinician at every visit. Seven items on the movements (face, lips, jaw, tongue, upper limbs, lower limbs, trunk), then the overall severity, the incapacitation and the patient's awareness, each from 0 to 4, and two yes/no items on the teeth. The dictionary gives the body parts of items 1 to 9. Total. The extraction stores no AIMS score and the application computes none. aims_movements is the sum of the seven movement items (0 to 28 by construction, 0 to 24 observed on 4,149 visits); it needs its seven items and cannot be compared with a stored value. In the one source read the published total is the ten components, items 1 to 10 (0 to 40) (Menzies and Farrell 2002 after Guy 1976; scale_reference.md, section 9); whether items 8 to 12 enter a total of the manual is unknown, as the 1976 manual itself could not be read (literature check 2026-11-21). The overall severity (item 8) equals the highest of items 1 to 7 on 3,422 of 4,111 visits (it is higher on 18 and lower on 671); no source read states a rule that links item 8 to items 1 to 7 (literature check 2026-11-21). Teeth (decision D78; closes open question O6). aims0111 is item 11, current problems with teeth or dentures (field rad_pbactu, order 18 in the form), and aims0112 is item 12, the patient usually wears dentures (rad_portprothese, order 19). The form and the export agree on this (eschizo_hetero_aims.sql, lines 84 to 91). Only the dictionary swaps them: it names them in one line with two orders, "11: portprothese, 12: pbactu" for the labels and "rad_pbactu et rad_portprothese" for the fields, copied from the order of the columns of the table. The first is "yes" on 13% of the visits and the second on 6%. In the published scale items 11 and 12 are the dental status (current problems with teeth or dentures, usually wears dentures); which of the two is 11, and their yes/no coding, could not be confirmed: the source read (Menzies and Farrell 2002) asks about both without numbering them (literature check 2026-11-21). No item loses an answer: the levels 0 to 4 all occur, the highest rarely.

aims.description: Abnormal Involuntary Movement Scale, rated by the clinician at every visit (SZ): seven items on the movements by body area, then the overall severity, the incapacitation and the patient's awareness, each from 0 to 4, and two yes/no items on the teeth.
aims.reference: Guy W. ECDEU Assessment Manual for Psychopharmacology, revised 1976, as cited in Menzies V, Farrell SP. Schizophrenia, tardive dyskinesia, and the AIMS. J Am Psychiatr Nurses Assoc 2002;8:51-56
aims.reference_confidence: confirmed in source (secondary); 1976 edition itself not read
flags: aims_movements is not the published total: in the one source read the total is the ten components, items 1 to 10 (0 to 40). The application computes no AIMS score.

The published rule for probable tardive dyskinesia is on the items, not on the sum: at least moderate (3 or more) in one body area or at least mild (2 or more) in two areas, after at least 3 months of antipsychotic exposure and no other cause (confirmed in source: Gharabawi 2005 abstract, Menzies and Farrell; the wording of Schooler and Kane 1982 is 'to verify'). It is not delivered.
The two dental items are yes/no. The dictionary swaps their numbers; the schema follows the form: aims_dental_problems is item 11 and aims_dentures item 12.

barnes.title: Barnes Akathisia Rating Scale

sz.notes: Rated by the clinician at every visit. Three items from 0 to 3 and a global clinical assessment. The dictionary does not name the three items; the labels are those of the published scale in its order (objective, awareness of restlessness, distress). The global assessment goes from 0 to 5 in the form (six options: absent, doubtful, mild, moderate, marked, severe) and in the published scale (Barnes 1989; scale_reference.md, section 10); the dictionary says 0 to 4, which is wrong: 15 visits hold a 4 and 3 hold a 5. Akathisia from a global rating of 2 is the natural reading (2 is the first level called akathisia, mild), but no source read states it as a cut-off (the Barnes 1989 abstract and a reproduction of the scale; literature check 2026-11-21). Stored scores. bars0105 ("sum of the objective and subjective ratings") is the sum of the three items, as the script of the form computes it on a button (hetero_barnes.js, line 16): equal on 4,349 of 4,352 visits. The three others are stored one below the items (score_mismatch; probably an item edited after the button was clicked), and 20 visits with the three items have no stored value. It is read to check ours and is not delivered. bars0106, called "total Barnes score (akathisia if 2 or more)", is the global assessment again (the script copies the global item into barnes_score): equal to bars0104 on 4,359 of 4,360 visits. It is not loaded (ignored.yaml). The columns are named bars01xx for the Barnes scale. The columns bars01 to bars03 and bars_ are another instrument, the Brief Adherence Rating Scale (bars.yaml); the two share the dictionary prefix BARS.

barnes.description: Barnes Akathisia Rating Scale, rated by the clinician at every visit (SZ): three items from 0 to 3 (objective restlessness, awareness of restlessness, distress related to restlessness) and a global clinical assessment of akathisia from 0 (absent) to 5 (severe).
barnes.reference: Barnes TR. A rating scale for drug-induced akathisia. Br J Psychiatry 1989;154:672-676
flags: The documents give the range of the three items (0 to 3) but not the wording of their levels, so no direction is written for them or for barnes_sum.
The dictionary says the global assessment goes from 0 to 4; the form and the published scale go from 0 to 5.
The Barnes columns share the dictionary prefix BARS with the Brief Adherence Rating Scale (instrument bars), which is another instrument.

bars.title: Brief Adherence Rating Scale (BARS)

sz.section: Questionnaire Brief Adherence Rating Scale BARS
sz.notes: Adherence to the treatment over the 30 days before the visit, rated by the clinician at every visit: three questions and a percentage. It is the Brief Adherence Rating Scale (Byerly, Nakonezny and Rush 2008; scale_reference.md, section 11), not the Barnes akathisia scale: the Barnes columns are bars0101 to bars0106 (barnes.yaml) and share only the prefix of the dictionary. The three questions are counts (doses prescribed per day, days without the treatment, days with less than the prescribed dose), and the clinician's own estimate of the percentage of doses taken is the score. No source read gives a formula that links it to the three counts, and the 2008 paper itself could not be read (literature check 2026-11-21). Doses per day. The form puts no upper limit on this question (it only asks for digits: eschizo_data.sql line 94850) where the two questions on days are limited to 0 to 31. Most answers are 1 to 10. 250 cells hold a number above 20 (100 on 193 cells, 50 and 80 on a few, 999 on 8...): two thirds of them in one centre and 4% to 15% of the answers of each year since 2018; on 146 of the 193 cells at 100 the percentage is 100 too, so a percentage was typed in the field of the doses. These cells end out_of_range. 271 visits hold 0 doses, which is hard to read for a patient under treatment. Days. On 85 of 4,265 visits the days missed and the days with a reduced dose add up to more than the 30 days of the period. The percentage is the clinician's own estimate, as the dictionary says: 73% of the values are multiples of ten. It is not a formula of the days: it equals the share of days with the treatment taken, rounded, on 2,334 of 4,283 visits (within one point on 2,675) and differs on 1,949. It is delivered as stored. The unlimited dose question and the percentage typed in the dose field are defects of the form of the application, not of the export (request A65).

bars.description: Brief Adherence Rating Scale: adherence to the treatment over the 30 days before the visit, rated by the clinician at every visit (SZ). Three counts (doses prescribed per day, days without the treatment, days with less than the prescribed dose) and the clinician's estimate of the percentage of doses taken, which is the score.
bars.reference: Byerly MJ, Nakonezny PA, Rush AJ. The Brief Adherence Rating Scale (BARS) validated against electronic monitoring in assessing the antipsychotic medication adherence of outpatients with schizophrenia and schizoaffective disorder. Schizophr Res 2008;100:60-69
flags: It is not the Barnes akathisia scale (instrument barnes), which shares the dictionary prefix BARS.
The percentage is the clinician's own estimate, not a formula of the days: it differs from the share of days with the treatment taken on 1,949 of 4,283 visits. 73% of the values are multiples of ten.
Whether the published score combines the three counts is 'to verify' (the 2008 paper could not be read).
Doses per day: the form has no upper limit and a percentage was sometimes typed in this field; values above 20 end out_of_range, and 271 visits hold 0 doses.

calgary.title: Calgary Depression Scale for Schizophrenia (CDSS)

sz.section: Questionnaire CALGARY depression scale for schizophrenia
sz.notes: Rated by the clinician at every visit: nine items from 0 (absent) to 3 (severe) over the last two weeks, in a structured interview; item 9 is the interviewer's own observation (Addington et al. 1990, 1992, 1993; scale_reference.md, section 8). The dictionary does not name the items; the labels are those of the published scale and of the form. What the columns hold (decisions D76 and D105, request R136, done). The form numbers the items 1 to 9 (depression, hopelessness, self-depreciation, guilty ideas of reference, pathological guilt, morning depression, early wakening, suicide, observed depression) and the script of the form adds the nine (hetero_calgary.js, lines 20 to 22). Since SZALL_20261123 the export reads each item in its own field (eschizo_hetero_calgary.sql, export commit c39fd720, eSchizo v4.46): calgar08 is the suicide item and calgar09 the observed depression. Checked against the file before, cell by cell on the 6,609 visits that both hold: items 1 to 7 are unchanged, the new calgar08 equals the old calgar09 on every visit, and calgar09 is new (0 to 3 on 4,671 visits, above 0 on 1,052; it is the copy of no other item, and its rank correlation is highest with item 1, depression, +0.56, and lowest with item 7, early wakening, +0.14). Up to SZALL_20261121 the export read the early-wakening field twice: calgar08 was a copy of item 7, calgar09 held item 8 (suicide) and item 9 was exported nowhere. The package then delivered eight items (calgary08 read in calgar09) and their sum, calgary_sum8, and no total. calgary08 is the same item with the same values as before; calgary09 is new; calgary_sum8 is no longer delivered (it is calgary_total minus calgary09). Before 2026-11-20 the suicide item was delivered as calgary09, "observed depression" (D76): a table made with that version does not hold item 9. Do not read a file older than SZALL_20261123 with this schema: its calgar08 is item 7 and its calgar09 is item 8, and nothing would flag it, since its stored total is the sum of those columns. The suicide reading of item 8 was checked on the follow-up visits against the questions of the suicide tab (D76, on the file of 2026-11-17): its mean is 0.04 where the patient felt that life is not worth living since the last visit is no and 0.49 where it is yes (2,337 visits), and 0.16 against 0.58 where an attempt since the last visit is no or yes (2,331); early wakening (item 7) moves much less (0.10 against 0.20 on the first question). The total. calgary_total is the sum of the nine items (0 to 27; 0 to 23 observed), given when the nine are answered: 4,669 visits (4 visits have seven or eight items and no total). The stored total (calgar) is read as a check and equals it on every one of them, in every year; it is empty on the 4 incomplete visits. Up to SZALL_20261121 the stored total counted item 7 twice and held no item 9: it differed from the true total on 1,238 of 4,669 visits. The usual rule is "above 6", seven or more (the form says "superieur a 6" and the author's table gives 85% sensitivity and 82% specificity at 7): 815 visits. extrapyramidal.title: Extrapyramidal side effects (Simpson-Angus Scale, parkinsonism)

sz.notes: Rated by the clinician at every visit: ten items from 0 (normal) to 4 (severe). It is the Simpson-Angus Scale (Simpson and Angus 1970): the ten items are the ten of the form, in its order (scale_reference.md, section 12). The dictionary calls the columns ESRSA01 to ESRSA10 and the items "Q1 to Q10", and the name esrsa stays here; but the form is not the ESRS of Chouinard (another instrument, with items of 0 to 3, 0 to 6 and 0 to 8, no mean). The items (form fields in brackets): 1 gait (radhtml_dempatient), 2 arm dropping (chut), 3 passive shoulder movement (epaule), 4 elbow rigidity (coude), 5 wrist rigidity (poignet), 6 leg pendulousness (jambe), 7 head dropping (tete), 8 glabella tap (yeux), 9 tremor (entree), 10 salivation (parole). The export writes them in this order (eschizo_hetero_extrapyramidaux.sql). Item 8 counts the blinks after the taps, in five classes: 0 to 5, 6 to 10, 11 to 15, 16 to 20 and 21 or more; the 112 cells at 4 are "21 or more". Score. The stored score (esrsa, "parkinsonism if 1 or more" in the dictionary) is the mean of the ten items, as the script of the form computes it (the sum divided by 10, on a button; nothing is rounded: a sum of whole numbers over 10 has one decimal by itself). It is equal to ours on 4,185 of 4,195 visits. The ten others get score_mismatch, all with a stored value below the items (probably an item edited after the button was clicked). A mean needs its ten items; 46 visits have the ten items and no stored score, and one visit has a stored score and fewer than ten items (score_not_recomputed). The dictionary rule "parkinsonism if 1 or more" has no published basis: the mean is 1 or more on 3.6% of the visits and 0.3 or more on 27.2%. The published cut-offs for the mean of this scale are 0.3, which Janno et al. 2005 call widely used and find too low, and 0.65, the optimum that Janno et al. 2005 propose. Who first proposed 0.3 could not be found (literature check 2026-11-21). No cut-off is delivered.

panss.title: Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS)

sz.section: Questionnaire Positive and negative Syndrome Scale for Schizophrenia PANSS
sz.notes: Rated by the clinician at every visit: 30 items from 1 (absent) to 7 (extreme). The columns panss101 to panss107 are P1 to P7, panss108 to panss114 are N1 to N7 and panss115 to panss130 are G1 to G16, as the dictionary says. It gives no label to the items; the labels are those of the published scale. The level 7 is rare on some items and all the other levels occur on every item: no answer is lost. The three scales and the total. Each stored score is exactly the sum of its items, on every visit that has it (4,646 to 4,670), in every year. A sum needs all its items. The five-factor scores. The extraction stores fifteen of them, five for each of three published models (Wallwork 2012, Lançon 1998, van der Gaag 2006). All fifteen are plain sums of items, exact on the 4,646 complete visits, in every year from 2010, and they exist exactly where the items of their formula are filled, also for visits older than the publications. They are not typed. Two programs compute them: the form of the application, on a button, with the formulas of hetero_panss.js (lines 70 to 88), and the score step of the export, which adds the items again with strict sums and overwrites the column (nucleus score definition panss.yaml). The two agree on 12 of the 15 and the stored value is the export's (decisions D10 and D77). Three stored scores, those of the export, sum a wrong item (request R137). They are corrected here: the score delivered follows the application and the publication, and a second score, not delivered, repeats the stored formula so that the stored column is still checked. - Wallwork, positive factor. Application and publication: P1, P3, P5, G9 (hetero_panss.js line 70; the table of the paper as reproduced by Pinna et al. 2014, and by the COSMIN review of 2025 for the core items; the primary table of Wallwork 2012 could not be read, literature check 2026-11-21). Stored: P1, P3, P5, N2. G9 is the 23rd of the 30 items (PANSS123); the export lists PANSS109, which is N2 (panss.yaml line 88). The two differ on 3,276 of 4,661 visits that have both; on 6 more visits the factor is stored although G9 is empty. - Wallwork, negative factor. Application and publication: N1, N2, N3, N4, N6, G7 (line 74). Stored: N1, N2, N3, N4, N5, G7: PANSS112 (N5) in place of PANSS113 (N6), one item off (panss.yaml line 99). They differ on 2,973 of 4,656 visits. With these two slips the stored model counts N2 and N5 twice and has 18 items, where the paper has 20, each in one factor. - Lançon, negative factor. Application: N1, N2, N3, N4, N6, G7, G16 (line 75). Stored: N1, N2, N3, N4, N6, N7, G16: PANSS114 (N7) in place of PANSS121 (G7) (panss.yaml line 156; the comment of line 161 repeats the letter N7). The paper left six items out of its analysis, N7 among them, and kept 24. The stored formulas use 24 items, each once: the 23 others that the paper kept, and N7. The one kept item that they do not use is G7. So the published factor has G7 where the stored formula has N7, which is what the application does. The two differ on 2,830 of 4,660 visits. The paper's own table could not be read (open question O5): the choice rests on the application, on the abstract and on the number of items of each factor. The label says "corrected as in the application (G7 for N7)" (the user's decision of 2026-11-21); the doubt stays until the table of the paper is read. The twelve other factor scores are the same in the application, in the export and here, and are delivered with that formula. For Wallwork (disorganised, excited, depressed) it is the published one. For Lançon the four other factors fit the paper's count of items per factor; their items could not be read in the paper either. The Wallwork paper reports each factor as the mean of its items; the extraction stores sums, and so does this schema, for the three models alike. A mean is the sum divided by the number of items. van der Gaag. The stored scores are the application's own lists, labelled van der Gaag 2006: 29 terms of 28 items (G8 in two factors, G1 and G15 absent), each item in one factor except G8, and no subtraction. The published model (van der Gaag et al. 2006) is a revised model in which items load on several factors and all 30 items are used; two later papers quote it with 45 terms and with N5 subtracted from the positive factor and P2 from the negative one. Each list of the application is a subset of the matching factor of the published model as reproduced by Jerrell and Hrisko 2013, which fits a simplification to the main loading of each item; the primary loading table of van der Gaag et al. 2006 could not be read, so where the simplification comes from is not confirmed (literature check 2026-11-21; scale_reference.md, section 7). They are delivered as stored, labelled "van der Gaag 2006, the application's list" with their items (the user's decision of 2026-11-21): the labels say whose list it is, and the doubt above stays in these notes until the primary loading table is read (open question O5). The positive factors of Lançon and van der Gaag are the same sum, and so are the excited factors of Wallwork and van der Gaag. The composite. panss_composite is the positive scale minus the negative scale (Kay et al. 1987; scale_reference.md, section 7), from -42 to 42; it is not stored and not computed by the application. It exists on 4,656 visits and runs from -33 to 25.

psp.title: Personal and Social Performance scale (PSP)

sz.notes: Rated by the clinician at every visit, from 2012 on, but the form came into use slowly: it is filled on 8% of the inclusion visits of 2012, 13% in 2013, 33% in 2014, 53% in 2015, 74% in 2016 and 80% to 94% from 2017 (at follow-up 4% in 2013, 17% in 2014, 62% in 2015 and 77% to 94% from 2016). Four domains from 0 (absent) to 5 (very severe): socially useful activities, personal and social relationships, self-care, disturbing and aggressive behaviours. From them the clinician chooses a band of ten points, then a score from 1 to 100 inside it (higher is better). The band is coded 1 (100 to 91) to 10 (10 to 1). It is the band of the stored score on 3,047 of 3,262 visits; the custom check psp_band_differs flags the 215 others (check_failed), 190 of them by one band. The values are kept: the cell does not tell which of the two the clinician meant. Nothing is computed. The form has no script and the export no formula: the four ratings, the band and the score are typed, and the band is typed independently of the score (the form is stored in the auto-questionnaire group of the application, but the clinician rates it). It is the PSP of Morosini et al. 2000 (scale_reference.md, section 14); the dictionary numbers the levels 0 to 5 where the publication numbers them 1 to 6. A band that differs from the score is more frequent where the score ends in 0 (12.5% of 771 visits, the top of a band) or in 5 (7.3% of 1,090, the middle) than where it ends in 1 (2.3% of 750, the bottom). Three scores are outside 1 to 100 (one above 300) and end out_of_range. The export drops the done / not done flag of the form (rad_psp_nf, request R141).

sumd.title: Scale to assess Unawareness of Mental Disorder (SUMD, abbreviated)

sz.section: Questionnaire Self-Unawareness of Mental Disorder SUMD
sz.notes: Rated by the clinician at every visit. Three general items (awareness of having a mental disorder, of its consequences, of the effects of the medication), then six symptoms, each rated twice: awareness of the symptom (columns ending in c) and attribution of the symptom to the disorder (columns ending in a). 1 is aware or correct, 2 partial, 3 unaware or incorrect. The code 0 is "cannot be rated": 29 to 148 visits for the general items, and 34% to 59% of the visits for a symptom, where it mostly means that the patient does not have the symptom. It is read as a missing code (not_applicable). The dictionary. It lists SUMD01 to SUMD09 as one range; the extraction holds sumd01 to sumd03 and twelve columns sumd04c to sumd09c and sumd04a to sumd09a, which the dictionary does not list. It does not name the six symptoms, so they stay numbered here. The attribution and the script (request A62). The script of the form (hetero_sumd.js) is meant to set the attribution of a symptom to 0 ("cannot be rated") when the awareness of the same symptom is 0 or 3, and, for the three general items, to tick attribution radios named labelfieldsradhtml_attribu10, 20 and 30 (lines 37 to 47 and 79 to 89), which the table of the form does not have (it has attribu4 to attribu9 only). When a general item is 0 or 3 the script stops with an error on those lines before it reaches the rules of the symptoms. So 530 attributions of 1 to 3 remain under an awareness of 0 or 3 (symptom by symptom 82, 124, 108, 93, 53 and 70; 522 of them under awareness 3, 8 under 0), and 6 more sit under an empty awareness. Among the cells with an awareness of 0 or 3 and an attribution, 12.1% (507 of 4,182) hold an attribution of 1 to 3 on the visits where a general item is 0 or 3, against 0.2% (23 of 10,419) elsewhere. The cells stay as recorded and get no shown_if: the form does not hide the attribution (only the script was meant to zero it), and 522 of the 536 cells that a rule would blank are an awareness of 3 where the clinician rated the attribution. Missing codes. The 0 is read as missing: 29, 128 and 148 visits for the three general items, 1,570 to 2,294 awareness cells and 2,014 to 2,701 attribution cells per symptom. Stored scores. sumd1, sumd2 and sumd3 are the three general items again (equal on 4,539 of 4,541, 4,534 of 4,540 and 4,537 of 4,537 visits; the eight others are stale). They are not loaded (ignored.yaml). The scale has no total in the application and none is built here. The abbreviated SUMD-A of the literature scores three dimensions (items 1 to 3, 4 to 6, 7 to 9, the mean rescaled 0 to 100, "cannot be rated" as missing: Michel et al. 2013, scale_reference.md, section 13); the attribution items are outside it.
