barona.title: Premorbid IQ expected from occupation and diploma (Barona)

sz.notes: The IQ that the occupation, the diploma, the age and the sex of the patient let expect, and its difference with the IQ estimated from the WAIS. Filled with the WAIS of both editions: an expected full-scale IQ on 1,546 visits (2010 to 2026) and, on the 555 WAIS-III visits (2010 to 2015), an expected verbal IQ and an expected performance IQ. The expected IQs are recomputed and delivered; the values that the application stored are checks (barona_expected_qit_stored, barona_expected_qiv_stored and barona_expected_qip_stored, not delivered). The formula is the one of the scripts of the application (psy_neuropsychologie_barona.js for the three IQs, _barona_sz_wais4.js for the full-scale IQ of the WAIS-IV): a constant, the sex (1 for a woman, 2 for a man), the rank of the diploma (1 to 7), the rank of the occupation (1 to 7) and the class of age, rounded to two decimals. The coefficients are in norms/wais3_barona_qit.csv, wais3_barona_qiv.csv and wais3_barona_qip.csv, one line for each of the 12 classes of age from 16 to 89 years; outside them there would be no value and no flag (no visit is). The dictionary gives no formula. The age is the age typed in the form where it is within a year of the age at the visit, else the age at the visit. The two spellings of the label of the highest diploma are both rank 7 here (78 visits of 2010 to 2016 and 177 of 2015 to 2026); each script of the application knows one of them. Against the stored values. Full-scale IQ: 1,458 of the 1,507 visits that have both are equal (to 0.01) and the 49 others are score_mismatch. The 49 have a cause in the scripts on 47 visits. 29 lost a term of the formula: the script gives no coefficient to an answer whose label it does not know, and JavaScript counts that empty coefficient as 0 (psy_neuropsychologie_barona.js, lines 42 to 63; psy_neuropsychologie_barona_sz_wais4.js, lines 45 to 68; defect A93). The diploma term is lost on 18 WAIS-III visits of centre F in 2011 to 2014: every visit of that centre and period whose diploma label holds a comma (23 of 23) lost it, and no visit without a comma did (0 of 25). Both the diploma and the occupation terms are lost on 8 (centres F, A, C, 2011 to 2015), and the occupation term alone on 3 (centre A, 2015; 'Artisans, commerçants' on 9 of these 11 occupations). Which labels the forms of these centres held then is question M86. 17 used another age: 11 the age typed in the form where it is more than a year from the age at the visit, 4 one class of age lower and 2 two classes higher. The script recomputes the expected IQ only when the occupation or the diploma changes (lines 15 and 16 of the first script, 16 and 17 of the second), so an age typed or corrected afterwards leaves it stale; the export gives one typed age for the three neuropsychology forms (request R168). 1 used the other sex (2021): the WAIS-IV page reads the sex of the patient record. 2 are not explained (2015; one is a visit labelled WAIS-III that holds the WAIS-IV sequencing task). Verbal and performance IQs: 515 of the 547 WAIS-III visits that have both are equal. Of the 32 others, the same visits for the two IQs, 24 lost the diploma term or both terms (centre F, and one visit of A), 5 used the typed age, 2 another class of age and 1 is not explained (2015). The mismatches are 12 of 218 visits to 2012, 26 of 413 in 2013 to 2015 and 11 of 876 after (full-scale IQ). On the visits that lost the diploma term the stored differences are wrong by that term too; they keep derived_doubt and are delivered as stored. More and fewer values than the application stored. 39 WAIS-IV visits of 2015 and 2016 that have both answers had no stored expected full-scale IQ, and 8 WAIS-III visits of 2015 no stored verbal and performance IQs: their expected IQs are delivered. 34 stored full-scale values cannot be recomputed (score_not_recomputed, not delivered): 11 visits have neither answer, 22 no occupation and 1 no diploma; 8 stored verbal and 8 stored performance values cannot be recomputed either. A visit that has only one of the two answers gets no value and norm_missing (117 visits for the full-scale IQ, 10 for each of the other two): the application needs both. The occupation is not reliable (decision D13, open question O17, to send first). The form lists seven occupations and seven diplomas. On 1,111 of the 1,546 visits that have both (72%, against 15% if the two were independent), the occupation holds the same place in its list as the diploma in its own: 221 of the 225 farmers have a vocational certificate (CAP BEP), 218 of the 237 retired patients a general baccalaureate, in a cohort whose median age is about 32. It happens in every year and in every centre (27% to 91% of the visits). The diploma agrees with the education level of the patient tab, so the diploma is the answer and the occupation is, on most of these visits, a copy of its place in the list. The cell does not tell a copy from a true coincidence (a higher professional with a university degree). The expected IQ depends on the occupation and the stored one used the copy: the recomputed value, which reads the same answers, equals the stored one on 1,042 of the 1,079 visits where the occupation mirrors the diploma and 416 of the 428 others (full-scale IQ). So the expected IQs carry the error. On these visits (1,111 for the full-scale IQ, 428 for the verbal and for the performance IQ) the occupation, the expected IQs and the differences keep their value and get check_failed. The differences are the expected IQ minus the IQ estimated from the WAIS, as the application stored them. With the stored expected IQ: verbal on 508 of 508 visits (against the verbal IQ as stored) and performance on 516 of 516; the estimated full-scale IQ of the WAIS-III is not in the extraction (the IQ recomputed from the sum of the scaled scores gives 504 of 504 on the load of 2026-11-18). WAIS-IV: the full-scale difference uses the seven-subtest IQ where it exists (292 of 293 with the stored IQ corrected as in wais4_efficience.yaml, 287 of 293 with the delivered IQ, which follows the recomputed sum, D137) and the two-subtest IQ otherwise (154 of 161). The differences are delivered as stored and derived from the expected IQ: a difference whose stored expected IQ is not the recomputed one is kept and gets derived_doubt (38 full-scale, 29 verbal and 30 performance). The occupation and the diploma differ between two visits for 108 and 69 of the 266 patients seen at least twice. Two typed ages written 'NN ans' stay unparsed (the age at the visit is used, and both visits get their expected IQ), and 22 of the 33 visits read as WAIS-IV hold a stored expected verbal IQ and a stored expected performance IQ (barona05_wais3 and barona07_wais3: 44 cells) that the WAIS-III variables do not read there, so they are not delivered. The full-scale difference steps down from 2019 (median 12.9 on the 308 WAIS-IV visits of 2015 to 2018 that have the seven-subtest IQ, 4.0 on the 155 visits of 2016 to 2026 that have only the two-subtest IQ, 114 of them in 2019 to 2021): the estimated IQ it implies is 100 against 90 (medians) while the expected IQ stays within 2 points (102 and 104), so the step is the change of the estimated IQ, not of the expected one; the centre shift of the full-scale difference follows from it (centre B, median 2.7, has 12 of its 21 visits from 2019). The stored values that differ are errors of the application's scripts (a label they do not know, a value not recomputed after an edit); the recomputed values are delivered. 2 full-scale and 1 verbal and performance mismatches are not explained (0.1% and 0.2%).

asp.notes: The occupation (885 inclusion visits) and the level of education (803) that the form asks before the WAIS-IV, an expected full-scale IQ and a difference. The Barona estimate, as in FACE SZ: an IQ expected from demographic variables, which is why it holds decimals (the thesaurus calls it the expected IQ of Barona). The application stored the expected IQ (qita) on 241 visits and the difference (qitdif) on 131. The expected IQ is recomputed and delivered, with the formula of the script of the application (280_score.js, barona()), which is the same formula as the WAIS-IV one of FACE SZ (coefficients in norms/wais3_barona_qit.csv): a constant, the sex (1 for a woman, 2 for a man), the education, the occupation and the class of age (16 to 89 years), rounded to two decimals. The two lists are used as numbers, as the script does: the code 0 of the occupation and the code 8 of the occupation and of the education count as 0 and 8 (116 of the expected IQs rest on an occupation code 0, 344 on a code 8, 1 on an education code 8). The form has no typed age: the age is the age at the date of the assessment form (qsdtc) where that date is within a year of the visit, as in the WAIS schemas of this cohort (decision D139), else the age at the visit. A visit under 16 years has no adult norm and no value (42 visits of children have both answers). 763 visits get a value (761 at V0), 537 of them on visits where the application stored none: both answers are there, so it is delivered. The stored value is the check (barona_expected_qit_stored, not delivered). Against the stored values, 226 visits have both: 213 are equal (to 0.05, the stored value has one decimal) and 13 are score_mismatch (6 are one class of age away, 2 are visits where the application left out the term of the occupation code 8, 5 are not explained). 15 stored values cannot be recomputed (score_not_recomputed): 14 visits have neither answer and 1 is a patient under 16 years. 81 visits that have only one of the two answers get no value and norm_missing. The difference is the expected IQ minus the full-scale IQ of the neuropsychology form: with the expected IQ and the IQ as stored it is exact on 131 of 131 visits; with the delivered IQ (recomputed, D137) 123 of the 130 visits that have the three numbers are within 0.2. The difference is delivered as stored and derived from the expected IQ: where the stored expected IQ is not the recomputed one it is kept and gets derived_doubt (4 visits). qitdif_a, its copy for the abbreviated form, is on 1 visit. The two lists are exported as numbers and named from the thesaurus; the code 0 of the occupation and the code 8 of the education are not in its lists (O16). In FACE SZ the occupation is most often a copy of the rank of the diploma. Not here: the two codes are equal on 117 of 805 visits, which is what chance gives. qita_a is an exact copy of qita (241 of 241, ignored.yaml). Centre B's expected IQs are lower (median 98 against 105 to 112 at the other centres, 0.7 of the interquartile range): its patients are younger (median age 19 against 20 to 29) and 125 of its 145 occupations are the code 8 (no occupation), which the script counts as 8. Same instrument as in FACE SZ, in other columns; lists as numbers.
asp.difference: the occupation and the education are exported as numbers, named from the thesaurus (one code of each list is not in it); one expected IQ and its difference; no edition to choose

barona.description: The IQ that the occupation, the diploma, the age and the sex of the patient let expect, and its difference with the IQ estimated from the WAIS. SZ: a full-scale, a verbal and a performance IQ; ASP: the full-scale IQ only.
barona.reference: Barona A, Reynolds CR, Chastain R. A demographically based index of premorbid intelligence for the WAIS-R. J Consult Clin Psychol 1984;52:885-887
flags: In SZ the occupation is not reliable: on 72% of the visits it holds the same place in its list as the diploma, a copy on most of them. The expected IQs and the differences keep their value there and get check_failed: read the flags before comparing.

The published equations use age, sex, race, education, occupation, region and residence of the United States; no French adaptation was found (to verify). The application's formula uses the sex, the diploma, the occupation and the class of age.
Published limit of the equations: they underestimate an IQ under 80 and overestimate an IQ above 119 (Paolo 1996, confirmed in the abstract).
The differences are delivered as stored; where the stored expected IQ is not the recomputed one they get derived_doubt.
In SZ the full-scale difference steps down from 2019, when the estimated IQ became the two-subtest one: the step is the change of the estimated IQ, not of the expected one.
In ASP the occupation codes 0 and 8 are outside the seven ranks of the formula and are used as numbers, as the script does; a visit under 16 years gets no value.
A visit with only one of the two answers gets no value (norm_missing).

common.note: The expected full-scale IQ and its difference with the measured one are in both cohorts; the expected verbal and performance IQ in SZ only. The expected IQ is computed from the sex, the diploma, the occupation and the age (regression of the application, BP D138-D143): in SZ with the typed age, in ASP with the age at the date of the form. In SZ the occupation is not reliable (it follows the diploma on 72% of the visits) and the expected IQs keep their value with the flag check_failed: read the flags before comparing. The ASP codes 0 and 8 of the occupation (about 460 expected IQs) are outside the seven ranks of the formula; the difference is the stored one (derived_doubt where the expected IQ moved).

cpt_ip.title: Continuous Performance Test, Identical Pairs (CPT-IP)

sz.notes: Sustained attention: numbers of 2, 3 and 4 digits flash on the screen and the patient answers when the same number comes twice in a row. Each of the three parts has 30 targets, 30 near-targets (an answer there is a false alarm) and 90 other numbers. 1,009 visits hold any cell: 1,008 from 2010 to 2018 and one in 2025. The numbers are those of the test software, typed by the rater. The d-prime of each part (the ability to tell a target from a near-target) is delivered as typed. It is the normal deviate of the hit rate minus that of the false-alarm rate, each rate being a count over 30 kept between 1/59 and 58/59 (norms/cptip_rate_z.csv, made by norms/make_cptip_tables.py), and the three checks cptip_*_dprime_check, not delivered, compute it again. The typed d-prime is the recomputed one to 0.011 on 896 of 992 visits for 2 digits, 922 of 994 for 3 digits and 932 of 990 for 4 digits (90% to 94%); the others (score_mismatch on the typed d-prime: 96, 72 and 58) are all from 2011 to 2017, in 8 centres, and hold another value: nothing tells which of the hits, the false alarms or the d-prime was mistyped, so the typed d-prime stays the delivered one. A few counts are impossible (34 hits out of 30, 90 hits) and are out of range. The mean d-prime is recomputed here as the mean of the three parts. It equals the stored one on all 956 visits that have the four numbers (955 delivered, one part d-prime being out of range), but it is not rounded: the application rounds it to 2 decimals. 3 stored means cannot be recomputed (score_not_recomputed): two visits have an unparsed part d-prime and one an out_of_range part d-prime. The percentile was typed by hand, from 2013 to 2017 (417 visits of 8 centres, 3 more in 2018 and 2025), against norms that the dictionary does not name. 335 cells hold a number (one above 100 is out of range), 16 a value under a limit ("<1": censored_left) and 59 a band ("10-25"), read as its middle and flagged band_middle. 10 cells are bands cut by the export ("1.4-1.", "1.5 - "), as the percentile labels of the DR tab (open question O23, 4): they are unparsed. The 6 other unparsed cells are 3 d-prime values written as two words, 2 d-prime values written with two decimal points and 1 count of random answers that starts with a point; none can be read with certainty.

cpt_ip.description: Sustained attention: numbers of 2, 3 and 4 digits flash on the screen and the patient answers when the same number comes twice in a row. Each of the three parts has 30 targets, 30 near-targets and 90 other numbers; hits, false alarms and d-prime of each part, typed from the test software. SZ, 2010 to 2018.
cpt_ip.version: CPT-IP (Identical Pairs), parts of 2, 3 and 4 digits
flags: The d-prime of each part is delivered as typed; on 6% to 10% of the visits it is not the value that the hits and the false alarms give (score_mismatch), and nothing tells which number was mistyped.
The percentile was typed by hand against norms that are not named: its direction is left out.
Not the Conners tests of BP (cpt2, cpt3), where a higher T-score is a more atypical performance: no CPT name is shared across cohorts.

doors_test.title: Doors test (visual recognition memory)

sz.notes: Recognition of photographs of doors: part A (12 easy sets) and part B (12 hard sets), one point per door recognised. 987 visits with a part A from 2010 to 2018 (one in 2025). The total is recomputed here as A + B and equals the stored one on all 771 visits that have both (the 3 other stored totals have a part out of range). Part B holds words on 42 visits ("NA", "non réalisé", "DCM": missing codes): the part was not given, and the EMR left the total empty. Three scores are above 12 and out of range. Percentile bands, recomputed. The percentile of part A, of part B and of the total is read again in the norm tables of the application (norms/doors_*_band.csv, one band for each score and age group) from the score and the age typed in the form (cclin01_), where it is within one year of the age at the visit, and from the age at the visit elsewhere. The value is the lower limit of the band; a band wider than one step ("75 - 95") is read as 75 or more and has <variable>_cens = +1 (censored_right, 83 visits for part A). The stored percentiles are kept only as checks (doors_*_band_stored, not delivered); a band that differs from the stored one is flagged score_mismatch: 2 of 986 visits for part A, 1 of 772 for part B and 1 of 769 for the total, all before 2013. The share of each band is stable from one period to the next. The percentile of part B is "<1" on 172 visits where part B is empty: 171 of the 171 visits with part A typed and part B empty, and one visit where both parts are empty (its part A percentile is "<1" too). The cause is the script of the form: it tests !isNaN(value), which is true for an empty cell, so an empty part writes "<1" (the same error as for the CVLT recency in FACE BP); the total and its percentile are blanked when either part is empty. Nothing is delivered for these visits, and they get score_not_recomputed (the stored value is in the flag log). Not counting them, "<1" is the percentile of 119 visits for part B. The SZ form has a box "test not done" (chk_porte_test_non_fait) that the extraction does not hold (nor the boxes of the verbal fluency, the errands test and the six elements test: chk_fv_, chk_com_, chk_test_6element_): ask the data managers. Besides the checks above, 2 typed ages written 'NN ans' and 7 stored percentiles of '>99' (a limit that the list of bands does not have: part A 1, part B 2, total 4; checks, not delivered) stay unparsed, and the age at the visit is used where the typed one is not read. Centre C (70 visits with a total) sits below the other centres, 13 against 16 for the total (part A 8 against 9, part B 5 against 6), as it does on the CVLT total z-score and the WAIS-III matrices z-score, where it is the second lowest: a centre difference, with no step in time (the yearly medians of the total are 15 to 17 from 2011 to 2017).

doors_test.description: Recognition of photographs of doors: part A (12 easy sets) and part B (12 hard sets), one point per door recognised, with the total and percentile bands. SZ, 2010 to 2018.
doors_test.version: parts A and B, 12 sets each
flags: No document says in words whether a higher percentile band is a better performance: the direction of the bands is left out. A band with <variable>_cens = +1 is this band or a higher one.
Where part B is empty the application wrote '<1' as its percentile: nothing is delivered for the band of part B and of the total on those visits.
The total needs the two parts.

fnart.title: French National Adult Reading Test (fNART)

sz.notes: Reading aloud of 40 irregular French words, each scored correct or incorrect: an estimate of the premorbid IQ. The words are recorded on 686 visits from 2010 to 2016 (684 with the 40 words, 2 with some of them), all with the old neuropsychological form; the test is not in the form that replaced it. A total and three IQs are stored on 1,295 visits: 685 of them have words, 610 have none (2014: 2, 2015: 150, 2016: 239, 2017: 208, 2018: 10, 2025: 1). The total is the number of words read correctly. Recomputed, it equals the stored total on the 684 visits that have the 40 words. Where no word is recorded and a total is stored (the 610 visits), the total is delivered as stored and gets score_as_stored. The visit with only some of the words has a stored total that cannot be recomputed (score_not_recomputed). The three estimated IQs (full scale, verbal, performance) are each an exact straight line of the total, with one intercept and one slope for all ages; the coefficients are in norms/wais3_fnart_qit.csv, wais3_fnart_qiv.csv and wais3_fnart_qip.csv (read in psy_neuropsychologie_fnart.js; the dictionary does not give the equations). They are recomputed from the total and delivered on 1,294 visits, where they equal the stored IQs on 1,294 of 1,294 (the stored ones, fnart_qit_stored, fnart_qiv_stored and fnart_qip_stored, are checks). On the 610 visits where the total is the stored one, the IQs are the line of that stored total. The stored IQs of the visit with only some of the words cannot be recomputed (score_not_recomputed). Centre D (82 visits with the words, 174 with a total) reads items 12, 22 and 30 correct on 61%, 38% and 9% of its visits against 92%, 74% and 66% in the other centres, which costs 1.2 points of the total on average and accounts for most of its median total of 23.5 against 25: a centre habit on three words, with no step in time (the yearly medians of the total are 24 to 25).

fnart.description: Reading aloud of 40 irregular French words, each scored correct or incorrect: an estimate of the premorbid IQ. The total and three estimated IQs (full scale, verbal, performance). SZ; the words are recorded from 2010 to 2016, the total alone on later visits.
flags: The notes say that each estimated IQ is a straight line of the total but not the sign of its slope: the direction of the three IQs is left out.
Where no word is recorded and a total is stored, the total is delivered as stored (flag score_as_stored) and the IQs are the line of that total.
The coefficients are read in the script of the application; the dictionary does not give the equations and no reference is given in the project documents.

laterality.title: Edinburgh handedness inventory

sz.notes: For each of ten activities, and for the foot and the eye, the hand used: two crosses in a column for a strong preference, one in each column when either hand is used. The extraction holds the number of crosses in the left and in the right column of each line (0, 1 or 2). The 24 item columns are filled on 505 visits from 2010 to 2016, nearly all at inclusion; the stored quotient is on 869 visits (2010 to 2018, and one in 2025). The dictionary lists the quotient and names the 24 item columns in one line; the labels of the 12 lines are those of the published inventory. The laterality quotient is 100 x (right - left) / (right + left), from -100 (left-handed) to +100 (right-handed), over the ten activities of the inventory: the foot and the eye are not counted (Oldfield 1971). The script of the application rounds it to one decimal, hence compare_tolerance 0.051. Recomputed that way, it equals the stored quotient on 460 of 501 visits (the largest difference among them is 0.0; the smallest among the others is 1.7). The 41 others are all in centre F, the one centre that stored the quotient of the 12 lines: of its 52 visits with the items and a stored quotient (2010 to June 2015), the stored value equals the 12-line quotient on 52 and the 10-line one on 11. In the 9 other centres none of the 313 visits where the 10-line and the 12-line quotients differ follows the 12 lines; the current script has its 12-line sum commented out. The 41 visits get score_mismatch and the ten-activity quotient is delivered, so that every centre is on the same scale. 368 stored quotients have no item to recompute them from (score_not_recomputed), in all ten centres (A 110, G 58, D 51 are the most): by year 2011 1, 2014 2, 2015 89, 2016 148, 2017 117, 2018 10, 2025 1; 350 at inclusion; one of them (centre H) holds 16 of the 24 cells. The cause is in the export, not in the form: decision D35 extended the export to the quotient of the later forms, not to the items. The WAIS-IV form of the application (psy_neuropsychologie_sz_wais4.php) still loads the inventory script, so the test was not dropped from the form that replaced the old one. Question for the data managers: export the 24 item columns of the later form. The stored quotient alone is not delivered (that needs a code change, left for later).

laterality.description: Edinburgh handedness inventory: for each of ten activities, and for the foot and the eye, the hand used, as the number of crosses in the left and in the right column (0, 1 or 2). SZ; the items are recorded from 2010 to 2016.
laterality.version: ten activities, plus the foot and the eye, which are not counted in the quotient
laterality.reference_confidence: Confirmed for formula and range (secondary sources); the class cut-offs depend on the paper
flags: No fixed classes: Oldfield reported deciles; a limit of 40 on either side is a common later convention and other papers use 60 (scale_reference_rest.md section 5).
The quotient is delivered only where the 24 item columns exist. The quotients stored without items (the later form, mostly from 2015 on) are not delivered: the export does not hold their items.
One centre stored the quotient of the 12 lines; the ten-activity quotient is delivered for every centre.

lis.title: Attribution of intentions in six film clips (LIS)

sz.section: Film A : l'amende. Question : Pourquoi l’homme parle-il de son fils au policier ?
sz.notes: Lecture Intentionnelle en Situation: six short film clips, and for each a question about the intention of a character with five proposed answers. The patient rates each answer from 1 (very unlikely) to 4 (very likely). 1,162 visits from 2013 to 2026 have ratings, 1,148 of them the 30 ratings. The score is the distance to a reference group: the sum, over the 30 answers, of the gap between the rating and the mean rating of the reference group (the higher, the further from the usual reading). It is recomputed and delivered (distance, norms/lis_reference.csv: one reference rating for each answer, read in psy_neuropsychologie_lis.js, where it is written as 30 constants); the stored score (lis_total_stored, not delivered) is the check. The stored score equals the recomputed one, to 0.01, on 983 of the 1,011 visits that have both (962 to 0.00001; 21 were stored rounded to two decimals). The 28 others, from 2022 to 2024 in 6 centres (23 at V0), hold a score that the ratings do not give: score_mismatch. 137 visits with the 30 ratings have no stored score (2015 to 2026, 135 of them in 2018 to 2024 and 53 in 2022; 7 centres): their score is delivered. 7 stored scores cannot be recomputed (3 visits with no rating and 4 with 29 ratings): score_not_recomputed. The 28 scores that the ratings do not give were typed, not computed by the form. The button of the form writes the unrounded sum into a field that cannot be edited (psy_neuropsychologie_lis.js, lines 37 and 40 to 90): 883 of the 962 scores equal to 0.00001 carry more than two decimals, while the 28 carry two decimals at most (7 whole, 7 with one, 14 with two), and no score of centre E in 2022 and 2023 (19) carries more than two. No other rule gives them: a squared distance, reversed ratings, an answer or a film shifted, one answer left out, a rounded reference. They are entry errors, and the recomputed score is delivered; how they could be typed in a field that cannot be edited is question M85. The 137 missing scores stay open question O18. The scores of 2014 and 2015 are higher: 45 visits of centres D (36) and F (9), mean 20.2 against 17.3 from 2016 to 2026, with the whole distribution moved (median 19.9 against 16.0). Every film and every answer adds to it, the stored score equals the ratings, centre D is at the later level in 2013 and 2016 (median 16.1 and 15.0), and 8 of these patients tested again later moved by -1.2 (median). No cause in the scoring; the step is documented here (item 6).

lis.description: Lecture Intentionnelle en Situation: six short film clips, and for each a question on the intention of a character with five proposed answers. The patient rates each answer from 1 (very unlikely) to 4 (very likely): 30 ratings. SZ, from 2013.
lis.reference: Bazin N, Brunet-Gouet E, Bourdet C, et al. Quantitative assessment of attribution of intentions to others in schizophrenia using an ecological video-based task. Psychiatry Res 2009;167:28-35
lis.reference_confidence: Confirmed (full text of Urbach et al. 2013, which describes the task; Bazin 2009 is paywalled)
flags: The score needs the 30 ratings. Range 0 to at most 90 in theory; it is not a whole number because the reference means are not.
ASP has a LIS score too (instrument social_cognition), typed by hand with no ratings: do not pool the two.
The scores of 2014 and 2015 are higher in two centres, with no cause in the scoring; the step is left as measured.
No cut-off is given in the project documents.

common.note: The total is in both cohorts (a distance to reference ratings: lower is better); the answers to each clip are in SZ only, where the total is recomputed from them (BP D138-D143). In ASP the total is typed by hand, with no ratings and a different scale: do not pool the two. Added in 2018 in ASP.

six_elements.title: Six elements test

sz.notes: Planning and self-organisation: six tasks (two routes, two series of pictures to name, two series of sums) to share out in a limited time, without doing two tasks of the same kind in a row. About 865 visits from 2010 to 2018 (one in 2025). Three stored scores are sums, recomputed here. The points score is the sum of the six task scores (the stored one equals it on 861 of the 862 visits where both exist). The total of rule breaks is time + alternation (860 of 860). The total error score is inefficiency + rule breaks + errors of interpretation + errors of execution (849 of 852). Totals that are not recomputed (score_not_recomputed: 3 points, 1 rule breaks, 2 error score). Five of them come from a part above its maximum (a task score above 185, up to 1010, for the points; an alternation of 80 where the maximum is 10, for the rule breaks and one error score): the part is out of range and missing, and the stored total was summed from it. The other error score has an inefficiency written as text, which stays unparsed. "NaN" is stored as text in the total of rule breaks (2 visits) and in the total error score (10): missing. The script refreshes only the inefficiency z-score when the inefficiency is typed (elements3), not the total error score: one of the 3 error scores that are not the sum equals the sum without the inefficiency. Five z-scores. The dictionary labels one and leaves four without a label (elem616_, elem620_, elem623_, elem625_). They are computed again as the application computes them, from the score before each: z = (score - mean) / SD for the points and (mean - score) / SD for the inefficiency, the rule breaks, the errors of execution and the total error score, so that a higher z-score is a better result; one mean and one SD per measure, the same at every age (norms/six_elements_*_z.csv). The stored z-scores are kept only as checks (six_elements_*_z_stored, not delivered); a recomputed z-score that differs from the stored one by more than 0.0101 is flagged score_mismatch (the opposite sign, sign_flipped). The z-score follows the recomputed score (the sum of its parts), so a stored total that is not the sum no longer makes the z-score doubtful (derived_doubt). The recomputed z-score differs from the stored one on 1 of 862 visits for the points, none of 807 for the inefficiency, none of 858 for the rule breaks, none of 863 for the errors of execution and 3 of 852 for the total error score. A stored z-score with no usable score is flagged score_not_recomputed (4, 1, 0, 2 and 2 visits): the 4 z-scores of the points have a task score above its maximum, the z-score of the inefficiency and one of the total error score an inefficiency in text, the other one of the total error score an alternation of 80. The 2 z-scores of the errors of execution are not recomputed because their execution cell is empty: the stored value is the z-score of an empty cell read as 0 (the script tests !isNaN(value), which is true for an empty cell: elements5). A few cells hold impossible values (a route score of 1010, a z-score of -637) and are out of range. The total time is in minutes. 83 of 854 cells hold minutes and seconds in words ("12min 30sec", "12'30"): they are unparsed and missing (a reading rule m + s/60 is left for later). The 91 unparsed cells of the instrument are these 83 times, 1 inefficiency and 7 numbers of times the instructions were looked at. The two last columns are free text (how much the patient relied on the examiner, and a description of what the patient did). They are delivered as text and never appear in the report. The box "test not done" of the SZ form (chk_test_6element_) is not extracted: ask the data managers. Centre I writes longer times (median 18 minutes on 44 visits against 15 overall, 64% above 15 minutes against 42% in the other centres) and ticks time exceeded on 84% of its 80 visits against 49%, and centres E and I have the most rule breaks for time (mean 1.6 and 1.4 against 0.95): a centre habit in applying the time limit, with no step in time (the yearly median is 15 to 15.8 minutes from 2011 to 2017).

six_elements.description: Planning and self-organisation: six tasks (two routes, two series of pictures to name, two series of sums) to share out in a limited time, without doing two tasks of the same kind in a row. Task scores, rule breaks, errors, a total error score and five z-scores. SZ, 2010 to 2018.
flags: The five z-scores are computed again and all go the same way (higher is better), although the points score is better when high and the four other scores are better when low.
A time written in minutes and seconds is unparsed and missing.
One centre applies the time limit differently (longer times, more rule breaks for time): a centre habit, with no step in time.
No reference is given in the project documents.

sstics.title: Subjective Scale to Investigate Cognition in Schizophrenia (SSTICS)

sz.notes: Self-rated cognitive complaints: 21 items from 0 (never) to 4 (very often). 2,354 visits from 2013 to 2026 hold items, 2,338 of them all 21. The columns carry the suffix _wais4 but the scale is not a WAIS test; it came with the new neuropsychological form and is read on every visit. The six factor scores and the total are the sums of the publication (Stip 2003): working memory items 1 and 2, explicit memory 3 to 11, attention 12 to 16, executive functions 17 to 19, language 20, praxia 21. Recomputed from the items, they equal the stored scores on all visits but 2, both in centre A (2013-15 and 2016-18): 4 score_mismatch cells (working memory 1, attention 1, total 2). The stored total is the sum of the six stored factors on 2,329 of 2,329 visits. A score needs all its items. Where an item is missing the EMR writes "Qu" or "Ques" (questionnaire incomplete) in the score: a missing code here, on 21 visits (2 of them have all 21 items, 6 none; "Ques" in the z-score and "Qu" in the scores are the same cut to the width of the field). Two visits of centre G (2015 and 2018) hold stored scores and no item: 12 score cells that cannot be recomputed (score_not_recomputed). The z-score is computed again from the total, as the application script (psy_neuropsychologie_sstics_sz_wais4.js) does: (13.1 - total) / 6.2, a decreasing straight line of the total; a negative z-score is more complaints than the reference group. The script rounds it to two decimals; it is delivered with all its decimals. The form field takes four characters, so the stored value is the rounded z cut to its first four characters (-1.11 is stored as -1.1): the rule gives the stored value on 2,329 of 2,329 visits, and the cut changes the value on 1,838 of them. The delivered z therefore differs from the stored one by 0.15 at most on 2,326 of the 2,328 visits that have both (the largest difference is at a total of 76, where the cut leaves -10.). The 2 others are the visits of centre A whose stored total is not the recomputed one: score_mismatch on the z-score as on the total (they were derived_doubt when the stored z was delivered); compare_tolerance is 0.151, for the cut. 10 visits gain a z-score (all 21 items, the stored total empty on 8 and "Qu" on 2) and one loses it (stored scores and no item: score_not_recomputed): 2,338 z-scores in all, against 2,329 stored. The reference group of the constants 13.1 and 6.2 is not sourced: neither the dictionary nor the script names it. Question for the data managers: which sample gave this mean and this standard deviation. Item 10 (explicit memory) is higher in centre I (mean 1.4 against 0.7 elsewhere, on 188 visits) while the total of that centre is only 0.12 SD above the others (31.3 against 29.8): an item-level centre difference, no step of the scores.

sstics.description: Self-rated cognitive complaints: 21 items from 0 (never) to 4 (very often), six factor scores, a total and a z-score. SZ, from 2013.
flags: The z-score goes against the total: a higher total is more complaints, a higher z-score is fewer complaints.
The reference group of the constants 13.1 and 6.2 is not sourced: neither the dictionary nor the script names it.
A score needs all its items.
The z-score is delivered with all its decimals; the application stored it cut to four characters.

wais3_arithmetique.title: WAIS-III arithmetic

sz.notes: WAIS-III and WAIS-IV are two instruments stored in the same columns (decision D10 of the BP file). This schema reads the arithmetic columns on the WAIS-III visits (533 visits, from 2010 to 2015): 20 items, the last two scored 0 to 2 (a point for speed). wais4_arithmetique.yaml reads the WAIS-IV visits. Edition rule (decision D138, question O16): the 33 visits that the form labels WAIS-III and that hold the WAIS-IV digit-span sequencing task (columns mcoc_w and mcocemp_w) are read as WAIS-IV (override in the version block, flag version_overridden). 25 of them hold arithmetic items and are read in wais4_arithmetique.yaml, not here. All 533 visits have the 20 items. The stored raw total is their sum on 532 of 532 visits (one visit has no stored total, and the recomputed one is delivered). The z-score is (scaled score - 10) / 3 on every visit. No stopping rule shows in the data: no visit has an empty item. A total with an empty item would not be computed, as in the application ('Questionnaire incomplet'). FACE BP does not have this subtest. Scaled score and z-score (decision of 18 November 2026). Recomputed from the raw total in the application's own norm table (norms/wais3_arithmetic.csv, 12 age groups read from the scripts of the EMR; not part of the repository) and delivered; the stored ones are read as checks (keep: false) and a difference is score_mismatch on the delivered score. The EMR read its table with the age typed in the form (cclin01_); the package uses that age where it is within one year of the age at the visit, else the age at the visit (age: wais3_arith_age). The z-score is (scaled score - 10) / 3 (tolerance 0.006). On the 532 visits that have a stored and a recomputed scaled score, 2 differ (before 2013), both with a typed age more than a year from the age at the visit (read with the typed age as it stands the table gives the stored score on all 531 visits that have a typed age). The z-score differs on the same 2. The typed age is within a year of the age at the visit on 515 of the 533 visits that have a total, farther on 17 and missing on 1. Two typed ages written 'NN ans' are unparsed; the age at the visit is used where the typed one is not read (1 of the 2 visits have this subtest).

wais3_arithmetique.description: WAIS-III arithmetic: 20 items (the last two scored 0 to 2, a point for speed), the raw total, the age-scaled score and its z-score. SZ only, 2010 to 2015.
flags: WAIS-III and WAIS-IV are two instruments stored in the same raw columns; each schema reads only the visits of its edition. Do not pool the two editions.

Scaled scores and z-scores are computed again from the raw scores with the norm tables of the application; the stored ones are only checks. The tables are not checked against the manuals (open question DM-4).
The norm tables are read with the age typed in the form where it is within 1 year of the age at the visit, else with the age at the visit.
A total needs every item: the application writes none when an item is empty.

wais3_complement_images.title: WAIS-III picture completion

sz.notes: WAIS-III and WAIS-IV are two instruments stored in the same columns (decision D10 of the BP file). wais3_efficience.title: WAIS-III intellectual efficiency (seven-subtest short form)

sz.notes: The IQs and the working memory index that the EMR estimated from the seven WAIS-III subtests of the battery, on the WAIS-III visits (2010 to 2015, 527 with a stored verbal sum). The WAIS-IV visits are read by wais4_efficience.yaml. Edition rule (decision D138, question O16). The form labels 33 visits WAIS-III although they hold the WAIS-IV digit-span sequencing task (the columns mcoc_w and mcocemp_w, which only the WAIS-IV has). They are read as WAIS-IV: the version block lists the two columns under override, and the visits get the flag version_overridden. 25 of them hold the WAIS-IV indices and are read in wais4_efficience.yaml. One of the 33 also holds values in the WAIS-III columns of this schema (and in the WAIS-III-only item columns of other subtests); it follows the marker, is read as WAIS-IV, and its WAIS-III values are not delivered. The dictionary gives no formula. In the data the sums are those of a seven-subtest short form, on every visit where the scaled scores are there: verbal sum = 2 x similarities + 2 x information + arithmetic + digit span (527 of 527 visits, with the stored scaled scores), performance sum = 2 x picture completion + 2 x matrices + coding (538 of 538), working memory sum = digit span + arithmetic + letter-number sequencing (472 of 472); the stored total sum is the stored verbal sum + the stored performance sum on 523 of 523. tests/test_real_data_sz.py checks the three formulas. The four sums are recomputed here from the scaled scores that the other schemas deliver (uses; the two doubled terms are scores that are not delivered), and the stored sums are checks (wais3_*_sum_scaled_stored, not delivered), as in wais4_efficience.yaml (decision D137). The stored sums were built on stored scaled scores: the recomputed sum equals the stored one on 522 of 527 verbal sums, 532 of 538 performance sums, 517 of 523 total sums and 468 of 472 working memory sums. Every difference (5, 6, 6 and 4, score_mismatch) is before 2013 and on a visit where one stored scaled score differs from the table. The sums are also delivered on 1 visit each (verbal, total, working memory) where the application stored none. Each sum gives one IQ or index, and each percentile rank is the one of the normal curve (mean 100, SD 15) for its IQ, within 0.5: the stored percentile ranks are, for the stored IQ, on 526 of 526 verbal, 537 of 537 performance and 465 of 466 working memory visits (the full-scale IQ is not stored). A percentile written "<0.1" is read as 0.1 and flagged censored_left. The estimated full-scale IQ (ei06_wais3 in the dictionary) is not in the extraction, although its percentile rank and its confidence interval are (open question O14). Where the Barona difference is filled, the expected IQ minus that difference gives it back: a whole number on 504 of 504 WAIS-III visits, inside the stored interval on 503 of 503 that have one. The confidence intervals are texts ("85-95") and are delivered as stored. The verbal interval does not hold the stored verbal IQ on 14 of 526 visits. The Barona expected verbal and performance IQs are in barona.yaml. IQs, working memory index and percentile ranks (decision of 18 November 2026). Each IQ and the index is recomputed from its sum in the application's own age-free table (norms/wais3_qiv.csv, wais3_qip.csv, wais3_qit.csv and wais3_imt_index.csv, read from the scripts of the EMR; not part of the repository) and delivered; each percentile rank is read from the same sum in the application's own table (norms/wais3_qiv_percentile.csv, wais3_qip_percentile.csv, wais3_qit_percentile.csv and wais3_imt_percentile.csv) and delivered; the stored values are checks (keep: false, wais3_*_stored and wais3_*_percentile_stored) and a difference is score_mismatch on the delivered value (tolerance 0.051 for a percentile). From the stored sums the tables give the stored verbal IQ on 527 of 527 visits, the performance IQ on 538 of 538 and the working memory index on 467 of 469, and the stored percentile rank on 526 of 526, 537 of 537, 522 of 522 (full-scale) and 463 of 466 (working memory). From the recomputed sums the delivered values differ from the stored ones on 4 verbal IQs, 6 performance IQs and 6 working memory indices, and on 3, 6, 4 and 7 percentile ranks (verbal, performance, full-scale, working memory): the visits whose sum differs, plus the working memory ones where the table does not give the stored value (2 indices, 3 percentile ranks). The percentile rank of the working memory index is delivered on 7 visits that have no stored one. At a few IQs (full-scale 45 to 50 and 141, verbal 62) one cell of these tables differs by 0.1 to 0.5 from the other tables; the 7 WAIS-III visits at those IQs have the stored percentile rank, and nothing is claimed about the manual. The full-scale IQ (ei06_wais3, open question O14) is not in the extraction; it is delivered as wais3_qit, read in the table from the total sum (524 visits), and it is the Barona expected IQ minus the stored difference on 499 of the 504 visits that have both (504 of 504 from the stored total sum). The confidence intervals of the verbal and performance IQs get derived_doubt where the stored IQ differs from the recomputed one (4 and 6 visits); that of the full-scale IQ stays as stored, there is no stored IQ to compare with. One stored working-memory percentile rank typed as a range ('NN-NN') stays unparsed (a check, not delivered).

SZ only, 2010 to 2015.

wais4_arithmetique.title: WAIS-IV arithmetic

sz.notes: WAIS-III and WAIS-IV are two instruments stored in the same columns (decision D10 of the BP file). This schema reads the arithmetic columns on the WAIS-IV visits (489 visits, from 2013 to 2025): 22 items scored 0 or 1. wais3_arithmetique.yaml reads the WAIS-III visits. Edition rule (decision D138, question O16): the 33 visits that the form labels WAIS-III and that hold the WAIS-IV digit-span sequencing task (columns mcoc_w and mcocemp_w) are read as WAIS-IV (override in the version block, flag version_overridden). 25 of them hold arithmetic items and are read here, not in wais3_arithmetique.yaml. Of the 489 visits, 475 have all 22 items and a stored raw total, which is their sum on 475 of 475. 14 visits have empty items (the last item filled is 0 on 13 of them, the mark of a stopping rule): 1 has a stored total, equal to the sum of the items present, which cannot be recomputed (score_not_recomputed), and 13 have none. The application adds the 22 items and writes 'Questionnaire incomplet' when one is empty. The first four items are 1 on 480 of the 480 visits that have them: the test starts further on and credits them. The z-score is (scaled score - 10) / 3 on every visit. FACE BP does not have this subtest. Scaled score and z-score. They are recomputed and delivered (decision of the project lead for the standard scores of the neuropsychological tests): the scaled score is read in the WAIS-IV table of the application (norms/wais4_arithmetic.csv) from the raw total of the items, and the z-score is (scaled score - 10) / 3. The table is read with the age typed in the form (cclin01_, delivered as neuropsy_age by neuropsy_conditions) where it is within 1 year of the age at the visit, and with the age at the visit elsewhere (462 of the 475 visits that have a total use the typed age, 13 have a typed age more than 1 year away). The stored scores are wais4_arith_scaled_stored and wais4_arith_z_stored, not delivered. Verified: the scaled score differs from the stored one on 3 of the 475 visits that have both, and so does its z-score (score_mismatch, 2 in 2016 to 2018 and 1 from 2024); no total gives norm_missing; the stored total that cannot be recomputed gives score_not_recomputed on the total, the scaled score and the z-score. Items 21 and 22 are filled on 2 visits labelled WAIS-III that hold no sequencing task, so the edition rule leaves them there: they are read as WAIS-III and the 2 cells of each item are not delivered.

dr.notes: WAIS-IV Arithmetic: the raw total, the age-scaled score and its z-score. SZ also has the 22 items; here only the totals are entered. 621 visits. One edition. No column names the edition of the WAIS in this cohort. The data show the WAIS-IV in every year. Within a band of the typed age a raw score has one stored scaled score for digit span and similarities, and for arithmetic, coding and symbol search on every cell but one (2, 3 and 4 visits). The stored score is the same before and after 2018 on every cell seen in both periods but one (symbol search). 95 digit span totals are above 30, the maximum of the WAIS-III. The processing speed index stored by DR follows the WAIS-IV table of BP (norms/wais4_ivt.csv) on each of its 35 distinct sums, all seen in BP (the WAIS-III table on 21 of 35). The version block gives wais_version = wais4 on the 731 visits that hold a subtest, so that the column exists as in BP and SZ. Scaled score and z-score. They are recomputed and delivered (decision of the project lead for the standard scores of the neuropsychological tests): the scaled score is read in the WAIS-IV table of the application (norms/wais4_arithmetic.csv) from the raw total, and the z-score is (scaled score - 10) / 3. The plain table that the other cohorts use is used here too, not the table of the DR script (norms/wais4_arithmetic_dr.csv): where the script has another value (a typo), the stored score is flagged. The 35-44 row of the DR script holds 18 cells instead of 19 and differs from the table on 10 age-by-raw cells (one raw score at each of the ten ages): on 3 of the 621 visits the script gives another value (the stored score is the script's, 1 point below the table's). One visit aged 80 or over at the visit (its typed age is more than 1 year younger, which is why a score is stored) has no value in the table, and the DR script has no row from 80 either: norm_missing, and the stored score is not recomputed. Age. The table is read with the age typed in the form (cclin01, delivered as neuropsy_age by neuropsy_conditions) where it is within 1 year of the age at the visit, and with the age at the visit elsewhere: 579 of the 621 visits use the typed age and 42 have a typed age more than 1 year away (35 of them typed younger). The 7 of them that differ from the delivered score equal the table at the typed age (see wais4_memoire_chiffres.yaml for the four schemas together). The stored scores are wais4_arith_scaled_stored and wais4_arith_z_stored, not delivered. Verified: the scaled score differs from the stored one on 11 of 620 visits (1.8%, score_mismatch, 2013 to 2023: 7 typed age, 3 table typo, 1 unexplained), its z-score on 25 of 605, which include the 14 visits of 2013-10 to 2015-05 where the stored z-score is not (scaled score - 10) / 3 (the old z table described in wais4_memoire_chiffres.yaml).

asp.notes: Arithmetic: 22 items scored from 0 to 1, their total, the scaled score and its z-score, on 209 inclusion visits. The WAIS-IV of this cohort is recorded item by item, on about 210 to 295 inclusion visits depending on the subtest (302 visits in all, 12 of patients under 18), from 2013 to 2026. It is on 14% of the inclusion visits of 2013, 42% of 2014, 36% of 2015, 18% to 19% of 2016 and 2017, 3% to 11% of 2018 to 2023, 21% to 22% of 2024 and 2025 and 7% of 2026 so far. It is the fourth edition: the visual puzzles and the sequencing part of the digit span exist only in it. No other edition of the scale is recorded in this table. The extraction has no column for the edition: wais_version (wais4) is read from the first item of each subtest, with the same block in the eleven schemas of the WAIS-IV, and is filled on the 302 visits that hold one of them. Checked on every visit: the stored total is the sum of the items, and the stored z-score is the scaled score minus 10, over 3. The stored total equals the sum of the items on 209 of the 209 visits that hold every item. Same instrument and output names as in FACE SZ, in other columns. Scaled score and z-score. They are recomputed and delivered (decision of the project lead for the standard scores of the neuropsychological tests): the scaled score is read in the WAIS-IV table of the application (norms/wais4_arithmetic.csv) from the raw total, and the z-score is (scaled score - 10) / 3. The plain table that BP, SZ and DR read is used. The ASP copy (norms/wais4_arithmetic_asp.csv) holds the same values at every age from 16 to 79 and only reuses its 75-79 row from 80 years: it is not needed, no visit of this cohort is 80 or over, and no table has a row from 80 years or below 16 (nothing is extrapolated). The form has no typed age in this cohort: the table is read with the age at the date of the assessment form (age basis, below). The visits are of patients from 15.9 to 65 years; the one of 15.9 years is below the first age of the tables (16) and gets norm_missing on ten subtests: the script gives every age under 18 the first band, the tables start at 16. The stored scores are wais4_arith_scaled_stored and wais4_arith_z_stored, not delivered. Verified: the scaled score differs from the stored one on 11 of the 208 visits that have both (5.3%, score_mismatch; 7 in 2013 to 2015, 4 later; 12 with the age at the visit), and so does its z-score; 1 visit is not recomputed (the patient of 15.9 years). The 25-29 row of the script. 9 of the 11 differences are visits aged 25 to 29 dated 2014 to 2017 (9 of the 16 visits of that age and period; none of the 22 later visits of that age differs). The row of that age group in the ASP script replaced a commented row marked as an error about 2017-18 (read in the script history): the stored score equals the old row on 9 of 9 visits of 2014 to 2017 where the two rows differ and the new row on 6 later ones. The table that is read is the one of the current script, so the stored scores of 2014 to 2017 at that age group are the differences. Age basis. The application (eAsperger, script 280_score.js, function gere_ageNPSY) computes the age at the date of the assessment form (QSDTC), not at the visit date, and the data show that it did so from about 2015 on. The table is therefore read with the age at the form date (wais4_arith_assessment_date, read from the raw column qsdtc and not delivered; score fields age_date and age_date_since 2015-01-01) where the visit is dated 2015 or later and the form date is within 366 days of the visit, and with the age at the visit elsewhere. In this subtest the differences are 12 with the age at the visit and 11 with the form date. All subtests together. Over the eleven subtests that read a table with the age (picture completion included), the scaled scores that differ from the stored ones fall from 62 to 50 with the age at the form date (12 scores, none new), and the three span z-scores of the digit span from 36 to 26 (10 scores). Reading the form date for the visits before 2015 too would leave 6 more differences, which is why the date starts in 2015. Of the 50 that remain, 13 equal the reading with the age at the form date where that date is more than 366 days from the visit (10 visits; the pipeline does not read it, and a limit of 1,000 days instead would explain 13 more and create 1), 6 equal the reading of the first age band (4 where the form date is empty, 2 where it gives an age under 18: the script reads such an age as the first band) and 31 follow neither. In 2024, 11 of the 52 WAIS visits (two centres) have a scaled score that differs with the age at the visit; the form date explains 3 of them (it is 40 to 90 days from the visit: 44 of the 51 WAIS visits of 2024 that have a form date have it more than 31 days from the visit) and 8 remain.

wais4_complement_images.title: WAIS-IV picture completion

sz.notes: WAIS-III and WAIS-IV are two instruments stored in the same columns (decision D10 of the BP file). This schema reads the picture completion columns on the WAIS-IV visits (490 visits, from 2013 to 2025): 24 items scored 0 or 1. wais3_complement_images.yaml reads the WAIS-III visits. The dictionary files the columns under the WAIS-III; the section of this schema repeats that label, '(WAIS-3) ancienne version', and the WAIS-IV visits are recognised by the version rule, not by the label. Edition rule (decision D138, question O16): the 33 visits that the form labels WAIS-III and that hold the WAIS-IV digit-span sequencing task (columns mcoc_w and mcocemp_w) are read as WAIS-IV (override in the version block, flag version_overridden). 25 of them hold picture completion items and are read here, not in wais3_complement_images.yaml. Of the 490 visits, 479 have all 24 items and a stored raw total, which is their sum on 479 of 479. 11 visits have empty items (the last item filled is 0 on all 11, the mark of a stopping rule) and no stored total, and get none: the application adds the 24 items and writes 'Questionnaire incomplet' when one is empty. The z-score is (scaled score - 10) / 3 on every visit. FACE BP does not have this subtest. Scaled score and z-score. They are recomputed and delivered (decision of the project lead for the standard scores of the neuropsychological tests): the scaled score is read in the WAIS-IV table of the application (norms/wais4_picture_completion.csv) from the raw total of the items, and the z-score is (scaled score - 10) / 3. The table is read with the age typed in the form (cclin01_, delivered as neuropsy_age by neuropsy_conditions) where it is within 1 year of the age at the visit, and with the age at the visit elsewhere (464 of the 479 visits that have a total use the typed age, 15 have a typed age more than 1 year away). The stored scores are wais4_pc_scaled_stored and wais4_pc_z_stored, not delivered. Verified: the scaled score differs on 5 of the 479 visits that have both, and so does its z-score (score_mismatch, 1 in 2013 to 2015, 2 in 2016 to 2018, 1 in 2019 to 2021 and 1 from 2024); no total gives norm_missing. 3 of the 5 differences are on visits whose typed age is more than 1 year from the age at the visit (3.1% of the visits), where the package reads the table with the age at the visit and the EMR with the typed one.

Same instrument and output names as in FACE SZ, in other columns. Scaled score and z-score. The plain table is used, the one that BP, SZ and DR read; it holds the values of the ASP script (norms/wais4_picture_completion_asp.csv is an identical copy, no longer needed). Verified on the 5 visits that have both: none differs; 1 more stored scaled score is not recomputed (the visit holds that score alone, no item and no total). Age basis. In this subtest the age at the form date changes no score. The script. The row of the ages 55 to 64 that the ASP script uses is complete: the row above it, commented out and marked as an error, held a typo (one cell), which the SZ script still has. The rows of 25-29 and 75-79 have empty cells (the last cell of 25-29, the first two of 75-79): a raw score that falls there has no scaled score. No visit of this cohort does (no norm_missing).

wais4_efficience.title: WAIS-IV intellectual efficiency (estimated indices)

sz.section: Efficience intellectuelle (WAIS-4) - nouvelle version (données à partir de juin 2015)
sz.notes: The indices that the EMR estimated from the seven WAIS-IV subtests of the battery, on the WAIS-IV visits. Two periods. From 2015 to 2018 the seven subtests were given and the four indices and the full-scale IQ are filled (about 475 visits: the verbal comprehension sum is stored on 480 visits, 2014 to 2019 and one of 2025, the full-scale sum on 454). From 2019 the battery keeps similarities, matrices and digit span, and the only estimate is the two-subtest IQ that the dictionary calls "Denney 2015" (538 visits, 2016 to 2026). It is stored for 41% to 68% of the inclusions of 2019 to 2021 and for 10% to 28% of those of 2022 to 2026, while its subtests are still done (open question O28 in PROGRESS.md). Edition rule (decision D138, question O16). 25 visits of 2013 to 2016 that the form labels WAIS-III hold the WAIS-IV indices and the WAIS-IV digit-span sequencing task (the columns mcoc_w and mcocemp_w, which only the WAIS-IV has). The version block lists the two columns under override: these visits are read as WAIS-IV, with the flag version_overridden, and are delivered here (they were not read before). The dictionary gives no formula. In the data, on the visits where the scaled scores are there: verbal comprehension sum = 1.5 x (similarities + information) (479 of 480), perceptual reasoning sum = 1.5 x (matrices + picture completion) (475 of 475), working memory sum = digit span + arithmetic (469 of 471), full-scale sum = 10/7 x the sum of the seven scaled scores (451 of 454), with the stored scaled scores. The scaled scores are in other schemas: the sums are recomputed from the scaled scores that those schemas deliver (uses), and the stored sums are checks (wais4_*_sum_scaled_stored, not delivered); tests/test_real_data_sz.py checks the formulas. The stored sums were built on stored scaled scores: 3 of 473 verbal comprehension sums, 4 of 474 perceptual reasoning sums, 3 of 471 working memory sums and 4 of 447 full-scale sums differ from the recomputed ones (score_mismatch), all but one on a visit where a stored scaled score of one of their subtests differs from the table. Only 2 of the 133 flagged similarities visits have a stored sum: the EMR stored the sums up to 2018 (3 later ones) and the similarities error is 4 visits before 2021 and 129 from 2021. "NaN" in a stored sum is a missing code: a subtest was not given. A visit whose stored sum cannot be recomputed (a subtest missing) gets no sum and no index (score_not_recomputed): 7 verbal comprehension sums, 7 full-scale sums and 1 perceptual reasoning sum, 6 of the first two being visits where the information raw total can no longer be recomputed (an item is empty, see wais4_information.yaml). Two stored indices are 0.7 and 2.9 lower than the index of the table (decision D12, open question O15). The stored working memory index always ends in .3 and the stored full-scale IQ in .1, while an index is a whole number. Three facts say that the working memory index is 0.7 too low and the full-scale IQ 2.9 too low, on every visit, in every year and centre: (1) at the centre of the sum, where every index is 100, they are 99.3 and 97.1; (2) their percentile ranks are those of the normal curve for the stored value plus 0.7 and plus 2.9, as the percentile ranks of the two other indices are for their stored value; (3) the Barona difference of the same visit is the expected IQ minus (the stored IQ plus 2.9) (310 of 314 visits that have both). The verbal comprehension and perceptual reasoning indices are right as stored. The two-subtest IQ follows the sum of the scaled scores of similarities and matrices (about 47.6 + 2.38 x the sum, rounded) on 512 of 535 visits (with the recomputed scaled scores; 504 of 536 with the stored ones); the 23 others, 3 in 2019 to 2021 and 20 from 2022, hold another value. "undefined" is a missing code: one of the two subtests was not given. One value of 10 is out of range. The cell is empty on 1,317 WAIS-IV visits that have both scaled scores. The processing speed index is in wais4_code_symboles_ivt.yaml. Indices. They are read in the tables of the manual and delivered (decision of the project lead for the standard scores of the neuropsychological tests), from the sum of the recomputed scaled scores of each index (norms/wais4_icv.csv, wais4_irp.csv, wais4_imt.csv and wais4_qit.csv, with their wais4_*_percentile.csv; the tables are the same in the four applications). The stored indices and percentile ranks are wais4_*_index_stored, wais4_qit_stored and wais4_*_percentile_stored, not delivered. For the working memory index and the full-scale IQ the stored value is the table value minus 0.7 and minus 2.9 (compare_offset): the table value is delivered. This replaces the correction by +0.7 and +2.9 of the stored values. Verified: from the stored sums, on every visit that has both (480 verbal comprehension, 475 perceptual reasoning, 471 working memory, 454 full-scale IQ) the table gives the stored index (with the two offsets) and the stored percentile rank, to 0.051 (453 for the full-scale percentile rank): no norm_missing. From the recomputed sums the delivered indices differ from the stored ones where the sum differs (score_mismatch: 3 verbal comprehension, 4 perceptual reasoning, 3 working memory and 4 full-scale visits, and 3, 4, 2 and 3 percentile ranks). A percentile of 0.1 or 99.9 is censored (wais4_*_percentile_cens). The two-subtest IQ is delivered as stored.

dr.notes: WAIS-IV working memory index: the sum of the scaled scores of Digit Span and Arithmetic, the index and its percentile rank. SZ has the other indices of the WAIS-IV in the schema of this name; DR can deliver none of them: its form has only similarities, digit span, arithmetic, coding and symbol search, so there is no verbal comprehension index (it needs information or vocabulary), no perceptual reasoning index (no matrices, block design or picture completion) and no full-scale IQ. The indices of this cohort are this working memory index and the processing speed index of wais4_code_symboles_ivt.yaml. 615 visits hold a stored sum, 614 a recomputed one. One edition. No column names the edition of the WAIS in this cohort. The data show the WAIS-IV in every year. Within a band of the typed age a raw score has one stored scaled score for digit span and similarities, and for arithmetic, coding and symbol search on every cell but one (2, 3 and 4 visits). The stored score is the same before and after 2018 on every cell seen in both periods but one (symbol search). 95 digit span totals are above 30, the maximum of the WAIS-III. The processing speed index stored by DR follows the WAIS-IV table of BP (norms/wais4_ivt.csv) on each of its 35 distinct sums, all seen in BP (the WAIS-III table on 21 of 35). The version block gives wais_version = wais4 on the 731 visits that hold a subtest, so that the column exists as in BP and SZ. Scaled scores, sum and index. They are recomputed and delivered (decision of the project lead for the standard scores of the neuropsychological tests). The sum adds the two scaled scores that the digit span and arithmetic schemas deliver (uses: wais4_ds_scaled and wais4_arith_scaled, as the SZ schema of this name does, decision D137): this schema reads no raw total and no typed age and repeats no table lookup, and the sum is the digit span score plus the arithmetic score on 614 of 614 visits. The index and its percentile rank are read from the sum in the index tables (norms/wais4_imt.csv and wais4_imt_percentile.csv). The stored sum, index and percentile rank are wais4_imt_*_stored, not delivered. The stored index is right here: in SZ the stored index is 0.7 too low and the SZ schema reads the table with that offset; here no offset is needed. Verified on the visits that have both (614): the sum differs from the stored one on 17 visits (2.8%, score_mismatch), the index on 16 and the percentile rank on 16; one more visit has a stored sum and no recomputed one (the visit aged 80 or over has no value in the arithmetic table: norm_missing in the arithmetic schema, score_not_recomputed here). Of the 17 sums that differ, 15 are visits where the digit span or the arithmetic scaled score differs from the stored one (8 and 11 visits: causes in wais4_memoire_chiffres.yaml and wais4_arithmetique.yaml); the 2 others are stored sums more than 15 points above the sum of the two scaled scores. 2 stored sums are above 38, the highest possible: out_of_range.
dr.difference: the working memory index only (the form has no information, vocabulary, matrices or picture completion, so no other index and no full-scale IQ), read in the table of the application from the sum of the scaled scores that the digit span and arithmetic schemas deliver (uses); the stored index is the table's value (in SZ it is 0.7 too low and is read with an offset); no column names the edition

asp.notes: The sums of scaled scores, the indices and their percentile ranks, as the neuropsychology form computes them: verbal comprehension, perceptual reasoning, working memory and the full scale, on about 205 inclusion visits (the processing speed index is in wais4_code_symboles_ivt). The WAIS-IV of this cohort is recorded item by item, on about 210 to 295 inclusion visits depending on the subtest (302 visits in all, 12 of patients under 18), from 2013 to 2026. It is on 14% of the inclusion visits of 2013, 42% of 2014, 36% of 2015, 18% to 19% of 2016 and 2017, 3% to 11% of 2018 to 2023, 21% to 22% of 2024 and 2025 and 7% of 2026 so far. It is the fourth edition: the visual puzzles and the sequencing part of the digit span exist only in it. No other edition of the scale is recorded in this table. The extraction has no column for the edition: wais_version (wais4) is read from the first item of each subtest, with the same block in the eleven schemas of the WAIS-IV, and is filled on the 302 visits that hold one of them. Each index is one function of its sum of scaled scores on every visit, as a norm table gives it. The sums of scaled scores come from subtests that are in other schemas: they are recomputed from the scaled scores that those schemas deliver (uses) and the stored sums are checks (wais4_*_sum_scaled_stored, not delivered). Verbal comprehension is similarities + vocabulary + information, perceptual reasoning block design + matrices + visual puzzles, working memory digit span + arithmetic, the full scale the ten core subtests; the sets (_a) are 1.5 x (similarities + information) and 1.5 x (matrices + picture completion). The stored sums differ from the recomputed ones on 3 to 12 visits per sum (verbal comprehension 4, perceptual reasoning 3, working memory 12, full scale 12; 4 to 13 with the age at the visit), each on a visit where a stored scaled score differs from the table (score_mismatch). The full-scale sum of the second set (stored on 6 visits) is the plain sum of the seven subtests information, similarities, matrices, picture completion, digit span, arithmetic and coding, without a factor: 5 of the 5 visits that can be compared are equal, and the 6th has no picture completion and is not recomputed. It is delivered computed, with the stored sum as a check (wais4_qit_sum_scaled_a_stored, not delivered). The application looks this sum up in the table of the sum of ten subtests, so its stored full-scale IQ of the second set is lower than the first set's on all of the 4 visits that have both (an observation, nothing is claimed about the manual); wais4_qit_a reads the same table and reproduces the stored value on 5 of 5. In ASP the verbal comprehension of the first set is similarities + vocabulary + information (3 subtests), while SZ uses 1.5 x (similarities + information), which is the second set (_a) here. **Two sources for the same index.** The clinician copies the indices into the medical evaluation (schema wais4_indices, about 995 visits), where they are named wais4_icv_index_clinician, wais4_irp_index_clinician, wais4_imt_index_clinician, wais4_ivt_index_clinician and wais4_qit_clinician. The indices of this form have the names that BP, SZ and DR give them (wais4_icv_index, wais4_irp_index, wais4_imt_index, wais4_qit; the processing speed index is wais4_ivt_index in wais4_code_symboles_ivt). Where both exist the delivered indices agree on 162 of 187 visits for verbal comprehension, 157 of 188 for perceptual reasoning, 176 of 192 for working memory and 120 of 159 for the full-scale IQ (86.6%, 83.5%, 91.7% and 75.5%; the stored indices of this form agree on 161, 156, 168 and 115); neither source is corrected from the other. A second set of numbers, whose names end in _a, exists for verbal comprehension (207 visits) and, on six visits, for perceptual reasoning and the full scale. It is the set of the abbreviated form (thesaurus), equal to the first set on few visits (28 of 205 for verbal comprehension, none of the 4 comparable visits for the other two). Same instrument and names as in FACE SZ and DR (the indices have the shared names), in other columns. Indices. They are read in the tables of the manual and delivered (decision of the project lead for the standard scores of the neuropsychological tests), from the sum of the recomputed scaled scores of each index (norms/wais4_icv.csv, wais4_irp.csv, wais4_imt.csv and wais4_qit.csv, with their wais4_*_percentile.csv; the tables are the same in the four applications). The stored indices and percentile ranks are wais4_*_index_stored, wais4_*_index_a_stored, wais4_qit_stored, wais4_qit_a_stored, wais4_qit_sum_scaled_a_stored and wais4_*_percentile_*_stored, not delivered. No correction is needed (unlike the SZ working memory index and full-scale IQ). A sum follows the scaled scores recomputed in the other schemas of this cohort. Verified: on every visit that has a stored sum and a stored index (205 verbal comprehension, 202 perceptual reasoning, 207 working memory, 196 full-scale IQ for the first set; 207, 6 and 6 for the second set) the stored index is the table value of the stored sum, and so is the stored percentile rank, to 0.051 (204, 201, 207 and 194 visits; 206, 6 and 6). The delivered indices come from the recomputed sums, so they differ from the stored ones where a sum differs: score_mismatch on 4, 3, 12 and 8 visits for the first set (5, 4, 13 and 9 with the age at the visit) and on 4, 0 and 0 for the second, the percentile ranks on 4, 3, 12 and 7; no norm_missing. A percentile of 0.1 or 99.9 is censored (wais4_*_percentile_cens). The one score_not_recomputed of each sum, index and percentile rank of the first set, and of the verbal comprehension of the second, is the visit of 15.9 years (no scaled score for its subtests).

Age basis. The application (eAsperger, script 280_score.js, function gere_ageNPSY) computes the age at the date of the assessment form (QSDTC), not at the visit date, and the data show that it did so from about 2015 on. The table is therefore read with the age at the form date (wais4_info_assessment_date, read from the raw column qsdtc and not delivered; score fields age_date and age_date_since 2015-01-01) where the visit is dated 2015 or later and the form date is within 366 days of the visit, and with the age at the visit elsewhere. In this subtest the age at the form date changes no score.

hospitalisations_12m.title: Full-time hospitalisations in the past year (at follow-up: since the last visit)

sz.notes: Asked at inclusion and at every follow-up visit (4,513 visits): was the patient hospitalised full time, how many times, for how many weeks in all, and why. 780 of 2,173 inclusion visits say yes (36%) and 453 of 2,340 follow-up visits (19%); "Ne sais pas" (19) is a missing code. Time frame (decision D70, R14b). At inclusion the question is about the past year. At follow-up the form uses the same words ("au cours de l'année écoulée", under the heading "characteristics of the disorder over the last 12 months") and has no change gate, but the answers follow the time since the previous visit: among the answered follow-up visits the share of yes is 17% for the 1,469 that come up to 420 days after the previous visit and 23% for the 868 that come later (the median gap is 391 days), where the somatic sick leave of the same form, worded 12 months, stays at 7% in both. So a follow-up answer is read as "since the last visit", as in BP (D54, D123); the names keep _12m, and the labels say both. The number, the length and the reason are asked after a yes. After "Non" the number is filled on 4 of 3,261 visits (3 above 0), the length on 2 and the reason on 2; after "Oui" the number is filled on 1,179 of 1,233 (96%), the length on 1,142 and the reason on 1,182. The number is 0 after a "no", and the length is 0 where the number is 0 (asked_if, as decision D122 for the whole life): 3,257 and 3,258 cells were missing, 6 yes visits hold the number 0 themselves. The reason is a detail and stays missing after a no. "Ne sais pas" is a missing code. The length stops at 52 weeks (the form limit; none above). In FACE BP the number and the length of the past year are asked at inclusion only (hospitalisations_v0); the names are the same. Care use. The follow-up form of the application also holds a block of care use since the last visit (general practitioner, psychiatrist, psychologist, nurse interviews, specialists, other consultations, psychiatric and somatic emergencies without admission, non-psychiatric care and examinations): the clean model reads 36 columns of it, but face_sz_10 (line 46) selects none, so SZ has no care_use schema (request R124). When it is exported, the BP care_* names are the ones to use, with care_nurse as a variable of its own.
