alcohol_use.title: Alcohol use

sz.notes: Has the patient drunk alcohol more than ten times in their life, the amounts and frequencies over the whole life (in the periods of heaviest use, "périodes de consommation maximales" in the form) and in the last 12 months, the frequency of heavy drinking (more than 6 glasses on one occasion), the age at the first drink, the longest abstinence, the family history and a craving score. 3,477 visits answer the first question; 75% say yes at inclusion and 73% at follow-up. The question is "more than ten times in your life", not "ever": the patients who say no are asked a second question, whether they never drank at all (alcohol_never_once, primary abstinence). That question is shown after a no only, so after a yes it is delivered as 0 (asked_if on a hidden variable that reads the first answer the other way round and is not delivered): 2,578 cells missing become 0 (1,218 at inclusion, 1,360 at follow-up). Asked at inclusion and at yearly visits, used from 2015 and not from 2012: the first question is answered on 9% of the inclusion visits of 2012, 18% of 2014, 48% of 2015 and 83% to 93% from 2016 (yearly visits: 14% in 2014, 55% in 2015, 68% to 90% after). The questions about the whole life keep that meaning at follow-up on average only: the share of yes is the same at the two, but 169 of the 1,154 later answers (15%) of the patients who said yes at inclusion are no, and at follow-up the age at onset of the disorder equals the age given at inclusion in 65 of 97 pairs (substance_fu.yaml). The details are filled after a yes. 999 and 9999 mean "does not know" in an amount or a duration, 99 in an age. "Ne sais pas" is a missing code. Not asked, not no. The questions at the end of the section (age at the first use, longest abstinence, family history of a use disorder, craving) are shown only with two or more DSM-5 criteria, a count that is in another tab (auto_questionnaire/dsm5_alcohol.yaml): they are filled on 0 of 1,500 visits with none or one criterion and on 80% to 85% of 546 with two or more. An empty cell means "not asked"; it is not encoded. The number of times per week is filled after "1 to 7 times a week" (98% of 1,247 answers for the whole life) and after "less than weekly" on none of 740: not encoded. "Less than weekly" holds the non-users of the last 12 months: 559 of the 1,266 answers of that frequency have an amount of 0. Amounts are glasses (10 g of alcohol) per day of use. The range is 0 to 40 glasses: 49 amounts over the whole life are above it (22 from 41 to 60, 22 from 61 to 100 and 5 above 100; 8 more are 999) and 5 of the last 12 months; they are flagged out_of_range and delivered as missing. Ages are plausible: the first use is at 6 or later and none is above the patient's age. Two frequency columns of the last 12 months have names of their own (rad_add_alc6b, rad_add_alc6c). The twelve criteria of an alcohol use disorder are in auto_questionnaire/dsm5_alcohol.yaml. The questions of the form on a drug treatment of the alcohol use disorder and on a hospitalisation for withdrawal (yes, number, age at the first) are not in the extraction (export request R120). By year, "never once" is delivered as yes (0 after a yes to the first question included) on 8% of the answers of 2014-16, of 2017-19 and of 2020-22, and on 15% from 2023, with a rise in eight of the nine centres that have 20 answers in both of the last two periods. The longest abstinence (months, a question over the whole life) has a median of 4 in 2014-19, 11 in 2020-22 and 6 from 2023, and of 3 to 6 in five centres against 12 and 18 in two others; the family history is yes on 30% to 52% by centre: no known cause.

cannabis_use.title: Cannabis use

sz.notes: Has the patient used cannabis more than ten times in their life, the amounts (joints per day of use) and frequencies over the whole life (in the periods of heaviest use, "périodes de consommation maximales" in the form) and in the last 12 months, the age at the first use, the longest abstinence, the family history and a craving score. 3,451 visits answer the first question; 50% say yes at inclusion and 46% at follow-up. The question is "more than ten times in your life", not "ever": about 70% of the inclusion answers have used cannabis at least once (the patients who say no and are not primary abstainers have used it one to ten times). The patients who say no are asked a second question, whether they never used it at all (cannabis_never_once). It is shown after a no only, so after a yes it is delivered as 0 (asked_if on a hidden variable that reads the first answer the other way round and is not delivered): 1,661 cells missing become 0. Asked at inclusion and at yearly visits, used from 2015 and not from 2012: the first question is answered on 6% of the inclusion and yearly visits of 2012, 16% of 2014, 52% of 2015 and 83% of 2016. The questions about the whole life keep that meaning at follow-up on average only: the share of yes is the same at the two, but 80 of the 725 later answers (11%) of the patients who said yes at inclusion are no (55 of 748 the other way round). At follow-up the age at onset of the disorder equals the age given at inclusion in 119 of 169 pairs (substance_fu.yaml); it is below the age at the first use on none of 685 pairs. The details are filled after a yes. 999 and 9999 mean "does not know" in an amount or a duration, 99 in an age. "Ne sais pas" is a missing code. Not asked, not no. The questions at the end of the section (age at the first use, longest abstinence, family history of a use disorder, craving) are shown only with two or more DSM-5 criteria, a count that is in another tab (auto_questionnaire/dsm5_cannabis.yaml): they are filled on 1 of 433 visits with none or one criterion and on 80% to 85% of 835 with two or more. An empty cell means "not asked"; it is not encoded. The number of times per week is filled after "1 to 7 times a week" (98% of 1,143 answers for the whole life) and after "less than weekly" on none of 144: not encoded. "Less than weekly" holds the non-users of the last 12 months: 763 of the 887 answers of that frequency have an amount of 0 (use the amount, not the frequency, to tell a user from a non-user). The twelve criteria of a cannabis use disorder are in auto_questionnaire/dsm5_cannabis.yaml. The questions of the form on a drug treatment of the cannabis use disorder and on a hospitalisation for withdrawal (yes, number, age at the first) are not in the extraction (export request R120). By year, "never once" is delivered as yes (0 after a yes to the first question included) on 32% of the answers of 2014-16, 24% of 2017-19, 27% of 2020-22 and 37% from 2023 (in one centre from 12% to 33% between 2017-19 and 2023-26). The frequency of the last 12 months is "weekly" on 32% of the answers of 2014-16, 27% of 2017-19 and 22% since 2020 (12% to 36% in the three centres with 150 answers or more), and the longest abstinence (months, a question over the whole life) has a median of 13 to 16 to 2019 and 24 since (10 to 33 by centre); the family history is yes on 14% to 44% by centre: no known cause. Two longest abstinences above 2,000 months are out of range.

depressive_episodes.title: Major depressive episodes outside the psychotic episodes

sz.section: Trouble thymique (survenant en dehors des épisodes psychotiques)
sz.notes: Asked at the inclusion visit only (2,149 of the 2,353 visits answered: 1,016 yes, 966 no): has the patient had major depressive episodes (including post-psychotic depression), the age at the first one and their number over the whole life. "U" is a missing code (167 answers). The age and the number are shown after a yes: the number is 0 after a no (asked_if: 965 cells, where the form shows nothing; one cell is filled under a no and stays), and the age stays missing after a no (3 cells are filled under a no and stay as recorded). Under a yes the age is empty on 7% of the visits and the number on 10%. The number is capped. The options of the form run from 0 to 20 and ">20", and the export removes the sign, so ">20" is delivered as 20 (12 cells at 20, a lower bound) and "Ne sais pas" is 999 (215 numbers; the dictionary says so). The options of the age run from "<5" to ">89", read as 5 and 89 ("<5" cannot be told from 5); 999 is "does not know" there too (58 ages). The yes share of the first question differs by centre, from 34% to 74% (ten centres with 20 answers or more). The version block keeps the table to the inclusion visits: the follow-up visits do not hold the question. By year, the yes share of the first question is 45% of the visits to 2013, 55% in 2014-16, 51% in 2017-19, 49% in 2020-22 and 55% from 2023. Inside a centre it moves more (from 52% to 28% in one centre and from 31% to 74% in another, between the visits to 2013 and those of 2020-22), so the pooled share follows the mix and the practice of the centres: no known cause.

drug_use.title: Use of sedatives, heroin, cocaine, opiates and other products

sz.notes: One question opens five sections: sedatives, heroin, crack or cocaine, opiates and other products. For each, has the patient used it more than ten times in their life (the question says "plus de dix fois dans votre vie", as for alcohol and cannabis), how (smoked, sniffed, injected, oral, sublingual: one yes/no per way, several can be ticked; the list of the form has no "sniffed" for the sedatives, whose 118 answers are oral, smoked or sublingual), the amounts and frequencies in the periods of heaviest use over the whole life and in the last 12 months, the age at the first use, the longest abstinence, the family history and a craving score (the maximum in the last week). The opiates have no amounts; the other products have a name, amounts and frequencies only. The opening question (rad_add_4) is not in the dictionary: its label is read from the form. It is answered on 3,436 visits (481 yes), and the five sections are filled only after a yes (456 of the 481 visits for sedatives, heroin, opiates and other products, 459 for cocaine; none after a no). After a "no" the five "more than ten times" are delivered as 0 (asked_if). The same question also hides the boxes of use disorder of four of the substances in substance_v0.yaml and substance_fu.yaml. 77 of the 212 later answers (36%) of the patients who said yes at inclusion are no (sedatives 53 of 84, cocaine 23 of 88, opiates 4 of 25, heroin 2 of 14). Asked at inclusion and at yearly visits, used from 2015 and not from 2012: the opening question is answered on 9% of the inclusion visits of 2012, 18% of 2014, 47% of 2015 and 84% to 93% from 2016 (the same pattern as alcohol, alcohol_use.yaml). The questions about the whole life keep that meaning at follow-up on average only: the share of yes is the same at the two, but a third of the later answers of the patients who said yes at inclusion are no. The details are filled after a yes. 999 and 9999 mean "does not know" in an amount or a duration, 99 in an age. "Ne sais pas" is a missing code. The number of times per week is filled when the frequency is "1 to 7 times a week" (378 of 387 answers) and after "less than weekly" on none: not encoded. At 12 months "less than weekly" mostly means no use: the amount is 0 on 32 of 33 sedative answers, 27 of 33 heroin, 98 of 138 cocaine and 55 of 67 other products. Not asked, not no. The questions at the end of each section (age at the first use, longest abstinence, family history, craving) are shown only with two or more DSM-5 criteria, a count that is in another tab (the dsm5_ schemas of auto_questionnaire). Age at the first use, filled on 0 of 41 sedative visits with none or one criterion and on 82% of 60 with two or more; heroin 0 of 15 and 21 of 23; cocaine 0 of 94 and 83% of 98; opiates 0 of 18 and 91% of 34. An empty cell means "not asked"; it is not encoded. Amounts are tablets or capsules per day (sedatives), grams per day (heroin, cocaine) and standard units per day (other products). The sections are small: 126 patients-visits with sedatives, 55 with heroin, 254 with cocaine, 73 with opiates, 186 with another product. In the form the details of the other product are shown by a question that is not in the extraction (rad_add_autre4e2): the amount is filled on 71 of the 186 visits that say yes and the name on 179 (export request R116). The questions of the form on a drug treatment of the use disorder and on a hospitalisation for withdrawal (yes, number, age at the first) are not in the extraction for any of the five sections (export request R120). Ages are plausible: the first use is at 14 or later and none is above the patient's age. rad_add_heroin7a (24 inclusion and 14 follow-up answers, yes or no) is the question "a symptom of a use disorder over the whole life" for heroin, the counterpart of the boxes of substance_v0.yaml, which has no heroin box. It is not read (ignored.yaml; open question O21). The criteria of a use disorder are in the dsm5_* schemas of auto_questionnaire. One centre's step in the sedatives: the question "more than ten times" is yes on 12% to 13% of the answers of 2014 and 2015, 7% of 2016 and 2% to 4% from 2017. Before 2017 it comes mostly from one centre (37 yes on its 241 answers, 15%; 10 on the 296 answers of the other centres, 3%), and from 2017 it is 3% in that centre (17 of 580) as in the others (62 of 2,294): no known cause (the boxes of substance_v0.yaml show it too). Cocaine smoked (crack) is ticked on 20% of the cocaine sections of 2014-19, 30% of 2020-22 and 40% from 2023, and on 10% to 50% by centre (centres with 20 answers or more): no known cause. Two amounts of 99 grams of cocaine a day are out of range.

tea_coffee.title: Tea and coffee

sz.notes: Cups per day and frequency of tea and of coffee, over the whole life (in the periods of heaviest use, "périodes de consommation maximales" in the form) and in the last 12 months. 2,572 visits answer for tea and 2,665 for coffee. The form is asked at inclusion and at yearly visits, from 2015 and not from 2012: the tea questions are answered on 7% of the inclusion visits of 2012, 16% of 2014, 42% of 2015 and 71% to 79% of 2016 to 2018. There is no gate: a patient who does not drink tea or coffee answers 0 cups (0 on 41% of the 2,572 lifetime answers for tea and 19% of the 2,665 for coffee). The frequency "less than weekly" includes the non-consumers: 813 of the 1,246 tea answers of that frequency have 0 cups (361 of 548 for coffee); use the number of cups to tell a consumer from a non-consumer. The number of times per week is filled after "1 to 7 times a week" and, in the whole-life questions, on 6 of 1,079 tea answers and 3 of 1,980 coffee answers that do not say weekly: a shown_if would blank those cells, so there is none. The frequency category of the last 12 months (weekly, less than weekly) is not in the extraction, for tea and for coffee. The dictionary maps two form fields to the same name (SUDOSFRQ_theLY and SUDOSFRQ_cafeLY: the category and the number of times per week), and only the numbers 1 to 7 are exported (841 cells for tea, 1,965 for coffee); they are delivered as the times per week of the last 12 months (export request R118). 999 means "does not know". A few amounts are out of range (365 cups of coffee a day on 3 visits: a number per year). sudosnb_cafelt, the times per week for coffee, is not in the dictionary; it is filled with the frequency "1 to 7 times a week", as its tea counterpart is. The cups differ by centre: the median of tea over the whole life is 1 cup in five centres and 0 in the five others (means from 0.7 to 1.6), and the median of coffee in the last 12 months is 1 in three centres and 2 or 3 in the others; by year the means are stable (tea 1.2 to 1.5 over the whole life, coffee 2.2 to 2.7 in the last 12 months): centre habit or practice, no known cause.

care_changes.title: Changes in the non-drug care

sz.section: Modification de la prise en charge non médicamenteuse
sz.notes: Asked at inclusion and at follow-up (3,156 visits: 648 yes, 2,418 no, 90 "Ne sais pas"): did the non-drug care change, and for four approaches whether it started, ended, or both (the cell lists the boxes ticked: one yes/no for "started" and one for "ended"). "Ne sais pas" is a missing code. The last column is free text and never appears in the report. Time frame. The question has no period of its own. It sits under the heading "characteristics of the disorder over the last 12 months" of the inclusion form and of the yearly form, so a follow-up answer is a yearly update (BP D84, R14), not strictly the time since the last visit. Branching (decision D72). The four approaches are shown only after a yes to the first question (positions 0 of it in the field table). After a "no" they are blank on 2,418 of 2,418 visits and, as for every yes/no box after a no, they are 0 (asked_if): 19,344 cells (2,418 visits times 8 variables). The approaches are the boxes of one list, ticked one by one and never answered with "Non": where one is ticked (419 of the 648 yes visits) the empty ones are 0 too (box_list care_change_kinds; 2,250 cells), as the rater ticked what applied. These are sets of boxes, not Oui/Non radios, so the rule of the radios (R3) does not apply. 180 yes visits hold only the free text and 49 hold nothing: they stay missing. 3 visits that hold an approach under an empty first question stay as written (decision R2). 21,594 cells in all were missing and are 0. The 2019 step. The first question is answered on 38% of the visits up to 2017 (30% to 58% by year), 30% in 2018, 48% in the first half of 2019, 82% in the second half and 91% to 94% from 2020. Among the answered visits the share of yes falls from 38% (to 2017) and 27% (2018) to 14% (from the second half of 2019; 11% to 19% by year). Before mid-2019 an empty cell is "no change, or not shown". In the field table the first question depends on a parent, rad_tbpsychoan_modpec (and the drug counterpart rad_tbpsychoan_modpec_med), that has no row of its own and is not exported (request R132; question M67): the question is shown only after a yes to it, which we cannot see.

care_changes.description: Changes in the non-drug care (SZ): whether it changed and, for the cognitive behavioural approach, cognitive remediation, the psychodynamic approach and the family approach, whether it started or ended. Asked at inclusion and at follow-up.
care_changes.period: no period of its own; it sits under the heading 'over the last 12 months' (a yearly update)
flags: Before mid-2019 the first question is answered on 30% to 58% of the visits, and an empty cell is 'no change, or not shown'; from 2020 it is answered on more than 90%. Among the answers the share of yes falls from 38% to 14%.
The approaches are 0 after a 'no', and an approach left unticked beside a ticked one is 0.

medication_classes.title: Number of medications of each class in the list of the patient

sz.section: Nombre de traitements psychotropes présents AU MOMENT DE LA VISITE
sz.notes: Six counts that the export computes from the medication list: how many antipsychotics, antidepressants, anxiolytics, anticholinergic correctors, mood stabilisers and hypnotics it holds. What a count counts (decision D72; this answers the former open question O25). It is the number of distinct product NAMES, as typed in the list, that match a fixed list of name patterns (face_sz_11_traitements.sql: COUNT(DISTINCT name) with ILIKE patterns, 29 for the antipsychotics, 25 for the antidepressants, 13 for the anxiolytics, 4 for the anticholinergic correctors, 10 for the mood stabilisers and 9 for the hypnotics). It is not a count of molecules, nor of the treatments of a visit: two spellings of one product count twice, and a product that no pattern names counts for nothing. The six counts are reproduced from the names of the list for 1,975 of 1,975 patients. What the patterns miss and mix. 480 of the 10,188 rows of the seven psychotropic groups of facedata/medications.csv (356 patients) fall in no class (168 benzodiazepines, 126 second-generation and 34 first-generation antipsychotics, 78 anticonvulsants, 61 antidepressants, 13 other anxiolytics or hypnotics). The anxiolytic count is 0 for 112 of the 696 patients who have a benzodiazepine in the list, and the hypnotic count is 0 for 52 of the 271 patients who have another anxiolytic or hypnotic. The antipsychotic count exceeds the number of distinct molecules of the two antipsychotic groups for 588 of the 1,961 patients who have one (the same molecule under several names). The classes are not the groups of the table: the anxiolytics are 812 benzodiazepine rows and 82 rows of other anxiolytics, the hypnotics 269 rows of other anxiolytics or hypnotics and 54 benzodiazepines, the anticholinergics 438 of the 487 rows of other nervous system drugs, the mood stabilisers 166 lithium rows and 451 of the 529 anticonvulsant rows. One value per patient, not per visit (decision D19 in PROGRESS.md). The dictionary calls them the treatments "at the time of the visit", but each count is the same on every row of a patient, like the lists: it counts the whole list, not the visit. What a patient takes at a visit is in medications_at_visit (medications.yaml). The counts are empty for the 378 patients who have no list. SZ has no question on the classes taken in the whole life: the table medicament_lifetime of the application holds the columns rad_psylifetime_* (as in BP), but no form of SZ shows them. The six yes/no columns of the same classes (psychotic, depress, anxiolyt, antichol, thymoreg, hypnot) are ignored: each is 1 where the count is above 0, on every row that has a list, and 0 on the rows that have none, where nothing is known.

medication_classes.description: Six counts that the export computes from the medication list of the patient (SZ), one value per patient in the table patients: antipsychotics, antidepressants, anxiolytics, anticholinergic correctors, mood stabilisers and hypnotics.
medication_classes.period: the whole medication list of the patient, not a visit
flags: It is not a count of molecules, nor of the treatments of a visit: two spellings of one product count twice, and a product that no pattern names counts for nothing (the anxiolytic count is 0 for 112 of the 696 patients with a benzodiazepine in the list).

The dictionary of the extraction calls them the treatments 'at the time of the visit', but each count is the same on every visit of a patient. What a patient takes at a visit is in medications_at_visit.
The counts are empty for the patients who have no list.

treatment_help.title: Help with taking the treatment

sz.notes: Who helps the patient take the treatment: nobody ("Autonome"), the family, the outpatient clinic or the hospital, a nurse at home. Several boxes can be ticked, so each is one yes/no (4,222 of the 4,941 inclusion and follow-up visits). "Autonome" is ticked on 2,977 visits and with another help on 166 of them, so the variable is treatment_help_autonomous (it was named treatment_help_alone: the values are the same). The question has no period: it is the state at the visit, asked at inclusion (2,009 answers) and at every yearly visit (2,213). The frequency is asked when the clinic or the hospital helps (the third box of the list in the field table): it is filled on 511 of the 523 visits where that box is ticked, and on 6 visits where it is not (5 of them with the whole question empty, all from one centre, 2011 to 2015): kept as recorded (decision R2, no shown_if).

treatment_help.description: Who helps the patient take the treatment (SZ): autonomous, the family, the outpatient clinic or the hospital, a nurse at home (several boxes can be ticked), and how often the clinic or the hospital helps. Asked at inclusion and at every yearly visit.
flags: 'Autonomous' can be ticked together with another help.

alimentaire.title: Food frequency questionnaire

dr.notes: Food frequency questionnaire: 23 questions (question 9 has two parts) on how much of each food the patient takes per day, per week or per month. Not in BP. The SZ application has the same form (autoq_alimentaire, 23 questions), but the SZ extraction does not carry it (request R152). Filled at inclusion and at the visits of 1, 2 and 4 years: 868 visits, 74% to 86% of the inclusions in every period. The break of 2018 does not touch it: the form (218) is on the lists of the simplified visit (visite.SVUPDES = 1, config/globale2.php, DESTVISIMP; PROGRESS.md D55). Each answer is a class of quantity, numbered from 0. The classes are those of the dictionary and differ from one question to the other (for bread: 0 none, 1 for 30 g, up to 7 for 150 g or more; for wine: glasses, then bottles); the number of classes gives the range of each variable. The classes are delivered as stored: they are not quantities, and no score is computed. No cell is outside its classes.

alimentaire.description: Food frequency questionnaire. Twenty-three questions (question 9 has two parts) on how much of each food the patient takes per day, per week or per month. Each answer is a class of quantity numbered from 0. No score.
flags: The classes are not quantities and differ between questions: the number of classes gives the range of each variable. No score is computed.
No reference is given in the project documents.
Not in BP. The SZ application has the same form but the SZ extraction does not carry it.

bfi.title: Big Five Inventory, French version (BFI-Fr)

dr.notes: Big Five Inventory, French version: 45 statements, each 1 (strongly disagree) to 5 (strongly agree). Not in BP or SZ. Filled at inclusion and at the visits of 2 and 4 years: 551 visits. Items: read back to the answer as asked. The published key reverses 17 statements, those that describe the opposite pole of their dimension: 2, 6, 8, 9, 12, 18, 21, 23, 24, 27, 31, 34, 35, 37, 41, 43 and 45. This form (214) stores these 17 already reversed, and its script adds every item as stored: on the values as stored every item rises with the other items of its dimension (Cronbach's alpha 0.69 to 0.83 with no item reversed). They are read back to the answer as asked (6 - value, written as codes), so that every item is 1 strongly disagree to 5 strongly agree, and the key is in the scores (reverse), as for the other scales that are stored as asked. The older form 135, before 214, keyed item 29 from 5 to 1 where form 214 keys it 1 to 5 (found in two centres, on visits dated 2014 or earlier); which visits used it is not known, so item 29 is delivered as stored (A82, M75). Scores. Five means of items (1 to 5): extraversion (8 items), agreeableness (10), conscientiousness (9), neuroticism (8) and openness (10). The stored means (bfi_extr, bfi_agre, bfi_cons, bfi_emo, bfi_ouve) are written with two decimals and equal ours on every visit for extraversion, agreeableness and openness (544 or 545 visits). Conscientiousness and neuroticism are swapped on 16 visits. On 16 visits of 16 patients, from 2014 to 2018, in four centres, the stored conscientiousness is the mean of the neuroticism items, and the stored neuroticism is the mean of the conscientiousness items, cut after two decimals instead of rounded. On the 507 other visits the two stored values equal ours. Ours are delivered; the 32 values carry score_mismatch. Open question O19. Direction. Neuroticism rises with depression (r = 0.49 with the QIDS); the four other dimensions fall. The break of 2018 (open question O1, answered by the application). 95% and 88% of the inclusion visits of 2012 to 2014 and of 2015 to 2017 hold the scale, 44% to 51% in 2018 to 2020, 2021 to 2022 and 2023 to 2026. The BFI (form 214) is one of the forms that the simplified visit leaves out (visite.SVUPDES = 1, config/globale2.php, DESTVISIMP; PROGRESS.md D55): an empty scale after 2018 is "not asked" on a simplified visit, not "no". The extraction does not say which visits were simplified (request R127 and R155: the svupdes column; question M69).

bfi.description: Big Five Inventory, French version. Forty-five statements, each rated by the patient from 1 (strongly disagree) to 5 (strongly agree). Five dimensions of personality, each the mean of its items.
bfi.reference: Plaisant O, Courtois R, Réveillère C, Mendelsohn GA, John OP. Validation par analyse factorielle du Big Five Inventory français (BFI-Fr). Ann Méd Psychol 2010;168:97-106
bfi.reference_confidence: 45 items confirmed (extracted: Lignier 2016, abstract); citation confirmed (search result + em-consulte record)
flags: The key reverses 17 statements: the 16 of the English 44-item form and item 45. The French list of reversed items and the dimension of the 45th item are 'To verify' in the literature notes.
The form stores the 17 statements already reversed; they are read back to the answer as asked.
An older form keyed item 29 the other way on some visits of 2014 or earlier. Which visits is not known, so item 29 is delivered as stored.
On 16 visits the stored conscientiousness and neuroticism are swapped. The recomputed scores are delivered.
An empty scale after 2018 can be 'not asked' (simplified visit).

detc_cage.title: DETC-CAGE cannabis

dr.notes: DETC-CAGE for cannabis: four yes/no questions (need to cut down, remarks of the family, feeling of smoking too much, cannabis in the morning). Not in BP or SZ. Filled on 100 visits of 95 patients, nearly all inclusions: 45% of the inclusions of 2012 to 2014, 19% in 2015 to 2017, 2% to 5% since. The number of yes (0 to 4) is computed; the extraction stores none. The median is 0: most of the patients who fill it answer no four times. The fall (45%, 19%, then 2% to 5%) follows a change of form, not of the patients. The nurse's record (form 112) shows the four items only after a yes to "Consommez-vous du cannabis ?" (DCCAN, instrument cannabis of the SUBSTANCES tab). 79 of the 100 visits that hold the items have this question empty: 78 are dated 2012 to 2015 and one 2016, and 78 of the 79 have a total of 0. The 21 others are under a yes (21 of the 24 yes) and none is under a no (0 of 558). The forms 103 and 119, other versions of the nurse's record, hold the four items and no opening question: if they are the source of the 79 (question O31), the total of 2012 to 2015 covers everybody who filled that form, and a 0 is mostly a patient who does not use cannabis, whereas the total since 2016 covers only the patients who use it now. The two are not comparable. A value under an empty question is kept as recorded (R2), not turned into missing. Whether the scale is still part of the protocol is asked in O21.

detc_cage.description: DETC-CAGE for cannabis. Four yes/no questions answered by the patient (need to cut down, remarks of the family, feeling of smoking too much, cannabis in the morning).
detc_cage.period: lifetime (the questions ask whether it 'ever' happened)
flags: The totals of 2012 to 2015 and those from 2016 are not comparable. Until 2015 everybody who filled the form answered, and a 0 is mostly a patient who does not use cannabis; from 2016 the items are shown only after a yes to the question on cannabis use.
No reference and no cut-off are given in the project documents, and the literature notes have no section on this instrument.
Filled on 100 visits only. Whether the scale is still part of the protocol is an open question.

leaps.title: Lam Employment Absence and Productivity Scale (LEAPS)

dr.notes: Lam Employment Absence and Productivity Scale. Not in BP or SZ. Filled at inclusion and at the visits of 1, 2 and 4 years: 762 visits (58% of the inclusions of 2012 to 2014, 64% to 69% since). The break of 2018 does not touch it. The form starts with the work: its kind (free text), the hours scheduled and the hours missed over the last two weeks, and a box "not working at present" (sick leave, disability, retirement). The box is ticked on 584 of the 754 visits where it is answered. The seven items are asked only of the patients who work: how often, at work over the last two weeks, each problem was felt, from 0 (none of the time) to 4 (all the time). They are filled on 168 visits, the seven together, and never when the box is ticked. The gate is the box: the form shows the seven items when the box is 0 (not ticked; script of the form, formulaires.js, the field LEAPS3BIS), and they are delivered only then (shown_if). All 168 visits with the items are under a 0, so no cell is hidden: the line documents the gate. Total. The sum of the seven items (0 to 28, higher is more impairment at work). The stored total (leaps_) equals it on the 167 visits where it exists. It rises with depression (r = 0.72 with the QIDS). One number of scheduled hours is above 200 (out_of_range). 10 cells of the kind of work hold a word read as no answer (missing_code). The hours missed are above the hours scheduled on 59 of the 594 visits that hold both: kept as typed.

leaps.description: Lam Employment Absence and Productivity Scale. The patient gives the kind of work, the hours scheduled and missed over the last two weeks, and, if working, rates seven problems at work from 0 (none of the time) to 4 (all the time).
leaps.reference: Lam RW, Michalak EE, Yatham LN. BMC Psychiatry 2009;9:78
flags: The seven items and the total exist only for the patients who work (168 visits): the total is missing, not 0, for the others.

The literature notes describe a published scale of 10 items; the total of the first 7 items (0 to 28) and its severity bands are 'To verify'. A change of 3 points is the minimal important difference (Sachdeva 2026, abstract).
The hours missed are above the hours scheduled on some visits and are kept as typed.

paykel.title: Paykel list of life events (64 events, past 12 months, interviewer-rated)

dr.section: LISTE PAYKEL Liste de 61 evènements de vie
dr.notes: Paykel list of life events (form 166). Not in BP or SZ. Interview of the last 12 months: the form asks, for each event, whether it happened in the year before the visit (a), the month it started (b), how independent of the illness it was (c, 1 almost entirely independent to 5 almost entirely dependent) and its objective negative impact (d, 1 severe to 5 none); the two ratings are the interviewer's (the form carries the instructions of the rater). Each visit asks about the year before it, so the answers of two visits do not add up; whether the interval since the previous visit was meant at the visits of 2 and 4 years is a question for the data managers (O34, M78). Filled at inclusion and at the visits of 1, 2 and 4 years: 581 visits. 81% and 76% of the inclusions of 2012 to 2017 hold it, 19% to 34% since: the form is in none of the lists of the simplified visit (the break of 2018, D55, open question O1). 64 events, not 61. The dictionary announces 61 events and lists the columns of events 10 to 64; the extraction also holds events 1 to 9. The wording is in the form, not in the dictionary: the variable names stay numbered and each label gives a short English version of the title (63 numbered titles, and a 64th for any other event of primary importance that fits no earlier category). Events 47 and 48 have the same title, a marriage of a child, with and without consent; events 31 to 33 are the three moves of house (the form prints the three places and an instruction on moves, no heading). "Happened" is stored 1 for yes and 2 for no; it is delivered 1 and 0. The three details are filled only after a yes: of the 976 events answered yes, 898 have a month, 835 an independence and 846 an impact. Month of onset. Typed on two digits and printed "from 01 to 12". Of the 898 months, 894 are from 1 to 12: they peak at 1, 6 and 12 (135, 114 and 89), as round numbers of months before the visit would and calendar months would not. Whether the month is a calendar month or a number of months before the visit is not told (O34, M78). The four others (13, 17, 20 and one above 24) are out of the range. Out of the scale. The independence holds 0 on 13 cells and the impact on 18, 11 other cells hold a value above 5, and four months are above 12: 46 cells, out_of_range, not delivered. Nothing says what 0 means here. The number of events answered yes (paykel_events, 0 to 64) needs the 64 answers: 530 visits, median 1.

paykel.description: Paykel list of life events. In an interview, the patient is asked for each of 64 events whether it happened in the 12 months before the visit and the month it started; the interviewer rates how independent of the illness it was and its negative impact.
flags: No reference is given: the schema notes cite none, and section 27 of the literature notes describes the Paykel Suicide Scale, which is another instrument.
The count mixes events of every kind, wanted ones included (a marriage, a financial improvement), hence the neutral polarity.
Each visit asks about the year before it, so the answers of two visits do not add up. Whether the visits of 2 and 4 years meant the interval since the previous visit is an open question.
The month, the independence and the impact are filled only after a yes. Values out of the scale (0, above 5, a month above 12) are not delivered.
An empty list since 2018 can be 'not asked' (simplified visit).

pcl_s.title: PTSD Checklist (PCL-S)

dr.notes: PTSD Checklist, specific version (PCL-S, form 216): seventeen symptoms, each 1 (not at all) to 5 (very often), about "this stressful episode". Not in BP or SZ. It is another form than the list of events (traumatic_events.yaml, form 208), under the same section header of the dictionary, and it does not say which event of the list the patient has in mind: on 64 of the 127 visits no event of the list is answered yes. The form prints no time frame (the published PCL-S asks about the past month: ISTSS page on the PCL for DSM-IV; whether the French PCLS of Yao 2003 prints it was not settled by the literature check of 2026-11-21). Filled on 127 visits of 111 patients, at inclusion and at the visits of 2 and 4 years (25% of the inclusions of 2012 to 2014, 7% since 2024); the form is in none of the lists of the simplified visit (D55). The labels give the three clusters of the published checklist: re-experiencing (items 1 to 5), avoidance and numbing (6 to 12) and hyperarousal (13 to 17). Total. The sum of the seventeen items (17 to 85). The stored total (ptsd_) equals it on the 127 visits. Every item rises with the others.

pcl_s.description: PTSD Checklist, specific version. Seventeen symptoms, each rated by the patient from 1 (not at all) to 5 (very often), about a stressful episode. The checklist does not say which event the patient has in mind.
pcl_s.reference: Weathers FW, Litz BT, Herman DS, Huska JA, Keane TM. The PTSD Checklist: reliability, validity and diagnostic utility. ISTSS annual meeting, San Antonio, 1993 (conference paper)
pcl_s.period: none printed on the form (the published PCL-S asks about the past month)
flags: The labels give the three clusters of the published checklist (re-experiencing items 1 to 5, avoidance and numbing 6 to 12, hyperarousal 13 to 17). No cluster score is delivered.
The form labels the answer 5 'very often'; the published anchor is 'extremely'.
Filled on 127 visits only. On half of them no event of the list of traumatic events is answered yes.
Not to be confused with the PCL-5 (DSM-5, 20 items).

rosenberg.title: Rosenberg self-esteem scale

dr.notes: Rosenberg self-esteem scale (form 134): ten items with four answers (1 strongly disagree to 4 strongly agree, as asked), about how the patient sees himself in general. Not in BP or SZ. Filled at inclusion and at every follow-up visit: 947 visits. Items: stored as points, read back to the answer as asked. Five items of the scale are worded negatively (3, 5, 8, 9 and 10) and are reversed in the published key. The form of this cohort stores them already reversed: its options for these five items are keyed 1 (strongly agree) to 4 (strongly disagree), so that every item is stored as points, 1 low self-esteem and 4 high. Here every item rises with every other one (the 45 correlations between two items are between 0.21 and 0.77). The five items are read back to the answer as asked (codes 1 to 4, 2 to 3, 3 to 2, 4 to 1), as for the CTQ and the BIS-10, so that rosenb03 to rosenb10 mean the same as the other items of the scale; the total reverses the same five items and does not change. Total. The sum of the ten items after the reversal of the five negative ones (10 to 40, higher is a better self-esteem). The stored total (rosenb) equals it on the 946 visits where the ten items are filled. It falls when depression rises (r = -0.70 with the QIDS). The break of 2018 (open question O1, answered by D55). 95% and 83% of the inclusion visits of 2012 to 2014 and of 2015 to 2017 hold the scale, 40% to 50% in the three periods since 2018. The form (134) is in none of the lists of the simplified visit (its display rule is commented out in the application): an empty scale since 2018 is "not asked" on a simplified visit, not "no", and it is missing data here, never 0. The extraction has no flag that tells a simplified visit from a full one with an empty scale (R127, R139, R155).

rosenberg.description: Rosenberg self-esteem scale. Ten items on how the patient sees himself in general, each from 1 (strongly disagree) to 4 (strongly agree).
rosenberg.reference: Rosenberg 1965 (the literature notes give no full citation)
flags: No official cut-off (literature notes).
The form stores the five negative items already reversed; they are read back to the answer as asked.
The reversed items here are 3, 5, 8, 9 and 10. The literature notes list 2, 5, 6, 8, 9 for the English order and warn that the French item order may differ.
An empty scale since 2018 can be 'not asked' (simplified visit). It is missing, never 0.

shaps.title: Snaith-Hamilton Pleasure Scale (SHAPS, these last days)

dr.notes: Snaith-Hamilton Pleasure Scale (form 224): fourteen situations that usually give pleasure, about "these last days", each answered on four levels, stored 0 (strongly disagree) to 3 (strongly agree). Not in BP or SZ, and not in the dictionary. In the extraction from 2015 (42% of the inclusions of 2015 to 2017, about 80% since) and at every follow-up visit: 948 visits. The form is on the four lists of the simplified visit, so the break of 2018 does not touch it. Score: the stored one is wrong; ours is delivered. The published score gives one point for each item answered "disagree" or "strongly disagree" (0 to 14, higher is more anhedonia). The fourteen stored items all point the same way: each falls when the MADRS rises (r = -0.35 to -0.55), so a low value is the answer of anhedonia for every item. The stored score (shaps_) counts "disagree" on nine items and "agree" on the five others (2, 4, 5, 7 and 9): this rule gives the stored value on each of the 943 visits where the fourteen items are filled. The cause is the export, not the EMR: the score definition of the export (nucleus shaps.yaml, line 34) reverses items 2, 4, 5, 7 and 9 before the count, whereas the script of the form (224_score.js, lines 31 to 36) counts the answers 0 and 1 as one point on all fourteen items, as ours does. Counting "disagree" on the fourteen items gives a score that follows depression better (r = 0.61 with the MADRS against 0.42 for the stored one; median 5 against 7). The score is written in the schema as a sum of points (no function of custom.py); the twin shaps_total_as_stored adds the nine items counted on "disagree" and the five items counted on "agree" and reproduces the rule of the export, to check the stored value, and is not delivered. Open question O18 (the reversal of the export is the cause; its correction is requested in R147).

shaps.description: Snaith-Hamilton Pleasure Scale. Fourteen situations that usually give pleasure, rated by the patient about these last days on four levels, stored 0 (strongly disagree) to 3 (strongly agree).
shaps.reference: Snaith RP, Hamilton M, Morley S, et al. Br J Psychiatry 1995;167:99-103 (PMID 7551619)
flags: The items and the score run in opposite directions: a high item is pleasure, a high score is anhedonia.
The stored score is wrong (the export reverses five items before the count) and is not delivered.
In the extraction from 2015.

spin.title: Social Phobia Inventory (SPIN, last weeks)

dr.notes: Social Phobia Inventory (form 197): seventeen items, each 0 (not at all) to 4 (extremely), about how much the problems "bothered you during the last weeks" (the form's own words; the published SPIN says the past week). Not in BP or SZ, and not in the dictionary. Filled on 147 visits, most of them inclusions (28% of the inclusions of 2012 to 2014, 10% from 2018, 3% since 2024): it is filled by few patients and less and less. The form is in none of the lists of the simplified visit (D55). Gate. The application offers the form by the type of the visit only, the initial visit (config/global.php, line 396), not by a diagnosis such as a social phobia in the MINI; yet 46 of the 147 SPIN visits are follow-up visits (13 at 6 months, 8 at 18 months, 12 at 1 year, 13 at 2 years). Nothing here tells why; the visits are delivered as they are (question M74 for the data managers). Total. The sum of the seventeen items (0 to 68, higher is more social anxiety). The stored total (spin_) equals it on the 147 visits. Every item rises with the others.

spin.description: Social Phobia Inventory. Seventeen items, each rated by the patient from 0 (not at all) to 4 (extremely), on how much the problems bothered the patient during the last weeks.
spin.reference: Connor KM, Davidson JR, Churchill LE, Sherwood A, Foa E, Weisler RH. Psychometric properties of the Social Phobia Inventory (SPIN). Br J Psychiatry 2000;176:379-386
spin.period: the last weeks (the form's own words; the published SPIN says the past week)
flags: Filled on 147 visits only, by few patients and less and less. Why a third of them are follow-up visits is an open question.
The fear, avoidance and physiological sub-scales are 'To verify' in the literature notes and are not delivered. No French version was found.

traumatic_events.title: List of traumatic life events

dr.notes: List of seventeen traumatic life events (form 208): the events of the Life Events Checklist, 16 events and a seventeenth, "another very stressful event", with a free text. Not in BP or SZ. The dictionary puts this form and the PCL-S (pcl_s.yaml, form 216) under one section header; they are two forms of the EMR, and the PCL-S does not say which event of the list its items are about. For each event: whether it happened (1 yes, 0 no), the age at the event and whether it had a negative impact (a box, 1 ticked). The wording is in the form, not in the dictionary: the variable names stay numbered and each label gives a short English version of the event. Event 15, "sudden, unexpected death of a close person", differs from the published checklist item (a sudden accidental death): to verify against the French version used. Period. The form prints none; the published checklist asks about the whole life and the inclusion answers are read so. At follow-up the answers are not cumulative: of the events answered yes at inclusion, 21%, 17% and 14% are answered yes again at the visits of 1, 2 and 4 years (105, 61 and 27 patients with both forms complete), and new events appear (29, 21 and 12). Whether the follow-up form asks about the time since the previous visit is a question for the data managers (O34, M78). Filled at inclusion and at the visits of 1, 2 and 4 years: the seventeen questions are answered on 544 visits (30% of the inclusions of 2012 to 2014, 71% in 2015 to 2017, 29% to 43% since: the form is in none of the lists of the simplified visit, D55). Of the 624 events answered yes, 575 have an age, 417 an impact of 1 and 207 an impact of 0. The impact is 0 wherever the form was opened. The form writes 0 in the impact of every event that is not answered yes: 10,137 cells. On the rows where the event is answered no, this 0 says the same as the answer. But on 89 visits the seventeen impacts hold 0 and no event is answered: there the 0 is not an answer. These 1,513 cells, and 23 cells of an event left empty on other visits, are delivered and flagged derived_doubt (the impact is declared derived_from its event). The zeros are left as the form wrote them. Count the visits of this form with the events (trau01 to trau17), not with the impacts. The number of events answered yes (trauma_events, 0 to 17) needs the seventeen answers: 533 visits.

bilan_urinaire.title: Urine drug screen

dr.notes: A urine drug screen: the question "test done" is answered on 807 visits, 228 yes, then four results, 1 for positive and 0 for negative: cannabis (3 positive of 228), benzodiazepines (42 of 227), psychostimulants (5 of 226) and opiates (6 of 227). The coding is plausible (benzodiazepines are positive on 19% of the results, cannabis on 1%). The test is done in practice in a few centres: four give 212 of the 228 yes answers (93%). The columns of the psychostimulants and of the opiates hold a number that is not 0 or 1 on 20 and 22 visits, all of one centre, up to 2022 (the opiates: numbers of 4.2 to 6.9, nearly all with decimals): it looks like another urine result typed in these fields. These cells are removed: 31 are unparsed (27 numbers with decimals and 4 written "<" a number: none is a whole answer) and 11 are out_of_range (open question O12 in PROGRESS.md). This schema belongs to the pool biology (implausible_visits: 3, implausible_pool: biology; see the blood-count schema): a visit with three or more impossible values over the eleven laboratory schemas of DR loses all its values and gets visit_removed. The pool removes 35 visits in all (1,403 cells); this schema loses 55 answers on 26 visits: 48 on 23 visits of the block, whose 0 and 1 answers look like results and would be delivered (26 of the 83 positive results among them), and 7 on 3 other visits. The odd cells above count in the pool only through their out_of_range values (the decimals are counted as unparsed, which the rule does not count). A section of the TRD dictionary only.

vitamines_cortisol.title: Vitamin B12, folates and morning cortisol

dr.notes: Vitamin B12, folates and morning cortisol, on 1,059, 1,055 and 1,017 visits. For each the form has a choice of unit, exported as a code. Vitamin B12, delivered in pmol/L: code 2 (pg/mL, 408 results) and code 3 (ng/L, 295) are the same scale, 685 results converted; code 4 is pmol/L (323). Code 5, "mmol/L" (6 results, median 275, that of code 4, 271), is read as pmol/L, as the "mmol/L" codes of folates, cortisol and vitamin D are read as the molar unit of their scale (5 delivered, 1 impossible). Code 1, "pg/L" (27 results), has a median of 272, equal to code 4; read as pg/mL it would be 201. It fits both scales, so 22 results have no unit (unit_unknown) and 5 are impossible; which unit is meant is open (O10 in PROGRESS.md), with low confidence either way. 24 values are impossible, 21 of them on the shifted visits (below). Folates, delivered in nmol/L: code 2 is ng/mL (521 results), and code 1, "ng/L" (77), is read as ng/mL too (a folate level of 6 ng/L does not exist; its median, 6.5, is that of code 2, 6.2): 580 results converted. Code 3 is nmol/L (419) and code 4, "mmol/L" (17), is read as nmol/L (median 12.7 against 13.8). 16 results of the shifted visits have no usable code (unit_unknown) and 28 values are impossible. Cortisol, delivered in nmol/L: code 1 nmol/L (804, median 392), code 4 "mmol/L" read as nmol/L (32, median 363), code 3 ng/mL (51, x2.759) and code 5 µg/dL (67, x27.59): the converted medians, 352 and 356, are close to that of code 1, which confirms both factors. Code 2, "nmol/dL" (42 results, x10), fits neither scale: 28 are between 5 and 30 (the size of µg/dL: x10 gives a median of 165 and x27.59 gives 456, against 392) and 14 are 149 or more (the size of nmol/L or ng/mL, median 331); for the 42 together x10 gives 192 and x27.59 gives 528. They are left as the label says (29 converted, 1 read by its size, 12 impossible): note only. The dictionary labels the cortisol unit "Unité des folates", a copy of the folates label. 143 results are converted, 15 are read by their size (unit_inferred: 13 have a number in place of the code, on the shifted visits, and 2 do not fit their label) and 27 values are impossible, 8 of them on the shifted visits. Shifted visits. A number in place of the unit code marks 23 of the 30 visits of one centre, up to 2022, whose block of results is shifted (see the blood-count schema): the unit field holds a number on 22 visits for cortisol, 21 for folates and 9 for vitamin D, and the values beside it (median 1.2 for cortisol, 1.1 for B12, 3.4 for folates) are those of another analyte. The impossible values are removed by the ranges, but 11 cortisol and 5 folate values of these visits fall in the plausible range once read by their size and would be delivered. This schema belongs to the pool biology (implausible_visits: 3, implausible_pool: biology; see the blood-count schema): a visit with three or more impossible values over the eleven laboratory schemas of DR loses all its values and gets visit_removed. The pool removes 35 visits in all (1,403 cells), among them all 30 visits of the block; this schema loses 29 cells on 17 visits: the 11 cortisol and 5 folate values of the block, and 4 B12, 4 cortisol and 5 folate values on 5 other visits. Values are winsorised at the 1st and 99th percentiles: the tails become the cut values (B12 98 and 653 pmol/L, folates 3.9 and 56.7 nmol/L, cortisol 63 and 782 nmol/L; 19, 19 and 20 cells), so a clinical tail turns into the cut value, and the hard ranges (B12 50 to 1,500, folates 2 to 100, cortisol 30 to 1,500) remove the impossible values. Analytes that FACE BP and FACE SZ do not have.

vitamines_cortisol.description: Vitamin B12 (pmol/L), folates (nmol/L) and morning cortisol (nmol/L) from the blood sample of the visit (DR).
flags: The form exports a unit code for each analyte, and some codes name a unit that the values do not fit: they are read as the unit of their scale. The 'pg/L' code of the vitamin B12 fits two scales, so 22 results have no unit (unit_unknown, missing).

By default each number is clipped at its 1st and 99th percentiles (winsorising), so a clinical tail becomes the cut value; only the hard range removes impossible values. Load with winsorise=False to keep the tails.
BP and DR: a visit with three or more impossible values over the laboratory schemas loses all its laboratory values (visit_removed).

episode_described.title: One depressive episode described at inclusion

dr.notes: One episode described at the inclusion visit: its number, its length, and whether it was treated, resistant, hospitalised, with psychotic or mixed features, seasonal, followed by a full remission. 221 inclusion visits (220 with the number of the episode): 42% to 59% of the inclusion visits of each year from 2012 to 2017 (45% in all, 122 of 271) and 18% to 37% of those of 2018 to 2026 (27%, 98 of 363). Not in BP or SZ. No rename: the table is headed "Episodes" in form 116, not "depressive", and its questions (resistant, recurrence under treatment, switch under an antidepressant) are those of a depressive episode; which episode a row describes is not stated (low confidence, the name stays). One row per visit reaches the extraction, although the form is a table with an add-row button and no limit (episode numbers 1 to 20: 1 on 102 visits, 2 on 55, 3 on 36, 4 on 14). The export keeps one arbitrary row per visit (face_dr_10 lines 5-7: select distinct on (usubjid, visitnum) with no ORDER BY): the number typed on the row kept is 1 on only 102 of 220 rows, so the pick is not the first episode. The other episodes of the form are lost to this extraction, not left out by the raters (the table of the application has a row id, EPISODE, that the clean model keeps: request R142, all rows). Answers O26(1). The counts of episodes of mood_history_v0 include the current episode (a single-episode course has a count of 1 on 58 of 70 visits, a recurrent course 2 or more on 256 of 270). The number of the episode described is above the total counted (depressive, hypomanic, manic and mixed) on 8 of 213 visits, and the episode is ticked resistant with a resistant count of 0 on 4 of 117 visits that have the count (123 resistant episodes in all). 2 is "DM", missing data (29 cells).

mood_course_fu.title: Mood episodes since the last visit (follow-up form)

dr.notes: The mood episodes since the last visit, at the follow-up visits: 836 visits (88% to 97% of the visits of each kind: 91% at 6 months, 89% at 12, 93% at 18, 88% at 24, 97% at 48). The section of the patient-state form (form 183) is headed "DEPUIS DERNIERE VISITE": the counts say since the last visit, with no other period. The window is not the same for every visit: the median gap to the previous visit is 190 days (quartiles 177 and 231) and 744 days at the 4-year visit, which often follows a 2-year one. The dictionary lists the visits of three of these questions (the manic psychotic yes/no, the induced yes/no and the suicide attempts) as 6 months and 1 year only; they are filled at the later follow-up visits too (18 months to 5 years). Names. The counts that BP's DSM-IV follow-up form also asks (depressive, depressive with psychotic features, hypomanic, manic with psychotic features, mixed) carry BP's names (dsm4_fu_n_mde, dsm4_fu_n_mde_psychotic, dsm4_fu_n_hypomania, dsm4_fu_n_mania_psychotic, dsm4_fu_n_mixed): the same question in other raw columns (evnum_*, BP reads evnum_*_spv). BP's hard limit of these counts is 20 and so is this one (largest typed here: 8 depressive, 3 hypomanic). The counts that BP does not have keep their name: the resistant episodes, the induced episodes with their yes/no, the yes/no for a manic episode with psychotic features, and the suicide attempts (the ETAT_SUI_NB field of the form, not BP's attempt question: D49). BP's follow-up gate "at least one episode since the last visit" and the total number of episodes do not exist in the DR form. Two forms in the same columns. The inclusion visit asks about the whole life; the follow-up visits use the same columns for the time since the last visit. The two are never delivered in one column: visit_form says which form a visit uses (inclusion for the screening and inclusion visits, follow_up for the others), and each form has its own schema and its own variables. Forms 116 and 183 never meet on one visit, though they share the evnum_* columns (mood_history_v0.yaml). A major depressive episode since the last visit on 327 of 809 visits, a resistant one on 252 of 796, a suicide attempt on 44 of 796. A resistant count above the depressive count on 13 of 795 visits, a count of episodes with psychotic features above the depressive count on 1: both are delivered as typed and flagged check_failed (not_above). Gates. The induced episode is a yes/no (mhoccur_eind) and a count after a yes: the form shows the count only after a yes and leaves it blank after a no (asked_if: 821 cells missing become 0; 9 yes answers hold the count 1, 2 no answers hold a typed 0, 2 "not known" stay missing). The manic psychotic yes/no is NOT a gate for its count: the form shows the yes/no only when the hypomanic count is above 0 (formulaires.js line 4617 reads ETAT_EPI_HYPOMAN where there is no manic count in this form: a defect; line 4618 does the same for the mixed psychotic question). Only 17 yes/no cells are filled (16 "no", 1 "not known"; 14 of them under a hypomanic count above 0, 3 under 0) while the always-shown count is filled on 791 visits (2 above 0): the count is the usable answer, its yes/no stays as typed and the 774 blanks of the yes/no beside a count are not "no". Not in the extraction. Form 183 also asks, since the last visit, the mixed episodes with psychotic features (yes/no ETAT_EPI_MIXTE_PSYCHO and its count; the label says "maniaque" at line 50 of 183.php), the complete and the incomplete remission between the episodes and the seasonal pattern. The table holds them, the clean model of the form (edepression_hetero_etatp.sql) and the export do not select them (request R142): evnum_emixt_psy and the remission and seasonal columns of this extraction come from form 116 only. Four columns that the dictionary does not list (etat_epi_maj, fetat_epi_edm, etat_epi_depress, etat_sui_nb) are the fields of the follow-up form: they equal evnum_edm, evnum_edm_psy, evnum_edr and evnum_suicid on every follow-up visit and are not read (ignored.yaml).

Who fills the form is not stated in the notes.

mood_history_v0.title: Mood disorder over the whole life and current episode (inclusion form)

dr.notes: The mood disorder over the whole life and the current episode, at the inclusion visit: 635 rows (634 inclusion visits and 1 screening visit). This cohort has one form (117 for the kind of disorder, 116 for the episodes) and no column for the version: not the BP schemas, which are split by DSM edition. Names. The questions of form 116 on the first episode, the remission, the seasonal pattern, the first psychotropic treatment and the current episode are the ones of BP's DSM-IV form and are read from the same raw columns (agedebutpremier_episode, cetermpremier_episode, ppartpremier_episode, remisc, saison, agetrt, cesevtrouble_humeur_actuel, chrontrouble_humeur_actuel, pparttrouble_humeur_actuel): they carry BP's dsm4_ names. Two labels of form 116 say "selon critère DSM IV" (the mixed episodes and the severity of the current episode) and the form counts mixed episodes, as DSM-IV does. The counts of episodes are in the columns evnum_* here (BP's DSM-IV form reads evnum_*_lt) and take BP's dsm4_lt_n_ names. What BP does not have keeps its name (the age at the first episode treated or diagnosed, the resistant episodes, the partial remission, the delay, the weeks before a treatment). The specifier of the current depressive episode (none, melancholic, atypical, catatonic) takes BP's name dsm4_current_specifier: the same question and the same four answers, which BP reads from another raw column (cedecodtrouble_humeur_actuel_type; BP reads cedecodtrouble_humeur_actuel as the catatonic box, dsm4_current_catatonic). The hard limit of the counts is 50 here (the form takes two digits; the largest count of depressive episodes typed is 50, on one visit, then 23, 20 and 20; the other counts are 10 or less); BP's limit is 20. Two forms in the same columns. The inclusion visit asks about the whole life; the follow-up visits use the same columns for the time since the last visit. The two are never delivered in one column: visit_form says which form a visit uses (inclusion for the screening and inclusion visits, follow_up for the others), and each form has its own schema and its own variables. The follow-up form (183) and form 116 never meet on a visit (no follow-up visit holds a cell that only form 116 writes, no inclusion visit one that only form 183 writes) although they share the evnum_* columns; the export takes the first non-empty of the two and its order is not the same for every count (face_dr_10 lines 26-36: form 116 first for the depressive, resistant and hypomanic counts, form 183 first for the manic, mixed and induced ones). The visit. The kind of disorder (form 117) is answered on 625 of the 635 rows (617 known, 8 "Ne sais pas"). Its answer to "specify the type" is also the gate of the menu: the page of form 116 is offered for the answers 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6 (config/global.php line 271: a gate of the menu, not of the questions) and all 625 answers are among them (no patient has the substance-induced one), but the page is saved on only 358 of them, and on 2 rows with an empty answer (38 cells, kept as recorded): 360 of the 635 rows (359 of the 634 inclusion visits). An empty page 116 means the page was not saved, not "no episode". No shown_if. armcd (the type of disorder of form 117, ignored.yaml) is 7, major depressive disorder, on every row: the other branches of form 117 never run in this cohort. The numbers of episodes (evnum_edm and the others) are counts over the whole life here: median 3 major depressive episodes, of which 1 resistant to two treatments or more. They include the current episode: a single episode has a count of 1 on 58 of 70 visits and a recurrent course 2 or more on 256 of 270 (note: the course says recurrent for 509 and single episode for 123 of the 632 visits that answer it). The same columns hold the counts since the last visit at follow-up (mood_course_fu.yaml). The three numbers with psychotic features (depressive, manic, mixed) have no yes/no question here (BP asks one): a number of episodes of the kind that is 0 gives 0 for the psychotic ones (asked_if, decision D122: with no manic episode no manic episode had psychotic features): 4, 302 and 299 cells missing become 0. Where the number of episodes of the kind is above 0 and the psychotic one is empty it stays missing (49 depressive visits). One manic psychotic number is typed under a manic count of 0 and stays as typed (flagged check_failed, not_above). Codes are those of the form (forms 116 and 117 give the lists). The type of the first episode has 0 to 6 and 7, "Ne sais pas", a missing code. The extraction also holds 8 and 9 on 21 visits (15 "resistant", 6 "not resistant", visits of 2013 to 2017): they are not in the list of the form and not the type of an episode, so they are missing here (not_recorded, missing_code). The resistance of the first episode is the radio TYPE_PREM_EPIR of form 116 (1 resistant, 2 not resistant), in the table and the clean model but not in the export: request R142. "Not known" is a missing code (62 cells before this change, 83 with the 21 above). The current episode is severe on 234 of 342 inclusion visits (217 without, 15 with congruent and 2 with incongruent psychotic features) and lasts for more than two years on 238 of 343. The delay. DELAI_CHRONO_EPI is headed "Délai", in weeks, hint "Max 52", two characters (ecedr.sql); the form never says a delay of what. It is filled on 142 rows and equals the weeks before a treatment of the current episode on 52 of the 130 rows that have both. The hard limit is 52, the hint: two values (80 and 90) are out of range. Ages are numbers of years (whole numbers, two characters in the form), never winsorised. Consistency (aggregates, inclusion visits). No age is above the age at the visit. The first psychotropic treatment comes before the declared first episode on 14 of 340 visits (12 by two years or more) and before the first episode treated or diagnosed on 21 of 338 (18 by two years or more); the treated or diagnosed age is below the declared age on 1 of 348. A psychotropic can precede the first mood episode: not an error by itself. The resistant count is above the depressive count on 2 visits (flagged check_failed, not_above; the three ages are checked against the age at the visit in the same way). The first episode is a major depressive one with a depressive count of 0 on 4 visits, and of the 18 first episodes with psychotic features 4 have a psychotic depressive count of 0. A current postpartum episode is ticked yes on 1 of 141 men.

amiel_lebigre_fu.title: Life events questionnaire (Amiel-Lebigre), follow-up form

dr.section: AMIEL-LEBIGRE (Questionnaire d'évènement de vie, Amiel-Lebigre et al.,2005)
dr.notes: The life-events questionnaire of Amiel-Lebigre asked again at follow-up (form 210): the 53 events of amiel_lebigre_v0, each answered 1 (yes) or 0 (no), and for a yes "when", chosen in a list of two (six months, one year). Filled at 157 follow-up visits from 2013 (98 of the 146 visits of 24 months, 56 of the 69 of 48 months, 2 at 36 months and 1 at 60 months); 153 answer all 53 events, with a median of 1 event (mean 2.0, at most 16). It is one form shown at 24 and 48 months (visit types 6 and 8; decision D60 in PROGRESS.md) and written in the same columns as the inclusion form: see amiel_lebigre_v0 for the wording of the events, the two forms and their notes. The second column holds the code of the list, 1 six months or 2 one year, on all 309 events answered yes at follow-up (delivered as a category; no other code is ever found at a follow-up visit). The follow-up form has no change gate: an empty form means not done. The median gap to the previous visit of the same patient that answered the questionnaire is 748 days (124 visits), longer than the longest option of the list: the options stop at one year, so the answers read as the last year at most and not as the whole interval since the previous visit; they are not delivered as "since the last visit". amiel_events_fu is the number of events answered yes, when the 53 are answered (153 visits). The inclusion count (amiel_events, 330 visits) covers up to the whole life and cannot be compared with it. An instrument of the TRD cohort only.

amiel_lebigre_v0.title: Life events questionnaire (Amiel-Lebigre), inclusion form

dr.section: AMIEL-LEBIGRE (Questionnaire d'évènement de vie, Amiel-Lebigre et al.,2005)
dr.notes: The life-events questionnaire of Amiel-Lebigre at the inclusion visit (form 209): 53 events, each answered 1 (yes) or 0 (no), and for a yes a second answer, "when", chosen in a list of four (six months, one year, two years, whole life). Filled at 354 inclusion visits from 2013 (the share of the V0 visits runs from 16% in 2013 to 90% in 2017 and 43% to 72% since); 330 answer all 53 events, with a median of 8 events (mean 9.2, at most 39). The follow-up form is another instrument, amiel_lebigre_fu (decision D60 in PROGRESS.md). The dictionary names the columns in two lines ("53 items", "if yes, date of the event") and gives neither the events nor a coding. The 53 texts are in the form (the same in forms 209 and 210), and the labels here are their English wording; the 53rd is "other events than these in the last two years". The second column is not a date: it holds the code of the list, 1 six months, 2 one year, 3 two years, 4 whole life ("Date :" is the label of the form), on 3,209 of the 3,284 events answered yes at inclusion and never otherwise. It is delivered as a category (before the review as the code: 3,518 cells of the two forms change representation, 3,209 here and 309 at follow-up). The form does not say whether "one year" means within the last year or between six and twelve months ago. 75 events answered yes on 12 inclusion visits have no "when": delivered as written, no flag. Event 18 (prison sentence) is never answered yes; the most frequent yes is event 23 (death in the close family, 192 inclusion visits). A step in time with no known cause: the count has a median of 4 or 5 events a visit in 2015-2018 and 11 to 16 from 2019 (7 of the 8 centres with 6 visits or more in each period rise); the events of the last two years go from a median of 2 to 4 and those ticked "whole life" from 0 to 6, with the same four options of the form since 2014 (PROGRESS.md D66, QUESTIONS.md DM-11). amiel_events is the number of events answered yes, when the 53 are answered (330 visits); no score is stored and the instrument has none. No published definition matches this form (Amiel-Lebigre and others 1984: a 53-event schedule with an impact rating of 0 to 100; 1990: 51 events; 1998: counts of upsetting events; the windows of the form and the "2005" of the dictionary have no published counterpart; scale_reference.md, section 20: the literature check of 2026-11-21 found no "2005" source, no published total or weights and no published form with these windows): the count is the package's own and not a published score. Two forms in the same columns. Form 209 is shown at the initial evaluation and form 210 at the evaluations of 24 and 48 months (visit types 2, 6 and 8; both are on the simplified visit). They read the same raw columns (amiel01 to amiel53 and amiel01d to amiel53d); the events are the same, and the list of "when" has four options in form 209 and two in form 210. The two are never delivered in one column: visit_form says which form a visit uses (inclusion for the screening and inclusion visits, follow_up for the others), and each form has its own schema and its own variables (the C-SSRS and the ISF of this cohort do the same). An instrument of the TRD cohort only.

athf.title: Antidepressant Treatment History Form (ATHF)

dr.section: ATHF Criteria for Rating Medication Trials for Antidepressant Failure (2009)
dr.notes: The Antidepressant Treatment History Form (Sackeim; scale_reference.md, section 18): one rating per antidepressant, per biological therapy, per augmentation agent and per psychotherapy that the patient received for the current episode, 42 in all. A rating of 0 means no prescription. For an antidepressant, 1 and 2 are trials that were too short or under the adequate dose, and 3 and more an adequate trial (the published rule also needs adherence and an insufficient benefit); the levels of each line are in form 154 (the dictionary lists them). Filled at the inclusion visit (514 visits, and one at screening) and at the follow-up visits (530), at 77% to 84% of the V0 visits in every period from 2013. No score is stored and none is computed here: the ratings are delivered as rated. The published form has no single total either (number of trials, number of failed adequate trials, most potent rating, total potency). A failed adequate trial is a rating of 3 or more (Sackeim 2019, Table 2, the original ATHF criteria); a count of them is not added here, as the choice of the lines that enter it is the user's. The meaning of 0 beyond "no treatment", the level of thyroid augmentation and the "2009" revision of the criteria were not found in the literature check of 2026-11-21. When the form is offered. At the initial evaluation (V0) always; at the other visits only when the MADRS saved on the same visit is above 10 (class.menu_init.php, verif_athf, dated 3 November 2015; before that date it was offered at every follow-up visit: config/global.php). So an empty ATHF is "not offered", never "no trial". At follow-up it is filled on 73% of the visits with a stored MADRS above 10 (484 of 662; 78% since the rule: 402 of 518) and on 19% of those at 10 or below (46 of 237; 9% since: 16 of 188), on none of 26 with no MADRS; at V0 on 81% (514 of 634; 7 of the 11 V0 visits with a MADRS of 10 or less). The audit lines "MADRS -> ATHF asked_if MISSING" (42) are false positives: the form is not a question under a gate, and an empty ATHF is not a 0. The follow-up form can copy the previous visit ("Recuperer les donnees de la derniere visite"): of the 509 follow-up ATHF with an earlier ATHF of the patient, 99 (19%) are identical in all 42 cells. The four points that the dictionary did not settle (open question O8, closed by form 154 and the review, PROGRESS.md D59). (1) Two columns are called bupropion: athf05e is bupropion (ATHFE5), filled on every visit and rarely above 0, and athf05f is vortioxetine (ATHFF5, "Vortioxetine (Brintellix)"), rated 3 or 4 on 149 of its 572 visits: it is delivered as athf_vortioxetine (rule R12, name by content). Vortioxetine and phenelzine (athf04d, MAOI D) are filled on 59 of the 500 ATHF visits of 2013 to 2017, on 68 of the 71 of 2018 and on 96% of the later ones, so the two lines look added to the form around 2018 (the earlier note said "from 2019"). (2) The two columns called antipsychotics are the two lines of the same section: athf10b is "antipsychotics, any dose for any duration" (not an augmentation agent), athf10c the option that rates antipsychotics of a non-psychotic patient as one continuous trial, whatever their number. (3) Bilateral ECT (athf06b) holds the keys 3 and 4, which the form labels B4 (7 to 9 sessions) and B5 (10 or more): they are rated 4 and 5 (the published table has no 3 for a bilateral course; 33 and 93 cells recoded). Lithium alone (athf08a) and carbamazepine (athf08c) are selects with two groups of options: 1 to 3 by plasma level and 4 to 6 by dose, which give the same levels A1 to A3 and C1 to C3. The keys 4, 5 and 6 are recoded 1, 2 and 3 and the range is 0 to 3 (54 and 16 cells); the basis of the rating (plasma level or dose) is lost; the options by dose appear from 2017 (53 of the 54 lithium cells are from 2018 on). (4) A resistance score computed from the form is not in the extraction (the application has none). Consistency of the ratings: lithium as an augmentation agent rated 5 needs an antidepressant rated 4 and has one on 105 of its 119 cells; rated 4 it needs an antidepressant rated 3 or more and has one on 99 of 109. The tutorial notebook counts adequate trials on a list of antidepressants that lacks phenelzine and vortioxetine. An instrument of the TRD cohort only.

bas.title: Brief Anxiety Scale (Tyrer)

dr.section: BAS (Tyrer Brief Anxiety Scale, Tyrer P et al. 1984)
dr.notes: Ten items rated 0 to 6 by the clinician; the total is their sum (0 to 60). The stored total (the application's own, written when the form is saved: js_scores/124_score.js, which empties it when an item is empty) equals the sum on all 1,034 visits that have both; 4 visits have the ten items and no stored total, and get the recomputed one. 1,038 visits have the ten items; the observed maximum is 39. The scale is Tyrer's Brief Scale for Anxiety (Tyrer, Owen and Cicchetti 1984; scale_reference.md, section 15): ten clinician-rated items on a 7-point scale (Tyrer 1984, abstract) and a 0-60 sum (Kazmi 2022). Which ten items of the CPRS form the scale, their order and which are observed rather than reported (the form: the last two) were not settled by the literature check of 2026-11-21. The items are named for the field of the form, not for the screen position, and the dictionary labels them by screen position (decision D57 in PROGRESS.md; rule R12 of the review). The form numbers its fields out of screen order (form 124): the screen shows BAS1 to BAS5 (inner tension, hostile feelings, hypochondria, phobias, worry over trifles), then BAS9 (reduced sleep), BAS10 (autonomic disturbances reported by the patient) and BAS6 (pain) as the last three of the block of symptoms expressed by the patient, then BAS7 (autonomic disturbances observed) and BAS8 (muscular tension) as the block of observed symptoms. The export names its columns by field number, so bas06 holds pain, bas07 the observed autonomic signs, bas08 the muscular tension, bas09 the reduced sleep and bas10 the reported autonomic symptoms; the dictionary (and an earlier version of this schema) read them as sleep, reported autonomic, pain, observed autonomic and muscular tension. The data agree with the form: bas09 correlates with the MADRS item "reduced sleep" at 0.89 (1,026 visits; 0.79 to 0.93 in the six periods) and bas06 at 0.14; bas01 with the MADRS "inner tension" at 0.85; the reported (bas10) and observed (bas07) autonomic items at 0.56. The total does not depend on the order; no value changes. Rated at the inclusion and follow-up visits. Filled at 90% of the V0 visits until 2017 and at 53% of them since 2018, and at 75% of all visits in 2016 and about 28% in 2024-2026 (open question O1: the BAS is one of the forms that the simplified visit omits, PROGRESS.md D55; request R139). A scale that FACE BP and FACE SZ do not have.
