erd.title: Depressive Retardation Scale (ERD, Widlöcher)

dr.notes: The Depressive Retardation Scale of Widlocher (ERD; Hardy, Jouvent and Widlocher 1984; scale_reference.md, section 16). Fourteen items rated 0 (normal) to 4 (very severe) and a fifteenth, the general appreciation of the retardation, on the same scale. The stored score is the application's own (js_scores/228_score.js, which leaves the item of the general appreciation out and empties the field when an item is empty): the sum of items 1 to 14 (0 to 56), on all 507 visits that have both; the general appreciation is not part of it. 11 visits have the fourteen items and no stored score, and get the recomputed one (518 visits in all; observed maximum 47). Whether the original instruction counts the general item in the total was not settled by the literature check of 2026-11-21 (the primary papers were not read): secondary sources describe fifteen items and a total of 0 to 60 with a retardation cut-off of 20 on that total (Bennabi 2013; Robin 2019), which counts the general item; a threshold taken from the literature must not be applied to the 0-56 sum without adding item 15. The items follow the matching MADRS items of the same visit: the concentration item with the MADRS "difficulties of concentration" at 0.68, the interest item with the MADRS "inability to feel" at 0.60, the fatigability item with the MADRS "lassitude" at 0.51 and the rumination item with "pessimistic thoughts" at 0.44; the ERD score with the MADRS total at 0.62 (507 visits). The scale came into use in 2016 (196 inclusion visits, 325 follow-up visits): it is on 43% of the V0 visits since 2016 (60% in 2017, 30% to 73% since). The ERD is one of the forms that the simplified visit omits (PROGRESS.md D55, request R139). A step in time with no known cause: the total has a median of 7 and 9 in 2020 and 2021 (110 visits) against 13 in the other years, and the same centres are lower (5 against 14 in the centre with the most visits), all fourteen items together (PROGRESS.md D66, QUESTIONS.md DM-11). A scale that FACE BP and FACE SZ do not have.

sachs.title: SACHS score (Bipolarity Index)

dr.notes: Five ratings and their sum, filled at the inclusion visit from 2014 (243 visits, and one at screening and one at six months), on 46% of the V0 visits from 2015 (71% in 2016, 41% to 73% a year since 2017). The dictionary gives no label and no coding ("Items de la SACHS"). The form (form 225, "Bipolarite de Sachs") is the Bipolarity Index of Sachs (Aiken, Weisler and Sachs 2015; the scoring sheet; scale_reference.md, section 17): five dimensions (episode characteristics, age of onset, course of illness with associated features, response to treatment, family history), each a single choice among statements that carry 20, 15, 10, 5, 2 or 0 points (the age of onset has no 2-point level), the highest true statement counting, and a total from 0 to 100 (50 or more: bipolar disorder likely, to read as a published threshold only: the stored total is 50 on 3 visits, median 21). The labels below follow that order, which the form confirms. The stored option key is not always the points. Where a dimension holds several statements of the same points, the form keys the extra ones 1, 3, 4, 6 to 9, 11, 12, 16 or 21 (the label of each statement starts with its points, "10 - Manie secondaire a l'utilisation d'antidepresseur" is key 11). The application brings each key back to its points when it computes the total (js_scores/225_score.js, val_inverse: 15 to 19 count 15, 10 to 14 count 10, 5 to 9 and 21 count 5, 1 to 4 count 2). The table of the form and the script give the same points for every key, and the schema is the complete key table (decision D58 in PROGRESS.md), per column: episode 3 counts 2, 6 to 8 count 5, 11 counts 10; course 1, 3 and 4 count 2, 6 to 9 and 21 count 5, 11 and 12 count 10, 16 counts 15; response to treatment 6 counts 5, 11 and 12 count 10, 16 counts 15; family history 3 counts 2, 6 counts 5, 11 counts 10, 16 counts 15; age of onset has none. Key 21 of the course ("worsening of mood during the menstrual cycle", 5 points in the published index) counted 20 in an earlier version of this schema: one course cell and one total (27, now 12) change. 104 of the 242 visits with a total hold a key that is not a point, all from 2016 on. The ratings are delivered in points, so that a dimension is on one scale. The stored total (the application's own, written when the form is saved) equals the sum of the five delivered ratings on 239 of 242 visits (the plain sum of the keys on 141); the 3 others (score_mismatch) are the 3 earliest visits of one centre where the recode matters, in March, June and December 2016, where the stored total is the plain sum of the keys. On the other 101 of the 104 visits where the recode matters the stored total equals the recode, and the 12 later visits of that centre (from March 2017) do too: the application script probably changed there between December 2016 and March 2017. This is read from the data, not from the history of the application, which starts in 2024. Dimension II (age of onset) matches the published age bands of the form on 123 of the 153 visits that have the age at the first mood episode in the mood history (80%; 83% if the age of 30 belongs to the 30-45 band). It is 0 on 11 visits ("no mood disorder") although the cohort requires a depressive episode: delivered as written. One visit lacks the course and treatment ratings and another the course alone: they have no total. An instrument that FACE BP and FACE SZ do not have. The SACHS is one of the forms that the simplified visit omits (PROGRESS.md D55, request R139).

thase_rush.title: Stage of treatment resistance (Thase and Rush)

dr.notes: One rating at the screening visit: the stage of resistance of Thase and Rush (Thase and Rush 1995 and 1997; scale_reference.md, section 19), from 1 (failure of one adequate antidepressant trial) to 5 (failure of bilateral electroconvulsive therapy as well; each stage includes the one before). It is the clinician's radio button (form 122, THASE1): no formula and no link with the ATHF. Filled for 517 of the 634 patients: 81% to 96% of the screening visits a year until 2020, 53% to 72% since 2021. Stage 2 for 256 patients, 3 for 211, 4 for 22, 5 for 26, and 1 for 2. The application copies the stage into the inclusion box "stage 2 or more" when form 122 is saved (js/DRONE.js, case 122: 1 for stages 2 to 5, 0 for stage 1). The inclusion criterion "stage 2 or more" (inclusion_criteria, incl03) is ticked for 631 patients: all 515 patients with a stage from 2 to 5 have it ticked, 1 of the 2 patients at stage 1 has it ticked (the script writes 0 for stage 1) and 115 patients have it ticked and no stage here (the box can be ticked by hand in the inclusion form 193). The box is therefore what the application wrote where there is a stage, and what the clinician ticked elsewhere. Agreement with the ATHF, over the 445 patients with a stage and an ATHF at some visit (the highest rating of each line over the visits): at stage 3 (180 patients) 93% have a tricyclic trial rated above 0 and 24% an adequate one (3 or more on the dose line); at stage 4 (19 patients) 58% have a MAOI trial; at stage 5 (24 patients) 88% have a bilateral ECT rating of 3 or more on the key of the form. The stage is declared, not derived from the ATHF. An instrument of the TRD cohort only.

inclusion_criteria.title: Inclusion and non-inclusion criteria

dr.notes: Seven yes/no boxes filled at the screening visit, for 633 of the 634 patients: three inclusion criteria, three exclusion criteria and the conclusion "eligible". Almost every patient has the three inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria, and fewer than five patients have another answer to any box. The MADRS score and the Thase and Rush stage that two of the criteria refer to are in the instruments madrs and thase_rush. Three boxes are written by the application (rule R33 of the review). (1) "MADRS above 20" (incl01) is written when a MADRS form (100 or 123) is saved: 0 for a total of 0 to 20, 1 for 21 to 60 (js/DRONE.js, lines 1849 to 1862). The clinician can change it afterwards, so it is delivered as stored, with a hidden check from the MADRS total of the screening visit (criterion_madrs_check): it agrees on 550 of the 560 patients with both; the 10 others are stored 1 with a total of 8 to 20 (score_mismatch); 73 have no screening total. (2) "Stage 2 or more" (incl03) is written when the form of the Thase and Rush stage (122) is saved: 1 for the stages 2 to 5, 0 for stage 1 (js/DRONE.js, lines 1871 to 1882). Delivered as stored, with a hidden check from the stage (criterion_resistance_stage_2_check): it agrees on 516 of the 517 patients with a stage (one score_mismatch). The 115 others are ticked yes with no stage rated, a share that rises from 9% of the screenings in 2013-15 to 35% and 36% from 2022: ticked by hand in the inclusion form (193). (3) "Eligible" (excl04) is fully derived: the form sets it to 1 only when the six criteria are filled and all pass, else to 0 (is_eligible, js/formulaires.js, lines 884 to 916), and a batch script set it to 1 where the six stored criteria pass (script/script_inclu.php, lines 20 to 27). It is recomputed here (1 when the three inclusion criteria are yes and the three exclusion criteria no) and the stored value is the check (eligible_stored, not delivered): 3 patients change, 2 stored eligible with a criterion that fails and one stored not eligible whose six criteria pass (score_mismatch). A section of the TRD dictionary only. Yes is 1 and no is 0.

mini_a_depression.title: MINI, module A: major depressive episode

dr.notes: Module A: the symptoms of a major depressive episode, over the last two weeks (the columns that end in p2w) and in a past episode (pe). The MINI is a structured diagnostic interview, here version 6.0.0 (DSM-IV; the version, its suicidality points and the reading of form 229 are question M87). It is given at the screening visit (form 142) and again at the visits of 2 and 4 years (form 229, the same form; 3 more rows at 3 and 5 years): 583 visits of 493 patients answer it (89%, 86% and 82% of the screening visits until 2020, 57% in 2021 to 2023, 66% since; 35% to 100% by centre; open question O24). Not in BP or SZ. The variables keep the number of the question (mini_a01a is question A1a); the conclusions have a name that says what they are. Answers are 1 for yes and 0 for no. Skips. After a "no" to the first questions of a module the page hides and clears the later ones, or sets some of them to 0 (A1b, A2b, C1b, C2b, D5 to D7, E2 and the conclusion boxes). Module A has no enforced skip: the page shows a message only (formulaires.js 946-952), and 16 of the 27 visits with A1a and A2a no hold a later answer (14 a yes, 12 of them at follow-up). Module C is skipped from 2017 only: 137 of the 506 visits with C1a and C2a no hold later answers, all dated 2012 to 2017. Elsewhere a later answer after the skip is rare (D 20 of 393 visits, E, F, G and H 0 or 1). Boxes written by the form. The diagnosis summary of the form (module Q) means to read a03ea_actuel, but a typo makes it ignore it (attr('cheked'), formulaires.js 2415 and 2447, defect A92). The number of episodes of the life (a06a) holds 99 on 6 visits (5 at inclusion, 1 at follow-up), read as "not known". One screening visit holds a slash instead of a number (unparsed).

mini_b_suicidality.title: MINI, module B: suicidality

dr.notes: Module B: suicidality over the last month (B1 to B10) and the attempts of the life (B11). The MINI is a structured diagnostic interview, here version 6.0.0 (DSM-IV; the version, its suicidality points and the reading of form 229 are question M87). It is given at the screening visit (form 142) and again at the visits of 2 and 4 years (form 229, the same form; 3 more rows at 3 and 5 years): 583 visits of 493 patients answer it (89%, 86% and 82% of the screening visits until 2020, 57% in 2021 to 2023, 66% since; 35% to 100% by centre; open question O24). After a "no" to the first questions of a module the page hides and clears the later ones, or sets some of them to 0 (A1b, A2b, C1b, C2b, D5 to D7, E2 and the conclusion boxes). Module A has no enforced skip: the page shows a message only (formulaires.js 946-952), and 16 of the 27 visits with A1a and A2a no hold a later answer (14 a yes, 12 of them at follow-up). Module C is skipped from 2017 only: 137 of the 506 visits with C1a and C2a no hold later answers, all dated 2012 to 2017. Request R169 asks the export to leave the boxes of an unanswered module empty. Follow-up (rule R32). The form of the visits of 2 and 4 years (form 229) is the screening form and asks the same lifetime questions, but the answers show that the interviewers read them as "since the last visit" (question M87): of the yes answers to B11 (an attempt in the life) of the screening visit that are answered again at the first follow-up, 5 of 17 are no. The lifetime and past-episode questions are therefore delivered at inclusion (screening visit) only, and at follow-up in twins named _fu (versions read from the visit label, block visit_form, as in the treatment schemas); the current and past-month questions stay one variable. Here B11 alone (mini_b11_fu); B1 to B10 ask about the last month. Gates. The page shows B1a and B1b after B1 yes, B5a to B5c and B6 after B5 yes, B10a and B10b after B10 yes; these details stay missing after a no. b10a and b10b are boxes written by the form, derived_from B10: derived_doubt where B10 is empty (83 visits each). B5a is the frequency (1 occasionally, 2 often, 3 very often) and B5b the intensity (1 mild, 2 moderate, 3 severe), as form 142 asks; the dictionary codes B05A as an intensity (request R171). It needs one answered item. The stored score (bb, mini_suicide_risk_score_stored, not delivered) is its check: it is stored on 446 visits and equals the recomputed score on each of them; where no question is answered yes the form stores no score and mini_suicide_risk (ba) is 0, read as 0 (asked_if). 6 visits answer the items and have no stored score (the button was not pressed): they get the recomputed score. Whether these points are those of the French MINI 6.0.0 is open (question M87). The schema holds the long item list (B1 accident to B11), not the 6-item list of the 1998 MINI (Lim 2014: weights 1, 2, 6, 10, 10 and 4; bands 1-5, 6-9, then high). The 9-item English form of 2006 gives 10 points, not 9, to an attempt of the last month (here B10) and has a single 1-point item (here B2 and B3), but its points were read from a garbled copy; the points of the French 6.0.0 were not found in the literature check of 2026-11-21 (local/out/scale_reference_rest.md). Level. The same button writes the level (bc) from the score with the tests >1 and <9, >9 and <17, >17 (formulaires.js 933-935, defect A85): a score of 1, 9 or 17 gets no level from the button, and the rater ticks one by hand (66 of the 73 visits at 1 point, 6 of 6 at 9, 1 of 1 at 17). The published bands of MINI 7.0.2 are 1 to 8 low, 9 to 16 moderate, 17 or more high (MINI 7.0.2 form, 2016); the bands of the French 6.0.0 were not found in the literature check of 2026-11-21 (question M87). mini_suicide_risk_level is recomputed from the recomputed score with the 7.0.2 bands (decision D85, function mini_risk_level of custom.py); a score of 0 has no level, as in the form (mini_suicide_risk is 0 there). The stored level (bc, mini_suicide_risk_level_stored, not delivered) is its check: it follows the bands on 432 of the 442 visits where both exist. The 10 others are a hand level that the score does not give (3 at 9 points and 2 at 10 or 12 are low, 3 at 19 to 40 low, 1 at 20 moderate, 1 at 16 high): score_mismatch. 9 visits with a score and no stored level get one (7 at 1 point, the button left them empty; 2 where the button was not pressed). If the French 6.0.0 has other bands (M87), only the function changes. Centres (2026-11-20). B2 (hopelessness) is yes on 8 of 26 visits in the centre that started in 2022 (47% to 83% in the other centres with 20 visits or more), B3 on 10 of 30 in another (50% to 74% elsewhere), and B5c on 7 of 26 in a third (52% to 76% in the three other centres with 20 answers); the other items, the risk and the score differ by 20 points or less between centres. No known cause.

auditory_span.title: Auditory verbal span, forward and backward

dr.notes: Auditory verbal span, forward and backward, with a z-score for each and their difference (the form of the application, 199.php, calls the test "Empan audio-verbal"). Not in BP or SZ. The dictionary names the five variables D2_END_RES, D2_END_ECART, D2_ENV_RES, D2_ENV_ECART and D2_ECA_RES, as if they belonged to the d2 test; their labels (Endroit, Envers, Ecart) are those of the span. 434 visits: 426 with a forward span and 430 with a backward span in range. Eight forward spans (11 to 14) and two backward spans (11 and 15) are above 10: out_of_range. The stored difference is the forward span minus the backward span on all the 417 visits where both spans are in range (425 visits hold a difference, and 2 more hold a dash: unparsed). Z-scores, recomputed with the rule of the application (neuro.js, the tables tab_empd and tab_empv, which write the mean and the SD of each cell as "mean-SD"): z = (span - mean) / SD, to two decimals; a higher z-score is a better span. The cell is the one of the age class (20 to 24, 25 to 34, 35 to 44, 45 to 54, 55 to 64, 65 to 69, 70 to 74, 75 to 79) and of the class of education (1 to 6 years, 7 to 11, 12, 13 to 14, 15 to 20). The age is the one typed in the form (cclin01) where it is within a year of the age at the visit and the age at the visit elsewhere, as for the other tests of DR; the years of education are cclin08. The tables are made from the script (norms/make_dr_empan_tables.py; norms/ is not in the repository). The stored z-scores are kept as checks (auditory_span_*_z_stored, not delivered) and compared with a tolerance of 0.0101. The script has no age class under 20 years (the class of 17 years is taken for "no class" and the class of 18 to 19 years is written so that no age fits it) nor from 80 years. No visit is under 20; one visit has an age at the visit of 80 or more, with a typed age that is lower: its stored z-scores are not recomputed (score_not_recomputed). Three more forward z-scores are stored for a span above 10 (out_of_range: no span to compute from). One visit holds the word false in both stored z-scores (unparsed, checks only): the script of the application writes it when it finds no education or age class, and the recomputed z-scores are delivered there. With the typed age the recomputed z-score equals the stored one on 287 of 287 forward and 291 of 292 backward visits; with the reconciled age it differs on 5 forward and 6 backward visits (score_mismatch), 5 and 5 of them visits whose typed age is more than a year from the age at the visit. No norm. The table has no norm ("PA") in the class of 15 to 20 years of education, at every age, and in one other cell (1 to 6 years, 20 to 24 years). The script tests for "PN", which no cell holds, so it computes a z-score from "PA" and writes "NaN". The extraction holds "NaN" (123 forward, 121 backward) and "PA" (15, 14), and both mean that the table has no norm: every one is a visit with 15 to 20 years of education. Both are read as not_applicable, on the stored variables; the recomputed z-score is missing with norm_missing on the 136 forward and 135 backward visits that have a span in range and 15 to 20 years of education. The neuropsychological assessment is given at inclusion and at the visits of 1, 2 and 4 years: 744 visits of 436 patients. The auditory span is present at 64% of the inclusion visits until 2017, 30% in 2018 to 2020 and 13% since 2021. The form (199.php) has a "test non réalisé" box for each test (EMPAN_TEST here) and a "Non effectuée" box for the whole assessment (NEUROPSY_OFF). Their columns exist in the database (ecedr.sql) but are not in the dictionary, so they are not exported: the data managers should be asked to export them, to tell a test that was not done from one that was not entered (open question O22).

baddeley_dual_task.title: Baddeley dual task

dr.notes: Baddeley dual task: the score mu (the performance kept when two tasks are done together, in percent), its z-score and its percentile band. Not in BP or SZ. 353 visits. It fades: of the inclusions (V0), 59% hold it until 2017 (61% to 2015, 55% in 2016-17) and, by year, 48% in 2017, 31% in 2018, 17% in 2019, 12% in 2020, 4% in 2021, none from 2022 to 2025 and 5% in 2026 (open question O22). The z-score and the band are recomputed as the application computes them (the function doutache of apps/ecedr/www/js/neuro.js, which is the TMT function; tables made by norms/make_baddeley_tables.py, which reads them from the script): z = (mu - mean) / SD in the cell of the age class (under 40, 40 to 59, 60 and over, from the age typed in the form, reconciled with the age at the visit as in the other DR tests) and of the level of education (0 years, 2 to 11, 12 and over; cclin08), 9 cells of 7 limits and a mean and an SD (63 limits and 18 means and SDs). Exactly 1 year of education belongs to no level and gives no score (no visit). A higher z-score is a better performance. The stored z-score and band (dual_task_mu_z_stored, dual_task_mu_band_stored) are kept as checks, with a tolerance of 0.011 for the z-score. Agreement. With the age typed in the form, as the application reads it, the stored z-score and band are the recomputed ones on 346 of 353 visits (the 7 others are from 2013 to 2015), and on 326 of the 331 visits where mu is in range. With the reconciled age, which is delivered, score_mismatch is flagged on 7 visits for the z-score and 7 for the band (2014 to 2017). Of these 7 visits, 2 have a typed age more than a year from the age at the visit; the 5 others differ with the typed age too (2014 and 2015, centres E, G and F) and have no known cause. 22 values of mu are below 0 (14) or above 200 (8), from -548 to 930, in 2013 to 2018 (10 of them in centre D): out_of_range. The application computed a z-score and a band for them all (the z-scores are beyond 10 on 15 of them, which end out_of_range on the stored z-score). The delivered z-score and band are missing on these 22 visits, and the stored ones, which cannot be recomputed, get score_not_recomputed (7 z-scores, 22 bands). The delivered z-scores are between -7.3 and 7.3.

d2.title: d2 test of attention

dr.notes: d2 test of attention. Not in BP or SZ. Five measures: GZ (signs processed), F (errors) with F% (errors over signs processed), GZ - F (overall performance), KL (concentration performance) and SB (the largest line minus the smallest). 631 visits. Percentiles. GZ, GZ - F and KL have a percentile rank written as a number (0.1 to 99.9); F% and SB have a band, with the limits 10, 25, 50, 75 and 90. Each percentile rises with its raw score. All of them are recomputed here as the application computes them (apps/ecedr/www/js/neuro.js, tables made by norms/make_d2_tables.py, which reads them from the script): the raw score and the age typed in the form (cclin01, reconciled with the age at the visit as in the other DR tests) in four age classes (under 25, 25 to 34, 35 to 44, 45 and over); the level of education is not used. The tables hold 223 limits for GZ, 235 for GZ - F, 241 for KL, 20 for SB and 20 for F%, and two lists of labels (percentile ranks and bands). Every raw score is cut to an integer before it is read in its table, the F% after a rounding to one decimal. The stored percentiles and bands (d2_*_stored) are kept as checks. Agreement. With the age typed in the form, as the application reads it, the recomputed value is the stored one on 630 of 631 visits for GZ, 624 of 624 for GZ - F (from the typed GZ - F), 602 of 605 for KL, 624 of 629 for the F% band and 615 of 617 for the SB band. With the reconciled age, which is what is delivered, 6 of the 631 visits fall in another age class, and score_mismatch is flagged on 5 visits for GZ, 9 for KL, 5 for the F% band and 1 for the SB band (and on 30 for GZ - F, below). The SB band of 3 visits is lost: the SB is three digits (out of range) and its stored band cannot be recomputed (score_not_recomputed). GZ - F. The stored GZ - F is not GZ minus F on 35 of 623 visits (differences from -465 to +312; 14 years, 12 centres), while the percentile of GZ and the F% follow GZ and F (F% is F over GZ on all but 2 visits). The delivered GZ - F is GZ minus F (627 visits, 6 more than stored; score_mismatch on the 35, and score_not_recomputed on 1 visit that has a stored GZ - F and no GZ or F), the stored one is the check d2_gzf_stored. The percentile of GZ - F is read from the delivered value: it differs from the stored one, which was read from the typed GZ - F, on 30 visits (score_mismatch), and 2 visits have a GZ - F above the last limit of their age class (norm_missing). Three SB values of three digits are out of range. One stored SB band holds a decimal that is no limit of the band list (unparsed, check only). The neuropsychological assessment is given at inclusion and at the visits of 1, 2 and 4 years: 744 visits of 436 patients. The d2 does not fade; the assessment does (open question O22). Share of the inclusions (V0) that hold any assessment, the d2, the Baddeley dual task, the memory for designs and the auditory span: until 2017 76%, 63%, 59%, 47%, 64% (271 inclusions); 2018 to 2020 76%, 67%, 19%, 16%, 30% (135); 2021 on 51%, 41%, 2%, 0%, 13% (228). The d2 is held by 83%, 89% and 81% of the inclusions that have an assessment.

d2.description: d2 test of attention. Five measures: GZ (signs processed), F (errors) with F% (errors over signs processed), GZ - F (overall performance), KL (concentration performance) and SB (the largest line minus the smallest), with percentile ranks or bands. DR only.

The raw errors and the fluctuation are worse when high, but their bands are better when high.

memory_designs.title: Memory for designs, two parts

dr.notes: A memory test for designs in two parts, each with a raw score, an age-scaled score (1 to 19) and its z-score. Not in BP or SZ. The dictionary calls it "MÉMOIRE DESSIN" and does not name the test; it labels the second part "Dessin1", like the first (DES201 to DES203). The form of the application (199.php) calls it "MEM IV : Dessin", the Designs subtest of the WMS-IV, with the parts "Dessin 1" and "Dessin 2", read as the immediate and the delayed recall. The script accepts raw scores from 0 to 120. 245 visits. Scaled scores and z-scores, recomputed with the rule of the application (neuro.js, the tables tab_bornes_dess1, tab_bornes_dess2 and ns_ecart). The scaled score is the number of the first of 19 upper bounds that the raw score does not exceed, in the age class (18 to 19, 20 to 24, 25 to 29, 30 to 34, 35 to 44, 45 to 54, 55 to 64, 65 to 69); there is no norm under 18 or from 70 years, and no visit has such an age. The z-score is read in a table of the 19 scaled scores: the scaled score minus 10, over 3, to two decimals. The age is the one typed in the form (cclin01) where it is within a year of the age at the visit and the age at the visit elsewhere, as for the other tests of DR. The tables are made from the script (norms/make_dr_designs_tables.py; norms/ is not in the repository). The stored scaled scores and z-scores are kept as checks (designs*_scaled_stored, designs*_z_stored, not delivered). With the typed age the recomputed scaled score equals the stored one on 241 of 243 (part 1) and 234 of 234 visits (part 2); with the reconciled age it differs on 5 and 1 visits (score_mismatch), 3 and 1 of them visits whose typed age is more than a year from the age at the visit. Two visits of part 1 have a stored scaled score and z-score but no raw score: they are not delivered (score_not_recomputed). The stored z-score is not the table's value for the stored scaled score on 19 visits (part 1) and 18 (part 2), all of 2013 to 2015 (2, 13 and 4; 2, 13 and 3 by year) and, but for 2 and 1 visits, of one centre (F: 17 and 17). On 5 and 10 of them the difference is 0.01, a rounding that the tolerance of 0.0101 does not flag; on 14 and 8 it is 0.02 to 0.33 (0.17 on 13 and 7 of them): the stored z-score is in steps of 0.5 (0.5 stored where 0.33 is computed), the old z table of the application that the WAIS-IV z-scores show (wais4_memoire_chiffres.yaml), in the same window (2013-10 to 2015-05: 16 and 9 of the 18 and 9 visits that differ) and the same centre (F: 14 and 7). The recomputed z-score is delivered and differs from the stored one by more than 0.0101 on 18 (part 1) and 9 (part 2) visits: the 14 and 8 above, and 4 and 1 visits whose scaled score differs. Used until 2020. The neuropsychological assessment is given at inclusion and at the visits of 1, 2 and 4 years: 744 visits of 436 patients. The test is present at 47% of the inclusion visits until 2017, 16% in 2018 to 2020 and 0.4% since 2021 (1 of 228). The form (199.php) has a "test non réalisé" box for each test (MEM_DESS_TEST here) and a "Non effectuée" box for the whole assessment (NEUROPSY_OFF). Their columns exist in the database (ecedr.sql) but are not in the dictionary, so they are not exported: the data managers should be asked to export them, to tell a test that was not done from one that was not entered (open question O22).

neuropsy_substances.title: Coffee, tea and tobacco before and during the testing

dr.notes: Coffee, tea and tobacco before the appointment and during the break of the testing. Not in BP or SZ. Filled with the assessment: 723 visits. Each "how many" is asked only after a yes: where the answer is no and the cell is empty, the number is 0 (asked_if). The two questions on tobacco are asked only of smokers (smoker): the 500 non-smokers leave "smoked before the appointment" and "smoked during the break" empty, and 207 of the 219 smokers answered the second. With asked_if: smoker the 500 empty cells are 0 (for smoked_before it was already so), and the number of cigarettes of the break, which hangs on it, goes from 194 to 694 visits. A "yes" with an empty count stays missing: coffee before 3 visits, coffee at the break 1, tea none, the cigarettes of the break 13 of 101. The observed maxima, 8 cups and 2 cigarettes, are inside the ranges. "How long before" is stored 1, 2 or 3. The dictionary gives no code; the form of the application (eCEDR, form 199.php) does: 1 "5 to 30 min" (min_5_30), 2 "under 1 hour" (under_1h), 3 "over 1 hour" (over_1h). Coffee 101, 73 and 195 visits, tea 20, 7 and 51, tobacco 118, 37 and 35. The neuropsychological assessment is given at inclusion and at the visits of 1, 2 and 4 years: 744 visits of 436 patients. About three inclusions in four hold it until 2020 and about one in two since 2021 (open question O22).

rlri16.title: Free and cued recall of sixteen words (RL/RI-16)

dr.notes: Free and cued recall of sixteen words (the RL/RI-16 procedure; the form of the application, 199.php, calls it "RL-RI 16 items"): an immediate cued recall, three trials of free then cued recall, a recognition and a delayed recall. Not in BP or SZ, which use the CVLT. The dictionary calls the section "MÉMOIRE" and does not name the test. It labels MEM23 and MEM24 "Rappel libre différé", like MEM21 and MEM22, but they are the delayed total recall (free and cued) and its band; the delayed free recall is MEM21 and its z-score MEM22. 716 visits. Sums. The stored sum of the three free recalls and the stored sum of the three total recalls equal ours on every visit that has them (712 and 712; the stored total sum is missing on 1 of our 713). Z-scores of the free recalls (three trials and the delayed recall): recomputed with the rule of the application (neuro.js, the tables tab_normes_rl and tab_ecart_RL), z = (free recall - mean) / SD, to two decimals; a higher z-score is a better recall, on every trial. The mean is the one of the cell of the age class (16 to 29, 30 to 49, 50 to 64, 65 to 74, 75 and over), of the sex and of the class of education (1 to 11 years, 12, 13 to 20); there is one SD for each measure. The age is the one typed in the form (cclin01) where it is within a year of the age at the visit and the age at the visit elsewhere, as for the other tests of DR; the years of education are cclin08 and the sex is the one of the patient file (the application reads 1 as a man and 2 as a woman). A missing education gives no z-score and norm_missing. The tables are made from the script (norms/make_rlri16_tables.py; norms/ is not in the repository). The stored z-scores are kept as checks (rlri16_*_z_stored, not delivered) and compared with a tolerance of 0.0101. With the typed age the recomputed z-score equals the stored one on 711 of 711, 710 of 712, 711 of 712 and 705 of 707 visits (trials 1 to 3, delayed recall); with the reconciled age it differs on 12, 13, 12 and 13 visits (50 of 2,843 z-scores, 1.8%): score_mismatch. 44 of the 50 are visits whose typed age is more than a year from the age at the visit, 5 are stored values that are not the table's even with the typed age, and 1 is the stored "<0.25", which agrees with the recomputed value but is compared as 0.25 (censored_left on the stored variable). The tables of the script break their own pattern in a few cells. In each measure the mean rises by the same step from the class of 1 to 11 years to the class of 12 years and to the class of 13 to 20 years, except in five cases: trials 2 and 3 and the delayed recall for women of 16 to 29 (the cell of 13 to 20 years equals the one of men of 16 to 29 with 1 to 11 years; 19 visits), the delayed recall for men of 50 to 64 (the step to 13 to 20 years; 55 visits) and for men of 75 and over (the step to 12 years; no visit with 1 to 12 years, 1 with 13 to 20). They look like typos of the script (no manual is available to say). The stored z-scores follow the script, so they do not show as a mismatch, and the recomputed ones follow it too. Percentile bands of the cued recalls (immediate, total of trials 1 to 3, delayed total): left as stored, not recomputed. Each band is a function of the raw score alone (for the immediate recall: 16 words gives 99, 15 gives 25, 14 gives "5-25", 13 gives 5). The script writes a label for each raw score, and the stored band is that label on 714 of 714, 713 of 713, 712 of 713, 712 of 713 and 707 of 708 visits; the three exceptions are visits with 16 words stored "50-99" or "25-99". They are read as bands with the limits 1, 5, 25, 50 and 99; "5-1" is the band from 1 to 5 written the other way. The recognition band is not a percentile band but a flag with two values: perfect or not perfect. 16 words recognised gives 100 on 615 visits and 99 on 8 (7 until 2014 and 1 in 2021); any other score gives 5 (85 visits). 100 and 99 are read as 99. Checks. The total recall of a trial is its free recall plus its cued recall, so it cannot be lower than the free recall: it is, on 2, 2, 6 and 9 visits (trials 1 to 3 and delayed recall). The check scores (cued recall, total minus free; not delivered) are out_of_range there. The neuropsychological assessment is given at inclusion and at the visits of 1, 2 and 4 years: 744 visits of 436 patients. The RL/RI-16 is present at 72% of the inclusion visits until 2017, 73% in 2018 to 2020 and 48% since 2021. The form (199.php) has a "test non réalisé" box for each test (RL_RI_TEST here) and a "Non effectuée" box for the whole assessment (NEUROPSY_OFF). Their columns exist in the database (ecedr.sql) but are not in the dictionary, so they are not exported: the data managers should be asked to export them, to tell a test that was not done from one that was not entered (open question O22).

A few cells of the norm table of the script break the pattern of the table (they look like typos, and no manual is available to say); the stored and the recomputed z-scores both follow the script.
The dictionary does not name the test; the name comes from the form of the application.

verbal_fluency_form2.title: Verbal fluency, second form (fruits and letter R)

dr.notes: The second form of the verbal fluency, "Fruits et lettre R" (the form 199 of the application: a category, fruits, and a letter, R), used at the retest: 96 visits. Not in BP. The number of words of each task is filled on 95 visits, the z-score on 39 for the letter and 40 for the fruits (one of them unparsed); the percentile band is nearly never filled (2 cells for the letter, 3 for the fruits). Of these 5 band cells 4 are unparsed (3 numbers that are no limit of the band list and the code PA that other DR tests write for no norm), and the unparsed z-score of the fruits is a word typed in the number field. No norm. The script of the application holds tables for this form (tab_part_cat_fruits and tab_part_phono_r) but never applies them: the code that would is commented out, "en attente du tableau", and choosing form 2 empties the result fields. The z-score and the band are typed by hand, with no norm, and nothing is recomputed. The table of the first form (the letter P table for the letter, the animals table for the fruits) gives 2 of the 39 typed z-scores of the letter and none of the 39 of the fruits, so they follow no known rule. Two forms of the test. The form used is in fv01, stored 1 or 2. The dictionary only says "animals or fruits", and the form of the application (FLUE_VERB_CHOI) names them: form 1 is "Animaux et lettre P", form 2 is "Fruits et lettre R" (open question O23 and PI-4 are answered by the form). Form 1 is used at inclusion (388 of 394 inclusions) and form 2 at the retest of the first year (81 of its 96 visits): the usual sequence of a patient is 1, 2, 1, 1. The words differ: the medians are 21 words for the letter and 26 for the category on form 1 (24 for the letter P and 32 for animals in BP), 18 and 18 on form 2. The two forms are two tests: each has its own schema and its own columns, and fluency_form says which one was used. One visit has results and no form (version_unknown).

The two forms are two tests: this form is not pooled with the letter P and animals (verbal_fluency). Fewer words are produced on this form.
No reference is given in the project documents.

care_use_year.title: Use of care and help over the year

dr.notes: Use of care and help over the year, by kind: full-time and day hospitalisation, specialists, emergency department, help received at home and from whom, general practitioner, psychologist, physiotherapist, nurse and other professionals, each with a number of times. Not the BP schema care_use, which is another questionnaire. The form is form 194 (the only one wired in config/global.php; forms 188 and 169 are older copies). It asks "au cours de l'année" and is shown at the inclusion visit and at the visits of 12, 24, 36 and 48 months (visit types 2, 4, 6, 7 and 8): 997 visits (85% to 96% of the inclusions in every period). Answers are 1 and 0, or Y and N for the general practitioner. A number of visits is 0 after a no (asked_if). The place of a hospitalisation or of a consultation is the key of the list of the form: 1 private clinic and 2 hospital (hospitalisation and day hospital), and 3 town practice (specialist only); 356, 146 and 697 cells are named (they were code_N). The specialties are free texts. Two forms of the hospitalisation question (csri_form, read from the columns filled). Form 188 asks one question, "hospitalised, complete or day hospital" (hospit): 284 of the 996 answers come from it, 262 of them from 2012 to 2016, and are delivered as hospitalised_or_day_year (yes on 52%). Forms 194 and 169 split the question into full-time (hospit, delivered as hospitalised_year: 712 answers, yes 35%) and day hospital (hospitj, day_hospital_year). The two are not one variable: hospitalised_year was filled on 996 visits (394 yes) and is now filled on 712 (247 yes), and the 284 visits of the single question are hospitalised_or_day_year (147 yes). The day-hospital yes/no did not exist before 2016: 19 visits of 2012 to 2016 hold day-hospital details with an empty yes/no. One visit holds care use data and neither question: its form is unknown (csri_form version_unknown, 1 flag). The lists that the export crosses. The hospitalisations, the day hospitalisations and the specialists are lists of the form (a Tableau with an add button and no row limit). The export keeps one arbitrary row of them for each visit (select distinct on (usubjid, visitnum) with no ORDER BY, request R122 for the DR list tables): the specialty, the days and the place of a hospitalisation and of a day hospital, the specialty and the place of the specialists and n_specialist (the number of consultations) are the values of one row of several, not totals. The export also casts a number written 00 to an empty yes/no (R73): saw_gp is empty on 6 visits where the number of general practitioner visits is 00. No sum score is computed.

care_use_year.description: Use of care and help over the year (DR), by kind: full-time and day hospitalisation, specialists, emergency department, help at home, general practitioner, psychologist, physiotherapist, nurse and other professionals, each with a number of times. Asked at the inclusion visit and at the yearly visits.

Two forms of the hospitalisation question: the older form asks one question, full time or day hospital (hospitalised_or_day_year, mostly 2012 to 2016); the later ones ask full time (hospitalised_year) and day hospital (day_hospital_year) apart. They are not one variable.

The hospitalisations, the day hospitalisations and the specialists are lists of the form, and the export keeps one arbitrary row per visit: their specialty, days and place, and n_specialist, are the values of one row, not totals.

dr.notes: Hospitalisations since the last visit, counted apart for depression and for another reason, with their total length in months: 800 follow-up visits (83% to 96% of the visits of each kind). The form is form 183, section "DEPUIS DERNIERE VISITE" (the title of the block says since the last visit, so the name is right). A hospitalisation for depression on 182 of 792 visits. Not in BP or SZ in this form. The total length is asked after the number of hospitalisations: asked_if, so it is 0 after a count of 0 (+5 cells for depression and +3 for another reason). It is typed in a box that keeps digits only, so a decimal comma is lost and "0,25" is stored "025": "025" and "05" are read as 0.25 and 0.5 month (codes; 5 cells). No censoring: the months are typed numbers (maximum 45).

cannabis.title: Cannabis

dr.notes: One question, "Consommez-vous du cannabis ?" (do you use cannabis?, 1 yes, 0 no): CURRENT use, in the present tense, and not use at any time of the life. It opens the four DETC-CAGE items of the nurse's record (`DCCAN` of form 112). The export names the column like the lifetime questions of the other cohorts (`suoccur_cannabis_lt`) and the dictionary lists Y, N and U for visit v0 only, but the values are 1 and 0 (never unknown). Asked at inclusion (429 of 634 visits answered), at 2 years (92 of 146) and at 4 years (57 of 69), plus 4 answers at other visits (3 years, 5 years, screening); never at 6, 12, 18 or 30 months (0 of 702 visits), although the nurse's record is filled at those visits (the tobacco status is, on 84%). 582 answers, yes on 24 (22 at inclusion, 5%, and 2 at 2 years): the share is small because the question is about the present, so a 0 does not mean "never used". In the extraction from June 2013 (0 of 6 inclusions of 2012). Answered on 43%, 45% and 45% of the inclusions of 2013, 2014 and 2015, then on 67% to 89% a year from 2016 (80%, 81% and 73% in 2016-18, 2019-21 and 2022-26). An empty cell is "not answered": 11% to 33% of the inclusion visits a year since 2016, and 23%, 31% and 37% of the visits at 2 and 4 years in 2016-18, 2019-21 and 2022-26 (0% to 69% by year, on 1 to 34 visits): a drift, not a step. The yes share of the inclusions by year (the years with 20 answers or more) stays between 0% and 12%, with no trend. By centre the question is answered on 62% to 100% of the inclusions since 2016 in 13 centres and on 10% in the 14th (31 inclusions), which holds no cannabis answer and no tobacco status at any of its 70 visits since 2017: a centre habit, no cause known (DM-7, DM-8). Not joinable with the other cohorts. SZ asks "more than ten times in your life" (about half of the inclusions say yes); BP and ASP deliver a cannabis use disorder (abuse or dependence) from their substance forms. Do not stack them with this variable. The DETC-CAGE items (instrument `detc_cage`, AUTO-QUESTIONNAIRES) are filled on 21 of the 24 yes and on 79 of the 100 CAGE forms that have this question empty (all dated 2012 to 2016); under a no on none of the 558 (the form hides and clears them unless "yes" is ticked; the forms 103 and 119, two other versions of the nurse's record, hold the four items and no opening question). The CAGE belongs to the review of that tab (O31).

isf_lifetime_fu.title: Suicidal ideation and attempts, asked again at follow-up

dr.notes: The five questions of isf_lifetime.yaml asked again at follow-up: 140 visits (94 at 24 months, 42 at 48 months, 4 at other visits), most of them from 2015 to 2019. Form 145 is one form, shown at the inclusion visit and at the visits of 24 and 48 months (visit types 2, 6 and 8). Another question than BP's (decision R12). The DR form says "ever" and prints no period, at follow-up as at inclusion: the schema is named isf_lifetime_fu and its variables isf0N_lifetime_fu, and it is not joined with the BP and SZ schema isf_since_visit, whose form says "since the last visit". An answer here is a yearly update: the question asked again at the follow-up visit, which the raters read both ways. 26 of the 44 follow-up visits of patients who said at inclusion that they had attempted suicide answer "no" (read since the last visit) and 29 of the 91 "yes" to the first question are dated "more than a year ago" (read as the whole life). A "when" of more than a year is also valid at 24 months (the median gap since the previous visit is 24.5 months): it is no longer flagged (136 period_doubt flags removed; the schema had flagged it). At follow-up "attempted" is yes on 26 of 140 DR visits (18.6%), against 2.4% in BP and SZ; of the patients yes at inclusion, the first follow-up answer is yes again for 11 of 30 in DR, 117 of 1,359 in BP and 20 of 331 in SZ. Two forms in the same columns. The inclusion visit and the follow-up visits use the same columns, and the two are never delivered in one column: visit_form says which form a visit uses (inclusion for the screening and inclusion visits, follow_up for the others), and each form has its own schema and its own variables. The follow-up form has no change gate: an empty form means not done.

isf_lifetime_fu.description: The five yes/no questions of isf_lifetime (from life not worth living to a suicide attempt, each with "when last"), asked again in DR at the visits of 24 and 48 months with the same lifetime wording.

isf_lifetime_fu.reference_confidence: Record confirmed (no abstract). The schema notes do not name the form: it is matched to this scale on its five questions only (to verify)

Not the BP and SZ follow-up question: it is not joined with isf_since_visit, whose form says 'since the last visit'. 'Attempted' is yes on 18.6% of these visits against 2.4% in BP and SZ.
140 visits only, most of them from 2015 to 2019. An empty form means not done.

sis.title: Suicide Intent Scale (SIS)

dr.notes: Suicide Intent Scale: fifteen items rated 0 to 2 on the circumstances of an attempt and on what the patient expected. Not in BP or SZ. 140 visits, 122 of them inclusions (inclusion and screening visits) and 18 follow-up visits. The stored score (sisv16) is the sum of the fifteen items (the script 153_score.js is a plain sum) and is blank unless all fifteen are answered: it is on all 139 visits that answer the fifteen items, and sis_total recomputes the same 139 values (0 mismatch). One visit answers fewer than fifteen items and has no score. When the form is asked. Form 153 is shown only after a yes to ISF5 (attempted suicide): the 140 SIS visits all have a yes, and 46 of the 186 visits with a yes have no SIS (38 at inclusion, 8 at follow-up). The 18 SIS of follow-up visits describe an attempt that the patient dates more than a year before the visit on 15 of the 18; at follow-up the form is asked again (a yearly update, R14c). Of the 8 patients rated at inclusion and at follow-up, 6 have answers that differ. One schema for both forms, no split: the items are the same. sis04 is the item "seeking help during or after the attempt": 0 the patient told a potential rescuer, 1 contacted one without mentioning the act, 2 told no one.

sis.description: Suicide Intent Scale (DR only): fifteen items rated 0 to 2 on the circumstances of a suicide attempt and on what the patient expected, with their sum. The form is shown only after a yes to "attempted suicide" (ISF5).

Rated only after a reported attempt: 140 visits (122 inclusion or screening, 18 follow-up); 46 of the 186 visits with a yes to 'attempted' have no SIS.
One schema for the inclusion and follow-up visits. Of the 8 patients rated at both, 6 have answers that differ.

suicide_attempts_fu.title: History of suicide attempts, asked again at follow-up

dr.notes: The history of suicide attempts of form 145 asked again at the follow-up visits (24 and 48 months mostly): 140 visits answer ISF5 (26 yes, 114 no). The inclusion visit is suicide_attempts.yaml. The variables carry the suffix _fu and not since_visit (R12, R14d): the DR form says "ever" and prints no period at follow-up either, so these are not the BP and SZ questions "since the last visit" (suicide_attempts_since_visit) and the schema is not joined with them. An answer is a yearly update, asked again at the follow-up visit, which the raters read both ways (isf_lifetime_fu.yaml). The follow-up form has no change gate: an empty form means not done. Counts that are 0 by logic, as at inclusion. After a no to ISF5 the history is empty on all 114 visits (hidden dates stored 0000-00-00: 112), so the number of attempts is 0 (asked_if on the hidden copy attempted_ever_fu, which isf_lifetime_fu delivers as isf05_lifetime_fu), the violent and serious attempts are 0 after 0 attempts and their numbers 0 after a no. n_attempts_fu is on 136 visits: 22 typed (all above 0, 4 of the 26 yes give none) and 114 zeros. The 124 cells of the follow-up visits that used to share the inclusion columns are here (21 first-attempt dates, 22 numbers, 23 and 21 yes/no answers, 9 and 10 numbers, 9 and 9 dates). The date of the first attempt is a question about the whole life: it is read and checked (21 real dates) and not delivered at follow-up (keep false; decision of the project lead, as BP and SZ). The dates of the most violent and of the most serious attempt are delivered (9 and 9 cells); a date on the day of the visit or later would be impossible (before_visit; no cell concerned).

devices.title: Electronic cigarette, pacemaker, CPAP and deep brain stimulation

dr.notes: Four yes/no questions of the section "Dispositifs médicaux" of form 203, asked with the non-drug treatments: electronic cigarette, pacemaker, CPAP and deep brain stimulation (columns CI_ELEC, PACE, CPAP, SCP; the target and the indication of the stimulation are CIB_STIMU and INDI). The four are flat radios with no gate; only the target and the indication are hidden behind a yes to deep brain stimulation (f_traitement, SCP1): 0 of 989 are filled after a no and 3 of 3 after a yes. Not in BP or SZ. The question has no period: it is the state at the visit, asked at the inclusion visit and at every follow-up visit. 1,023 visits answer at least one question (1,018 answer all four); every one of them also holds a non-drug answer, as do 1,350 visits in all. The form was not always shown: of the visits that hold the non-drug part, 0 of 14 before June 2013 answer the devices, 76 of 349 (22%) from June 2013 to the end of 2015, and 947 of 987 (96%) from 2016 (V0 93%, follow-up 98%). So the questions are asked at every visit only since 2016. 2 is "not known" (120 cells, missing_code). Seven of the 23 patients with a CPAP yes answer no at a later visit.

medications_lifetime.title: Psychotropic treatment of the past, one row per treatment

dr.notes: The psychotropic treatment of the past (PSYCHOTROPE LIFETIME), one row per treatment in the table treatments, where the column list says "medications_lifetime". 406 patients, and one product for 404 of them: the file holds a single past treatment per patient in almost every case, which the form does not force (a table of rows, shown by patient, with an add button and no limit of rows) and the export may cause (one arbitrary row per visit is kept, lines 6-8 of face_dr_12_traitements.sql; request R122). Most are antidepressants (venlafaxine, fluoxetine, escitalopram, clomipramine, mirtazapine). The variables keep the names of the BP and SZ lists with one exception: substance_name, not medication. The export writes the name of the substance of the drug catalogue (nomsubstance): no digit on any of the 408 rows, a salt in brackets on 12% (49 rows); BP and SZ keep the product as typed, with its strength. The lists are crossed by the export (request R122), as in medications.yaml (which gives the lines of the SQL): the export writes every product of the patient next to every prescription line. Only 2 of the 406 patients have two products and are affected; the other 404 keep their line. A patient with several products keeps one item per product, without form, dose or date (list_crossed on these variables, SCHEMA_SPEC section 15). The class and catalogue-code columns (cmclas, cmclascd) are lists of another length and are not read (ignored.yaml). Six patients have catalogue (CIS) codes but no substance row (products with no ATC match). The list of a patient is the history of the patient (the form is shown by patient), the same on every row of the patient. Dates are written day/month/year; 313 treatments have a start and 233 an end. The at-visit columns of medications.yaml do not read this list. daily_dose is the daily dose in mg as typed (the forms title the field "posologie journalière en mg"); units_per_day is derived by the export, as in medications.yaml. No treatment ends before it starts (check end_date).

medications_somatic.title: Somatic treatments, one row per treatment

dr.notes: The somatic treatments recorded as current (TRAITEMENTS SOMATIQUES ACTUELS), one row per treatment in the table treatments, where the column list says "medications_somatic". 273 patients, 408 items delivered. No molecule table is used: the generic name of the catalogue is delivered as written (esomeprazole, colecalciferol, pantoprazole and levothyroxine are the most frequent). The table medications.csv is a table of psychotropic drugs: it would find 162 of the 408 items and leave the others as unknown_code, so it is not used until it has the somatic drugs. The variables keep the names of the psychotropic lists with one exception: substance_name, not medication (R17). The export writes the name of the substance of the drug catalogue (nomsubstance): 4 of the 408 rows hold a digit, a salt in brackets on 6% (25 rows). The lists are crossed by the export (request R122), as in medications.yaml (which gives the lines of the SQL; form 158 is a table of rows that belong to the form of the visit, with an add button and no limit of rows). 72 of the 273 patients have several products. A patient with one product keeps every line. A patient with several products keeps one item per product, without form, dose or date (list_crossed on these variables, SCHEMA_SPEC section 15): the molecules are known, their dates are not. In the file there are 709 items. The class and catalogue-code columns (cmclas, cmclascd) are lists of another length and are not read (ignored.yaml). Thirty-one patients have catalogue (CIS) codes but no substance row (products with no ATC match), and 36 more have fewer substances than codes. The raw table also holds three columns that look like the reasons for stopping (psy_arret_som_1 to 3; the form has a "Motif" column), which the export does not select. The list of a patient is the same on every row of the patient, but it is not a history of the past: the rows are the somatic treatments of the visits, pooled by the export. Dates are written day/month/year. daily_dose is the daily dose in mg as typed; units_per_day is derived by the export, as in medications.yaml. No treatment ends before it starts (check end_date).

psychotherapies_fu.title: Psychotherapies, asked again at a follow-up visit (follow-up form)

dr.notes: The history of psychotherapies (form 155, PTHF) asked again at the follow-up visits: 737 visits (77% to 84% of the visits of each kind). A supportive therapy on 241 of 736 visits, a cognitive behavioural therapy on 83. Another 45 follow-up rows hold only the placeholder dates of the form, and no answer. The question has no period. Form 155 prints no time frame, at the inclusion visit or at follow-up; at follow-up raters read it both ways. An answer here is a yearly update (asked again at the follow-up visit), never "since the last visit": the suffix is _fu and not since_visit, and the BP and SZ questions that carry the same names (cbt_fu, psychodynamic_fu, other_therapy_fu) say "since the last visit" (the catalogue notes it). It reads the same fourteen kinds as psychotherapies_v0.yaml, which gives the codes, the names shared with BP and SZ, the two kinds and the reasons for ending that the extraction lacks (request R133), and the disagreement of the kinds with the question TT_PSYCHO (111 of the 451 follow-up visits that answer no to it hold a kind yes; 16 of 260 that answer yes hold every kind no). Neither reading holds alone, as for ECT: not "ever", for 105 of the 245 follow-up visits of patients who had had a supportive therapy at inclusion answer no; not "since the last visit", for 92 of the 141 supportive therapies with a start date at follow-up began more than a year before the visit. Two forms in the same columns: the whole life at the inclusion visit, the question asked again at follow-up. visit_form says which form a visit uses, and each form has its own schema, as in BP. The expertise of the therapist and the result are decoded as in psychotherapies_v0.yaml (expertise 0 is "not known", missing_code, 36 cells). The number of sessions is 0 after a no (asked_if). The result of the behavioural therapy is in a column named tcom_result.

psychotherapies_v0.title: History of psychotherapies over the whole life (inclusion form)

dr.notes: The history of psychotherapies (form 155, PTHF) at the inclusion visit, over the whole life: 473 visits (58% of the inclusions until 2014, 72% to 85% since). A supportive therapy for 215 of 471 patients, a cognitive behavioural therapy for 80, a psychoanalytic one for 50. A patient form, like non_drug_lifetime.yaml (level patient): the answers are in the table patients; no patient has the form on both the screening row and the V0 row (473 rows with an answer, 473 patients). Another 50 inclusion rows hold only the 28 dates of the form, all placeholders, and no answer. For each of fourteen kinds of therapy the form asks whether the patient had it, the number of sessions, the dates, the expertise of the therapist and the result. The 14 kinds are radios that are always shown: they are answered as a full list on 461 of the 473 visits, so no empty kind is read as a no. The number of sessions is 0 after a no (asked_if); the other details stay missing after a no. The form has sixteen kinds and a reason for ending each therapy: dialectical behavioural therapy (TDIACOM), family therapy (TFAMI) and the reason for the end of each therapy (MOT_FIN_THE: 0 in progress, 1 the patient decided to stop, 2 the therapist recommended to stop, 3 joint decision, 4 other) are in form 155 and in the table, not in the extraction (request R133). The codes are those of the form: expertise of the therapist 0 not known (missing_code, 87 cells), 1 no specific qualification, 2 trainee, 3 under supervision, 4 senior independent, 5 expert; result 1 no improvement, 2 minimal, 3 certain, 4 definite, 5 sustained improvement, 6 complete remission. The result of the behavioural therapy is in a column named tcom_result. Names. Three kinds are also asked in BP or SZ and carry their names: cognitive behavioural therapy (ever_cbt, cbt_sessions, cbt_start_date, cbt_end_date), psychodynamic therapy (ever_psychodynamic; SZ asks it at follow-up as psychodynamic_fu) and another therapy (ever_other_therapy, other_therapy_name; the BP and SZ question is "another non-drug treatment", and the BP free texts hold kinds that DR lists apart). The other eleven kinds are DR only. BP's three non-drug therapies (cognitive behavioural, psychoeducation groups, interpersonal and social rhythm therapy) are specific therapies, not aggregates, so these are not the same questions and stay apart: DR interpersonal therapy and BP IPSRT, SZ family psychoeducation and BP psychoeducation groups, SZ cognitive remediation and DR cognitive therapy, DR "other" and BP "other". ever_psychotherapy (TT_PSYCHO, in non_drug_lifetime.yaml) disagrees with these kinds: of the 211 inclusion visits that answer no to it and hold this form, 85 have at least one kind yes; 12 of the 228 that answer yes have every kind no. It is delivered as the stored question, with no derived "any psychotherapy".

psychotherapies_v0.description: History of psychotherapies over the whole life at the inclusion visit (DR), one value per patient in the table patients: for each of fourteen kinds of therapy, whether the patient had it, the number of sessions, the dates, the expertise of the therapist and the result.

family_neurodevelopment.title: Neurodevelopmental disorders of the relatives, one row per relative

asp.notes: For each relative described, nine answers: autism spectrum disorder, intellectual disability, communication disorder, ADHD, learning disorder, motor disorder, another specified neurodevelopmental disorder, a neurodevelopmental disorder not specified and an oppositional disorder. 562 relatives for 434 inclusion visits, from 2019 to 2026 (no yearly visit holds the table). One row per patient and relative in the table treatments, where the column list says "family_neurodevelopment". The export packs the relatives of a patient in one cell, nine fields each, and writes who each relative is in a second cell (srel), a code per relative in the same order. The nine answers are those of the form 196 (TSA, HI, TRBCOM, TDAH, TRBAPPR, TRBMOT, AUTRETRB, NEURONSP, TOP); the eighth, NEURONSP, is a neurodevelopmental disorder not specified (it was first read as a neurological disorder: the internal field of the packed record keeps the old name fam_neurological_nos). The relative is named from the list of the form (father, mother, brother, sister, son, daughter). A 9 is "Non connu" (not known). The nine answers are radios Oui/Non/Non connu in the form 196 (a version with checkboxes is commented out there): an empty radio beside a ticked one is not an answer, so the schema has no box_list (decision R3 of the review of the history tab). 387 relatives have at least one yes; 171 of them leave other answers blank (159 tick only the yes, 12 hold a yes, a no and blanks). The blanks stay missing: read as no they would be 1,271 cells (open question O20). 85 relatives hold nine empty fields: a relative was opened and nothing was answered. Who the relative is. The field srel is not required in the form: 191 of the 562 relatives have no code (170 visits hold records and no srel at all, 180 relatives, and 11 visits have one code fewer than records); the two cells have the same number of records on 253 of the 264 visits that hold both. A relative with no code is delivered with no relative. The form 247, the follow-up form of the family history, holds only the box genchang (see psychiatric_care) and nothing to enter: later answers do not exist. The question atcdfam of the form (is there a family history?) is not a gate of the table: the script that should hide the table binds the names ANTFAM* while the field is ATCDFAM, so the table of the relatives is always shown (request A50 of EXPORT_REQUESTS.md). 305 visits describe a relative with at least one yes and only 62 of them have atcdfam yes (233 blank, 10 no or 9): family_neurodevelopmental_history is not the family history; read this list. A summary per patient (a relative with an ASD, a first-degree relative with any of the nine) is not delivered (open question O20). **Year and centre.** The shares of yes of the ASD and ADHD answers do not differ beyond chance between years (49% to 69% and 29% to 62%, six years with 20 relatives or more) or between centres (38% to 71% and 38% to 67%, five centres): no step. An instrument of the ASP cohort only.

Inclusion visits from 2019.

hospitalisations.title: Psychiatric hospitalisations, one row per hospitalisation

asp.notes: The reason, the year and the length of each hospitalisation: 588 hospitalisations for 392 visits (388 patients), from 2009 to 2026. One row per visit and hospitalisation in the table treatments, where the column list says "hospitalisations" and the column visit names the visit. The export packs the hospitalisations of a visit in one cell, three fields each: the reason in free text, the year and the length in days. A visit's list holds the rows typed at that visit; the lifetime history is the union of the visits (588 rows, 4 more than when only the first visit of a patient was read). What is filled depends on the form. The inclusion form (197) asks the year of the start and the length: the year is filled on 3 of the 185 records of the visits to 2019, 17 of 33 in 2020 and 344 of 361 from 2021; the length only from 2020 (15 of 33 in 2020, 224 of 361 from 2021). The follow-up form (248) asks the dates of the start and of the end (DDEBHOSP, DFINHSOP), which the export never reads: it reads ANDEBHOSP and DURHOSP, so the year and the length are blank on 8 of the 9 follow-up records (request R109 of EXPORT_REQUESTS.md). 22 years are out_of_range, all between 3 and 28 and on visits of 2021 to 2026: they are not lengths; 2 lengths equal 999. **Year and centre.** The year of a stay is a date: its median follows the year of the visit (2018 to 2022 by year of the visit and by centre, years and centres with 20 values or more), and it is filled almost only from 2020 (above). A section of the ASP cohort only.

psychiatric_care.title: Family history and psychiatric care: the questions

asp.notes: Whether a relative has a neurodevelopmental disorder, the first contact with psychiatry and its age, hospitalisations and a current treatment: 1,927 inclusion visits (689 of children), from 2009, and 235 follow-up visits, from 2014. Named from the column names and checked against the thesaurus V2.13 (PROGRESS.md D14). A hospitalisation is reported on 422 visits (413 at inclusion) and a current treatment on 715 inclusion visits. The hospitalisations are described in the instrument hospitalisations and the treatments in medications, one row each in the table treatments. early_development.title: Early development

asp.notes: The milestones (sitting, walking, first words, first sentences), a delay or a loss of language, eating and sleep problems in childhood, and seizures: 2020 inclusion visits (843 of children), from 2009 to 2026; asked at the inclusion visit. The follow-up form (244) repeats the sections of the first acquisitions and of epilepsy: 117 follow-up visits (2014 to 2019) hold a box of those sections, 105 of them only the two boxes "change since the last visit" (early_acquisitions_changed, 111 visits: 109 no, 2 yes; seizure_history_changed, 116 visits: 114 no, 2 yes), and 12 hold an answer; neither box gates anything. Named from the column names and checked against the thesaurus V2.13 (PROGRESS.md D14). The ages are in months. A psychomotor delay is reported for 216 of the 1804 patients with an answer and a language delay for 415 of 1804. The age of the first words is 99 on fewer than five visits and the age of the first sentences on 4: 99 is read as "not known". The ADI-R asks the same two ages (items 9 and 10) to the parent; this section is the clinician's record. **Ages with no gate.** The four ages (age_sitting, age_walking, age_first_words, age_first_sentences) hang on no question: the answers to psychomotor_delay and language_delay (RETPSY, RETLANG) appear in no rule of the form, and the ages are typed whatever they are. The age of sitting is filled on 532 of the 1588 inclusion visits with no psychomotor delay (the age of walking on 1161), the age of the first words on 709 of the 1389 visits with no language delay (the first sentences on 693); the share of "no" visits that hold an age shows no step by year since 2015. They are delivered as typed: nothing is encoded. The age of a sudden complex language is filled only after a yes (174 of the 253 yes, none of the 1469 no). **After a no.** The effect of the eating disorder on the weight, the four boxes of the sleep disorder and the seizures still present are Oui/Non/Non connu radios that the form shows after a yes to eating_problems, sleep_problems_first_year or seizures: after a no they are empty in 100% of the cells and are 0 (`asked_if`: 1475, 4 x 1389 and 762 cells). A radio left unticked is saved empty, so there is no `box_list` on the four sleep boxes. The age at the first seizure and the highest frequency are details and stay missing after a no, as does the current level of language. **The seizure block stops in 2020.** The seizure question is answered on 0.75 to 0.86 of the inclusion visits of each year from 2012 to 2019 (0.84 in 2019), on 0.45 of those of 2020, on 0.04 of 2021 and on none from 2022 (one visit in 2025). The application writes the question (CRISCONV) in the medical history forms 193 and 347 (table aut_atcdlt), and the export reads it in the table of this section (aut_c1antmed): request R108 of EXPORT_REQUESTS.md. **Year and centre.** The ages are typed from memory in rounded months (79% of the ages of the first sentences and 70% of the first words are multiples of 6). Medians by year and by centre (20 values or more): sitting 6 to 8 months and 6 to 8, walking 13 to 14 and 13 to 15, first sentences 24 to 36.5 and 20 to 31, the age of the sudden complex language 24 to 36 by year (three years). These are one or two rounding steps and follow the age mix of the patients (children are 0% to 100% of the inclusion visits of a centre and 9% to 59% of a year): the median of the first sentences is 24 months among the children from 2018 and among the adults from 2020, on groups of 22 to 32 values before. No change of the form is known. A section of the ASP cohort only.

pregnancy.title: The mother's pregnancy with the patient

asp.notes: What the parents report of the pregnancy: earlier miscarriages and stillbirths, consanguinity, assisted reproduction, folic acid, bleeding, infections, vaccination, medications and substances during the pregnancy, and the diseases of the mother and of the foetus. 2051 inclusion visits (868 of children) hold an answer of the section, from 2009 to 2026; asked once, at the inclusion visit (form 192). The follow-up form (244: sections pregnancy, vaccinations, first acquisitions and epilepsy) repeats the first questions of the section only: on its 149 visits (2014 to 2020) the section holds the boxes described below and, on one visit, another answer. The section was first read without a dictionary; the labels and the lists are now those of the thesaurus V2.13 (PROGRESS.md D14), and every variable that kept its column name has a descriptive name. The questions are yes/no with a 9 for "not known", read as missing with its reason: the answer is not known for 224 to 790 of the inclusion visits by question (790 for the folic acid, 684 for the vaccination). A detail (trimester, which, name of the drug) is filled only after a yes and stays missing after a no. **Boxes written on every saved form.** The boxes of the trimesters and of the drug classes (miscarriage_before_trimester_1 to 3, stillbirth_before_trimester_1 to 3, pregnancy_medication_antiepileptic to _other) are checkboxes: the application saves a 0 for each box that is not ticked (class.update.php), and the column cannot be empty (tinyint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 in the table, on exactly these twelve columns). They are 0 or 1 on 2139 inclusion visits and on 149 follow-up visits; 88 inclusion visits and 148 follow-up visits hold no other answer of the section. A 0 there is "not ticked": it is not an answer, and it is also what an unanswered question gives, under a yes as well as elsewhere. No box is 1 under a question that is not a yes (at inclusion: 328 visits with a trimester of an earlier miscarriage, 30 of a stillbirth and 247 of a medication, all under a yes). The boxes are delivered as written and flagged `derived_doubt` where their question (miscarriage_before, stillbirth_before, pregnancy_medication) is empty or not known: 7713 flags (5931 at inclusion, 1782 at follow-up), on 821 visits. The form shows the number of a trimester when its box is ticked, but a box cannot say "not ticked" from "not asked", so the numbers hang on the question, not on the box (below). **Yes/no questions after a yes.** The nine infections and the six substances are Oui/Non radios shown after a yes to infection (pregnancy_infection) or to substance use (pregnancy_substance). After a no they are empty in 100% of the cells (1545 and 1500 inclusion visits): they are 0 (`asked_if`). A radio left unticked is saved empty, so an empty radio beside a ticked one is not an answer and there is no `box_list`: 23 of the 98 visits with an infection yes and 27 of the 196 with a substance yes have a yes next to an empty radio; those stay missing. After a no to their question, the numbers of earlier miscarriages and of earlier deaths in utero by trimester (3804 and 4929 cells), the cigarettes a day (1529), the drinks a day (1643), the joints a day (1674) and the doses of another substance a day (1670) are 0. The lists that start at 1 (trimester of an infection, of the first intake or of a bleeding, severity of a bleeding, time of the folic acid) hold no 0: they stay missing after a no, as does every detail. After a no or a "not known" nothing is typed under a question, not a number and not a trimester (0 cells in the 38 pairs of a question and its details); under an empty answer three cells are: the time of the folic acid on one visit, and the trimester and the text of another infection on a visit whose infection answer is no. The form hides one level only: a click on a question hides and clears the fields under it, not the fields that hang on those (a number, a trimester). At load it hides the time of the folic acid when the answer is no, not known or empty, but does not clear it: one inclusion visit holds it with the folic-acid answer empty. pregnancy_section_changed is the "change since the last visit" box of the pregnancy section of the follow-up form: 0 on 147 visits of 2014 to 2020, never 1; it gates nothing. The same box of the first acquisitions, which the first reading put here, is early_acquisitions_changed in early_development, where the form places it. **Year and centre.** folic_acid has steps whose cause is not known. Among the answers yes and no the share of yes is 32% to 36% in 2013 and 2014, 13% to 20% from 2016 to 2020, 42% to 44% in 2021 and 2022 and 30% to 51% from 2024; it is 8% to 54% by centre (five centres with 20 answers or more). The steps are made of changes inside the centres: in one centre the share of yes is 48% to 2015, 3% from 2016 to 2020 and 0% from 2021 while its share of "not known" goes from 11% to 14% and then 45%; in another it is 33% and then 69%. No change of this question is known in the form (open question O25). The age mix plays a part in the completion of the section (an answer on 84% of the inclusion visits of children, 62% of adults), not in these steps: they are found among the children and among the adults. A section of the ASP cohort only.

somatic_history_fu.title: Somatic history at the yearly follow-up visits: the questions

asp.notes: One yes/no question per body system, then gynaecology, genetic diseases, other diseases and allergy: 2,060 inclusion visits (815 of children), from 2009, and 72 yearly follow-up visits, from 2014, hold an answer; the screening visits hold none. The inclusion form (form 193) and the form of the yearly visits (form 347) use the same columns, so they are delivered as two instruments, somatic_history_v0 (inclusion visit) and somatic_history_fu (yearly visits); visit_form says which form a visit used and is read from the visit label, as in BP. A 9 is "not known" and is delivered as missing with its reason. Two forms in the same columns. The form 347 is the form 193 with one question added, "change since the last visit for the whole medical history" (atcdchang), and the shortcut "Non pour tous les critères" (ATCDLTN, not in the extraction) left out. A yearly answer is an update given at that visit (BP decision D84): neither a history of the whole life nor strictly an answer about the time since the last visit. Of the 146 yearly answers to a question answered yes at inclusion, 45 are no (31%; the first answer of each patient and question: 40 of 126). The change question exists in the yearly form only: somatic_history_changed_fu holds 202 no and 42 yes. After a yes all 42 visits hold at least one answered question; after a no 28 of 202 (14%) do, and one holds all twelve: a "no change" does not make the questions below it no, and they are left as recorded. The 174 others leave the whole section empty, so an empty yearly section may mean "no change": it stays missing. The question is required and gates nothing. The inclusion visits hold 747 answers to it (723 dated 2014 to 2020) although the form 193 has no such question (it is commented out there): they are read and not delivered (somatic_history_changed_v0, keep: false). The change boxes of the other sections (groschang, acqchang and esichang of the form 244, answered to 2019 (groschang to 2020) and retired from the menu of the application (request A51); genchang of the form 247) gate nothing either. vaccinations.title: Vaccinations

asp.notes: Seven lines of the vaccination record, each with a vaccine and a box done or not done: 529 inclusion visits (356 of children) and 7 follow-up visits (2014 and 2015), from 2009 to 2026. Each line names a vaccine of the list of the form: diphtheria, tetanus, poliomyelitis, pertussis, BCG, measles, rubella and the code 8, "vaccin antivariolique", delivered as smallpox (24 lines on 23 inclusion visits of 2009 to 2019; the list of the current inclusion form has it commented out). 3420 lines hold a vaccine, on 523 visits. The box (vaccine_i_done) is done 1 or not done 0: 3375 lines are done and 29 not done; 32 lines hold a vaccine and no box, and 16 lines a box and no vaccine (14 of them the first line). A line is a position in the table, not a vaccine: the code equals the number of the line on 1748 of the 3420 lines (51%), and 95 visits repeat a vaccine on two lines. Read the vaccines of a visit as a set over the seven lines, not line by line. **Year and centre.** The share of inclusion visits with a vaccination line is 36% for the children and 12% for the adults and moves from year to year with no lasting step: 7% to 57% by year among the children and 1% to 41% among the adults (years with 30 visits or more).
