spq.title: Schizotypal Personality Questionnaire (SPQ)

asp.notes: Seventy-four items answered 0 or 1, nine sub-scale scores and a total: 138 inclusion visits (50 of children) and 71 follow-up visits, from 2009 to 2021 (199 of the 209 between 2013 and 2018). It belongs to the old set of forms. Identified from its name, its seventy-four items and its nine sub-scales as the Schizotypal Personality Questionnaire (Raine, 1991), sure: the nine stored scores have the items of the published sub-scales, in their order. The scores, each fitted on the data: - SPQ ideas of reference: the sum of 9 items (1, 10, 19, 28, 37, 45, 53, 60 and 63), equal to the stored score on 184 of 184 complete visits. - SPQ excessive social anxiety: the sum of 8 items (2, 11, 20, 29, 38, 46, 54 and 71), equal to the stored score on 184 of 184 complete visits. - SPQ odd beliefs or magical thinking: the sum of 7 items (3, 12, 21, 30, 39, 47 and 55), equal to the stored score on 184 of 184 complete visits. - SPQ unusual perceptual experiences: the sum of 9 items (4, 13, 22, 31, 40, 48, 56, 61 and 64), equal to the stored score on 184 of 184 complete visits. - SPQ odd or eccentric behaviour: the sum of 7 items (5, 14, 23, 32, 67, 70 and 74), equal to the stored score on 184 of 184 complete visits. - SPQ no close friends: the sum of 9 items (6, 15, 24, 33, 41, 49, 57, 62 and 66), equal to the stored score on 184 of 184 complete visits. - SPQ odd speech: the sum of 9 items (7, 16, 25, 34, 42, 50, 58, 69 and 72), equal to the stored score on 184 of 184 complete visits. - SPQ constricted affect: the sum of 8 items (8, 17, 26, 35, 43, 51, 68 and 73), equal to the stored score on 184 of 184 complete visits. - SPQ suspiciousness: the sum of 8 items (9, 18, 27, 36, 44, 52, 59 and 65), equal to the stored score on 184 of 184 complete visits. - SPQ total (0 to 74): the sum of 74 items, equal to the stored score on 184 of 184 complete visits. On 2 visits (2015 and 2016) an item is blank and scores are stored (the total on one, the excessive social anxiety sub-score on both): they cannot be recomputed and are not delivered (`score_not_recomputed`). **Year and centre.** 22 of the 84 variables reach 0.5 or more (19 by year, 15 by centre), 1 of the 10 scores (0.5 by centre). The age mix explains the centres: children are 90% of the visits of centre C, 3% of D and none of E; the median total is 23 in C and 33.5 in D (34 among the adults of D), E holds 16 visits and only D holds 20 values or more among adults. Between centres 43 of the 84 variables differ beyond chance (permutation test, p below 0.01); between years 1 does, none among children or among adults: no step. An instrument of the ASP cohort only.

systemizing_quotient.title: Systemizing Quotient (SQ)

asp.notes: Sixty items and a score, filled by adults: 166 inclusion visits (18 of children) and fewer than five follow-up visits, from 2012 to 2021 (156 of the 166 between 2013 and 2018). It belongs to the old set of forms. Identified from its name, its sixty items and its score as the Systemizing Quotient (Baron-Cohen and others, 2003), sure. The answers are stored from 1 (definitely agree) to 4 (definitely disagree), and the score is not their sum: an answer on the scored side counts 2 points when it is definite and 1 when it is slight. The key was fitted on the data and is the published one: agreement scores on 20 items (1, 4, 5, 7, 13, 15, 19, 20, 25, 29, 30, 33, 34, 37, 41, 44, 48, 49, 53 and 55), disagreement on 20 (6, 11, 12, 18, 23, 24, 26, 28, 31, 32, 35, 38, 40, 42, 43, 45, 51, 56, 57 and 60), and 20 items are not scored (2, 3, 8, 9, 10, 14, 16, 17, 21, 22, 27, 36, 39, 46, 47, 50, 52, 54, 58 and 59). It reproduces the stored score on 152 of 158 visits that hold the 40 scored items. The 6 visits that differ are all dated 2013 (two centres). One visit lacks one of the scored items and has a stored score: not recomputed. One score is typed without any item (2018) and is 145, above the maximum of 80: read out_of_range, so no score is delivered for it. **Year and centre.** 37 of the 61 variables reach 0.5 or more (31 by year, 29 by centre): 60 items answered 1 to 4 whose median moves by one unit; the score is at 0.18 by year and 0.28 by centre (median 28 in C, where children are 71% of the 24 visits, 34 in D and in E). Between years 3 of the 61 variables differ beyond chance among adults (permutation test, p below 0.01; about 0.6 expected), between centres 1: within chance. An instrument of the ASP cohort only.

tas20.title: Toronto Alexithymia Scale (TAS-20)

asp.notes: Twenty items answered from 1 to 5, three factor scores and a total: 33 inclusion visits (27 of children) and 8 follow-up visits, from 2013 to 2018 (32 of the 41 in 2013 and 2014). It belongs to the old set of forms; the children's alexithymia questionnaire and the BVAQ replace it in the new set. Identified from its name and its twenty items as the TAS-20 (Bagby and others, 1994), sure: the stored total and the externally oriented factor follow the published key, with its five reversed items (4, 5, 10, 18 and 19). **The two other stored factors swap the items 7 and 11**: the publication puts the item 7 in "identifying" and the item 11 in "describing". The script of the form (233_score.js) confirms it: it adds the item 7 to the describing score and the item 11 to the identifying score. The factors delivered follow the publication; two scores "as stored" reproduce the EMR to check the stored columns, and are not delivered. The scores, each fitted on the data: - TAS-20 difficulty describing feelings: the sum of 5 items (2, 4, 11, 12 and 17; reversed: 4); the stored score counts the item 7 for the item 11 (38 of 38 complete visits). - TAS-20 difficulty identifying feelings: the sum of 7 items (1, 3, 6, 7, 9, 13 and 14); the stored score counts the item 11 for the item 7 (38 of 38 complete visits). - TAS-20 externally oriented thinking: the sum of 8 items (5, 8, 10, 15, 16, 18, 19 and 20; reversed: 5, 10, 18 and 19), equal to the stored score on 38 of 38 complete visits. - TAS-20 total (20 to 100): the sum of 20 items (reversed: 4, 5, 10, 18 and 19), equal to the stored score on 38 of 38 complete visits. **Year and centre.** No year has 20 values (2013: 18, 2014: 14) and one centre has them (C, 35 of the 41 visits, children 91%): no year comparison, and the 3 items that reach 0.5 or more by centre (0.5 to 0.67) compare centre C with the overall median of a form that has 6 other visits. An instrument of the ASP cohort only.

tics.title: Tics (section of the old forms)

asp.notes: A checklist of motor and vocal tics answered from 1 to 3 (some lines with a description in free text), severity ratings for the last week and for the life, the age of onset, and the diagnosis of Tourette's disorder: 206 inclusion visits (48 of children) and 52 follow-up visits, from 2012 to 2021. It belongs to the old set of forms. The thesaurus calls the section "chronic motor and vocal tics" (form 216, "Tics moteurs et vocaux chroniques"): a checklist of 37 tics (1 to 24 motor, 25 to 37 vocal) answered 1 never, 2 in the past, 3 in the last week, then questions on multiple tics, the severity (in the last week and in the worst period of the life), the ages and the diagnosis. The labels give the wording of the form in short. Gates. The 13 description boxes of the checklist (free text) are filled under an answer 2 or 3 of their item (434 cells), never under 1, and under an empty item on 19 cells: they are delivered as written, with no shown_if (it would blank the 19). The question on a medication for tics (tourtt) asks about "tics and/or Tourette", wider than the Tourette diagnosis (tourdiag) that precedes it, so it is not asked_if the diagnosis (it is empty on the 209 visits that answer no to the diagnosis, and has one answer in all). The form offers the answers of the tic-free-period question (0 always tic-free to 5 never tic-free) to the two questions on the intensity of the tics in the worst period of the life (ticvie3 and ticvie4), copied from the two questions above them: the intensity questions of the last week (ticsem3 and ticsem4) have their own answers (0 absent to 5 severe). The two variables are delivered as written and labelled so. The ages are whole years: the export casts them with a rule that keeps only the cells made of digits, so a decimal or a word typed in an age is lost (request). **Year and centre.** 12 of the 76 variables reach 0.5 or more (12 by year, 4 by centre; 27 variables have a group of 20 values). A step with no known cause, by year: the 37 tics are answered 1 never, 2 in the past, 3 in the last week, and on the inclusion visits of adults the share of 'never' is 63% to 71% in 2013 to 2016 (mean answer 1.43 to 1.55), 76% and 78% in 2017 and 2018 (1.33, 1.31) and 93% in 2019 (1.12; 19 visits); it is 94% to 97% on the 48 follow-up visits of 2018 to 2020. 14 of the 54 variables differ between years beyond chance (permutation test, p below 0.01), 17 among adults and none among children (only two years hold 20 values of them), and 10 between centres, 6 among adults. The centres differ by age (children are 94% of the visits of C, 1% of D, none of E) but the step is among adults, and the form shows no change. The same fall of the yes is seen in the yes-or-no boxes of repetitive_behaviours (from the end of 2018) and in the box of MCDD (ticked on 86% of the visits of 2018 and 98% of 2019); the history gates of ANTECEDENTS fell from 2017 (D47 of PROGRESS.md). An instrument of the ASP cohort only.

asp.notes: Eight examinations, each with a code and a date, and an eye-tracking code: brain CT scan, brain MRI, EEG, karyotype, fragile X test, audiogram, auditory evoked potentials and another examination, on 1,004 inclusion visits (1,069 over all visits; 687 inclusion visits hold at least one result other than "not done"). A date is given with the code 1 on 103 rows and with the code 2 on 49, almost never with 9: which fits. "Not done" is an answer and is delivered as such, not as a missing value. The eye-tracking code is 9 on 446 of its 459 answers. The dates of the karyotype and of the fragile X test are centred on the day of the visit (a median of 0 days): the day itself on 96 and 98 rows, after it on 99 and 111, before it on 60 and 48; 31 more rows of the other examinations are dated after the visit. A date after the visit date is expected here, not an error. Three free texts name another examination and describe an anomaly. exchang is the box "changed since the last visit" of the follow-up form. The schema was written from the column names and the answers, then checked against the thesaurus V2.13, which names these columns (PROGRESS.md D13 and D14). An instrument of the ASP cohort only.

puberty_and_handedness.title: Handedness and Tanner stages

asp.notes: lateral is the handedness, on 996 visits (883 at inclusion, 113 at follow-up; right-handed on 836, 745 of them at inclusion), delivered with the names of FACE BP (right, left, both). The follow-up form 245 asks the same questions as the inclusion form 194 (codes as in the form and the thesaurus); 69 of the 76 follow-up answers of patients with an inclusion answer agree with it. Four stages of puberty from 1 to 5, read as the Tanner stages: tang and tanpg for the boys (tang on 292 visits, 222 at inclusion; 288 of them are boys), tans and tanpf for the girls (tans on 134 visits, 125 at inclusion; 132 girls). Which of each pair is the pubic hair is given by the thesaurus. They are filled for adults too. The form has no sex or age gate: the 4 boys' stages typed for girls and the 2 girls' stages typed for boys stay as recorded (R2). fnmchang is a box of the follow-up form 245 (98 visits, 2014 to 2024; 1 on 3 of them). It sits after the Tanner block and before the neurological examination, and the form does not say which block it covers (question M84): the label says so. The schema was written from the column names and the answers, then checked against the thesaurus V2.13, which names these columns (PROGRESS.md D13 and D14). An instrument of the ASP cohort only. Years and centres (definition of done, D88; centres lettered as in D77, A the children's centre): the Tanner stages of boys have a median of 1 in centre A (children only) and 4 to 5 elsewhere, and of 1 in 2018 and 2019, when A holds most visits: the age mix. Handedness has no step.

anxiety_disorders_fu.title: Anxiety disorders at the yearly follow-up visits

asp.notes: The anxiety part of the clinician's list of psychiatric comorbidities (the same table and forms as mood_disorders: form 202 at inclusion, form 348 at the yearly visits). A first question (tranxi, any anxiety disorder; 9 is a missing code) opens the disorders, each with an age at onset and a remission: panic disorder with agoraphobia (panag) and without (pansa), agoraphobia without panic disorder (agspa), social phobia (phso), specific phobia (phsp, five types), separation anxiety (anxsep), obsessive-compulsive disorder (toc, with a box 'treated with an SSRI' and the response), obsessive-compulsive symptoms (soc, with the age when the compulsions and the obsessions began), generalised anxiety (anxge) and post-traumatic stress (spt). The names come from the thesaurus V2.13 (PROGRESS.md D13 and D14). Gates. After a no to the first question the eight older sub-disorder questions are 0 (asked_if). Separation anxiety and post-traumatic stress have no rule: they are answered only after a yes to the first question (empty on all 650 visits with a no), but they exist only from 2020-21, so a rule would write 0 on the 321 visits with a no dated to 2020 where nothing was asked (PROGRESS.md D50). They were added late: the valid yes/no answers at inclusion are 1 visit in 2017, 1 in 2018, 3 and 2 in 2019, 18 and 14 in 2020 and 97 and 96 in 2021 (separation anxiety, post-traumatic stress); among the visits with an anxiety yes they are answered on 1, 1, 4 and 24 of 45, 71, 83 and 74 in 2017-2020 and on 86% to 92% (separation anxiety) and 86% to 99% (post-traumatic stress) from 2021 ('two more added in 2020' was wrong, and the labels say 'from 2021'). The ages and the remission stay missing after a no (a 0 on a remission would read 'disorder present, not in remission'); so do the five types of the specific phobia and the SSRI boxes. The 9 of the remission of separation anxiety is a missing code (the form offers 'Non connu'; none is on the column). Panic disorder. The form has a box with agoraphobia and one without. panic_disorder_<edition> is their highest where both are answered: 157 yes at inclusion and 4 at the yearly visits (161 in all); a visit with one box yes and the other empty or 'not known' is not scored (16 visits: 10 + 6; the highest of what is present would give 177 yes). It is the BP name and meaning (panic disorder, with or without agoraphobia). Names and joins. The stems are the BP and SZ ones with the ending of the form: anxiety_disorder, agoraphobia (agoraphobia without panic disorder), social_phobia, specific_phobia, ocd and ptsd, each with _onset_age, and panic_disorder (a score here, as in BP). They are catalogued with BP and SZ by the lead; the hard limit of the ages is 0 to 70 here (BP: 0 to 90), kept (the oldest patient is 65). Not joined: generalised_anxiety (BP's gad_v0 is the question about the current episode only, the ASP form has no such wording) and the remissions (the ASP question is the state now, BP's is the last month). The ages are now in years (unit); the data are unchanged. Two forms in the same columns, so two instruments (PROGRESS.md D49). The inclusion form and the yearly form hold the same questions and print no period, so a follow-up answer is an update given at that visit (BP decision D84): neither a history of the whole life nor strictly the time since the last visit, and not the BP or SZ 'since the last visit' (rule R22 of the review): the follow-up instrument is _fu without since_visit and is not joined with those. Within patients the follow-up answers do not repeat the inclusion ones. Over the six sections of the comorbidity forms (49 yes/no questions) there are 290 patient-question pairs with a yes at inclusion and a later answer, and the last later answer is no for 60 of them (21%; insomnia 9 of 20, reading disorder 4 of 4, recurrent depressive disorder 2 of 2); the ages at onset are given again in 110 of 114 pairs, and a count of episodes that is above 0 twice never falls (13 pairs: 8 equal, 5 higher). So the columns are two sets, _v0 (the screening and inclusion visits) and _fu (the yearly visits); visit_form says which form a visit used and is read from the visit label, as in the other twin schemas of the cohort (suicide_and_self_harm_v0, somatic_history_v0). An empty section at a yearly visit means 'no change' when the form has a change question, never 'no disorder' (rule R25 of the review). At the yearly visits. 71 follow-up visits answer at least one question: any anxiety disorder yes on 47 of 71; social phobia 17 of 66, specific phobia 24 of 64, obsessive-compulsive symptoms 20 of 62, generalised anxiety 17 of 66, agoraphobia 8 of 63, panic 2 and 3 of 63 and 64; separation anxiety 3 of 11 and post-traumatic stress 1 of 11. The change question of form 348 is delivered in mood_disorders_fu (axis1_summary_changed_fu), because it covers the whole of the axis I summary: an empty yearly section here means 'no change' (R25). Checks (aggregates). A first answer yes with no sub-disorder yes: 3 of 47, all three with the whole sub-section empty. **Year and centre.** 71 answers: at most two centres and one year hold 20 values, and the three variables that reach 0.5 or more (any anxiety disorder, specific phobia, obsessive-compulsive symptoms; yes 41% to 85% between the two centres for the first) are within chance on groups this small.

asdi.title: Asperger Syndrome Diagnostic Interview (ASDI)

asp.notes: Twenty items named asdi1 to asdi20, each answered 1 yes, 2 'a little' ('Oui, un peu'), 0 no or 9 'Non connu' (a missing code), with a box before them (asdinf, 'ASDI réalisé ?') and one after (asdicrit, 'Critères diagnostiques Asperger selon ASDI'): form 198, section G.1.3, table aut_c1cridsm. The items are answered on 423 visits (408 at inclusion, 15 at follow-up) from November 2009 to February 2026, on 79% of the inclusions to 2014 and 9% of those from 2021; 78% of the inclusion visits are adults. The schema is not split into _v0 and _fu (15 follow-up visits, same columns and meaning). Identified as the Asperger Syndrome (and high-functioning autism) Diagnostic Interview (Gillberg, Gillberg, Rastam and Wentz, 2001; the thesaurus confirms the instrument). The form groups the twenty items in six domains with the number of symptoms that each requires: social interaction (items 1 to 4, at least 2), narrow interests (5 to 7, at least 1), routines (8 and 9, at least 2), speech and language (10 to 14, at least 3), non-verbal communication (15 to 19, at least 1) and motor clumsiness (item 20, 1); all six must be met. The published rule for the routines domain is 'at least one of the two' in the secondary sources found (the form requires both); the 2001 paper and the 1991 chapter were not read, and the literature check of 2026-11-21 did not settle the primary rule, nor the split of the items (4, 3, 2, 5, 5, 1). The ASDI is built for informants who knew the person as a child. The answers are not in order: 1 is yes, 2 is 'a little' and 0 is no (the form and the dictionary agree). The data agree too (the criteria are met on 35% of the answers 0, 61% of the answers 2 and 67% of the answers 1), so the items are delivered as words (no, a_little, yes), not as numbers. The published answer options, and how a 'a little' counts, were not found in the literature check of 2026-11-21. No total exists and none is computed: asdinf is used by no script, and asdicrit is typed. Recomputing it with the form's own thresholds (2, 1, 2, 3, 1 and 1 across the six domains) on the 290 inclusion visits with the twenty items and the box agrees with the stored value on 199 visits when 'a little' counts as a symptom (214 if the routines domain needs only one of its two items) and on 161 when only 'yes' counts (176): the stored value follows no rule that reproduces it, and no score is proposed. 13 visits have the twenty items at no and asdicrit at 0 (the shortcut 'Non pour tous les critères', ASDIN, ticks no on the items and on the box). asdicrit is yes on 252 inclusion visits. asdinf ('ASDI done') is answered on 483 visits from December 2017 (yes on 149, the first in January 2018, no on 334); 279 visits with items hold no answer to it (233 dated to 2017, 46 from 2018 on), and items are filled on 7 visits where it says no. An instrument of the ASP cohort only. **Year and centre.** 2 of the 22 variables reach 1.0. The box 'interview done' (`asdinf`, from December 2017; 483 answers) is yes for 60% of the visits of 2020, 41%, 35%, 21%, 24% and 22% in 2021 to 2025, and 12% to 77% by centre (four centres with 20 answers): the habit of the centre. The conclusion box (`asdicrit`, 453 answers, 57% yes) runs from 38% to 87% by year (groups of 21 to 64) and from 42% to 83% by centre. The items show no step; the rule of the box is O28.

dsm_criteria.title: DSM criteria of the autism spectrum diagnosis

asp.notes: Ten yes/no boxes, cridsm17 to cridsm26, filled by the clinician in form 198 ('Critères DSM 5 autisme', table aut_c1cridsm, section G.1.1): 1,963 inclusion visits hold at least one of the ten, 1,831 of them all nine criteria, and the conclusion is on every one of the 2,318 inclusions; 19 follow-up visits hold the ten boxes too (17 conclusions yes, 2 no). 9 ('Inconnu') is a missing code. The schema is not split into _v0 and _fu: 19 follow-up visits against 1,963 at inclusion, with the same columns, the same wording and no change question. The count fits the DSM-5 criteria of autism spectrum disorder: three criteria of social communication (A1 to A3, cridsm17 to cridsm19), four of restricted and repetitive behaviours (B1 to B4, cridsm20 to cridsm23), the early onset (C) and the impairment (D) (cridsm24, cridsm25), then a conclusion (cridsm26). The names come from the thesaurus V2.13 (PROGRESS.md D13 and D14). cridsm26 equals the column arm for 2,318 of 2,318 patients: it is the diagnosis of the cohort (identite). The nine criteria are all yes for 944 patients. The conclusion is typed, not computed. The application has no script for form 198 (js_scores holds none; the only script on these fields is the shortcut below). The headings printed on the form say that A is 'manifested in the three cases' and B 'at least two' of the four, and the line above the conclusion says 'tick yes if the criteria A, B, C and D are met'; but the instruction at the top (198.php:12) is the DSM-IV counting ('6 items or more yes in A: at least 2 in (1), at least 1 in (2), 1 in (3), at least one in B and C'), left from the old form, and may steer the raters. The published DSM-5 rule is all three A criteria, at least two of the four B criteria, C and D (American Psychiatric Association 2013; recalled: the DSM-5 text was not read, and the literature check of 2026-11-21 did not settle it). On the 1,831 inclusion visits with all nine criteria the conclusion differs from that rule on 138 (133 yes with the criteria not met, 5 no with all of them met); a plain '6 of 9' rule would differ on 51. The conclusion is delivered as typed. The shortcut. iq_assessment.title: Intellectual assessment: date, age and general ability index

asp.notes: The summary of the intellectual assessment that the clinician copies into the medical evaluation (form 119, typed numbers, no script): the date of the assessment, the age at the assessment in years and months, a box "assessment done" and the general ability index (iag). The box "an IQ was already done" (qirea): 795 inclusion answers (yes 514, no 254, 9 read as "not known" 27) and 87 at follow-up visits, filled from 2010 and mostly from 2013 to 2020 (four answers in 2021, one in 2025): the radio is commented out of form 119 (119.php:9), so it left the form around 2021. It does not tell whether an assessment exists: it says no on 268 visits, 205 of which hold an index of one of the three editions. The date (qi_date, "date de passation"): 1,957 non-empty cells, of which 262 hold 0000-00-00 (the empty date of the export, silently empty; 184 of these visits hold an index) and 2 are out of range (1921 and 2107): 1,693 dates are delivered. (The earlier note said 1,866: that is the number of non-empty V0 cells, the 262 empty dates included.) The date is the date to which the indices belong: the norm tables of the application read the age at this date, so the indices of wais4_indices, wisc4_indices and wisc5_indices describe the assessment, not the visit. The edition boxes agree with the age at the assessment only in part: the WISC-IV is ticked on 37 visits of patients aged 18 or more at the visit and the WISC-V on 19 (5 and 2 of those with a date were 18 or more at the assessment), and 10 WAIS-IV assessments are dated under the age of 16. The general ability index (iag, "indice d'aptitude generale"): 675 visits, all inclusion visits (301 of children), one dated 2016 and the others from 2018 on; 666 are delivered, 9 are outside 40 to 160 (8 below 40, one above 160: out_of_range). The form has one field IAG for the three editions of the Wechsler scales, so the index cannot be tied to an edition. The GAI of the WAIS-IV is made of three verbal and three perceptual subtests (Canivez 2010); the composition of the French IAG of the WISC-IV and of the WISC-V, and whether the French WISC-V has one, were not settled by the literature check of 2026-11-21 (scale_reference.md, section 22). The indices themselves are in three instruments, one per edition of the Wechsler scales: wisc4_indices, wisc5_indices and wais4_indices. The schema was written from the column names and the answers, then checked against the thesaurus V2.13, which names these columns (PROGRESS.md D13 and D14). An instrument of the ASP cohort only. **Year and centre.** 3 of the 5 variables reach 0.5 or more. 'Assessment done' is yes for 90% of the children and 47% of the adults, 26% to 89% by centre (age mix, habit of the centre); the age at the assessment is 12 years in children and 24 in adults. **The general ability index** (675 visits, 666 delivered) is 107 in children and 114 in adults and 110 to 116 in five centres, but 66 in one (81 values, all children, 75 of them from 2023; quartiles 53 and 104): at the visits of that centre where the WISC-V full-scale IQ is typed too (80 pairs) the index is 46 points below it (median difference, correlation 0.43), against +2 points and 0.97 elsewhere (140 pairs). The field holds another number there (a sum of scaled scores, or an index of another edition: O32). The values between 40 and 160 are delivered as typed; the 9 out of range (below 40 or above 160) are removed. The state of the field is a documented step with no known cause.

learning_difficulties_fu.title: Reading, spelling, mathematics and writing difficulties at the yearly follow-up visits

asp.notes: Four questions of the clinician (form 120, table aut_c1trappr, 'Trouble spécifique des apprentissages avec déficit'; 9 'Non connu' is a missing code): a specific learning disorder with impairment in reading (retlec), in written expression (orth) or in mathematics (math), and dysgraphia (ecri), each with two radios after a yes: it interfered with school or daily life (ending vi) and an assessment or re-education by a professional (ending reed; a speech therapist, except for dysgraphia, where the form says 'un professionnel'). The form carries an older, narrower wording in its other language slot (reading delay in childhood, 8 to 18 years; spelling and mathematics difficulties 'âge + 8 ans'; writing difficulties 8 to 18 years): the current label is the DSM-5 disorder, with no age window. The names come from the thesaurus V2.13 (PROGRESS.md D13 and D14). The same twelve columns exist without the ending _med in the table autoquestionnaires: exact copies, not loaded (ignored.yaml). The two boxes after the disorder stay missing after a no (they are details of a disorder that is absent, R1). Not joined. The reviewed learning_disorders (neuropsychology tab, trbapp01 to trbapp10, asked before the assessment) holds other questions in other columns: reading difficulty here and dyslexia agree on 598 of the 630 visits where both are answered (writing and dysorthographia 588 of 640, mathematics and dyscalculia 596 of 637); the stuttering of the developmental part and trbapp07 agree on 186 of 196. The questions are close but are not the same, so the names are not shared. Two forms in the same columns, so two instruments (PROGRESS.md D49). The inclusion form and the yearly form hold the same questions and print no period, so a follow-up answer is an update given at that visit (BP decision D84): neither a history of the whole life nor strictly the time since the last visit, and not the BP or SZ 'since the last visit' (rule R22 of the review): the follow-up instrument is _fu without since_visit and is not joined with those. Within patients the follow-up answers do not repeat the inclusion ones. Over the six sections of the comorbidity forms (49 yes/no questions) there are 290 patient-question pairs with a yes at inclusion and a later answer, and the last later answer is no for 60 of them (21%; insomnia 9 of 20, reading disorder 4 of 4, recurrent depressive disorder 2 of 2); the ages at onset are given again in 110 of 114 pairs, and a count of episodes that is above 0 twice never falls (13 pairs: 8 equal, 5 higher). So the columns are two sets, _v0 (the screening and inclusion visits) and _fu (the yearly visits); visit_form says which form a visit used and is read from the visit label, as in the other twin schemas of the cohort (suicide_and_self_harm_v0, somatic_history_v0). An empty section at a yearly visit means 'no change' when the form has a change question, never 'no disorder' (rule R25 of the review). At the yearly visits. 77 follow-up visits answer at least one question. Yes: reading 2 of 74, written expression 11 of 74, mathematics 2 of 71 and dysgraphia 27 of 72. The form has no change question. **Year and centre.** 77 visits: at most one year or one centre holds 20 values: there is nothing to screen.

psychotic_symptoms_fu.title: Psychotic symptoms and schizophrenia at the yearly follow-up visits

asp.notes: The psychotic part of the clinician's list of psychiatric comorbidities (the same table and forms as mood_disorders: form 202 at inclusion, form 348 at the yearly visits; 9 'Non connu' is a missing code). A first question (symppsyh, psychotic symptoms) opens four groups, each a yes/no with boxes: delusions (idel, four mechanisms: intuitive, hallucinatory, interpretative, imaginative), hallucinations (hal, five senses), disorganisation (diss, 'dissociation' in the French sense, three mechanisms: thought blocking, diffluence, morbid rationalism) and deficit symptoms (def: blunted affect, poverty of speech, athymhormia), then the onset (acute, progressive) and the course (chronic, intermittent, episodic) of the symptoms. A second question (tskizo) is a schizophrenia spectrum disorder, with five type boxes, an age at the first episode, a number of episodes, an age at the first treatment and a remission, filled for fewer than five patients; the duration of the longest episode (durepilg, months) is in the form and the export, but its column is empty on all 4,500 rows (ignored.yaml). The names come from the thesaurus V2.13 (PROGRESS.md D13 and D14). Gates. The yes/no of the four groups (delusions, hallucinations, disorganisation, deficit symptoms) hangs on the first question (symppsyh) and is 0 after a no (asked_if; 1,502 visits with a no, 6,008 cells that were missing: 1,438 at inclusion and 64 at the yearly visits, four questions each; the extraction leaves them empty and no cell is filled under a no). The mechanisms and senses under a group, the type boxes and the remission stay missing after a no: they are details of a symptom that is absent (R1). The rule is one level deep: 9 mechanism cells are filled while their group question is empty (all 0, none positive; the four group questions are empty on 7, 5, 10 and 11 visits with the first question yes), and none is filled under a no. Not joined with SZ. The SZ list of symptoms (lifetime_symptoms, ever and last month, many more items) asks other questions in another window: symptom_hallucination_bodily_* is the cenesthetic hallucinations here, symptom_alogia_* the poverty of speech and symptom_avolition_* the athymhormia, with other wording; no variable is shared. Two forms in the same columns, so two instruments (PROGRESS.md D49). The inclusion form and the yearly form hold the same questions and print no period, so a follow-up answer is an update given at that visit (BP decision D84): neither a history of the whole life nor strictly the time since the last visit, and not the BP or SZ 'since the last visit' (rule R22 of the review): the follow-up instrument is _fu without since_visit and is not joined with those. Within patients the follow-up answers do not repeat the inclusion ones. Over the six sections of the comorbidity forms (49 yes/no questions) there are 290 patient-question pairs with a yes at inclusion and a later answer, and the last later answer is no for 60 of them (21%; insomnia 9 of 20, reading disorder 4 of 4, recurrent depressive disorder 2 of 2); the ages at onset are given again in 110 of 114 pairs, and a count of episodes that is above 0 twice never falls (13 pairs: 8 equal, 5 higher). So the columns are two sets, _v0 (the screening and inclusion visits) and _fu (the yearly visits); visit_form says which form a visit used and is read from the visit label, as in the other twin schemas of the cohort (suicide_and_self_harm_v0, somatic_history_v0). An empty section at a yearly visit means 'no change' when the form has a change question, never 'no disorder' (rule R25 of the review). At the yearly visits. 68 follow-up visits answer at least one question: psychotic symptoms yes on 3 of 67 answers (both of the 2 patients with a yes at inclusion and a later answer say yes again), delusions 1, hallucinations 2, disorganisation 1 and deficit symptoms 0 among 67 valid answers; schizophrenia spectrum 0 of 68. The change question of form 348 is in mood_disorders_fu (axis1_summary_changed_fu); an empty yearly section here means 'no change' (R25). **Year and centre.** No variable has a year or a centre with 20 values (68 visits): there is nothing to screen.

substance_use.title: Substance use disorders at inclusion (clinician's list)

asp.notes: The clinician's list of psychiatric comorbidities, substance part (form 202 at inclusion, form 348 at follow-up). A first question, "trouble d'utilisation de substances" (utisubst), opens nine substances: tobacco, alcohol, benzodiazepines, cannabis, psychostimulants, cocaine, hallucinogens, androgenic steroids (the column utiste: the form says "steroides androgenes") and solvents. The form hides all of them after a no or a not known (eASPERGER.js:5533-5535). For each substance: a level coded 0 no, 1 abuse, 2 dependence or 9 not known, then the age at onset (tobacco: the age at the start of smoking) and a status coded 1 past or 2 current (steroids have no age and no status in the extraction). Two forms in the same columns, as for the suicide questions. The inclusion form is delivered here, in variables ending in _v0, on the V0 visits only (1,538 answers: yes 142, no 1,381, not known 15; the screening visits hold none). The follow-up form (348) is read by variables that are not delivered (substance_disorder_fu and the _fu twins, keep: false): 70 follow-up answers, 69 no and one yes, whose substance cells (9 levels, 4 ages or statuses) are the only filled ones; they are not delivered because 70 answers do not make an instrument, and the coverage check counts them as read. The change box of form 348 (RESCHANG, filled on 212 follow-up visits) heads the whole axis I section and is delivered with it, not here. There is no _fu schema. The substances are 0 after a no. After a no to the opening question the nine substance boxes, ages and statuses are empty in the extraction (0 of the 1,381 inclusion no answers hold one), because the form hides them: each substance has a second variable, `<substance>_disorder_v0`, that reads the same column once more (separator, codes 0 no, 1 and 2 yes, so that abuse and dependence are one yes) and is 0 after a no (`asked_if: substance_disorder_v0`; 1,381 cells per substance, 12,429 in all; a not known stays missing, the ages and statuses stay missing after a no). Where a substance has the same name as in BP (alcohol, cannabis, cocaine, stimulant, hallucinogen) the question is the same as BP's abuse or dependence. The benzodiazepines are narrower than BP's sedatives, hypnotics and anxiolytics and the solvents are one of the substances of BP's "other substance": they keep names of their own, as the tobacco (a schema of its own in BP and SZ, not a disorder) and the steroids. ASP has no question on opiates. The three-level answers are delivered too (`<substance>_use_disorder_v0`: no, abuse, dependence). The age is the age at onset of the disorder. The form says "age de debut de l'alcoolisme", "age de debut du tabagisme" and "age de debut"; the dictionary says the same. The alcohol median is 18.5 (42 answers), as the SZ onset of the use disorder (18, 281 answers) and not the SZ age at the first use (15, 465): the variables are named `_onset_age_v0` as in BP and SZ (they were `_first_age`). The cells at inclusion: tobacco 68, alcohol 42, cannabis 40, cocaine 7, stimulants 6, hallucinogens 2, benzodiazepines 9 (and one at a follow-up visit), solvents 2; the largest age is 46. The tobacco age of this form is `smoking_start_age_clinician`: the tobacco examination of the clinical tab (tobacco.yaml) asks the same thing as `smoking_start_age`; the two are equal on 12 of the 13 visits that have both, and the name of the examination is kept. SZ's tobacco_first_age is the age at the first cigarette, another question: the names must not meet. The status (past or current) is another question than BP's "in the past month" (`_last_month_v0`): it keeps its name. The ages and the statuses are details of a substance, and stay missing after a no (R1): 174 of the 176 ages sit under an abuse or a dependence (one under a not known, one under an empty level) and 89 of the 263 abuse or dependence answers have no age; 225 of the 240 statuses sit under an abuse or a dependence (8 under a no, 4 under a not known, 3 under an empty level) and 38 of those 263 have none. Nothing is blanked. Almost all the answers are those of adults (128 of 137 for tobacco). Tobacco: 0 on 38 inclusion visits (39 with the follow-up one), abuse on 12, dependence on 86. The utiste columns for the age and the status (utisteag, utistest) are empty on every row (ignored.yaml). Of the 142 yes answers to the opening question, 140 have at least one substance answered. The schema was written from the column names and the answers, then checked against the thesaurus V2.13, which names these columns (PROGRESS.md D13 and D14) and against forms 202 and 348. An instrument of the ASP cohort only; its names follow BP's substance_v0 where the question is the same. **Year and centre.** No variable reaches 0.5, but the screen is not defined for a yes under 25%, so the rates were read directly: the opening question is yes for 1% of the children and 18% of the adults (age mix), 0% to 39% by centre (eight centres) and 0% to 26% by year (14 years); alcohol 0% to 16% by centre, cannabis 0% to 18%, tobacco 0% to 29%. The list is answered on 91% of the inclusions of 2013, 64% to 80% in 2018 to 2022 and 43% to 63% in 2023 to 2026 (M71).

suicide_and_self_harm_fu.title: Suicide attempts and self-injurious behaviour at the follow-up visits (the lifetime form asked again)

asp.notes: The same two questions at the follow-up visits (form 203, one form for all the visits): 124 answers, 4 of them yes for a suicide attempt and 21 for self-injurious behaviour. They are the columns of suicide_and_self_harm_v0, read on the follow-up visits only and named like it, with the ending _fu: `isf05_lifetime_fu` (as DR's follow-up ISF), `first_attempt_age_fu`, `last_attempt_age_fu`, `n_attempts_fu`, `serious_suicide_attempt_fu` and the four `self_harm_*_fu`. The period. The section of the form is titled LIFETIME at every visit and the questions print no period, so the form does not ask "since the last visit" as the BP and SZ follow-up forms do (R22): the names end _fu and not _since_visit, and the answers are not joined with those of BP and SZ (`n_suicide_attempts_since_visit` is DR's different question, the clinician's summary of the course). Within patients the follow-up answers do not repeat the inclusion ones, so raters read the question as "since the last visit" or as "now": of the 7 follow-up answers of patients with a suicide attempt at inclusion, 2 say yes and 5 no; of the 45 of patients with self-injurious behaviour at inclusion, 20 say yes and 25 no (open question O9, closed as to the wording, open as to what the raters meant). The change question. The form shows "changement depuis la derniere visite" (OTRCHANG) from the third visit type only, and it is mandatory there (203.php:92, eASPERGER.js:688-700); another schema reads it (the sleep and self-injury block, table aut_c1trsomm). It does not stop the questions below it: of the 150 follow-up visits that say no change, 93 still answer the attempt question (the same 93 answer the self-injury question); of the 34 that say change, 31 answer; of the 189 with the box empty, none. An empty follow-up answer therefore means that nothing was asked or typed, and a no is an answer. The serious attempt is never filled under a no (0 of 120 follow-up visits that say no): it is 0 after a no (`asked_if: isf05_lifetime_fu`, +120 cells), as the number of attempts. The ages are details and stay missing. Ages are 0 to 99 in years and the number of attempts 0 to 50, as in the other cohorts (three answers of each here). The schema was written from the column names and the answers, then checked against the thesaurus V2.13, which names these columns (PROGRESS.md D13 and D14). An instrument of the ASP cohort only. **Year and centre.** No variable has a year or a centre with 20 values (124 answers): there is nothing to screen.

suicide_and_self_harm_v0.title: Suicide attempts and self-injurious behaviour in the life (inclusion form)

asp.notes: Two questions of the clinician at the inclusion visit (form 203, "Autres troubles associes", section G.4.2 "Conduites auto-agressives (LIFETIME)"), answered on 1,671 V0 visits for the first (9 is read as "not known", 13 times) and 1,680 for the second: a suicide attempt (yes on 191 visits), with the age at the first and at the most recent attempt (168 and 114 answers), their number (156) and whether one was serious (186); self-injurious behaviour (auag, yes on 365 visits), with the age at the first one and its kind at the first episode and now (biting, hitting oneself, scratching, burning, cutting, amputation). The screening visits hold none. Names (clinical scales review). The question is the one of the ISF in the other cohorts: `isf05_lifetime` is the name BP, SZ and DR give to "attempted suicide, ever", and `n_attempts` to the number of attempts. The form words the question "conduites suicidaires" (suicidal behaviour; the thesaurus too) and its details "TS", the French abbreviation of a suicide attempt: the names follow the details. The yes rate is 11.5% (191 of 1,658 answers), 15.0% in adults (161 of 1,071) and 5.1% in children (30 of 587), against 38% of the BP inclusions: the populations differ, and whether the question is answered as an attempt only is not known (question to the clinicians). `serious_suicide_attempt` keeps a name of its own: the form gives no definition of "grave", it is not BP's "intensive care" attempt. `self_harm` has no equivalent in the other cohorts (it is not the C-SSRS self-injurious item). The questions hang on a yes. The form hides the ages, the number and the serious attempt after a no or a not known (eASPERGER.js:5960-5973), and the kind and the age of the self-injurious behaviour after its no (5974-5983). The serious attempt is never filled under a no: 0 of 1,467 inclusion visits that say no, so it is 0 after a no (`asked_if: isf05_lifetime`, +1,467 cells; a not known stays missing), as the number of attempts already was. The ages, kinds and the age of the first self-injury are details: they stay missing after a no. Two forms share these columns. At follow-up the same form 203 is shown with a question "changement depuis la derniere visite" (OTRCHANG, shown from the third visit type only and mandatory there: 203.php:92, eASPERGER.js:688-700); the answers of the follow-up visits are in suicide_and_self_harm_fu, which keeps `_fu` names and not `since_visit`: the form is titled LIFETIME at every visit, unlike the BP and SZ follow-up forms (R22). The ranges: ages 0 to 99 in years (the largest answer is 50), the number of attempts 0 to 50 as in the other cohorts (the largest is 30). No cell changes. The schema was written from the column names and the answers, then checked against the thesaurus V2.13, which names these columns (PROGRESS.md D13 and D14). An instrument of the ASP cohort only. **Year and centre.** 3 of the 9 variables reach 0.5 or more, all ages: the first attempt at 13 years in children and 17 in adults, the last attempt at 13.5 and 20.5, the first self-harm at 8 and 15 (age mix; the first attempt is 15 to 20 years by centre). The question of the attempt (11.5% yes) has no defined shift (yes under 25%); it is 15.0% yes in adults and 5.1% in children, and the BP comparison is O30.

The three cohorts deliver it from the inclusion visit only, where it is about the whole life; the follow-up visits are in suicide_attempts_since_visit in BP and SZ, and in suicide_attempts_fu in DR (the lifetime form asked again at 24 and 48 months: not joined). vineland.title: Vineland Adaptive Behavior Scales

asp.notes: The scores of the Vineland scales, as copied into the medical evaluation (form 119): a box "done" (yes on 964 of the 1,613 inclusion answers; 9 is read as "not known"), the date, the age in months, then for each of eleven sub-domains a score and an age equivalent in months, the standard score of the four domains (communication, daily living skills, socialisation, motor skills), their sum and the adaptive behaviour composite. Raw scores are on 956 inclusion visits and 162 follow-up visits (954 and 161 hold a standard score, the sum or the composite); the age equivalents are on 463 visits; the motor domain, meant for young children, on 10. Nothing is computed by the application. The script 119_score.js (lines 8-82) would put the sums of the sub-domain raw scores and of the sub-domain age equivalents into the fields that the form labels standard scores of the domains, and it never runs: the call is commented out in eASPERGER.js:3951, the global age-equivalent field SCGLOBA is commented out of the form (119.php:110) and the script of the follow-up form (349_score.js) does not exist. The domain standard scores, their sum and the composite are typed by the clinician, so the stored sum is delivered as typed (`vineland_sum_standard`) and is NOT recomputed (rule R18, "no application formula"): a recomputed sum would gain 134 delivered cells, lose 36 and change 30 (127, 32 and 41 on the raw cells), and disagree with the composite on 19 visits where the stored sum fits it. The check (vineland_sum_check, not delivered) adds the standard scores of the communication, daily living and socialisation domains, and the motor domain when it is there (three of the four are enough), and compares the result with the stored sum. The stored sum equals the sum of the three domains on 902 of the 943 visits that hold the four numbers. The 41 others are: 7 that include the motor domain (the sum of the four domains, in children of about 6.5 years: the check agrees with them since the motor domain is added), 7 where the sum and the composite are swapped (the composite holds the sum of the three domains and the stored sum is below 60: one centre, 2019-2020; 6 of the swapped composites lie inside 20 to 160 and cannot be told in YAML), 4 with a domain score below 20 (removed, not comparable) and 23 that remain. On the delivered table the mismatches fall from 30 (41 less the 7 swapped sums, which are out of range and removed, and the 4 below 20) to 23. Of the 23, the composite is within 3 points of the relation (read on the 902 agreeing visits) for the stored sum on 19 (for that sum only on 13: a domain score is probably wrong), for the sum of the domains on 8 (for that sum only on 2: the stored sum is wrong) and for neither on 2. Thirty-two stored sums have no socialisation score; the composite fits the relation within 3 points on 30 of them, so the stored sum is probably right there. The published scales (Sparrow, Cicchetti and Balla 2005, Vineland-II; the manual was not read, the rules come from a trial analysis plan and a Pearson page): the domain and composite standard scores run from 20 to 160; the composite is read from the sum of the domain standard scores, the motor domain being in it below 7 years only, which is the 7 sums above. The French brochure also gives the motor domain for adults over 50; whether the French composite counts it then was not settled by the literature check of 2026-11-21. The sub-domain raw scores of this form stop at 40, 108, 50 (communication), 82, 48, 88 (daily living), 76, 62, 60 (socialisation) and 80, 72 (motor), the number of points of the items of that edition (Vineland-II): 8 raw scores are above their limit (the largest are 138 and 143) and are removed. One age equivalent is above 300 months (the largest is 412) and is removed. The age equivalents are in months (unit: months); published, they cannot be added or averaged (Pearson). The age at the Vineland (vineland_age_months) is typed in months: 8 values below 40 are the age in years (within a year of the age at the date), and 22 differ from the age at the date of the Vineland by more than 2 years. Quality: three centres hold 1,053 of the 1,078 socialisation scores. The median socialisation standard score of the children (under 18) is 76 up to 2017 (112 visits), 45 in 2018-2021 (319) and 63 from 2022 (425): the raw scores do not move, so it is not case-mix, and the cause is not known (see Year and centre, below). Identified as the second edition (Vineland-II): the largest score found in each of the nine sub-domains is the number of points of its items in that edition. Standard scores, age equivalents and the composite need the norm tables of the test, which are not available: they are delivered as typed. The same 42 columns exist a second time in the extraction, without the ending _med, in the table autoquestionnaires: exact copies on every row, not loaded (ignored.yaml). An instrument of the ASP cohort only. **Year and centre.** 17 of the 31 variables reach 0.5 or more (7 by year, 15 by centre). The age mix explains most of the shifts by centre: the box 'done' is yes for 96% of the children and 27% of the adults, the raw scores of the sub-domains are higher in adults (written 46 against 39, community 75 against 59) and the age at the Vineland is 155 months in children and 252 in adults; three centres hold 1,053 of the 1,078 socialisation scores, and the children's scores up to 2017 come from one centre (109 of 112). **A step with no known cause**: in children the raw scores do not move (the median receptive raw score is 33 to 37 in every year from 2013 to 2026, written 33 to 42, play 41 to 51), but the typed standard scores of the domains fall in 2018-2021 and return from 2022: socialisation 76 to 2017 (112 visits), 45 in 2018-2021 (319) and 63 from 2022 (425), communication 77, 68 and 76, daily living 76, 74 and 84, the composite 74, 57 and 69. The two centres that hold the children's scores from 2018 both type socialisation 41 and 48 in 2018-2021 and 63 and 61 from 2022, so case-mix does not fit; a change of the table or of the rule that converts the raw score is possible and the scores are typed (the script never runs, A67). The standard score 20, the lowest of the scale, is typed for 163 of 1,074 socialisation scores (15%; among the children none to 2017, 58 of 319 in 2018-2021, 46 of 425 from 2022) and 80 of 974 composites. The age equivalents (463 visits: 2013 to 2015 and 2018 to 2025) run from 57 to 102 months by year among the children, highest in 2014-2015 (78 and 102) and lowest in 2020 (57). The cause is not known (O31).

Nothing is computed by the application.
vineland.version: Vineland-II (second edition), identified from the largest raw score of each sub-domain
vineland.reference: Sparrow SS, Cicchetti DV, Balla DA. Vineland Adaptive Behavior Scales, Second Edition. Pearson/AGS 2005; French: Echelles de comportement adaptatif de Vineland-II (ECPA/Pearson)
vineland.reference_confidence: confirmed in source (publisher pages, trial plan); manual unread; French edition year (2015?) to verify
flags: Nothing is computed: the domain standard scores, their sum and the composite are typed, and the norm tables of the test are not available to check them.

A step with no known cause: in children the raw scores do not move over the years, but the typed standard scores fall in 2018 to 2021 and return in part from 2022 (median socialisation 76 to 2017, 45 in 2018 to 2021, 63 from 2022; composite 74, 57 and 69). Case-mix does not fit; a change of the table or of the rule that converts the raw score is possible.
The standard score 20, the lowest of the scale, is typed for 15% of the socialisation scores (none among the children to 2017).

The sum holds three domains, or four with the motor domain in young children: the two are not comparable. On 23 visits the stored sum differs from the sum of the domain scores, and on a few visits the sum and the composite were typed in each other's field (6 such composites lie inside 20 to 160 and are delivered).
The age equivalents are on 463 visits only and the motor domain on 10.

wais4_indices.title: WAIS-IV: the four indices and the full-scale IQ

asp.notes: The indices of the Wechsler Adult Intelligence Scale, fourth edition: verbal comprehension, perceptual reasoning, working memory, processing speed and the full-scale IQ, as the clinician copied them into the medical evaluation (form 119; typed numbers, no script). A box says that this edition was used (wai4: yes on 1,043 of the 1,750 inclusion answers, 1,053 visits in all); the indices are filled only after a yes (1,041 visits hold one, all with the box ticked, 9 of them follow-up visits). The first index is on 987 inclusion visits (75 children, 912 adults), from 2012 to 2026; the full-scale IQ on 788. The full-scale IQ is typed whether or not the indices agree. The form says it in red: "Le QIT est a renseigner meme s'il est heterogene" (119.php:8; the radio "homogene / heterogene" is commented out, line 51). Yet it is missing on 193 of the 974 visits that hold the four indices (20%); the median spread between the highest and the lowest index is 29 points where the full-scale IQ is typed and 31 where it is missing, so the idea that it is left out when the indices differ too much is not supported (the WISC-IV differs, see wisc4_indices). It is more than 10 points outside all four indices on 4 visits (typed against the profile). One schema per edition: an index of one edition is never delivered in the column of another. The medical evaluation holds the indices and no sum of scaled scores to read them with in the norm tables: they are delivered as typed. Hard limits as in the neuropsychology schemas for the same indices: 45 to 155 for verbal comprehension and perceptual reasoning, 50 to 150 for working memory and processing speed, 40 to 160 for the full-scale IQ (the full-scale IQ range is Canivez 2010; the ranges of the four indices were not found for the WAIS-IV in any source read by the literature check of 2026-11-21: scale_reference.md, section 22). Four typed values are below the limits (one verbal comprehension, one perceptual reasoning, one processing speed and one full-scale IQ) and are removed (out_of_range): the limits change no cell. Edition against age. The box is ticked for adults almost always (975 of 1,053 visits are aged 18 or more at the visit) and 10 assessments are dated when the patient was under 16: the indices belong to the date of the assessment (iq_assessment_date), not to the visit. The French WAIS-IV is normed from 16 years. Five visits tick two editions (four the WAIS-IV and the WISC-IV, one the WAIS-IV and the WISC-V): read the box of each schema. The clinician's copy against the neuropsychology form. The same indices, recomputed from the sums of the neuropsychology form, are in wais4_efficience.yaml and wais4_code_symboles_ivt.yaml, under the names that BP, SZ and DR give them (wais4_icv_index, wais4_irp_index, wais4_imt_index, wais4_ivt_index, wais4_qit); the names of this copy end in _clinician so that the two do not share a column. Where both exist they agree on 162 of 187 visits for verbal comprehension, 157 of 188 for perceptual reasoning, 176 of 192 for working memory, 185 of 206 for processing speed and 120 of 159 for the full-scale IQ (the clinician's copy against the recomputed index of the form). The agreement does not depend on the gap between the dates of the two assessments: for verbal comprehension 83 of 96 are equal within 31 days and 25 of 28 further apart; 28 of the 39 full-scale IQ differences are 2 points or less. The copy has 808 to 819 visits per index (628 for the full-scale IQ) that the neuropsychology form lacks, and 15 to 56 the other way round. Both are kept (D28). The schema was written from the column names and the answers, then checked against the thesaurus V2.13, which names these columns (PROGRESS.md D13 and D14). An instrument of the ASP cohort only. **Year and centre.** 1 of the 6 variables reaches 1.0: the box 'WAIS-IV done' is yes for 89% of the adults and 11% of the children, 1% to 100% by centre and 30% to 71% by year: the box follows the age and the share of children differs by centre and year (age mix). The five indices show no shift of 0.5.

Typed numbers; nothing is computed.

wisc4_indices.title: WISC-IV: the four indices and the full-scale IQ

asp.notes: The indices of the Wechsler Intelligence Scale for Children, fourth edition: verbal comprehension, perceptual reasoning, working memory, processing speed and the full-scale IQ, as the clinician copied them into the medical evaluation (form 119; typed numbers, no script). A box says that this edition was used (wis4: yes on 155 of the 1,208 inclusion answers, 215 visits in all); the indices are filled only after a yes (213 visits hold one). The first index is on 151 inclusion visits (115 children, 36 adults), from 2013 to 2026, and 59 follow-up visits hold one; the full-scale IQ is on 81. The full-scale IQ is typed whether or not the indices agree (the form says so in red: 119.php:8) and is missing on 119 of the 198 visits that hold the four indices (60%). Here the spread is larger where it is missing: the median distance between the highest and the lowest index is 37 points against 24 where it is typed, so for this edition the raters may well leave it out of a heterogeneous profile (the WAIS-IV and the WISC-V show hardly any difference); no value is typed more than 10 points outside all its indices. One schema per edition: an index of one edition is never delivered in the column of another. The indices need the norm tables of the test, which are not available: they are delivered as typed. Each index has its own hard limits: 45 to 155 for the four indices and 40 to 160 for the full-scale IQ, the ranges that Pearson gives for the WISC-V (WISC-V interpretive report sample, 2020) and Canivez and Watkins (2016); no source read by the literature check of 2026-11-21 states them for the WISC-IV (scale_reference.md, section 22). No typed value falls outside them (the lowest index is 45, the highest 155, the full-scale IQ runs from 40 to 158), so the limits change no cell. Edition against age: the box is ticked on 37 visits of patients aged 18 or more at the visit, but only 5 of the 34 with a date of assessment were 18 or more on that date (iq_assessment_date): the indices belong to that date, not to the visit. The schema was written from the column names and the answers, then checked against the thesaurus V2.13, which names these columns (PROGRESS.md D13 and D14). An instrument of the ASP cohort only. **Year and centre.** 4 of the 6 variables reach 0.5 or more: the four indices (199 to 213 values; verbal comprehension median 101 in children and 129 in 36 adult visits, O33) differ by year (72 to 114 for verbal comprehension, five years with 20 values; the edition is used mostly to 2017, 138 visits, and on 67 visits since 2018) and by centre (79 to 118, three centres): age mix and small groups; no step with a known cause.

wisc5_indices.title: WISC-V: the five indices and the full-scale IQ

asp.notes: The indices of the Wechsler Intelligence Scale for Children, fifth edition: verbal comprehension, visual spatial, fluid reasoning, working memory, processing speed and the full-scale IQ, as the clinician copied them into the medical evaluation (form 119; typed numbers, no script). A box says that this edition was used (wis5: yes on 657 of the 1,234 inclusion answers); the indices are filled only after a yes (657 visits, all inclusion visits). The first index is on 654 inclusion visits (635 children, 19 adults), from 2017 to 2026; the full-scale IQ on 555. The full-scale IQ is typed whether or not the indices agree (the form says so in red: 119.php:8) and is missing on 95 of the 650 visits that hold the five indices (15%); the median spread between the highest and the lowest index is 26 points where it is typed and 29 where it is missing: no clear sign that it is left out when the indices differ. It is more than 10 points outside all five indices on 3 visits. One schema per edition: an index of one edition is never delivered in the column of another. The indices need the norm tables of the test, which are not available: they are delivered as typed. Each index has its own hard limits, those of the publisher: 45 to 155 for the five primary indices and 40 to 160 for the full-scale IQ (WISC-V interpretive report sample, Pearson 2020; Canivez and Watkins 2016: scale_reference.md, confirmed in source). Three low values are outside (two visual spatial indices, one processing speed index, all below 40) and one full-scale IQ above 160: removed (out_of_range) as before, the 45 and 155 limits change no cell. Edition against age: the box is ticked on 19 visits of patients aged 18 or more at the visit, and 2 of the 18 with a date of assessment were 18 or more on that date (iq_assessment_date): the indices belong to that date, not to the visit. The general ability index of iq_assessment is one field for the three editions and cannot be tied to one. The schema was written from the column names and the answers, then checked against the thesaurus V2.13, which names these columns (PROGRESS.md D13 and D14). An instrument of the ASP cohort only. **Year and centre.** 1 of the 7 variables reaches 1.0: the box 'WISC-V done' is yes for 88% of the children and 4% of the adults, 0% to 93% by centre and 0% in 2016 (25 answers: the edition starts in 2017) to 77% by year: age mix. The six indices show no shift of 0.5.

assessment_conditions.title: Conditions and history of the neuropsychological assessment

asp.notes: What the form asks before the tests, on 839 inclusion visits that hold npsy_1 (and one visit at 4 years). 103 of the 839 are of patients under 18 (41 under 16): the form is not only for adults. Seven boxes (npsy_1 to npsy_7, the conditions of the assessment: each is yes on almost every visit but npsy_5 and npsy_6, with a text after npsy_5), the handedness (a code), an earlier Wechsler assessment (atcd_w1, yes on 27 visits, with a code, texts and an age in years and months) and an earlier neuropsychological assessment (atcd_npsy1, yes on 195, with the same details), the date of the assessment and a comment. The date (qsdtc) is on 326 visits, not on all 839, and is more than 1 year from the visit date on 14 of them. The six questions of npsy_1 to npsy_6 carry the names that the other cohorts give to the same questions (the question texts are the same): neuropsy_french_fluent (BP and SZ; DR asks whether French is the mother tongue, neuropsy_french_native, which is another question), neuropsy_state_compatible (SZ and DR), neuropsy_no_visual_disorder and neuropsy_no_hearing_disorder (BP, SZ and DR), neuropsy_learning_disorder and neuropsy_psychotropic_treatment (SZ and DR). Only the names changed. The handedness keeps its own name, handedness_np, and its own codes: 1 left, 2 right, 3 both, as on the form (DR codes 1 as right). It agrees with the handedness of the clinical form on 237 of the 251 visits that have both. NPSY_5 and NPSY_6 hold 1 (yes), 0 (no) and 9 ("does not know", read as missing: 67 visits for npsy_5, 29 for npsy_6). The form (237.php) and the data say 1, 0 and 9; the dictionary V2.13 says 1 yes and 2 no for both: the schema is right and the dictionary wrong. The schema was written from the column names and the answers, then checked against the thesaurus V2.13, which names these columns (PROGRESS.md D13 and D14). An instrument of the ASP cohort only.

executive_functions.title: Executive function tests

asp.notes: A block added in 2018, on 869 inclusion visits: a box "done" (yes on 572, no on 293, "Non connu" on 4, read as unknown), five results, the date and the age in months. The block holds only one test, the revised errands test ("test des commissions révisé"), 569 visits with a result: the time to do the task in seconds (median 380 seconds, 6.3 minutes, against 6.0 minutes in BP and SZ, where the time is in minutes; 9 values of 60 seconds or less look like minutes and are kept), the numbers of useless detours (0 to 4), of times not respected (0 to 6) and of logic errors (0 to 2), and the total number of errors (0 to 9; 6 visits above 6). The stored total, which the schema reads with the range 0 to 20, is the sum of the three counts on 563 of 565 visits (one more has a count missing); in BP and SZ the same stored total has the range 0 to 30. No z-score and no band is delivered, unlike BP and SZ. The application has no rule for this block (its form only shows and hides the boxes, no script computes a score), the version of the test ("revised") is not confirmed as the one of the BP and SZ tables (the literature check of 2026-11-21 did not cover this test), the form has no education and no percentile field, and the years of education of the sociodemographic table (column sd_edulevel, read as education_years_as_stored and not delivered: two scales by centre, O17 (4), M90) are missing on 73% of these visits (418 of 569), where the norms of BP and SZ need them. The schema was written from the column names and the answers, then checked against the thesaurus V2.13, which names these columns (PROGRESS.md D13 and D14). An instrument of the ASP cohort only. The age in months (executive_age_months) is typed in years on 19 of the 36 visits that are more than 2 years from the age at the visit x 12 (24 of the 36 at centre C): not corrected. The TMT, the Stroop, the London tower and the RMIE of the form 240 (426 fields) are in neither the extraction nor the dictionary: requested from the data managers (D29).

common.note: The four counts of errors and their sum are in the three cohorts (from 2017 or 2018; in BP on inclusions from 2021). The time, the z-scores and the bands are in BP and SZ and are computed again from the raw counts with the same tables in both (BP D135; a higher z-score is better; the age typed in the form, 20 to 60 years, and the years of education: 12 years or more is the class of the baccalaureate, as for the other tests, whatever the class ticked in the form). The z-scores typed in BP mix two sign conventions (BP D126) and are only checks. ASP has the counts only, in seconds, with no norm: no z-score, no band (the schema executive_functions holds this test only).

social_cognition.title: Social cognition: faces, faux pas and the six films

asp.notes: Tests added in 2018, on 996 inclusion visits (273 children): a box "done" (cogsoc, yes on 906, no on 87, not known on 3), the date and the age in months; a facial emotion test (tref: done on 708 visits, seven scores from 0 to 100, read as the percentage of correct answers in all and for six emotions); a faux pas test (faupa: done on 819, one score from 0 to 100); and the six films of FACE SZ (lis: done on 707, one score on 698 visits, the distance to reference ratings: lower is better). 9 is read as "not known". The seven scores of the facial emotion test are the percentages of right answers for every emotion together, then joy, anger, sadness, disgust, contempt and fear. The six films. The ASP forms (119, 346 and 349) have no field for the thirty ratings that FACE SZ records: LIS_SCORE is typed in, with no script that computes it. Only the score is in the extraction, so it cannot be recomputed as in SZ. Its 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles are 9.5, 15.0 and 26.9 (SZ: 9.9, 16.0 and 29.5). One value is 99.0 (the next is 59, the SZ maximum is 71): it is inside the range of 0 to 100 and is delivered as typed; it may be a typing error. Scores above 100. The scores of the facial emotion and of the faux pas tests are percentages: one value of tref01 and 5 of faupa01 are in the 700s (out_of_range). The form checks the six emotion scores against 100 but not the total score of the facial emotion test nor the faux pas score (eASPERGER.js lines 3024-3090; A94), which is why the values in the 700s are in these two columns only. The faux pas field takes four characters and 305 of its 806 values carry a decimal, so a value in the 700s is a lost decimal point or a typing error. They are not repaired. Question for the centres. Ages in months. The age at the social cognition tests is more than 2 years from the age at the visit x 12 on 85 of 809 visits; on 59 of them the typed value is within 1.5 of the age in years (typed in years). The age at the executive function tests (executive_age_months) does the same on 36 of 550 visits (19 of them within 1.5 of the age in years). Not corrected. Centre D types the age in years (37 of its 43 values are within 1.5 of the age in years, and it holds 37 of the 59 typed in years above), which is the step of its median. The schema was written from the column names and the answers, then checked against the thesaurus V2.13, which names these columns (PROGRESS.md D13 and D14). An instrument of the ASP cohort only. At centre D the scores for anger, sadness, disgust and fear are one photo of nine lower than at centres B and C (medians 66, 67, 55 and 78 against 78, 78, 67 and 89, adults only). Every centre types percentages of nine photos for each emotion (C and D sometimes truncate them, by less than 1 point), the children are 4% of D's tests, the test is on one form only and the gap has no date. No cause is known; the step is documented here. Years and centres (definition of done, D88; centres lettered as in D77, A the children's centre): the two steps of centre D (the age in years, the four emotions one photo lower) are stated above; the other scores and the boxes 'done' (58% to 100% by centre, 58% to 96% by year) have no other step.

Adults and children.

wais4_cubes.title: WAIS-IV, block design

asp.notes: Block design: 14 items scored from 0 to 7, their total, the scaled score and its z-score, on 215 inclusion visits. The WAIS-IV of this cohort is recorded item by item, on about 210 to 295 inclusion visits depending on the subtest (302 visits in all, 12 of patients under 18), from 2013 to 2026. It is on 14% of the inclusion visits of 2013, 42% of 2014, 36% of 2015, 18% to 19% of 2016 and 2017, 3% to 11% of 2018 to 2023, 21% to 22% of 2024 and 2025 and 7% of 2026 so far. It is the fourth edition: the visual puzzles and the sequencing part of the digit span exist only in it. No other edition of the scale is recorded in this table. The extraction has no column for the edition: wais_version (wais4) is read from the first item of each subtest, with the same block in the eleven schemas of the WAIS-IV, and is filled on the 302 visits that hold one of them. Checked on every visit: the stored total is the sum of the items. The stored total equals the sum of the items on 215 of the 215 visits that hold every item. An item of the block design is scored 0, 2 or 4, and up to 7 with the time bonus of the last items. The raw total is the sum of the items (wais4_bd_total); the stored total is a check (wais4_bd_total_stored, not delivered). No z-score is stored for this subtest: wais4_bd_z, (scaled score - 10) / 3, is computed and has no stored value to be compared with. An instrument of the ASP cohort only. Scaled score and z-score. They are recomputed and delivered (decision of the project lead for the standard scores of the neuropsychological tests): the scaled score is read in the WAIS-IV table of the application (norms/wais4_block_design.csv) from the raw total, and the z-score is (scaled score - 10) / 3. The form has no typed age in this cohort: the table is read with the age at the date of the assessment form (age basis, below). The visits are of patients from 15.9 to 65 years; the one of 15.9 years is below the first age of the tables and gets norm_missing. The stored score is wais4_bd_scaled_stored, not delivered. Verified: the scaled score differs from the stored one on 2 of the 214 visits that have both (0.9%, score_mismatch; the same with the age at the visit); 1 visit is not recomputed (the patient of 15.9 years). Age basis. The application (eAsperger, script 280_score.js, function gere_ageNPSY) computes the age at the date of the assessment form (QSDTC), not at the visit date, and the data show that it did so from about 2015 on. The table is therefore read with the age at the form date (wais4_bd_assessment_date, read from the raw column qsdtc and not delivered; score fields age_date and age_date_since 2015-01-01) where the visit is dated 2015 or later and the form date is within 366 days of the visit, and with the age at the visit elsewhere. In this subtest the age at the form date changes no score.

earlier_diagnosis.title: Diagnoses made before the expert centre

asp.notes: One value per patient, from the form filled before the assessment (the columns are repeated on every row of a patient and never change). Filled for 1,072 of the 2,318 patients: 62% of the adults and 24% of the children, and 20% to 73% of the inclusions depending on the year. The schema was written from the column names and the answers, then checked against the thesaurus V2.13, which names these columns (PROGRESS.md D13 and D14). oldiag ("ancien diagnostic") is 1 for 106 patients, 0 for 956 and 9 for 10: an earlier diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder, 9 read as "not known". Its date is given for 61 patients and "by whom" (oldiag_ki) for 95, (psychiatrist, paediatrician, general practitioner, other). diag_autr is another earlier diagnosis (yes for 495 patients, no for 542, 9 for 22); a free text adds to it for 143 patients. Its kind (diag_autr_kel) is a list of 18 boxes in form 241 (lines 15-37), several of which can be ticked, and the export keeps one: the label of the lowest-numbered box ticked (easperger_screening.sql lines 29-50). It is delivered as a category with the labels of the export (490 patients, 15 labels: depression or mood disorder 131, ADHD 106, other 89, the others 36 or fewer); the other boxes ticked are lost (request R165). Three limits: the boxes 10 and 12 both carry the label 'Nevrose obsessionnelle' and the boxes 4 and 8 'Trouble de l'attachement' in the form (the export writes '4' for the box 4); an older list of the form (commented out, line 14) had other kinds under the same numbers (box 1 'Psychose infantile', 10 OCD, 11 social phobia, 16 dyspraxia), so a label may stand for the old kind of its box on the forms of the first years; and with no box ticked the export writes the free text into this column (line 48), which no row of this extraction holds (decision D79). An instrument of the ASP cohort only. Years and centres (definition of done, D88; centres lettered as in D77, A the children's centre): the other earlier diagnosis is yes for 36% to 79% of the patients by centre and period (A 52%, B 51%, C 41%, D 45%, E 58%, F 58%, G 65%) and 40% to 54% by year from 2015: a habit of the centres around a yes near one half, which flips the median; no step by year.

non_drug_care.title: Non-drug treatments (fifteen boxes)

asp.notes: One value per patient. Fifteen yes/no boxes named trt_non_parmaco_1 to _15 ("traitement non pharmacologique"), filled for 1,116 patients (boxes 1 to 5; 695 delivered, see below) and 1,145 (boxes 6 to 15): 64% of the adults and 25% of the children. The most frequent are the boxes 11 (320 patients), 10 (235) and 12 (96); the boxes 4 and 5 are 0 for every patient. The thesaurus names the kinds 6 to 15 (SESSAD, school inclusion, speech therapist, psychomotor therapist, psychologist, psychiatrist, other, occupational therapist, social skills group, mobile autism team). Small groups or habits, no known cause, documented here.
